        Observing how foolish and useless his father was, Baal made a decision.

        “I am the only one who can revive the glory of the royal family and step onto the dominant throne.”

        To overthrow the corrupted aristocracy, the first thing Baal did was to send his brother Belial away from the battlefield. Baal didn’t do it just to protect his sibling, it was also a plan against the aristocracy— Even if Baal was killed by them, Belial would remain as a legitimate heir to the throne.

        This was how “Pioneers” came about. After sending Belial away, Baal started preparing for his plan. Lacking military power and resources, he went to Eve the grand duchess, who had the most frivolous reputation among the aristocrats.

        Persuaded by Baal, the two married each other and Eve transferred all of her power to him. With authority, bringing the rebellious aristocrats under control was but a piece of cake to Baal.

        The capture of other aristocrats alerted their leader, who immediately sought allies from the remaining aristocrats to stop Baal’s schemes.

        “I shall be able to defeat them with my current power, but the prize for my victory would be a war-torn country.”

        Just when Baal was nonplussed, he came— Laplace, the demon from the ancient times who possessed prodigious power, was here to assist Baal by crushing the aristocracy with minimum force. Baal then reallocated the aristocratic resources to help the people and restore the authority of the royal family.

        Baal was hailed by the public as his father passed away “coincidentally” at the same time. Naturally, Baal was the one who ascended to the throne. Standing in the grand hall during his enthronement, he observed the joyful crowd. 

        “So this is what you get for victory.” A proud, haughty grin spread over Baal’s face.  

        Baal had always been pursuing pleasure on his own. He preferred going into the wild for hunting rather than sitting in the palace and waiting for tributes.

        “Now it’s time to conquer him.” Baal hid his smile and returned to the palace. Striding to the end of the corridor, he entered the bedroom.

        There he was, standing on the starlit balcony— Laplace, the young, handsome man who took Baal’s breath away, the demon from the ancient times.

        Sitting on the railing, Laplace stuck up his fair, slender legs. The way he held a glass of dew between his fingers carried a natural look of mellowness and seductiveness.

        “Congratulations, we can now carry out our plans.” Laplace toasted Baal, who grabbed his hand and downed the glass. 

        “Thanks to your help.” Baal refilled the glass with some crimson liquid that resembled the color of blood.

        “Hmm, I did make some predictions, but you wouldn’t be able to succeed if you weren’t so adroit. Not only did you succeed, but you did it so flawlessly that you exceeded my expectation.” Laplace took a sip of dew, which dyed his lips red. He looked unbelievably alluring.

        “If you say so, do me a favor.” Baal requested in a low voice.

        Laplace smiled cunningly with a shrug, “Fair enough, go on.”

        “Give me a kiss.”

        “... Are you kidding me?”

        “No… Or is it that you’re scared?” said Baal tauntingly.

        “Shush.” Upon the utterance of the word, Laplace came infinitely close to Baal. Pulling Baal’s sleeve, Laplace tipped his toes and stuck even closer. They were so intimate that they could feel the breath of each other. But before their lips met, Laplace turned away with an artful smile. His long eyelashes caressed Baal’s cheek and retreated, leaving his face burning.

        “We’ll talk about that after our plans are carried out.” said Laplace, looking so innocent in his smile that Baal could hardly wait to tame him. Staring at Laplace as he took leave, a burning desire filled Baal’s heart. 

        “Someday, I will own you, even the parts of you that you’ve not yet recognized.”
STORY_2585:
In a luxurious bedroom, a female demon was lying on the bed. Her body was so emaciated that everyone would believe she was dead if they didn’t see the heaving of her chest.

        The demon was by no means ordinary. She was the grand duchess and the leader of the 7 aristocrats. However, the tides turned as she fell in love with a disgraced god. Giving birth to her daughter had wrecked her body. And there she was, lying in bed helplessly.

        A pitter-patter of footsteps echoed in the hallway, bringing a girl with a petite figure to the bedroom door. Her orange hair flipped as she bounced up and down. She looked gorgeous.

        “Mom!” The 5-year-old girl thrust herself to the bedside and grabbed her mother’s skinny hands. Her movements woke the grand duchess up.

        “It’s you, Eve… My beloved daughter...” The grand duchess wanted to hold the girl’s hands, but was too weak to do so. She covered her hands on Eve’s and murmured feebly, “I can’t be with you any longer.” 

        “Boohoo… No, no… Don’t leave me, Mom...” Poor little Eve was crying her eyes out. As young as she was, her beauty was already blooming.

        “Eve… Your road ahead must be really tough, but remember, you have to stay strong...”

        “Okay… I will try my best,” said Little Eve in a reassuring manner, arching her back. The grand duchess was relieved by her response and gave her a smile.

        “Maybe, if I hadn’t fallen in love with your father and given birth to you, I could’ve lived longer and enjoyed the privileges of my status as the leader of the seven aristocrats. But a life like this wouldn’t be a complete one,” said the grand duchess as she looked at Eve affectionately. “Dear Eve, I feel so complete after falling in love with your father and finding my true love. I’m so much happier than I was before I met him.”

        The smile on the grand duchess’ face was full of bliss and peace, radiating the brilliance of life. Eve was deeply moved. 

        “Eve, my daughter. May you find the love of your life too. That’d be a marvelous miracle...” The last beam of light in the duchess’ eyes faded; her life perished.

        Observing the peaceful face of her mother, Eve was not afraid at all. Rather, she was a little envious. A fanciful imagination about “true love” was implanted in her heart. Someday, she prayed, that she’d be able to find the love of her life just like her mother.

        However, as the heiress of the grand duchess, it was impossible for Eve to find a lover freely. The pressure from her kin almost suffocated her. Like a bird trapped in a fancy cage, she witnessed how her relatives manipulated each other for their own benefit.

        Eve wanted to escape from these despicable people but lacked what she needed until his presence—Baal, the grand prince.

        He courted her actively and wrote her passionate letters, but Eve was clear that all Baal had wanted was her power. She considered it a golden opportunity to break free, so she proceeded to meet Baal.

        “You’re just as gorgeous as I imagined.” Elegantly, Baal gave Eve a light kiss on her right hand and looked into her eyes lovingly. “Even if you rejected me a million times, I’d still wait for you.”

        “...Ha, grand prince, you’re quite good at acting. Very interesting.” Eve giggled, her stunning eyes examined Baal closely. “You didn’t fall in love with me at all. I detest lies; they’re despicable. Tell me your wish and what you can offer.”

        Baal’s loving smile vanished, giving way to an expression of haughty pride as he proudly declared, “Get engaged with me, and I’ll grant you the freedom that you’ve always wanted.”

        Baal took out a sphere, which reflected a lively world.

        “Just lend me your name. I’ll eliminate all the unloyal aristocrats for you and make you a pioneer, then you can go to a whole new world and pursue the life that you’ve been longing for.”

        Eve was completely ignorant of what Baal said since the world reflected in the sphere had attracted all her attention.

        “In such a magnificent world, I can definitely find the true love that mother told me about.”

        As a result, Eve accepted Baal’s terms and became his fiancée. Granting him the power of her family, Baal managed to eradicate the corrupted aristocrats.

        “Eve.” Baal called her as he came to the balcony. Eve was looking at the landscape somewhere far away.

        Eve didn’t move until Baal came to stand next to her. She said lightly, “It used to be beautiful here, but everything has withered.”

        “Nothing lasts forever.” Putting his hands behind him, Baal looked into the distance too. But what he saw was completely different from what Eve saw. “Even if you go to Continent Tarones, you won’t be able to find what you want.”

        “How would you know without trying?” Eve smiled optimistically. The expression on her delicate and innocent face resembled that of a fearless youth. “I’ve got to find it, the marvelous miracle.”

        “Is that so… Good luck, then.” Baal refrained from saying more and left Eve alone, who got her hopes up and travelled to the continent in excitement.

        Nevertheless, Baal was right. 

        Drenched in blood and mud, Eve sat on the ground in the icy rain.

        “Ah… If this is how fragile true love really is, does anything even last forever?”

        “Yes. Something does.” A young man’s clear voice came through the rain. Eve turned to see two men walking toward her: Baal, her “fiancé”, and a handsome young man she did not recognize.

        But Eve had no interest in who he was. She wanted only one thing from him—the answer he seemed so certain of. So she asked, “What is it?”

        The young man smiled as he stepped closer. He gestured toward Eve’s heart and said, “The love you have for yourself.”

        “My love...”

        “If someone else’s love can’t fill that void inside you, then why not give yourself that love?” He continued, “That way, it will last forever.”

        “...Heh. I never thought of it that way.” Eve chuckled. “You’re interesting. I like you.”

        “I like you too, Eve.” Laplace, the ancient demon, extended his hand toward her. “Come join our plan.”

        Without the slightest hesitation, Eve took his hand.
STORY_2595:
In the Heavenly Kingdom, two men were sitting on the summit surrounded by clouds. A white-haired, burly man Chiyou pulled a long face as he played chess with Huangdi Huangdi. “I...lose.” Chiyou was so reluctant to accept this result.

        “Then?” Huangdi asked calmly as he spread his paper fan.

        “I’m a man of my word. Xiao Feng...is yours, temporarily.” With a whistle, Chiyou summoned a firebird to come.

        “Ha, this is truly breathtaking. I'll take good care of it——”

        “This is just temporary! I’ll win it back next time!” Chiyou jumped off the peak after the conversation; thoughts kept flashing in his mind.

        “First, I need to improve my chess skills...Only she could help me!” Changing direction, Chiyou rushed to the eastern side through the sky, arriving at an exquisite residence by the lake. The aroma of lotus filled the air even from a distance.

        “Here it is, the residence of He Xian’gu,” Chiyou thought to himself. When he was about to step forward, the door was opened, revealing a graceful figure.

        “Lady He Xian’gu, please wait!” Chiyou tried to stop her, but He Xian’gu was in a bad mood today, glaring at him with a frown.

        “You’re...Chiyou, one of the Divine Xians…” Her brows tightened even more.

        Although she had never talked with Chiyou, He Xian’gu still heard of his history from the Xians, who was nicknamed “Heartstring Tugger” among the females. It was known that Chiyou’s actions often misled other female Xians unintentionally, so He Xian’gu did not have a liking for him.

        Nevertheless, Chiyou was totally unaware of his mistaken impression. “Yes! I’d like to invite you——”, he requested with a carefree smile.

        “Sorry I’m busy, so please excuse me.” He Xian’gu cut in without any hesitation and walked away.

        However, something miraculous happened. A gust of strong wind caught He Xian’gu off guard and blew her down——

        She fell into someone’s warm embrace, with her gaze fixing on a handsome face from such a close distance. “He’er, did you get hurt?” Chiyou asked worriedly.

        “What did you just call me?!” The call sent ripples into He Xian’gu’s heart, but she managed to maintain her composure.

        “It’s rumored that the lotus will look particularly beautiful when you’re next to them. The fragrance of you and the aroma of the lotus are a perfect match, which makes me call you even without realizing it.” Chiyou meant what he said.

        He Xian’gu was not only put on such a cute nickname by Chiyou, but she was also described with her body scent explicitly, which had completely flushed her face. He Xian’gu made a cough to calm herself down and changed a topic. “What can I do for you?”

        Chiyou was reminded of his original purpose of the visit. “I heard that you’re an exceptional chess player. Can you teach me?”

        “I owed him a favor. Wouldn’t it be cold if I turn him down…” Then, He Xian’gu had a good idea.

        “My chess skills are not sophisticated enough to be your teacher, but I don’t mind sharing some experience with you. But in return you need to do me a favor.”

        “Fair enough.” Chiyou patted his chest with confidence. “Consider it done.”

        Therefore, Chiyou followed He Xian’gu to descend to the realm, heading east to the bottom of the sea——the underwater world full of corals and algae.

        “Your mission is to collect this pink seaweed. Remember, it has to be pink.” He Xian’gu handed it over to Chiyou.

        “The pink seaweed...but what for?” He asked in puzzlement.

        “Ah...It’s important for my own purposes. Stop talking and go find it.” He Xian’gu was guilty of speaking too much, but the straightforward Chiyou did not pay attention, and followed her order to collect the seaweed.

        At dusk, Chiyou brought loads of seaweed back to He Xian’gu. When he was about to return, a shout was heard.

        “What do you mean by this?”

        “It’s He’er. She seems to be in trouble. Gotta help her!” Following the voice, Chiyou found He Xian’gu quickly, who was confronting a troop of prawns and crabs.

        “He’er!” Chiyou rushed to her in no time; his solid voice somehow made her heart pump fast.

        “Tut! Another god, how annoying!” The prawn general said with disdain.

        “This is our turd. Just because Master Ao Guang isn’t here, it doesn’t mean you can trespass on our land! Leave or die!” The crab general raised its pincer to intimidate.

        “Ha, funny! Then show me what you’ve got!” The charming smile of He Xian’gu had caught the attention of the generals. Before long, shame and anger made them flush all over when they stayed focused.

        “Ignorant fool! Let us show you the power of our clan! Everyone, march!” Under the general’s command, troops of sea monsters swarmed to surround He Xian’gu and Chiyou.

        “Humph! Weaklings are weaklings. Let me—— Chiyou?” When He Xian’gu was gathering power, he covered her hand with his palm.

        “I’ll be sad if you get hurt, so let me handle this.” Chiyou fixed his gaze at He Xian’gu, who was touched by his low yet gentle voice. Her heart was beating fast like a girl falling in love——

        “Hold your horses and wake up, He Xian’gu! This guy doesn’t mean what he says! Don’t forget other Xians’ comments about him.”

        “Cough, well I’ll leave them to you then.” She pretended to be calm.

        “Stop the show! We’ll send both of you to heaven,” said the prawn general.

        “Right, we have the advantage in water. You can’t beat us!” The crab general continued.

        “Ha, indeed. I’m not good at fighting underwater.” Chiyou took out a piece of flint and swallowed. Soon he was coiled up by flames. A crimson eye was revealed in his chest, exuding with an intimidating aura.

        “In this case, I’ll just evaporate all water.” Chiyou, buffed by the berserk power, was releasing an overwhelming Xian energy, which was turned into fire, overspreading the entire area. In the blink of an eye, the water nearby was evaporated; those sea monsters were therefore immobilized due to a lack of water.

        Chiyou summoned a bone sword, approaching the generals step by step——

        “Hold!” An azure figure stood in front of the army. “I, Ao Guang, Dragon King of the Sea, apologize for my troops’ recklessness.”

        “Humph! You’re the one who started with this fight! Do you think you can settle it just by an apology——” Chiyou stopped talking as He Xian’gu patted his shoulder.

        “For the sake of Tianzun, we’re even now,” He Xian’gu said in a low voice. 

        “Thank you.” Ao Guang signalled a soldier with a gaze to hand a basket to He Xian’gu, which contained the pink seaweed she was looking for.

        “I know you’re looking for skincare ingredients. Consider this as our gratitude.”

        “Skincare?” Chiyou murmured and looked at her. “So you’re using this for making skin products?”

        Embarrassed, He Xian’gu had no choice but to admit. “Recently I’ve been busy dealing with the Holy Gods overnight. Yesterday Lü Dongbin even said I looked old, so I was counting on the pink seaweed for skincare. What? Isn’t it normal——Em!” 

        Chiyou raised her chin with his right hand to take a closer look at her face. Unable to break loose, He Xian’gu could not help but looked him in the eyes. Then he wore a smile suddenly as if he found an exciting thing. “You’re as perfect as lotus in nature. Those skincare products are completely unnecessary.”

        “You——!” Chiyou’s words touched He Xian’gu’s heart. Blushing, she turned around and summoned a lotus in order to cover up the embarrassment. “Let’s, let’s go back!”

        “Okay!” The upright Chiyou was unaware of the trouble he made and followed her back to the Heavenly Kingdom buoyantly.

        Under the guidance of He Xian’gu, Chiyou successfully won the chess match against Huangdi afterwards, getting his Xiao Feng back. However, things were not over yet...

STORY_2601:
The mysterious R’lyeh released light; the crystals on the scales exuded dazzling colors, and ample water elements surrounded Ursula with soft waves. Immersed in her thoughts, she saw an illusion of the elements...

        Novalis acquired power from Moonlight Golem; the purplish-dark flame ignited bloodlust in his eyes, against the frightened villagers. Triggering the power of resonance, Ursula used her soft energy to pacify the restlessness of the Dragon Follower, thereby successfully saving the lives of those villagers. She pulled Novalis and bowed for apologies, and the villagers also left in awe.

        “Why did you stop me! They blamed us for bringing the monster!”
        “They’re afraid of us because they know nothing about us. As long as we show kindness, one day they’ll accept us.”
        “Impossible.”

        At this moment, Ursula had a feeling that someone was pulling her hem. She looked down and saw a little girl handing her a medicine bottle. “Please take the medicine and, thank you...for saving us.” The girl glanced at Novalis timidly, then put the medicine bottle into Ursula's hand and hurried back to her family hiding behind the house. After the farewell, Ursula turned to Novalis and smiled, who turned away with a displeased face.

        “One day, we and humans will be able to understand each other and live harmoniously. By then, the message of Primordial Dragon shall be delivered.”

        Ursula decided to stay in this village, hoping to establish relationships with these villagers, and eventually become a stronghold for humans and hybrids. However, the villagers still remained alert, so they headed out for the Deep Ones nearby, in an attempt to persuade them to coexist with the villagers. However, the Deep Ones knew well that the villagers would not even accept Ursula, let alone the half-fish hybrids.

        Until one day, a metal figure appeared at the entrance of the village, hurting the people with its purple-ish aura claw. The wounded villagers fled with fear. On the other hand, although Ursula and Novalis faced up to the enemy, their strength was no match for this demon. Therefore, they lured the enemy to the sea in the battle, and let the Deep Ones support to repel the enemy together.

        Saved twice from the verge of death, the villagers felt sorry for Ursula and finally accepted her suggestion to coexist peacefully with the Deep Ones. Even though the villagers could not hide their terror at the appearance of the half-fish, the hybrids finally found a place to live after the two species worked hard together. Full of joy, Ursula  succeeded in creating a harmonious world.

        “The dawn of the Ethereal Dragon is meant to liberate the humans from wars. He wants humans to survive...Let’s listen to resonance.”

        Ursula preached the purpose of Dagon to the people on the seaside square; the hybrids were there too, learning to understanding the language of the dragon. As the children were curious about the Dracospirit next to the Dragon Maiden, they sat around trying to touch the floating Dracospirit. But as soon as the child returned to his mother, he got scolded immediately.

        “That’s the soul of the monster! Why did you touch it! From now on you’ll never go to see that Maiden anymore.”
        “She did save us, but isn’t too much for us to live with those monsters?”
        “I can’t take it anymore! If we get rid of the Maiden, the village will be back to normal, right?”

        The villagers were obedient on the surface because they feared the power of the Ethereal Dragon, but in the bottom of their hearts they had never accepted the hybrids and the Dragon Maiden. In secrecy, the villagers were discussing how to drive the aliens away.

        One day, a villager screamed out of fear as he saw the Deep Ones summon a strange whirlpool in the sea, which had drawn Ursula’s immediate attention. “Alright, everything is fine now. Your ship can sail past.” Ursula was unaware of the malice in that villager’s eyes.

        “Now!” The villager captured Ursula with a fishing net. When he was about to stab her with a spear, the Dragon Follower withstood the attack with his halberd. “Ursula! I’ve already said it’s impossible!” Blank, Ursula looked at the villager who was beclouded by the bloodlust.

        “Ursula, humans, can never, live, harmoniously, with us.” The Deep Ones pulled the fishing net into the sea in order to release Ursula, who was deeply in the pain of being betrayed by people. Although tears could not be seen in the water, her emotions seeped from the unstable resonance…

        “Even if I’m betrayed and abandoned, I still have to pass on the voice of the Ethereal Dragon, because only I can be the bridge between humans and dragons.”

STORY_2603:
In Mount Holy Cthugha, Agatha immersed herself into the heat of fire. The Dracospirit inside her resonated with the fire elements, bringing Agatha to another life journey in the illusion…

        “You don’t like this?”
        “I have wings! I don’t need your help!”
        Waking up from a sleep, Agatha saw a blond youth so close to herself as soon as her eyes opened——Agatha immediately broke free from Honor’s arms. With mixed expressions, Honor wanted to lean forward, but Agatha stepped back promptly, knocking over a water bottle beside her.

        Despite the fact that this same scene had happened so many times, Agatha still did not know how to handle it properly, and the strange emotions that arose in her heart made her unbearable. Agatha had never been in any relationship before. What's more, she witnessed this youth growing up in front of her, just like the Dragon Follower she raised up in the past. This made her feeling even more complicated...The fire Dracospirit surrounded Agatha closely and touched the blond youth as if they were familiar to each other.

        “What am I exactly...Am I affected by the Dracospirit? What’s my feeling to him…?”

        Agatha covered herself with the dragon wings and cried. At a loss, Honor tried to reach out to touch her wings, but got rejected.

        “Just, just let me calm down alone…” Agatha suppressed her voice; clearly she was sobbing. Puzzled by her own emotions, Agatha did not respond to Honor anymore. Faced with the current situation, she did not want to leave, even if she was confused, she wanted to understand the connection between her rippling feelings and the youth in front of her...

        When Agatha got herself together, Honor had already gone. A feeling of loss struck her spontaneously, but this sense of loss made her feel even more perplexed. It was Agatha’s decision to avoid his embrace, why did she feel empty for the moment...Was it because she expected Honor to stay by her side forever? Then, Agatha got up and searched for Honor's whereabouts.

        Hustle and bustle were the theme of the city. The fountain reflected the colorful light under the sun. Lush green leaves swayed gently in the wind. Iridescent flowers were blooming brilliantly...These all added up to the season of spring. But how many times had the fall gone and spring come...Agatha had no clue about it. Searching around, she was unable to catch a glimpse of Honor, but bumped into a female demon who was about to pass out. As the demon fell into her arms, Agatha immediately carried her to sit down in the shade. The demon could not help gasping; a blush came into her pale complexion. 

        It turned out that the female demon was thirsty for blood. Agatha offered some as she could not bear to see her suffer, which had successfully relieved her symptom...The demon said her lover would soon come to pick her up. During the waiting, Agatha also talked to her about her own inner struggle.

        “Are you afraid of opening your heart because you can’t bear to lose again?”

        The words of the demon hit Agatha’s weak spot. She walked down memory lane to the prison cell, looking back at the appearance and disappearance of golden silhouettes one by one...the Dragon Followers she loved but gone for good. Every time the light ignited the holy flame, she always wanted to subconsciously avoid it, as if she would see the soul of the previous one emerging from it, and heard the only kind and loyal calls to her in the Holylight City in the past generations…

        “You are our guiding light! I can never give you up.”

        However, this voice was the only thing which created a different future for Agatha who had been imprisoned for many years. Her tears slowly dripped on the cold skin of the female demon. Such coolness made Agatha miss the warmth that she had experienced many times since the first waking from the dragon's sleep...

        Embarrased, Agatha turned away. Tears still welled up in her eyes, smearing the streets into a hazy view, and the light in front of her became more and more dazzling...Agatha wiped her tears. When she refocused, she found that the light silhouette was not an illusion, but the person she had been missing——Honor. He was running in her direction with a man in a yellow suit…

        The man picked up the female demon from Agatha’s arms. She then hugged the man back and sucked his blood with a bite without hesitation. However, Agatha’s attention was all on the blond youth before her.

        “Agatha, I——” Before he finished the conversation, Agatha held Honor tight and even covered him with her wings. Surprised, Honor slowly reached out to embrace Agatha...

        “Sorry, I don’t have the courage to admit my feelings about you. Just let me stay with the flames. Rather than taking the risk of losing someone, I’d pick a stable path to be the eternal fire.”

STORY_2605:
In the embrace of the wind, Barbara had a dream of her alternative life accompanied by the elements in the air and voice of Byakhee…

        “...The breeze continues to circulate. It is your breath that brings vitality! The immortality provides shade for me, and the towering giant tree shelters all beings…”

        The wizard in front of her chanted prayers, making it difficult for Barbara to hear the whispers of the wind anymore. She held a wooden ball in her hand, looking around curiously. The elders and adults were all watching where they were all intently. The surrounding floating stones reflected the green light of the circle, and the children nearby were embracing each other anxiously…

        Suddenly, the wind was blowing violently. Everyone remained calm, except Barbara who was the only one understanding the implied warning. “Leave now!”

        The magic circle began to emit a strong green light; sounds like flies vibrating wings were surging in everyone’s heart. The children screamed in panic, while Barbara immediately followed the wind's warning to escape from the circle!

        “Hey! Don’t run away!” The wizard wanted to stop Barbara but his attention was caught by a Dracospirit summoned in the circle…

        “The spirit has dawned! It’s my honor to receive your blessing!”

        Barbara ran desperately. Her petite body was rushing among the bushes, until she could no longer hear the footsteps chasing behind. By then she realized that she was lost in the woods. Barbara held up the magic ball in her hand, unfortunately receiving no guidance. She had to listen to the sound of the wind.

        “Something is approaching!”

        Several werewolves emerged; Barbara drew back in horror. When she was about to be attacked, another wild beast repelled! The shadow let out an intimidating roar above Barbara, frightening the werewolves back. As she turned around, a white tiger was seen, which was staring at herself with a pair of sharp eyes...

        The wooden ball suddenly emitted a soft green light. Drawn by which, the white tiger became tame and gentle, crouching before Barbara with a curious look. Noticed by the sound of the wind, Barbara knew that the white tiger was not hostile, so she stretched out her hand to stroke its fur. They met and became the support of each other. Barbara used the magic ball to feed the white tiger with earth elements; in return, the white tiger protected Barbara from monsters. Years had passed. Barbara had grown into a young girl, and the white tiger became huge and stronger than before.

        “Leave, gnomes! This is our territory!” Barbara swung a staff that evolved from a wooden ball as she ran. The core of the staff radiated a green light as it absorbed the elements from the gnomes. The white tiger leaped to Barbara's side and watched them fleeing.

        “Alright, what next...Let’s take the elements from the elves then!” However, the white tiger remained still, as if signalling her to stop.

        “Why! Are you sure such a small amount of elements can fill your stomach?” Barbara was puzzled, but still insisted on heading towards the habitat of the elves, who ran away immediately as soon as she came. When Barbara raised her staff, the white tiger stood in the way between her and the elves.

        “Don’t overdo it. Must maintain, ecological, balance.” The white tiger's heartfelt voice reached Barbara through the wind of elements. Putting down the staff, she let the white tiger breath towards the core, which released the light of the elements, eventually turning into a breeze sent across the jungle. Nourished by the elements, the elves were energized, and the whole forest was blessed with shine and vitality...

        “The evergreen forest is truly beautiful…” Barbara felt.

        However, an uninvited guest was drawn by the wind——a giant toad, which leaped over and smashed the woods; its shockwave turned into the wind sharp as a blade to destroy everything around. The giant toad not only absorbed the elements nearby, but also devoured the lives of the forest. From the sound of the wind, Barbara learned that there was greater power hidden in this strange beast, and the sound of the wing vibration resembling a fly evoked her deep memory...

        “I won’t let you destroy our home even if you’re the emissary of the Ethereal Dragon!”

        Barbara raised her staff to collect the elements in the wind, and directed this power into the body of the white tiger to make it even bigger. At last, the enemy was defeated; the elements were given back to the creatures of the woods. The rescued live beings thanked Barbara and the white tiger for the good deed, and praised them as the guardians of the forest.

        As the defeated giant toad was unable to provide elements, the starving Ethereal Dragon could no longer remain silent but let out an echoing roar in the wind...The sound sent an earthquake from the obelisk to the city and the jungle. Touching the white tiger, Barbara gazed at the source of the wind——Cassilda ruins.

        “Only by rescuing the Ethereal Dragon and satisfying his hunger can greater chaos be prevented. I will dedicate myself to the forest, gather strength and prevent the wind from fading away.”

STORY_2607:
Honor fell asleep under the holy flame.   Tulzscha’s power was churning in his body, as if the elements could sense his inner desire, thus forming a dream that allowed him to experience a different choice of life…

        Her horns and long eyelashes glowed with gold, with her hair hanging down to the red scales. Looking at the asleep demi-dragon maiden, a sense of warmth sent a ripple to Honor’s heart, who could not help but reach out towards her.

        “A gentleman shouldn’t do this! This is only the affection of the previous Dragon Spiritors, but not mine!” Honor turned his face away, doing his best to suppress the desires in his heart. He threw the Sword of Dracospirits on the mud ground angrily, trying to put aside the memories that were not his own. But when Honor met the face of the sleeping maiden again, he could not help imagining that he was lying in her arms...

        “Only by leaving her, I can get rid of this perplexity. I’ve fulfilled my mission to cut off the shackles of the dragon maiden and set her free. I guess it’s time to say goodbye.”

        Honor looked back at the maiden, imprinting her face in his mind before he left alone. While flying in the sky, the Sword of Dracospirits on his waist started vibrating, as if disagreeing to Honor’s decision. The leak of the holy flame made him pain; Honor changed his hand to hold the sword. As he gazed at the reflection, it seemed to reflect the appearance of the Dragon Spiritors of the past...

        “I love the glints of the sword!”
        “Mother…”
        “He’s dead. I am his successor, Toler.”
        “Don’t die that easily, okay?” A familiar female voice came to his ears.

        “Enough! Stop that! That’s not me!” Honor could not stand the gush of memories. Losing sanity to swing his sword, he flew out of control in the air, and eventually crashed into a tree and fell to the ground. When his consciousness was dim, he saw a red figure with dragon wings running towards him…

        “Ag...Agatha?”

        Sunlight came through the window. The color of the sky outside was reflected in Honor's eyes. He got up in a daze and found himself in a wooden house. A strange girl came to see Honor’s injuries, but his attention only focused on the dragon horns, red scales and dragon wings on the girl…“You are not Agatha. Who are you?” “I’m Magrence.”

        Magrence, who was also a demi-dragon, rescued Honor who had fainted in the woods and took him to the village for healing. She carefully bandaged his wound. When her dragon claws touched him, Honor subconsciously turned his face away. However, it was a surprise that his heart did not give him a great throb as expected. Confused, Honor looked at Magrence, whose scaly face did not evoke his urge to kiss. He felt at a loss for this unusually peaceful heart.

        Honor climbed over to grab the Sword of Dracospirits, which was placed on the edge of the bed. His heart was still calm, and the energy agitated in the past did not bring any emotional fluctuations. Fearing that his movements would make the wound even worse, Magrence stepped forward to help him get out of bed. Since then, Honor had been staying in the village for a while. Unfortunately, Magrence’s meticulous care did not result in Honor’s affection but only gratefulness...

        One day, the children in the village came to Magrence, clamoring to hear the story of the dragon. Magrence asked the children to sit around her; the children looked at her intently. This scene reminded Honor of the interaction with Agatha in the prison...and those memories that did not belong to him. The picture in front of him overlapped with the thoughts in his mind, as if the Dragon Spiritors of the past were the children sitting next to Agatha , listening to her teaching...

        “Look, Sister Magrence! I grew a new tooth!”
        “Sister Magrence! Hug me!”
        “Me too! My turn, my turn!”
        “Okay, one by one.” The children fought for favor around Magrence, while she smiled to fulfill their requests one by one. The youngest child couldn’t compete with others, so he hugged Magrence’s leg directly.
        “Little Po needs Sister Magrence’s spoiling again!”
        “Little Po, you’re my favorite kid.”
        “What about me!” “And me!”
        “Alright alright, no arguing. I love you all…”

        It came to Honor’s mind that he might now understand what Agatha's complicated gaze meant when she first looked at him. At that time, Agatha saw not only him, but all the Dragon Spiritors in the past, each of whom had a unique relationship with her, but she ended up enduring the parting of the loved ones. The interaction between Magrence and the children seemed to reflect the relationship between Agatha and the Dragon Spiritors. Agatha loves them, and they all loved Agatha…

        “As for me…”

        After Honor recuperated, it was the day for him to say goodbye to Magrence and the villagers. He thanked her for taking good care of him all along. With a smile, Magrence bid farewell, but never had she understood that she brought the Dragon Spiritor not just the healing favor, but a deeper enlightenment. Honor spread his silver wings; the light of the holy flame waved along with it. Eventually, he disappeared into the sky like a meteor in front of the villagers.

        “Although I run away, I still can’t deny my feelings for her. The throbbing in my heart proves that she is the eternal light that illuminates me.”

STORY_2609:
In the Enochian Tower, Novalis was busy avoiding the falling rocks; Faugn’s voice wrestled with him. The surging dragon power burst from his body, drowning Novalis' thoughts, and the illusion of elements engulfed his irrational soul…

        Novalis witnessed his parents’ death in the demon’s assault. Since then the surviving Novalis became taciturn. The haze of trauma had been haunting him, until he was sent to his uncle’s house under a cold rainy night.  Sophie, Novalis’ cousin, led him to the fireplace; the warmth from the palm of his hand melted the darkness in Novalis’ heart.

        “Don’t worry. It’s fine. I’m holding your hand.”

        The flames flickering on the girl's gentle eyes made Novalis feel relieved, which slowly dissipated the fear in his heart. He liked this family. They were the only relatives he could rely on. Novalis just wanted to stay with them and led a peaceful life, but the good times were short. One day, they went to visit a monument exhibition. Novalis was invited by the wizards to be the envoy of the Primordial Dragons because he understood Faugn’s stele runes.

        “Life is the beginning of death, which terminates at destruction. Therefore, death is the end and the start——”

        “You’re talented! My son, you’ll become our envoy!”

        Novalis had been assisting his uncle's research, for he was literate in runes on the stele. Therefore, with new breakthroughs achieved in research, more and more people came to listen to his uncle's speech...including the mad wizards. The wizard took a fancy to his uncle's study and came to negotiate many times. Knowing that the visitors were unkind, Novalis hid behind the door with Sophie every time, staring hostilely from the crack of the door.

        “I will never give in my research! It’s our brainchild!”
        “Very well, I’ll make you do it.”
        “Ah——” The wizard did not hesitate to kill in order to obtain the research of the Primordial Dragons. He stretched out his hand to strangle uncle's neck. Sophie rushed over when she saw this, but got hit by witchcraft together. Purple smoke exploded from the room. The scene before him evoked the fear at the bottom of his heart, just like when his parents were killed back then…

        “Don’t! Don’t take everything away from me…”

        “Call upon the power of horror! Defeat him. Crush him. Rip him off!”

        The voice in his heart became the only guide. Novalis' eyes lit up; his lips chanted the stele runes spontaneously. Purple light started to surround him, and the summoned power was casted against the wizard. "This, this is the power of Faugn!" The wizard was knocked down. When Novalis got back his mind, he saw three bodies lying down in the broken home...

        The dying Sophie gently stroked Novalis' face. Novalis held her feeble hands tight. The temperature of the palms was slowly receding. Novalis stood silently by her side, until the fire in Sophie's pupils also went out. In the face of her death, there was a greater voice in his heart calling him other than fear…

        “Follow me. Reborn from horror! I’ll be waiting for you in the end.”

        “I have lost everything...what else can I get from death? What is waiting for me in the end?” Novalis thought blankly. “No, I understand. Death is not just death. The death of my parents in the past brought me to Sophie. At this moment, the death of Sophie and uncle will lead me to another beginning…”

        Novalis sensed Faugn's call from his strength. Now that he had nowhere to go after losing his close relatives, he had no choice but to embark on a journey to find Faugn. When he came to the foot of the mountains where  Ethereal Dragons were located, he saw someone familiar on the beach. The blue-haired maiden with a long horn turned her face. A pair of bright red eyes caught the hesitant heart of Novalis…

        “Even if I refused the power of the Primordial Dragons, losses and death are still inevitable. I resent everything related to the Ethereal Dragons. I just rather wipe it out!”

One of the navigators that appear in 《Mega Man X8》.

STORY_2615:

Axl is a teenager-like Reploid, but there is no official record about him.

STORY_2617:
First appearance in《Mega Man X5》. Alia was a researcher, she is a highly intelligent Reploid.

STORY_2618:

She is targeting to steal new information and technology. Joined X's group for saving Cinnamon from Dr. Psyche.
STORY_2619:
First showed up in Mega Man X: Command Mission A female robot with golden hair and in nurse outfit.

STORY_2620:
First Armor X made his debut in "Mega Man X" With pure white color, this armor was the first one X has ever had.

Although its performance isn't as good as the armors thereafter, it's no doubt a great progress to X at the time.
STORY_2621:
Second Armor is the second set of armor for Mega Man X. It first appeared in "Mega Man X2".

This armor not only can let X switch between left or right hand to fire two charge shots and deal huge damage, but also can turn received damage into energy.

When accumulating enough energy, Second Armor X can release all the energy to blast all enemies nearby.
STORY_2622:
First appearance in 《Mega Man X4》. Upgrade from the Fourth Armor, it's the one of most powerful armor that X can use.

Its powerful Nova Strike can be performed an unlimited number of times, and owns a wider attack range than the Fourth Armor.
STORY_2623:
First appearance in 《Mega Man X》. Vile was in Sigma's 17th Elite Unit, and he is very strong.

Because of a short circuit in his electronic brain, he is eager to destroy. Vile likes hunting in the missions, but finally he was defeated by X.
STORY_2625: Known as Vajurila FF, Bit is one of the members of the Nightmare Police, also a Reploid designed by Dr. Doppler with a focus on speed. Bit was responsible for protecting Dopple Town with his partner Mandarela BB. After Dr. Doppler’s uprising, he became the Maverick who commanded to join the Doppler’s forces.
STORY_2626: Being the classic antagonist in the Mega Man X series, he is the greatest creation by Dr. Cain and the best Reploid of the world in terms of brain or fighting power. STORY_2627:
A female Reploid in pink armor with avian wings,

Showing high team awareness and self-esteem, while sometimes it enjoys giving devastation to enemies caught in quicksand. After the death of teammates and Redips, it held the Force Metal and leapt off the space station to its death. Wielding an electromagnetic whip as weapon.
STORY_2628:
First appeared in "Mega Man X2", Black Zero was a replica produced by Sigma and defeated by the original Zero afterwards.

However Black Zero is not a fake in ROCKMAN X DiVE but came from another mode of X; that is, after Dr. Light released X's potential power, Black Zero was born...

Known as the Lord of the Snowy Plains, Chill Penguin was a Maverick Hunter from the 13th Polar Unit. After the news of Sigma’s uprising, he took down his own commander and joined Sigma’s forces.

STORY_2634:
“Come. No matter if it's good or bad, I’ll seal everything into the depth of the world.”

        Since the seal of the Mechanical City, Pompeii fell into a deep slumber with Monesis in the depth of underground. A long time passed. His consciousness sank in the dream, blending with the power of creation of Monesis and occasionally recalling his good old memories...

        Laughter of different races came one after another; everyone was immersed in Zana’s singing. Awakened by the music, the very first thing that caught Pompeii’s eyes was iridescence of vessels, with brilliant colors all over the earth. The feeling was like he had just had a nightmare but completely forgotten. Pompeii immediately got up and walked towards his fellows. Bahamut and Behemoth were waving, waiting for him to come to the center of the celebration.

        “Did my longing dream finally come true?”

        Suddenly, a crack appeared in the air between Pompeii and his fellows. Crack! It prolonged, followed by the sound of shattering glass. A dark breach was opened in the air.

        “Destroy...Follow your instinct…” The ominous purple aura overflowed from the breach, coiling around Pompeii. The terrifying voice reached deep into his consciousness. He knew that it was not Monesis, but the call of another sinister power!

        The surrounding scenery changed in response to the noise——Shamash the eldus attacked Pompeii's fellows with a magic blast. The sound of explosions and screams overwhelmed the music. Pompeii saw himself using a flame wall to protect the people, but Shamash went away...The injuries of his fellows once again appeared in front of him, and Pompeii could not help blaming himself.

        “Back then I chose giving in and redemption…”

        “It’s because you don’t understand...Plunder and destruction are the instincts of all beings…” A strange voice sounded again.

        “No, not like that! As long as we don’t give up the connection, we’ll understand each other one day!”

        A strong hatred surged from his heart, wrestling with his will of protection. Mush as Pompeii was unwilling to succumb to that power, the more he struggled, the more cracks appeared in front of him...In order to resist that trembling voice, he spontaneously casted the fire around. However, everything was unaffected. He could not intervene...nor could he drive away that voice.

        Phi’s beauty was distorted into an expression of consternation. Her kinetic core was pierced through by a purple blade. With an ear-piercing sound, the attack approached ferociously; a silhouette stood before him to take the strike, who was burnt to a crisp. White smoke rose from the scorched body with the scent of burnt metal, but that face was trampled in front of him…

        “Because you’re too kind...Your kind-heartedness will get everybody killed…” Schnauzer’s last words were like a curse haunting his mind.

        An uncontrollable rage shattered Pompeii’s kinetic core, tearing his body apart like razor-sharp claws. Sadness, self-blame and powerless emotions seemed to stab him like a knife. The sense of dominance began to erode him, constantly demanding and corrupting his will…

        “So it’s my fault isn’t it...I did this…” Pompeii stopped struggling with his eyes closed.

        The crackling sound spread to all directions...Finally, all the scenes shattered and collapsed, making a huge noise. Memories were scattered like glasses, turning into silver dust, eventually nothingness...

        Everything came to dead silence. In the boundless darkness, a pair of crimson eyes filled with desire for destruction opened...

STORY_2731:
It has been several years since the war with Gilgamesh ended. The war-torn capital city had also been reconstructed and fortified. The people enjoyed peaceful days happily along with the thriving country.

        Atrahasis seized this valuable time to study various knowledge. Even if he could not completely make up for the treasures recorded in the Tome of Fate washed away by water, he realized that the knowledge discovered by his own ability was easier to apply effectively.

        The fall came. Dumuzi was away for the time being. Therefore Atrahasis was entrusted to take up the acting role for the national affairs.

        It was the season of harvest. Atrahasis went out of the city to inspect the harvesting conditions of the farming. It was comforting to see that farmers have been able to make good use of the horse-shaped armor to greatly speed up the harvest and transportation.

        Although the horse-shaped armor was specially designed for war, with the wit it could also contribute to the welfare of civilians.

        Something suddenly flashed across Atrahasis’s mind. How about that double-stringed bow?

        After his meticulous transformation, the double-stringed bow was able to achieve a faster arrow speed. When combined with an elemental arrow, it could deal more powerful damage, which was considered to be an advantage on the battlefield.

        However, when it was at peace, could the bow be put into good use?

        The double-stringed bow was expensive and not small in size. It would be a pity if it was only kept in a warehouse worthlessly. However, you could not start a war just for the use of the weapon? Was there a way to find other uses?

        “Ahhh! It’s on fire!”

        Hearing the horrified cry, Atrahasis turned around and saw that a raging fire ignited over a nearby mountain. The flames seemed to burn even the sky; the smoke was so dense that it could even be smelt by him as far as on the walls of the city.

        The weather was dry. Given a lot of withered leaves and branches on the mountain, it only took a small spark to cause wildfires. Atrahasis has always reminded the people to be careful, try not to light up fire on the mountain, and the campfire must be completely put out before leaving. Nevertheless, it was still inevitable that some people might have caused this disaster accidentally.

        Atrahasis found it unsettling that the wildfire spread very quickly, immediately burning down to the bottom of the hill. At the foot, there were whole fields of farmland, a large number of crops being harvested, not to mention countless farmers.

        His first thought was to use elemental shields to transform the water element to put out the fire. The problem was that the number of shields was not enough, and it was too late to deliver before the fire reached the village.

        Unless with that thing, fast as wind, the water was able to be delivered in time…

        “Bring me the double-stringed bow and arrows!”

        After setting up the bow and enchanting the arrows with affluent water elements, Atrahasis ordered several strong men to tighten the bowstring together. With an order, the arrows were shot and they flew towards the fire at an astonishing speed. As water elements on the arrows spewed out, the flames were extinguished. The high-speed arrows also swept away the air in the fire area, the majority of which had been put out. Only a few flames remained.

        Relieved, Atrahasis commanded all the people to help fight the fire, and soon the intensity was quenched.

        Although this wildfire destroyed part of the forest and caused some sequelae due to the smoke and dust, the situation was not serious because it was extinguished in time, and the lives and properties of the farmers were not taken.

        Everyone praised the quick wit of Atrahasis with respect.

        For Atrahasis, the happiest thing was that his precious invention could find better uses other than killing. In addition, he also proved once again that learning and knowledge were indeed hidden everywhere. As long as you looked for it with your heart, you would eventually find it.
STORY_2732:
With a swing of the sickle, the sinister Imdugud was beheaded, with blood splashing all over his body.

        “Won...I won! I can bring the old man’s book back!” When Ninurta picked up the Tome of Fate and Imdugud’s head to leave, chirps of woe came into his ears.

        “These three fluffy...are the birdlings of Imdugud?” The birdlings snuggled together, crying for the death of their mother.

        “Well well, your mother was slaughtered by me, and no one will take care of you in the future. You three are going to starve to death for sure. Alright then, I’ll take you home. Hey! Stop pecking at me!” Back in the city, Ninurta began to nurse the young birds.

        “Come, it’s supper time. I’ve got you some fresh meat.”

        “Chirp!”

        “Why don't you eat? Why staring at me with that look? Oh, you mean you’re not gonna eat anything given by the murderer right? Okay, suit yourself. No one will avenge your mother if you starve to death. And I’m perfectly fine with that. Ha, never expected the children of Imdugud to be that useless. Hilarious, isn’t it?”

        “Chirp, Chirp, Chirp!”

        Oops! Now you want the food, don’t you? Then stop pecking at me and eat already!” The birdlings gulped their meat and grew up well. Their feathers gradually plumped. It was finally time to learn to fly.

        However, it somehow racked Ninurta’s brain.

        “Bloody hell, I’m not a bird after all. How can I possibly teach you? Forget it. I’ll jump from the city wall. You follow. Then you’ll learn how to fly at the verge of death!”

        Ninurta enlarged his body and jumped off the city wall easily, but the young birds were hesitating. “Hurry up to jump, or I’ll just call you all cowards,” he yelled.

        “Chirp, Chirp, Chirp!” The birds jumped down angrily, caught by Ninurta before they broke their necks. After a few tries…

        “Wonderful, you got it! It seems you’re not that stupid...Ah! Stop flying and pecking at me! That’s not fair!” The birds hovered over the town every day, flying down from time to time to steal food from Ninurta.

        “Hey, you thieves! Ouch! Peck and run!” Ninurta grumbled with a smile.

        Atrahasis came for him.

        “Ninurta, I helped you make this huge bird cage. Put them inside. They’ll feel comfy.”

        “Are you joking? They’re sacred birds! They should be free in the sky, but not in this cage.”

        “People have been threatened by the sacred bird before, and you killed it to save everyone. But now you’ve adopted three of them. How can you make the people feel at ease?”

        “Imdugud attacked people to protect its birdlings...Sigh, don't worry. I didn't intend to keep them forever.” Ninurta took the three to the mountain far from the town.

        “Go, you all can live on your own now. Birds are supposed to fly freely in the sky. No one can trap you in a cage. But do remember, if you attack humans, I’ll definitely chop your heads off, understand? Next time when we meet, we’re enemies!” The three sacred birds came over silently, pecked at Ninurta once and flew away.

        Ninurta gazed at the sky, until they were completely gone.

        So long. I wish you all the best, and I wish we would never see each other again.
STORY_2733:
As a patriarch, Dumuzi needed to handle endless business affairs every day. Originally, Inanna would be there to help, but after the birth of Mesopotamia, she could not accompany him as taking care of their daughter had already occupied her. Because of that, the couple had not spent time together for a long time.

        This day, Dumuzi was taking stock of the livestock, but suddenly heard a laugh. It turned out to be Atrahasis holding Mesopotamia in his hands and teasing her. The child had a good giggle, and Inanna next to him also chuckled happily.

        “They...look like a family…” Dumuzi was sad. “The one next to Inanna should have been me instead.”

        Therefore, he made up his mind.

        “No. I have to change this situation!”

        He walked to them.

        “Atrahasis, can you please help us to take care of Mesopotamia tomorrow? Inanna will be tied up.”

        “Huh? Did I forget something?” Inanna was surprised.

        “You and I will be going to boat by the river we loved when we were young!”

        Despite only a day, he wanted to go back to the happy time they spent in their teenage years. Then he would spend some time playing with his child.

        However, just when they were about to go out the next morning, a guard reported,  “Dumuzi, the barn caught fire!”

        “What? Inanna, wait for me by the river. I’ll be there soon.”

        “Alright!” Soon after, Dumuzi could finally meet her by the riverside.

        “Fortunately, the fire was not serious. Let's push the boat into the water.”

        Then, someone reported again. “Dumuzi, our caravan has gotten into a fight with the people from the western tribe. Please help!”

        “Sigh...pardon me, Inanna. I’ll be back soon.”

        “Take your time.” Inanna smiled to see him out. Then she sat down and began to squeeze the soil with water.

        By the time Dumuzi returned, the sky had already become dark.

        “Sorry, the patriarch of the western tribe insisted on holding me to talk about the deal for the next year…”

        “Never mind. Let’s go back.” Inanna shook her head with a smile.

        Dumuzi felt upset that it was a rare opportunity to be with Inanna, but he messed up.

        At night, when Mesopotamia was asleep, Inanna woke Dumuzi up silently.

        “Come with me. Don’t worry. The child won't wake up until morning.” The two came back to the riverside.

        “What are we going to do here? It’s too dark to boat.”

        “Of course we can.” Inanna took out two small boats she made of mud from the grass during the day. “See?”

        “Haha, indeed.”

        Putting the boats into the river under the moonlight, they watched them drift away side by side.

        “I remember. When we were young, we used to race on the riverside with small boats.”

        “Yes, I still remember that you’d let me win the match intentionally,” Inanna smiled.  

        Inanna leaned on his shoulder. Her gentle voice was sentimental, “Dumuzi, although you’re very busy and exhausted, and you don’t have much time to spend on me, I’m happy as long as we’re together.”

        Dumuzi then held Inanna’s hands tight.

        “So am I.”

        Under the silver moonlight, their hearts were tied together again.
STORY_2734:
While Inanna was walking home with the sleeping Mesopotamia on her back, she saw a young man and a lady in front of her, talking and laughing.

        “Ah, so sweet, just like me and Dumuzi back in the days.” She recalled the time when she and Dumuzi studied together with Teacher Anu. At that time, the two were just like this, walking and laughing, sometimes chasing each other, like a pair of innocent, naughty children.

        “We can’t do that now.”

        Since they became the King and the Queen, they had been bearing the safety and happiness of the entire tribe, not to mention the responsibility of raising a child. These were all heavy burdens. Therefore, they could no longer be carefree like before.

        “Sigh, why bother to think of it?” Inanna shook her head. “I said clearly. No matter how hard it is, I’m happy as long as Dumuzi and I are together.”

        “Ahhh! A mouse!” The lady ahead screamed, hiding into the young man’s arms. “It’s scary!”

        “It’s ok. The mouse is gone.” The young man wiped away her tears while patting her head. “You really love to act like a baby, don’t you? But this is also the cutest part of you.”

        “She makes me envious…” Inanna heaved a sigh. “I wanna do that to Dumuzi too.”

        She made up her mind.

        “Anyways a feminine play won’t give the King any trouble. Let me try!”

        Next day, Inanna and Dumuzi went to inspect the farmland together. They were discussing the harvest conditions on the way. All of a sudden, Inanna screamed. “M-mouse!”

        Dumuzi found it baffling because she was never scared by a mouse. Plus, her cry did not sound like she was frightened at all.

        “Oh, I saw it too. So?” Then he figured. “Ah, are you worrying that the mouse will eat the crop? That’s truly a seriou issue. Well done.”

        “Em...right.”

        Despite the embarrassment, Inanna did not feel discouraged at all. She decided to try again.

        Walking to another section——

        “Dumuzi, s-snake!” Inanna did her best to fake a scream of terror, but failed again.

        “Well, then the snake can eat the mouse. Problem solved.”

        “AH! Leave me alone!” She strode forward in anger.

        “Humph, anyway, I’m too old to act cutesy now. It’s just a waste of time!” Inanna grumbled bitterly, unaware of Dumuzi who came behind to hug her up.

        “Wh-what are you doing?”

        Dumuzi whispered gently with a smile. “Just want to say you’re adorable.”

        “You——put me down already!” A blush came into her cheeks.

        “No.” 

        “Dumuzi is such an idiot!”

        “You look pretty cute too even when you’re angry though.”

        Dumuzi stretched out his hand to stroke Inanna's face and looked at her affectionately. Unable to resist the indulgence in love, Inanna could not help waiting for a kiss on the lips...
STORY_2735:
“Surely fate is impossible to grasp, let alone understand it.”

        Having been through plagues and wars, Namtar finally had a chance to read the Tome of Fate after so many hardships. However, it was washed away by the flood. For some reason, he was not disappointed.

        “I’m destined not to read that book. What's so regrettable?” Namtar left the town of humans and returned to the swamp where he lived. He continued to study various herbs and poisonous weeds, in order to compile his knowledge into a book.

        This day, he climbed up a cliff to pluck a rare poisonous herb growing on the top, only to see a hole. Inside which there was a book.

        “Tome of Fate? Could it be fate that led me here?” Just as Namtar was about to stretch out his hand, a venomous snake suddenly sprang out from the depths of the hole, spouting viciously and threateningly at him. Caught off guard, he slipped and fell, breaking several bones.

        “So it’s a snake’s lair over there, but it’s  impossible for the flood to rush the Tome of Fate to such a high place. It should be some animals that carried the book into this snake hole. Anyone who takes it will either be bitten or fall to death. It must be fate. Fate wants me to stay away from the Tome of Fate right? Very well, then I won’t bother anymore.” Namtar endured the pain and went home to recuperate. However in the next few days, there were a lot of stray thoughts in his head, which made him unable to concentrate on doing anything or to sleep.

        “Fate wants it to stay in the lair, right?”

        “But that day I was planning to go to other places to collect herbal medicine. Only when I saw the poisonous herb on the cliff, I found the Tome of Fate by coincidence. This must be the arrangement of fate, which allows me to discover the book. In this case, it means fate wants me to retrieve the Tome of Fate.”

        “No, perhaps fate is trying to tell me to give up. Otherwise, the book wouldn’t be placed in such an inconvenient location.”

        “But...As long as I’m more cautious, there should still be a way to deal with that venomous snake. If I don’t take action, it might go against the will of fate.” The more Namtar thought about it, the more he got confused.

        “Oh fate, I’ve been following you wholeheartedly. If you don't give me a guide, how am I supposed to go on?”

        “The teacher said that I won’t understand my destiny, maybe that’s what this means right? The guidance of fate is confusing and difficult to interpret.” After days of bewilderment, Namtar, gazing at the rising sun, had made a decision.

        “I’m going to try. Whether I can get it or not, whether I’ll die or not, it’s all on fate.” He collected several kinds of poisonous herbs, dried them to make incense and lit them at the bottom of the cliff. The dense smoke drifted into the snake’s lair, forcing the snakes to flee unbearably.

        “I did it! Fate really wants me to get the Tome of Fate!” Namtar finally had the book. However, the writing on it was soaked in water and became completely unreadable.

        “Of course, this is the arrangement of fate. Accidents happen no matter how hard you try.” Although it was in vain, Namtar still remained calm. If it wasn’t for this wasted effort, he would never understand what fate had to tell him.

        “If nothing is done, nothing will happen and nothing will be learned. Do as best as we can, obey the fate. This is what fate is about.”
STORY_2739:
Lining up on both sides of the hall, the ministers welcomed the emissary of the neighboring country and his team, who came in with livestock and valuable gifts. On the litter in the middle sat a woman. A sheet of scrim draped over the litter, covering her figure.

        The leading emissary opened the treasure box in his hand and handed it to King Dumuzi, said, “This is a gift from our princess for making a proposal of marriage to the prince. ”

        “A marriage proposal?” Dumuzi was seemingly calm, yet he caught sight of Inanna who was standing beside and looking at him worriedly.

        “It’s time for our prince to settle down!”
        “Marrying the princess must benefit diplomatic relations between us and the neighboring country! ”
        “This is great news for both countries! We have to celebrate it!”

        After helping the envoys settle down, Dumuzi ended the morning court to have a private meeting. There were only Inanna, Mesopotamia and him in the room. 
　　
        Fondling her daughter’s cheek pitifully, Inanna said with worries, “We can’t hide it after all, can’t we?”

        “If we turn it down, it might hinder the diplomatic relations between two countries; but if we accept it, everything will be exposed,” said Dumuzi with a frown.

        Mesopotamia put her hand over her mother’s and said, “Mother, I’ll do whatever it takes to keep the country’s peace. But I can’t let other people’s daughter down so I have to turn down this marriage proposal.”

        “Meso… You always want the best for others.” Inanna gently caressed her daughter’s long hair with her fingers.

        “Father, let me handle it. I’ll talk to the princess myself.”

        Mesopotamia walked into the side hall where the princess was received. As soon as she closed the door she saw the princess come to her, trying to hug her. The tulle on the princess’s sleeves brushed past 

        Mesopotamia’s face with a hint of seduction. She immediately kept her balance and broke the fall. Then she subconsciously pushed the princess away.

        “Princess, please respect your…!” Before Mesopotamia could ever finish her sentence, she met the beautiful eyes of the princess, then she knew what was happening and asked,
“Chessia, what are you doing?”

        A bright flame appeared and burned down the tulle dress, revealing the true face of Chessia. Raising her eyebrow, she said, “I just wanted to know if you like your fiancée or not. Just by you pushing ‘her’ away, I’m happy with the answer.”

        “Stop messing around. Where’s the princess?”

        “Oh, why do you sound like you’re blaming me? I found her big secret when I broke in but I helped her instead. Come on in.” Chessia led Mesopotamia into a room in the side hall, in which she saw the real princess and a male guard.

        The princess got wound up as she caught sight of Mesopotamia. Chessia smiled at her and said, “Don’t worry. I believe the prince will help you.”

        It turned out that the king of the neighboring country brought the marriage proposal without asking the princess just to establish diplomatic relations. Yet, the princess already met the love of her life and even planned to elope on their way back to the kingdom if the prince accepted the proposal. She only loosened up a little bit after knowing that Mesopotamia had no intent to marry her.

        “But what about diplomatic relations? My father won’t just let it go.”

        “I have an idea. Princess, just leave it to me,” said Mesopotamia, sharing a mutual gaze with Chessia as if they knew each other’s minds.

        Chessia blinked and said, “You have to think twice, my prince.”

        On the wedding day, the sun blazed down on the golden bowls and silver plates on the feast table, reflecting bright golden light. The ministers and envoys toasted and sang along with the music for celebration.

        The suited Mesopotamia held the princess’s hand. In the sound of horns and cheers, together they walked up to the end of the staircase.

        As the two of them toasted, the princess pouted her lips, leaned forward on tiptoes, and looked at Mesopotamia flirtatiously. A tiny frown crossed Mesopotamia’s solemn face but it soon turned into a decent smile when she turned to greet the guests.

        “Cheers for the prince and princess!”

        At night, after they returned to their room, the princess threw herself on the bed and said, “Sigh, being a princess is really troublesome. This gown is so tight!” The princess took off the floral jewelry, stretched a little, and looked at Mesopotamia, who had walked to the window.

        “Now, the princess should be somewhere safe...”

        Mesopotamia was watching the scenery of trees and woods outside the window, which seemed more tranquil under the night sky. Suddenly a piece of white tulle covered her sight-a bridal veil was put on her head.

        Warmth came from the back of Mesopotamia’s neck and a sly whisper rang in her ears, “Do you know why I told you to think twice? Now you can’t get rid of me for your whole life.”

        The “princess” returned to her original appearance as Chessia. She gently lifted the veil and looked at Mesopotamia’s pondering face.

        Mesopotamia removed the veil and said, “You weren’t going to leave me anyway.”

        “Humph, then I’ll disappear at the state banquets, official duties and special ceremonies, when you most need the princess’s accompany—— ”

        “Inseparable, that’s good enough.” Mesopotamia reached and grabbed Chessia’s arm.

        Blushed crimson in a second, Chessia gave a coquettish gaze and said, “then, my prince, we shall be together forever, till eternity. ”
STORY_2740:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.1

        'This kind of soulless bladesmithing is the greatest insult to bladesmiths. Darn it, this black magic. I must crush it!' Galahad shouted furiously.

        Tilting his head, Galahad’s father gave her a cold gaze that sent a strange feeling to her. He dropped the smith hammer and took the claymore aside instead. With his face preoccupied and distorted by some kind of madness, he roared wildly, 'You don’t understand. This suit of dark metal armor is the best of a bladesmith! Galahad, if you’re not on the same page with me then show me if your heart as a bladesmith is stronger than mine!'

        'Forge every sword with all your heart. This is what you’ve taught me since I was small. So I’m gonna beat you with this faith and wake you up!' Galahad raised her hammer as she confronted her father.

        Under the fiery sparks, the father and daughter waited in bated breath. Suddenly, the father strode forward and swung his sword! Galahad struggled to defend yet the sheer force almost knocked the hammer out of her hands.

        Seeing his daughter’s discomfiture, the father showed no mercy with attacks that got even more vicious. Galahad was forced to retreat and felt the growing heat behind her back. The flames painted her father’s ferocious face red ——Her father forced her to the forge and there was no way out!

        'Is that all you got? Then you can never surpass me,' said the father with rage as if he didn’t realize that he was driving his daughter towards the forge fire. Madness was the only thing left in his eyes.

        As she looked at her father, Galahad’s eyes brimmed with tears. Struggling under her father’s pushes, she murmured with shivers, 'Father has always been my idol… The swords that father made with all his heart are the strongest… You’re the one that I thought I could never surpass... '

        A sign of wavering flashed across the father’s eyes.

        Galahad grasped the chance and immediately pushed her father back. Then she said with a firm tone, 'Because… I’ve seen my father's passion for bladesmithing! He takes pride in forging and will never succumb to dark metal… The father I used to know will never do such things! '

        'Come back, father! Retrieve your heart as a bladesmith!' shouted Galahad, as she swung her hammer and aimed for the weakness of his sword! 

        Clink! The sword and hammer made a clattering sound as they met——the sword cracked!

        'How could that be...' Looking at the broken pieces on the ground, Galahad’s father was flabbergasted.


        “I can’t compare to my father in terms of strength but I know better about my father's work than anyone else, including its weakness!” Staring at her father’s dark metal armor, Galahad locked her eye on a point and  flung her hammer at it.

        The armor smashed into pieces and fell onto the ground with a click. As Galahad put down her arms pantingly, she looked at her father who was brought to his knees.

        The madness in his eyes was gone and they regained their tenderness as in the old days. Galahad dropped her giant hammer, ran to her father and hugged him like a little girl, saying, 'You… you’re back… Father, I miss you so much!' 

        Holding each other, the father and the daughter burst into tears until a figure came——Merlin patted Galahad on her shoulders and said, 'I’m glad you’re both safe! Since Morgan le Fay had fled, let’s go and look for the clues for the Vile Core! '

        Yet, Galahad’s father said with a grim expression, 'It’s too late… The Vile Core  is in the hand of Mordred.'
STORY_2741:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.3

        To overthrow Mordred, save Guinevere and find the last Star Stone, Gawain and his friends sneaked into the palace and split into three teams.

        Following Tristan's lead, they went smoothly with only a few guards patrolling along the way and came to a wide unmanned corridor. Suddenly, Gawain felt a chill down his spine so he immediately defended with his sword!

        That brute strength with a presence of black magic-it was Lancelot.

        'Tristan! Go!' Gawain flung Lancelot off forcefully.

        'But… You take care of yourself!' Said Tristan, who ran right away and disappeared at the end of the spiral staircase.

        'Kill… Kill the intruders.' said Lancelot with a hoarse and deep voice. He raised his sword and fiercely slashed with murderous eyes and the looming purple airstream of black magic.

        Gawain blocked the attack, wielding his sword with a reverse grip. Lancelot drew his sword and attacked again. For a while, the clink of metal knocking together continued to ring. Compared to Lancelot who had no scruples, Gawain was rather unaggressive with his attack which placed him at a disadvantage. Flesh wounds on his body gradually increased.

        Boom! A resonant sound came from underground.

        'It is an explosion caused by a magic collision… Was it Merlin?' While Gawain was pondering,  Lancelot knelt on the ground as if he was racked with pain as the purple airstream on him somehow became thinner.

        'Um… Gawain…' Lancelot let out a faint murmur.

        'Lancelot! You’re awake!' Surprised, Gawain stepped forward and was about to help Lancelot up. Yet, a strong gust of purple airstream came in his way. Not only did it enfold Lancelot, it even got into his body arbitrarily.

        'Argh! Stop… Stop controlling… Arrgh——!' Lancelot uttered an anguished cry. Yet, soon he stopped and got up, standing like a lifeless doll.

        'Lancelot!' shouted Gawain. Meanwhile, part of the purple airstream turned into an exquisite figure——a beautiful woman, who seemed to be badly injured as her gorgeous face was pale with blood stains that had not yet been wiped off the corner of her mouth.

        'Morgan le Fay! What did you do to Lancelot?!' Recognizing her immediately, Gawain asked her with mounting anger.

        'I came to take my pawn back so that I can kill that detestable sorcerer!' Losing her usual poise, Morgan le Fay champed with rage and said, 'How dare she disguised as my son to sap me! Unforgivable!'

        'The sorcerer that disguised as her son… is properly Merlin… Morgan le Fay must have been seriously damaged by Merlin and her power weakened, which gave Lancelot a chance to break free… I must seize this opportunity!'

        'Lancelot! Wake up!'

        'It’s useless. Even though my power is weakened, it’s still enough for me to control him. Go, go kill that cumbersome guy!' Morgan le Fay flashed a bewitching smile.

        'Ki-... Kill…' With his eyes brimmed with menace, Lancelot drew his sword and lashed madly against Gawain. Blocking the attack, Gawain yelled hysterically, 'You just let her control you that easily? Why did you seek power in the first place?! Don’t you remember what King Uther had taught us?!' 

        '...King Uther… No… Hmm...' Lancelot paused for a second, but he soon returned to his wooden expression and said, 'Kill the cumbersome guy.'

        'Ha, he can’t get rid of my restraint. Give up. He belongs to the dark, just like me.' Morgan le Fay gave a scornful laughter softly, 'Enough for playing. Finish him.'

        Following Morgan le Fay’s words, Lancelot let out a low growl with a ferocious hint of menace and launched attacks that were even more fierce than before, which became hard to ward off for the wounded Gawain.
