        Gawain kept stepping back until he hit the stone pillar behind him. Just as Lancelot raised his sword and was about to thrust it into Gawain’s left chest, a reflection of light fell into his eyes——it was the battle steed badge of Juvenile Knights, a token given by King Uther.

        The sunlight reflecting off the badge stung Lancelot and recalled the memory buried deep inside him—— That person whom he saw as his second parent and the blonde girl who inherited these clear blue eyes. Together they shone a light that could dispel all darkness.，

        'King Uther, Arthur…' As Lancelot’s pupils contracted, his hand drew back——

        Slash! Blood dribbled down from the blade to the hilt and stained Lancelot’s hand with crimson. Looking at Lancelot in shock, Gawain slowly slid down and fell to the ground, motionless.

        'You’re certainly a former Juvenile Knight. Now I can teach that sorcerer...a lesson——argh…' Morgan le Fay looked at the blade that pierced through her abdomen unbelievably. She tilted her face and looked at Lancelot, who was holding the sword behind her, and asked, 'How did… you break my control...'

        'Because I have something more powerful in my heart.' Lancelot retracted his sword. Losing her support, Morgan le Fay fell with blood spreading on the ground.

        'Finally you’re back.' Gawain stood up and looked at Lancelot’s bleeding right hand. 'Are you alright?'

        'Humph. A little pain couldn’t have awoken me.' said Lancelot, tearing the cloth on the hem to wrap the wound on his right palm. A moment ago, Lancelot pretended to attack Gawain and stabbed himself to gain back sanity instead.

        'What’s the deal now?' asked Lancelot.  As Gawain told him their plan, Lancelot thought for a while and said, 'now we only need the Excalibur back.'

        'Yeah, I’m afraid it is already in Mordred’s hand.'

        'Then let’s go and take it back.'

        'No. You go take it back.' Gawain’s words drew Lancelot’s gaze. But soon he knew what the former meant——a swamp of dark-metal-armored soldiers appeared on the other end of the corridor.

        'You alone——'

        'Who do you think I am?' Raising a confident smile, Gawain held his sword upright. Sunlight reflecting on the blade cast a brilliant halo. 'I’m the Knight Commander chosen by King Uther himself.'

        Lancelot looked at Gawain with his eyes full of joy. As he gave Gawain a few slaps of trust on his shoulder, he left...
STORY_2742:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.2

        Aria, the follower of the holy grail, gave Merlin two Star Stones. Unexpectedly, Mordred had already laid in ambush with his army for them. In the end, Lancelot was brainwashed and Arthur was seriously injured while Guinevere disguised herself as Arthur with the help of Merlin’s magic and surrendered herself to Mordred so as to help the others defuse the crisis.

        Tristan and his companions survived. After they consolidated, they decided to sneak into the palace to stop Mordred’s evil deeds. They tiptoed into the palace while Arthur was recuperating and split into three teams for operation.

        Merlin and Galahad were responsible for finding the source of dark metal and destroying it. Soon they came to the underground smithy and found Galahad’s father who was controlled by dark metal. Yet, Morgan le Fay intervened in their rescue. Merlin stepped forward to hold Morgan le Fay back so that Galahad could go and find her father.

        'Humph, you think you little rat can stop me?' Purple airstream rose from Morgan le Fay’s hand and formed into clones, ringing Merlin. As they drew small circles with their fingers, the purple airstream on their fingertips converged into daggers and darted towards Merlin!

        'Argh!' Merlin unfolded elements to defend but the attack was too intensive that her arms and legs were cut. Blood splattered.

        'How dare you rats try to sabotage my son’s plan. Unforgivable! I have to teach you a lesson!' Morgan le Fay flashed an enthralling smile.

        “There are so many clones. How can I even deal with them? That’s unfair!” Blocking the attacks, Merlin kept stepping back. Only until she hit the stone wall behind her did she realize she had been cornered in the smithy.

        'Tut-tut, is this the end——'

        “No, there’s still a way…” A wispy voice broke into Merlin’s mind. She recognized the voice immediately and called out a name in astonishment, “the follower of the holy grail… Aria.”

        “Yes, it’s me. Everyone has his or her weakness, including Morgan le Fay...”

        “Weakness...” Recalling what Morgan le Fay had just said, Merlin quivered and soon cracked a sly smile. As she raised her wand and conjured magic power, a blinding light draped over her, making her figure unclear for a moment.

        'Still trying to fight? It’s useless——' As Morgan le Fay raised her hand, all the clones conjured magic and aimed at Merlin. When they were just about to attack, a slender figure stepped out of the light.

        'Mother, are you really gonna kill me?' Merlin questioned Morgan le Fay with the appearance of Mordred.

        'My son… Mordred… No!' Merlin’s move shook Morgan le Fay successfully. All the attacks of the clones missed and scattered around Merlin, who certainly seized the moment. As she dispelled the illusion, she conjured power and threw an energy sphere at the true Morgan le Fay.

         Morgan le Fay retracted her clones at the very last minute and changed the power into an elemental shield to resist Merlin’s attacks. Unfortunately, she wasn’t able to resist them all that she staggered back as she got hit. 

        'Urg——! You—— how dare you use such a despicable trick!' Morgan le Fay glared at Merlin with grinding teeth.

        'Humph! It’s nothing despicable! Are you saying that only your son is precious and the others are just worthless?!' Merlin glowered back at her with no signs of fear, 'Do you have any idea of how many families were broken because of you and your precious little boy!? You are such a thick skin to call me despicable!'

        'Every great thing comes with sacrifices. They should be honored that they could help my son! '

        'You——unreasonable!' Merlin was choked with rage. She raised her wand again and conjured magic power again. A blazing golden light flew towards Morgan le Fay.

        'Humph!' Morgan le Fay resisted with her power. A gust of ominous purple air billowed and attacked the golden light——

        Two magic powers collided! Instantly, a dazzling light burst out with mountainous shock waves. The purple air got the upper hand within a short while and kept swallowing the golden light.

        'Darn it! I will not succumb!' Putting up with the pain and pressure, Merlin struggled to hold her body straight. Suddenly, a refreshing breath of water floated in and wrapped Merlin, alleviating her physical pain.

        “The staunch sorcerer… Let me help you…”

        'Tut! The follower of the holy grail, how dare you get in my way!' Morgan le Fay lost her usual poise and her enchanting face was distorted.

        'Get lost!' Merlin shouted lowly as she forced out all the magic power in her body, releasing a dawning light that covered the entire smithy.

        'Cough… I will get you for this next time...' Morgan le Fay, who had consumed a lot of magic power, lay on the ground, panting. With her remaining magic power, she cast a spell, turned herself into a purple mist and fled.

        Merlin couldn’t chase after her. Yet, behind her came the voices of Galahad and her father...
STORY_2743:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.4

        After Lancelot accidentally injured Arthur under Morgan le Fay’s control, he followed Morgan le Fay back to the palace. As Gawain sneaked into the palace with his crew to steal the Star Stone, he met Lancelot on his way. He awakened Lancelot’s will during the fight that helped the latter get rid of Morgan le Fay’s manipulation.

        Gawain and Lancelot wanted to retrieve the Excalibur yet they were chased by battalions of soldiers armed with dark metal. Gawain stayed behind so that Lancelot could break through. Without further hesitation, Lancelot ran to the palace’s interior.

        “Where the hell did Mordred go?” Clueless, Lancelot could only walk from room to room. Suddenly, a searing heat arose in front of his chest, as if it sensed his trouble. He took out the thing in his pocket-it was the Star Stone. Arthur entrusted one of the Star Stones to Lancelot. He had kept it in an inside pocket of his clothes since then. Luckily, Morgan le Fay did not find out.

        “The Star Stone is glowing… Tristan must have gotten the other Star Stone and awakened it. King Uther once said the awakened Star Stones will be drawn to the Excalibur for return… Let me give it a try.”

        Lancelot moved while observing the Star Stone. Its radiance changed as expected. So he followed the Star Stone’s guidance and soon arrived at the palace hall.

        “The Excalibur is right inside...” Lancelot pushed the gate open and saw Mordred sitting proudly on the throne on the top of the stairway in the hall. As the Mordred caught sight of Lancelot, he frowned, 'You’re awakened. What happened to Mother? How could she let a pawn get out of her control? '

        'She died.' Lancelot thought his words could waver Mordred but, contrary to his expectation, Mordred simply pursed his lips and said with a hint of disgust on his face, 'She’s too weak. Not only she couldn’t keep her pawn under control, she even got killed by it.'
　　
        'Are you still a human?! Your mother died helping you! Not only you don’t feel sorry about it, now you’re despising her for her vulnerability!?'

        'Is humanity helpful for a king?' Mordred said indifferently, 'I’m the destined king and I shall eradicate whoever interferes with my kingship.'

        'You don’t deserve to touch the Excalibur! Give it back!' Lancelot roared in anger.

        'Humph. What an overweening guy. I’ll let you know how inferior you are.' As Mordred drew another long sword from his waist, he strode down from the throne and slashed at Lancelot fiercely.

        Every move of Mordred was in absolute precision, neat and decisive. His sword was strong and skilled. On the contrary,         Lancelot with an injured right hand was rather ragged that every defense he made seemed like an impending crisis.

        As time went by, the scratches on Lancelot’s body increased with blood oozing from the wounds, leaving crimson bloodstains on the floor.

        Seeing that, Mordred began to gloat. For the young man’s inflating vanity, he couldn’t help but bawled, 'The strongest knight of the Juvenile Knights is nothing but crap.'

        Ridiculed, yet, Lancelot was not angry. Instead, he flashed a smile and stabbed Mordred noiselessly. Mordred took a step but he accidentally slipped then a stab of pain shot through his shoulder that weakened him and caused him to kneel on the floor.

        Lancelot walked towards Mordred and stopped in front of him, looking down on his opponent. With all the wounds and scratches all over his body, still, his spirit was unyielding.

        'As I thought, jeune monsieur.'

        'Did you take the attacks and leave the trails of blood on purpose?!' Mordred champed with rage.

        'Yeah. You’re strong but you can’t withstand the test of storms. You are strong only when you’re in a predictable place and favorable conditions. It only takes one accident to break you down because you’re just a little bird kept in a golden cage——'

        'NO! I’m born to be a King!' Mordred said hideously, 'You despicable bastard. Don’t you look down on me… No one can look down on me!'

        Mordred took out a purple round stone and shoved it into his wound. Then a sheet of black flame burst out! As the purple light rotated around his body, his wound was healed immediately and his bones and muscles grew and changed. With his eyes full of greed, he murmured, 'I… am a king…I’m born a king...'

        'You… are really crazy!'

        Looking up at the taller and black-magic-distorted monster that could barely call a human, Lancelot turned around and ran to the exit hastily.

        Instead of chasing after Lancelot, the monstrous Mordred blocked Lancelot’s way easily with just one leap and grabbed him with one hand. Mordred’s immense strength almost suffocated Lancelet.

        “Arthur… I’m sorry but it seems like I can’t see you again...”
Lancelot thought regrettably as his consciousness slowly became fuzzy...
STORY_2744:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.6

        Following Tristan’s lead, Arthur and her friends found the temple where the holy grail was but they were blocked by the enchantment. Luckily, Merlin solved the problem and was given two Star Stones from the follower of the holy grail. 

        However, luck doesn’t always turn around. They were caught in the ambush of Mordred’s army. In the end, Lancelot was brainwashed and Arthur was seriously injured. To help the others defuse the crisis, Guinevere disguised herself as Arthur with the help of Merlin’s magic and surrendered herself to Mordred.

        Tristan and his companions survived. After they consolidated, they decided to sneak into the palace to stop Mordred’s evil deeds. Gawain and Tristan were responsible for finding the last Star Stone in the palace yet they encountered Lancelot, who was controlled by black magic, half the way. Gawain stayed and fought against Lancelot to make a way for Tristan.

        Tristan walked along the spiral staircase to the upper floor and found a difference between the map and the actual hallway-it was much narrower than the one downstairs. He observed and puzzled out that, ‘there must be a hidden space! Be it a secret tunnel or a secret room, there must be a trace of it!’ 

        Tristan immediately groped around the stone wall. Eventually, he found a switch and opened the hidden door, in which he saw a cavernous hall with pennants hanging on both sides. Next to the stone pillars stood a row of bookshelves and armor with portraits hanging on the wall. Under the stained glass in front of him, there was a round table on which laid a Star Stone.

        “It’s the Star Stone! I have to take it to Gawain as soon as possible!”

        Tristan ran towards the round table. On his way, suddenly, a magic circle appeared at the tip of his foot. A misty purple stream seeped out of the circle and ran through the hall. Then a disturbing metal grinding noise came from all corners. Tristan felt an inexplicable chill down his spine and instinctively stepped back.

        Crack! Flashes of sharp blades came and thrust into the spot where Tristan just stood!

        “It’s a trap. It attacks once I step into the magic zone… Darn it! I’m so close… I can’t just give up!”

        Suppressing his worries, Tristan looked around the hall calmly. The rapidly moving eyes eventually landed on a standing bookshelf. A thought crossed his mind. Then he ran over, got all the books off the shelf and cautiously pushed the shelf towards the direction where he just walked to.

        The magic circle engraved on the ground was activated again with the terrifying metal sound. Leaning against the shelf, Tristan moved with his eyes shut——Crack! The blades came again yet landed on the shelf this time.

        “I did it! I knew the trap was fixed! As long as I know the trap spot, I can break through it with the barrier made with the things in this hall!”

        Clenching his fists, Tristan no longer hesitated and tested the trap spots one by one speedily. Soon he made a small intricate maze by moving the bookshelves, sofa and armor.

        ‘I-I’ve made it…’ Tristan scratched the cloth on his chest nervously. He had been only studying the maps made by others in depth for the past years but now he was creating a word of his own.

        He took a deep breath and made a start. As the magic circle was activated again, various sounds traveled through the hall with different sharp weapons darting from each direction, which were all stopped by the tortuous maze. Under the protection of the maze, Tristan managed to get to the round table and hold up the Star Stone.

        Before Tristan could unwind his excitement, a deafening boom from the outside wavered his heart again.

        “That’s from the main castle! I have to hurry and take the Star Stone to Gawain!”

        Tristan bagged up the Star Stone and hastily left the room. The moment he stepped out of the room, a dark metal armored soldier came. Just as the soldier was about to wield his sword and gash Tristan, a figure rushed over and shoved the soldier away with a shield.

        ‘Tristan, are you alright?’ A familiar male voice let Tristan’s guard down. As he opened his eyes and looked, he let out a scream in surprise, ‘Lamorak!’

        ‘I just saw Bedivere and Arthur riding a lion to the palace hall. Something must have happened with that boom. Let’s hurry!’

        ‘Ok!’ Without further ado, Tristan followed Lamorak and ran towards the palace hall. Gripping the Star Stone above his chest with his right hand, he silently prayed in his heart.

         “Arthur! Don’t die before I give you the Star Stone!”
STORY_2745:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.5

        In the dungeon of the castle, Guinevere sat quietly in a corner, looking at the transom on the ceiling with her eyes filled with worries.

        'I wonder if Arthur and the others have escaped safely...'

        Bam! Bam! Two sounds of hard objects hitting the group came from the cell door, then brisk footsteps came closer-a man with a mushroom haircut came to Guinevere’s cell door, with the key chain spinning on his index finger. Smiling arrogantly, he said, 'Ha, the guards of the palace are no big deal.'

        'Gareth!' Guinevere let out a quiet scream, surprised.
        'We’ve come to your rescue.' Gareth tilted his chin triumphantly.

        Earlier, Gareth, Arthur and their friends were encircled by Mordred’s army at the temple.  In the end, Lancelot was brainwashed and Arthur was seriously injured while Guinevere disguised herself as Arthur with the help of Merlin’s magic and surrendered herself to Mordred so as to help the others defuse the crisis.

        Gareth and his companions survived. After they consolidated, they decided to sneak into the palace to stop Mordred’s evil deeds. Gareth was the one responsible for going to the dungeon to save the captured Guinevere.

        'How did you get in here? There are a lot of guards outside,' asked Guinevere.

        'Humph, how could those morons resist my hypnosis. Enough with that. Let me open the door and get you out of there.'

        Just as Gareth’s hand touched the cell, an ominous purple light flashed. He stepped back in fright and yelled in confusion, 'Wh- what happened?'

        'I can feel that the light just now contains magic power. Maybe you just triggered some kind of magic...'  After thinking for a while, Guinevere gave a start and yelled at Gareth nervously, 'they anticipated that you would come to save me, so they enchanted the cell with magic. I'm afraid the soldiers will be here soon. Run away now!'

         'No, we’re so close! How can I go by myself!' Gareth gritted his teeth, picked up the key and tried to unlock it. 'No, this isn’t it either! How come there are so many keys! I don’t think they have this many cells here.'

        He tried every key-'Why are they all wrong! Wait, could it be a trap in the first place!?'

        It was a pity that Gareth realized it too late. Meanwhile, footsteps came from outside the dungeon.
        'Leave me here. You just go! They’re coming! You can’t defeat them!'

        'No! I won’t leave you here alone, not even if I can’t beat them.' Gareth grabbed the long sword at a corner and stiffly held it in front of his chest.

        Just then, two soldiers wearing dark metal came. They raised their swords and slashed at Gareth mercilessly.

        'Noooo——! Don-don’t kill me!' Gareth’s courage dissipated as soon as he faced such fierce attacks. He dropped the sword flusteredly and dodged the attack by rolling on the ground. Then out of the corner of his eye, he caught a glimpse of the broken bricks and stones at the spot where he had been, and the iron branches of the side window that were all cut off——

        ‘Tha-tha-that’s terrifying. Their attacks can even break through the iron cell… Ah! I’ve got an idea!’

        A flash of wit hit upon Gareth. He walked to the iron fence and asked Guinevere to take a few steps back.  The dark metal armored soldier let out a purple stream and slashed brutally at Gareth. Yet, the latter dodged the attack easily as he caught the knight’s heavy footwork.

        Two strokes of heavy sword hit the iron fence and broke the cell! Under the flying dust, Gareth took Guinevere’s hand and ran out. Then he helped her climb onto the wooden table to the tattered side window.

        Just as the soldiers were going to chase after them, Gareth raised his eyebrow and threw the torch on the wall at them. The soldiers dodged it but the haystacks on the ground caught on fire. The fire spread and smoke filled the room.

        When the soldier realized, Gareth and Guinevere had already disappeared at the window...
STORY_2746:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.7

        A light of sword shone. Arthur ran desperately and reach out her hand to stop it, but she was still too late that she could only watch the sword pierce through Lancelot’s body——

        ‘Nooooo——!’ She panted breathlessly. Her chest rose and fall in abrupt undulations. As she opened her eyes, she saw an ashen ceiling.

        Arthur got up and looked around this unfamiliar and quiet room. Then she saw the perturbed eyes of Bedivere so she said ardently, ‘Bedivere! Did you save us? Where’s everybody? Has Lancelot regained his consciousness yet?’

        Seeing  Bedivere’s complex expression and hesitation in speaking, Arthur recalled that Bedivere told her the truth under this kind of sullen silence before they got separated. Thus, she became nervous. ‘Just tell me! I’m not a kid anymore. And my friends matter to me!’

        Since Bedivere told her the whole story, Arthur immediately said, ‘I’m going to the palace and fight with everyone.’

        ‘But you’re seriously wounded——’
        ‘I can’t let everybody take the risk for me! Only I can draw out the Excalibur and stop Mordred!’

        Arthur looked at Bedivere straight in the eye, showing no trace of fear. After a while, Bedivere gave up. She took the equipment and handed the Star Stone left by Merlin to Arthur, said, ‘Arthur, stick to your father’s will of protecting everything. Use this power and bring changes to this country!’ 

✽

        In the palace hall.

        A man was clasped by a giant monster. His face was bluish because of suffocation. He seemed to be out of breath. Suddenly, an enormous shadow appeared before the right window. A sharp noise of broken glass came before the monster could ever react. Then a violent force kicked it to the other wall, creating a deep hole.

        The man who was clamped just now fell onto the ground and choked because of rapid breathing. Then someone held him up and called his name worriedly, ‘Lancelot!’

        ‘Cough… You’re late, monkey.’ Even though he looked piteous, Lancelot still teased Arthur as he always did

        ‘You… Stop calling me monkey!’ Despite the unforgiving words coming from Arthur’s mouth, her eyes were already filled with tears since she knew the Lancelot she used to know was back.

        Standing aside, Bedivere watched the two’s interaction with a smile. However, it soon turned into a stiff smile as she felt an immense hint of menace approach, which left her no time to warn the two but only stand in front of Arthur and block it.

        Mordred, who had turned into a moster, abruptly rushed over and swung his sturdy arm at Bedivere, knocking her into the air like a weightless doll.

        ‘Bedivere!’ Arthur dashed to catch Bedivere, only to see her pale face, dazed eyes and blood dripping from the corner of her mouth.

        ‘I-I’m fine… Arugh!’ Still, Bedivere was seriously injured that she passed out. Just then, Mordred came again but failed as Lancelot stopped him with his sword.

        However, the difference in power was too great. Seeing that Lancelot was being suppressed, Arthur got frantic.

        “If this goes on like this, Lancelot will be defeated. Is there any way we can take him down...”

        Just as Arthur was racking her brain for a solution, the door was suddenly opened. Two people, one tall and one short, broke in. The short one-Tristan waved his hand with prismatic light shining at his fingertips and yelled, ‘Arthur! The last Star Stone is here!’

        The Excalibur hanging on Mordred’s waist kept shaking and shimmering as if it had sensed something. Arthur didn’t miss the opportunity. She put down Bedivere, raised her right arm and yelled, ‘Excalibur, come to me!’

        With a swish, the Excalibur got away from Mordred and flew to Arthur.

        ‘No! Th-that’s my sword!’ Mordred wanted to chase after but he was stopped by Lancelot.

        Meanwhile, a light glowed on Tristan, Lancelot and Arthur. As the five Star Stones on them turned into streams of light, they darted towards the Excalibur and filled the five holes on the scabbard. Embedded on the scabbard, the Star Stones shone in five colors.

        Arthur slightly pushed open the sheath. Upon the blade’s first reveal, it released a blinding and dazzling light, which was so hallowed that brought people in awe. Under the bright silver light, Arthur drew out the Excalibur completely and raised it to the air!

        ‘That’s mine! I AM the destined king!’ Regardless of his bleeding wounds, the monstrous Mordred shoved Lancelot aside and hurtled towards Arthur with black flames conjuring on his hand and red veins standing out on his hideous eyes.

        ‘You are not the king and you never will be!’ Arthur spoke every word loud and clear, staring at Mordred’s chest. As she found the vile core hidden inside, she immediately swayed her right arm and stabbed at it——the Excalibur hit the vile core right in the middle. The vile core then broke into pieces, turned into dust and disappeared into the air along with the wind.

        Losing the protection of his black magic, Mordred slowly turned back to his human form. The backlash of magic sapped all his strength and power. Like a wilted plant, he knelt in front of Arthur, eyes wide opened with reluctance, murmuring, ‘No way, I’m the real——’

        Unfortunately, he had his last breath before he could finish his last word.

        ‘We… w-we did it!’ Raising a loud cheer, Tristan hugged Lamorak. As if they were attracted by his cheers, Merlin, Galahad, Gareth, Guinevere and Gawain came to the palace hall one after another. Everyone was full of joy, except Arthur, who was still at a loss.
　　
        A breeze of wind came and gently stroke her hair as if it sensed her confusion.  Realizing something, Arthur looked up at the throne, where a reflection of light shone and formed a holy halo.

        Arthur took a step as if she was lured. She climbed up the stairs step by step, cautiously and earnestly, walked to the back of the throne and knelt. Then she finally had a clear sight of the spot where the light landed. There was a line of elegant handwriting craved on it. 
　　
        ——Power is meant to serve and protect others. King Uther
　　
        An inexplicable feeling boiled over in Arthur’s heart, which eventually turned into tears and rolled down from her virescent eyes. She reached her hand and caressed those words. Leaning her head devoutly on it, she whispered softly, ‘Father, I will always keep your teachings in mind.’
STORY_2747:
Finale of Knights of the Round Table - Ch.8

        With the help of her companions, Arthur gathered the Star Stones, drew out the Excalibur successfully and defeated Mordred. As the vile core had been broken, the imperial soldier armored with dark metal was no longer controlled by black magic.

        After the loss of their leader, the imperial army was brought to the brink of chaos but was soon conquered by the Excalibur. Later, Bedivere led the opposition party and subdued the remnants of Mordred’s party. She then convinced the people to support Arthur by spreading the news of the Excalibur being drawn out. Eventually, the long-illed Accolon announced abdication.

        This day was Arthur’s coronation. 

        The sun poured in the palace. Arthur stood in the middle of the room with her arms open and a blush of embarrassment when Merlin and Guinevere were helping her get in the full royal gown.  Merlin straightened her collar, then said with a satisfied smile, ‘Arthur, finally you’re wearing something decent. Try more dresses after you take the throne!’

        ‘No! This gown is so tight and troublesome. It takes too much time to put it on——Ouch! It‘s too tight. I can't breathe!’ yelled Arthur. Guinevere, who was girding her waist, immediately let go and said, ‘Sorry. Is it better now?’

        ‘How about you do it for me, Guinevere? Let Merlin disguise you as me. You sure will be more decent than me! ‘ Arthur suggested.

        The two instantly shook their head. Guinevere giggled, ‘I can’t draw the Excalibur. You have to do it yourself!’

        ‘Oh right! My sword!’ Arthur wanted to turn around but she was restrained by the tight-fitting dress. Afraid that she might tear the dress apart, Merlin immediately held her shoulders and stopped her.

        Just then, Galahad’s voice came from her back, ‘I have cleaned the scabbard for you. Take it!’

        ‘It is the real Excalibur this time, right?’ asked Arthur.

        ‘Of course! If you don’t believe me, just unsheathe it yourself!’ Galahad came to Arthur, blushed with anger and shame.

        Slowly pushing up her long sleeves, Arthur wanted to pet Galahad’s head but the latter dodged it and ran right away. ‘I’ve told you many times. Don’t treat me like a kid!’

        Galahad was so absorbed in talking to Arthur that she almost bumped into Bedivere, who was coming right in the door.

        When everyone saw Bedivere, they greeted her with a respectful nod then showed her Arthur’s look elatedly. As Arthur turned around stiffly, Bedivere expressed amazement at seeing her dressed with formality and elegance. She then stepped forward, straightened Arthur’s dress, leaned back and took a look. Her eyes were filled with love and profound emotions.

        Bedivere gave Arthur a hug then held her arm and looked her in the eye, ‘From today on, you will be the lord of the kingdom. You can no longer act recklessly.’

        ‘Sure! I will become a better king than my father!’ Arthur said confidently with her arms akimbo. Just as she was about to step forward, she almost tripped because of the unfamiliar high heels.

        Merlin promptly held her up and said with a sigh, ‘But first, you have to learn how to walk elegantly.’

        Bedivere smiled and said, ‘That’s right. You still have a lot to learn after you’ve become the king. But I’m relieved since you have them by your side.’

        Then She looked around the room. Everyone gave a bright smile as they heard her. ‘Alright, the ceremony is going to start soon.’

        Following Bedivere’s lead, Arthur stepped into the hall. All people stood up as the horns echoed. In the seats, she saw some familiar faces-Gareth and his father were standing next to each other, while Tristan and Lamorak were standing on the other side. They all looked at Arthur with respectful and expectant eyes.

        Holding their swords, Gawain and Lancelot were already standing in front of the stage with one on the left and one on the right. As Arthur walked closer, the corners of their lips couldn’t help but curve up with blessings shining in their eyes.

        Arthur carefully walked up the stairs. As she bowed and lowered her head, Bedivere placed the crown upon her. The two met eye to eye and smiled. After Bedivere gave her a nod, Arthur turned around and was greeted with a big round of applause from her people.

        Then, Arthur and her trusted aides, which were her friends, walked to the balcony to meet her people. Bedivere stepped to the back and watched with her arms crossed.

        Under the witness of the crowd, Arthur unsheathed the radiant Excalibur. The sacrosanct light of holiness left the crowd in awe. As the light faded, thundering cheers and applause broke out. People yelled, ‘May the holy light be with King Arthur!’

        The bell rang; ribbons and confetti flew in the air. Smiling, Arthur waved at the crowd then looked at Bedivere.

        Bedivere smiled as well and nodded, sighed in her heart, ‘King Uther, I’ve done my best for what you have entrusted me. Arthur has inherited your kindness. It must be her will of protecting others, that has earned the recognition of the Excalibur.’

        “There is still much for her to learn in the coming days, but don’t worry. She has a bunch of great friends. I believe she will be a great king with their help!” Bedivere looked up and saw a flock of birds glide across the sunny sky.
STORY_2751:
In flying snow, a scrawny orphan was stumbling down the street with a rag being her only clothing. Starved and cold, she walked on the ground barefoot; every step was a prickle for her. She thought that she might just as well collapse and let the wind and snow burry her. Just as she was about to fall, a pair of warm arms caught her.

        ‘From today on, you’re Idun.’

        After taking the orphan home, Angrboda gave her the name Idun and took care of her. This was the first time Idun knew the warmth from others. The two lived in a chalet. During their stay, Angrboda taught her all kinds of knowledge.

        However, the more Angrboda taught Idun, the more she felt that something was wrong. Until one day, Idun found Angrboda packing.

        ‘Are you… leaving me too?’ Hanging her head low, Idun said in a low voice that broke Angrboda’s heart.

        ‘I have to leave, to find a power from ancient times. This is my fate… It is the only way to keep my clan's people from war.’

        Idun tugged at Angrboda’s sleeve and said that she wanted to go find the ancient power with her. Yet, she was still reluctant to bring Idun with her, even she put on the weeps. The journey to finding the ancient power was too dangerous that Angrboda couldn’t even ensure her own safety, let alone bring a little girl with her.

        For Idun’s desperate pleas, she finally relented and stated that Idun could go with her on the condition that she passed her trial: she must walk through a road called the Path of Trial and pick a purple flower that only grew at the end of the path.

        At first, Idun thought that it was an easy test. Yet, she could only return to the starting point no matter how hard she try. She still wasn’t able to pass the test until the day when Angrboda took her backpack and set off. Watching Angrboda leave, Idun swore that she would catch up with her one day.

        On the Path of Trial, where trail marks would disappear the next day, one could only return to the starting point if he or she walked blindly. To find the clues about how to pass the Path of Trial, Idun started reading Angrboda’s notes and her library. She began to understand the world bit by bit through books; through her notes, she knew that the Path of Trial was actually a giant and magical maze.

        In order to pass the test, Idun went to the Path of Trial every day. Since there was no shortcut, she tried time after time and learned all the changes and patterns little by little from every mistake she made on the road. With her encounter on the path, Idun gradually integrated all the knowledge she had learned…

        As the days went by, Idun grew up—from a little girl to a maiden. Every year, Angrboda would come back to the chalet and spend the winter with her. Then she would leave by the time the snow melted. It was a gracious time that the two enjoyed and treasured. Idun’s heart wrenched when she saw Angrboda’s wounds she got from her journey alone, so she worked even harder to solve the Path of Trial.

        For years Idun had not talked about accompanying Angrboda on her journey, she thought that she had given up. That year, Angrboda packed up alone as usual when the snow melted. Just as she was about to set off, she found Idun standing before her with a backpack on her back and a bouquet of purple flowers in her hands.

        Looking at each other, the two simultaneously laughed. Then they went on their journey to find the ancient power.

        That memory was the only one that Idun had never forgotten no matter how long time passed. Perhaps it was also the thing that kept her on the right track in the torrent of time.

        Just then, the only wish Idun had was to follow Angrboda closely. Little did she know that Angrboda would still leave her for good one day…
STORY_2752:
In a golden hall of magnificence, where red beams were engraved with phoenixes and sandalwood was chiseled with dragons, spirals of smoke rose from an auspicious animal censer slowly to the dais high above.

        Leaning against the extravagant throne erected on the dais, Ying Zheng was looking down with his right hand fiddling with the glittering ring of white jade on his thumb. Yet, his leisurely posture made all the courtiers who were kneeling below even more nervous. 

        ‘How is the barbarian state in the west?” asked Ying Zheng unemotionally. 

        One of the courtiers replied respectfully, “Your majesty, our mighty army broke through the enemy’s palace five days ago and captured their ruler alive. He is now imprisoned, waiting for your judgment.”

        “I heard that the ruler of the west is a true hero with an unyielding mind. I would like to see him.” Ying Zheng lifted his head and said, “Bring him here.”

        Soon, a man was sent to the hall under guard by two soldiers. Although the man looked haggard, his eyes were still shining with unbending will. When they came to the end of the hall, the soldiers asked the man to kneel down yet the latter refused to do so. The soldiers still failed even after they tried to press him by force.

        Just when the soldiers were about to draw their swords and threaten the man, Ying Zheng stopped them with a wave of his hand. He then stood up from the dragon chair, walked down the stairs serenely, and came to the king of the west, ignoring the dissuasion from his courtiers.

        “No prostration?” asked Ying Zheng.
        “No.”
        “Good.” Instead of getting angry, Ying Zheng flashed him an intriguing smile and said, “Men, go gather all the children under ten in the west and off with their heads by tomorrow morning.”

        Ying Zheng’s order aroused exclamations of shock and voices of discussion around the hall. Yet no one dared to admonish him, except the king of the west state who dashed forward and grabbed Ying Zheng’s shoulders and growled, “You——You monster! Kill me as you like. Leave the children alone!”

        “By killing you, I would be just giving you what you want, but killing the children can drive you mad so it’s worth it.” As Ying Zheng pushed the king aside, he asked again after a deliberate pause, “Still no prostration?”

        “You—” With his eyes wide open, the king of the western state gritted his teeth as if he would rip Ying Zheng’s throat off the next second. Seeing his scowling face, the courtiers standing aside shrank in fear; whereas Ying Zheng stayed put with a sardonic smile and watched as the man’s mounting rage gradually subsided and eventually disappeared.

        Pop——the king of the western state went down on his knees, put his arms forward with his head against the ground, and prostrated himself to Ying Zheng. However, Ying Zheng still shook his head discontentedly and said, “Not enough.”

        “...Long live the emperor.” Losing its vigor, the king’s voice was weak and powerless like an underdog.

        The confrontation ended with Ying Zheng’s crushing victory. Nevertheless, the victory was not as gratifying as Ying Zheng had imagined but rather pale and insipid.

        ‘The so-called true hero is nothing greater than that.’ With a flick of his sleeves, Ying Zheng headed back to his bedchamber, leaving the courtiers and the kind of the west state. Yet, he stopped the moment he set foot in the door. There was nothing strange in his sight but the experience he had gained through years was telling him that something was off in the room.

        Stilly, Ying Zheng looked around the chamber. His whole body tensed up but soon relaxed when he caught a glimpse of the purple tail hanging behind the partition. He then looked up at the ceiling where a four-headed violet dragon coiled himself around the beams, looking down on Ying Zheng with a satirical smile. It seemed he wanted to see him embarrass himself but he failed his expectation. 

        “What are you doing out here?” asked Ying Zheng composedly.

        “I didn’t swallow souls for nothing through all these years. I was only trapped in your little white bottle because I was injured. Now that I’ve recovered, it can’t trap me anymore.” Violet Dragon—Xuan Huang the Runedragon—flew to Ying Zheng and squinted at him, saying, “But worry not. For the contract we’ve made, I won’t hurt you.”

        “Since you are healed now, why don’t you leave?”
        “Of course I’ll leave, but I still have some unfinished business.”
        “What is it?”

        “...I need pure souls to cure my Souliade.” Perhaps it was that his wound had been healed; or that he thought Ying Zheng was no threat, Xuan Huang surprisingly let his guard down and answered Ying Zheng’s question.

        ‘Souliade?’
        “To put it in the easiest way with human words, he’s kind of like my twin brother.”
        “What happened to him?”

        “He was seriously injured in a war against some powerful monster years ago. He could have healed himself with elements by taking ample rest. However, given the unstable flow of elements, it may take years for him to heal. That’s why I came to the human realm for pure souls to cure him but—” As if there was a lump in Xuan Huang’s throat, he paused and only continued after a moment, “It’s none of your business. You just keep getting me pure souls.”

        “...So your clan is very strong?”
        “Humph, of course, far stronger than the fragile humans.”

        ‘The world of the strong… What will it be like if I become the king…’ thought Ying Zheng, lowering his eyes. A thought was born at that moment. With the nourishment of time, it gradually grew and became a desire that Ying Zheng could not turn his back on; he eventually took action to achieve it.

        Dozens of little girls and boys were sent to the main hall, all tied up. Sitting on his throne, Ying Zheng kept a poker face, whereas Xuan Huang behind him could barely hide his excitement.

        ‘I will have enough power to awaken Bai Hu as soon as I swallow this batch of souls.’ Swaying his towering body, Xuan Huang wandered among the children while devouring the souls he had drawn out one by one. Then dozens of breathing lives turned into stiff corpses in the blink of an eye.

        “Finally… I finally made it… Ying Zheng, now it’s time we part…AHHHHH—!” Suddenly, an inexplicable and excruciating pain shot through Xuan Huang from his soul, so excruciating that he could not help but scream and fell to the ground for his lack of strength.

        ‘Something is gnawing at my soul… Could it be—!’ Xuan Huang raised his head and looked at the man on the dragon chair. With his eyes turning crimson in hatred, he clenched his teeth and yelled, “The Soul-eating Gu... You planted the gu poison on them!”

        “Bingo. Unfortunately, it’s too late,” said Ying Zheng with a pleased smile, who seemed to be happy about his successful plan.

        “You… You…bastard…” Xuan Huang struggled desperately. However, his soul was soon gnawed off by dozens of Soul-eating Gu. The brightness of his dragon eyes gradually dimmed as his mind began to fade.

        “You once asked me what I am, didn’t you?” Ying Zheng walked down from the throne and came to Xuan Huang, looking down at him for the first time.

        “Mon…ster… You’re…a monster…” At the very last moment, Xuan Huang uttered a few words as soft as a whisper. His voice was so weak that one could hardly hear but Ying Zheng somehow just knew what he was saying.

        “No, I… I will be the ruler of heaven that dominates everything.” The moment when Ying Zheng made his claim, Xuan Huang’s entire soul was devoured by the Gu and his eye lost their gleam completely.

        As Ying Zheng closed his eyes and started chanting the runes, his soul turned into dense dark smoke and went inside Xuan Huang’s body…
STORY_2755:
In a desolate valley, Madeleine the maiden was tied to a stone pillar. She was a princess whose kingdom was invaded by the Demons not long ago. Although the Queen successfully repelled the enemy with her army, they took Madeleine away and held her captive.

        Leading her army, the Queen tried to rescue Madeleine but her soldiers were gravely wounded after running into the Demons’ ambush several times. Luckily, the Queen broke through the Demons’ siege with a small troop of cavalry and finally came to the valley standing in front of her.

        The Queen, of all people, was fully aware that there would certainly be countless traps in the valley ahead of her. But for the sake of her daughter, she led the army forward, come what may. Along the way, the Queen was frazzled and covered with scars; her armor was also heavily stained with blood and mud.

        Just then, a volley of arrows came at the Queen and her cavalry from the top of the mountain. When the arrows were about to hit the Queen, she activated the power of the Azure Armor and fended off the arrows in mid-air with a water wall.

        Seeing the arrows flop in vain,  a swarm of Demon soldiers rushed down towards the Queen and her cavalry. Riding her horse, the Queen led the charge with her eyes locked on the shackled Madeleine.

        Commanding the water to form an airtight shield, the Queen protected the vanguard. Just when she reached Madeleine, a loud bang came from the ground, followed by a mountainous shock wave that almost wrecked the entire valley.

        It turned out that the Demon leader, who had been hiding on the summit, detonated the dynamite buried in the valley, trying to entomb all the lives there—including those of his comrades. In the nick of time when the blast was about to sweep away all living creatures, the Queen evoked all the power that remained on her armor and protected everyone.

        The valley was thrown into complete shambles after the explosion. Yet, all the cavalry survived by dint of the Queen’s protection.

        Holding her sobbing daughter tightly in her arms, the Queen consoled her softly and said, ‘Now we can… go home…’
　　
        However, just when the Queen intended to take Madeleine and leave, an arrow darted towards the latter from a distance. The alerted Queen pushed Madeleine away at the very last moment while the arrow ripped through her chest.

        Only till then did the Demon troopers reveal themselves slowly, assaulting the survivors with mocking laughter.  Although Madeleine was saved from the arrow, her face was deeply gashed by the gravel as she was pushed to the ground and blood kept oozing from her wound with burning pain.

        However, she didn’t have the time to ease her pain. She held the Queen’s body in her arms with tears pouring down her face.  Resenting her own incompetence, she was tired of being weak that she didn’t want her loved ones to die because of her again.

        “I killed my mother… If only I was stronger, I wouldn’t be imprisoned by the Demons… I don’t want to be a burden anymore!”

        Feeling Madeleine’s determination, the Queen’s armor turned into a current of water and draped around her. Then, a voice that she was very familiar with sounded in her heart.

        “There, there… I’ll always protect you.”

        A Demon soldier went to the back of Madeleine with a sword in his hand ready to slash, yet Madeleine stopped him onehanded. As the combat techniques of the past Paladin Queen of Water kept flooding into her mind, she conjured a water blade in her palm and stabbed the Demon in the chest after a twirl of the sword.

        She then took the sword and the giant shield of the Queen. Like a stream of water, she danced swimmingly on the battlefield, bringing an enemy down with each swing of her sword.

        Madeleine slew every Demon in the valley, whose blood smeared all over her armor and painted it red. She then carried the Queen’s body in her arms and left the valley, lurching back to their kingdom.
STORY_2756:
Origin of Demons - Supreme Reckoning Story Ch. 5

        For Mastema’s discontent with Belial, she conspired to revolt against him yet failed as Belial saw through her attempt and captured her soul. However, her soul was soon taken by the traitorous Abadon and Beelzebub.

        Even though Azazel chased after them immediately, he lost them so he could only beg for Belial’s forgiveness. Instead of blaming him, the latter said with a sarcastic laugh, “Mastema’s body has been destroyed. It is useless even if they have taken back her soul so don’t bother to trace them.”

        “...Yes.’ Azazel could only respond respectfully. Yet, there was an inexplicable bad feeling lingering in his heart, which soon came true.

        In an afternoon when the sky was obscured by a dense gray cloud, Azazel was about to leave the barracks and head to Belial’s house with some documents. He stepped out of the camp, however, five demon soldiers stopped him.

        Azazel asked with a frown, “What happened?”

        “Please come with us, sir,” said one of the soldiers.

        “I’m busy. I have to report the investigation results to Master Belial.” Azazel adamantly refused. When he planned to go around the soldiers, a soldier grabbed him by his shoulder and pulled him back.

        “I’m sorry but we’re not asking you, sir.” As the soldier made eye contact with his comrades, the other soldiers immediately stepped forward, attempting to subdue Azazel with force. However, before their hands even touched him, a burst of strong power flicked them off.

        At the same time as Azazel unleashed his power, he flung off the hand that had been holding him. The moment he regained his freedom, he went ahead with his attack before the soldier could even realize it, knocking the four soldiers unconscious in the blink of an eye.

        “Who sent you?” Azazel callously asked the only soldier who was still awake.

        The soldier struggled to utter a few words, ‘It’s… Mas… Master Mastema.”

        “What?!” exclaimed Azazel. The anxiety that crept in on him since Mastema’s soul had been stolen now grew rapidly and eventually turned into a sharp thorn in his heart.

        Azazel no longer dealt with the soldier. After battering the soldier unconscious with a hand chop, he immediately rushed to the mansion of Belial. When he saw that mansion sunk in damp gloom, he dashed inside, putting his own safety behind him. The moment he pushed open the door, he saw Baal, Belial’s older brother, grabbing Belial’s hair and forcing him to lift his head.

        “Master Belial!” Azazel felt his heart stopped beating at that moment. Luckily, his body moved instinctively and unshackled a burst of water elements which then turned into a water dragon and attacked Baal. Dismally, his attack didn’t waver his enemy, not even a bit.

        Lifting his arm, Baal wiped Azazel’s dragon off with just a wave. The unusual noise awakened Belial, who propped his blood-soaked body up and looked at Azazel.

        “Go… Azazel… Go” said Belial weakly.

        “No! I’m not leaving!” Azazel shouted though he knew clearly in his heart.

        ‘With my current power, I can’t protect Master Belial… I need a stronger power…’ Gritting his teeth, Azazel took out a sphere containing dark power, which he took from the dragonkin. He had no idea what it was, only that he knew the sphere was the only bargaining chip he had.

        As Azazel shattered that sphere, he took all that gloomy and despairing darkness into his body. Then, an agonizing pain of being destroyed shot through every part of his body.

        “AHHHH——” The second Azazel let out a hysterical scream of pain, countless tentacles broke out from his body and attacked Baal in an earth-shattering manner. Baal, who could not brush off the attack as easily as the last time, could only let go of Belial and took a step back.

        Seizing this chance, Azazel controlled the tentacles and snatched Belial. Then, he ran out of the door, leaving a bunch of demons that were stunned by his power. Just then, Mastema walked forward and came to the side of Baal.

        “Lord, should I send people to pursue them?”

        “No need.” Baal wasn’t provoked by the fact that Belial had been rescued; instead, he gave an intrigued smile and whispered softly, “That power is the same as his… No, they’re different. It is much more stable than his… How interesting it is. I knew this world would be more compelling than what I had imagined.”

        Since his escape from the mansion, Azazel desperately fled in one direction, running tremendously as if he would be caught once he paused for a second. However, his body soon reached its limits. As the heart-racking pain suddenly befell him, his movements stopped, and fell hard to the ground together with Belial.

        “Azazel!” Pressing the wound on his chest, Belial walked towards where Azazel fell. For the injuries on his leg, his stumbling steps made him look ignominious. Still, he made his way to Azazel, who had scars all over his body. Dark blood was oozing from his wounds, which seemed to indicate the fact that the power of darkness was gnawing Azazel’s body.

        “Mas… Master Belial… Are you alright?” Despite the excruciating pain, Belial was still the first and most important thing that came to Azazel’s mind.

        “Humph, these are just scratches.”

        “That’s a relief… Cough!” Coughing up blood, Azazel could feel that his mind was reeling so he spoke with the last bit of his strength, “Master Belial, I’m afraid Baal will send pursuers after you. Please just leave me here… and go as soon as possible… Hm!”

        “Azazel!” yelled Belial, yet no one answered him. He smacked his tongue displeased, looking into the boundless wilderness. At last, he carried Azazel’s body with the latter’s hand over his shoulder and walked toward the unknown...
STORY_2757:
Origin of Demons - Supreme Reckoning Story Ch. 1

        As the ringing sound of the communication device horned in on the sweet atmosphere between Abadon and Beelzebub, she looked at Abadon with worries all over her face.

        “Brother...”
        “Don’t worry.” After taking out the device, Abadon shut it down decisively and pulled the anxious Beelzebub into his arms, saying, “We will stay together forever. No one can break us apart.”

        “Yes, Beelzebub just wants to stay with you…” Beelzebub, who gained courage from Abadon’s warm hug, soon loosened up and held him back with her arms, circling a corner that only belonged to the two of them.

        Later, Abadon and Beelzebub went around the main battlefields between gods and demons and lived in a remote mountain. Sadly, their tranquil life didn’t last long—Baal sent two demons, Leviathan and Belphegor, to them.

        They had a fierce fight, which eventually ended with the successful escape of Abadon and Beelzebub. Just when Leviathan wanted to chase after them resentfully, the sound of the communication device stopped her. It was a call from Baal. 

        “Oh, so he betrayed Belial for his little pet?” Baal’s deep voice melted Leviathan’s heart. “Then there’s no need to pursue them. He’ll soon come to me.”

        Leviathan didn’t know why Baal had such confidence, but for her unconditional trust in him, she left with Belphegor, letting Abadon and Beelzebub run away.

        Abadon and Beelzebub found another place to live a secluded life, yet that was just the start of a nightmare—Beelzebub fell sick. For some reason, her body was running a fever that no medicine could cure.

        ‘This is not a common illness…’ Suddenly, Abadon had an epiphany. As he looked at the fragile Beelzebub lying in the bed, he gritted his teeth and made up his mind. He then picked up the communication device that had been left out for a long time and dialed it. Soon, a male voice sounded, “You finally call me, Abadon.”

        “You did that to Beelzebub.”

        “Yeah, I mixed it in the first medicine given to her. It was supposed to be a safety pin but I didn’t know that you take her so seriously.”

        “What do you want?”

        “Worry not. I’m not as ignorant as my spoiled brother. I play fair. Just get me Mastema’s soul and your debts to me shall be settled.”

        “...Fine.” Abadon had no other choice, no matter he believed Baal or not, so he resolutely said yes.

        ‘Belial has great trust in Azazel. Something as important as Mastema’s soul must be entrusted to him. Maybe I’ll find a clue in his room.’

        And so, Abadon asked the neighboring villagers to look after Beelzebub while he sneaked into the base of demons alone. With his memories from the past, he went to Azazel’s room through a secret tunnel and surprisingly found the container that captured Mastema’s soul right in a cabinet.

        Just when Abadon was about to leave with the container after breaking the magical lock with tremendous effort, he felt a hint of malice arising behind his back so he immediately sprang to the right and barely dodged the water ball thrown at him. The water ball contained brute force that smashed the cabinet into pieces.

        “How dare you traitor come back!” When Azazel, who was already boiling with rage, saw the container in Abadon’s hand, his fury mounted to another level that he shouted aloud, “How dare you try to steal the thing of Master Belial. Inexcusable!”

        Azazel conjured water elements and formed them into a giant water ball, then he threw it at Abadon.

        Maintaining his composure, Abadon put the container into his arms and conjured elements with a derisive laugh. His arms then burst into flames. As he raised his arms, the water ball stopped with a boiling sound and disappeared shortly.

        “That’s all you got? Now it’s my turn,” said Abadon, who pounced on Azazel, lifting his blazing arms. The latter dodged him ignominiously and soon was cornered to a wall.

        Just as Abadon was about to give him the last blow, his body shuddered the moment he met Azazel’s eyes. He pulled back at once; still, he was not quick enough—a sharp blade cut off his left forearm from behind.

        “Argh——!” Screaming in pain, Abadon still managed to leap backward.

        “Tut! You only got his left forearm.” Azazel smacked his tongue regrettably.

        “He has great reflexes, too great that he retreated the moment he saw me in your eyes,” said the swordswoman, Samael, shaking the blood and bone fragments off her sword.

        “So what? Now he is outnumbered and injured. It is only about time that he loses.” Azazel snorted jubilantly, “I will not spare anyone who betrays Master Belial.”

        Standing the agonizing pain, Abadon saw the murderous Azazel and Samael. With cold water poured on his pompous vigor, bleak despair began to creep up on him. However, his will was reignited when Bezeelbub’s face flashed across his mind.

        ‘I can’t lose… Beelzebub is still waiting for me!’
STORY_2758:
Origin of Demons - Supreme Reckoning Story Ch. 3

        Abadon and Beelzebub wanted to leave Belial and they had to fight for it. The fight eventually ended with the successful escape of Abadon and Beelzebub.

        Samael thought that she would not see them again. However, Abadon showed up again, attempting to steal Mastema’s soul; Beelzebub also came to protect his weak body. Seeing the two supporting each other, Samael’s heart softened. She blocked Azazel’s attack and let Abadon and Beelzebub go.

        Later, Azazel left after giving her a glare. Samael knew that he was going to Belial, who should come and ask her for an explanation soon.

        Samael didn’t go into panic or anxiety; instead, she felt a sense of relief waiting for her final judgment. As usual, she went to the laboratory and did the scheduled experiments, until storming footsteps broke the tranquility in the lab.

        Raising her head, Samael looked at the intruder whose face was still fine as always only that it was now stained with inexplicable turpitude and ruthlessness. The light that once defended her with a crown of thorns on his head and a coat draped on his shoulders was gone for good. 

        “...Master Belial,” Samael greeted him respectfully, lowering her eyes. Then it suddenly dawned on her that this was the most appropriate distance between him and her—as a superior and a subordinate.

        “Why did you let Abadon and Beelzebub off the hook?” It seemed that Belial was trying to control the anger inside him, yet the bulging veins and his gravelly tone revealed his sharpness.

        “Because they reminded me who we were a long time ago.”

        “Oh, yeah, so weak and powerless that they can only be trampled and manipulated.”

        “Is that all you could see?” The sorrowful words of Samael’s misery only made Belial even more frustrated.

        “What else do those two losers have?”

        “The unconditional trust and the willingness to sacrifice everything for each other.”

        “So now you’re talking about trust and sacrifices after letting them go behind my back?”

        “...You won’t understand… No, you never wanted to understand. How long have we ever talked about things other than power struggles...” said Samael blankly as if her mind slipped into the river of memory. ‘I can’t even recall when the last time we talked heart to heart was. You’ve changed so much——”

        “Enough!” Belial yelled. As if it was not enough, he swept all the instruments on the lab table with both his arms. The shrill noise of breaking glass echoed across the room, which intensified the atmosphere between them.

         Belial no longer hid his wrath and scolded Samael, “Stop fooling me with gibberish. Just tell me your intention.”

        “I’ve already told you, but you never believe——”

        “That’s just an excuse! I know your true intention.” Losing control, Belial stared at Samael tempestuously and growled, “It’s because you’ve fallen in love with Baal! You think he is more powerful and authoritative than me. That’s why you betrayed me and let those two losers go!”

        “Is it what you really think it is?” Samael’s face was overwhelmed with shock, sorrow and pain.

        “Yes, but I wonder how did you hook up with Baal in the first place. Was it with your body——”

        Slap! A resounding slap put a stop to Belial’s ceaseless accusation. As Samael finally came to the end of her tolerance, she could not help but move her hand. Yet, she was more embarrassed at that moment as though she was the one being slapped than the one giving it.

        Agitated, Samael’s chest rose and fell violently and she only calmed down after taking a few deep breaths. Then, she tilted her face away from the unrecognizable lover in front of her.

        “Now we’re both too emotional. There won’t be a conclusion even if we keep talking like this. I think we should spend some time alone,” said Samael, who then turned and walked towards the gate.

        ‘Even Samael is betraying me… No, I won’t let that happen.’ Madness filled Belial’s eyes. He abruptly stepped forward and grabbed the back of Samael’s head, with gloomy green light sparkling like an ominous sign.

        “Belial… St-stop...” Samael felt that her body had become empty; her soul was pulled away from her body even though she wanted to stay. Still, she couldn’t escape the fate of being torn apart. 

        With one of his hands holding Samael’s soul, Belial held her feeble body with the other. As a crazy and distorted smile crossed his face, he murmured with satiation, “Now you can’t betray me.”

         ‘No… Then you’ll be alone forever…’ Sorrows permeated into Samael’s heart and eventually turned into a crystal tear that trickled down from a corner of her eyes...
STORY_2759:
Origin of Demons - Supreme Reckoning Story Ch. 2

        After Beelzebub confessed her feelings to Abadon and received the same answer, they decided to leave Belial and live an ordinary life away from power struggles. However, Belial wasn’t willing to let them go.

        Although they got rid of Belial’s pursuit successfully, they couldn’t escape from Baal’s coercion. 
        Baal poisoned Beelzebub and put her into a raging fever. Seeing Beelzebub on the point of dying, Abadon was pressured to help him take Mastema’s soul back.

        While Beelzebub's mind was in turmoil because of the boiling fever, she sensed that Abadon came to her bed, knelt down, and said softly with her hand in his, “Beelzebub, don’t worry. I will complete Baal’s task and come back to save you with the antidote.”

        “No...Don-don’t go!” As Beelzebub woke up, she propped herself up and looked around. Yet, Abadon was nowhere to be found. She realized Abadon had left when she was in a coma.

        ‘I need to find him… find Brother!’ Under the lead of flies that she summoned, Beelzebub went to the base of demons. All the demons that came in her way were gnawed by the flies with only their bones left. However, as the fever that might well melt her body went up again, Beelzebub could only keep going solely relying on her will to find Brother.

        ‘Mmm… So hot… So painful… Brother... where are you?’ Supporting herself with the wall, Beelzebub stepped forward slowly. Suddenly, she caught a smell of burning flesh that gave a hard squeeze in her heart. A burst of energy channeled through her frail legs out of nowhere. She then ran towards where the smell came from only to find a heartrending scene—

        With their backs towards Beelzebub, Azazel and Samael were facing Abadon, who was standing in front of a cabinet dispiritedly. The part below his left elbow was gone with charred skin at the stump. Beelzebub knew that Abadon had burned his wound with fire to stop his bleeding. However, she was still dumbfounded—perhaps the picture in her eyes was too traumatic for her.

        Besides Beelzebub, there was another person who was stunned by Abadon’s action—Samael, who wavered and asked, “Is it worth it just for her?”

        “...Humph, if it wasn’t for her, you think I would put my life at stake for Belial, who only sees me as his pawn?” Even Abadon’s severe injuries and the cold sweat on his forehead couldn’t stop his scornful words.

        “How dare you disparage Belial’s name! Prepare to die!” Once again, Azazel attacked Abadon with a water ball.

        Beelzebub’s mind instantly became clear as she saw Abadon in danger.

        “Don’t hurt Brother!” While Azazel and Samael were staggered, she ran and stood in front of Abadon, driving the flies to surround the water ball. Unfortunately, the continuous use of power eventually exhausted Beelzebub and her body swayed and fell forward.

        “Beelzebub!” The moment Abadon caught Beelzebub, he felt the raging heat from her body so he asked worriedly, “Why did you come?! You could’ve died!”

        Beelzebub murmured weakly, “I’m not afraid…as long as...I’m with you… Beelzebub…” A happy smile spread over her face because she had found her Brother.

        “Is that so? Then I shall grant you your wish and let you two die together!” Azazel said with a contemptuous laugh. Just as he was about to attack, a figure stepped before Abadon and Beelzebub.

        “Samael! What are you doing? You aren’t gonna betray Belial either, are you?” yelled Azazel loudly.

        “Just get her out of here now.” Samael didn’t answer Azazel but talked to Abadon in a low voice.

        Astonished at Samael’s help, yet, Abadon didn’t miss the chance. Holding Beelzebub in his right arm, he turned and ran to a safe forest. When he was about to contact Baal with the communication device, he heard footsteps from his back.

        Alerted, Abadon turned around only to find an unexpected man. “Baal..”
　
        “You got it.” As Baal got straight to the point, Abadon hesitantly took out the container.

        “Yes, that’s it.” After taking the container, Baal put his hands in front of Beelzebub and channeled his magic power. With deep purple energy flowing out of Beelzebub’s body and dispersed, Abadon felt the body temperature in his arms immediately go down to a normal one.

        “Beelzebub!” yelled Abadon nervously. As if she was awakened, Beelzebub blinked her eyes and looked at Abadon. Then she gave him a sweet smile and said, “Brother…”

        “Great, you’re okay…” Overwhelmed, Abadon choked up but soon he suppressed the excitement in his heart. Even though Baal undid the poison he put on Beelzebub as he promised, that didn’t change the fact that he was the man who started it.

        “Bezeelbub, let’s go.”
        “Wait,” said Baal.
        “...I thought we’re even now.”
        “I can heal your arm.”

        “Really? You can heal—” Beelzebub asked in desperation as soon as she heard Baal, but Abadon stopped her.

        “No, I don’t want to owe you anything. I just want to spend my life with Beelzebub alone.”

        “Is it so? What a shame,” said Baal yet his face showed no wavering at all. “Then I shall wish you all the best.”

        “Let’s go.” With a relieved smile, Abadon took Beelzebub’s hand and said, “To find our own home.”

        “Yes.” With Abadon’s hand in hers, she rubbed their hands against her face like a child, whispering words of happiness, “A home of Brother and me.”
STORY_2760:
Origin of Demons - Supreme Reckoning Story Ch. 4

        Mastema wanted to overthrow Belial, yet her plan was discovered long ago by the prince. As a result, she fell into Belial’s trap which captured her soul in a container. Her mind was plunged into turmoil until that spellbinding man came and brought her back to the light one day.

        “Hmm!” With the sudden return of her five senses, Mastema was overwhelmed by the swarming information that gave her a headache. Just when she was racked with excruciating pain, a dark shadow fell over her. Then she heard a low and mellow male voice saying, “No rush. Your soul just returned to its body. You still need time to get used to it.”

        Squinting her eyes that were watering because of the pouring light, she looked at the shadow and finally recognized him. “...Lord Baal! Did you save me? This body…” 

        “The is a new body specially rebuilt for you. The one before has been destroyed and can’t be used anymore.”

        “Oh, is it…” Mastema thought she would be frustrated or apoplectic, yet her heart was instead calm and unfeeling. Now she only found it ridiculous when she looked back at her past obsession with Balial.

        “...Why did you save me?” Getting hold of herself, she looked Baal in the eye.

        “You should know better than me.” Baal bent over, lifted her chin with his hand, and murmured softly like a whisper in a lover’s ear, “Bring Belial to me, daughter of one of the seven aristocrats, Mastema.”

        Without any second thought, Mastema knelt on one knee. Holding Baal’s hand, she kissed it lightly with submission and said, “As you wish, Lord Baal.”

        Later, Mastema secretly contacted her subordinates before and talked the other nobles into compliance with the aristocratic name of her father. Then, she laid a trap one night, waiting for her prey named Belial to come.

        As the door of the elegant mansion was pushed open, a young man with green hair walked in. When he walked to the parlor, he was stunned by the dozen demons dressed in noble standing in front of him. But soon he hid his surprise and wore an arrogant and wilful smile.

        “What is everybody doing in my house at this late hour of night? We’re having a war against the gods tomorrow. It’d be better for you to get rest earlier, or else I’m afraid it may sap your strength.”

        “Humph! You insolent kid,” a middle-aged man with a ponytail stepped forward and said disdainfully. “If we don’t come today, I’m afraid we will be dead tomorrow without even knowing why.”

        “...What is that supposed to mean?” Belial scowled and put his hands behind his back. “Slandering a royal’s name for no reason is considered a felony. Now apologize to me and I shall spare you.”

        “Stop making excuses! It seems like you need a lesson to know what is right!” Just when the demon with a ponytail was about to draw the sword on his waist, a hand stopped him.

        “Wait.” A female voice familiar to Belial sounded. Incredulous, Belial abruptly turned and looked over. The moment he saw that figure, he gritted his teeth and growled, “Mastema!”

        “Yes, it’s me.” Without the animosity heaped in the past, Mastema showed a sharply posh aura under her gorgeous patrician gown. “What a surprise, isn’t it? I never thought that I could return to this world again after you took my soul away as I saw your trade with the gods.”

        “You’re lying! I never traded with the gods!” Belial refuted loudly. However, the cold gaze of all the other demons made him realize that they didn’t want his rebuttal nor would they let him.

        “It’s you again… You come to stop me again. I won’t let you get away with this!” A flame called rage suddenly rose from Belial’s heart. As he channeled his power, a green light appeared on his fists.

        He then focused and pounced on Mastema in a fierce and imposing manner. Some demons tried to stop him yet they were all knocked down by Belial. When the attack was about to hit Mastema, the corners of her mouth lifted. The next moment, a burst of monumental power broke out and shot directly at Belial’s body. Although he twisted his body and avoided fatal injuries, still he could not escape fate with him covered in blood. 

        “This isn’t your power… Who… Who gave you the power…” Belial knelt on the ground feebly; his right eye was closed because of bleeding so he could only stare at Mastema with his left eye.

        “Belial, who else has such immense power that can save me,” said Mastema with a scornful laugh. “You should’ve known the answer.”

        Belial immediately knew the answer. Then, as if he had sensed something, he abruptly raised his head and saw the man walking down the stairs—it was Baal, his elder brother.

        “Long time no see, my dear little brother,” said Baal with a smile and his hands behind his back.
STORY_2761:
There was a rumor that Baphomet held a library of forbidden knowledge. Whoever mastered the knowledge would acquire exceptional power. So a rapacious sorcerer set up a trap and captured Baphomet in an enchantment so as to steal his knowledge.

        ‘Give me your knowledge and I shall give you your freedom,’ said the sorcerer gloatingly to Baphomet. He even hoped that Baphomet would repulse him, then he could satisfy his sadistic desire by torturing the latter.

        As much as Baphomet despised that human who imprisoned him, he was fully aware that he could not resist, for he knew that the human wouldn’t let him live even if he handed over all his knowledge. Thus he came up with a fiendish plan that could lead the human into self-destruction…

        ‘Of course. Sorcerer, your greatness, I can give you anything you want. The question is, what do you want? The location of all the hidden treasure? Or the power of devastation?’

        Under the voice of Baphomet, numerous pictures flashed across the sorcerer’s mind—he became the greatest sorcerer in the world, omnipotent and invincible, and everyone was falling at his feet…

        ‘Give me the power!’ Rashly, the sorcerer shouted at Baphomet with his eyes reddened.

        ‘Sure. I can teach you the forbidden spells.’ Keeping his mockery to himself, Baphomet left the second part of his words unsaid—“only at a little price.”

        So Baphomet taught the sorcerer a set of spells and told him that he could strengthen his magic by using the spells constantly, and eventually he could rule over everything.

        At first, the sorcerer didn’t take Baphomet’s word completely. He only tested the Baphomet’s spells under layers of protection and he kept checking his own body afterward to ensure his own safety.

        However, as the sorcerer’s magic power grew rapidly, he no longer questioned Baphomet’s spells. He stopped studying and analyzing the spells; instead, he started using them frequently just like what Baphomet had told him at the beginning.

        Engrossed by the satisfaction of growing power, the sorcerer gradually fell in the grip of pursuing power. Consequently, he noticed a small crack on his body after using the spells one day.

        Nonetheless, he didn’t care, for he had already lost control by then.

        The sorcerer’s heart was already preoccupied with madness and destructive desire. The more so, the more difficult it was for him to restrain himself from using the forbidden spells.

        Finally, one day, the sorcerer died in an explosion and wound up in chunks of meat as his body failed to withhold that disproportionate power. Following the sorcerer’s demise, the enchantment that trapped Baphomet disappeared. The latter then left with a bellow of derisive laughter.

        “The blind pursuit and impercipient use of knowledge only leads to the depths of a chasm.”
STORY_2762:
Finale of Sengoku Samurai - Ch. 4
　　
        In the company of Azai, Oichi began her journey to find her older brother, Nobunaga. On their way, they bumped into some people from the Sanada family, who held an old feud with the Oda family, and thus started a fight. In the end, their opponents fled for their inability to contend against Azai. Azai wanted to go after them yet was stopped by a wildfire. 

        ‘It’s dangerous here. Let’s go.’ Azai ran in the opposite direction of the wildfire while screening Oichi from the flames. They only walked out of the forest and stopped to rest after running for a while.

        When Oichi finally got her breath back after the run, she heard a faint splashing noise, as if something was lapping against the shore.

        ‘...It’s the sea!’ Oichi clutched Azai’s sleeve and said in excitement, ‘I can hear the sound of waves. Maybe we can find a way out here.’

        “I don’t think that man would be so kind to leave such an easy escape route.” As Azai recalled that cloaked man who invited him to the island, he brought to mind that blatantly burning desire and inhuman presence. That man was definitely not a saint.

        However, his thought stopped at the tip of his tongue when he saw that elated look on Oichi’s face, so he held her hand instead and said gently, ‘Let’s go and see, but be careful.’
