STORY_2777:
Inside the Enochian Tower, Skuld sedated Odin, who had gone out of control again. After using up all her powers, she leaned against the wall to take some rest. As though to relieve her weariness, the elements created a realistic illusion, showing her an alternative reality of the other choice she could have made…

        When the Seal was triggered and Odin set foot in the path of no return, Skuld’s scissors went forward; its cold blade touched his neck. ‘Shall I kill you?’ she asked.

        The violet light of the Seal veiled Skuld’s face, but Odin could still hear her voice, in the same tone as usual. Little did he know that Skuld was trying her best to conceal the rising tide in her heart from him.

         Now that the Seal was complete, Odin could ask Skuld to cut the thread of his life if he did not want to spend the rest of his days in infinite torment.

        Skuld recalled all the sacrifices Odin had made for the people over the past years. At that moment, she ached to give him the eternal peace he deserved. However…

        ‘No. I shall live forever in the Seal as a warning to others,’ said Odin.

        ‘You do not have to do this. Do you know what lies ahead of you?’

        ‘I do. As Mimir and you have mentioned…’
　
        Skuld had been watching the fate of others and she never interfered. Yet, she lost her usual composure when it came to Odin—she could not bear to watch this man who had devoted himself completely to the North live in endless suffering. A question kept churning in her mind, “Is he destined for such a tragic life?”

        “A hero deserves to die well.” At such a thought, Skuld defied her father, Mimir’s teaching. She channeled her godly power and thrust her scissors into Odin’s body, cutting the thread of his life.

        ‘Skuld, you——’ Disappointment and sorrow flickered across Odin’s face, and his body that had been riddled with scars stopped breathing before he could finish the sentence.

        The long-lost peace was restored in the North after the Dragon of Poison had been sealed. Nonetheless, there were still demon intrusions from time to time. In such times, Skuld would put on her armor and hunt down the remnant troopers of demons.

        On the ice field, Skuld swung her giant scissors to dispel the arrows and swords of the demons. Conjuring her godly power, she stamped her foot on the ice, sending lines of flames from the tip of her toe.

        As the scorchingly high temperature broke the ice into pieces, the demons around fell into the water instantly. No one survived—even those who were able to squirm back to the surface of the ice floe could not escape the blade of Skuld.

        Just when Skuld flung off the blood on her scissors, she heard a nerve-racking howl from afar, followed by a colossal dragon shadow flying across the sky. The Dragon of Poison that the North had sealed at the cost of numerous lives was unexpectedly released back into the world…

        The remnants of the demon army secretly broke the Seal of the Dragon of Poison, making it the ultimate weapon to destroy the North. The Dragon of Poison once again brought the realm of humans to its end, with its rotten body and corrosive breath putting the unknowing people of the North to death.

        Only then did Skuld realize that Odin's decision was right—the Dragon of Poison needed to be guarded. Hence, she made up her mind in an instant.

        Skuld called upon all the heroes of the North to stand against the Dragon of Poison again. It was just that years of tranquility had worn their fighting spirit.

        “Since I am the one who cut Odin's thread of life, I shall bear the consequences. Even if it costs everything, I ought to make amends in my own way.”

        Raising her giant scissors, Skuld took the lead to charge at the dragon. Even though her hands were corroded by venom and her scissors cracked, she still stood at the forefront so as to boost morale.

        Under her desperate efforts, they finally sealed the Dragon of Poison back in the magic circle. Just when everyone breathed a sigh of relief, they saw Skuld walking into the Seal alone without a backward glance.

        ‘Skuld! What are you doing?!’ Verthandi exclaimed.

        ‘I shall be bound to the Tower to guard the Dragon of Poison,’ said Skuld, who looked back with determination and resolution.

        ‘You do not have to do this!’ shouted Urd.

        It was the same old conversation in the same situation, just with different people. History always repeats itself.

        Skuld slowly shook her head and replied, ‘This is what it meant to be. Now I am just leading everything back to the right track of fate.’

        And so, everyone in the North could only watch as Skuld gradually disappeared into the Seal…

        “There are always sacrifices and decisions ought to be made in the wheel of fate. Since Odin has made up his mind, I shall respect his wish.”

Yet, she lost her usual composure when it came to Odin—she could not bear to watch this man who had devoted himself completely to the North live in endless suffering. A question kept churning in her mind, “Is he destined for such a tragic life?”

        “A hero deserves to die well.” At such a thought, Skuld defied her father, Mimir’s teaching. She channeled her godly power and thrust her scissors into Odin’s body, cutting the thread of his life.

        ‘Skuld, you——’ Disappointment and sorrow flickered across Odin’s face, and his body that had been riddled with scars stopped breathing before he could finish the sentence.

        The long-lost peace was restored in the North after the Dragon of Poison had been sealed. Nonetheless, there were still demon intrusions from time to time. In such times, Skuld would put on her armor and hunt down the remnant troopers of demons.

        On the ice field, Skuld swung her giant scissors to dispel the arrows and swords of the demons. Conjuring her godly power, she stamped her foot on the ice, sending lines of flames from the tip of her toe.

        As the scorchingly high temperature broke the ice into pieces, the demons around fell into the water instantly. No one survived—even those who were able to squirm back to the surface of the ice floe could not escape the blade of Skuld.

        Just when Skuld flung off the blood on her scissors, she heard a nerve-racking howl from afar, followed by a colossal dragon shadow flying across the sky. The Dragon of Poison that the North had sealed at the cost of numerous lives was unexpectedly released back into the world…

        The remnants of the demon army secretly broke the Seal of the Dragon of Poison, making it the ultimate weapon to destroy the North. The Dragon of Poison once again brought the realm of humans to its end, with its rotten body and corrosive breath putting the unknowing people of the North to death.

        Only then did Skuld realize that Odin's decision was right—the Dragon of Poison needed to be guarded. Hence, she made up her mind in an instant.

        Skuld called upon all the heroes of the North to stand against the Dragon of Poison again. It was just that years of tranquility had worn their fighting spirit.

        “Since I am the one who cut Odin's thread of life, I shall bear the consequences. Even if it costs everything, I ought to make amends in my own way.”

        Raising her giant scissors, Skuld took the lead to charge at the dragon. Even though her hands were corroded by venom and her scissors cracked, she still stood at the forefront so as to boost morale.

        Under her desperate efforts, they finally sealed the Dragon of Poison back in the magic circle. Just when everyone breathed a sigh of relief, they saw Skuld walking into the Seal alone without a backward glance.

        ‘Skuld! What are you doing?!’ Verthandi exclaimed.

        ‘I shall be bound to the Tower to guard the Dragon of Poison,’ said Skuld, who looked back with determination and resolution.

        ‘You do not have to do this!’ shouted Urd.

        It was the same old conversation in the same situation, just with different people. History always repeats itself.

        Skuld slowly shook her head and replied, ‘This is what it meant to be. Now I am just leading everything back to the right track of fate.’

        And so, everyone in the North could only watch as Skuld gradually disappeared into the Seal…

        “Heroes deserve a glorious end, and I will gladly do them the favor even if it means devoting the rest of my life.”
STORY_2779:
Time after time, Verthandi watched as her sisters ran themselves down by sedating the madding Odin in the Tower. She knew that it was their destiny that they could not resist, but it did not stop her empathy toward them.

        Leaning alongside her sisters, she fell into a deep slumber, where the elements showed her an illusion of a different choice she could have made…

        Odin sat under the tree planted by Verthandi, but Verthandi helped him up and put him into the swing she used to play on when she was small. Only through undulation and turbulence could she peek into the fate of a person.

        ‘I know why you are here,’ said Verthandi.

        ‘Then will you promise me?’ asked Odin.

        ‘What do you think?’ Verthandi asked him back with a mischievous grin, shrugging her shoulders.

        With his head hanging low, Odin hesitated for a moment and said, ‘Fighting demons is everybody’s responsibility. This is our only choice!’

        Hearing Odin’s rebuttal, Verthandi suddenly found everything uninteresting. She did not understand why this man in front of her was so stubborn and unashamed to drag other people into his own fate when he knew what waited ahead was nothing but tragedy.

        ‘...No, you cannot make decisions for the others.’

        ‘No, I can’t, but still, I’ll say it—we have to do it. There is no other choice for us!’ Odin lifted his head and said, his eyes blazing with determination and staring at Verthandi provocatively. The smile on her face deepened, yet her heart was somehow moved.

        ‘No, you are wrong. At least I can choose not to thread the needle for you, and they still have a choice to leave you and the North.’ Verthandi hurriedly walked away as she threw away her needle. Looking at her back, Odin heaved a deep sigh resignedly.

        Verthandi thought that everyone might be able to break free from the dreadful web of fate as long as she did not thread the needle for Odin and transfer his power to his fellows, but her choice only brought an even worse future…

        Although the warriors of the North did not get Odin’s godly power, they did not run away from the North but confronted the demons to repel the intruders one after another.

        Blood stained every inch of the land in the North; people dropped like meteors, leaving Odin alone.

        In the face of the mighty army of demons, he raised his spear and charged at his foes alone without saying a word.

        For the overuse of godly power, Odin’s soul was close to being completely devoured. He lost all his emotions without even knowing whether he had fallen into madness. He kept slaying every demon in front of him like a slaughter machine, standing tall and still even after the very last moment when the godly power in his body drained and the fire of his life burned out.

        Even the demons were awed by his dignified posture. They dared not blaspheme his body but only left it standing on the battlefield that was littered with corpses, until one evening when Verthandi came.

        Verthandi, who had always been smiling, now lost her composure; her eyes were filled with grief and sorrow.

        ‘It turns out that you were right. They have been linked to you by the thread of fate all along.’ Verthandi took out her needle and said, ‘As it should be, I, as both the thread and the needle, shall weave the web of fate for you.’

        Wetting the thread, Verthandi passed it through the eye of the needle and pulled. Then, she pierced the needle fiercely into Odin’s body, sewing his fate onto herself.

        Amid the howling wind in the North, she continued to weave silently until the sun sank below the horizon. As she finished weaving, she reached out her blood-stained hands and took the Gungnir out of Odin’s. Then she put on the Armor of Runes and carried on the fate that should have belonged to him…

        “The web of fate is irrevocable. All creatures are powerless before its greatness.”

STORY_2781:
Idun was gradually lost in the eternity of life. Her hourglass had long been full of overflowing memories. Time no longer meant anything to Idun. She was frazzled in the course of subduing the Dragon of Poison in the Tower over and over again. To soothe her, the elements showed her an astonishingly realistic illusion…

        In the past, Idun and Angrboda traveled in search of the golden apple, hoping to protect their fellow folks in times of war with its power. Later, however, Angrboda was put under a curse, so Idun had no choice but to continue the journey alone. And now she was finally back in the North with the power of the golden apple.

        In a snowstorm, Idun knocked on the door of Angrboda’s house, only to see the careworn Loki…

        Loki told her that Angrboda had already died a long time ago because of the curse. Yet, that was not the end of their misfortune—Angrboda’s curse had spread to their daughter, Hel. The girl was skinny and weak; her legs looked like dried branches. It was palpably the consequence of the curse. Looking at Hel, Idun was deeply shocked with tears brimming in her eyes.

        ‘Hel will probably die of the curse like Angrboda in a few days… The only way to save her is to infuse the power of the golden apple into Hel’s body. Did you find the golden apple?’ said Loki in a serious tone, with the last flicker of hope in his eyes.

        At that moment, Idun hesitated. She had always seen Angrboda as her only family and Hel was the only offspring of Angrboda, but the power of the golden apple was still a mystery that she had not fully comprehended.

        Idun dared not risk Hel’s life, nor did she want to. She deeply feared that Hel might die because of the choice she made. Eventually, she succumbed to her fear of uncertainty and chose to lie to Loki.

        ‘...No, I did not. I’m sorry.’

        The light in Loki’s eyes completely faded as he heard Idun.

        Idun walked out of—more precisely, ran away from—Loki’s house. That night, Hel’s condition dramatically worsened. Suffering from the torment of the curse, the girl finally died on her bed, while Loki, the wise man of the North hanged himself under a beam in his house.

        Looking at the two bodies, Idun was stunned and racked by choking sobs, with her heart drowned in remorse and fear.

        From that day on, Idun embarked on a journey to the further depths of the North alone, hoping to live her life incognito in a place where she could run away from everything and the past…

        Without Loki’s wisdom, the North Alliance kept losing ground to the demons. Their leader, Odin, was also seriously wounded in a battle which almost took his life. In order to save the North, Tyr the war deity asked around for the golden apple. After he finally learned the whereabouts of Idun, he took Odin to her place, hoping that she could heal him.

        Looking at Odin, the terribly scarred leader of the North, Idun could not help but feel the bitterness of life. If Odin, who had the Armor of Runes, was even covered in bruises, the ordinary soldiers without godly power could only be worse.

        “Running away does not make my mistakes disappear. The shackles of guilt are still tightly fixed on my limbs, forcing me to confront the malice of fate.”

        Idun finally gave up escaping and took up that heavy wheel of fate.

        “Still, I could not stop myself from falling victim to fate. Just like Odin, we are all nothing but sacrificial lambs.”

        And so, Idun extracted the power of the golden apple and infused it into Odin’s body. The hero of the North was saved, but Idun slowly shrank—her fully grown body turned back into a child’s one in a short moment.

        “Everyone has that moment when fear takes over them, but fate never spares its prey. We are all sacrificial lambs to the world.”

STORY_2783:
Brynhildr was weary of the repeated battles in the Tower. In response to her overtired soul, the elements indulged her with an illusion…

        For the sake of the North, King Budli forwent his claim to his kingdom, making it a line of defense against the demons so that his people could live under the protection of Aesir and the North Alliance.

        ‘But… why us?!’ asked Brynhildr in an anguished voice.

        ‘Because it has to be us,’ Budli answered after a moment of silence.

        ‘But——’

        ‘Enough.’ Budli stood up abruptly. Smoldering resentment and agony flickered across his face, but he soon suppressed those emotions and said, ‘Brynhildr, we must give up our kingdom to survive, so that we can have a future.’

        Seeing her father’s red-rimmed eyes, Brynhildr could not blame him. She knew it would be best for her to leave obediently so her father could retain his pride. However, the churning emotions in her heart froze her legs.

        “Father is right. We need the North Alliance in order for everyone to survive. BUT, there is something more important than our lives, something we can never give up!”
　
        Biting her lips, Brynhildr made up her mind and unsheathed the long sword on her waist.

        ‘Brynhildr! What are you doing?! Put down your sword!’ screamed Budli, trying to halt Brynhildr. The latter did not listen but shook her head.

        ‘Father, I know you. You will definitely stay on the battlefield till the very last moment because running away is never an option for you.’

        ‘...This is not a decision I made alone.’

        ‘No, but you know exactly what will happen if you abandon your homeland—your soul and the ones of our people will die bit by bit. Losing their homes, our people will only end up being enslaved and living in lifelong torment!’

        Budli did not respond, but the swirling grief in his eyes still revealed his true desire.

        ‘Father.’ Brynhildr swung her sword and cut her long hair off her back. She then looked right into her father’s eyes with great valor and determination, and said, ‘I would like to volunteer myself to the battlefield and fight alongside our people to defend our homeland to the end! I am sure that our people will make the same choice as I do. They are no cowards; they sure will not desert their homes to spend the rest of their lives in disgrace!’

        Budli was already wavering and Brynhildr’s words gave him a push to follow his heart. In the end, with his people’s support, he decided to call off the deal with the North Alliance and defend his kingdom.

        However, his kingdom kept losing ground to the powerful demon army, and eventually, the demons pushed into the imperial city. Under the crossing blades of soldiers and demons, the land was soaked in crimson. Amid the deafening screams of slaughter, the military base where Brynhildr and Budli were was besieged by the demon army.

        Swamped by the enemies, the guards all fell, one by one. With King Budli sacrificing himself for his daughter, Brynhildr was left alone in a despairing situation.

        She drew her sword to take down one demon after another until she used up all her strength. Just when she was about to stab herself to end her own life, someone knocked down her sword to the ground. Brynhildr looked back in despair, only to find a young swordsman…

        Riding a horse, Sigurd broke into the demons’ siege alone to save Brynhildr.

        ‘Your Highness, you are safe now.’ Sigurd’s gentle words flowed into Brynhildr’s heart, dispelling her loneliness with a touch of warmth.

        After Sigurd got off the horse and lifted Brynhildr to let her sit on it, he saddled up again and immediately rode away before the demons rushed to attack them.

        Along the way, Brynhildr felt unprecedentedly safe as she put her arms around Sigurd’s sturdy body and listened to his heartbeat. With her stretched nerves being finally relaxed, she could not help but fall asleep.

        When Brynhildr woke up, she had been escorted back to the imperial cityby Sigurd. After that, she promptly called upon the remaining soldiers to guard the city.

        In the days of defending the city together, Brynhildr and Sigurd fell in love with each other and even had a simple wedding. 

        Gazing at Sigurd before the altar, Brynhildr recalled the prophecy Mimir the sage had given her.

        “Princess of the North, please remember that bravery will be at the heart of your husband’s life.  Under the sun, there is no man nobler than him.”

        “You were right. My husband is indeed the bravest and noblest warrior in the world,” Brynhildr thought with a smile, then she kissed Sigurd.

        Soon after their wedding ended, Sigurd put on his armor to banish the invading demons while Brynhildr earnestly issued commands to transport supplies to the frontline.

        Still, their efforts were all in vain before the ceaseless army of demons—the city finally fell.

        ‘It’s time,’ whispered Brynhildr, looking at the flying sparks in the distance.

        ‘Yes, and everyone is ready.’ Reaching out his hand, Sigurd stroked Brynhildr’s cheek and gently wiped the blood from her forehead. Then he said in a soft voice, ‘I will be with you till the very end.’ 

        ‘So do I.’  The two smiled at each other. Without saying another word, they joined hands and headed to the battlefield. Brynhildr and Sigurd did not stop wielding their swords at the demons until the last moments of their lives…

        “Perhaps I have been too vain and obsessed with glory—life shall be the cornerstone of soul.”

STORY_2791:
In order to save Uther, Aria used the power of the holy grail to take the curse into her body. However, the curse was so powerful that even the holy grail could not reverse but only suppress it.

        Under the curse, Aria wandered in between consciousness and slumber from time to time. Thus, she moved to the sanctuary of the royal family and set up an enchantment so as to keep the power of the holy grail from unscrupulous and uninvited guests.

        Even though Aria rarely showed herself in front of the public, her heroic deed in saving Uther had made her the saintess in the kingdom. Throughout all these years, Aria learned to hide her emotions; the more so, the more she became accustomed to the cool and prestigious façade of being the saintess.

        Today was the wedding of King Uther and Aria was cordially asked to be the king’s officiant.

        As Aria watched Uther walk to her with someone’s hand in his, her hands were clenched so tight that they went white behind her back; still, she wore a placid and restrained smile on her face.

        ‘Today’s his wedding, I have to make it perfect.’

        “Your Holiness… Your Holiness?” Seeing the spaced-out Aria before the altar, Uther the groom gave her a gentle reminder with a smile.

        “Cough… Uther Pendragon, do you take her as your lawfully wedded wife? Do you promise to love and cherish her in good times and in bad, in sickness and in health, for richer or poorer, for better for worse, through all the days of your life?”

        At that moment, every word Aria said hurt as if they were being engraved on her bones.

        “I do.” The unhesitant answer of Uther thrust into her heart like an invisible sword.

        Aria could hardly recall what happened next—the only thing she knew was that everyone was smiling so she followed, wearing a smile that was splendidly radiant as if she was hiding something. However, when someone talked to her, she just answered them like a puppet on a string.

        ‘Is it worth it?’ asked the holy grail in her body.
        ‘...It doesn’t matter, as long as he is happy.’
        ‘But what about you?’
        Aria didn’t answer, nor could she.

        After King Uther’s wedding, Aria just lived  blandly in despair as though she had lost all her sparks. It was only when she spied on Arthur with the magic mirror of water while she was awake would she feel a flicker of hope and smile.

        ‘He has recruited many knights. Everyone admires him.’
        ‘His wife gave birth to a girl. She looks very cute, just like him.’
        ‘He…is busy endorsing the documents. Look at him, all frowning. He hated reading the documents back then and he hasn’t changed.’

        Aria thought that these days would go on and she would see Uther age. Never would she have thought that one day she would be awakened by a stab of agonizing pain after years of slumber.

        ‘The curse has grown stronger! Something must have happened!’

        Racked with anxiety, Aria rushed out of the temple and hurried to the palace in spite of everything, only to find the entire palace engulfed by a miasma of black magic.

        Hiding her presence with magic, she went straight to Uther’s bedroom and saw a man— emaciated and scrawny—lying on the bed, who looked completely different from the tall and handsome Uther back in the days.

        Uther was shrouded in the black miasma which was exactly what aggravated the curse on him.

        Looking at Uther’s body contaminated by black magic, Aria—who had not shed a tear after becoming the saintess—broke down in tears which dripped on the face of the sleeping man.

        “I will not let you die! I will protect you no matter what.” As she held out her hand to caress his cheek tenderly, she washed away the black magic on him with the power of the holy grail.

        Yet, the black magic was much stronger than she had imagined. Even Aria used all her power, still, she could not remove all the black magic but only relieve his pain so that he could regain a slight consciousness.

        “Your… Holiness… Take the star stones and leave now… be-before they come back…” As Uther strenuously propped up himself, he took two star stones from a secret shelf beside his bed and put them into Aria’s hands.

        “Your Majesty, don’t you think it’s a bit too late?” A bewitching voice cut in Uther’s words.

        A ravishing woman slowly walked out of a dark corner. She was the wife of Accolon, King Uther’s younger brother—Morgan le Fay.

        “It’s you…” Aria glared at Morgan le Fay.

        “My son can never be the king as long as King Uther is still alive… Hand me the holy grail and I shall spare your life.”

        “Do you really think that I’ll believe you? You’ll kill us the either way… So, NEVER!” A powerful azure light blasted from Aria’s hand.

        Aria channeled all the magic power in her body for one attack—an extremely complicated magic circle appeared beneath her feet with a shivering chill that almost froze the space around her.

        “Everything. FREEZE. NOW!”

        A purple shield appeared before Morgan le Fay. Yet, she still moved a few steps back and hit the wall when the cold light struck against the shield. Just when her shield was about to be shattered——

        A blade flashed—Accolon, the husband of Morgan le Fay, made a stab right at Aria’s flank with a rapier.

        “Die!” Accolon growled with depravity and hatred written all over his face. Controlling the blue light with all her strength, Aria could hardly move so she could only watch as Accolon charged at her with the sword.

        However, someone stood before Aria—it was Uther, who was supposed to be lying on the bed. He threw himself in front of Aria to protect her, just like what he did on that day years ago.

        “Uther! …How dare you hurt him!” Aria’s intense emotions caused a surge in her power. With a great flash of icy light, she blasted Morgan le Fay and Accolon away while holding the fallen Uther in her arms.

        “Wh… Why…” Tears kept falling from Aria’s eyes like a burst dam.

        “Your Holiness? Why… would I feel so familiar seeing this… Oh… Right, now I remember…” Distant memories came flooding back to Uther’s mind, filling in for the loss of his life,.

        “Ha… You’re still such a crybaby… even after all these years.” Uther lifted his hand to wipe away the tears from Aria’s eyes. His words staggered Aria, who said, “You… You remember…”

        Responding her with a nod and a smile, Uther said breathlessly, “Now go… Aria… You can’t defeat them alone… Take the star stones with you…”

        “No! I will never leave you alone!”

        “Your Holiness… Don’t forget… your duty.”

        At that moment, the star stones in Aria’s arms felt like scorching stones.

        “This is my… last wish…”

        Gritting her teeth, Aria looked at the man imploringly as though she was engraving him on her mind. Then, she jumped out of the window and fled.

        “You can’t get away from us!” shouted Morgan le Fay.

        “Aria——” Uther should have something else in his last words; it could have been “I’m sorry” or “I love you”, yet Aria could never know the answer.

        With all her might, Aria fled to the sanctuary and built an extensive enchantment that covered everything around the temple.

        For the promise she had made, the saintess blessed by the holy grail shall wait here for someone who could be entrusted with the star stones…
STORY_2795:
Even since Apollo had taken back Cassandra’s prophetic powers, he never showed himself to her again. Losing her ability to dream the future, Cassandra could only feel a numbing void in her heart that grew bigger day by day. One night, the elements brought Cassandra a vision in her deep slumber…

        ‘Your Highness, I really need this lead dancer position…’ said the female dancer with sobs who knelt before Cassandra. Pursing her lips, Cassandra did not say a word.

        Cassandra knew that the dancer was betrothed to a magnate who was said to have beaten a maid to death. The dancer was terrified, yet the only way out of this betrothal was for her to become the priestess of the God of the Sun, and only by becoming the lead dancer could she get the god’s attention.

        As much as Cassandra wanted to be the lead dancer in the rite to get the blessings from Apollo and become his priestess, she felt the dancer’s desperation. Slowly loosening her clenched fists, she thought to herself, ‘All I have to lose is just a chance to be his priestess, but what she is losing is her whole life.’

        ‘Please stop crying, or else your beauty will be blemished by your puffy eyes when you lead the dance,’ Cassandra said softly, her eyes filled with love and compassion.

        Knowing that Cassandra had agreed to help her, the dancer immediately prostrated herself before the princess with water brimming in her eyes.

        On the day of the rite in admiration of Apollo, Cassandra, the princess of Troy was absent because of sickness while the dancer got her wishes and became the priestess of the God of the Sun.

        Sitting at the bay window in a dim room, Cassandra looked at the temple that was ablaze with lights. A feeling of loss quietly crept up in her heart. Hearing the music outside the window, she could not help but begin dancing alone in the room, only to be discovered by her mother who suddenly pushed open the door.

        Instead of asking Cassandra why she feigned her illness, Cassandra’s mother took her to a masquerade ball, hoping to cheer her up.

        Everyone at the ball was required to wear a mask. However, the crowd of aristocrats somehow only left Cassandra breathless so she went to the garden outside the hall with her mask on instead.

        Cassandra looked up at the moon in the sky. Suddenly, she heard the sound of heavy breathing. Then she was shoved to the ground. Her mask fell off; her knees scraped on the ground which caused a burning pain.

        She turned around, only to find a flushed drunk man lying on her back. As she took a closer look, she recognized that the man was the prince of the neighboring kingdom.

        ‘Hehe, pretty… You’re pretty… Let’s play…’

        ‘Your Highness, please show some respect to yourself and let go of me!’

        ‘So you’re Princess Cassandra, right? I’ll just ask my father to put in a word and make you my wife. That should solve the problem,’ said the prince unashamedly while putting his lips close to Cassandra’s skin. Just as Cassandra was in the depths of despair, a ray of strong light brightened the gloom in the garden and turned into a ball of light that blasted the prince away.

        ‘What a hideous piece of garbage, get out of my sight!’

        It only took one glance for Cassandra to recognize the beautiful man who descended from the air. His dazzling face took her breath away and brought a ray of sunshine to her heart.

        ‘God of the Sun…’ Cassandra immediately prostrated herself before Apollo. Finding Cassandra’s voice familiar, Apollo slowly walked toward her.

        ‘Look up and let me see your face.’ At Apollo’s words, Cassandra slightly lifted her head and looked at him. He immediately recognized those sparkling eyes that had not changed a bit over the years.

        “It’s her?” Apollo recalled that he had once disguised himself as an old ugly man while manipulating demonic beasts to fake an attack in a village so as to test the nature of humans. 

        He thought that no human would put their lives at risk to give him a hand, but a little girl proved him wrong and protected him regardless of her own safety. Now that kind and selfless girl had grown into a beautiful woman, and it tickled Apollo’s heart.

        “Who knows my spontaneous decision of coming to the human ball would lead to a reconnection with the past… Perhaps it’s destiny.” Apollo thought to himself introspectively while extending a hand to Cassandra.

        ‘Cassandra, the princess of Troy, I am here to keep my promise to you. From now on, I shall light up your path, and you shall serve by my side and be my woman.’

        A radiant smile spread across Cassandra’s face. She replied with great respect and sincerity, ‘Dear God, thank you for the gift. It is the highest honor for me to receive such a blessing, to be the priestess of God of the Sun.

        At first, Apollo was stunned by Cassandra’s innocent answer, but he soon let out a sigh of compromise. ‘Well, so be it then.’

        No matter what choice Cassandra made, her unwavering faith would always lead her to the God of the Sun and make her a part of his fate.

        “It’s never the wisest choice to sacrifice oneself for others unconditionally.”

STORY_2797:
In the sheet of flames, Medea was weeping tears alone with a headless corpse in her arms. To mollify her in the depths of despair, the elements created an illusion in which she made another choice and lived a different life…

        Jason won the martial arts tournament and earned the eligibility to marry the princess, Medea. However, the king forcibly imprisoned Jason lest his royal bloodline was contaminated by a peasant. In order to save her lover, Medea planned on a jailbreak, only to be intercepted by the prince, her elder brother.

        ‘Medea Sarmatia!’

        ‘Brother?’

        ‘You really think that you can solve the problem by running away?’ the prince asked coldly.

        ‘Get out of my way!’ Medea uttered a threat to him through clenched teeth, ‘I won’t hold back even if you’re my brother!’

        In order to stop Medea, the prince turned himself into a centaur with the animal morphing magic and charged at her. After a while of tussling, the prince began to be disadvantaged by the unequal powers between him and his sister. Just when Medea was about to throw a fireball at him——

        “After all, he is still my brother by birth. Should I really kill him for love—for Jason?” Medea’s attack paused for a second at such thought. Seizing the moment of advantage, the prince trapped her with magic.

        ‘Dang it! Let go of me!’ Medea struggled in desperation, but to no avail, so she looked at Jason, who was standing aside, and called for help, ‘Jason! Save me!’

        However, instead of helping Medea, the man who had exchanged vows with her just a moment ago wore an awkward expression on his face.

        ‘...I’m sorry, Medea, but I don’t want to die yet.’ Leaving those words, Jason turned around and ran away without a backward glance. At that moment, Medea felt the flames of her dignity had been quenched by cold water along with a biting chill running through her whole body as if she had fallen to the glacier.

        Deeply traumatized, Medea barely had any memory of the things that happened after that, but only a vague one of her brother taking her back to the castle and the enraged king locking her up in the room. Under the king’s order, she was betrothed to the prince of the neighboring kingdom shortly thereafter.

        It was only until the day of Medea’s wedding when she put on an exquisite wedding dress that she truly realized a fact.

        “I have been betrayed and abandoned by my brother, my father, and my lover who said he loved me.” Medea let out a soft sneer. Then she burst into hysterical laughter and lost herself as though she had fallen into utter madness. Due to her indecency, the wedding was put off and she was sent directly to the prince’s bedroom.

        That night, when the prince of the neighboring kingdom came to the room to copulate with her, she did not resist. She just let him play with her body on the bed like a lifeless doll, which bored the prince and resulted in him leaving her for amusement somewhere else.

        Medea’s heart completely sank; even the emotional abuse from her husband could not send a ripple through her. She simply sat by the window and watched as the days went by.

        The maid who followed Medea to the neighboring kingdom could not bear to watch the princess suffer from chronic depression, so she suggested that Medea go out and get some fresh air during the town’s festival.

        “The festival… Right, the first time I met Jason was at the festival…” The sweet memories of the past slightly enlivened Medea. After a short hesitation, she accepted the maid’s suggestion, changed her clothes, and went to the town, roaming around the bustling streets alone.

        Suddenly, someone gripped Medea hard by the wrist. She tried to break away, but her body froze when she heard that familiar voice.

        ‘Medea! I… I finally found you!’ Even though it had been years since the last time the two saw each other, Jason’s face still looked attractive. The traces of time only served to make him more charming and magnetic than before, which gave Medea a bitter-sweet ache in her heart.

        However, rage passed through her body when she recalled the sight of him leaving her alone and fleeing. Hence, she raised her other hand and gave him a sharp slap with so much strength that even stung her palm.

        ‘How dare you show your face to me again!’ Medea said with a heavy note of sarcasm, turning a frigid gaze on him.

        ‘I was wrong!’ Jason did not slacken his grip on Medea’s hand despite the slap but only tightened it. With guilt and remorse shimmering in his deep eyes, he looked perfectly genuine and he said, ‘I was too weak back then. I was afraid that I would be executed if the prince caught me and that would mean I could never see you again!’

        Jason’s word melted Medea’s heart. The churning agony and regret in her heart made her lost for words. She only began to speak after a while with a softer tone, ‘...What's done is done. We can never go back to the way we used to be, so I don’t want to see you again. Let me go.’

        ‘No, I won’t!’ Jason could tell that Medea was wavering, so he forcibly drew Medea into her arms and held her tightly.

        ‘What are you doing?!’ Flushing with embarrassment and anger, Medea raised her hand as if to cast a magic spell. ‘I will burn you to ashes!’

        ‘Then burn me! I’ll gladly take the punishment if that makes you happy!’

        ‘You——’

        ‘I love you, Medea.’ Jason looked Medea deeply in the eye. Tears fell off his eyes that were brimming with great affection.

        Medea could not help but indulge herself in his eyes. She knew that she lost again—she lost to love again. She rested her head on Jason’s shoulder; her tears wetted his clothes. Then she whispered with a choked sob, ‘Don’t… leave me again this time…’

        Jason’s vehement confession rekindled their love and the two began to meet secretly in the town. With the nourishment of love, Medea regained the confidence and grace she had had as the “Kolchis” in the past.

        Unfortunately, no secret can remain hidden forever. Their love affair eventually reached the prince’s ears, and they were caught on the spot in one of their secret meetings.

        ‘How dare you cheat on me! Catch this tramp for me!’ The prince commanded the soldiers bitterly to besiege Medea and Jason.

        Just when Medea was racking her brain to find a way to break away, out of the blue, Jason pushed her toward the soldiers. Her left eye coincidentally hit the sword of a soldier and blood splattered. While everyone was stunned by this accident, Jason took the opportunity to run out of the door.

        “You made a promise that you wouldn’t leave me again… Jason... How many times are you going to lie to me… So all those words of love were nothing but a lie?” Covering her bleeding right eye, Medea curled her lips and let out a short laugh, then she exploded with hysterical laughter again just like the time she did at her wedding.

        “I won’t let you get away this time!”

        Putting a hand on her left chest, Medea summoned a fire drakon at the expense of her own heart. As the drakon spewed inextinguishable flames, the fire immediately spread across the land and engulfed everything, including the building, the soldiers and the prince, turning all of them into ephemeral blossoms of bright flares.

        ‘What a loathsome world. I shall burn it all down and purge all the betrayals and pains…’ Leaning against a wall, Medea looked up at the sky that had turned an apocalyptic shade of red because of the fire, then she slowly closed her eyes…

        “This is my life, so I will ruthlessly eradicate all the obstacles even if it means my brother”

STORY_2799:
Since Circe had obtained the texts of magic from the foreign Ithaca tribe, she had immersed herself completely in them all day long until she tired herself out and fell asleep on the desk. In her dream, the elements showed her an illusion of another choice she could have made…

        Circe was completely heartbroken after learning that her daughter killed her own brother, and she put all the blame on the king. Sitting on the throne, Circe looked at the scowling king and felt an inciting hatred flare up inside her, yet she paused at the silver glint on her hand.

        As Circe lowered her head and saw the shining ring on her left hand, she recalled the vow she and the king had made on the day of their wedding as well as the sweet days after that and the peaceful moments of them taking care of their children together… Every bit and piece of the past melted the sudden fit of rage inside her.

        “Even though he has made mistakes, he is still my husband whom I have spent years with. I can’t do this… Forget it. The most important thing now is to find our daughter.” So Circe gave up the idea of poisoning the king and chose to run away to find Medea, her daughter alone instead.

        However, never would have Circe known that the king had no thought of sparing her despite her mercy on him. The king was enraged when he knew that Circe had run away, thus he sent troops to search for her and soon found her.

        The king set off with his soldiers in pursuit of Circe as soon as he learned Circe’s whereabouts, and he finally intercepted her in a forest.

        ‘Go back with me now, and I can pretend that nothing happened,’ the king commanded egotistically, with his chin raised in a proud gesture.

        Circe looked at her husband who had not shown a sign of remorse; her heart was as calm as a stagnant pond. Then she said indifferently, ‘There is no way back between you and me. It is best for us to part.’

        ‘Circe! So even you are going to betray me! Fine… Great! If that’s so, then don’t blame me for this!’ With his eyes filled with resentment, the king waved his hand and gave an order, ‘Knights! Queen Circe has turned her back on our kingdom! And now it is my decree that she shall be executed immediately!’

        At the king’s order, all the knights unsheathed their swords. The cold glint of their blades froze Circe’s heart.

        While the knights charged at Circe, the latter opened her arms with her mouth chanting. A flash of green light emerged and the earth shook. Then countless tree roots sprouted from every corner of the forest and attacked the knights like snakes, hanging hundreds of them in the air in a second.

        When Circe was about to turn around and leave, the king hurled the long sword in his hand with all his strength, which ripped through the air, aiming at her throat——

        Just then, a spear suddenly darted at the sword. Sparks flew, and the sword thrust into the ground.

        Malphas the demonic spirit slowly descended from the sky and stood beside Circe, warning her, ‘You must never let your guard down, my Lord.’

        ‘Malphas, what are you doing here?’ Circe was surprised. In the past, she set Malphas free despite the backlash of the pact so that he could escape from the king’s torture. She never thought that he would come back.

        ‘You’re still my master even without the pact. As your demonic spirit, of course, I have the responsibility to protect you when I know you’re being hunted by that idiot king.’

        ‘Thank you.’ Circe gratefully thanked Malphas with a nod. When she looked back at the king, the latter’s face had already twisted into a frigid grimace. She then slowly walked to the king and looked down at him. The love, kindness and forbearance she once had were now completely gone.

        ‘Your Majesty, I was going to spare your life, considering all those years of our marriage, yet you just keep getting on my nerves, so foolishly…’ Pulling the sword out of the ground, Circe controlled the tree roots to tie the king up and hang him high in the air like crucifixion. The king struggled to break away from the tree roots but their grip only got tighter.

        ‘I-I was wrong… Please—— Argh!’ The king did not get the chance to finish his sentence—Circe stabbed at his throat with the sword. Her eyes narrowed, exuding a compelling aura.

        ‘It’s too late for repentance, your Majesty,’ Circe whispered softly. Just like that, the king breathed his last with his eyes widened and bitter resentment.

        “He doesn’t deserve to be the king. If that be so, I shall take his place.”

        And so, Circe returned to the palace with Malphas. She used his power to clear all the opposing voices in the kingdom and became the queen of Sarmatia. Then, she even took control of the 72 demonic spirits one after another with overpowering magic and stratagem, and eventually became the master of all demonic spirits…

        “Humans never change, and thus I shall never show leniency for my personal feelings.’

STORY_2801:
In a secluded forest, Katherin was practicing the painting magic her master had taught her. Filling her pen with runic power, she drew a few birds on a piece of white paper. Then as white light emitted from the paper, all the birds came to life and flew around her, making her chuckle. After a while, they disappeared into the air.

        “I wonder how many kinds of birds there are in this world.”

        Just then, Katherin heard the sound of crackling leaves. She was so frightened that she hid behind a tree, only to see a young man in armor walking into the forest alone. Her brows drew together in a frown as she noticed the sword sheathed on the man’s waist.

        In years of continuous wars, Katherin’s family—like most people on the continent—was caught in the wave. She was found by her current master, the Forest Witch, when she was still a baby. Under the witch’s nurture, she grew up studying the art of painting magic. Every once in a while, however, someone would break into the forest and disturb their lives. Some broke in by mistake while some came with malice, but either way, they were all banished by the Forest Witch.

        ‘This man came to the forest fully armed, he must be up to no good! Let me rout this intruder out of the forest!’ Katherin thought. As she drew on the paper, several beasts came to life and pounced on the young man.

        Katherin thought that she would see the young man being chased away by the beasts embarrassingly, but instead, she only heard a swish—the young man pulled out the sword on his waist. As his blades flashed like lightning, he defeated the beasts that Katherin had created one by one with a few swings.

        Just when Katherin was dumbfounded, mouth agape, by his sword techniques, the latter dashed to her in the blink of an eye after a hard kick on the ground. With his sword pointing at Katherin, the cold gleam of the blade stunned her.

        Only then did the young man find that the person hiding in the dark was a teenage girl. When he was about to retract his sword, a blast of strong wind blew him away. It was the Forest Witch, who descended from the sky riding a giant eagle.

        “Who are you? What are you doing in this forest?” The Forest Witch asked coldly as she stood in front of Katherin while pointing her staff at the young man.

        Seeing that, the young man immediately sheathed his sword. Making a deep bow to the witch, he said sincerely, “The Forest Witch, your mightiness, please forgive me for my insolence. My name is Nathaniel. We need your power to defeat those repulsive demons! Please help us to free the innocent people from this scourge of never-ending wars and end it once and for all!”

        However, the Forest Witch decisively turned down Nathaniel’s invitation and said, “No, I will not leave this forest and I hold no interest in the outside world. So leave, now.”

        The Forest Witch turned around and walked away. As much as Nathaniel wanted to catch up with her, his leg was held down by the tree roots that the witch had summoned with magic. Disheartened, he could only cut off the roots and left after a while.

        ‘The outside world…’ Katherine fell into contemplation. For she had never left the forest ever since she could remember, she basically knew nothing about the outside world so she could not help but begin to imagine.

        Curious about what the outside world looked like, Katherine chose to jump on the tree and follow Nathaniel. Unexpectedly, Nathaniel suddenly turned around and shot a leaf that whistled past Katherin’s ear. He was only trying to prank her but did not expect her to be so startled that she would fall from the tree.

        “Are you alright?” Nathaniel hurriedly went to Katherine. He nervously bandaged her wound as soon as he saw her knees bleeding from the fall.

        “I’m so sorry for pointing my sword at you just now and causing your injury. Here, take these cookies as a gift of my apology.” Nathaniel took out a small bag from his chest and gave it to Katherin. As the latter carefully took one of the cookies and took a bite, the crispy texture made her eyes light up.

        “These cookies are delicious! They must be expensive.”

        “There are many other kinds of desserts. These are all the specialties of my hometown.” Nathaniel’s gaze softened a lot when he talked about his hometown, which made Katherin begin to wonder what kind of place it was.

        “It must be a very nice place.”

        “Yeah, we’ve got magnificent rivers and mountains, a vast meadow, and golden paddy fields…”

        Different kinds of unseen scenery appeared in Katherin’s head as Nathaniel continued to describe his hometown, which only deepened her fascination with the outside world. Just when Katherin was almost intoxicated by what Nathaniel was depicting, his tone suddenly changed.

        “But now the demons have almost taken everything from us. That’s why I came here for the Forest Witch, hoping she could help us. Unfortunately… She has already shot me down.”

        “So what are you going to do now?”

        “I’m planning to find someone strong to join our team. Speaking of someone strong… Oh right, as the disciple of the witch, would you like to join us?”

        “Me? I… How can I? I’m not strong enough to join you.” Katherin lowered her head, yet Nathaniel still caught the gleam of uncertainty in her eyes.

        “Well… If you change your mind, come find me at the camp outside the forest tomorrow morning. As for your ability and strength, I think you’re already qualified to join us.” Nathaniel turned around and left soon after he said those words without giving Katherin a chance to respond.

        On that night, no matter how hard Katherin tried, she just could not push Nathaniel’s words out of her mind. Her curiosity about the outside world kept her awake the whole night and it was only until dawn did she realize what she truly desired.

        So she discreetly packed her bag. Just when she was about to open the door after leaving a farewell letter, a cold voice sounded behind her.

        “Where are you going?”

        “Ma-ma-master!” Katherin frantically lifted her head, only to find that her master was not as angry as she had expected. She seemed nonchalant as if she had known that Katherin would leave.

        “I… wish to see the world.”

        “The outside world is full of dangers. I can no longer protect you and you’ll have to live on your own once you step out of the forest. Do you understand?”

        “Yes, I know, but still, I want to go out and see. I have this feeling that there is something I can only understand after seeing the world outside, and only by doing so will my painting skill be improved,” said Katherin determinedly.

        “Since you have made up your mind, I shall not stop you. Take this with you.” The Forest Witch tossed Katherin a pen that held magic power with starry sparkles.

        “Thank you, Master!”

        After giving the Forest Witch a big hug, Katherine walked out of the forest and went to Nathaniel in the pleasant sunlight.
STORY_2802:
After bidding Nello farewell, the Merry Puppy and Grumpy Puppy stayed on the knoll. They did not feel different for the first two days, but the two began to miss Nello more and more day after day.

        Lying down on the grass, Merry and Grumpy were gazing upon the sky. Just then, a cloud drifted across.

        “Hey, Grumpy, does that cloud look like Nello to you?” Merry whimpered gloomily.

        “No,” Grumpy answered placidly. No matter how hard Grumpy tried to use its imagination, the cloud still looked nothing like Nello except for its roundness which was similar to his head.

        “But it just looks like Nello to me, and now everything just looks like him… Grumpy, what should I do? I miss him so much. Do you miss him? If you do, how about we——”

        “How about we go find him together? That’s what you wanted to say, right? But we don’t know where he is. Where are you even going to start?” Grumpy saw through Merry at a glance and ruthlessly cut the latter off.

        “We-we can just go out and take a look first. Maybe we can smell him as soon as we leave the knoll.” Merry tried to defend itself, but deep down it knew that Grumpy was right.

        “I think you’re more likely to get lost first.”

        “What?! That’s not true!” Merry barked bitterly and pouted, facing away from Grumpy. Seeing that, Grumpy tried to mollify Merry by giving the latter a gentle push with its paw.

        Merry did not turn around at the first and second push but only at the third. ‘What is it? Are you coming with me to find Nello?’

        “No,” Grumpy shook its head and paused before it continued, ‘Do you have any idea of what to give as a gift?’

        “Umm… The fruits on the trees on the eastern hill are big and juicy. They should be ripe by now. They must taste very good…”

        The thought of juicy fruits made Merry salivate. It was not until Grumpy had left for a while that it came back to its senses. “Wait, why did Grumpy ask me that?”

        So the puzzled Merry tracked Grumpy’s scent, only to find that the latter went toward a forest it had never been to after plucking a fruit. It then kept following Grumpy, only by doing so that it could keep itself from getting lost.

        Soon, Grumpy stopped in front of a cottage. Carrying the fruit in its mouth, it knocked at the wooden door with its paw. Then a smiley female dog with soft hair and tender eyes showed up and welcomed Grumpy into the house.

        ‘Wh-wh-what the heck?! Grumpy has found a mate?!’ Thunderstruck by what it saw, Merry unwittingly began to wander in the forest in complete perplexity.

        Suddenly, rain started to pour. As Merry’s hair was drenched in the rain, it finally came to its senses and found itself lost in the woods.

        What was even worse was that the rain had washed away Grumpy’s scent and it could not find its way back by smell. A sense of frustration began to well up at the thought of the current despairing situation it was in.

        “Now that Nello is gone and Grumpy has a mate, I’m just a forlorn dog that nobody cares! Boohoo!” wailed Merry, without noticing a paw on its shoulder which jolted it into a jump. It then looked back, only to see Grumpy looking at it resignedly.

        “What are you doing here? …Were you following me?”

        “Yeah. I would never know that you have been keeping a secret from me if I didn’t.”

        “A secret? What am I keeping from you?”

        “Stop the act. I saw it. Your mate was beautiful.” Merry wiped its tears and smiled at Grumpy, yet its tail was hanging low.

        “A mate?” Grumpy frowned, not knowing what Merry was talking about. It only dawned on it after pondering for a while. “Oh, you saw that.”

        “Yeah. Don’t worry. I’ll take care of myself. You can just stay with your mate—— Ouch! That hurts! What’s that for?!”

        “For what an idiot you are! There was nothing between me and that female dog. I was asking it for information.”

        “Huh? Information for what?” asked Merry curiously while rubbing the bump on its throbbing head.

        “You said you wanna find Nello, so I went to gather information regarding his whereabouts. You aren’t expecting us to roam around the world to find him, are you? That was an informant dog!”

        ‘“Aww, Grumpy! I’m sorry for misjudging you!” Merry howled in excitement, raising its head up high. After circling around Grumpy for a while, it pounced on the latter with its tail wagging in delight.

        “Sigh. Stop it. Hurry up and get packed. We’re leaving tomorrow.”

        “Okay!” Merry followed Grumpy closely, sticking together just like the day when they were born…
STORY_2803:
With Apollo’s endorsement, Andromeda and Hercules had an audience with Aether, who granted them the power of astralists. After that, they were commissioned to carry out different missions in places of Tarones. It was not until the Summoners and the Zodiacs broke into the realm of gods that they were summoned by Apollo in an emergency.

        “Andromeda, Giemsa has betrayed us and fled. Take Hercules and a batch of god soldiers with you to search around the entrance, and be sure to capture her!” Apollo gave the order in a deep voice.

        “Don’t worry. I will definitely bring her back to you.’ Andromeda walked to Apollo, reaching out her hand to gently rub his furrowed brow. “So stop frowning.”

        “Mm.” As Apollo looked at Andromeda, his stretched nerves were slightly relieved. He then took Andromeda’s hand and gave her a word of warning tenderly, “Giemsa has a highly experienced constellation with her, so please be careful.”

        ‘That’s great. Then I can avenge Perseus’ death.’ Andromeda, who had obtained the astralist power, thought to herself confidently. Little did she know that what awaited her would be a quirk of fate—she saw Perseus, her young love whom she thought had been dead!

        The two met again at a ruin at the entrance to the realm of gods when Andromeda was searching for Giemsa with Hercules and the other god soldiers. Just then, Andromeda caught a glimpse of a flashing shadow so she promptly chased after it, only to find that the figure looked uncannily familiar.

        It was only when the man turned around and Andromeda saw his familiar face that she believed she was not having hallucinations.

        “Perseus! You…are alive! Thank god… Boohoo.” With her eyes filled with sudden tears of joy, Andromeda was too overwhelmed to notice the less joyous look on Perseus’ face. Just when she wanted to run into his arms, Hercules grabbed her by the wrist and stopped her.

        “Herc, why are you stopping me?” As much as Andromeda wanted to free herself from Hercules’ grip, the latter held her hand even tighter. She then asked him in bewilderment, “What is it with that sullen look on your face? Aren’t you happy to see Perseus alive?”

        “Didn’t you see?” Hercules stared at the person behind Perseus. Andromeda followed the direction of his gaze and found a woman hiding behind Perseus.

        “That is Giemsa…” A ripple of disquiet spread across Andromeda’s heart. Yet, she still tried to make excuses for Perseus and talked to him with a smile, “Perseus, I know that you must have captured her since you knew her disloyalty. That’s excellent. Master Apollo has sent us to capture her, so hand her over to us. Master Apollo will surely reward you justly.”

        Instead of answering Andromeda, Perseus looked at the circle of god soldiers around him more vigilantly, as if he was looking for an escape route. 

        “Perseus! Please!” Without getting any response from him, Andromeda began to beg anxiously.

        “...I’m sorry.” However, Perseus’ words shattered her hope. At a loss for words, she could only let tears brim in her eyes.

        On the contrary, Hercules, who was standing aside, was not much surprised. Looking at Perseus, he calmly said, “Then don’t blame me for this.”

        Then he kicked his foot, raised his fist and charged at Perseus. Even though Perseus vigilantly lifted his arms to block the attack, he was still knocked a few steps back. Meanwhile, Hercules seized the moment to press home his advantage, leading to a neck and neck fight for a while.

        ‘Why…Perseus and Hercules are best friends. Why are they fighting against each other now?’

        Seeing as Perseus clashed with Hercules, Andromeda felt like her heart had been torn into pieces. Anger and resentment flared up within her. With no place to vent her rising emotions, she could only glare at Giemsa while placing the blame on her, “It’s you! You must have beguiled Perseus! You are not getting away with this!”

        With the power of astralists, Andromeda conjured a giant water ball to attack Giemsa. The latter promptly created a shield with a wave of her hand to protect herself. While the water ball fell on the shield and spattered into countless water drops, Giemsa remained uninjured inside it.

        “Darn it!” Andromeda resentfully gritted her teeth. Then she raised her hand to signal the god soldiers behind her, giving a command aloud, “Soldiers, attack!”

        All the soldiers began to attack Giemsa’s shield. Even though each of their attacks was weak—many a little makes a mickle—they managed to weaken the shield over time.

        “Perseus will regain his sanity soon after I defeat her!” Andromeda naively thought. To make her wish come true, she channeled her astralist power again and conjured numerous ice spikes over Giemsa’s head. As she swung her arms down, the spikes fell down on Giemsa with immense killing intent.

        With a clatter, Giemsa’s shield was finally shattered.

        “Cough!” Giemsa coughed up blood as her power backfired on her. Kneeling on the ground feebly, she lifted her head to look at Andromeda, who had walked to her front.

        “As long as you are gone, Perseus will come back to me, so…” With a blade made of water elements in her hand, Andromeda’s appealing face was distorted by an inexplicable sense of paranoia along with an unusual madness. Then she continued, “Please DIE!”

        She abruptly slashed the blade at Giemsa, yet a long sword cut in horizontally and knocked the blade out of her hand. As the water blade flew past Andromeda and cut her wrist, blood began to gush out, followed by a sharp pain shooting through her. However, that pain was nothing compared to one in her heart.

        Andromeda looked at Perseus in shock. Even though the latter was covered in blood after defeating Hercules, he still managed to save Giemsa with the little strength he had left. Alert and defensive, he looked at Andromeda in a completely different way from the past, which eventually turned the shock inside Andromeda into a bitter chill as cold as the winter snow.

        Andromeda’s head was buzzing. Her mind was flooded by the memories of her and Perseus: he stood up for her when she was bullied by the other dancers; he cheered for her when she shone brightly on stage. He was always there with her, supporting and protecting her. She thought that she held a special place in his heart. What had happened to all those beautiful moments? What had turned them into irretrievable memories that seemed to be only fading away?

        “You used to take care of me in every possible way. You couldn’t even bear to see a wound on me, but why…” Andromeda sobbed with agony with tears falling from her eyes, “How could you hurt me so ruthlessly now… My heart is aching… and I feel so hurt… Why… Tell me why!”

        “...Because this is the justice I have to uphold.” After gazing at Andromeda deeply for a moment, Perseus then helped Giemsa up and walked in another direction while screening her with his body.

        Andromeda lifted her hand to aim at Perseus, but it took forever for her to launch an attack. In the end, she just watched as the two figures disappeared into the gate of the realm of gods…

        ‘Still, I can’t bear to hurt you even though you’ve gone the opposite way to me…’
STORY_2804:
After seeing the unpardonable tyranny and depravity of gods, Perseus chose to turn his back on his kind and embark on a journey of escape in the Tarones until he met Giemsa, who saw his dedication to justice and gave him the astralist power, guiding him to help the Zodiacs.

        However, Zeus, who noticed Giemsa’s plan, came in the way. Luckily, Perseus and Giemsa were able to move on thanks to the help of Orlos, one of the Mach-Forces.

        On the way, yet, they met a troop of god soldiers in a ruin. What shocked Perseus even more was that the love of his life and his friend—Andromeda and Hercules—were the ones leading the troop.

        ‘Perseus! You…are alive! Thank god… Boohoo.’ While Andromeda was weeping tears of joy, Perseus was having extremely mixed feelings.

        “They must be here to arrest Giemsa. I must not hand her over to them, but I don’t want to fight against them either… What should I do?”

        Without knowing how ambivalent Perseus was feeling, Andromeda wanted to run into his arms but Hercules stopped her by grabbing her by the wrist.

        ‘Herc, why are you stopping me?’ As much as Andromeda wanted to free herself from Hercules’ grip, the latter held her hand even tighter. She then asked him in bewilderment, ‘What is it with that sullen look on your face? Aren’t you happy to see Perseus alive?’

        ‘Didn’t you see?’ Hercules stared at the person behind Perseus.

        “..He saw. I knew I couldn’t keep her long from Hercules.” As Perseus knew that his attempt to hide Giemsa was of no avail, he stopped doing so.

        ‘That is Giemsa…’ A ripple of disquiet spread across Andromeda’s heart. Yet, she still tried to make excuses for Perseus and talked to him with a smile, ‘Perseus, you must have captured her since you knew her disloyalty. That’s excellent. Master Apollo has sent us to capture her, so hand her over. I’m sure that Master Apollo will reward you justly.’

        Instead of answering Andromeda, Perseus looked at the circle of god soldiers around him more vigilantly, as if he was looking for an escape route. 

        ‘Perseus! Please!’ Without getting any response from him, Andromeda began to beg anxiously.

        Seeing Andromeda in agony, Perseus could feel a lump in his throat. Still, he swallowed all the bitterness and anguish, and said with a deeper voice than usual, ‘...I’m sorry.’ 

        The bright eyes of Andromeda dimmed and tears began to well up. On the contrary, Hercules, who was standing aside, was not much surprised. Looking at Perseus, he calmly said, ‘Then don’t blame me for this.’

        Hercules kicked his foot and raised his fist to punch Perseus. Even though Perseus vigilantly lifted his arms to block the attack, he was still knocked a few steps back. Seizing the moment to press home his advantage, Hercules lifted his legs to give Perseus a hefty kick.

        Just when Hercules’ kick was about to land on Perseus, the latter did a backflip and dodged it, which led him away from Giemsa. Sensing Hercules’ purpose, Perseus tried to run back to her immediately but Hercules blocked his way.

        ‘Do you really think you still have the time to care about someone else?!’ With a roar, Hercules summoned his astralist power that draped over his fists and turned into a pair of glowing gauntlets. Then he threw a spate of powerful jabs at Perseus.

        Bang! Hercules’s punches landed on Perseus’ crossed arms before his head with such brute force that even paralyzed his arms for a moment.

        “His power has grown much stronger than before. My arms would have been fractured if I didn’t guard with my astralist power. But I won’t stay beaten!” Perseus suddenly lowered his body and swept his leg at Hercules. However, his opponent seemed to have expected his attack—Hercules forcibly took the attack while keeping his footwork as steady as a mountain.

v‘You can’t beat me in strength! Ha!’ With a twist of his waist, Hercules swung a right punch at Perseus and hit his shoulder. Unable to dodge the attack, Perseus was knocked flying and fell to the ground after leaving a trajectory in the air.

        As Perseus struggled to stand up, a metallic taste suddenly welled up in his throat and turned into a cough of blood. However, instead of smiling with victory, Hercules’ face darkened even though his punch landed successfully.

        ‘Why didn’t you draw your sword?’ Hercules questioned Perseus, squinting his eyes.

        ‘...It’s none of your business.’ Perseus refused to answer the question, yet his averted gaze confirmed Hercules’ suspicion.

‘Are you going easy on me?’ Hercules sneered, ‘Stop it. You have become our enemy since the moment you refused to turn Giemsa in, and you should never show mercy to your enemy. Or is it that you don’t think I’m qualified to be your enemy?’

        ‘No, it’s not that…’ Perseus closed his eyes and thought to himself, “Yeah, he’s right. Since I have made my choice, I should no longer hesitate as it would be nothing but an insult to me and Giemsa as well as to Hercules and Andromeda.”

        When Perseus opened his eyes, the perplexity and uneasiness inside them were gone and replaced by conviction. As he unsheathed the long sword on his waist and summoned his astralist power, scorching flames spread on his blade with thriving vitality.

        ‘Come.’ As soon as Perseus looked at Hercules, the latter immediately knew that he was going to end the fight with this final blow. So Hercules returned him a smile while conjuring his astralist power that made the gauntlets on his fists shine even brighter.

        The next second, the two flexed their legs and charged at each other at the same time——Boom! The clash of powers brought a wave of booming sound and stirred up a cloud of sand and dust.

        Everything became blurry for a while; only two standing figures could be vaguely seen. A moment later, the slightly burlier one fell forward while the thinner one dropped to his knee.

        ‘...I lost… Go… My brother…’ Hercules passed out soon after he finished speaking. Perseus was overwhelmed by mixed emotions, but a male voice suddenly pierced through his head before he could sort out his feelings.

        “Protect her!” Filled with anxiety and impatience, the voice shouted, “Protect Giemsa!”

        Enduring the pain, Perseus abruptly stood up and looked in Giemsa’s direction, only to find that the latter was kneeling on the ground with blood seeping from the corner of her mouth, while Andromeda walked to her and raised the water blade in her hands——

        “No! NO!” Like a shooting arrow, Perseus dashed toward Giemsa while brandishing his sword horizontally.

        The sword knocked the water blade away, which cut Andromeda’s wrist as it flew past her. Blood gushed out with a dreadfully vivid red that pierced into Perseus’ eyes and gave him a terrible squeeze in the heart.

        ‘You used to take care of me in every possible way. You couldn’t even bear to see a wound on me, but why…’ Andromeda sobbed with agony and tears falling from her eyes, ‘How could you hurt me so ruthlessly now… My heart is aching… and I feel so hurt… Why… Tell me why!’

        “Yeah, we can never go back to the old days. No matter how my heart aches, she will always be my enemy.” Perseus could feel a throbbing ache in his chest, but instead of groaning in pain, he took a deep breath and said in a low voice, ‘...Because this is the justice I have to uphold.’

        After gazing at Andromeda deeply for a moment, Perseus then helped Giemsa up and walked in another direction. However, the moment he turned around, he failed to hold back the grief in his heart which turned into scorching tears that rolled out of the corners of his red-brimmed eyes. But even so, it still did not stop his steps forward…

        “I will still keep my faith even if that means I have to go against the one I love.”
STORY_2805:
Lyra, the constellation who had acquired the chaotic power, ran into the battlefield between the gods and the Zodiacs and vowed to take revenge on her former owner—Persephone, the Court of Virgo. A pitched battle broke out between the two. Lyra thought that Persephone had forgotten her; to her surprise, the latter recognized her at the very last minute.

        A huge crack appeared on the ground, slowly moving Lyra and Persephone apart to the sides. The pillars around them kept crumbling one after another. Judging that the situation had become perilous, Armstrong promptly carried Persephone in his arms, trying to take her away from the battlefield. However, Persephone broke away from his arms and dashed toward Lyra as fast as she could.

        ‘Lyra!’

        Watching as Persephone ran toward herself while jumping over the crack, Lyra could not help but feel dazed. Yet, a beguiling voice sounded in her head, “Didn’t you always want to kill her? Now it’s the best chance! Despite all the effort you had taken to protect her, she left you behind alone for many years, remember?” 

        Induced by the strange voice in her head, Lyra ruthlessly lifted her hands, her palms facing Persephone with a threatening ball of intertwined purple and golden light coalescing in the middle.

        ‘Persephone! Watch out!’ Armstrong warned Persephone, who did not seem to hear him.

        “Shouldn’t she be afraid that I will kill her?” The closer Persephone came to her unguardedly, the more flustered Lyra felt. In the end, she did not get the chance to launch the attack as she fell into Persephone’s arms.

        The warm embrace brought tears to Lyra’s eyes. With Persephone’s tenderness melting her frozen heart, her true emotions eventually broke the wall and turned into the most authentic words that had been long buried in her heart, ‘I have been waiting for you. I kept telling myself that you would never abandon me, but when I finally saw you again, you told me you didn’t know me, and that breaks my heart so, so badly.’

        ‘I’m sorry, Lyra. It’s all my fault. I didn’t know back then.’ Persephone held Lyra tighter. With guilt and remorse spreading over her pretty face, she said with a choked sob, ‘I am so sorry for keeping you waiting. I will never leave you again.’

        ‘That’s all I want, just staying with you forever——’ Suddenly, a wormhole appeared in the air and interrupted Lyra’s words— a hand stretched out from the wormhole. Then the purple mist at its fingertip turned into a monstrous bird that swooped down on Persephone with tremendous power.

        ‘Look out!’ At the moment of peril, Lyra blocked the attack without a second thought, just like back in the days when she did everything to protect Persephone.

        As the monstrous bird slammed into Lyra’s chest, it disappeared into her body and started a wanton and dominating rampage inside her, bringing her excruciating pain as if her body was torn apart.

        ‘AHHHHHH——!’ Lyra let out a shrill scream in pain.

        ‘Lyra!’ Persephone wanted to hold Lyra but the latter pushed her away.

        ‘Go… Go… NOW!’ Lyra shouted in agony. Meanwhile, a dense purple mist closed in and shrouded her body.

        Persephone shook her head and said determinedly, ‘No, I’ve said it. I will never leave you again!’

        With a wave of Persephone’s right hand, a scythe-shaped harp appeared in her hand. Summoning her astralist power, she nimbly plucked the strings. The sound of the harp then turned into beams of dazzling golden light that shot at the purple mist around Lyra and purified it.

        The war-scarred ground and walls continued to crumble and fall apart at the clash of powers. Even so, Persephone did not waver but kept playing the melodious tune unremittingly.

        Seeing the determination in Persephone’s eyes, Armstrong quietly blasted the fallen pillars away from her so that she could continue to play the harp.

        By then, Lyra had already floated into the air. With her body cloaked in the purple mist, she looked like a purple cocoon from a distance. The chaotic power was gnawing away at her mind along with her emotions and memories, taking away all the precious pieces of the past from her and sapping her strength. She could hardly do anything but fell into the bottomless darkness…

        ——Twangle.

        Like a pebble that was thrown into a placid lake, the refreshing sound of the harp aroused Lyra’s tumultuous mind. As Lyra opened her eyes, she saw a thread of golding light shining in the boundless darkness. It was the same color as her favorite master’s hair.

        “...We shall stay together forever.” The maiden’s soothing voice echoed in the world of chaos, bringing power to Lyra.
