        “Yeah, we made a promise that we will stay together forever.” Lyra abruptly opened her eyes wide and unlocked the astralist power inside her. “So I can’t be devoured! I don’t want to disappear!”

        The golden light bloomed in Lyra’s body, shining through the cocoon of purple mist. The next moment, a pair of magnificent wings of light broke the cocoon and spread majestically, dispelling all the ominous purple mist.

        Flapping her wings, Lyra flew to Persephone and Armstrong. As she landed gracefully, she was drawn to a tight embrace before she could steady herself.

        ‘Thank goodness! You’re fine!’ Persephone said with overwhelming joy, ‘We will never be apart this time!’

        However, contrary to the joyous Persephone, Lyra gave her a melancholic smile and said, ‘No. Persephone, I’m afraid I have to leave you for a while.’

        ‘What are you talking about…’ Persephone was confused, but soon she saw the fading body of Lyra. She said in disbelief, ‘How could it be… We did dispel that purple mist! But why are you fading?’

        ‘I used too much energy to get rid of the chaotic power.’

        ‘No… No…’ Watching as Lyra’s body faded away, Persephone could not help but burst into tears. Lyra reached out a hand to gently wipe the tears for her, then she said softly, ‘Persephone, please don’t cry. I’m just taking a break, a short break. I’ll be back soon, so…’

        Standing on tiptoe, Lyra planted a kiss on Persephone’s cheek and said with a smile, ‘Wait for me.’

        After leaving those words, Lyra’s body completely disappeared whereas a dingy little harp appeared in Persephone’s arms. Stroking the harp lovingly, Persephone whispered, ‘Sure. I’ll be the one waiting this time.’
STORY_2806:
Obeying Khaos’ order, Lynx went to assassinate John, the Court of Cancer, whom she found in a volcanic field. She seized the moment and tried to kill him, only to be captured by the latter. Lynx attempted to beg John to free her by giving him a guilt trip with her adorable eyes, yet he brought her up to the volcano instead.

        There were various powerful beasts living in the volcanic field. As they avoided the beasts, the climb took more days than they had expected. Being hog-tied by a rope and carried on John’s shoulder, Lynx had silently cursed John a thousand times during the bumpy trip.

        ‘I really don’t know anything. I’m just a victim of Khaos so it’s pointless to take me with you. How about you just let me go?’ Lynx said pitifully.

        ‘Shut up. I don’t trust a word from you,’ said John coldly without casting her a glance.

        ‘But I’m no use to you, so just let me go, please.’ Lynx persuaded John with her round watery eyes and flattery. 

        ‘No, that’s not exactly right—at least I can use you as a decoy when I encounter a beast.’

        ‘You!’

        “This man is impossible! What is wrong with him?! How could he be so unfeeling to my cuteness… Anyhow, I am going to find a chance to kill him!”

        So Lynx began to observe John carefully along the way. The longer she observed, the more she felt frustrated. John knocked down the beasts in the volcanic field easily with his excellent fighting skills; not even the most menacing beast could leave a scratch on his black armor. However, there was one thing that Lynx found ludicrous—John only repelled the beasts and hardly killed any of them.

        To Lynx, the world had always run by the law of the jungle—weak prey never lived long. Showing mercy to the beasts could lead to retaliation in the future. Nonetheless, that would work in Lynx’s favor since she had been hoping for nothing but John’s death. It was just that her wish never came true.

        The closer they got to the top of the volcano, the more anxious Lynx was. Although Khaos never told her the reason why he wanted John dead, her instinct told her that it was all connected to the machine on the top.

        “I don’t have much time left. Khaos is gonna kill me if I fail my mission. Holy—— Why is it so hot in here?” thought Lynx with sweat running down her forehead, which fell to the ground and evaporated. As Lynx looked around from John’s shoulder, she found that they had come to a small cliff where she could see the flowing lava down below.

        “Oh right, the lava! No matter how hard his armor is, he surely can’t survive the lava!” With a sinister grin flashing across her face, Lynx began to come up with a plan to make John fall into the lava.

        After putting up a tent to rest, John took out that unmelting ice again and started examining it.

        “He has been holding on to that ice along the way… If that ice falls, he will definitely try to catch it and that will be my chance to kill him.” Picking the right moment, Lynx summoned the chaotic power inside her and attacked her own body! Then blood spurted out of her mouth.

        ‘Arghhh! It hurts!’　

        Hearing the Lynx’s groan and seeing her rolling on the ground, John walked to her with a frown, only to find an energy running amok in her body.

        Just when John put down his guard to help her, Lynx broke away the rope with all her might and snatched the ice from his hand. Then she leaped toward the edge of the cliff with the ice in her arms.

        Just as Lynx had expected, John immediately jumped off the cliff. Falling to the lava with the ice in her arms, Lynx could not help but feel triumphant when she saw the anxious look on his face which brought a wicked smile to her face.

        ‘Die!’ Lynx let go of the ice, forcing John to catch the ice in mid-air. As she conjured her power, a blinding purple light appeared around her legs. Like a flash of purple lightning, she then leaped in the air, stepped on John’s back, snatched the ice again, and climbed back up to the cliff.

        After Lynx had gotten back to the ground, she looked at the ice in her arms and thought, “If I bring this cube of ice with me, maybe Khaos will reward me with more power or even set me free…”

        Recalling the taste of freedom she had as the leader of the stray cat group, Lynx could not help but dream about her future. Just as she was about to turn around and leave, a blade of wind attacked her from the rear——

        Someone kicked the ice in Lynx’s hands into the air and caught it before it fell to the ground. Lynx looked back, only to find that John was standing behind her composedly.

        ‘You—— How could this be possible?!’ Lynx exclaimed.

        ‘I have never let my guard down over you from the beginning, so of course, I was well prepared for your scheme after seeing you jump off the cliff.’ John nonchalantly showed her the grappling hooks in his hands.

        ‘Dang it! Give that ice to me!’ Filled with rage, Lynx conjured a giant cat’s phantom with her chaotic power to attack John.

        “I wanted to see if it could change, but it seems impossible now.” Letting out a soft sigh, John no longer hid his power. As he channeled his astralist power into his right hand, he tore apart the phantom with a wave of his hand and a burst of radiant light. Then, he charged at Lynx with his other hand.

        By quick reflex, Lynx kicked her feet and jumped to the edge of the cliff to dodge the attack. Then she said victoriously, ‘Humph! You missed—— Hmm?”

        When Lynx was halfway through finishing her sentence, she suddenly felt a tremor under her feet, which gave her a sense of foreboding. However, it was already too late—the cliff edge began to collapse at the unbearable impact of their fight.

        Lynx fell into the boiling lava with the debris and disappeared into the vivid burning orange before she could even let out a scream.

        ‘What comes around goes around, huh?’ Looking at the flowing lava, John showed a derisive smile. Then he walked away, heading toward his destination…
STORY_2807:
‘I’m a constellation blessed by the astralist. I shine for the peace of this realm,’ the determined Auriga said to Athena righteously, and he continued, ‘I will not tolerate any beings who try to break the world’s balance, not even the sacred gods!’

        ‘Do you really think you can defeat me by hitting me once?’ Athena got back up, using her spear as a cane. She wiped the blood from the corner of her mouth, her eyes flaring with rage. She said, ‘What a foolish man! Now let me bring you back to reality!’

        As Athena held her spear vertically, a bolt of lightning suddenly flew across the sky and struck her. Astonishingly, the lightning did not hurt her but ran along her body like a shield, healing all the wounds Auriga had inflicted on her in an instant.

        It was a blessing from Zeus, the King of Gods, to his daughter, Athena, the Goddess of War, wishing for her victory. 

        Auriga was stunned by the illogical phenomenon until he heard Galio shouting——

        ‘Don’t just stand there! She’s coming!’

        ‘Eh?’ In the blink of an eye, Athena rushed to the front of Auriga with her deadly spear aiming right at his head. Fortunately, Auriga’s fighting instincts kicked in—he raised his weapon to cover his forehead and narrowly escaped the fate of his head being pierced through by the spear.

        However, his weapon was not as lucky as he was. With a clunk, his weapon broke into two under Athena’s crushing power. When Auriga glanced at the shattered weapon in his hand after jumping back clumsily, a shudder passed through his body.

        “This was a weapon given by the ancient gods but she just broke it in one blow. Given her delicate appearance, she is unreasonably strong. That’s a complete fraud! No one would ever like a violent liar like that so I bet she must be single!” thought Auriga, who was plunged into a state of confusion by the sudden attack.

        On the contrary, Athena was breathtakingly calm. Wielding her spear, she went after Auriga again like a venomous snake pursuing its prey. Without another weapon to deflect the attack this time, Auriga could only cross his arms before his vitals. Unexpectedly, he did not feel any pain but heard a groan of pain.

        ‘Argh!’ Even though Galio raised his sword to protect himself, his wounded body still failed to withstand Athena’s power, resulting in him being smashed into a tree. 

        ‘Galio!’ Auriga screamed with agitation.

        ‘It’s you again… Now be gone!’ Gritting her teeth, Athena aimed her spear at Galio to give him the final blow——

        “No! Don’t hurt my friend!” Auriga came back to his senses as he saw Galio take the attack for him. Suddenly, an unknown burning sensation ran through his body and concentrated in his right hand, heating his weapon that had been shattered by Athena. From the crack of the weapon rose a new blade of flames.

        ‘STOP IT!’ Auriga dashed to stop Athena. Perhaps it was the fit of rage—he and Athena fought neck and neck, and startlingly, he was the one getting the upper hand.

        “I have to take her down!”

        However, a few flying arrows came from a distance and shattered Auriga’s hope—the god soldiers finally came to Athena’s aid!

        “Uh… Galio is injured. I can’t keep fighting her. We have to get out of here before the soldiers surround us!” Clamping his teeth together, Auriga swung a heavy blow at Athena and knocked her away. Then he turned around and ran toward the carriage while picking up the wounded Galio, who was lying on the ground.

        After getting into the carriage, Auriga scrambled up to the driver’s seat. As soon as he gently tugged the reins, Mr. Horse began to run. Yet, it was stopped before it could take the third step—its body and the carriage were both entangled with the vines that sprouted up from the ground.

        ‘Humph! You can’t run away from me!’ As Athena waved her hand, the vines rose into the air along with the horse, the carriage and the people inside it.
　　
        ‘No…’ Still, Auriga’s eyes were shining like stars. The light in his eyes did not die in the adversity but burned even brighter. When he put his hands on the carriage, the burning sensation reappeared and circulated through his body again, turning into sparks that blossomed in his palms!

        ‘No one can stop the flames of hope! Even the weak can blaze a trail of their own!’ With a low shout, Auriga summoned the astralist power inside his body. The burst of power generated a blinding light like a supernova and enveloped the horse and the carriage.

        In the next second, a pair of extravagant fire wings spread from Mr. Horse’s body. With a neigh, Mr. Hoses flapped the wings. The sparks on it fell onto the vines and started a magnificent fire that burned all the vines around the carriage down in an instant.

        The moment Mr. Horse regained freedom, it led the carriage into the air, leaving a trace of vivid red flames in the sky. Still, some god soldiers tried to shoot arrows at the carriage but the trace of flames burned them all before they could reach it.

        And so, Athena could only watch the carriage recede into the distance and eventually disappeared on the horizon.

        ‘Phew… We made it.’ After wiping the cold sweat from his forehead, Auriga looked at Galio, who was lying weakly, and said anxiously, ‘We need to find a place to treat your wound’——」

        ‘No. Go to the Enochian Tower.’ Holding Auriga’s hand, Galio continued, ‘They… My friends are still there, waiting for me.’

        ‘Okay.’ Auriga nodded. Just when he was about to tug the reins, he seemed to have remembered something and looked back at Galio timidly, adding,  ‘But don’t you die on me, okay?’

        ‘...I won’t. I don’t want to be jinxed,’ said Galio, who took a moment to choke back his anger.

        ‘That’s good to hear.’ Auriga nodded in satisfaction. As he finally pulled the reins, Mr. Horse let out a soft neigh and flew in the direction of the Enochian Tower…
STORY_2808:
Just when Summoners were put into a bitter struggle, the Court of Ophiuchus came just in time to shield them away from the battlefield. In the end, with the help of Mitty and Marble, the Canis Major and Minor, Ophiuchus managed to defeat Pontos.

        After the fight, Ophiuchus, Marble and Mitty walked up the stairs wearily where they ran into a man and a woman.  From the overpowering aura of the two, Ophiuchus could tell that they were no ordinary people. Grim-faced, Ophiuchus clenched his hands into fists and slightly bent his body, like a beast that encountered formidable predators.

        “I can’t have another long fight with the injury I got just now. I have to make it quick.” At such thought, Ophiuchus leaped into the air to give the man a thundering punch with all his strength.

        Yet, Ophiuchus’s punch was stopped by an elemental shield. As the man snapped his fingers with a snort, the shield released a beam of scorching fire and blasted Ophiuchus into the distance. Seeing that, Marble and Mitty immediately ran over to catch him.

        ‘You foolish mortal. How dare you defile this sacred land and challenge the might of the God of the Sun!’ The God of the Sun, Apollo, said coldly while looking down at Ophiuchus as if he was looking at something unclean. Then, he raised his bow into the air. A blinding light gathered at the bow riser and gave Ophiuchus a shiver of fear.

        “I have to stop him before he shoots that arrow!”

        Ophiuchus and Mitty simultaneously launched an attack but they failed to notice Artemis, who had already aimed her bow at Ophiuchus behind the light of Apollo. With a flash of silver light, a silver arrow appeared precisely before Ophiuchus’ forehead.

        It was a terrifyingly fast arrow that gave Ophiuchus no time to react. Fortunately, Marble leaped and pushed him away in the nick of time. Yet, the silver arrow hit Marble’s hind leg, causing a splatter of blood on Ophiuchus’ face.

        ‘Marble!’ Ophiuchus screamed. Meanwhile, Mitty rushed to catch Marble. However, Apollo’s attack soon came before they had the time to grieve. Like a shower of rain, a hail of light arrows descended from the sky, so Ophiuchus could only bite down on his resentment and channel his astralist power to conjure phantom snakes over his head as a shield.

        Amid the constant sound of arrows beating against Ophiuchus’ shield, his face grew paler with every second past.

        Blood drained from Ophiuchus’ face. Even so, he did not move a step but kept holding the shield of snakes to protect Mitty and Marble from the rain of light.

        “Why… Why do they always have to take away everything I love…”

        As Artemis aimed her bow at Ophiuchus again, a sense of despair swept through the young man. Just then, Mitty gave Ophiuchus a grin. Even though no words were spoken, Ophiuchus understood what it meant…

        “Mitty! NOOO!”

        With a burst of dazzling light coming out of Mitty’s body, it dashed into the rain of light, targeting the two gods. Countless wounds appeared on Mitty’s body in an instant. Still, it showed no fear. Seeing Mitty, Artemis immediately changed her target.

        When Artemis fired her silver arrow at Mitty, the latter summoned all its astralist power and swung its claws, creating a gigantic thunderbolt that ripped through the rain of light and broke her arrow in an instant. At the same time, Mitty, who had exhausted all his strength, fell to the ground.

        At that moment, the sight of Mitty falling down overlapped with Ophiuchus’s memories of Ellie being injured by Khaos, the old man being slaughtered by the god soldiers, and Marble being shot the arrow. The rage and sorrow inside Ophiuchus eventually erupted, starting a fire in his soul and turning into swirling starlight in his right eye.

        ‘I won’t let you hurt the people I love again!’ Yelling aloud, Ophiuchus flexed his legs and stepped into the path that Mitty had opened for him. As he ran forward, the countless starlight on his body all coalesced into a giant phantom snake that slithered its way to attack the gods with a storm of sand and dust.

        With a frown marring his forehand, Apollo concentrated all his godly power to repel the phantom snake with  Artemis.

        Unexpectedly, the phantom snake broke into pieces easily when the two powers collided, which gave the two gods an ominous feeling. At the same time, a fist fell from the sky and hit the ground, creating a blinding burst of starlight. The blast of wind knocked Apollo and Artemis away, causing them to cough up blood.

        When the two gods got back up and stared at Ophiuchus with blood lust, a majestic voice sounded in Apollo and Artemis’ heads.

        “Come back. Don’t waste your time on ants.”
        “Lord Khaos!” Apollo said respectfully as he recognized the voice. However, he hesitated because of his rage about Ophiuchus.
        “But he——”
        “Don’t make me say it twice.”
        “...Yes.”
　　
        Without any choice but to obey Khaos’ order, Apollo gave Ophiuchus a resentful glare before he and Artemis turned into two streams of light that flew back to the top of the tower.

        Watching the two gods leave, Ophiuchus fell to the ground with a sigh of relief.

        ‘Ophiu, Ophiu…’

        In a haze, Ophiuchus saw Marble and Mitty, who were horribly scarred, walking slowly toward him.

        ‘Thank goodness… You guys are okay…’

        ‘Mitty and I are gonna be fine because we are staying with Ophiuchus forever…’ said Marble.

        ‘Marble, Marble, Mitty, Mitty, Ophiu, Ophiu, forever, together!’

        ‘Yeah…’ Ophiuchus drew Marble and Mitty into his arms and held them tightly yet gingerly with joy as if he had found his lost treasures, and said, ‘The three of us will stay together forever.’
STORY_2809:
After regaining his memories, Ophiuchus decided to leave alone so as to keep Mitty and Marble safe. Reluctant to bid farewell to Ophiuchus, Mitty and Marble tried to track him down with his scent.

        The long journey eventually led them to Ophiuchus again in front of the Enochian Tower. Before they had a moment to celebrate the reunion, however, they saw him being attacked by Pontos.

        To save Ophiuchus, Mitty and Marble attacked Pontos at the same time and knocked him off his feet. Yet, they soon fell into a tight corner. Luckily, Ophiuchus saved them and restored the balance of the fight. The two parties stared at each other in silence.

        “This man holds tremendous elemental power. We need to find a way to tie him down.” At such thought, Ophiuchus kicked his leg with all his strength while swinging his right fist forward. Unexpectedly, Pontos also threw a straight punch at him. The two ended up dashing toward each other—

        ——Boom! The two fists touched, creating gusts of wind that blew away the dust on the ground.

        Pontos’ powerful punch sent tingles through Ophiuchus’ hand which led to a frown on his face. On the other hand, Pontos gave him a bellicose smile and took a step forward with his right fist covered in a ball of blue light, ready to make the strike.

        Marble, who sensed the danger, then shouted at Mitty, ‘Mitty, do it!’

        Mitty immediately summoned its astralist power and moved to the back of Pontos like a flash of lightning. Just when it was about to dig its claws into his back, Pontos said, ‘Do you really think I’ll fall for the same trick again?’

        It seemed that Pontos had already known. Instead of landing on Ophiuchus, his right fist went upward. Immense aqua power rose from the ground and turned into countless water snakes that coiled around Mitty and Ophiuchus’ bodies, hanging them in the air until they could barely move.

        Although Ophiuchus and Mitty kept struggling, they began to lose their strength and consciousness under the tight coil of water snakes.

        ‘This works pretty well,’ said Pontos, cracking a malicious grin. Conjuring two aqua spears in the air, he aimed them at their chests.

        Seeing that, Marble recalled how Orion died before him. Gritting its teeth, it smashed its body toward Pontos in desperation.

        ‘STOP IT!’

        However, little Marble’s tackle was nothing but a scratch to a mountainous man like Pontos, who caught it easily. Just when Pontos was about to fling Marble away, the latter bit his right hand hard.

        ‘So you want to die first, huh?!’ Pontos shouted in rage, using his left hand to catch Marble. The flickering blue light on his hand sent a chill down Marble’s spine.

        “Is there nothing I can do now? No… not this time!”

        As starlight gathered on Marle’s body, a powerful blast shot from its forehead at Pontos with sparks and bolts. Pontos immediately let go of Marble and tilted his head to dodge the attack that landed right past him.

        After dodging the thunderbolt, Pontos made a full swing at Marble and knocked it into the air, saying, ‘Is that all you’ve got? You stupid dog! Now die!’

        In the narrow space between the ground and his arm, Pontos saw an unexpected smile on Marble’s face that shocked him. By the time he tried to take a step back, a giant paw had pierced through his body with countless bolts.

‘Don’t, don't bully, bully, Marble! Standing behind Pontos, Mitty was shrouded in dangerous lightning.

        “So I wasn’t its target all along?!” Unfortunately, Pontos’ realization came too late since thunder had run through all his body from the giant paw.

        Pontos gave a roar and blasted Mitty and Marble away with the power of elements like an injured beast. The blue light on his body suddenly began to flicker.

        ‘You… Damn it! You’re not getting away with this! I will make you pay—— Argh!’ Numerous wooden snakes emerged from the ground and stopped Pontos’ threat. It was Ophiuchus, who conjured the wooden snakes and manipulated them to wrap around Pontos’ body tightly.

        ‘Mitty! Marble!’ As soon as Ophiuchus shouted their names, Mitty and Marble simultaneously released a thunderbolt at Pontos.

        ‘ARGHHHH——!’ Pontos let out a long painful cry that gradually weakened and subsided into silence, with its burly body falling to the ground feebly.

        It was then Ophiuchus and the two dogs breathed a sigh of relief. As weary as they were, they climbed up the tower while supporting each other. Little did they know that they would encounter another group of formidable enemies soon…
STORY_2810:
In a simple village surrounded by beautiful nature, a man was standing under a tree while a spring breeze rustled his hair. As the man lifted his head, his handsome yet languorous face came to light. However, his eyes were filled with sorrow and pity the moment he saw Draco.

        “No… Don’t look at me like that!” With a groan, Draco woke up from the dream only to find herself trapped in the rubble.

        ‘Where am I…’ Draco looked around in the darkness and recalled her memories. ‘Oh right, Belial that bastard sent me here for investigation, saying the secret of gods lies here.’

        Draco, who was once an astralist candidate, defected to the demons after being told that she was unqualified to be an astralist. She had been working for Belial since then. This time, she was sent to a ruin to carry out an investigation.

        Draco thought it was just a false intel but she accidentally discovered the secret entrance where she fought against Dolu, the mechanical guardian. The fight ended with Draco crushing the floor, causing both of them to fall into the underground.

        Due to the fall, Draco lost consciousness for a while. Now that she woke up, she climbed out of the pile of gravel and started exploring the basement. The deeper she went, the more surprised she got.

        ‘I can’t believe there is such a huge space underground. What are they going to do with this?’ Draco pondered. Her question was soon answered when she pushed open the door. Behind the door was a boundless space in which she saw an array of mechanical soldiers standing quietly. It seemed that they had not been activated.

        “These are… Tut! Those damn gods hide an army here!” Draco bit her nails nervously and thought, “I have to tell Belial as soon as possible and make some countermeasures.”

        Draco decisively made up her mind, but a chill ran up her spine when she was about to turn around and leave. She immediately spread her dragon wings and flew into the air.

        Boom! A murderous ball of light hit the spot where Draco had stood and charred the ground. Draco would have ended up like the charred floor if she moved a second later just now.

        “It seems we have an agile thief here today.” A female voice sounded from above so Draco looked over only to see a woman with a scepter of stars in her hand, exuding a tremendous amount of godly power.

        “You must be Lady Aether whom that weird mechanical soldier mentioned earlier.” Draco soon figured out who the woman was.

        “Oh, so not only you’re an agile thief, but you’re also a quick thinker,” said Aether in a confident manner. “It’s such a shame you’re not smart enough to know the right place for you from the wrong one. Since you’ve discovered this place, I can’t let you leave now. My suggestion to you is to try not to struggle. At least, you won’t suffer much pain in that way.”

         “Let’s see who’s the one that will struggle.” Draco argued against Aether proudly. Yet, her words sounded nothing but a dog’s bark to the latter.

        Aether shook her head in pity, then she raised her scepter and conjured countless sharp blades with her immense power to attack Draco.

        Draco flapped her wings to dodge the blades. When she was dodging the last one, she deliberately swooped down and let the blade make a cut on Aether’s face. Only after then did she destroy all the blades that followed her.

        “Ha, it seems you’re wrong.” Draco gave Aether a triumphant smirk.

        To Draco’s disappointment, Aether did not show any sign of rage or embarrassment. Instead, she calmly wiped the blood from her face and said with easy confidence, “No, I’m never wrong.”

        “What—— Ahhhhh!” Before Draco could finish her words, an excruciating pain shot up her body and forced a scream out of her. Numerous spears made of godly power suddenly protruded from Draco’s body, puncturing her wings. Blood splashed, creating several wisps of white smoke in the air.

        “You have inherited such great talents but you don’t know how to use them. What a waste. Since you can’t make the best use of your talents, why don’t you give them to me.” Finally, a hint of excitement broke through the composed façade of Aether. She slowly approached Draco, who was hung up in mid-air.

        Before the looming crisis, however, Draco could barely react due to the excessive loss of blood. In a state of turmoil, she saw that phantom in her dream again—the man under the tree looked at her, his eyes filled with sorrow and pity, as though he was looking at an unwise and impenitent child.

        ‘Don’t look at me like that! I did nothing wrong! I never regret my choices! I want power! Endless power! And I will get it even if I have to lose all my emotions!’

        The man disappeared—perhaps he feared Draco’s strong will. Replacing him was a small ball of dark green light that kept growing and pulsating. Draco could not help reaching her hand to it at its vibrant energy.

        ‘Yeah, this is all I want, endless power.’ As soon as Draco touched the ball of the light, it shone and enveloped her whole body.

        Draco felt that every part of her body was being torn apart and reshaped. The bone-crushing pain made her scream, but all she heard was a hoarse and low-pitched roar.

        ‘This is my voice?’ Draco lowered her head in bewilderment, only to find that her hands had completely turned into the arms of a dragon and those spears that pierced through her wings had all been broken. She was free again.

        “Oh my… She wakes up.” Aether’s face sank when she saw the dark green dragon. Feeling entertained, Draco gave Aether a grin while summoning her power to deliver a series of heavy blows.

        ‘This is not what I expected… I should better run first.’ As soon as Aether drew an conclusion from her analysis, she decisively fled from the basement after launching an attack. Draco did not go after her, more precisely, she could not.

        Even though Draco awakened her power, she still had not get used to it. On top of that, the injuries she received had made it impossible. In fact, she was basically a spent arrow since she had used up most of her power. Even the spate of desperate attacks she launched just now was a bluff.

        After Draco landed on the ground, she returned to her human form and sat on the ground to take a rest. Then she propped herself up again and walked toward the exit step by step.

        ‘Anyways, I have to go back to the base and tell Belial the secret here.’
STORY_2812:
One day, Zhu Bajie, Tang Sanzang, and the other three apprentices came to Mingnan Mountain on their ascetic journey. When they reached the foot of the mountain, two women reeked of undesirable odors suddenly appeared and took them all aback.

        Pinching his nose, Sun Wukong asked the women, “What monsters are you?! I won’t let you take away our master!”

        “Wukong, calm down. They are not our enemies,” said Tang Sanzang, who pressed down the Vajra Staff in Sun Wukong’s hands.

        “Wukong? So you’re that monkey our master mentioned before?” One of the women asked.

        “You know me?”

        “Sure we do. We are the apprentices of Yuanshi Tianzun. I’m Jiutian Xuannü, the most beautiful Xian in the Heavenly Kingdom, and she is He Xian'gu, an old lady,” said the other woman.


        “Who did you just call an old lady?! Don’t listen to this narcissistic woman! I’m He Xian'gu and I never age.”

        Standing on the side, Zhu Bajie sized up the two women—both of them were soaked to the skin, with unknown thick brown liquid all over their hair and clothes. For their not-very-Xian-like appearances, Zhu Bajie couldn’t help but ask, “Are you really the apprentices of Yuanshi Tianzun? You don’t quite seem so…”

        “I’m glad you asked. It just makes me so mad! When Jiutian Xuannü and I passed by this mountain, we heard that there was a group of brigands who had been capturing people and forcing them to make pig food, so we thought we should bring the brigands to justice and save those innocent people. Little did we know that those barbarous pigs would attack us with pig feces and urine the moment we stepped into their base, leaving us no time to use Xian arts but to run away!”

        “So the odors from your bodies are all because of their attacks?” asked Sha Seng.

        “Yes! My Peach Essence is now completely ruined!” Jiutian Xuannü answered through clamped teeth.

        Clenching her hand into a fist, He Xian'gu added resentfully, “I will make those hateful pigs pay if it’s the last thing I do!”

        Zhu Bajie suddenly felt a chill down his spine, giving him goosebumps. Even though he knew that He Xian'gu wasn’t talking about him, he couldn’t help relating himself to the brigands.

        And then, Tang Sanzang asked, “Is there any way we can help you dispel the brigands? We’ll gladly do so if you need our help.”

        There was no way He Xian'gu and Jiutian Xuannü would ever take another step into the brigands’ base since they were traumatized by those repulsive pigs’ attacks. But how could they capture the brigand chief without venturing into the pigs’ lair? 

        Suddenly, an idea flashed across He Xian'gu’s mind. 

        “Oh right! I heard that the chief is looking for a pig husband. We can take advantage of that and sneak into their base!”

        “A pig husband?”

        Saying that in unison, Sun Wukong, Sha Seng, and Qiongqi looked at Zhu Bajie at the same time.

        “We have one right here.” Lifting its paw, Qiongqi pointed at Zhu Bajie. The latter immediately shook his head and said, “No! I’m not a pig now. I’m still stuck in my human form!”


        Zhu Bajie had turned into a good-looking man after drinking the demonic elixir in the gourd of Golden Horned and Silver Horned. Missing his handsome pig face, he had kept searching for a way to return to his true form ever since.

        “No problem! Leave it to me!” With a smile, Jiutian Xuannü took a porcelain bottle from her sleeve and said, “Ta-da! The true-self potion! This is a potion I made with the celestial essence and Peach Essence which can turn any monsters back to their true forms once they take a sip of it!”

        “Really?” Zhu Bajie took the bottle dubiously.

        “Humph! She may be dumb but she’s got some real talents in making potions. So just take a sip.” Reluctantly,  He Xian'gu defended Jiutian Xuannü.

        “Don’t worry. I will take you to Yuanshi Tianzun and seek vengeance if anything happens.”

        Hearing Sun Wukong’s promise, Zhu Bajie let down his guard and drank the potion. Just as promised, his body turned back into a boar under a white light in less than a second.

        Overjoyed, Zhu Bajie rushed to the river to check whether his handsome face was the same as before. However, he soon lowered his head in dejection after two glances.

        Sha Seng, who sensed his gloomy mood, asked, “What’s wrong? Shouldn’t you be happy that you’re finally back in your true form?”

        Zhu Bajie looked at his plump jawline and his pot belly that was about to touch the ground. He sighed, “Oink, I feel like I’m no longer the hottest pig.”

        “It’s okay! I know how to fix it!” He Xian'gu took a set of armor out of nowhere and put it on Zhu Bajie to cover his huge belly. Then, everyone helped Zhu Bajie polish the armor and his fangs. They combed his fur and put a ribbon on him, turning him into a handsome boar.


        Seeing his heroic reflection in the water, Zhu Bajie snorted proudly and said in a high spirit, “Oink! Oink! Now I’m ready to be a groom!”

        In order to lower the guard of the pigs in the brigand cottage, they decided to let Zhu Bajie go in alone while the rest stayed outside and waited for the best moment.

        As soon as the armored Zhu Bajie stepped into the cottage, he shouted to the pigs, “I'm here to marry the chief!”

        At the shout, all the brigand pigs looked back and they were instantly mesmerized by Zhu Bajie’s charms. They voluntarily made way for him and some pigs even offered to lead the way.

        Soon Zhu Bajie was brought to the chief’s room. Sitting on a large chair covered with white rabbit fur was the chief who was dressed in a glittery, rhinestoned and little dress with a golden ruby-jeweled headband on its head. With its whole body sparkling brilliantly, it kind of matched Zhu Bajie’s look.

        Seeing the chief’s back, Zhu Bajie couldn't help but think that it must be an exquisite pig lady and it might be wonderful if he could marry her.

        The maid pig, who was waving a banana fan beside the chief, said softly, “Chief, your suitor is here.”

        “Oink. Wonderful! Finally, someone came.”

        A sudden premonition rose in Zhu Bajie’s heart when he heard the chief’s voice. Why does the chief’s voice sound so deep and husky?
        Just then, the chief, who had been sitting with their back toward Zhu Bajie, sprang up from their seat and threw themself on Zhu Bajie. As its face expanded before Zhu Bajie’s eyes, the latter finally had a clearer look only to find that it was a boar!

        Zhu Bajie's dream was crushed. Thrown into a state of shock, he tried to escape, but the chief had already held his body tightly while gazing at him up close. The chief said, “Yes! Finally, a handsome one! Let me spoil you with a lot of love!”


        “Woah! You’re a man?!”
        
        “I never said I’m a girl!” 
  
        “But I’m a man too!” 

        “A man is exactly what I’m looking for! My guards at the door would have stopped you the other way! Come on, baby! Give me a kiss!” Pushing out its lips, the chief tried to give Zhu Bajie several kisses.

        Finding the chief unbearable, Zhu Bajie kicked it away, and then he ran away immediately. However, the chief didn’t take no for an answer but chased after Zhu Bajie, shouting, “Don’t run away from me! My dear!”

        Nauseated by the chief’s words, Zhu Bajie kept dashing forward, kicking away all the pigs standing in his way. Soon, Zhu Bajie reached the gate so he sped up and shouted, “Sun Wukong, help me!”



        In the blink of an eye, the chief, who was chasing after Zhu Bajie, was squashed into the ground by Sun Wukong with his Vajra Staff, which stunned all the pigs who rushed out following their leader.

        Just like that, the pig brigand incident came to an end.  However, this incident became Zhu Bajie’s nightmare that snuffed out his thought of returning to his true form again, haunting him ever since.
STORY_2814:
While Xiang Yu leaned against the temple wall, blood kept streaming from the wound on his abdomen, creating blossoms of crimson on the ground. Despite his heavy eyelids, he still stared straight ahead with deep affection and lingering tenderness in his eyes since it was the direction that Yu Miaoyi, the love of his life, left not long ago.

        “Miaoyi, please forget me and live a happy life.”

        Finally, Xiang Yu closed his eyes as his strength faded, waiting for his death in peace. However, his peace was soon disturbed by the sound of soft footsteps. Although Xiang Yu faintly knew that someone stopped in front of him, he no longer had the strength to open his eyes so he could only let his mind slowly slip into the darkness.

        It was some days later that Xiang Yu finally regained consciousness. The terrible pain in his abdomen drew his brows into a frown. Then he found himself lying on a strange yet comfortable bed, and his wounds were properly bandaged.

        “I’m still alive… Who saved me?”

        ‘Someone is finally awake.’ A tall figure came to his bed along with a husky female voice.

        ‘You’re… the queen of the Western Empire… What do you want?’ asked Xiang Yu with all his guard up since he knew clearly that the Queen would never save him for free.

        However, the Queen’s answer was beyond his expectation——

        ‘Find Miaoyi and take her away as far as possible,’ said the Queen who did not look at him but kept fiddling with the broken metal mask in her hands. The Queen had sent someone to the temple to retrieve the mask since it once belonged to Yu Miaoyi.

        ‘...Why?’

        ‘Yeah, why… Prince of the Eastern Empire, there isn’t a single moment when I don’t think of killing you with my own hands… But Miaoyi… Haoyue adopted her and she is my only sister now.’ Even though the Queen sounded exactly the same as usual, Xiang Yu could tell the great weariness and deep grief from her half-closed eyes.

        Years ago, the Western Queen proactively negotiated with the Eastern Empire so as to put an end to the chain of wars. As the relationship between the two empires had finally improved, she sent her own little sister, Haoyue, to the Easter Empire as an emissary to negotiate a truce. Little did she know that her sister would return in a coffin.

        Even though there was an unresolved mystery about Haoyue’s death, the Queen was blinded by hatred, and taking vengeance on the Eastern Empire had become her only wish ever since until she witnessed Xiang Yu and Yu Miaoyi trying to kill each other. Only then did the Queen realize that Yu Miaoyi had been living in such grave agony and despair that she would rather sacrifice her life for love.

        In a state of shock, the Queen could not take a step but only watched Panhe take Yu Miaoyi away. Consumed with a dreadful sense of guilt, she was too ashamed to see Yu Miaoyi. Still, there was a silver lining—she finally rose out of hatred and saved Xiang Yu from the verge of death.

        ‘I want nothing but her happiness and you’re the one who can make her happy. So, in return for saving your life, I want you to find Miaoyi, love her and protect her for the rest of your life.’

        Instead of saying yes, Xiang Yu remained silent. He knew that all it took was a single nod for him to get his wish and live a peaceful life with Yu Miaoyi away from the flames of wars that had been torturing him for life. However, he also knew that it would not be true happiness for both of them.

        ‘I’m sorry but I’m not going.’ Lifting his head, Xiang Yu turned down the Queen’s offer with anguish, despite how much he longed to see her again. Even though it broke his heart to pass up this opportunity, he knew he had to do it. With the radiance of determination shimmering in his eyes, he said, ‘As long as the war between the East and the West doesn’t end, Miaoyi and I can never live happily without the guilt over our people and repentance for our sins.’

        ‘That’s some fine-sounding talk. Actually, ending the war is easy. All you need to do is kill your father and I will wipe out the Eastern Empire. But you won’t do it, will you?’ The Queen sneered at Xiang Yu.

        ‘I won’t do that. It’s nothing but a massacre. Besides, it will only benefit the wolves behind no matter which empire wins. I bet you’ve noticed, your Majesty. Back then, we were just one step away from establishing peace, but your sister’s death happened to come in the way. It was just like someone wanted us to keep fighting. Was her death really just a coincidence, or someone’s scheme?’

        ‘You’re smarter than I thought. I didn’t think you could see through the hidden truth.’ The Queen showed no sign of surprise as if she had known. Indeed, the Queen knew of the conspiracy just as Xiang Yu suggested.

        ‘Your Majesty, let’s join forces. Together we can find out the mastermind behind all the flames and smoke.’ Xiang Yu turned his gaze to the Queen, his face filled with awe-inspiring righteousness and conviction.

        ‘...Sigh, you and Miaoyi truly make a silly couple. Both of you chose a difficult path. Do you understand what is waiting for you ahead?’ The Queen looked back at Xiang Yu with pity.

        Xiang Yu lowered his eyes. He knew that he would possibly have to wield his sword at his brothers and people if he worked with the Queen and disguised himself as one of the Western Empire subjects. Even just the thought of that made his body ache. Even though guilt and repentance swept over him like a tidal wave, still, he straightened his back and looked at the Queen unswervingly.

        ‘Yes, I know, but I have to bear these sins for Miaoyi and for my homeland so that the innocent will not have to suffer anymore.’

        ‘...Since you insist, let me give you a hand then.’ The Queen gave Xiang Yu her promise.

        From that day on, Xiang Yu put on Yu Miaoyi’s mask and dressed as a western soldier while carrying out an investigation secretly.

        In a collaborative effort, the two finally found the mastermind behind everything—the Qin Empire. The Qin Empire had been sowing discord between the two countries so as to wear down their national power and annex both of them once and for all.

        Even though the Queen and Xiang Yu figured out the truth, they felt powerless facing reality. Given the implacable animosity between the two nations, the people would not believe them even if they reveal the truth. For such a reason, they had to come up with the next step.

        ‘Your Majesty, only by joining forces with the Eastern Empire and exposing Qin’s scheme can we talk our people out of the deep-rooted hatred.’

        ‘But I don’t think your father will say yes to your plan.’

        ‘I will make him.’

        ‘You aren’t going to——’

        ‘I will sneak into the Eastern palace and meet my father to convince him.’ Taking a deep breath, Xiang Yu made up his mind and said, ‘If that doesn’t work, I will take the crown myself.’

        In the middle of that night, Xiang Yu successfully sneaked into the palace of the Eastern Empire and arrived at the Emperor’s bedroom door. When he was pondering how to distract the guards, he heard a familiar voice shouting, ‘Don’t expect me to open the door for you! Just get the hell in!’

        Xiang Yu knew that the Emperor had noticed him so he took off his mask and walked into the room. It had been a long time since the last time he saw his father. To his astonishment, the Emperor’s hair had turned white as if he had aged for decades in Xiang Yu’s absence.

        Looking at his aging father, Xiang Yu spoke with mixed feelings, ‘Father——’

        ‘I’m not your father. I lost my son the moment you defected to the Western Empire!’ With his face reddening in rage, the Emperor unsheathed his sword and made a slash at Xiang Yu, who did not move an inch to dodge the attack. Instead of cutting into Xiang Yu’s body, the sword stopped in front of his chest.

        ‘Why?! Why didn’t you avoid my sword?’

        ‘Why should I avoid it when I have nothing to hide?’ Unwaveringly, Xiang Yu looked at the Emperor. He seemed to be the one with the upper hand despite that the Emperor was the one holding a sword to his chest.

        ‘Father, my wish has never changed. All I ever wanted was to put a stop to the war between the two nations so that no more innocent lives will be lost.’

        ‘So your best solution was to turn your back on your homeland?!’ shouted the Emperor furiously.

        Xiang Yu did not flinch at the Emperor’s wrath but shook his head with pity and said, ‘Father, the Western Empire was never our enemy. Our true enemy is Qin, the empire far away.’

        ‘...Do you have any proof?’ The Emperor's Face slightly brightened. Still, he was dubious about what Xiang Yu said.

        Xiang Yu stepped forward and put some scrolls and evidence on the desk in front of the Emperor, who immediately opened them and started reading. The more he read, the more he sulked. Eventually, he could not help but hurl the scrolls onto the ground.

        ‘Very Well! Those ungrateful ministers! How dare they secretly work for Qin while taking the people’s money! What a disgrace to our empire!’ Trembling with rage, the Emperor felt short of breath. Xiang Yu immediately stepped forward to hold his body and pat his back to calm him down.

        ‘Father, calm down.’

        ‘I… am fine.’ As soon as the Emperor caught his breath, he said emotionally, ‘My son, you’ve done a great job. I knew that you would never turn your back on our people. But what should we do now? It is impossible to talk our people out of their hatred toward the Western Empire with solely this documentary evidence…’

        ‘I have a plan, but I need your help, father.’ And so, Xiang Yu told the Emperor his plan. After sitting silent for a while, the Emperor breathed a sigh and held Xiang Yu’s hand. He made up his mind and said, ‘Okay, I believe in you.’

        In the next few months, there had been several reports of the Eastern Empire’s defeat and casualties, and the Western Empire took the initiative to declare the final war.

        Wearing a mask, the general of the Western Empire came to the gate of the Eastern Empire palace and stood against the enemy troops. In a full suit of armor, the Eastern Emperor steered his horse to the front. Pointing his sword to the western general, he shouted aloud, ‘You have intruded on my land and made my people suffer! In response to your contemptible gesture, I hereby declare war! So come at me if you dare!’

        Instead of answering the Emperor, the general steered his horse and raised his sword to fight. It was a neck-and-neck fight, but soon the Eastern Emperor lost his strength—which made sense given his age—and fell off his horse under the general’s blow. His helmet fell into the general’s hand, who held it up to claim his victory. 

        Bang!

        Just then, a loud dull noise and a pungent smell of gunpowder came from the forest nearby and swept through the western general. Fortunately, the general was vigilant enough to dodge the first sneak attack. Still, he and his troops could not escape the siege of an army armed with muskets. 

        ‘Ha, nice move. But you and your weary army are no match for our soldiers,’ said Emperor Qin, who rode his horse to the forefront of his army. With his lips curling up into a triumphant smirk, he looked down at Xiang Yu and said, ‘I can spare your life if you surrender and declare your allegiance to Qin now.’

        ‘You finally came. I’ve been waiting for you, Emperor Qin.’ Unexpectedly, it was not the general who answered Emperor Qin but the Eastern Emperor, who should have been defeated. As soon as he got back on his horse, he blew a loud whistle with his two fingers.

        The next moment, a troop of soldiers rushed out of the Easter Empire palace and surrounded the Qin army. Riding a white horse, an exquisite woman came to the front of the army and said, ‘Ha, got you!’

        Knowing that he had been set up, the Emperor stared at the masked general and asked bitterly, ‘Who the hell are you?! How did you talk both the emperors into helping you?’

        ‘Because we all want the same thing—peace.’ Xiang Yu took off his mask and revealed his chiseled face. His true identity surprised Emperor Qin.

        ‘You are… Xiang Yu… I thought you were dead.’

        ‘Yes, I was dead, but I came back from hell to expose your scheme!’

        Raising his sword, Xiang Yu pointed it at the emperor of Qin, his eyes filled with burning anger and resentment. Then he shouted loudly, ‘I am Xiang Yu, the prince of the Eastern Empire, and the general of the West Empire! The emperor of Qin is a despicable man! He has sent spies to spread scandalous rumors and create discord between the two empires over the years, lurking in the dark, hoping to take advantage of our wars! And so, I talked to the Western Queen and the Eastern Emperor, and together we set up a trap. His presence is the best proof! Listen to me! Emperor Qin is the man who has ruined your families and destroyed your homes! He is the one that started the endless wars between the two empires! He and his people are our true enemies!’

        ‘Soldiers of the East! Hear me! Follow the prince and wipe out the Qin army!’ the Eastern Emperor roared, raising his sword up in the air.

        ‘Soldiers of the West! Hear me! Follow the general and wipe out the Qin army!’ shouted the  Western Queen with a fierce swing of her sword.

        The two armies, who had been fighting to the death over the years, finally made their first step toward concord. At Xiang Yu’s command, the two armies surrounded the forest where the Qin army stood.

        Seeing that the table had turned, Emperor Qin decisively ordered a retreat and fled under the protection of his elite cavalry. Xiang Yu saw and promptly steered his horse to catch him.

        “I’m only a step away… I can expose Emperor Qin’s scheme as soon as I catch him, thus the wars between the two empires will finally come to an end. Miaoyi and I can finally have our dream come true!”

        The excitement of having his dream at his fingertips took the best of Xiang Yu and blinded him from the risk of chasing after his enemies alone. That was why he failed to react when he saw Emperor Qin lift the musket in his hand. It was a few seconds later that he felt excruciating pain in his left chest. Blood seeped out of his armor, staining his clothes red.

        Xiang Yu, who was shot, could not continue riding his horse but watched Emperor Qin and his cavalry recede into the distance. A great sense of powerlessness swept over him. He stretched his arms in desperation only to break his balance and fall off the horse. It took several rolls to break his fall.

        By then, the night had fallen and the stars were strangely bright, just like the night he and Yu Miaoyi met. As much as he wanted to stand up, the excessive loss of blood sapped his strength and pulled him back to the ground. The overwhelming sense of resentment and regret burned his eyes.

        “Why… Our dream finally came true… We can finally walk on the street as a couple… But why did it end up like this… Is this the price for killing too many people?”

        His breath became weaker. Right before the moment that his mind fell into sheer darkness, he whispered softly, ‘Miaoyi… I love you…’

        A scorching tear dribbled from his right eye and fell into the puddle of blood underneath his body…

STORY_2816:
Hel was the daughter of Loki and his deceased wife. Loki loved her very much. However, her body was weak, and more fragile than normal people’s due to the curse that she inherited from her mother. Whenever the curse attacked, her legs would be racked with excruciating pain that could incapacitate her. That was why Loki was always worried about her.


        It was a sunny day—clear sky and gentle breezes—perfect for a hike. On a hill not far from the military camp, a tall, tanned woman was pushing Hel, who was in a wheelchair, to the top to admire the view. The woman was named Amy. She was a nanny hired by Loki to take care of Hel in his absence for military reasons.

        Looking at the picturesque scenery before her, Hel was wreathed in smiles of amusement, and she said, ‘It is beautiful here. Amy, thank you for taking me out for a walk here and letting me have a moment away from the camp.’

        “No, it’s nothing. I can take you here again at any time if you want!”

        Suddenly, they heard a rustling sound from the bushes nearby. Two beasts came out from the dark corner. Baring their teeth, they closed in on Hel and Amy step by step.

        “Amy! Run!” Hel tried to push Amy away but the latter who was standing at her back shook her head. With a confident and bright smile, she reassured Hel, “Hel, don’t worry. Leave it to me!”

        Soon after Amy left her words, she charged at one of the beasts and carried its body over her shoulders with one hand clamping its snout and the other around its body. Then she vigorously threw it at the other beast. Knowing that they were no match for Amy, the two beasts immediately got up and ran away with their tails between their legs.


        “Phew… They’re gone. Everything alright? Hel?” asked Amy worriedly, kneeling in front of Hel.

        It took a while for Hel’s senses to come back to her. The moment they did, she looked at Amy reverently with sparkles in her eyes and said excitedly, “Amy, you’re amazing! I can’t believe you just lifted a beast with your bare hands!”

        “Hehe!” Amy scratched her cheek. Hel’s words made her flush. Still, she could not help but say triumphantly, “I grew up on a farm so I often had to carry bundles of grass and buckets of milk around. Sometimes, I even had to carry calves. That’s how I built up my strength.”

        “Really? Tell me more!” Hel asked curiously. Amy then began to tell her the funny stories she had back on the farm all the way back home.

        When they got home, they saw Loki standing at the door, looking worried. Loki hurriedly walked to Hel and squatted down to check on her the moment he saw her. Confused by her father’s action, Hel asked, ‘Daddy, what’s wrong?’

        ‘I heard that there were beasts attacking people on the hill and I was worried sick that you would be in danger, so I rushed all the way back here. Thank goodness you’re okay.’

        Seeing Loki’s tightly knitted brows, Hel knew that she had caused her father worry again, so she immediately comforted him and said, “It’s all thanks to Amy. She chased all those beasts away.”

        Loki finally turned his gaze away from Hel and laid his eyes on Amy for the first time. He said in a gentle tone, “Thank you for saving Hel.”

        Amy returned him a sunny smile and said, “I was just doing my job.”


        Loki spotted a small wound on Amy’s arms. “Your arm is hurt.”

        Hel took Amy’s arm to take a look and said, “Amy, the beasts must have scratched you when you fought them just now.”


        “It’s just a scratch. It’s fine. I’m okay!”

        “Still, you need to bandage it properly.”

        Without saying another word, Loki began to take care of Amy’s wound after he took out a handkerchief and bandages. Holding Amy’s hand, he gently cleaned the wound with the wet handkerchief. His warmth spread through the thin cloth to Amy’s skin and tickled her heart.

        Then Hel saw Amy’s face flushing with vivid red spreading from her cheeks to her neck and ears. Covering her face, Amy said shyly, “Thank you.”

        Hel was surprised. She never saw this side of Amy, who had always been tough and outspoken.

        Amy never paid attention to her appearance. She did not care if her clothes were wrinkled or if they looked good or not. Loki happened to find her collar upturned so he gave a gentle reminder.


        After Amy touched her collar and found it just like what Loki had said, she gave him a silly smile and said, “Oh, you’re right.”

        Perhaps Amy’s innocent smile was infectious—Loki’s lips curled up unknowingly and that made Hel’s pupils slightly widen. Hel had not seen Loki smile for a long time. He always had a frown on his face either because of wars or her body


        Although Hel was not hurt by the beasts, the nerve-racking experience still brought her down with a fever that night.

        Loki promptly called a doctor for her. After taking the medicine, Hel’s body temperature began to drop and she was getting better. Still, Loki was worried that the fever might recur in the middle of the night so he decided to stay by her bed all night long.

        It upset Amy to see the careworn Loki so she walked to him and said, “Let me take care of Hel.”

        “No, let me. You take some rest.”

        “...I will be right outside. Just call my name whenever you need me.”

        In the middle of the night, Hel finally woke up. When she opened her eyes, she saw that Loki had fallen asleep on the table beside her bed. There were clear dark circles under her eyes that further underlined his raddled face. Hel could not help but feel a sense of guilt, thinking that it must be terrible for her father to run around between wars and her every day.

        Suddenly, a night breeze came through the window gaps, sending a shudder through the sleeping Loki’s body. As much as Hel wanted to put a coat on her father, his coat was hung on the coat rack by the door, somewhere out of her reach.

        Out of nowhere, a melancholic feeling welled up in Hel’s heart. Born with a curse, her body was weaker than normal people’s. She could barely move her legs, let alone take care of Loki. All she did was cause him trouble. Importantly, who knows how long she can live? Eventually, she would die from the curse and leave Loki one day. 

        While Hel let grief swallow her, Amy, who had been standing by outside, walked in and quietly draped the coat over Loki’s shoulders. It was then Hel saw the deep affection on Amy’s face and realized that Amy loved Loki, romantically, like a wife to her husband.

        ‘Yeah, if Daddy has someone by his side, he won’t be lonely even when I die. She can take care of him and share his burden. Most importantly, she can make him happy,’ Hel thought. Then she made up her mind.

        A few days later, Hel asked both Loki and Amy to have a walk in the bazaar near the village. However, Hel never showed up, leaving Loki and Amy alone in the bazaar.

        Seeing through Hel’s plan, of course, Loki turned down Amy and went back to the military camp alone. The next day, Hel knew that Amy was fired.

        During dinner that night, Hel looked at Loki dismally and asked, “Daddy, why did you fire Amy? Didn’t she make you happy?”
　　　　
        “I don’t need those fleeting moments of pleasure.” Holding out a hand, Loki touched Hel’s face which was haggard due to the curse and the fever, and said, “Hel, only your happiness is the eternal salvation to my soul.”

        Hel said in dejection, “But I’ll be gone eventually ——”

        “No! I won’t let that happen!” Loki abruptly stopped Hel. Leaning forward, he put his forehead against Hel’s and whispered, “Hel, you’re my heart, my life, my everything. I will cease to exist if you leave me. Do you understand?”

        “...Yes, Daddy. I will try my best to live, for you.” Only then did it dawn on Hel to realize what Loki truly desired. Even though living was nothing but suffering to her, she would strive for Loki and live as a drop of sweet nectar in his life of misfortunes.
STORY_2817:
Little Jinnie loved making spinning tops. One day, she ventured into the forest near the town to look for some wood pieces.
　　
        Focusing on finding the materials, Jinnie unknowingly walked into the depths of the forest where she had never been before. With towering trees standing in the depths of the forest, there was just a dapple of sunlight that helped Jinnie see where the wood pieces were.

        After hunting around, Jinnie finally gathered enough wood pieces. When she was about to head back home, a girl’s scream suddenly ripped through the air and startled the birds that were perching on the branches.

        “Someone must be in danger! I have to help her!” Jinnie thought anxiously. She ran toward the sound and found a ground of demons in the dappled sunlight, so she immediately hid behind a tree.

        Jinnie stealthily stuck her head out to see what the demons were doing. The demons were surrounding a girl about her age with one of them drawing his dagger to stab the girl.

        At the critical juncture, Jinnie forgot her fear and rushed toward the demon despite her own safety. Without seeing the attack, the demon was knocked onto the ground and the dagger slipped out of his hand. Jinnie immediately picked up the dagger and pointed it at the demons, shouting with all her strength, “Go-go away! Or-or else I will stab you!”

        Clearly, the demon leader did not see Jinnie as a threat, and thus he snorted, “Humph! You?”

        At the leader’s signal, one of his underlings charged at Jinnie and punched her to the ground. Jinnie fell heavily right next to the girl.

        The demon’s punch made Jinnie’s face swell. However, even though it hurt, she held back her tears, got back up shakily, and stood before the girl again to protect her.

        The girl looked at Jinnie quietly. Jinnie, who thought that the girl must be lost for words due to fear, bore the pain and forced a smile, saying, “Don’t worry. I’ll protect you.”

        Seeing Jinnie’s ludicrous move, the demon leader then said, “I’m telling you she is the only one I want! So beat it before I kill you too!”

        “No! I won’t!” said Jinnie firmly while straightening her little back.

        “What a foolish girl! Now die!” The demon leader raised his hand to thrust his dagger at Jinnie’s throat. Knowing she could not dodge it, Jinnie subconsciously closed her eyes. To her surprise, the expected pain did not come.

        Jinnie opened her eyes only to find the girl behind her back had come to her front before she knew it. Holding her right arm, the girl summoned a transparent shield to block the demon’s attack.

        “You’re the fool. You moron.” The girl gave a disdainful snort and waved her left hand. Then, a blade of light in a crescent shape swept through the demons around them and knocked them all down.

        As soon as the crisis was over, Jinnie fell to her knees and looked at the girl in surprise. “So you are strong…”

        “Why didn’t you run?” the girl asked in an uncannily imposing manner that did not match her age. Jinnie answered the question obediently, “Because if I left, you would be alone. Being alone is scary, but it will be fine if there’s another person with you.”

        The girl sneered, “You may not be smart, but you have such pure kindness that is rare to find in this world… My name is Woodbury. We’ll meet again someday when you have a wish to fulfill.”

        “When exactly will that be… Huh? She’s gone…” Jinnie lifted her head to ask, only to find that Woodbury had disappeared without a trace…
STORY_2818:
After Basti had successfully returned the Ancestral Elements to Tefnut, Mufasa was restored to power as the tribal chief. Together, the Spiritual Beasts brought prosperity back to their tribe.

        One day, the sky was covered by thick clouds. Rain poured like beads falling from a broken necklace. The water level was rising and the river was flowing fast. They were all signs of an impending flood. Since the tribe was near the river, the chief and the priest, Mufasa and Basti, promptly decided to evacuate the village while Odous, Iquitos and other strong Spiritual Beasts went to the border to build a dam with stones and sand to minimize the damage of the flood.

        Amid the lashing rain, Basti stayed at the back of the line lest any Spiritual Beasts would fall behind or walk out of the evacuation route accidentally.

        Basti’s anxiety grew as she saw the river running faster.

        ‘The water flow is getting faster! We need to speed up the evacuation.’

        “Everyone, hurry up! The flood is coming!”

        Just then, Basti heard a cry for help from a distance.

        “Help! Help…”

        “Someone is in danger!” Basti immediately ran toward the sound only to find a young Spiritual Beast drowning in the river that was pushing him into the distance.

        “Don’t worry! I’m coming!”

        Basti raised her staff to conjure dark elements. As she swung her staff in the direction of the child, the dark elements turned into a net and scooped the child out of the water.

        When Basti was going to check on the child as soon as he was back on the ground, the child pointed at her back and said with fright.

        “Oh no… The flood is here!”

        Basti turned around and saw that the river had burst its narrow banks with a great wave that was several meters tall coming at them. In a state of panic, Basti waved her staff again to send the child to the top of a big tree.

        The second after the child was sent to the tree, the wave smashed against the land and devoured everything ruthlessly. Seeing Basti being washed away by the wave, the child on the tree screamed, “Basti!”

        The river flooded the land in an imposing manner. When Basti finally managed to stick her head out of the muddy water, she found that the water had pushed her away from the shore in the distance.

        The velocity of the fast-flowing river kept increasing. Basti was plunged into a state of panic when she saw the end of the river where the water began to drop.

        ‘Oh no! It’s a waterfall!’

        Basti immediately conjured dark elements in an attempt to get herself out of the water. However, a sudden sharp pain in her back stopped her from doing so. It turned out that a broken tree in the flooding river hit and gashed her back, causing her to bleed.

        It was too late by the time Basti tried to conjure the elements again—she had been washed away by the water. Water splashed as she fell into the pond below the waterfall which was about ten meters tall. With the impact of the fall sapping Basti’s strength, she couldn’t swim up but only sank into the pond slowly.

        ‘Am I… going to die…’ The feeling of suffocation blurred Basti’s vision. She saw a vague figure swimming toward her but she passed out before she could have a clearer look at the swimmer’s face.

        When Basti regained consciousness, she found herself lying on the shore with a human man sitting next to her. Seeing her awake, the man said with a long face, ‘Finally, you’re awake.’

        ‘He must have saved me from the water,’ Basti thought, and so she thanked him, “Thank you for saving my life!”

        Unexpectedly, not only the man did not accept her words of gratitude but he scolded her, “Are you an idiot? You should be avoiding the water, not falling into it when there is a flood! If I didn’t save you, you could have——”

        The man turned his face away and stopped talking in the middle of his words. He did not dare to say the possible result that could have happened.

        “I’m not an idiot! I was saving that kid…” As Basti spoke, she found that the tone of the man in front of her sounded familiar, just like Felix.

        Felix was the captain of an army of mercenaries who had taken a job from the Nightfall Savant to steal the Ancestral Elements in the Spiritual Beast tribe. To help him sneak into the tribe, the Nightfall Savant turned him into a cat. However, Felix changed his mind about stealing the Ancestral Elements after spending a while with the Spiritual Beasts. In the end, he returned the Ancestral Elements to Basti instead of handing them over to the Nightfall Savant.

        However, Felix left without leaving Basti a note after returning the Ancestral Elements to the tribe.

        “You’re Felix…”

        Giving Basti a gentle smile, the man said, ‘Too slow, dummy.’

        “I’m not dumb! But how did you turn back into a human?!”

        “I found the potion. I’ve defeated the darkness and finished my job. That’s why I’m back.”

        “Then… Are you going to leave again?” Still, Basti was afraid that Felix would leave without saying a word like the last time he did.

        “No, I’m not leaving. But will you still let me stay after everything I did?”

        “Of course… Welcome back!”

        Basti opened her arms and held Felix tightly.

        A moment later, the rain stopped along with the rising river. Basti took Felix’s hand and started running, leading him into the tribe the way she did when they first met.
STORY_2819:
It was a night with a bright moon shining high in the sky. The gentle moonlight streamed into the room of Kejourou, who was the most famous geisha in the brothel. Impeccably dressed, Kejourou walked to the window and looked at the full moon in the sky. Then she turned her gaze on the row of lifelike wooden sculptures on the window sill. Her heart lightened up with excitement.

        “Today is the day. I can finally meet him again. I wonder what he will tell me today.”

        On every night of the full moon, a man would come to see Kejourou and listen to her singing behind the blind. On each of his regular visits, he would bring her a small wooden sculpture. Although the sculptures were no valuables, the man would share his stories and the things he had seen with Kejourou through them, giving her a chance to take a peek at the world outside the brothel.

        The man treated Kejourou like a friend. All he did was mostly chitchat in which he shared the trivial matters in his life with her. Unlike the stiff and nervous conversation with other customers, the meeting with the man had always been a pleasure to Kejourou. That was why she felt most relaxed and looked forward to meeting him the most.

        As usual, Kejourou went to the room and sat on the other side of the blind. Soon, the wooden door was pushed open—her customer had arrived.

        With a blind that hung from the ceiling to the ground between the two, they could only see a rough figure of each other. After the customer sat down, Kejourou pulled up a corner of the blind to serve the tea she had prepared. Then she began to play music and sing.

        There was only the sound of the shamisen and Kejourou’s singing voice in the room. Even though none of them spoke a word, Kejourou could still feel the silent communication between her and the man.

        However, Kejourou was not at her best that day. She found that her throat began to dry after singing just two songs.

        “I must have sung too much this week but he loves hearing me sing. I can’t disappoint him”

        So Kejourou put up with the sore throat and continued to sing. She sounded the same as usual except her voice cracked slightly when she hit a few notes. One could barely spot the difference unless they listened to her singing meticulously. Unexpectedly, a cup of hot beverage with rising steam was pushed toward Kejourou through a lifted corner of the blind as she finished another song.

        ‘This is… for me?’

        ‘Your voice is slightly hoarse so I ordered a cup of pear juice with honey for you. It should help with your sore throat.’

        At first, Kejourou was surprised. Then an indescribable feeling welled up inside her with a burning sensation. Softly, she said, ‘Thank you…’

        Holding up the cup gingerly, she sipped the warm pear juice that hydrated her dry throat in an instant.

        ‘And this,’ said the customer while sliding a wooden sculpture of a cherry blossom through the blind.

        ‘I saw the cherry blossoms on the mountain a few days ago and they were very beautiful, and I want to show you their beauty.’

        Kejourou took a closer look at the sculpture and made a complimentary remark without a second thought, ‘It’s really pretty. I bet the flowers must look even more beautiful when you see them in person… It’s such a shame that I couldn’t see them with my own eyes…’

        ‘I can take you there. I can take you to see all the beautiful things around the world… I can take you out of here, as long as you want.’

        Kejourou was stunned. Her heart skipped a beat. It was only after a few seconds that her blood began to circulate again and flow toward her pounding heart.

        It was not the first time that Kejourou was offered to be freed from the brothel by her customers. Yet, all of them only wanted to take her as their concubine or ask her to stay at their home and serve them forever. The man in front of her was different—he offered to fulfill her wishes instead of his own.

        “He will never despise me… He will give me the freedom that I’ve always wanted… I… I believe him.”

        ‘I——’ Just when Kejourou was going to say yes, a creak of the door stopped her. Then she heard some hurried footsteps and whispers on the other side of the blind.

        The man abruptly stood up and said to her, ‘I have to go but I will be back. I hope you can give me an answer by then.’

        Leaving those words, the man left in a hurry. When Kejourou pulled up the blind, her customer had already gone.

        Kejourou was a little disappointed but she was not upset because she had hopes that the man would come back again.

        Unfortunately, the irony of fate did not spare Kejourou—her purity was forcibly taken by a customer. Depression rendered her heart into dust, and yet fate left her a string of hope. When Kejourou was ready to meet her end, the man—Shuten-dōji—came and saved her, beginning a relationship that would turn her world upside down…
STORY_2820:
Ever since the Spiritual bBeasts returned the Ancestral Elements, the tribe constantly strived and flourished. Soon it was the day of the harvest festival. All the Spiritual Beasts were making preparations with laughter, putting a bumper of harvest on the altar. 

        Seeing the prosperity of the civilization, Tefnut and Shu couldn’t help but sigh pleasedly, ‘they have grown and they no longer rely on us like the way they did before.’

        ‘They are already strong enough. For all these years we’ve spent in the tribe, I wonder how much the world outside has changed,’ said Shu.

        ‘How about… we go out to see the world again?’ Tefnut asked Shu softly and got her answer from the latter’s sparkling eyes.

        Together again, they embarked on a new journey. With the power of the Ancestral Elements, they disguised themselves as humans for the convenience of traveling across the human land. When they revisited some old places, they noticed the changes and started talking about their memories of the past. However, Tefnut had never thought that this trip would evoke some memories of her long-lost past.

        One day when they were walking on a street in a small town, Tefnut’s ears twitched as she heard a cat's whimper.

        ‘Meow…’ The voice was small and weak.

        ‘A cat is hurt somewhere near. Where is it?’ Tefnut soon found the source of sound from a corner of the road—a kitten was whispering for help under a wooden cart that crushed its leg.

        Tefnut wanted to go forward and help it, but someone was one step ahead of her!

        Holding the kitten in his arms, the man hurriedly walked away as if he was doing something sleazy. Shortly, his burgundy tuxedo disappeared at the end of the alley.

        ‘He looked familiar… Could it be him?’ A disturbing memory came back to her; her hands slightly quivered as though the pain and red weals caused by the whip resurfaced on her palms.

        ‘Shu, we have to follow him. I’m afraid that he may abuse that cat!’ Tefnut said.

        Following the scent drifting in the wind, Shu soon tracked the man down. They came to a residence, in which faded tent canvas and rusted cages were placed in the backyard. They heard the cat’s wail from a wooden shed so they hid behind the back door and peeped through the cracks to see what was happening inside.

        There were all kinds of tools hanging in the shed; the metal tools were shining with cold light and there was a pile of ropes and whips on the table… Tefnut knew that she was right as she recognized the patterns painted on the tools—they all belonged to the man who once whipped her again and again, the circus owner.

        Alertly, Tefnut looked at Shu, who responded to her with a nod. Then, they promptly went into the shed. Targeting the man, Tefnut attacked him with water elements.
