        ‘Don’t you hurt the animals again! Shu, go and save the cat!’ said Tefnut.

        ‘Hurt? I’m curing it! Let go of me!’ That man shouted.

        ‘Curing?’ Tefnut turned and looked at the kitten that was lying on the table only to find that its injured leg had been bandaged. Yet, she still found it unbelievable so she asked, ‘why did you bandage it? You’re going to use it to make money, aren’t you… the circus owner?’

        ‘How did you know that… I’m not a circus owner anymore,’ said that man. ‘I stopped treating animals as my money maker since an animal had saved my life. They are also living beings.’

        Tefnut was startled for she was the one who saved the circus owner’s life back then.

        ‘But you walked so furtively…’ Tefnut’s voice gradually trailed off.

        ‘It would bleed to death if I didn’t walk faster——’ That man explained. Just then, the injured kitten made a grateful purring sound, as though it acknowledged what the man had said.

        Stepping forward, Tefnut held the man up and said with a nod, ‘I’ sorry. We’ve mistaken you.’ 

        Tefnut showed a genuine smile after seeing the change of her acquaintance. Those hands that used to whip her now help animals; they might look a bit wrinkled but they now seemed much more amiable.

        “It turns out that every small decision can bring about a change. Utopia might not be real but we can always make the world a little better as long as we choose rightfully.”
STORY_2821:
In a dark shrine, there was only a feeble light that came from a light ball held by a giant dragon in the center. The light of the ball was weak and uncertain, like flickering candlelight.

        “The Ancestral Elements were getting weaker. Why is that happening?” thought Seth.

        A shaft of brilliant sunlight came through the door crack and it grew brighter with the shaking sound of the stone door. As Seth opened his eyes, he saw someone open the shrine door and walked in. The comer’s silhouette against the daylight made the outside world seem more vivid.

        ‘I can’t find Tefnut and Shu. It seems like they’ve gone out for a journey again,’ Ra said.

        ‘Humph, they dared not take the Ancestral Elements with them this time… It’s fine. I’ll keep guarding them.’ Seth held the light ball in his arms tightly, as though he was afraid that someone might take it.

        ‘You’re still the same.’

        ‘Guarding the Ancestral Elements is my mission,’ said Seth, whose dragon eyes held a red gleam.

        ‘But the world outside is much larger. You’ll miss out on a lot of things if you just stay in the shrine,’ said Ra.

        Seth didn’t respond. He just kept gazing at the ball of light silently and intently, as if he was saying that nothing—not even a living creature—could catch his eye except it.

        Shaking his head, Ra stepped forward with his cane and said, ‘Have it ever crossed your mind that the true meaning of guardianship is not just grasping it firmly in your hands but using the power in it for good?’

        ‘...Of course it has.’ Lifting his eyelids, Seth finally answered Ra, ‘it’s a pity that the Spiritual Beasts have not been able to make use of it… I just don’t understand why they can’t take in the power of their origin, just like I can’t understand why you and Shu created the Spiritual Civilization in the first place.’

        ‘That was a thought we shared after traveling together. Maybe you’ll understand it when you go out and take a look at the world.’

        ‘No need.’ Seth turned around and walked to a wall of the shrine, brightening up the traces on it with the light of Ancestral Elements.

        Those were the claw marks Shu and he left from repelling the enemies to guard the Ancestral Elements throughout all these years. Yet, Shu once again left the shrine for his desire to explore the world outside, leaving his brother, Seth alone for the second time.

        Seth was sunk in gloom at the thought of this.

        Filled with melancholy, Seth wasn’t aware that the Ancestral Elements in his hands also dimmed as his heart did, but Ra saw all of that.

        ‘Did the light of Ancestral Elements just weaken?’ Startled by Ra’s sudden question from the side, Seth immediately hid the light ball behind him.

        ‘Let me take a look—Argh!’ Ra reached out his hands but only got grabbed by Seth, whose strength was so great that almost leave a bruise on Ra’s wrist.

        ‘The Ancestral Elements are getting weaker. No one shall touch them except Shu and me!’

        ‘Calm down, Seth! I have no intention to take it away from you!’

        Ra, who wanted to get away from Seth, raised his cane to repel. Unexpectedly, Seth’s eyes turned red with scorching breath coming out from his mouth where the energy of elements was concentrating. Knowing that this would be a powerful cannon blast, Ra could only channel his powers in desperation. His hands then shone a blinding and searing light——

        ‘Ahhhhhh—!’ Blinded by the strong light, Seth loosened his grip on both Ra and the Ancestral Elements. Seeing the falling light ball, Ra, who had no fear of the blinding light, leaped to catch the ball before it touched the ground.

        As the light faded, Seth shook his head and wanted to pounce on Ra again in anger but he was then stunned by the scene before him.

        The Ancestral Elements were shining brightly in Ra’s hand. That dazzling and stable luminosity was the same as it was at the very beginning, which overwhelmed Seth with surprise and joy. He slowly crawled up from the ground and asked, ‘What did you do to restore the Ancestral Elements?’

        ‘I have no idea.’ Ra gave the ball of light in his hands back to Seth.

        But when Seth took the ball back on his palms, its light dimmed in a second…

        ‘Why?!’ Seth was shocked. He had always wanted to make use of the Ancestral Elements power but never thought that he was the one suppressing them all along.

        “Am I the reason why the power of the Ancestral Elements fails?”

        Seth immediately flew to the wall of the hall and lit the ancient carvings and patterns on it with the light ball in his hands, trying to find a clue in the shrine.

        Seeing his attempt, Ra unleashed a light from his palm and lightened up the entire hall. Yet, even the numerous inscription on the walls didn’t have their answer.

        ‘For all these years in the shrine, the only thing I know was that Shu and I are responsible for guarding the Ancestral Elements but I never truly understand what they are and how to guard them.’

        ‘Staying here won’t get you your answer. Go out and see the world. Maybe you’ll get what you want out there.’

        ‘But my mission—’ Seth subconsciously clenched the light ball. But both Ra and he soon realized that the tighter Seth held on to the Ancestral Elements, the dimmer their light and luster got.

        ‘Try letting go, Seth,’ Ra put out his hand and said, ‘let the Ancestral Elements shine like the way it should.’

        “So it was not only the Spiritual Beasts but also me… I must be not strong enough to use their powers.” Seth gave the light ball in his hands to Ra after a moment of pondering.

        The moment Ra took it, the ball of light shone brightly, so bright that lit up the entire inner hall.

        Seth looked around this unduly familiar shrine. After he and Ra looked at each other for a while, he then said collectedly, ‘Guard the Ancestral Elements before my return.’

        Ra nodded and watched as that red dragon flew out of the shrine to the open sky, heading to the unknown…
STORY_2822:
After the Spiritual Civilization, Shu and Tefnut once again set out on a journey.

        This time, they went to a small village. Built on a mountain, the village held fertile farmland with simple folk customs. The villagers didn’t show any opposition when they saw the two foreigners; instead, they gathered around curiously and chatted.

        Just when the two were leaving, a breath of damp wind came towards them. Seeing the grey cloud looming on the horizon, Tefnut had a feeling, ‘there will be torrential rain here... no, a flood, and I can't stop such a catastrophe.’

        ‘We have to tell the humans nearby,’ Shu, who couldn’t bear the death of innumerable living creatures, said, ‘so that they can find a shelter as soon as possible. I want to save every one of them with all I can do.’

        So Shu and Tefnut together went to tell the villagers to take refuge. Following a rumble of thunder, raindrops the size of peas fell on the land; soon it started pouring rain. Luckily, thanks to the heads-up of Shu and Tefnut, the villagers were evacuated in advance.

        Shu and Tefnut took the villagers to a nearby highland for protection. By the time they looked at their homes from the highland, the torrential rain had already submerged the village completely.

        As the water level continued to rise, Shu and Tefnut instructed the villagers to build a simple dyke with the branches and soil close at hand. However, the rain came quicker than they had expected. Like a thousand troops, a raging torrent of rubble and soil ran down the mountain to where they were.

        Before the power of the earth, anyone would seem weak and insignificant. Holding out her arms strenuously, Tefnut used all her powers to slow down the flood with water elements, yet the flood still came nearer and nearer.

        Just when the flood was about to inundate this little high land, a figure stood in front of all villagers. Under a strong burst of light, Shu conjured his powers and built a thick soil wall to block the torrent for everyone.

        However, the flood kept hitting the wall. Suddenly, thin cracks appeared on the wall after the hitting sound of several boulders in the torrent. Sweat beaded Shu’s forehead. As he kept repairing and maintaining the wall with his powers, his face turned pale and drawn in an instant.

        ‘Shu!’ Tefnut screamed in panic.

        ‘I’m okay! Leave it to me! You keep controlling the water flow!’ Shu kept channeling his power to protect the island. His mind slowly reeled due to the loss of strength.

        Just then, a massive landslide swirled the nearly unconscious Shu away, putting him in endless darkness.

        “I… got buried by the landslide… I have to get out quickly…” As much as Shu wanted to move, his exhaustion made it an impossible mission. Even if he tried to channel his powers, he couldn’t concentrate his mind to do so.

        After an uncertain period of time—when he was about to sink to the depths of despair—he saw a ray of light. Then pairs of hands covered in mud and calluses dug him out of the darkness.

        Fresh air wafted in. As Shu gasped and took a deep breath, his mind came back to him from turmoil.

        ‘Shu!’ Tearfully, Tefnut ran into Shu’s arms.

        Sitting up straight, Shu saw the villagers around him. All their nails were broken, stained with blood and mud. They should be in acute pain but they all flashed a radiant smile when they found that Shu was still alive.

        “They did this to save me…” Shu was impressed. He once believed that humans were all horrid and vile for he had seen their greed and malice in the past. Yet, now he knew how arrogant he was.

        “There are good and bad in this world. That’s exactly why as the ones who hold powers, we should guide them to good instead of abandoning them.”
STORY_2823:
Ra was left to guard the Ancestral Elements in the shrine alone after his companions—who had created the Spiritual Civilization together—all left for their own reasons. As the Spiritual Beast tribe continued to flourish, they stopped relying on their creators that much like they used to. Fewer and fewer Spiritual Beasts would go to the shrine for Ra, and Ra also gradually disappeared from their sight.

        Then for a very long time, Ra lived in the shrine alone. One day, he met his first visitor in years—a fox Spiritual Beast. He walked into the shrine nervously; he was so nervous that he didn’t dare look up after seeing Ra.

        ‘Oh, Lord, the Almighty! My children have caught a strange disease and no doctor could help them… Lord, I ask for your mercy… Only you can save my family…’ The fox Spiritual Beast threw himself in full prostration with his forehead pressing against the icy cold floor.

        ‘Take me there.’ So Ra left the shrine and followed the fox to his house.

        However, the shocking scene behind the door stunned Ra in an instant—the cottage was covered in blood with carcasses of several young Spiritual Beasts. They were all brutally murdered; some of them were even butchered into pieces.

        In spite of the blood, Ra looked around the house to see if anyone survived. Suddenly, that fox who had asked for his help ran out of the door.

        ‘Help! Help! Ra went mad! He killed all my family! And he wants to kill me too!’

        A crowd of Spiritual Beasts came to see what had happened only to see Ra soaked in blood. Their gaze fell on Ra with different emotions—distrust and fear, which were something familiar to Ra.

        ‘My son… My lovely sons all died at the hands of a mad God… Ra has gone mad…’ The fox knelt on the ground and sobbed with grief. His moan of agony added the crowd’s credence to his words as well as their distrust of Ra.

        The Spiritual Beasts still recalled that Ra and the other Gods stood idly by without lending them a helping hand upon the Demons’ invasion back then. From that day on, the seed of suspicion had been planted in their hearts. Ever since then, they stopped relying on Gods and it turned out with a better and flourishing development of the Civilization.
　　
        ‘Why should we worship a mad God like him?!’ As the fox said, all the Spiritual Beasts before the cottage all retreated into a sullen silence.

        ‘Why should we let a mad God that kills us for fun hold the Ancestral Elements?!’ The fox let out a throaty roar at the sky.

        Ra soon knew that it was a set-up when he heard the fox saying the Ancestral Elements. “It’s another set-up for taking the Ancestral Elements.”

        Looking at the hushed beasts whose eyes were filled with distrust and fear, Ra felt drained… and disappointed. Not only was he disappointed at the beasts but also the unnecessary killings the Spiritual Beast made just to set him up.

        Just when Ra was about to speak, a werebird pushed along through the crowd and stood before him, blocking all the gaze for him.

        ‘My Lord is innocent. Those beasts all died of knife wounds. My Lord doesn’t need a knife if he truly wants to kill them.’

        The voice of the werebird sounded just and righteous with a hint of inexplicable familiarity that brought back Ra’s memory of an incident long ago. Facing a group of werewolves, a little werebird almost died for his nebulous justice just to return the stolen goods to their owners.

        Ra recalled the name of that valorous werebird—

        ‘You’re… Pluma.’

        Pluma now had become a well-known hotshot in the Spiritual Beast tribe. Hearing his words, the crowd dissolved into discussion.

        ‘Humph! What a foolish believer who still defends the mad God! I saw him butcher my sons with my own eyes! You said he didn’t need a knife to kill him! But how do you know that he didn’t use it deliberately just for fun?!’ growled the fox in anger.

        ‘If my Lord is the true murderer, how did you even escape from him and come to the street yelling for help?’ asked Pluma.

        ‘I… I… can’t… can’t tell what the mad God would do!’ Cowering, the fox subconsciously touched the necklace on his neck. The sharp-eyed Pluma immediately grabbed the necklace with his hand.

        ‘I don’t know if my Lord is mad or not but I know your necklace! I’ve seen it on the battlefield! This pattern belongs to the Demons! You’re a spy for the Demons, aren’t you?’

        The word ‘Demons’ stirred up the rage inside the Spiritual Beasts. For all those lives lost in the war against the Demons, their hatred for Demons was far deeper than their distrust of Ra. Seeing the outraged crowd, the fox fled right away.

        However, a beam of light fell from the sky and tied up the fox tightly like a belt as Ra raised one of his arms. The enraged beasts encircled the spy and dragged him away for interrogation. Yet, none of them dared to look at Ra. Soon peace was restored.

        ‘I was able to clear my name all thanks to you.’ Ra gave Pluma a smile of relief. The little bird that he had once protected now protected him.

        Perhaps it was exactly Ra’s guidance which led Pluma to a different path from the other Spiritual Beasts.

        He no longer trusted other’s words easily; instead, he made his own judgement, which eventually guided him to a path that was close to justice.

        ‘Pluma, You’ve grown up.’

        For once in a blue moon, Ra smiled. He found that he hadn’t felt such overwhelming joy for a long time ever since his companions all went out for a trip.

        “Perhaps the Spiritual Beasts just need the right amount of guidance to follow the right path.” He then returned to the shrine and started figuring out his next step.
STORY_2824:
One day, Osiris, who roamed around Tarones, came to a village that had been bloodbathed because of war. Seeing the myriad of lost souls, the kind Osiris felt sorry for them so he led them to the magic circle.

        Under Osiris’s guidance, it took quite a while for all the dead souls to go to where they belonged through the magic circle. Yet, a little girl’s soul stayed behind. Standing in front of Osiris, she looked scrawny and fragile.

        Osiris lifted his left hand and said in a gentle and calm voice, ‘come with me.’

        ‘No! I’m too hungry to walk!’ The girl closed her eyes and pouted, tilting her face away. With her arms and legs crossed, she sat on the ground and threw a tantrum, showing no intention to move on.

        He knelt down to the little girl and asked, ‘Then what should I do… so you’ll come with me?’

        Stealthily, the little girl opened one of her eyes and took a glance at Osiris, who was waiting patiently. Only then did she turn around and say excitedly while clenching her fists, ‘I want to eat a lot, a lot of food!’

        “What a wilful soul… Well, since it’s my decision, I’ll help her to the end,” thought Osiris. He then put out a hand, held her bony little hand, and took her to the bustling town.

        The town was even more buzzing in the night—there were dancers dancing along the main street to the accompaniment of piano and flute; the vendors on the sides were clamoring for attention. With the fragrance of flowers and spices filling the air, the astonishing variety of goods and delicacies on the street made a feast for the eyes.

        As the fat oil of the roasted meat dropped on the griller, tongues of flame rose, adding a more tempting glow to the meat. The fruits were ripe and fresh. The little girl drooled at the sweet smell of their juice.

        Her eyes alight with excitement immediately, she flung off Osiris’s hand and pounced on the table of gourmet food before her. Putting her face close to the enticing food before her, she closed her eyes and took a deep breath without reaching out her hand and picking up the food the entire time.

        It was because souls couldn’t eat.

        Watching her from the back, Osiris found the little girl flashed a smile of satisfaction, as though her gaunt face had retrieved its liveliness. Whenever she finished looking around a store, she would raise her head to find her next target, then she would rush to it elatedly.

        A faint smile flickered across Osiris’s lips when he saw the delighted look on the little girl’s face, just as if he could also taste the delectable food. He slowly followed as he watched that little figure bouncing between the stalls.

        Suddenly, a short figure bolted before them. A man was startled that he lifted his barbecue plate and yelled, ‘Beat it! You filthy kid!’

        That figure disappeared at the end of an ally. The little girl’s expression abruptly changed; she stopped in the middle of the street and gazed at the depths of the ally. Darkness was no obscuration to Osiris’s sight. As he followed the direction of her gaze, he saw a skinny kid squatting in a corner and nibbling on rotten food hastily. With a madness of hunger, his hollow eyes darted them a baleful glance.

        The little girl averted her gaze right away back to the fancy food on a stall on her left. She then skipped lightly forward again. As though Osiris understood something, he followed her quietly again with a sigh.

        After passing through the humming street, they came to the gate of the town’s border, where they saw a vast and boundless desert. Under the moonlight, sand swirled like a layer of silvery tulle fluttering in the wind.

        Finally, the little girl stopped. Hanging her head low in the gentle breeze, she whispered softly, ‘I… can go with you now.’

        ‘Okay,’ Osiris replied gingerly. His eyes were filled with inexplicable sorrow and distress. Yet, the little girl gave him a radiant smile in a reassuring way—like the full moon in the sky, bright and complete—as though she sensed his despondency.

        ‘I’m okay. Don’t feel sorry for me.’ The little girl voluntarily took Osiris’s hand and followed him back to the magic circle. As she hopped her way lightly to that sparkling magic circle, her body glowed with the unique blue light of dead souls and gradually dissipated into dust.

        ‘For my whole life… I’ve never felt well-fed and contented.’ Her hair drifting in the breeze soon shattered into pieces of light. Turning her head, she looked back at Osiris and said softly, ‘Thank you.’

        With a smile, Osiris watched the deceased go in solemn silence. As that chapped fingertips and that little figure all turned into flickers of light, they gently touched Osiris’s face like falling petals.

        ‘May you have a better life after reincarnation.’ Reaching out his hand, he held one of the light pieces, which slightly wobbled on his palm. Soon, it was blown away again and immersed into darkness, turning into little starlight…
STORY_2825:
As waves of heat soared with heavy smoke rising into the sky, a summer resort burned vigorously.  The doors and windows were spelled shut, trapping the servants in the inferno until all of them were reduced to ashes.

        Outside the resort was a group of noblemen who watched the heretics and demons stand in a circle around the building while muttering a strange prayer…

        Boom!

        As the house collapsed in the fire, the heretics enveloped the elements in the flames using the servants’ souls

        ‘Come!  My lord!  Here is, the food, we prepared, for you!’ A red monster shouted reverently. His rasping voice was filled with feverish excitement.

        Suddenly, a wave of ominous purple breath emerged and stained the crimson flames black, sweeping through the resort like a dark ocean. The azure sky darkened in an instant, followed by a bolt of lightning breaking through the clouds and creating an eerie magenta vortex.

        A black shadow slowly descended from the vortex. Its body was so enormous that its shadow shrouded everyone around the resort.

        Everyone was trembling in fear. Strangely, they all felt a sudden desire to take a look at the black shadow.

        Sensing the danger, the nobles followed their survival instinct despite their desire for great power. They bit their lips until they bled to suppress the overwhelming desire with the pain. Then they rode away embarrassingly from the sunken resort in the ocean of flames.

        On the other hand, the heretics and demons who worshiped ancient power succumbed to their desire for the unknown. They could not help but raise their heads to look at the mysterious creature hanging in the sky.

        It was a mammoth fiery egg that was covered with thousands of purple fireballs. Besides the unsightly orange blotches that mottled its dark surface, there were great columns of uncanny flames that arced around its rim.

        On the bottom of the flaming egg were countless tentacles of plasma. Pulsating slowly, they absorbed the elements and souls nearby so that the egg could hatch in flames. That was how Cthugha, the Burning One, revealed itself in another world.

        Boom! Boom! Boom! Soon, a series of explosion noises sounded. All the heretics and demons who had taken a look at Cthugha died in a second as their body exploded due to the unbearable pressure that came from the inconceivable manifestation. Their blood stained the ground with crimson.

        Yet, there was still one who managed to maintain his consciousness—it was the red monster. By then, half of his body had already exploded. His head was the only part of his body that still retained its shape. Even so, he kept gazing intently upon Cthugha as it slowly descended as if he could not feel any pain.

        “Oh… So this is my lord… How majestic and sacred… Even my words of praise are blasphemy against him…”

        Perhaps the red monster’s gaze was too passionate—Cthugha finally lowered its head to look at the insignificant creature that it usually would not lay its eyes on. Its gaze intensified the erosion in the monster’s body. Most of the monster’s flesh had been melted, except for one of his eyes.

        However, even that did not stop the monster from admiring Cthugha. Stretching out his right hand which had been reduced to bones, he murmured enthusiastically, ‘My… My lord of eternal flames… Thank you- Thank you for looking down at me… Please use me… use my flesh and blood to nourish your flames…’

        Even though Cthugha could not comprehend the intense emotions of such an insignificant creature, it liked the blazing fire inside his heart, so it decided to keep it burning—a purple fireball separated from Cthugha and wormed into the monster’s body.

        As the monster found his body filled with energy, his damaged flesh and nerves began to rebuild in a warm flame. It only took a while for the monster to gain a new body that was even stronger than before.

        Later, Cthugha and the reborn monster went to a volcano where abundant fire elements lay. After they stored enough power, it took on a new appearance that was close to the primordial dragons and met Agatha, the maiden of the sacred rites…
STORY_2826:
In the Heavenly Kingdom, a male Xian was riding a spotted tiger, galloping across the sky. With his sleeves fluttering in the wind and sparks of electricity running along the whip on his waist, he looked so unfettered and majestic that other Xians went around lest they stood in his way.

        The male Xian, Shen Gongbao, went all the way to a Xian’s residence. Without asking for the owner’s permission, he pushed open the door and walked into the house while shouting wantonly, ‘Brother! I’ve mastered a new technique! Come practice with me— Is he away from home again?’

        Shen Gongbao was plunged into disappointment when he walked to the study where he didn’t see Jiang Ziya. Perhaps because of the great discontent, he failed to notice a little fox that was watching him secretly in the dark.

        It was Daji, a vixen that had been saved by Jiang Ziya. By then, she was gritting her teeth while thinking spitefully, “Darn it! It’s the annoying Shen Gongbao again… Jiang Shang wouldn’t have gone to the human world and left me alone in the house if it wasn’t for him… Ugh! I have to find a way to get rid of him, or else Jiang Shang won’t have much time to be with me.”

        As Daji turned her brilliant eyes, an idea popped up in her mind. Soon after she mustered her power, the little fox turned into Jiang Ziya in an instant. Then, ‘he’ walked to Shen Gongbao, who was still searching around the room, from a dark corner.

        ‘Since Brother isn’t here, I guess I’ll just come back tomorrow— Brother!’Shen Gongbao’s eyes lit up as he saw ‘Jiang Ziya’. He immediately stepped forward and said excitedly, ‘So you are at home! Great! Let’s have a duel now!’

        ‘Brother, I’m sorry but I’m caught up in something more important, so please forgive me for turning down your invitation.’ 

        Daji’s incredible acting successfully fooled Shen Gongbao into believing that he was rejected by his Brother again, which frustrated him.

        ‘That excuse again… You’re always caught up in something whenever I ask you to practice with me. Just say it! Just say that you despise me and you don’t think I’m good enough to be your opponent!’

        ‘Brother, please don’t say that. You are extremely talented and I’m sure you will achieve great things. It’s just that I have  gotten too much on my plate.’

        ‘I’m happy to help you as long as you promise to have a duel with me!’

        ‘That helps a lot! The apricot flag was damaged in the fight with the elves a few days ago, and I need a hundred Phoenix Feathers to repair it. Brother, could you please help me get the feathers?’

        ‘A piece of cake!’ Shen Gongbao rode his tiger away after leaving those words.

        When the real Jiang Ziya went back to his residence and saw the gloating Daji, he couldn’t help but ask her curiously, ‘Why are you so happy?’

        ‘I’ve just solved a big problem for you.’ And so, Daji told Jiang Ziya about Shen Gongbao’s visit. ‘The Phoenix Feathers are hard to find so that should be able to keep him away from you for a few days.’

        Unexpectedly, Jiang Ziya didn’t burst into laughter. Instead, he scolded Daji severely, ‘Nonsense! It’s now the hatching season of the Phoenixes. Whoever breaks into their territory will be attacked by the clan! That’s way too much for a prank!’

        ‘I-I didn’t know! Don’t yell at me! I only did this for you!’ Distressed by Jiang Ziya’s harsh reprimand, Daji couldn’t help but stomp her feet, then she turned back into a fox and left.

        “This happens because of Ziya so Ziya has to fix it!”

        Riding his mystical pet, Sibuxiang, Jiang Ziya hurried to the Phoenixes' territory, only to find his Brother surrounded by a group of Phoenixes and covered with wounds halfway through.

        Since the Phoenixes were a kind of mystical creature in the Heavenly Kingdom, Shen Gongbao did not want to attack them with thunder. That was why he could not break through the siege but only tried his best to protect his body with Xian energy.

        However, the Phoenixes’ attacks only grew fiercer. Just when he was about to lose, dozens of yellow talismans came down from the sky and hit the Phoenixes precisely, causing them to fall to the ground unconscious.

        ‘Run!’ Jiang Ziya shouted.

        Shen Gongbao mounted his tiger and left with Jiang Ziya as soon as he had collected himself. The two later landed by a lake in the forest.

        ‘Brother, what are you doing here?’

        ‘It’s all my fault.’ Jiang Ziya then told Shen Gongbao how Daji had fooled him by disguising herself. Shen Gongbao, of course, was enraged, and he exclaimed, ‘That cunning vixen! How dare she disguises as you and play me!’

        ‘Please forgive me, Brother. I will take Daji with me and make a proper apology to you the other day.’ Jiang Ziya asked for Shen Gongbao’s forgiveness, making a Fist-and-palm salute.

        Soon, Shen Gongbao’s anger slightly subsided. He hesitated for a while before he thanked Jiang Ziya awkwardly with his face tilted away, ‘Well… Thanks. I would have no choice but to kill all the Phoenixes with thunder if you hadn’t rescued me just in time.’

        ‘Brother, it was the least I could do. I had to help you since it is my honor to have a worthy opponent like you.’

        “A worthy opponent… Does it mean he recognizes me?” Shen Gongbao was overjoyed to hear Jiang Ziya’s compliment. With the overwhelming excitement in his chest, he couldn’t help but ask, ‘So Brother, can we have a duel today?’

        ‘...You’re injured and I have used all my power. Let’s call it a day.’ Jiang Ziya rode Shibuxiang into the air and fled as soon as he finished saying those words…
STORY_2827:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.3

        On the day of the Century Feast, the rebel army stormed the banquet hall. Fortunately, Cornflower and Nepenthes arrived just in time to save Hyacinth. However, Papaver, the leader of the rebellion, had disappeared from the hall by then, so Nepenthes captured one of the rebels and interrogated him only to learn that she had headed to Blossomville with the rest of the rebel fighters.

        ‘She must be aiming for the Mother Tree! We can’t let her get what she wants! Nepenthes, you stay here and deal with the rebels while I take the troop to Blossomville!’ Cornflower led his troop to Blossomville as soon as he delegated duties to Nepenthes. Still, he was one step too late.

        When he stepped into Blossomville, Papaver was pulling a dagger out of Mysorensis’ body. With sap gushing from her wound, Mysorensis powerlessly fell into the ocean of flowers. Petals flew everywhere, some landing near Papaver’s feet.

        ‘Madam Mysorensis!’ Cornflower shouted.

        ‘He is… Cornflower the third prince… Great… He came just at the right time…’ As Papaver looked at Cornflower and his troop, a murderous smile appeared on her face. She ruthlessly trampled down the petals that were soaked in Mysorensis’ sap as though to release the madness hidden in her heart, foreshadowing what she was going to do next.

        ‘Everyone! Now it’s the time to eradicate those atrocious elves in the enchantment who have oppressed us! Let the Mother Tree be ours!’ shouted Papaver, who pointed her weapon at Cornflower. Her call heightened the rebel army’s blood lust, urging them to raise their weapons and charge at the imperial army after responding to their leader with a roar in unison.

        ‘Soldiers! At my order, capture all the rebels and kill whoever resists you!’ Corflower’s face darkened in an instant. As he raised his sword and gave the order, all the imperial soldiers unsheathed their weapons to repel the rebels.

        While the soldiers contained the rebellion, Cornflower ran straight to the Mother Tree, where Papaver was. Knowing that the female floral-elf was the rebels’ leader, he decisively drew his sword and thrust at her without mercy.

        Unexpectedly, Papaver took out a thorny whip from her waist as if she had anticipated what Cornflower would do. With a spin of her wrist, the whip caught the prince’s sword and restrained his movements.

        ‘Humph! It seems you’re nothing more than that!’ Papaver gave a cold snort. Then she pulled her whip trying to disarm Cornflower by taking away his sword. However, she failed to do so because of some force, so she took a closer look only to find that there was a thin layer of ice on her whip causing it to stick firmly to the sword.

        ‘You should be talking about yourself!’ Cornflower channeled his power to freeze Papaver’s entire whip with a sudden burst of cold gas. Then, crack! The whip shattered into pieces as he forcefully moved his hand.

        As soon as Cornflower broke the whip, he continued his attack with a nimble spin. Even though Papaver managed to protect her vitals, she still got stabbed in the right shoulder, and her sap began to spurt.

        Just when Cornflower was going to make another attack, he felt an ominous vibration from his right. His body took a step back by reflex but he still failed to dodge the attack. A gash as long as a palm was made on his right leg and he started bleeding. What was worse was that his skin around the wound began to turn dark purple and it was spreading over his body.

        ‘It’s… poison… You put poison on your dagger!’ Cornflower cried out in pain as he felt tingles in his wound.

        ‘That’s right.’ Papaver raised her left hand in which was her weapon—a dagger tipped with poison. She then continued, ‘I didn’t expect the prince to be such a skillful fighter. You left me no choice but to use my secret weapon. Just so you know, the poison on this dagger is rare to find. It only takes a few drops to paralyze an elf.’

        ‘You… Argh…’ The tingles had spread over Cornflower’s entire right leg over their short conversation. Losing the ability to stand, he could only support his body with his long sword.

        Papaver slowly leaned toward Cornflower and said with a cold laugh, ‘No one can stop me from getting back what belongs to me!’

        After leaving those words, Papaver held her dagger up high and thrust it straight at Cornflower.

        “No! I can’t die yet! I have to protect this kingdom and the Mother Tree!”

        Cornflower rolled over the ground in desperation to dodge Papaver’s attack. He then scraped the entire wound as well as the infected flesh using his sword. His right leg regained a little sensation as his sap spurted out along with the poison.

        ‘Now die!’ Gritting his teeth, Cornflower endured the agonizing pain in his wound and leaped to make a lunge at Papaver, who was defenseless against his unexpected attack, and naturally, his sword pierced through her heart.

        ‘Argh…’ Letting out a scream of pain, the seriously wounded Papaver fell under the Mother Tree. Petals fell from the sky like a flurry of snow with sunlight dappling her face through the branches. All the flowers and sunlight should have belonged to her but they had been stripped away from her because of some ridiculous reasons. That was why she decided to take back everything that she deserved, but she eventually failed.

        “Why?”

        “I was only a step away from the Mother Tree. I could have bathed in the light of the Mother Tree, and retained my pride and my parents’ dignity… ”

        “How unreasonable… Why… Why does the Mother Tree belong to those hideous elves?!”

“Since I can’t get the Mother Tree, then no one can have her!”

        Papaver mustered the power in her body and summoned an eerie purple flame with overflowing despair and hatred as her fuel, setting her flesh and soul on fire. The fire of madness climbed up the Mother Tree and ignited all her leaves, stems and branches.

        Seeing the Mother Tree in danger, Cornflower anxiously walked to her. Yet, his paralyzed legs dragged him down to the ground.

        Even though the concentration of the poison had been temporarily reduced when Cornflower removed the infected tissue, it did not stop it from flowing through his body. The tingling sensation slowly spread from his leg to his upper body. He could feel that his heart was slowing down. Even so, his mind was still fixated on the burning Mother Tree.

        “The Mother Tree… We have to… put out the fire immediately…” Cornflower reached out his hand. However, the poison has spread to his head, blurring his sight. There was only one thought left in his fading consciousness: “May Lily… Quick… Mmm''

        Unfortunately, Cornflower was already at the end of his strength. He fell into a coma before May Lily came, leaving the helpless imperial troop in a panic alone with the rebel fighters whose spirit had been dampened by the loss of their leader…
STORY_2828:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.7

        On the day of the Century Feast, Sakura came out of a deep coma with Rose’s help. The two hurried to Blossomville to save the Mother Tree as soon as they sensed that she was in danger.

        When they arrived at Blossomville, the Mother Tree was already engulfed in dark purple flames. Surrounding the Mother Tree like high walls, the eerie flames were so strong that the fire did not die down a bit even though the soldiers had been pouring water over it.

        “This… They’ve crossed the line… The Mother Tree will die in flames and the entire kingdom… No! I have to stop the fire and protect the Mother Tree!”

        Sakura clenched her hands into tight fists. All of a sudden, she decisively grabbed a water bucket from one of the soldiers and poured all the water onto herself. Then she dashed through the walls of flames and ran to the Mother Tree without saying a word. Her action was totally unexpected, leaving Rose and the soldiers no time to stop her but to watch her disappear into the sea of flames.

        “It’s so hot… It feels like my whole body is going to dry...”

        It was hot in the sea of flames. The steaming heat coming from all directions scorched every inch of Sakura’s body. Even her breaths were burning. The water that she had poured on her body evaporated in just a short moment.

        Sakura, who nearly fainted from suffocation in the fire, hurriedly bit her lip to retain her consciousness with pain. Holding the guardian’s staff, she mustered her power to break the fire and create a path to the Mother Tree.

        She hobbled down the path step by step using the staff as a walking stick. Suddenly, she heard a horrifying sound above her head—a thick burning branch snapped because of the fire, falling straight to where Sakura was standing!

        ‘I have to dodge it… Argh!’ As much as Sakura wanted to pounce forward to avoid the falling branch, her legs had dried up because of the heat. Unable to make a jump, she could only fall to the ground and watch the falling branch get closer to her—

        In the nick of time, a flash of golden light appeared and turned into a translucent figure who blocked the branch!


        Sakura recognized the figure at a glance. With her eyes widening in surprise, she shouted excitedly, ‘Teacher!’

        “Sakura, don’t give up. I have faith in you… I’m waiting for you under the Mother Tree…” While Mysorensis’s tender words echoed in Sakura’s head, her figure slowly faded away and eventually disappeared into the flames, leaving the young guardian alone.

        “Teacher… I won’t let you down!” Pulling herself together, Sakura propped herself up with the staff and walked toward the path that Mysorensis had created for her.

        Despite the tormenting heat, the scorching tongues of flames that touched her face, and her charred feet, Sakura did not stop. Finally, she made it to an unburning corner before the Mother Tree where Mysorensis breathed her last.

        Sakura’s body and heart shuddered when she saw Mysorensis’ body. Although she had known that Mysorensis was dead, it was still a heartbreaking and inconceivable truth for her to take in. Grief swept over her like a tide and cut her heart like a dagger, filling her eyes with tears.

        Sakura tried her best to fight back her tears because she was on an important mission. She simply walked to her teacher and gently held her hand.

        “I will protect the Mother Tree for you so please rest in peace, teacher. I will not run away from my responsibility again.”

        After saying her last goodbye to Mysorensis, Sakura walked to the Mother Tree and put her hand on the trunk while raising the staff. As she channeled her power into the staff, countless illuminating dust surged and swirled around her, flooding her thoughts and pushing the scorching heat away from her mind. She closed her eyes. In the darkness she saw countless sparkles flying up——

        She became one with the Mother Tree; she saw Blossomville, the whole kingdom, the entire Tarones, and then she learned the truth.

        “I see… The gluttonous gods want to take the elements as their own and that is what makes the Mother Tree weak and dampens her light…” Sakura closed her eyes in sorrow. 

        “There are only two choices left for me now: I either use my power to extinguish the flames and keep the Mother Tree alive, or I sacrifice the Mother Tree, release her power to give every floral-elves our mother’s last blessing and then find new opportunities for the kingdom.”

        In a dilemma, Sakura began rubbing her fingers unconsciously. She did not know which choice was the correct one. As the guardian, saving the Mother Tree should be her first priority; however, what would the floral-elves’ future be if she chose the Mother Tree? .

        “I don’t know what is the right decision. Bad things may happen if I make the wrong choice again just like the last time. Am I really capable of making the right choice…”

        Suddenly, a speck of illuminating dust emerged from the darkness and flew to Sakura. Then, a familiar voice sounded in Sakura’s mind and said, “You don’t have to be afraid. Something never goes away even after you make a choice. My child, there is hope as long as you’re still alive.”

        ‘Teacher…’ Looking at that speck of illuminating dust, Sakura was moved.

        “Yeah, I struggle to make a decision because I’m afraid of changes but changing is never wrong. Changes are both opportunities and hope!”

        Sakura blinked. She looked more determined than ever. Lowering her hand reverently, she clasped her hands and asked the Mother Tree, ‘Please release your power and lighten up our future!’

        At Sakura’s plea, the burning Mother Tree released a burst of blinding light. The eerie purple flames turned into white and burned even brighter.

        The magnificent Mother Tree withered and shrank in the white flames in an instant. Its body turned into numerous illuminating dust and scattered across the entire Plantdom like a milky way in a starry night, infiltrating every floral-elf’s body and bringing them new energy.

        Bathing in the Mother Tree’s last blessing, all the floral-elves uncontrollably shed tears of grief, mourning their mother who had given their land and their kingdom protection for years…
STORY_2829:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.1

        Since Welwitschia, the king of Plantdom, had fallen into a coma because of poisoning, Hyacinth became the host of the Century Feast with the support of the nobles. After giving an exuberant speech on the feast, he went back to the palace with the nobles to have an after-party. By the time Hyacinth arrived at the banquet hall, his wife, Paperwhite was already sitting on the dais waiting for him. He sat next to her, then he looked at the noble floral-elves below. Pleased and proud, he raised his glass.
　　
        ‘Thank you for all your hard work. The Century Feast would not be possible without your help, so cheers to you all!’

        Unexpectedly, all the nobles turned their glasses upside-down, pouring the dew onto the floor. Their actions and the mess on the floor made Hyacinth’s face darken in an instant.

        ‘What are you all doing? I thought everyone wanted the dew of the Mother Tree. Was I wrong?’ Hyacinth asked while suppressing his anger.

        However, Hyacinth’s question fell on deaf ears. Among the nobles who were all wearing frigid expressions, the one standing at the front gave a snort of contempt and said, ‘Your Highness, are you still trying to lie to us at this point? We knew the dew you’ve been giving us is fake.’

        As staggered as Hyacinth was at his crime being exposed, he still attempted to maintain his composure and said, ‘What are you talking about?! Who told you that ridiculous rumor? There’s no way I would lie to you!’

        ‘I told them.’ A voice sounded from the side of Hyacinth in a tone so soft and gentle that seemed incongruent with the strained atmosphere in the hall.

        ‘No… Why would you…’ Hyacinth turned his face and looked at Paperwhite—the elf who spoke—in disbelief.

        Paperwhite had an extremely pale face that barely had any colors except for her red-tinted lips. She gazed steadily into Hyacinth’s face. However, the admiration and love that used to fill her eyes were then replaced by a cold and profound determination that sent a shudder through the prince’s heart. Even so, the prince refused to believe the elf who loved him so deeply would do such things to him.

        ‘Paperwhite, stop messing with me. Clear things up now. This isn’t something you can joke about.’

        ‘I’m not joking,’ said Paperwhite with a scornful dry smile. Without seeing such an aggressive side of his wife in the past, Hyacinth was so staggered that he forgot to stop Paperwhite from continuing her words.

        ‘You plotted everything to marry me so that you could get to the Mother Tree. It’s such a pity that you never got your wish because you weren’t even allowed to be near the Mother Tree nor to get her dew under my mother’s order—’

        ‘Shut it!’ It was only then did Hyacinth finally realize that Paperwhite had gone out of his control. He abruptly swung his arm and yelled to cut her short. ‘Enough with your nonsense! Just beat it!’

        When Hyacinth strode to the front of Paperwhite trying to push her away, the noble elves all stood up and grabbed him, then forcibly pressed him against the floor.

        ‘You— Damn it!’ Even though Hyacinth struggled desperately, he alone could not resist the strength of multiple elves so he could only growl like a captured animal with his eyes bloodshot and his face contorting with rage.

        Paperwhite felt an indescribable sense of joy as she watched Hyacinth shaking with embarrassment. She could not help but recall the day she got her heart shattered—the day when Hyacinth told her that she would never be the elf he loved. She still had vivid memories of the pain she felt that day. His words were like countless daggers that kept stabbing her heart until it was completely broken into pieces.

        A sudden wave of mixed emotions—sorrows, grievance, resentment—swept over Paperwhite, trapping her like a black sealed box. All the negative emotions continued to gnaw away at her heart, tainting the vibrant love she had for Hyacinth with deep darkness.

        Paperwhite knew that she could never stop loving Hyacinth for the seed of love had been planted so deep in her soul that it wouldn’t disappear even though she knew that her husband had never loved her. It was also her overwhelming love for him that made it impossible for her to not feel jealous, whether it was the elf that her husband loved or the throne that he had always wanted; she was jealous of all the things that took Hyacinth’s attention.

        The jealousy she felt was even stronger, deeper, and more overpowering than the one she had felt for Sakura.

        She thought that she would eventually be the love and center of Hyacinth’s life one day as long as she kept loving him and helping him quietly. Yet, her dream was soon shattered by Hyacinth, who said that she would never be the one for him.

        So she crumbled.

        She decided to be Hyacinth’s deepest regret if she could never be the love of his life, and thus she made a plan of ruining the Century Feast as well as shattering Hyacinth’s lifelong dream of taking the throne.

        When Paperwhite was drawing up her plan, a noble elf came for Hyacinth, who just happened to be out of the palace, so she received him.

        The elf straightforwardly asked Paperwhite for more dew, mistaking her as an insider who knew about the trade of the Mother Tree’s dew between the nobles and the prince. Paperwhite realized that Hyacinth had been lying to the nobles the moment she heard the elf because her mother never allowed other elves to be near the Mother Tree and it was impossible for Hyacinth to collect her dew. He must have been deceiving the nobles and winning their loyalty with fake dew.

        Paperwhite immediately told the elf the truth and exposed Hyacinth’s crime while offering him a deal.

        ‘I can give you the real dew as long as you help me.’

        ‘How would I know if you aren’t lying to me like Hyacinth?!’

        ‘You can trust me because I’m the daughter of Mysorensis, the guardian of the Mother Tree. I can go in and out of Blossomville and see the Mother Tree whenever I want but Hyacinth can never do that.’ Paperwhite then pointed at the elf’s rotting arm and said, ‘Besides, I don’t think you have much time to waste.’

        Without any other choices except to say yes, the noble elf gritted his teeth and said, ‘Okay, what do you want?’

        ‘I…’ As Paperwhite closed her eyes, different images of Hyacinth appeared in her head; everything about him had been long imprinted on her mind.

        “I want him to always think of me. I don’t care if he hates me as long as he never forgets me.” 

        A wry smile tugged at the corner of Paperwhite’s mouth as a funny thought came up to her. 

        “If I can’t be the love of his life, then he shall not be the king of anyone’s life. From that perspective, we’ll finally be a match made in heaven.”

        When Paperwhite opened her eyes, they were no longer filled with tenderness but a deep gloom. Then she said in a rare ruthless tone, ‘I want Hyacinth to lose everything!’
STORY_2830:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.8

        In a musty room without sunlight where pots of plants and flowers wilted desolately in the shade, Stretlizia sat alone in a corner gazing out of the window quietly. She looked rather relieved for some reason. 

        Through the window, she saw the thriving Blossomville, which had recovered from the fire not long ago, and the sky looked even more boundless without the towering Mother Tree, which had been burned into ashes in the outcasts’ rebellion.

        On the day of the Century Feast, Papaver and her rebel army stormed into the palace. By Sakura’s choice, the Mother Tree was sacrificed. With all its power released, the Mother Tree met its end in flames after giving the floral-elves its last bloom of light.

        Although the Mother Tree’s light could spare the remaining floral-elves from withering temporarily, no one knew when it would be exhausted so the elves needed to find a new source of light.

        The rebel army, who also survived because of the Mother Tree’s light, fell apart as soon as they lost their target, and in the end, they were subdued by the imperial soldiers. All the elves, including Nepenthes, Rose, and the other innocent outcasts, managed to start a new life in the kingdom under Cornflower’s leadership.

        It was then that Hyacinth, the first prince, who was devastated by the death of his wife, Paperwhite, had a spiritual awakening. He finally let go of his fixation with the throne and volunteered himself to join the expedition team to find new light sources so as to make amends for what he had done to Paperwhite.

        On the other hand, Strelitzia, the first princess, was confined to the palace temporarily for her treachery of using her authority to sneak the rebellious outcasts into the palace, thus putting the kingdom in danger.

        As a result, Cornflower, the second prince, became the best heir to the throne, and today was his coronation. Yet, Strelitzia, who was forbidden to leave her chamber, had no choice but to miss the ceremony.

        Strelitzia was willing to receive punishment knowing her mistakes. The only regret she had was that she was unable to see Sakura, who had come out of the coma. She turned around and walked to her desk on which was a vase holding a cherry blossom branch that she had asked a maid to pick so as to ease her pain of lovesickness.

        She held out a hand to caress the buds on the branch. A stoical smile tugged at the corners of her mouth.

        “She should be standing beside Cornflower as the future queen right now,” she thought.

        However, Strelitzia was wrong.

        The door suddenly opened. Strelitzia turned around only to see Sakura, the elf of her dream.

        ‘Sakura!’ Strelitzia shouted in surprise. She hurriedly walked toward Sakura as soon as she found that it was not her imagination, and asked, ‘What are you doing here? Isn’t today Cornflower’s coronation? Shouldn’t you be by his side as his fiancée now?’

        ‘Cory sent me here. He has waived your punishment and you’re free now. As for our engagement, well…’ Sakura said with a smile that was no longer bashful but calm and sophisticated. She then continued, ‘I’ve broken off my engagement with Cory.’

        ‘Huh?’ Shocked, Strelitzia asked anxiously, ‘Why? I thought you two liked each other.’

‘Yes, we did but our feelings were different. Cory liked me in a sense that was romantically exclusive but I didn’t; I liked him just the same way I liked everyone else, like you, Strelitzia. So, I had to put things right.’

        “So I was no different from Cornflower…” Even though Strelitzia had long known that her feelings for Sakura would never be reciprocated, it still hurt her to hear the answer from Sakura. The heartbreak squeezed Strelitzia’s heart and she was at a loss for words for a moment.

        ‘Besides, I have my own mission now.’ Sakura lifted her hands to show Strelitzia a small flower pot. In the pot was a sprout sparkling with an iridescent glow.

        ‘I found this sprout in the soil where the Mother Tree used to be. I was worried that the bird might hurt it so I moved it to the pot. Maybe it will carry on the Mother Tree’s will and become the next Mother Tree!’ Giving Strelitzia a bright smile, Sakura added, ‘There is always hope as long as we’re alive, so I believe someone brilliant like you will be okay, Strelitzia.’

        The overflowing happiness on Sakura’s face warmed Strelitzia’s heart and she thought, “Yeah. I will learn to get over you and find my own path one day.”
STORY_2831:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.6

        In order to crush the rebellion of the outcasts, Rose and Nepenthes made a plan with Cornflower to capture all of them once and for all on the day of the Century Feast. Unexpectedly, Papaver used Strelitzia to sneak her army into the palace. Since the situation had changed, Cornflower and May Lily decided to split into two teams.

        Following Cornflower’s team, Rose and Nepenthes went to rescue Hyacinth. However, Papaver had already led her troop into Blossomville so Cornflower went to stop her while Nepenthes stayed at the place. In the meantime, Nepenthes sent Rose to find May Lily for help immediately.

        By the time Rose arrived at Strelitzia’s palace, May Lily had already headed to Blossomville. After knowing that Rosemellow had locked Strelitzia in a room, she helped break the door and saved the princess right before she was about to fall off the window.

        ‘Go save Sakura! Rosemellow has sent assassins to murder her!’ The drug and the fight with Rosemellow had completely exhausted Strelitzia that she uncontrollably passed out after telling Rose the news.

        “Oh no… Now that Madam Mysorensis is dead, Sakura is the only guardian of the Mother Tree. I must hurry!” Knowing how serious things had gotten, Rose hurried to where Sakura was with the elite soldiers.

        As soon as Rose stepped into the courtyard, she met a group of the outcasts. Amid the clanking swords, Rose, who remained safe under the soldiers’ protection, caught a glimpse of two outcasts running away from the battlefield under the cover of their companions; they were going straight to Sakura’s bedroom.

        “They must be the assassins! I have to stop them!” Rose gritted her teeth and chased after the two floral-elves. As much as the soldiers wanted to follow her, the outcasts got in the way so they could only watch Rose disappear into the hallway.

        ‘Ha… They… They run… so fast…’ Even though Rose ran desperately while holding her dress, she was still unable to catch up with the elves but only watched them break into Sakura’s bedroom. By the time she made it there, an elf was already aiming her dagger at the sleeping Sakura.

        “Ding it!” Like a cat on a hot tin roof, Rose was so anxious that she rashly picked up a brick on the ground and threw it at the two elves. Miraculously, the brick hit the back of the male floral-elf’s head.

        ‘Ouch!’ The male floral-elf let out a groan of pain. He turned around to look who attacked him, only to see another stone flying toward his face. Luckily, the female floral-elf beside him was quick enough to deflect the stone with a dagger.

        Enraged by Rose’s attacks, the male floral-elf strode to her. As he swiftly grabbed her hands, he gave her a knee strike on her knees to make her kneel on the ground. Then he put his dagger against her neck and asked in a stern tone, ‘Who are you?’

        ‘Are you stupid?’ The female floral-elf sneered. She walked to Rose and pulled her waist-length hair violently, and said, ‘Look at her silky and shiny hair. That only belongs to those overly pampered noble elves.’

        ‘Tut!’ Smacking his tongue in disgust, the male floral-elf gave Rose a sharp slap so vigorously that made her face swell up immediately. ‘It’s all because the trash elves like you that we have to live in misery!’

        ‘No…’ Rose murmured softly with her head hanging low. Her voice was so weak that it sounded almost inaudible for the male assassin who reflexively bent over to hear her better without noticing how close he had gotten to Rose. That was why he failed to avoid Rose’s head-butt when she abruptly raised her head. The awful pain in his chin forced him to let out a shrill scream and loosened his grip on her with the dagger in his hand falling to the ground.

        ‘What… Ah!’ Taken aback by Rose’s sudden attack, the female assassin hurriedly grabbed Rose’s hair but her attempt was meant to be vain since Rose had already grasped the dagger and swung it upward—

        —Swish! Rose cut off her hair with the dagger to free herself from the female floral-elf’s restraint. Then she immediately grabbed the arm of the male flower-elf who was still groaning in pain. Putting her right foot forward, she flipped him over her shoulder so neatly and threw him precisely at the female elf, knocking the both of them down at once.

        With a flick of her uneven short hair, Rose victoriously looked down at the unconscious assassins on the ground and said aloud, ‘I am a noble elf but I’m not the trash you said, just as I know not all the outcasts are bastards like you two!’

        Afterward, Rose tied the two assassins up with some bed sheets in case they would attack her and Sakura again. Just when she was going to take them out of Sakura’s bedroom, she heard a grunt of pain from the bed.

        ‘Mm…’

        Rose hurriedly ran to the bed only to find that Sakura was tossing and turning instead of sleeping soundly. Her face was sickly pale and her forehead was beaded with cold sweat, as if she was suffering from great pain.

        ‘No… Everyone will sink into misery… I have to… Mm!’

        ‘Huh?! Wait! What… What is happening?!’ Rose paced the room nervously. When she finally decided to call the doctor , she saw something shining on the bedside.

        “That is… the guardian’s staff!” Rose took the staff which was made of intertwined vine with a gallery of pink cherry blossom petals on the top that held a handful of limpid water. In the center was a clear crystal that was shedding a scorching pink light.

        “I can feel the power of the Mother Tree from the light… Could it be Sakura calling for the Mother Tree’s power…? I can’t figure it out! What the hell! Things can’t be worse anyway, let me just give it a try!”

        Holding the staff, Rose walked to Sakura and poured the limpid water into her mouth…
STORY_2832:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.4

        On the day of the Century Feast, May Lily learned dreadful news from the soldiers—Cornflower was dead. However, he refused to believe it without seeing the prince’s body himself so he left the soldiers and ran straight to Blossomville, where the Mother Tree was.

        In the middle of his way, he spotted that the towering Mother Tree was engulfed in purple flames which only continued to grow without any signs of going out. The unusual phenomenon sent a sense of dread in his chest so he broke into a sprint, fearing the worst.

        May Lily knew that there had been a bloody battle the moment he stepped into Blossomville; the flowerbeds were all trampled and there were petals scattered over the ground soaked in different elves’ sap.

        By then, the war seemed to have come to an end. The rebel army who had been defeated by the imperial troop was detained on the right side of an open space while the wounded soldiers gathered on the left. Meanwhile, the remaining soldiers who were still able to walk were busy carrying buckets of water to douse the flames on the Mother Tree.

        ‘Where’s the prince?’ asked Cornflower, grabbing a soldier’s collar. He could not care less about the Mother Tree for nothing mattered more than Cornflower to him. Panicked, the soldier pointed to a corner where three soldiers were squatting in a circle around someone.

        With a few strides, May Lily walked to the soldiers and shoved them aside only to see Cornflower motionless on the ground. His face looked deathly pale and he seemed to have no sign of life.

        ‘May Lily, Prince Cornflower has…’ One of the soldiers stumbled choking with tears.

        ‘No! There’s no way he’s dead!’ May Lily refused to accept the reality since he had a feeling that he would be denying the possibility of Cornflower being still alive once he nodded and accepted it as the truth, even though the chance was faint. Holding the prince’s body in his arm, he put both his hands on Cornflower’s chest and channeled his power so that the elements could heal his body. Still, there was no response from Cornflower.

        ‘You said you’d be my purpose of living . You asked me to live for you so you can’t die before I do!’ Instead of giving up, May Lily continued to send his power into the prince’s body.

        ‘Lub-dub.’ Suddenly, May Lily felt an extremely faint pulse inside Cornflower so he put his ear to the latter’s chest and listened carefully—the prince’s heart was beating slowly.

        “I can hear his heart beat. Even though it’s slow, his heart is still beating!” May Lily straightened up his body in excitement and shouted at the soldiers, ‘The prince is still alive! Call the doctor, now!’

        The soldiers immediately ran to fetch the doctor. A senior doctor soon came and performed a careful examination of Cornflower. After a moment, he said in a deep tone, ‘There is an extremely rare poison in Prince Cornflower’s body. It is a deadly poison that can paralyze an elf and cause heart failure as it circulates around the body through blood flow. It seems that the Prince had great blood loss that helped reduce the amount of toxin in his body, but I’m afraid he won’t be able to make it.’

        ‘Then what are you waiting for?! Just give him the antidote!’ said May Lily hastily, forgetting all his manners.

        ‘Unfortunately, there’s no antidote to this poison. The only cure is to replace his sap with another floral-elf’s but it is only a temporary solution—the other elf will die of the poison.’

        ‘That’s easy. Take my sap—’ Just when May Lily lifted his arm to give his hand to the doctor, a delicate dagger decorated with gems fell out of his sleeve. The dagger was a gift that Cornflower had given him in the past.

        Back then, May Lily and Cornflower accompanied Sakura to the mountain to collect some herbs but they encountered a ferocious giant spider on the way. In order to help Sakura and Cornflower escape, he used himself as bait to distract the spider only to put himself on the brink of death. Luckily, Cornflower came back just in time with a troop of soldiers to save him.

        It was only until later when Cornflower and Sakura expressed their anxiety and anger that May Lily finally realized how much they cared about him and began to value himself.

        On the next day after the incident, Cornflower paid him a visit. Putting both his hands on May Lily’s shoulders, he said seriously, ‘May Lily, don’t glorify the acts of sacrifice. You’d only be self-absorbed to think I wanted you to do that for me.’

        ‘But… How am I gonna help you then?’ A rare look of vulnerability and confusion appeared on May Lily’s face.

        ‘It’s simple.’ Cornflower took out an expensive dagger and shoved it into May Lily’s arms. He looked incredibly radiant as the sunlight fell on his azur hair.

        ‘If you really care about me and want me to be happy, then never sacrifice yourself for me. Instead, use this dagger to cut through all difficulties and live for me!’

        As Cornflower’s words sounded in May Lily’s head, they brought a resigned smile to his face.

        “You still manage to find a way to remind me not to sacrifice myself for you when you’re literally on your deathbed, don’t you?” May Lily took a deep breath to calm himself down and organize his disquieting thoughts.

        ‘Sir May Lily?’ The doctor asked in bewilderment after seeing May Lily lapse into silence.

        ‘...No. He would never want any elf to sacrifice their life for his.’ Clenching his hands into fists, May Lily said with determined gaze, ‘There should be another way! I will save him no matter how!’ 

        Coincidentally, a miracle that could save Cornflower happened the second after May Lily said those words—Sakura was there in Blossomville. To his astonishment, she came out of the deep coma and ran straight to the burning Mother Tree!

        When May Lily was going to rescue her after hearing the news, a burst of blinding light came from the Mother Tree, then it burst across the sky and scattered like sparkling dust, melting into every elf’s body, inside and outside the enchantment, including the poisoned Cornflower.

        The power of the Mother Tree purified the poison in Cornflower’s body and pulled him away from the brink of death, bringing him back to life.

        ‘Mmm…’ Cornflower utter a low groan.

        ‘Cornflower!’ May Lily shouted Cornflower’s name emotionally with tears brimming over his eyes uncontrollably; he completely lost his usual composure. Seeing May Lily like that, Cornflower could not help but burst into laughter. He raised a hand to wipe away May Lily’s tears and asked softly, ‘I’m still alive. What are you crying about?’

        ‘...Because I’m so mad at you!’ May Lily roughly wiped away his tears. Staring at Cornflower fiercely, he asked through clenched teeth, ‘Do you know you almost died?!’

        ‘I’m going to be the king so I won’t die so easily.’ With a smile, Cornflower looked into May Lily’s eyes and said in a tender tone, ‘...Thank you for living for me.’

        May Lily looked back at Cornflower. Knowing what the prince meant, he returned him a smile and whispered softly, ‘Yeah.’

        “Hope only exists when we live. Self-sacrifice is nothing but a way of giving up,” May Lily whispered to himself silently while gazing at the horizon. “Father, I will not follow your footsteps.”
STORY_2833:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.5

        On the day of the Century Feast, Rosemellow conspired with Papaver to sneak the rebel army into the palace and drugged the first princess, Strelitzia. Just when Rosemellow thought she could have Strelitzia all to her own, May Lily came with a troop and captured her but he soon left alone after hearing that Cornflower was in danger.

        Rosemellow was forced to stay in a corner along with the other rebels with her hands tied behind her back. Then, she looked at the sleeping Strelitzia, whose beauty had not been diminished by her disheveled hair caused by the commotion. The sight of the princess tickled Rosemellow’s heart and fueled her burning desire.

        “I’m only a step away from having you to my own. I won’t let those people ruin my plan!”

        However, Rosemellow became anxious when two soldiers were going to carry Strelitzia back to the palace. She hurriedly mustered her power to break free only to find that there were thorns on the vine that bound her hands; the more she tried, the deeper the thorns sank into her skin. She began to bleed and her sap even trickled down her fingertips.

        She had no choice but to chase after the soldiers who were carrying Strelitzia when the guard turned around. However, the other soldier caught her left arm when she was about to catch up. Letting out a groan of pain, Rosemellow looked at Strelitzia, who unexpectedly woke up from the coma and glanced toward her in a daze.

        ‘Nothing can stop me from getting Strelitzia!’ Steeling herself, Rosemellow kicked her leg hard which caused her left arm to bend in an unnatural angle in the soldier’s hand. The sound of stem snapping made the soldier freeze for a moment.

        The thorny shackles slipped from Rosemellow’s hand and fell to the ground along with her broken arm. Her sap smeared across the floor and released a strange floral fragrance. Despite losing an arm, Rosemellow snatched a sword that hung on the soldier’s waist and knocked down the other one who was carrying Strelitzia. Then she dragged the princess into the nearest small room.

        Rosemellow locked the door and barricaded it with multiple objects so that the soldiers could not break in for a while. Although Strelitzia remained in a state of confusion at first, she gradually woke up as Rosemellow’s warm sap ran down from the wound and fell on her skin. Her vision cleared and she saw the seriously wounded Rosemellow gazing at her zealously.

        Rosemellow flashed her a blissfully sweet smile. With her eyes shrouded in mist as if she was reveling in an intoxicating dream, she said fondly, ‘Here, there’s still time. Let’s escape from the window at the back and go back to the home that belongs to the only two of us.’

        ‘What is going on? You- Where is Papaver? I thought we were—’

        ‘Why do your eyes only see other elves? I’m hurt… Why wouldn’t you take a look at me? I want to be with you forever… I will do anything as long as I can have you, hehe.’ Rosemellow’s face which was splattered by sap contorted with obsession and desire swirling in her eyes.

        Yet, that did not frighten Strelitzia. She propped up her body and glared fiercely at Rosemellow, questioning, ‘What did you do to Papaver? Tell me!’

        Giving Strelitzia a distorted smile in pain, Rosemellow told her about Papaver’s betrayal. Her voice faltered while she threatened the princess, ‘Look what you’ve done to the kingdom, princess. You’ve lost your place so just come and flee with me.’

        ‘No, you’re lying! Papaver would never do that! She is so fine and innocent! You’re slandering her!’ In denial, Strelitzia grabbed Rosemellow, who forcibly pulled her hand away and said, ‘I colluded with those filthy floral-elves and I got rid of Sakura. I did everything for you but you never laid your eyes on me!’

        ‘What… So it was you who hurt Sakura?’ Strelitzia’s face darkened in an instant.

        Rosemellow uncontrollably exploded with a nervous laughter in a panic after the truth slipped off her tongue. She then wore a cold expression and said in a soft tone, ‘Don’t worry. The assassin will soon take her back to the Mother Tree’s embrace so she won’t have your attention anymore, and then I will finally be the only elf in your eyes. No elves can stop us after today!’

        ‘You— You’re crazy! I should kill you!’ An irrepressible rage erupted inside Strelitzia’s chest like a volcano and boiled her blood. She took a random sharp weapon and made a slash at Rosemellow, who dodged her attack by moving sideways. Throwing her only arm around the princess’ shoulders, Rosemellow said, ‘I’m the elf who has done the most for you, but why can’t you just love me back?!’

        ‘I will never love you even if you’re the last elf in the world!’ Strelitzia shoved Rosemellow away, pushing her to the window. As Rosemellow looked back, the height outside struck her with fear. She then turned around but her vision had become blurred due to the excessive loss of sap. By the time her eyes could finally focus, Strelitzia had already stabbed her with the weapon!

        The hatred and disgust in Strelitzia’s eyes as well as her words stabbed Rosemellow’s heart like pieces of broken glass. It hurt her a thousand times more than the wounds on her body. Sucked into a vortex of despair and heartbreak, she had a sudden thought, “Even after everything I have done for you, you still treat me like nothing… Since I can’t have you in my life, then we shall die together.”

        In a fleeting second, Rosemellow turned around and held Strelitzia against the window. Just when the two of them were going to fall out of the window, someone burst open the door—it was Rose with several soldiers behind her.

        ‘Get out of my way!’ Grabbing Strelitzia, Rosemellow jumped out of the window and said with a smile, ‘Now we can be together forever.’

        However, a few vines flew over and caught Strelitzia’s hand just in time but they failed to save Rosemellow, who involuntarily loosened her grip because of the sudden reaction force.

        ‘Rosemellow—!’ Under Strelitzia’s gaze, Rosemellow fell alone. Her dress fluttered in the wind and accentuated her exquisite body as well as the gaping hole in her left shoulder. The sweet smile on her face looked so exceptionally bewitching that it was forever burned into Strelitzia’s memory.

        “In the end, you finally lay your eyes on me, hehe.”
STORY_2834:
Finale of Elfish Perennials - Ch.2

        Hyacinth finally became the host of the Century Feast as he had wished. However, little did he know that his wife, Paperwhite, would expose his lies in front of the nobles on the day of the feast and let them pin him to the ground like a criminal as they lost trust in him.

        Paperwhite, who had been nothing but caring and loving to Hyacinth, simply stood on the side and watched her husband die of embarrassment, gloating over his failure.

        As a matter of fact, Hyacinth and Paperwhite were very much alike: they both had a complex about themselves. The only difference between them was that she showed it with timidity while he covered it with arrogance.

        As Hyacinth strenuously lifted his head, he glared at Paperwhite, who was standing in front of him. With his eyes blazing with crimson rage, he roared through clenched teeth, ‘How dare you betray me! I won’t forgive you!’

        ‘I betray you?’ A sardonic smile appeared on Paperwhite’s blandly pale face as though she found Hyacinth’s accusation quite funny. She then slowly opened her mouth which was the only color on her face.

        ‘You’re the traitor in our story… You told me that I could never be the one for you, remember?’ Even though Paperwhite spoke in an extremely soft tone, she sounded as frightening as a slithering snake, and she said, ‘Since I can’t get my wish, you can’t get yours as well—you will never be the king!’

        ‘You—!’ Hyacinth’s rage erupted at Paperwhite’s words. He was mad at the elf in front of him for she had completely ruined everything he had planned for years. The mounting rage gave him a sudden burst of strength that helped him break free from the nobles’ restraint.

        The moment Hyacinth regained freedom, he charged at Paperwhite with lightning speed. Embarrassed and furious, he raised his right hand to give the slender elf a slap but his body froze a second before he did when he saw her glazed eyes.

        “Why… Why is she looking at me like this… Why doesn’t she move or defend herself… It’s like she’s been waiting for me to hurt her and take my revenge on her…”


        Hyacinth’s heart fluttered the second he met Paperwhite’s eyes.
