        To attain a revolutionary evolution, Abhoth needed Daoloth to transcend its degradation and acquire the power to traverse dimensions. Only then could it become stronger and undergo its own transformation For that purpose, Abhoth conspired with Y’golonac, orchestrating the encounter between Azathoth and Daoloth.

        Moreover, it manipulated Y’golonac and Mordiggian, using Ghatanothoa and Atlach to destabilize Azathoth. For it knew that Daoloth would go to any lengths to save Azathoth, and thus be willing to cooperate with it.

        “Abhoth, so you have forsaken everything in pursuit of truth.”

        “Just the way you save Azathoth, Daoloth.”

        Boom! The earth behind Abhoth trembled as Daoloth’s strike created a deep crater.

        Narrowing its eyes, Daoloth exuded an overwhelming aura and declared, “Don’t compare your wretchedness to me. Disappear before my true wrath descends.”

        “No, I won’t leave, for you need me,” Abhoth stated fearlessly. “Given that everyone is gone now, I am the only one who can help you realize your plan.”

        “...I’m listening.”

        “Since this realm offers no means to save Azathoth, we must seek the answer in other realms. The transcendental power bestowed upon you by Azathoth enables your soul to traverse dimensions. However, gathering the truths of the realms will take a lot of time, even for you.”

        “So, you wish to become an entity that collects and stores the truths?” Daoloth cast a disdainful smirk, lowering its gaze upon Abhoth. “Can you shoulder such weight?”

        “Whether I fail or succeed, it will be no harm to you. Am I right?”

        “Indeed.” Daoloth nodded, extending its metallic claws within which the transcendental power gathered, entwined, and finally compressed into a seed radiating a swirling darkness. Then, it continued, “Since you are willing to give everything for this opportunity, we shall let fate decide whether the misfortune you endure will bring forth the miracle you desire.”

        Before Abhoth could respond, Daoloth implanted the seed directly into its being.

        The transcendental power swiftly coursed through Abhoth’s entire body. It first dissolved its flesh, then shattered its soul, consuming every fragment one by one.

        Nourished by its Abhoth’s essence, the seed sprouted. Its tendrils broke through the boundaries of dimensions, finding its place within the crevices between realms. Slowly, it grew and bore countless dandelion-like buds in this peculiar space.

        When the buds matured, they burst open, releasing seeds imbued with powers, carried away to different worlds. They took root again, recording and witnessing the histories and truths of each world.

        The buds would transmit the information back to their parents who would automatically transcribe them and transform them into books that would find their eternal abode on endless shelves—the enigmatic place henceforth known as the “Bibliotheca of Truth”.

        Under the silent gaze of fate, Abhoth, despite losing its flesh and cognition, got its wish, obtaining knowledge and truths from various realms.

        It was after an arduous passage of time that Daoloth finally discovered a method to save Azathoth. To accomplish its plan, it asked Abhoth to select destined individuals in Tarones, imparting upon them the selected histories and knowledge. However, something unexpected happened during the execution.

        To continue the plan, Daoloth returned to the continent of Tarones, assuming the identity of Tawil. It was with Ithaqua’s guidance that it regained its lost memories and finally fulfill the promise it had made to Azathoth…
STORY_2844:
Finale of Prologue of the Universe - Ch.7

        On the remnants of a dead planet, a headless mass of flesh, Y’golonac, chuckled while turning the handle of a spinning contraption. On the sides of the contraption were two upward-pointing spindles that pierced through two listless torsos—Ghatanothoa and Atlach, the twins whom Y’golonac and Mordiggian had cunningly ensnared through their vile machinations and used as the raw materials for making the thread of causality.

        Just then, the colossal contraption turned steadily, just like the eternal cycle of life and death; but for Ghatanothoa, it was nothing but a cruel torment.

        “AHHHHH—! It hurts—! Atlach! Help me! Help me!” The excruciating pain of its soul being squeezed and wrung drove Ghatanothoa to the brink of madness and chaos where it instinctively sought salvation from its most trusted brother.

        Right before Ghatanothoa’s consciousness crumbled, a gentle radiance enveloped it, bringing it unprecedented tranquility and solidity.

        Ghatanothoa returned to a state reminiscent of its preexistence when Atlach and it were still one undivided stone. Back then, they were both complete without any difference or distance between them. The fulfillment of returning to one slowly restored Ghatanothoa’s fractured soul, its consciousness becoming clear. From within that radiance, it heard a familiar voice.

        “With my flawed self merging into your innocence, I can now become a part of the grace, the existence you have always pursued and loved.”

        The radiance suddenly intensified, as if expending its final strength to kindle the brightest blaze of its existence. Engulfed by the scorching brilliance, Ghatanothoa felt its soul seared with an ominous premonition as if it was about to lose something important.

        Ghatanothoa attempted to reach out and touch the radiance, but its mending soul remained immobilized. It was only able to perceive the fading brilliance and the final words it whispered,

        “Ghatanothoa, it has been my utmost bliss to be your brother and the solace of your soul.”

        “No… No! Don’t leave me alone! Atlach—!” Ghatanothoa cried out, but the warm radiance had already departed, leaving its repaired form—vigorous and beastly—engulfed in a desolate and icy solitude. Ghatanothoa then awoke from the depths of its consciousness, only to find itself alone amid the remains of a silent planet, with only the colossal contraption as a solemn companion.

        The spindles on either side of the contraption had corroded as a result of its brother’s sacrifice. Atlach had used its venom to erode the spindles, paying the ultimate price for mending Ghatanothoa’s fragmented soul with its own essence.

        “Why… If I knew that my existence depends on the cessation of yours, I would rather step into eternal darkness, guarding you beyond the stars... Atlach... my brother... How deeply I love you, longing for your eternal bliss... Roarrrr—!” As the overwhelming grief exceeded Ghatanothoa’s threshold, it lost control and wailed in anguish with tears streaming down its face.

        The abundant power carried within Ghatanothoa’s tears revitalized the desolate land, causing vegetation and life to rapidly flourish, which alerted the lurking clone of Y’golonac in the lair.

        With a glance, Y’golonacpondered upon the events that had unfolded in this place mere moments ago, then it disdainfully sneered, “Tut! Atlach, that fool. I can’t believe it sacrificed its very soul to save you—Argh!”

        Upon hearing the mockery aimed at Atlach, Ghatanothoa was consumed by rage. It lunged toward Y’golonac’s clone and devoured it with a wide-open maw. With a ferocious snarl, Ghatanothoa declared, “This is the consequence of insulting Atlach, you vile destroyer!”

        “Ha, it seems you’ve forgotten that your brother was also a follower of destruction,” said another headless mass of flesh that materialized behind Ghatanothoa, its tone laced with a scornful and confident air.

        “And it appears you’ve also forgotten that this is my lair,” added another headless mass of flesh that emerged from a different direction.

        “Even if you kill one of me, there are still countless clones here.” Another Y’golonac’s clone sneered as it approached from the shadows.

        “Well then, I shall kill you all!” Ghatanothoa showed no fear as the anger of losing its brother consumed every fiber of its being. All that remained in its mind was the desire to eliminate the Y’golonac, who had tortured its sibling

        “Let’s put such arrogance to the test!” A colossal clone of Y’golonac, even larger than the others, descended from above, while numerous other clones surged forward from all directions, converging upon Ghatanothoa. In an instant, Ghatanothoa was engulfed by a multitude of headless flesh forms.

        “A weakling is always weakling, tsk… Wh-what is that?” The largest clone of Y’golonac chuckled softly, standing at a distance. However, its laughter abruptly ceased when it witnessed eight dark shadows emerging from Ghatanothoa, forcefully scattering the headless masses entangled around it.

        “I may be a naive and ignorant weakling but my brother…Atlach is certainly not! It is the most beautiful existence in this world! It is whom I admire and cherish the most… It’s the half of my soul and it always protects me!” exclaimed Ghatanothoa, wielding the eight dark shadows—eight spiky appendages identical to Atlach’s!

        The eight appendages deftly maneuvered through the scattered headless masses, piercing, crushing, and reducing them to mounds of indistinct flesh. In the blink of an eye, the tide had turned completely, and Ghatanothoa held a distinct advantage.

        “Tut! This creature is more troublesome than I anticipated. Nevertheless, we’ve got the thread of causality. It is not wise to continue this battle; escape is the prudent course of action!” The massive clone of Y’golonac, who had been observing from the sidelines, realized its inferior position and swiftly turned to flee. However, Ghatanothoa was quick to discern its intentions.

        “You can’t run away from me!” Ghatanothoa opened its maw wide, gathering energy to unleash a powerful beam—

        “Aaahhh—!” The beam pierced through the colossal clone’s body and then swept across all the Y’golonac’s clones as Ghatanothoa turned its gaze, filling the cosmos with cries of pain and agonized screams.

        It was only after a moment that the one-sided slaughter finally ceased. Not a single headless mass remained alive; they lay strewn across the flower-laden grassland. Their bodily fluids nourished the earth and vegetation; buds bloomed in abundance and released the most intense fragrance that mingled with the scent of death, creating a most eerie olfactory spectacle.

        “I won… Atlach, I have vanquished those who tormented you...” Ghatanothoa gazed upon the gruesome scene before it, yet devoid of any triumphant joy. Only deep-seated weariness emanated from its core, both mental and physical. “But what comes next... I am all alone... How am I to live alone... Atlach...”

        Ghatanothoa had lost the will to exist, yet could not abandon the life that Atlach had traded for. It could only allow its body to drift through the cosmos, letting its thoughts dissolve and staring blankly at boundless galaxies and stars until a shimmering figure of golden light appeared before them. 

        The power of vibrancy awakened Ghatanothoa’s long-dormant senses. It looked up at the exquisitely beautiful figure like a lost child catching sight of their parents. The wounds that had accumulated over numerous years once again festered, causing hot tears to well in its eyes.

        “Daoloth, you’re here,” Ghatanothoa whispered with a choked voice, extending its forelimb to embrace the golden figure. Daoloth returned the embrace, gently caressing Ghatanothoa’s rugged carapace.

        “Ghatanothoa, my pitiful child, I’m sorry that I arrived too late, and caused your suffering,” Daoloth lowered its gaze and comforted Ghatanothoa with a voice full of compassion and tenderness, “I have come to fulfill your desires.” 

        “My desires...” Ghatanothoa was confused at first, but upon seeing the scarred universe, it understood what Daoloth meant. At that moment, the desolate soul found solace and began to feel the pulsation of life once again.

        Ghatanothoa shed its despair and regained the purity of its early existence. It prostrated itself before Daoloth, lifting its head, and naively pleaded, “Please, use me and Atlach to mend this universe. Then we can be together forever, gazing and embracing both beauty and flaws until the end of the cosmos.”

        “This time, I won’t let you be alone. If understanding you and redeeming you means tarnishing the beauty of life, I shall embrace the mire and yearn to become imperfect. Atlach, being born as your brother is the most unparalleled miracle to me.”

        Holding the most devout faith, Ghatanothoa closed its eyes and returned to its primordial state in the embrace of Daoloth, and in the hands of the lord of creation, it was born anew once more...
STORY_2845:
Finale of Prologue of the Universe - Ch.4

        In a corner of the boundless cosmos, a cavernous structure fashioned from countless headless masses of flesh floated, resembling a hive. Through a labyrinthine passage, it arrived at the remains of a dead planet where a massive contraption similar to a spinning wheel stood.

        The contraption had two upward-pointing spindles that pierced through the torsos of two wretched beings whose bodies had been reduced to mere husks. From the lower halves of their mutilated forms, strands of fibers, shimmering with golden and silver radiance, extended towards the apparatus in the middle, which spun them into one resilient and sparkling thread of intertwined colors.

        The headless mass of flesh grasped the handle of the spinning apparatus. With a sinister chuckle, it turned the handle, setting the previously dormant contraption back into motion to extract every ounce of powers and souls from the tormented beings.

        “ARGHHHHH—!”

        Agonizing cries were squeezed out of the two barely living creatures, imbuing the silent celestial husk with a savage and harrowing ambiance. However, their horrifying screams soon faded away for their wills had been thoroughly broken. Their contorted bodies trembled ever so slightly, unable to retain a recognizable form.

        Impaled by the right spindle, Atlach turned its twisted form—resembling that of a spider—to the left. Enduring the excruciating pain, it opened its eyes to gaze upon its deformed and frail brother, Ghatanothoa. Hot tears welled up in its empty sockets but were still unable to conceal the gnawing sense of guilt within it.

        “Ghata… My brother… It’s all my fault… It’s all because of me that you have to suffer this torment…” Atlach berated itself relentlessly, its psyche consumed by regret.

        Not long ago, Atlach rescued Ghatanothoa, who had been gravely injured by Daoloth. It exerted all of its remaining powers to heal the shattered soul of its dearest brother, which yet plagued it with a surging desire for destruction that threatened to consume it. Atlach resorted to self-condemnation to suppress its maddening mind, fearing that it would harm its beloved brother, Ghatanothoa.

        Unfortunately, Atlach’s act of healing Ghatanothoa, coupled with its self-inflicted injuries, had emptied all its powers and drained it completely so it ran from Ghatanothoa as far away as possible before falling into a coma. Unexpectedly, it found itself saved by Y’golonac, a follower of destruction, upon awakening.

        Little did Atlach know, it was all a trap.

        Y’golonac, driven by the desire to disrupt the balance between Azathoth and Daoloth, allied itself with Mordiggian, an inferior by-product of Daoloth’s creation. They schemed to capture Atlach and Ghatanothoa, abducting them to a secluded corner of the universe—Y’golonac’s lair.

        Stripped of their limbs and quadrupeds, Atlach and Ghatanothoa were mounted upon the spindles on the sides of the spinning wheel, becoming the thread spools of this contraption of causality that twisted their powers, wills, and even their souls, spinning them down to form a thread of fate that could bind all things and change fate.

        After an eternity had passed, the spindle at the center of the spinning wheel was finally full of sparkling threads. Meanwhile, Atlach and Ghatanothoa, the very material for the threads, remained motionless. One would assume they were already lifeless if it were not for the occasional tremor in their mutilated forms.

        Y’golonac raised the spindle high. Basking in the radiant starlight, the ethereal threads looked like nothing it had ever seen in this world. With a hint of awe in its voice, it exclaimed, “This is surely the thread of causality. We only got such a small amount of it despite exploiting most of these two’s lives and souls. We must be cautious in its use.”

        Y’golonac handed the threads of causality to Mordiggian, who then looked up at the brothers still impaled by the spindles. It inquired, “What should we do with them? Should we kill them?”

        “No, keep them. They might prove useful if some unexpected circumstances arise,” Y’golonac replied. The mouth in the palm of its hand widened and teased with disdain, “Besides, they can’t accomplish much in their current state.”

        After a moment of hesitation, Mordiggian nodded and left the lair with Y’golonac.

        “Finally, they’re gone… It’s time,” Atlach murmured, lifting its eyelids to observe the receding figures of Mordiggian and Y’golonac.

        In order to confront Azathoth, Y’golonac had gathered half of its clones within the lair, merging them to form a formidable entity, while the remaining clones stood guard over its nest.

        It was the opportunity Atlach had been waiting for.

        “I will save you, even if it shatters my soul to pieces. I will save you!” As Atlach gazed at the unconscious Ghatanothoa on the other side, its obsidian eyes glistened with a maddening determination.

        Mustering the last remnants of its power, Atlach forced the venom within its body to the surface to erode the spindles that impaled it into decrepit ruins. Although the venom also gnawed at Atlach’s own damaged form, it remained undeterred. With its ruptured body, Atlach maneuvered towards Ghatanothoa, carefully guiding the venom to corrupt the other spindle while avoiding any harm to its beloved brother.

        Finally, Atlach’s efforts bore fruit as Ghatanothoa slipped free from the spindle. In that moment of descent, Atlach positioned its body to cushion Ghatanothoa’s fall and shield its brother with its own tattered form.

        “Why does such beauty exist in this filthy, grotesque world?” Overwhelmed by the familiar touch, Atlach burst into tears, finding the wounds it endured insignificant in that instant.

        Yet, its anxiety quickly resurfaced as it sensed Ghatanothoa’s fragmented soul and consciousness slowly dissipating. The successive soul-shattering torment had rendered Ghatanothoa even more fragile than before, putting it to the brink of annihilation if no one filled the void within its soul soon.

        However, in this desolate cosmos, Atlach, whose soul bore deep wounds, was the only soul capable of offering itself to heal Ghatanothoa. Only by merging its shattered soul into Ghatanothoa’s being could Atlach cure its brother. Yet, the fusion of their souls also meant Atlach had to forsake its own darkness.

        Though it was a fundamental transformation, Atlach made the choice without hesitation. With tenderness and indulgence, it gently rubbed its head against Ghatanothoa’s face.

        “Ghata, if saving you means I have to embrace the goodness in life and have my spirit cleansed, then I shall willingly cast aside my darkness,” Atlach whispered, closing its eyes to let its soul sink. Without a second thought, it dove into Ghatanothoa’s consciousness, filling the ravaged soul with its own.

        “With my flawed self merging into your innocence, I can now become a part of the grace, the existence you have always pursued and loved.”

        Atlach’s consciousness gradually faded into nothingness. In its final moments, its soul erupted with the most resplendent radiance it had ever possessed.

        “Ghatanothoa, it has been my utmost bliss to be your brother and the solace of your soul.”

        After leaving those words, Atlach’s soul dissolved completely into the vast ocean of Ghatanothoa’s mind. It was at that moment that it finally bid farewell to the regrets that had entwined its entire existence and embraced the happiness bestowed upon its soul…
STORY_2846:
Molly never stopped missing the good old days of her fighting along with her companions as well as the company of the young swordsman, even after she had merged with the power of elements. To console her lonesome soul, the elements showed her a fictitious future—

        “Open the door for me—” shouted Sean, who raised his sword and charged at the Valkyrie bravely.

        “No! I’m staying!” Molly wanted to go and help Sean but Nathaniel stopped her.

        “Molly! We’re on a more important mission! Don’t let your emotions get in the way!” Nathaniel’s harsh words cooled down Molly’s head. She hesitated as the memories of the unsparing battlefield and the pact with her companions flushed back into her mind.

        However, her heart ached as if it was stabbed by a knife when she saw the Valkyrie’s sword leave a cut on Sean’s body. Her reason and aspiration were shattered in an instant; all she had left was consternation for the man she loved.

        “No matter how important saving the world is, it’s not the reason for me to leave him in danger!” Showing her rare tough side, the soft Molly broke away from Nathaniel’s grip and ran to Sean. She took Sean’s hand and ran back to their companions while resisting the Valkyrie’s attack with her wand.

        Molly and Sean managed to escape the Valkyrie’s pursuit and made it to the Ocean of Gates thanks to the protection of their companions.

        With help from Sean and Duncan, Molly convinced Endor and Nathaniel to contribute their power to secure the seal on the tower so that humanity could have a short moment of peace.

        “Although we did stop the demons’ scheme, there’re still some demons left in the realm. I’m going back to the army to make the next plan. What about you guys?” asked Nathaniel, who stood tall and proud before the tower. His will did not waver despite having lost most of his strength.

        “Let me help you!” Sean answered hastily. However, Nathaniel shook his head and turned him down. “No, you’re too deeply wounded. Let’s talk about it after your body recovers.”

        “Nathaniel is right. You have always protected us and you’re the most wounded among us…” Lifting her head, Molly finally plucked up enough courage to look at Sean. With a flush of embarrassment rising to her cheeks, she asked, “Will you go back to the academy with me? Th-then I can take care of you.”

        “Molly…” Sean’s heart skipped a bit. The feelings that he had suppressed due to the war began to spurt. He could not help but answer with a smile of unconcealable joy, “Yes, please.”

        Molly’s heart bloomed as she heard Sean say yes, and it brought a radiant smile to her face. After watching Nathaniel, Duncan and Endo go, Molly and Sean headed back to the academy where they received a warm welcome.

        At first, Sean really enjoyed the rare peaceful days with Molly in the academy. As time went by, however, he found something missing. The void in his heart made him unconsciously irritable.

        To relieve the feeling of annoyance, he started practicing swordsmanship again, drenching himself in sweat in the dusk.

        On the other hand, Molly, who had spent days with Sean, noticed his change and she was not surprised at all. It was as if she had known the day of parting would eventually come from the moment Sean agreed to return to the academy with her.

        Finally, Molly saw Sean with his packed bags when she returned to the dorm after class one day. She remained silent for a while at first, but she soon gave him a smile and asked, “So, you’re leaving, right?”

        “Yeah. My wounds have all healed, and it’s time for me to do what I should do,” said Sean looking deeply into Molly’s eyes. He adored this girl who had grown throughout the tragic times of war and become a forgiving and visionary sorceress. Still, he could not hide his quivering ambition so he asked with little hope, “Will you come with me? Just like the old days.”

        Instead of answering the question, Molly looked at Sean with tears brimming in her eyes. Bathing in the evening sunlight, the young swordsman looked even more heroic with the burly body and unsightly scars he had gained from multiple fights against death.

        Sean had never stopped blazing a trail for his companions even in the face of difficulties. It was his courage and determination that touched her heart; it was what made her admire him and want to chase after him. However, people are not always free in the real world. With age comes a lot of worries and concerns that will dampen one’s spirit. Molly was no exception; she could no longer put Sean and saving the world as her first priority the way she did before, so she shook her head.

        “I want to go with you but I can’t. I can’t leave my students alone. I want to teach them everything I know so that they can live longer on the ruthless battlefield.”

        “Is that so?” Sean returned her a smile of relief, his eyes filled with deep affection. Proudly, he continued, “I knew it. You’re the best sorceress I know.”

        “Yeah, and you’re the best swordsman I know,” said Molly in a soft voice. She stepped forward to give Sean a hug as the grandest gesture of goodbye before their reunion in the unknown future.

        Although the two stayed connected through letters after they had parted ways, they inevitably grew apart in the ceaseless war between the gods and the demons. Even though they missed each other, their lives were interlaced with other people at the same time. Status and duty divided the lovers. War incessantly took friends away from Molly with their names carved onto headstones one after another, churning memories into shards of regret…

        “I must move on for peace and our pact even if I have to leave the man I love!”

STORY_2848:
Sean, whose soul had merged with the fire element, saw an alternative future in an illusion created by the runestones—

        “Molly! I’ll stall the Valkyrie! You guys go climb the tower!” shouted Sean, who raised his sword and charged at the Valkyrie bravely. Unexpectedly, his vision spun for a moment as if someone gave his soul a punch when he saw the Valkyrie’s face.

        “She… Why does she look so familiar… It’s just like she’s someone close—”

        “Sean!” Molly’s terrified scream brought Sean out of the trance. He abruptly lifted his head only to find that the Valkyrie’s scythe had come close to the tip of his nose, so he hurriedly raised his sword and summoned dragonfire to parry the strike.

        “I have to focus! Anyhow, the past has passed. Now the only thing I should do is to keep the pact with my companions and stop the wars on this continent with everything I have!”

        And so, Sean cleared his mind and focused on his enemy. Out of the state of confusion, he exerted an unexceptional strength and defeated the Valkyrie right before he was about to fall. Then, he made it to the Ocean of Gates with his companions.

        With help from Molly and Duncan, Sean convinced Endor and Nathaniel to contribute their power to secure the seal on the tower and stop the demons’ scheme.

        Having lost most of their strength, the five scattered: Duncan returned to the forest and became a teacher for the younger generations; Nathaniel continued to lead the army in combat; Endor embarked on a journey to appease the spirits of the deceased; Molly returned to the college with Sean, who was seriously wounded. Staying at the college dorm, he enjoyed a brief period of peace with Molly.

        However, Sean failed to resist the urge to return to the army after his body had recovered. Still, he stayed in touch with Molly by writing her letters every week and he looked forward to her writing back. At that moment, Sean was still full of hope and excitement for the future and the world.

        It was only until later when he was stationed in a chaotic war zone where the ground was strewn with corpses that he finally woke up from the beautiful fantasy in his head.

        With the bodies of his comrades sprawled across the moorland, the air was filled with the smell of blood and gunpowder. The wounded soldiers’ screams and groans of pain echoed in his ears. The battlefield was even more dreadful than the one where he and his companions made their pact.

        “In the end, the war still continues even after we lost so many things to seal the tower. So is our pact nothing but a joke… No! I will never admit that!”

        A roar of rage came through Sean’s clenched teeth. Yet, his roar could not change anything. War still came ruthlessly. He led a troop of soldiers into the battlefield but only he made it back alive.

        In one of the warring days, he survived the battlefield again. Yet, he barely had the strength to change his armor after his survival this time. He simply sat down before the campfire gloomily. Just when everyone thought that he had become a statue, he finally moved. He took out a crumpled, bloodstained yet unfinished letter from his armor and threw it into the fire silently.

        “Why did you burn it? It took you so long to write,” a comrade said with pity.

        “Because…” As Sean stared at the flickering flames, he recalled the time when Molly bandaged his wounds which were a product of his recklessness next to a similar campfire. Feeling nostalgia for the good old days, he let out a soft sigh and continued, “...that would only upset her.”

        “I can’t give her promises. The last thing I should do is to give her hope. I can’t ask her to tether her life to mine and wait for me with worry day after day just because she makes me happy. That’s just selfish.”

        Just like the promise they had made in the past.

        Sean’s lips curled up into a wry smile. It was something that had never appeared on his face. Disappointment after disappointment, his courage and conviction were dampened, and eventually, he stopped imagining the day when his dream would come true.

        At some point, Sean did not even know why he was still standing on the battlefield; he did not know what he was fighting for. Still, he could not give up as if he would lose direction once he stopped.

        “Perhaps death is my only way out of the battlefield,” Sean thought while writing another letter before the campfire.

        Sean’s premonition soon came true. He was tortured to death by the demons after he used himself as a diversion and lured the demon army away to protect the civilians during one of the enemies’ raids. Feeling humiliated, the demons tormented Sean and hung his body on a tree in revenge. It was also the reason why it did not take Sean’s comrades much time to find his body.

        Sean’s comrades sent out the bloodstained letter left on his body along with the letters of many other soldiers. When Molly received Sean’s letter, the circular burn marks and his final words filled her eyes with tears that could not wash away the blood stain on the letter.

        “The strange and familiar memories, and the confusing figures, everything makes me feel at a loss.”

STORY_2850:
After myriad battles, Duncan and the power of Earth had fused. The earth elements brought him into an illusionary land…

        Born in times of war, Duncan was raised by a group of druids in a forest. Believing that Duncan was blessed by the earth, the druids had always wanted him to be the priest of the forest but the young druid would rather be a cleric instead.

        One day, the elder of the druids came to persuade Duncan. He said, “Duncan, you have the earth’s blessing. Why don’t you put this gift into use?” 

        “Elder…” A look of puzzlement crossed Duncan’s face. Despite his extraordinary powers, he was still an innocent teenager at that point, so he could not help but ask, “I don’t understand… We protect the sheep but we also slaughter them and feed ourselves with their meat. Isn’t that an act of destroying nature?”

        “You’re a kind child, Duncan.“ With a gracious smile, the elder stroked Duncan’s hair which was as soft as the fur of a newborn lamb. He then continued in a gentle tone, “Death is also a gift from nature. It is a part of the circle of life. Life and death are inseparable. They form a balance that no one should break.”

        “...I still don’t get it,” said Duncan in dejection, unable to figure out what the elder meant.

        “Don’t rush, my boy. Be the priest, and time will tell you the answer.”

        “But I…”

        As reluctant as Duncan was, he finally compromised when he lifted his head and saw the gleam of expectation in the elder’s eyes. He agreed to be the priest of the forest instead of a cleric and began his learning under the elder.

        One day, a young earl came with a troop of soldiers when Duncan was studying some herbs with rapt attention. Since the elder had gone out to collect herbs, the duty fell on Duncan’s shoulders to receive the uninvited guests as the representative of the druids.

        “...You are the leader of the druids?” Although the earl was surprised by Duncan’s young age, he recovered his composure in the blink of an eye. Then he explained his purpose of visit to Duncan sincerely, “The demons’ invasion has become more rampant after the gods’ withdrawal from the human realm, and we would like you the druids to join us, the Human Forces.”

        Unfortunately, the young earl’s speech did not move Duncan but aroused his aversion—the young druid hated war since it had taken his parents. With such prejudice to violence, Duncan answered in a deep voice with his face darkened, “We the druids have no intention of participating in any wars. We only want peace in the forest, so please go back to where you come from, Your Lordship.”

        Duncan’s attitude enraged the soldiers who stepped forward to teach him a lesson only to be stopped by the earl. Remaining calm, the earl looked at Duncan composedly, “We respect your wish, but please allow me to say this: fate won’t spare anyone. You will also be forced to take up weapons one day.”

        The earl left after leaving Duncan a word of warning. Later, the elder came back and learned about what had happened. From the disappointment in the elder’s eyes, Duncan knew that the elder was not happy about his decision to turn down the earl even though the elder had not said a word to blame him.

        At that time, Duncan did not understand why the elder was disappointed at his decision of rejecting violence, but he soon understood because the demons attacked the druids for no logical reason.

        The devious and cruel demons tormented all the druids they captured to death no matter how they begged for mercy.

        As the earl had said, Duncan picked up a spear in desperation trying to kill the demons to protect his clan. However, the elder stopped him by knocking him unconscious. Although the elder managed to elude the demons’ siege while carrying the unconscious Duncan on his shoulder, he was seriously injured.

        By the time Duncan woke up, the elder was already lying in a puddle of blood. Tears overflowed Duncan’s eyes as the overwhelmingly cruel fact struck the young druid. On the verge of death, the elder looked at Duncan graciously just like the way he always did.

        “Duncan… Don’t harbor resentment… Think about where life comes from, where it grows from, and what it grows into… You have to understand what damage killing truly does to us… And then, if you find it is necessary, then it should be a death determined by nature…”

        After giving Duncan his final lesson, the elder closed his eyes and returned to nature and the earth where Duncan buried him. The unsparing reality forced the young druid to grow in one day and he finally understood the law of nature that he had found incomprehensible.

        “Elder, now I know. War is a part of nature. It is a disaster staged by the earth to filter out those who can’t survive. The suffering of life and death makes lives grow, and I won’t run away from violence and death again.”

        After bidding his last goodbye to the elder, Duncan took his spear and joined the young earl’s troop with regrets so as to maintain the circle of life…

        “I’m not powerful and I don’t understand the true meaning of nature. It is my best option to become a shepherd who travels around the world to experience different kinds of emotions.”

With such prejudice to violence, Duncan answered in a deep voice with his face darkened, “We the druids have no intention of participating in any wars. We only want peace in the forest, so please go back to where you come from, Your Lordship.”

        Duncan’s attitude enraged the soldiers who stepped forward to teach him a lesson only to be stopped by the earl. Remaining calm, the earl looked at Duncan composedly, “We respect your wish, but please allow me to say this: fate won’t spare anyone. You will also be forced to take up weapons one day.”

        The earl left after leaving Duncan a word of warning. Later, the elder came back and learned about what had happened. From the disappointment in the elder’s eyes, Duncan knew that the elder was not happy about his decision to turn down the earl even though the elder had not said a word to blame him.

        At that time, Duncan did not understand why the elder was disappointed at his decision of rejecting violence, but he soon understood because the demons attacked the druids for no logical reason.

        The devious and cruel demons tormented all the druids they captured to death no matter how they begged for mercy.

        As the earl had said, Duncan picked up a spear in desperation trying to kill the demons to protect his clan. However, the elder stopped him by knocking him unconscious. Although the elder managed to elude the demons’ siege while carrying the unconscious Duncan on his shoulder, he was seriously injured.

        By the time Duncan woke up, the elder was already lying in a puddle of blood. Tears overflowed Duncan’s eyes as the overwhelmingly cruel fact struck the young druid. On the verge of death, the elder looked at Duncan graciously just like the way he always did.

        “Duncan… Don’t harbor resentment… Think about where life comes from, where it grows from, and what it grows into… You have to understand what damage killing truly does to us… And then, if you find it is necessary, then it should be a death determined by nature…”

        After giving Duncan his final lesson, the elder closed his eyes and returned to nature and the earth where Duncan buried him. The unsparing reality forced the young druid to grow in one day and he finally understood the law of nature that he had found incomprehensible.

        “Elder, now I know. War is a part of nature. It is a disaster staged by the earth to filter out those who can’t survive. The suffering of life and death makes lives grow, and I won’t run away from violence and death again.”

        After bidding his last goodbye to the elder, Duncan took his spear and joined the young earl’s troop with regrets so as to maintain the circle of life…

        “I only live because of the earth’s blessing and I shall repay the earth by becoming the priest of the forest and leading my clan to protect nature.”
STORY_2852:
In the past, Michael guided Nathaniel’s spirit and allowed him to reside within the runestones after he was defeated by Molly. Yet, in the strange land of illusions projected by the power of elements, where the past continued to be replayed, there seemed to be an alternative ending to his story…

        “I cannot accept this! How can you expand the war? By opening the source of chaos, you would simply necessitate more sacrifices!” Molly shouted.

        “We must bring lasting peace, not a temporary one!” Nathaniel explained.

        Standing before the Ocean of Gates, Nathaniel made up his mind to open the seal and enter the realm of gods to seek divine intervention. He believed that only through the gods’ power could the demons be completely expelled but Molly disagreed, and their disagreement soon led to a fight.

        As Molly raised her wand to cast a magic spell, Nathaniel unsheathed his sword and launched a series of ferocious attacks. The sorceress did not flinch but fought back valiantly. However, the two remain locked in a stalemate since none of them was able to kill their companion.

        “Being criticized for doing good is part of being a noble.”

        Suddenly, Nathaniel remembered his grandfather’s words as well as the teachings of his father and uncle. It was like a reminder to him that a nobleman sometimes might have to stake his reputation to achieve great things, and thus he must stick to his belief even if he was judged and accused.

        “Yeah, I came here because of those soldiers who believe in me and follow my steps! How could I give up my faith just because of the words of a friend?! I have to move forward and take the path that I believe in!”

        As soon as Nathaniel made a decision, he thrust his sword mercilessly and defeated Molly. Keeping his spirit up, he took down Lucifer with Endor and the reinforcements. Together they entered the realm of gods to see Zeus, the King of Gods.

        In the hall of the gods, Nathaniel stepped forward with his head held up high. He remained confident and unyielding even though he was standing in front of the formidable king of the gods. Looking straight into Zeus’eyes, he said aloud, “Your Majesty, I am Nathaniel. The evil demons have stormed our homeland and humiliated our people! That’s why we climbed up the tower and came here representing the humans to ask for your help to expel the abhorrent demons!”

        “Humans, I heard your plea. But we, the gods, shall never intervene in the wars of the other kinds.”

        “In the past, we humans have worshiped and defended the demons for you. We are the reason why you gods can still stay peacefully in the realm of gods today and enjoy the power of elements without actually doing anything! Yet, you choose to stand by and watch us humans suffer in such a time of war! You’re being insufferably selfish and despicable!”

        Sadly, Nathaniel’s vehement accusation fell on deaf ears. With a quick wave of the hand, Zeus simply used his godly power to evict Nathaniel from the hall of the gods and said in a deep tone, “Insolent mortal, leave!”

        Nevertheless, Nathaniel did not give up but continued to circulate among different godly factions proactively through the ages until he fell under the fallen angel’s manipulation and suffered severe punishment from the gods.　

        The battle between the gods and demons did reach an equilibrium with the interference of the angels. However, the angels only defended the gate to their home. While the lives of humans remained difficult, the aged Nathaniel—as the hero of humans—was imprisoned in the realm of gods, waiting for a warrior to end his eternal suffering one day…

        ‘The noble’s mission shall never be the reason for me to point my sword at my companions. I should never break the pact with them!’

STORY_2854:
After countless battles, the spirits of the deceased gave everything to Endor and showed her a non-existent future with the dark elements’ power…

        “We all understand; this is an endless endeavor.”

        Standing before the Ocean of Gates, the necromancer and the young druid remained locked in a stalemate. She opened her monochromatic eyes to look at the robust man she admired.

        “The earth is perpetual, just as the soul is everlasting,” Ducan expressed his resolution in a warm tone.

        Endor knew that she and Duncan were merely heading in different directions and their common wish never changed. However, fate demanded an answer, so she started a fight with Duncan, who had the power of the earth, by using the bones of an ancient beast as a medium to control the deceased souls and activate the power of the dark elements.

        Yet, using the power of the dead came with a side effect—it deepened Endor’s connection with the dead whose sorrow and resentments kept flowing into her mind and stirring her emotions, making it difficult for her to concentrate.

        “Why are you fighting the man you love?”
        “Stop being so stubborn and just follow your heart.”
        “You will be happy as long as you compromise.”

        “No!” Endor screamed in her mind. “I have to open the seal on the Enochian Tower so that the homeless spirits can return to where they belong!”

        With unshakeable conviction, Endor ignored the spirits’ words and focused on performing necromancy. In the end, she defeated Duncan. Then, she joined forces with Nathaniel and defeated the angels with the human army, thus opening the gate to the realm of gods.

        As the road to the realm of gods was finally reopened, the spirits who had been abandoned by the gods rushed in like a swarm of hornets. However, the spirits’ return upset the plans laid out by some of the gods and changed the balance among different godly factions.

        It soon became Endor’s misfortune—she got entangled with the gods’ civil war. Captured by Zeus, the King of Gods, she was held in the hall of gods for trial.

        “Human, do you plead guilty?” asked Zeus, who looked down at Endor as if he were looking at an ant.

        Fearlessly, Endor chastised the almighty god, “It is you who should be guilty! You abandoned the spirits of your people and let them stray and wander in the human realm! You should be ashamed of yourselves!”

        “Human, how dare you!” In a fit of rage, Zeus pointed at Endor and commanded, “Take this impudent mortal to the frozen prison!”

        Under the order of the King of Gods, Endor was imprisoned in the depths of the realm of gods. She thought that she would die there but she later managed to escape with the deceased spirits’ help.

        Despite the setback, Endor refused to give up after escaping from the realm of gods. She continued to find ancient spirits who were lost on the battlefields and sneak them back into the realm of gods. Subsequently, the gods deemed her a criminal and sought her arrest.  People who were ignorant of the context were deployed to capture her. On the run, Endor’s life diverged greatly from what she was; life forced her to side with the demons and she was never freed from the constant danger in her everyday life.

        One day, eventually, she had no choice but to jump into the Dark Cove to elude the gods in pursuit. However, her successful escape only came with a deeply wounded body.

        “Ha, you’re as stupid as usual, the little soul bearing the body.” The evil deity—the lord of the Dark Cove—taunted Endor, who was lying prone on the ground.

        “You… It was you who took colors away from my eyes… It was you who gave me that power…” Endor murmured while running out of breath. With her monochromatic eyes shrouded by a mist of tears, she seemed to be mourning for her loss, yet at the same time, happy for what she had gotten.

        “So? You want me to restore everything?”

        “No, I…’ Not knowing how to answer the question, Endor pretended she was the young druid and said, “…I just wanted to complain.”

        “Humph, the weak always create trouble.” The evil deity chuckled mischievously as he had a stroke of inspiration. He said, “But you’re the good kind because you create troubles for those condescending gods.”

        Although the evil deity was bound to the Dark Cove, he still had ways to hear around the world, and thus he knew about what Endor had done in the realm of gods.

        Certainly, the evil deity’s deep-rooted hatred against the gods would not allow him to let go of this opportunity, so he bent towards the dying Endor and whispered, “You’re dying but I can save you.”

        “...What is the price?”

        “It seems like you’re not that stupid after all.” Extending a hand to touch Endor’s cheek just like the way he did a long time ago, the evil deity said with disdain and resentment, “Be my pawn and fool the gods.”

        Endor had no choice, just like when she was little. In order to survive and liberate the spirits of the dead, she could only make a deal with the evil deity and become his pawn, fighting against the gods…

        ‘I can’t ignore the cries of the deceased. Relieving their grief and pain is the price I have to pay for my power.’

STORY_2856:
The three sisters’ lives—Woodbury, Alice and Doris—returned to normal after they defeated Nome, their grandfather: Woodbury, the youngest one, continued to hunt down Nome’s henchmen while Alice, the middle one, stayed in Wonderland and Doris, the eldest one, embarked on a new journey.

        On a winter day, Doris was walking through a vast forest with her pet dog, Toto, which began to dash forward in wild excitement.

        “Toto! Wait!” Seeing that, Doris immediately halted Toto. With a stern look, she looked at it and said, “It’s dangerous here so don’t stray too far from me, okay?”

        “Woof!” Toto ran back to Doris after responding with an obedient bark. Unexpectedly, a ball of blinding light suddenly appeared in the sky and stunned Toto.

        “Whoa!” Someone fell from the ball of light. Skillfully, he managed to stabilize his body in mid-air and landed on the ground safely without dropping that dramatically tall hat on his head.

        “Mad Hatter!” Doris shouted the man’s name and asked in surprise, “What are you doing here?”

        “Miss Doris!” The Mad Hatter lifted his head elatedly and said, “I finally found you!”

        “Find me? Did something happen?”

        “Yes.” The Mad Hatter stood up straight and continued worriedly, “Miss Alice has been depressed recently. She is always frowning… and she barely talks except when it comes to eating or drinking. We are all very worried about Miss Alice. We’ve tried different methods to cheer her up but none of them worked…”

        “How come? There must be something wrong. Let me think…” Resting her chin on a hand thoughtfully, Doris asked Mad Hatter, “How was meat for dinner? Did you bring her desserts afterward?”

        “The meat was all of the highest quality and the desserts were also brought to Miss Alice on time.”

        “What about the two bedtime horror stories every night?”

        “Of course I didn’t miss them. I even told Miss Alice three bedtime stories in one night recently.”

        “Umm… If so, she shouldn’t be upset at all. Something is missing. What is it?” 
Doris looked around. All she saw was a white land buried under the snow. The freezing air sent a shudder through her body yet it also gave her an idea.

         “Oh! Maybe she wants that!”

        “That?” The Mad Hatter tilted his head to a side in bewilderment. He tried to figure it out for a while but he failed, so he asked instead, “Miss Doris, what do you mean by “that”?”

        “Don’t worry about that. I know why Alice is unhappy. But I have to get someone first. Just head back to Wonderland first and wait for me!” Doris hurriedly picked up Toto and ran away before the Mad Hatter could say anything, leaving the latter no choice but to return to Wonderland and try his best to cheer Alice up.

        However, Alice remained sullen and silent for the next few days no matter what tricks the Mad Hatter did, and it was driving the Mad Hatter crazy.

        “When is Miss Doris coming back?” While the Mad Hatter hoped that Doris could come back to Wonderland as soon as possible, he prepared Alice’s dinner as usual. It was only after making sure that every dish was perfect that he went to Alice’s room.

        “Miss Alice, the dinner is ready. Today’s dinner is as sumptuous as ever!”

        “Mm.” Alice responded with a soft snort which was one of the few reactions she had given the Mad Hatter for the past few days. As she got out of her bed, she followed the Mad Hatter to the dining room only to walk into the pitch black.

        “Why is it so dark in here? Miss Alice can’t have dinner in a dark room like this,” the Mad Hatter muttered to himself. Just as he was going to turn on the light, the room lit up with a sudden snap, revealing two figures who ran to Alice with a gift and a cake in their arms.

        “Alice! Merry Christmas!” Doris and Woodbury shouted in unison.

        “You two… What are you doing here?” asked Alice, whose voice sounded a bit hoarse after a long time of reticence; her face looked rather tense for some reason.

        “The Mad Hatter told me that you were feeling depressed. Since Christmas is around the corner, I guessed you must be craving presents, so I asked Woodbury to help me get you one,” Doris said with a smile while raising the teddy bear that was half of her height in her arms.

        “Doris told me you want a teddy bear so I made you one! Isn’t it pretty?” Woodbury said proudly, lifting her chin, arms akimbo.

        However, Alice did not show a smile of joy. Instead, she became nervous and stuttered, “Doris, Woodbury… You…”

        “Alice, what’s wrong? You don’t like the teddy bear?” Alice’s hesitant reaction dampened Woodbury’s spirit.

        Seeing the look of dejection on Woodbury’s face, Alice immediately continued, “Wh-what took you two so long?”

        Alice took out two delicately wrapped gift boxes from her pocket and gave them to Doris and Woodbury. Then she explained awkwardly, “I… I just happen to have two spares. I was going to throw them away… But since you two are here, I guess… I may as well just give them to you.”

        “What?! Are you really giving these to us?” Doris shrieked in surprise.

        “This is the first gift Alice has ever given me! I’m so happy!” Alice’s gifts brightened Woodbury’s spirit. She and Doris took the gift boxes excitedly and opened them right away. Inside the boxes were two delicate silver brooches.

        “It’s so pretty!” Doris and Woodbury hurriedly put on the brooches. Together, they gave Alice a big hug while bursting into laughter.

        They said, “We love them!”

        Locked in a passionate embrace, Alice smiled and put her arms around her two biological sisters. With deep affection, she whispered, “I’m glad you like them.”

        “Sigh, so Miss Alice was depressed because she missed her sisters. For goodness’ sake, she could have just told me that.” Moved by the heartwarming embrace of the three sisters, the Mad Hatter took out a handkerchief to wipe away a tear from the corner of his eye.

        “Well, but I guess that’s just who Miss Alice is…”
STORY_2857:
In a bedroom, a teenage minerelf was tossing and turning on his bed. Suddenly, a creak of the door startled him. He lifted his head to take a look only to be stunned by the beautiful “girl” standing by the door. Yet, the teenage elf knew clearly that the “girl” was actually a “him” not a “she” because they had been best friends for a long time.

        “Diamond!”  The teenage minerelf, Onyx, shouted out the “girl’s” name. Then he asked, “What are you doing in my bedroom so late at night and dressing like that?”

        Diamond, who was gazing at Onyx quietly, flashed a brilliant smile when he heard Onyx’s question. His exquisite face looked even more beautiful in the silver light. With a disarming chuckle, Diamond let his gaze roam over Onyx, then he slowly said, “But it seems you like it very much.”

        Diamond walked toward the bed step by step after saying those words. His smile seemed to have bewitched Onyx, who could only watch as Diamond climbed onto his bed until he felt an electric jolt to his body when his best friend touched his thigh—

        “Woah—!” Onyx sat up straight with a scream. He let out a sigh of relief as he found that Diamond was not in his room, and he murmured to himself, “So it was a dream—”

        Before Onyx’s voice trailed off, someone suddenly opened the door. It was Diamond in some girl’s clothing, walking toward him step by step. A strange feeling of déjà vu plunged the teenage minerelf into a state of bewilderment.

        “Am I… still dreaming?”

        Onyx soon got his answer—Diamond gave a slap on the back of his head mercilessly with a bang.

        “Ouch! That hurts!” Diamond’s slap brought Onyx’s mind back to reality. Glaring at Diamond, Onyx asked, “What was that for?”

        “The sun is up. But I saw that you were still sleepy so I just kindly woke you up. How was that?”

        “Well, thanks to you, I’m now all awake!” Feeling wronged, Onyx asked Diamond in annoyance, “What are you doing in my bedroom in the early morning? Besides, why do you dress like that… Don’t tell me you got addicted to dressing like a girl after trying it for the first time.”

        In order to escape from taking the throne, Diamond made a bet with his grandfather that he would get his wish if he managed to attend the Minerelf Girls’ School while disguising himself as a girl without exposing his true identity until graduation. That was why Diamond went to Onyx dressed in a girl’s uniform to see if his disguise was perfect.

        “Although you said I’m perfect in the girl’s uniform last time, I had this feeling that I needed to expand my sample base when I got back home. Then I saw this,” said Diamond, who showed Onyx an advertising poster.

        “New restaurant opening… A special buy-1-get-1-free dining offer for couples… The food does seem delicious but what does it have to do with you?”

        “It is a great chance for a test!” Diamond said emotionally. “Let’s go to the restaurant and have dinner as a couple. If we get that offer without anyone doubting us, that will prove that my disguise is truly perfect!”

        “Huh? You and I as a couple?!”

        “Yes! Enough with the talking! I heard that the restaurant is very popular so we have to get there earlier to get in line. So hurry up and get changed!”

        Left with no choice, Onyx changed his clothes and went to the restaurant with Diamond. The two managed to get a table in the first round. As soon as they were seated, they found themselves surrounded by affectionate couples who were either drinking from one glass or feeding each other food. Their public display of affection made Onyx feel awkward.

        On the other hand, Diamond had a good time. He took a full plate of food and started wolfing them down. He even gave a positive comment, “The food here is delicious! Go take some!”

        “O-okay.” Even though Onyx felt out of place, he took some food and began eating as he saw Diamond enjoying himself, suppressing the inexplicable feeling in his chest.

        “There’s new food! I’ll go get it!” Diamond rushed to the buffet table excitedly only to hear a commotion in the staff-only corridor. Out of curiosity, he stuck his head around the wall to see what the commotion was about. Then, he saw a man grabbing a waitress’ wrist while leaning toward her brazenly. It was clearly an act of molestation.

        Enraged by the sight, Diamond strode to the man and felled him with a punch in the face. Holding his face, the man glared at Diamond and shouted, “Ho-ho-how could you punch me?! This is not how a girl should act!”

        “Humph! No one can tell how a girl should act! There’s nothing wrong with defending oneself! Besides, who told you that I’m a girl?” Diamond looked down at the male staff with his arms folded before his chest, excluding an incredible masculine vigor and dominance.

        “You-you’re a boy?!”

        “Yeah, but that is none of your business. Now apologize to her!”

        “I—” The man sized up Diamond, thinking that he might have a chance over the slim minerelf. Just when he was about to hit back, someone burly came to the corridor.

        “Diamond!” It was Onyx, who came to find Diamond after seeing that he had gone for a long time. He sensed the hostile atmosphere in the corridor as he walked closer so he lowered his head and asked Diamond worriedly, “What happened?”

        “This bastard was going to molest the girl. I couldn’t stand it and gave him a punch but it seems that he hasn’t learned his lesson.”

        “What?” Onyx’s face darkened in an instant. He walked to the front of Diamond and stared at the man. As the man saw how brawny Onyx was, the man immediately dropped to his knees and begged for mercy, “I’m sorry! I was wrong!”

        Afterward, the man was kicked out of the restaurant. The waitress thanked Diamond and Onyx and even brought them dessert as a token of her appreciation. However, Diamond was rather unhappy because the people in the restaurant now knew that he was a boy.

        “Sigh… People still found out that I’m a boy.”

        Diamond remained depressed until the waitress handed him the bill.

        “I think we got the wrong bill. Why do we have 50% off?” Diamond asked in confusion.

        “It’s the right bill.” The waitress answered enthusiastically with her eyes moving around Diamond and Onyx, “Our restaurant also welcomes homosexual couples!”

        The waitress’ passionate enthusiasm made it hard for Diamond to clarify himself so he could only pay the bill quietly. As soon as the two minerelves stepped out of the restaurant, Diamond stroked his chin thoughtfully and asked Onyx, “So does it mean my disguise works…”
STORY_2859:
The night fell upon the remote town as usual, but tonight, the darkness brought an unsettling disturbance. Countless wicked creatures lurked in the shadows, their bloodthirsty eyes fixated on the peaceful town, ready to give the people a sanguinary nightmare.

        In a house nestled in a corner of the town, Alma, a little girl sleeping in her bedroom on the second floor, was awakened by some strange noises. Rubbing her groggy eyes, she sat up and called out softly, “Dad? Mom?”

        However, Alma heard no response from her parents. Instead, the disturbing noises downstairs grew louder. Alma walked out of her room, holding the handmade doll her father had crafted for her. The noises became clear and unobstructed, and the air was filled with a scent the little girl disliked.

        “Dad?” Alma paused for a moment before calling out again, “Mom?”

        “No… Alma… Don’t come down…” The voice was faint but Alma still recognized that it was his father immediately. A strong sense of unease crept up on her. Ignoring her father’s warning, she descended the stairs in her slippers, only to witness a horrifying spectacle at the moment her feet touched the floor. The doll slipped from her hands and fell to the floor as she let out a piercing scream, “Nooooooo—! Dad… Mom… No…NO!”

        “Grrr…” A gigantic scorpion-like monster turned its head as it heard the scream. With it standing in the living room, the once spacious space was now crammed. Its two massive pincers were dripping with blood. Alma’s beloved father lay weakly against a wall with a gaping wound in his left abdomen, while her mother whose right body had been torn apart lay motionless in a pool of blood.

        Despite the fatal injuries, the two parents struggled to move their damaged bodies upon seeing the monster walk toward Alma, summoning their last ounce of strength to shout to their daughter—

        “Alma! Run!”
        “Run and don’t look back!”

        However, the young Alma was paralyzed with fear by the gory scene before her. Her body went weak, and she could only silently watch as the gigantic monster slowly approached her with its wide mouth opened, emitting a putrid stench of savage desire.

        The monster raised its blood-stained pincers again, intending to tear apart the fragile little girl just like it had done to her parents. Yet, its vile wish went unfulfilled as two figures charged toward Alma, pushing her away and taking the brunt of the pincers for her.

        “Mom… Mom…” Alma murmured, trembling and huddling within the space created by her parents’ bodies. The blood dripping from their bodies stained her face red.

        “It… It’s okay… Mom and Dad…will protect you…” Despite the excruciating pain, Alma’s mother forced a smile and comforted her terrified daughter.

        “That’s right… Alma… Sweetie… Close your eyes… The nightmare will be over soon…”

        Alma listened to her father’s words and closed her eyes. Then she the dull sounds of something sharp stabbing a human’s flesh, one after another, repeatedly. To spare Alma from fear, her parents swallowed their agonizing screams of pain, only letting out a few stifled groans. It was until the two could no longer make a sound that the monster finally gave up its hunt for Alma and left the house.

        The little Alma had no clue that the monster had left, nor could she perceive the death of her parents. She simply closed her eyes and curled up in her own world, shutting off all of her senses, until someone carried her out from her parent’s cold bodies. As the sudden warmth scorched her numb soul, she abruptly opened her eyes. Tears immediately streamed down her face, yet she could barely produce a sound but only wept in silence.

        “Oh… Poor child…” The man sighed softly, holding Alma in his arms. Standing beside him was a beautiful cerapter.

        “Prometheus, what should we do with her,” asked the cerapter.

        “We’re always on the move, so we can’t take this girl with us. The only thing we can do is find a family in the nearby town and let them take care of her.”

        Afterward, Prometheus found a kind elderly couple for Alma, who treated the little girl as their own. They raised her into adulthood and passed away peacefully. Once again bereaved, still, Alma never forgot the hatred she held for her parents’ murderer, which eventually became the reason for her joining the gods’ army.
STORY_2860:
It was a bright morning when the sun shone brilliantly over the great lake that shimmered with the reflection of the vibrant blooming flowers nearby. Suddenly, a young man came and broke the tranquility, gasping for breath as he ran from afar. His eyes swiftly scanned the horizon until they landed on a peculiar rhombus crystal levitating by the lake, radiating a dazzling light.

        As the young man came to a halt in front of the rhombus crystal, he spent a moment to catch his breath. It was after he meticulously fixed his disheveled hair, ensuring his appearance was flawless, that he reached out and touched the rhombus crystal which unleashed a blinding white light and engulfed him in an instant.

        In the next second, the young man found himself standing in front of a beautiful cottage. In the cottage’s courtyard was an exquisite woman dressed in a flowing gown sitting at a small table,  gracefully sipping a cup of tea. As she noticed the young man’s arrival, she put down her cup and approached him, her face wearing a gentle and affectionate smile.

        “Billy, you came,” said the woman named Pandora. Furrowing her brows slightly, she asked with a hint of playfulness, “Why is your head covered in sweat? Did you run here? Didn’t I tell you not to rush?”

        Pandora took out a handkerchief and gently wiped the sweat from Billy’s forehead. As the young man’s gaze fell upon the woman’s captivating face and his nose took in her alluring fragrance, he became momentarily entranced, recalling the first time they met.

        Billy was the youngest son of a wealthy merchant in a prosperous town in the North. Despite being favored and privileged since childhood, he never wanted to follow in his father’s footsteps in running a business. Instead, he aspired to become a soldier on the front lines, defending humans against the constant onslaught of demons.

        However, his father disapproved of his aspiration, which led to a heated argument between the two. In a fit of rage, Billy stormed out of his home and ran into the forest outside the town, not knowing that a group of demons lurked nearby. Just as he was about to be surrounded by the demons, a golden bird appeared and guided him to the rhombus crystal—a magical portal that connected to a fantasyland where he eluded the enemies and met Pandora.

        Back then, Pandora approached him—just like the very moment—and tended to his wounds tenderly. Her kindness captivated him entirely. Later, he learned from Pandora that she was cursed and trapped inside the magical box, unable to return to the mortal realm.

        Of course, it was difficult for a young man like Billy to see a beautiful woman suffer, so he promised to free Pandora from the box. He also began to visit the magical realm in the box frequently to spare her from loneliness.

        “What’s wrong? Did you exhaust yourself during the run? That’s why I always tell you not to rush.” Pandora’s words brought Billy out of his reverie. As he regained his composure, he looked at Pandora, who was wiping the sweat off his forehead so attentively. His heart inevitably fluttered, and he could not help but say with deep affection, “Because I was afraid to keep you waiting for too long.”

        “I’m fine with waiting. I’m trapped here, after all. I have nothing else to do but wait,” Pandora said with a hint of sorrow in her voice, accompanied by a slight tug at the corners of her mouth.

        Seeing the melancholic look on her face, Billy felt a twinge in his heart. He firmly held Pandora’s hands and said with determination, “I will definitely free you out of this box! I’ve already planted your seeds around the town.”

        “You’re my hero,” Pandora said softly as she leaned into Billy’s embrace. She then whispered sweetly, “Thank you.”

        “No, it’s nothing at all,” Billy replied, putting his arms around Pandora. With a hesitant look on his face, he asked, “But is that all?”

        “Well, for now, all we need to do is wait for the night of the full moon. My curse will be lifted as soon as you bring the rhombus crystal into the town,” said Pandora, raising her head. With her captivating and alluring gaze constantly tugging at Billy’s will, she added, “And then, we can be together.”

        “...That’s good to hear.” Billy, bewitched by Pandora, suppressed his doubts and succumbed to the intimate entanglement with the exquisite woman. It was only when the sun set that Billy reluctantly left the magical realm, leaving Pandora alone.

        As soon as Billy’s figure disappeared, the tenderness and sweetness on Pandora’s face faded away, replaced by a cold, haughty expression. Unable to hide her jubilation, she said, “Men are truly stupid. They think of themselves as the savior as long as a woman pretends to be weak and adds a few sweet words. Little do they know they are nothing but easily manipulated fools…”

        Pandora looked up at the void above her head, a radiantly wicked smile spreading across her face. With her sinister intentions hidden within her voice, she shouted, “Oh, the box of hope, soon I will devour your power. Then I can return to the mortal realm without passively waiting for people to make wishes or losing my hatred for Loki. And then, I will torture him to death with my own hands... Ahahaha!”

        The thought of the coming glorious future filled Pandora with excitement. She could not help but burst into hysterical laughter with her hands on her face, her voice echoing throughout the magical realm…

❊

        Finally, it was the night of the full moon. Billy walked toward the center of the town with the rhombus crystal, as he had promised.

        “Billy, this is far enough,” Pandora said.

        “Okay, I'll let go then.” As Billy opened his palm, the rhombus crystal rose gently into the air and began to spin, reflecting a radiant halo under the moonlight. Eventually, the halo transformed into the figure of Pandora.

        “Pandora!” Billy shouted out Pandora’s name in excitement as it was the first time he saw her in the real world. He rushed toward her with joy only to find that his body passed through her. He turned back in astonishment and asked, “Wh-why?”

        “It’s because my curse hasn’t been completely lifted; something is still missing.” The translucent Pandora covered her mouth with a hand. She playfully stuck out her tongue and lightly licked her crimson lips. Her strangely flirtatious demeanor was nothing Billy had seen before, which gave him a sense of fear for a moment. But he soon pushed the feeling aside and anxiously asked, “What is it? I’ll get it for you!”

        “No need, because I’ve already found it,” Pandora replied with an unusually sweet smile that yet had a chilling undertone.

        “Huh? What are you talking about— Woah!” Vines suddenly sprouted from the ground, binding Billy and causing him to cry out in surprise. But what terrified him most were the countless screams and cries emerging from all corners of the town.

        “Pandora, what... what have you done?”

        “I simply broke free from the box’s restraints, using your life and the lives of the people in this town,” Pandora said, her chin resting on a hand. She tilted her head to the right, displaying the coquettish pose Billy used to love. But now, it only filled him with fear. 

        “So, you lied to me…” Billy strenuously lifted his head, his face was filled with sadness. He said, “So, you never liked me…”

        “Yeah, why would I like a fool like you?” Pandora said, her tone filled with disdain.

        “Ha... hahaha!” Billy laughed through the pain in his heart. With tears streaming down his face, he said, “Yes, you’re right—I am a fool! A miserable who believed you! But you’re even more miserable than I am, Pandora.”

        “What are you talking about? How could I be more miserable than a dying foolish man like you?” asked Pandora, her face darkened, displeased.

        “At least I have a family who truly loves me, but no one will ever love a wicked woman like you! And you’ll spend the rest of your life begging for someone’s—”

        With a loud snap, the vines, under Pandora’s control, strangled Billy. His blood splattered onto the ground. However, Pandora’s raging fury remained unquenched even after ruthlessly taking the man’s life. Clenching her fists tightly, she nervously bit her lower lip.

        “No! How would no one love me? No way!” Pandora vehemently denied Billy’s words. She raised her hands high, and a dark purple glow converged from all corners of the town, forming a massive vortex of power. Taking aim at the levitating box, she forcefully hurled it.

        “As soon as I consume the power of the box, I will be invincible! I will get all my wishes, and Loki will beg for my mercy and love me! I will become the happiest woman in the world!”

        As the two immense forces collided, a blinding light appeared, illuminating the town as bright as day.

        Crack! Unable to withstand the colliding force, the box emitted a cracking sound. Pandora’s face lit up with joy, and she fervently poured more power into it.

        “Look, everything is going according to my plan... Wait! What... The box is going to self-destruct and take me down with it... No! NOOO!”

        The moment the box shattered, the overflowing power rushed towards Pandora, engulfing her completely. She had no choice but to summon her remaining strength to protect herself. Still, she was propelled by the force of the box of hope, crashing into a wall and losing consciousness.

        It was not until the dawn’s rays shone once again that Pandora regained consciousness. She looked around in confusion, her eyes roaming around the unfamiliar surroundings.

        “Where… Where am I… No… Who am I… I.. I can’t remember anything… I need to ask someone… find someone…” In confusion, Pandora struggled to get up from the ground. She then dragged her weary body away from the town, in search of the memories she had lost...
STORY_2861:
In a cozy and elegant cottage, a young woman named Gretchen was trying on different clothes in her room. However, judging by the multitude of garments over the chairs, table, and sofa, she seemed unable to find one that truly pleased her.

        After quite some time, Gretchen finally selected three dresses from her extensive collection and placed them on the bed. Stroking her chin, she scrutinized them left and right.

        “Today is my wedding anniversary with Faust, and we must celebrate it properly. The food is ready, all that’s left is my clothes. Which one should I wear?” Gretchen pondered, torn between sweetness and worry.

        Gretchen had supported herself since she was young, due to her parents’ early passing. She had grown accustomed to bearing all hardships alone until, by a twist of fate, she met Faust. It was in that very instant when their eyes met that Gretchen knew she had found the person she had been searching for all her life—the shoulder she could lean on, so she married him shortly after.

        However, Faust was always overly concerned about Gretchen. He would search the entire city for her if she was home even slightly late. He would restrict her food choices, believing that only the foods he chose were best for her. This kind of life was supposed to be stressful, but in Gretchen’s eyes, it was Faust’s way of expressing his love for her. So, she chose to stifle her complaints even though she was not truly happy or satisfied.

        “All of this is because Faust loves me too much. It’s my fault that I haven’t given him enough security. Therefore, I must give him more love to put his mind at ease!”

        The kind-hearted Gretchen took the blame for everything despite the fact that it was none of her fault. She even hoped to fulfill Faust’s unreasonable desires by giving more of herself. That was why, from the three dresses she had chosen, she picked the one with a bolder design, hoping to showcase her determination to change for her husband.

        After dressing up and preparing dinner, Gretchen decorated the dining room to create a romantic atmosphere, all in an effort to surprise Faust. However, things turned out to be completely different from what she had expected.

        Creak. It was the sound of the door being opened. Gretchen immediately walked out to greet Faust at the entrance. Her heart pounded as she imagined Faust’s reaction upon seeing her in a different outfit—perhaps he would embrace her with delight or shyly blush. Contrary to her expectation, a deep anger filled Fuast’s eyes the moment he laid eyes on her.

        “Why are you dressed like this?” Faust accused loudly, his tone harsh as if she had committed a heinous and unforgivable crime.

        “I-I… Today is our wedding anniversary, and I wanted to surprise you, so I wore—” Gretchen's words faltered as she saw Faust’s increasingly darkened face. Panicked, she hastily said, “I can go change immediately!”

        “No…” The look on Faust’s face carried both paranoia and madness as he said, “You do resent my control over you after all.”

        “No, that’s not true! Faust, I love you!”
