         “I see… But if I were to offer my Xian energy to nurture the spirit, I might be unable to use my power freely for several days. Plus, I still need to venture into the human realm to gather materials for my new garments. What if I encounter demons along the way? It would be a dead end,” Zhongli Quan said. But as soon as he observed the anxious look on Cao Guojiu’s face, he changed his mind, “But, I guess I can give you a helping hand if you help me gather one of the materials.”

         “Deal! Xiao Suo is currently resting in the handcuffs. Just keep them with you. It should help him stabilize his form, ” Cao Guojiu responded.

         Then, Cao Guojiu hurriedly flew away soon after Zhongli Quan told him where to get the material.

         Carrying the handcuffs in his pockets, Zhongli Quan descended to the human realm. He headed to a vast forest and ventured into the depths until nightfall when he finally arrived at his destination—the Silver Moon Lake.

         According to ancient records, there existed a magical silk thread within the Silver Moon Lake. Only by scooping up the reflection of the full moon from the center of the lake could one obtain it. It was said that clothing woven from this silk thread would possess an ethereal beauty.

         And so, Zhongli Quan channeled his power to float above the water’s surface. He bent down and reached into the lake. As he raised his hand once more, several strands of silver-glowing silk thread lay in his palm.

         “It’s truly exquisite. Clothing made from this silk thread will undoubtedly complement my charming appearance. I should gather more while the moon is still high— Argh!”

         Just as Zhongli Quan became enraptured by the silver threads, an enormous fish suddenly leaped out of the water, catching hold of his legs and dragging him into the lake before he could react.

         Zhongli Quan attempted to muster his power to resist, only to feel an odd chill creeping from his legs to his entire body. His power seemed to congeal, rendering it ineffectual.

         “It’s poison!  The fish’s teeth are poisonous, preventing me from utilizing my Xian energy! Damn it!”

         No matter how hard Zhongli Quan struggled, he was still slowly dragged down to the lake’s depths. Just as he was on the brink of losing consciousness, a golden light shimmered from his clothes.

         From the light emerged a translucent boy, grasping Zhongli Quan’s hand to pull him to the water’s surface. Yet, his strength proved insufficient against the formidable fish which pulled the both of them down to the lake’s bottom.

         The boy was none other than the spirit of the handcuffs, Xiao Suo. Although he had already lost the ability to maintain his physical humanoid form, he still forcefully materialized upon sensing Zhongli Quan was in grave danger.

         “It’s so cold…so dark…and scary here, but… I have to save Dad!” A determined yet childish voice rang in Zhongli Quan’s mind, awakening his consciousness. He opened his eyes to see a resolute little face and felt a warm touch.

         A comforting warmth flowed from the boy’s hand into Zhongli Quan’s body, dispelling the poison within him. But as the boy’s power flowed into Zhongli Quan, his limbs began to fade and disappear.

         “He actually sacrificed himself to save me... even if it means he would vanish?” Zhongli Quan felt a sudden burn in his nose, and a silent flame ignited within him.

         Free from poison, Zhongli Quan clenched his teeth and unleashed a powerful blast of energy, pushing the monstrous fish away.

         As Zhongli Quan broke free, he took off the fan on his back and fiercely struck at the bottom, creating a tremendous force that propelled him and Xiao Suo out of the water in an instant.

         Back on the shore, Zhongli Quan began to relentlessly pour his Xian energy into Xiao Suo’s body. Seeing the frail and pale appearance of the spirit, he could not help but feel a mix of guilt and gratitude.

         “Hey, you, hang in there! Cao Guojiu will give me trouble if you disappear like this!”

         “Dad…”

         “Cao Guojiu isn’t here. I’m not your dad,” Zhongli Quan said, even as he continued to transfer his Xian energy. It was after he had exhausted his power that the fading figure of Xiao Suo finally stabilized.

         “But you are my dad… And this is what you were looking for, right?” The weak little boy raised a bundle of silver threads.

         In Xiao Suo’s hand were indeed the magical threads from the Silver Moon Lake.

         Zhongli Quan was inexplicably moved by the sight of the threads in his hand.

         Zhongli Quan brought the weakened Xiao Suo back home and met with Cao Guojiu, who had already gathered the material as requested. As Cao Guojiu saw Xiao Suo, he unexpectedly held him tightly. Witnessing the intimate connection between the Xian and the spirit. Zhongli Quan could not help but feel a strange sense of envy.

         “Xiao Suo, let’s go home.”

         “Wait.” Zhongli Quan intercepted them. “Xiao Suo has great potential. I think it’d be better for him to stay and be my assistant!”

         “You expect me to say yes? No!” Cao Guojiu retorted with discontent.

         “I’m not asking you! I’m asking Xiao Suo!” Zhongli Quan stubbornly replied. 

         “I’m his father, so my decision counts!”

         “Oh, so what? I’m also his dad!”

         “Humph, why don’t we just ask Xiao Suo what he wants?”

         “Fine, ask him! You don’t scare me!”

         “Xiao Suo, who are you choosing? Me or this fat pig?”

         “Humph, I’m definitely a better choice compared to a schmuck like you.”

         “Huh? You’re both my dads. How could I choose between you… How about we take turns? Is that okay?” Xiao Suo raised a pleading smile while holding and gently swinging both of his two fathers’ hands. His action melted Zhongli Quan and Cao Guojiu’s hearts, and they both agreed to his suggestion.

         From then on, whenever Zhongli Quan and Cao Guojiu met, they would argue as usual, but Xiao Suo would always calm them down before their fight escalated, bringing a peaceful atmosphere to the Heavenly Kingdoms…
STORY_2872:
As a result of a prank gone wrong, Han Xiangzi accidentally released the evil spirit in a mirror. The evil spirit lunged toward Han Xiangzi the moment the seal was broken. To protect him, He Xian’gu ended up being dragged into the mirror. Overwhelmed by guilt, Han Xiangzi sought help from Taishang Laojun to rescue He Xian’gu.

        Examining the mirror, Taishang Laojun shook his head.

        “Taishang Laojun… What is it?” Han Xiangzi asked nervously. 

        “The evil spirit has dragged He Xian’gu into the world inside the mirror, and it is currently absorbing her Xian energy. Her soul will scatter if we don’t manage to save her within four hours. In order to do so, we must work together. I need you to enter the mirror and rescue her while I will sustain the exit.” Taishang Laojun said solemnly.

        The news of a possible solution slightly dispelled Han Xiangzi’s anxiety, and he promptly nodded in agreement. As Taishang Laojun cast a spell on the mirror, a beam of light emerged and transported Han Xiangzi into the mirror world.

        When Han Xiangzi opened his eyes, all he could see was a dense fog. Faced with the unknown realm, even someone as playful as Han Xiangzi dared not make a reckless move but cautiously feel his way through the fog.

        “Hehehe.”

        Suddenly, Han Xiangzi heard a peal of sinister laughter behind him, but he saw no one when he turned around.

        Frowning, Han Xiangzi turned back and continued moving forward. However, something icy cold grabbed his ankle after he took a few steps. He quickly shook it off and stumbled forward. Just when he managed to steady himself, he felt the coldness tugging at his right arm.

        Although Han Xiangzi tried to grab hold of the evil spirit, it let go of his arm and started nudging him from another direction. It was obvious that the spirit was toying with him.

        “Heh-heh-heh.”

        Another burst of sinister laughter echoed from all directions, only fueling Han Xiangzi’s anger. ‘How dare this evil spirit play me like a toy! As the king of pranks, I shall teach it a lesson!’

        Closing his eyes, Han Xiangzi regulated his breathing and focused all his energy.

        “I got you!” As Han Xiangzi sensed a faint air movement behind his shoulder, he extended his hand without a backward glance and successfully grabbed hold of the icy thing—a cold wrist.

        “Reveal yourself” Han Xiangzi shouted, exerting all his strength to pull on the wrist. He forcefully dragged the person out of the dense fog, letting them fall to the ground. Only then did he see the true face of the evil spirit—a young boy with blue skin.

        Dazed from the impact, the evil spirit was surprised when he saw Han Xiangzi, who was staring at it fiercely.

        “Release He Xian’gu immediately!” Han Xiangzi demanded.

        “Heh! No, I won’t! What can you do to stop me? Once I absorb all the energy of that Xian, the rest of you will all perish!” The evil spirit glared back at Han Xiangzi, its body emitting an ominous glow.

        “What can I do to stop you, you ask? Humph! Let me show you the essence of a prank!”

        As Han Xiangzi spoke, he summoned his cloak and infused it with his Xian energy. He threw the radiant lion-headed cloak into the air. In an instant, the cloak transformed into an auspicious lion ten times larger than Han Xiangzi himself.

        Realizing the impending danger, the evil spirit attempted to flee but was caught in the lion’s jaws.

        “You should feel lucky. No one has experienced this ‘first-class seat’ before,” Han Xiangzi chuckled with a brilliant smile as he leaped onto the lion’s back. With the evil spirit held in the lion’s mouth, they raced through the dense fog at an astonishing speed.

        The lion’s speed gradually increased within the mist until it appeared as a golden streak of light. It was such a velociously rough ride that even the evil spirit’s blue face turned pale due to the giddiness.

        The dense fog, created by the evil spirit’s power, allowed the spirit to heighten its senses and effortlessly toy with those who entered the world inside the mirror. Never the evil spirit would have thought its advantage would turn against itself.

        “Are you going to release He Xian’gu or not?”

        “No!”

        “Xiao Shi! Shake him!” Noticing the evil spirit’s discomfort, Han Xiangzi commanded the lion to vigorously shake its head which intensified its dizziness. The spirit’s face turned purple as it felt a burn in its throat, seeing stars in its vision.

“Yes or no?”

        “I...I…”

        “Xiao Shi! Flip him, ten times!” Han Xiangzi gave another command while snapping his fingers.

        The lion immediately followed the command, hurling the evil spirit into the air and catching it just before it hit the ground.

        After several flips, the evil spirit was on the brink of collapse. As the lion prepared to flip it once more into the air, the spirit trembled and weakly raised its hand, saying, “Wait… I’ll talk…”

        However, the evil spirit’s surrender only let to a wicked grin on Han Xiangzi’s face.

        “Go on, Xiao Shi,” he commanded.

        “Wh-... WHY?!” pleaded the evil spirit in disbelief.

        “Because it’s fun!” Han Xiangzi replied with a smile that was so radiantly genuine that send a faint chill down the spirit’s spine.
        “Just kill me already!” the evil spirit cried out in despair. Still, its cry did not stop the lion from throwing it into the air again. After dozens of flips, the evil spirit finally vomited up all that it had had in its stomach and could only lie feebly on the ground.

        With all its fighting spirit drained, the evil spirit took Han Xiangzi through the dense fog to where He Xian’gu was. Together, the two returned to reality through the exit sustained by Taishang Laojun.

        Upon seeing Taishang Laojun, the evil spirit rushed forward and grabbed his robe, crying out desperately, “Please capture me now! You were the one who sealed me all those years ago. Now seal me once again! I’d rather be confined in the mirror than ever see that monster again!”

        “Ahem,” Han Xiangzi cleared his throat disapprovingly as he heard the spirit refer to him as “that monster”.

        “I mean the great Xian! Great Xian!” the evil spirit hastily corrected itself, acting its most obedient self ever, which left He Xian’gu and Taishang Laojun dumbfounded.

        Later, Xian’gu and Han Xiangzi left Taishang Laojun’s residence as he prepared to reseal the evil spirit within the mirror.

        “Um… He Xian’gu… Are you... alright?” Han Xiangzi asked, wearing a remorseful and dejected expression that resembled a wilted eggplant.

        Throughout all of Han Xiangzi’s pranks in the past, he had never truly harmed anyone. Yet, his prank this time had nearly cost He Xian’gu’s soul, and the thought of that made him feel repentant.

        “You did something wrong, so of course, you must ace the consequences,” He Xian’gu said solemnly, then slowly approached Han Xiangzi.

        Instead of attempting to escape as usual, Han Xiangzi obediently raised his head, closing his eyes to accept his punishment—

        “Ah! Ouch!” Han Xiangzi winced, rubbing his forehead reddened after He Xian’gu’s flick.

        “Now we’re ever,” she said.

        “Huh? That’s all?” Han Xiangzi looked at He Xian’gu, his mouth agape with surprise.

        Amused by his reaction, He Xian’gu asked, “What? That wasn’t enough for you? You haven’t finished copying the rule book yet, remember?” 

        As soon as He Xian’gu finished speaking, Han Xiangzi swiftly donned his lion-headed cloak and flew up into the air. Making a funny face at her, he retorted, “Humph! I’m never going to copy the rule book!”

        Watching Han Xiangzi’s receding figure, He Xian’gu could not help but smile and whisper, “That’s the Han Xiangzi I know.”

        Just then, a piece of paper fell in front of He Xian’gu, with the words written on it: Sorry, old bat! 

        “Han Xiangzi! Who are you calling an old bat?” As usual, He Xian’gu bellowed with rage as she saw the paper.
STORY_2873:
Zhang Guolao had been plagued by chronic pain in his knee recently. Fortunately, he learned about a famous massage parlor that specializes in bone pain from other Xians. It was rumored that the massage practitioner in that parlor—who was also known as the Xian of Bones—could dispel any bone pain.

        Exasperated by the knee pain, Zhang Guolao immediately descended to the human realm where the massage parlor was located. Yet, his knees began to ache as he looked at the seemingly endless flight of stairs in front of the parlor.

        “Ow, ow… No, I can do this. I’m just a staircase away from getting cured… The pain will be gone for good once I see the Xian of Bones…”

        Finally, after much effort, Zhang Guolao managed to climb the long staircase and make it to the massage parlor, only to find a small sign hanging on the door that said, “Closed.”

        Zhang Guolao breathed a long sigh, trying to alleviate the pain through a deep breath. Just as he was about to return home in disappointment, he heard the cries of a woman coming from inside the massage parlor.

        “I can’t just do nothing when there is someone causing harm!” Zhang Guolao muttered to himself.

        Enduring the pain in his knee, Zhang Guolao rushed into the house, inside of which he saw a monkey wielding a red rod, relentlessly beating a plump and beautiful woman.

        “Stop!” 

        Zhang Guolao shouted, gathering his Xian energy at his fingertips to form a ball of light that shot toward the monkey. Yet, the monkey swiftly blocked his attack with the rod.

        “Who dares to attack me, Sun Wukong!” The money, also known as Sun Wukong, roared angrily. He charged to the front of Zhang Guolao in an instant, raising his rod to strike. Zhang Guolao narrowly dodged the attack by turning his body to the side.

        Yet, Sun Wukong was unyielding—he changed his attack from a downward strike to a sweeping motion.

        Zhang Guolao intended to duck and evade the attack. However, the pain in his knee flared up, causing his movements to falter. As a result, Sun Wukong’s red rod hit his knee directly, which, unexpectedly, struck the misaligned bone back into place with a crisp sound, putting an end to the constant disturbing pain in just a second.

        “What… I’m cured!” Zhang Guolao thought in delight. His once stiff movements suddenly became fluid, allowing him to counter Sun Wukong’s attacks. This sparked Sun Wukong’s combative spirit, and his moves became even more fierce."  

        The Xian and the monkey engaged in a fierce exchange of punches and rod strikes. Shadows of their fists and rod flashed in the air, causing gusts of explosive wind between them. The intensity of their fight ignited excitement in the onlooking woman, causing her whole body to tremble like a leaf.

        Eventually, the woman who was unable to contain her inner desires impulsively rushed into the middle of the two’s intense clash of fists and rod, taking two heavy blows at the same time.

        The woman slumped to the ground upon impact. Zhang Guolao quickly ceased his attacks and approached her with concern. He asked, “Are you alright—”

        “Ohhhh— That was amazing!” The woman, Lady White Bones, abruptly lifted her head and exclaimed with joy. Excitement and satisfaction painted her delicate face with a rosy glow.

        The woman’s unusual reaction left Zhang Guolao puzzled. He turned to Sun Wukong, who was standing nearby, and asked, “What... What is going on?”

        “It’s obvious. This demon loves getting beaten by others. She insisted on me hitting her, so I got annoyed and tried to beat her away,” Sun Wukong explained.

        “Yes. And Sir, your punches were quite impressive. The teamwork between you two just now was marvelous. Can you do it again?” Lady White Bones eagerly invited. Her excitement was evident.
　　
        “Well… I didn’t know the demons in the human realm have become so strange these days. It appears that I have stayed in the Heavenly Kingdom for such a long time,” Zhang Guolao sighed lightly.

        “Nope. She’s the only strange one here,” Sun Wukong replied, heading toward the door. “Well, I still have some business to do. But maybe we can spar again another time.”

        “No! Wait—” Although Lady White Bones tried to chase after Sun Wukong, the latter swiftly leaped onto a cloud and disappeared into the sky.

        “Tut! He ran away!” Lady White Bones muttered. Then, she turned around and looked at Zhang Guolao, flashing a smile that was both appeasing and scheming. She slowly approached the Xian.

        “Um, now that I see you’re fine, it’s time for me to leave.” Zhang Guolao, who smelled trouble, quickly turned around and leaped out of the window, as if he feared that Lady White Bones would catch up to him, showing an agility far beyond his age as he escaped from the massage parlor…
STORY_2874:
In the depths of a lush forest, there was a secluded mountain cave. A young girl and a white puppy approached silently from a distance, taking cover behind the nearest tree trunk. 

        Putting her head round the tree trunk, the girl placed two fingers close to her right eye and began drawing a sigil in the air. As she completed the sigil, it shimmered with a golden light, allowing her right eye to see clearly into the dark depths of the cave. Inside the cave were numerous glistening spiderwebs, intricately woven into a dense network. Hanging below the webs were several cocooned figures, while beneath them was a giant spider youkai with the upper body of a woman. Holding a lifeless body—one whose eyes wide open, staring into the void with an eerie stillness—in her arms, the youkai continuously spun silk to encase it in a cocoon.

        Appalled by the cruel sight, the girl undid her spell. Her face grew solemn as she murmured softly, “So it’s true…The missing villagers have all been abducted and killed by that youkai in the cave.”

        The girl’s name was Suzuko. When Suzuko was little, an evil man murdered her parents while she and Woofy, an white inuyoukai, miraculously survived. They were later rescued by Shigeharu, an Onmyōji who became Suzuko’s master, teaching her the Onmyōdō of five elements.

        To avenge her parents’ death, Suzuko diligently honed her techniques, taking on various missions to gain experience and broaden her knowledge. A few days ago, she received a request from a small village where several villagers had gone missing. The witnesses claimed they had been abducted by a youkai, hoping Suzuko could save them.

        And so, Suzuko and Woofy set out from the mountain to visit the village. Following the scent left behind on the belongings of the missing villagers, they tracked it to this very cave. As expected, they found the spider youkai responsible for the missing villagers.

        ‘Woof! Should I go fight that spider youkai?’ Woofy’s voice brought Suzuko back from her thoughts.

        She shook her head and reached into her pocket, retrieving four small golden bells held between her fingers. It was a technique Suzuko had created herself to exact revenge against her parents’ murderer, Douman Ashiya. But for some reason, her technique was not complete—it always failed whenever she tried to use it.

        “This is the perfect opportunity to test my Golden Bell Technique,”  Suzuko whispered, calming her breath while channeling her power through her entire body. As she sensed the energy surging within her, she lunged toward the cave and rushed toward the entrance like a soaring swallow. Catching the spider youkai off guard, she hurled the golden bell in her right hand.

        With a crisp ringing sound, the four golden bells shot toward the spider youkai from different directions, releasing a fierce aura that subdued it. The spider youkai, of course, refused to be restrained. While swinging its appendages violently, it let out a ferocious roar, revealing its true barbaric nature which only fueled Suzuko’s hatred.

        ‘It’s all these abhorrent youkais’ fault. They killed my parents, and I shall exterminate them all,’ Suzuko thought, her heart filled with overwhelming resentment. For a fleeting second, her eyes flashed with a similar ferocity to that of the youkai.

        For some unknown reason, the four golden bells suddenly trembled, and then exploded with a loud bang. Once again, Suzuko’s technique failed at the critical moment, just like it had during her practise in the past. But this time, it was different as she was fighting a true youkai. 

        As Suzuko’s technique failed, the spider youkai regained its freedom. Filled with boiling rage, it raised its sharp appendage, ready to strike Suzuko, who had been immobilized due to the backlash from her failed technique. Just as the bladed appendage was about to land on her body…

        “Suzuko! Suzuko!” A white figure suddenly dashed forward, forcefully pushing the youkai aside. Relentless, the youkai extended its other appendage and swung it toward the white puppy, knocking it away. Unable to avoid the youkai’s retaliation, Woofy crashed heavily into a wall. Blood sipped through its mouth as it helplessly slumped onto the ground.

        “Woofy!” Suzuko’s eyes widened in shock. She hurriedly crawled over to Woofy’s side, drawing its listless body into her arms. Woofy opened its eyes and looked at Suzuko. Relieved to see her unharmed, its mouth curled up into a feeble smile as it let out a soft bark.

        “Suzuko… You’re okay… I’m…relieved…” Woofy weakly expressed.

        “Yes, I’m okay, and you will be too. I’ll take you back home now and Master will heal you!” After saying those words, Suzuko turned to leave the cave, only to be stopped by a swift attack that came from the side. Fortunately, Suzuko managed to leap away just in time to avoid it, witnessing a deep pit being formed on the spot where she had stood seconds ago.

        It was the spider youkai. As soon as it recovered from the impact and rose to its feet again, it pounced toward Suzuko with a ferocious cry, snarling, “I won’t let you leave alive! Now surrender and become one of my cocoons!”

        ‘I have no time to waste. I need to get Woofy to Master as soon as possible! I have to protect Woofy!’ Suzuko thought with absolute determination.

        Suzuko once again took out her golden bells and hurled it toward the youkai. The four golden bells rang out again, but this time, they did not explode like before. Instead, they burst into blinding light that captured the struggling youkai.

        “ARGHHH!” The spider youkai let out a miserable scream as it perished in Suzuko’s powerful blow.

        As soon as Suzuko successfully quelled the spider youkai, she hurried back home, bringing Woofy to her master, Shigeharu, for treatment. Fortunately, Woofy’s injuries were not severe, and with timely treatment, it would only take a few days of rest for it to fully recover.

        It was only then that Suzuko found relief and took the opportunity to share her doubts with her master. She asked, “Master, why did my Golden Bell Technique work this time?”

        “The Onmyōdō of five elements requires a clear and pure heart, free from hatred and resentment. You technique failed because your intentions are clouded,” Shigeharu explained with profound words. “Yet, empathy can unlock one’s hidden potential. Your strong desire to protect Woofy solidified your will, leading to the success of the technique.”

        “...I still don’t get it,” Suzuko replied dejectedly.

        With a warm smile, Shigeharu gently placed his hand on his beloved disciple’s head and said tenderly, “Don’t worry, my child. You will figure it out one day.”
STORY_2875:
Dark clouds loomed over the sky, casting an ominous shadow over a tranquil village.

        The clang of armor reverberated through the tense air, heavy and foreboding. Baldwin, the Paladin King of Darkness, consumed by the malevolence of his cursed blade, swung his sword toward the young villagers who dared to resist him. His strikes were swift and ruthless, precisely beheading each opponent until no one dared to defy him.

        Baldwin was once an innocent boy who lived in a village, where women constantly gave birth to deformed children. As the only able-bodied boy in the village, he shouldered the responsibility of caring for the elderly, catching the attention of a demon who carried a cursed blade. The demon murdered his parents, forcing the boy to take up the evil sword and become the inheritor of its malice.

        The will of many generations of paladins housed in the evil sword slowly distorted Baldwin’s mind, rendering him cold and merciless. He became deranged—even more than the demons he had fought against—as he sought the pinnacle of swordsmanship. However, the flow of time was unsparingly cruel, and thus Baldwin began to search for a successor—a strong and vengeful boy. Bloodshed befell numerous villages as he pursued his quest, and tonight another village, unfortunately, became his target.

        As always, Baldwin slaughtered all the robust men in the village, leaving only survivors lined up in a row. After plunging his cursed sword into the ground in the front of the line, he proceeded to behead each person taller than the blade, forcing the children who stood behind to witness their loved ones’ decapitated heads rolling down the square. Their cries of terror and sorrow filled the air. For a moment, the village seemed to have become a living hell.

        It was not until Baldwin beheaded a woman that a young boy ran to her lifeless body and burst into tears disregarding the the approaching blade of the evil sword. The sight of the fragile boy triggered a sense of familiarity within Baldwin, causing him to slow his sword’s momentum.

        ‘He…he’s me in the past… Back then, that demon slaughtered my parents and forced me to choose between death or becoming a puppet of the darkness… But I always wanted to be a great hero, someone who saves others... Why have I now become a merciless devil, reveling in bloodbath... Why...’ Baldwin thought.

        Suddenly, his thoughts cleared from the grip of the cursed blade’s influence. Memories of his childhood dream flooded his mind, accompanied by a dreadful sense of guilt and shame. The weight of guilt was so heavy that his grip on the sword slightly loosened. He stumbled and ran away from the village, straight into a nearby forest, where he leaned against a towering tree and slumped to the ground.

        Under the tree, Baldwin looked up at the sky where the dark clouds had lifted, revealing a full moon hanging over his head. As the gentle moonlight beckoned, he removed the helmet that had concealed his face for a long time. His weathered features, now clearly visible, no longer held the youthful vigor, and his eyes were no longer filled with a thirst for bloodshed but rather with confusion and remorse under the moonlight.

        “Senseless slaughter and the pursuit of ultimate swordsmanship were never what I desired,” he whispered, “My life was bound by the elders’ attachment to the village when I was young, and later, I became ensnared by the will of the evil sword… I don’t want this; I want to live my own life!”

        And so, Baldwin discarded his armor and buried the cursed sword in the forest. Then, he sought a prosperous town and found an ordinary job, living a peaceful life. There, he even met a woman who stirred his heart, someone he would like to start a family with.

        However, the ghosts of Baldwin’s past eventually got back to him. His massacre of the villages had stirred the wrath of both humans and gods, leading to a wanted notice being issued. As fate would have it, Baldwin’s lover happened upon the notice and noticed the resemblance to his features. Driven by the lure of the reward, she secretly reported him, conducting a covert operation with Baldwin’s enemies surrounding his home.

        Refusing to accept his demise, Baldwin fought back with all his might and managed to break free from the encircling pursuers. Still, outnumbered, he found himself trapped in a dead-end alley. Yet, something in the alley left him stunned—the evil sword he had buried in the forest was now impaled at the end of the alley alongside his discarded armor. It was as if fate had made it clear that he would never find solace in a peaceful life and he was destined to set foot in the vicious cycle again.

        “Heh... hahaha!” Baldwin let out a sorrowful laughter, resembling a cry. “So, I never truly escaped after all. Right, my hands are already stained with blood. What an idiot I am to expect that I could absolve myself of guilt and sins…”

        The sound of approaching footsteps grew louder, and soon a dozen figures appeared at the entrance of the alley, blocking Baldwin’s only escape route. Among them was a figure who had once evoked Baldwin’s tenderness, but now, only seething resentment remained, followed by an eruption of his long-suppressed murderous intent.

        In truth, Baldwin was aware, despite his desire to deny it, that an indescribable thrill surged within his heart every time he thrust the cursed blade into living flesh. It was the fleeting moment of unparalleled satisfaction—as if he held absolute control over the lives of others—that mesmerized him.

        For the past few days, he thought that a simple and contented life would fill the void within him. Yet, he was wrong—tranquility had never brought him happiness. Coming to the realization, without hesitation, he pulled out the cursed sword from the ground and drove its blade into the body of the woman who had once tugged at his heartstrings.

        With blood spattered across his face, he cracked a deranged grin, sending shivers down the spines of the humans and gods present. The momentary terror rendered them defenseless against Baldwin’s onslaught. They all fell victim to his blade, their lives extinguished, painting the ground with vibrant splashes of crimson.

        After catching his breath, Baldwin redonned his armor, hoisted the evil sword on his back, and left the town he once believed could be his resting place. He continued his journey of slaughter, even more frenzied and ruthless than before, leaving behind countless terrifying legends in the realm...

        “Now that I can never reclaim a pristine life, I shall sink into the depths of darkness, immersing myself in hatred and slaughter until they fester!”
STORY_2876:
In the middle of the night, a man ran through the dense forest, his footsteps frantic with fear. Unsurprisingly, he soon tripped over a rock and fell to the ground. In that fleeting moment, a massive black shadow leaped from behind and pinned the man down as he struggled to get back up.

        It was an agile wolf, appearing exceptionally robust under the moonlight. While its fur was stained with fresh blood accentuating its ferocity, its deep golden eyes fixated on the man beneath it, whose eyes widened in terror.

        “Please! Do-Don’t kill me!” the man pleaded in anguish, but the wolf remained unforgiving. It opened its jaws, ready to sink its teeth into the man’s neck, only to feel a sudden blast of scorching heat coming from afar. Instinctively, it leaped back, narrowly evading a torrent of pneuma-powered flames.

        “Who dares stop me?” the wolf growled with a deep, wrathful voice.

        “I am Dipankara, a disciple of the Abbey of Perfect Enlightenment,” a clear and youthful voice echoed through the silent forest as a young man walked toward the wolf. Undeterred by the wolf’s intimidation, the young man, Dipankara, gazed at the beast with his crystal-clear eyes and  a hint of youthful determination in his brows.

        “Ve-venerable Master!” The moment the man heard Dipankara’s name, he crawled toward the young man as if he had found a savior. Clutching onto Dipankara’s robes, he tearfully implored, “This demon wolf is a heinous murderer! It slaughtered everyone in our village. Please, Master, rid us of this monster!”

        “Hah! Yes, I did massacre the entire village but they had it coming! Boy, walk away now, or else I’ll kill you too!”

        ‘I knew demons are all born evil, with a natural inclination toward slaughter and violence. They shall not be spared!’ Dipankara thought. He had detected the scent of blood on the wolf’s fur right from the start, knowing that it had taken numerous lives. He hoped his words could turn the wolf away from its wicked path, yet its unrepentant nature extinguished his meager trace of compassion.

        “Since you persist in your sanguinary ways, you leave me no choice but to eradicate you for the world’s sake!” Dipankara formed intricate hand seals and chanted incantations, concentrating the essence of his pneuma-powered flames at his fingertips.

        “Humph! Bring it on!” The wolf let out an enraged howl and lunged toward Dipankara only to be blocked by an eruption of pneuma-powered flames. Yet, it remained undeterred as it rolled on the ground to put out the flames that licked its furs, and launched another attack.

        The battle continued, each exchanging blows, and neither gaining the upper hand. The standoff persisted until the moment the man attempted to flee.

        “Not a chance!” The demon wolf’s eyes, now bloodshot from the fierce battle, bulged with fury. Despite Dipankara’s blast of flames, it raced toward the man, enduring the scorching burns while baring its fangs to sink into the depth of the man’s flesh.

        ‘At last… I have avenged you all, my children…’ Tears of grief streamed down the wolf’s crimson eyes. Upon the completion of the wolf’s revenge, losing the reason to fight with Dipankara, it fled toward the peak of the mountain with its heavily wounded body, its bloodstained countenance revealed a hint of desperate longing.

        However, Dipankara was unaware of the wolf’s intent. Infuriated by his inability to prevent the wolf’s bloodshed, he muttered in a low voice, “Demon! I shall ensure your demise!”

        Soon after Dipankara formed hand seals to muster his powers, the wind gathered around his feet, propelling him through the clouds, chasing after the wolf until they reached a cave in the mountain.

        Inside the cave, the injured demon wolf could no longer support its own body. It crawled on the ground, painstakingly gathering several desiccated bodies of young wolves into its embrace. Each of the young wolves had a concave chest with visible knife wounds on their bodies, which indicated that someone had cut open their chests and extracted their hearts.

        It was then that Dipankara came to the realization of the reason behind the wolf’s massacre. Standing at the cave entrance, he gazed upon the barely breathing wolf. A profound sorrow welled up within him as he softly inquired, “So, you annihilate the village for revenge…”

        “Ha… Yes, those ignorant humans believed that consuming the heart of a demon wolf would grant them immortality. But those cowards didn’t dare to fight me, so they waited for me to leave the cave in search of food. Then they sneaked in and cut open the hearts of my children…” The wolf suddenly grinned, revealing its sharp, bloodstained teeth as it continued, “So I went and cut theirs open, one by one!”.

        “...Two wrongs don’t make one right. Only by letting go can we find solace and end the cycle of hatred.”

        “I don’t need solace, nor redemption. I only need a swift end…” The demon wolf lifted its head, an eerie light flashing across its dying eyes fixated on Dipankara. “So, monk, why don’t you join us?”

        “You—” It was until then that Dipankara realized that while the wolf was speaking to him, it had crushed the demon core within its body. A sudden wave of tremendous power erupted, bearing down on the defenseless Dipankara. Just as he was on the verge of death, someone arrived, scooping him up and swiftly carrying him away from the cave.
 
        Boom!

        A deafening explosion reverberated through the forest as the cave collapsed, crushing the ground around.

        The two miraculously escaped unscathed, finding solid footing in a safe spot. After steadying himself, Dipankara looked at the old man beside him, his voice filled with confusion. “Master, what…brings you here?”

        “I divined that you were in danger, so I hurried here,” said the Enlightened Master, placing his hands on Dipankara’s shoulders. After ensuring that Dipankara was unharmed, he gave him a faint smile and continued, “Fortunately, I came just in time.”

        “...Master, I don’t understand,” Dipankara asked while gazing at the collapsed cave. “Who was wrong between the mother wolf and the villagers? The wolf did kill a hundred people but she did it because the villagers had taken the hearts of her young children…”

        “Dipankara, don’t get too involved,” the Enlightened Master spoke with profound wisdom, “We meet and we part, it is merely a part of life; karma will take its course, and we, as ascetics, shall observe and seek insights. Never get too attached or you’ll lose yourself.”

        “I still don’t understand…”

        “Don’t worry,” the Enlightened Master comforted Dipankara with a gentle pat on his shoulder, “Time will lead you to the path of truth.”

        With a mind full of doubts, Dipankara returned to the Abbey of Perfect Enlightenment alongside his master. It was not until the wars of the gods’ investiture broke out, after witnessing scenes of chaos and conflict, that Dipankara finally grasped the meaning behind his master’s words...
STORY_2877:
In the courtyard of a certain villa, the feline duo, Plumpy and Fist, engaged in a fierce combat, while Mellow, another petite feline, sat on a raised chair nearby, watching them.

        The three cats were all thieves under the great bandit named Ali Baba. Some days ago, their leader, Ali Baba, was abducted by his dreaded admirer, Blodgett. To rescue Ali Baba, Mellow and the other cat thieves infiltrated the mansion where Ali Baba was imprisoned. They encountered numerous dangers along the way and came perilously close to failure.

        To prevent such mishaps from happening again, Mellow requested that Ali Baba provide specialized training for each member of the gang. Ali Baba readily agreed and lifted the restrictions on the cats. He even created a headquarters in the city center for Mellow to train the gang.

        As the frontline fighters of the gang, Plumpy and Fist were having their training session—a one-hour intensive combat session that Mellow had arranged for them to enhance their reflexes and endurance.

        “Five minutes left,” Mellow announced.

        “Thank goodness! It’s finally coming to an end. I’m exhausted,” Plumpy exclaimed with excitement.  Her lethargic kicks intensified as she was energized by the thought of the training session nearing its conclusion. Catching Fist off guard, her fierce kick unintentionally sent him flying across the courtyard. The latter ultimately crashed onto a round table on the other side, causing a loud commotion and knocking over a box placed on the table.

        The glass tube inside the box was propelled into the air, tracing a parabolic arc as it fell on Zero, who was about to enter the courtyard—

        Splash! The vial shattered upon impact, and the contents, a bright red liquid, splashed all over Zero, giving him a horrifying look.

        Taken aback by the consecutive accidents, Plumpy and Fist momentarily froze. Fortunately, the quick-witted Mellow hurried over to Zero. Lifting her head, she asked, “Are you okay?”

        Zero responded with his usual gentle smile, “I’m fine. It’s just a glass tube… Huh?”

        Mid-sentence, Zero noticed that his voice had become increasingly soft and high-pitched, resembling that of an innocent young boy. In addition to that, his gaze lowered gradually until it was level with Mellow’s gaze.

        Zero looked up to Plumpy and Fist, who had come to his side and appeared giant-like, and hesitantly said, “You guys… look huge.”

        “No! It’s you who has turned small!” Mellow anxiously corrected him.

        Zero extended his hands in confusion, looking at his dainty, adorable hands. The revelation was so stupefying that even someone as carefree as Zero was struck motionless until a warm sensation suddenly enveloped him. 

        “Awwww! Little Zero is so adorable!” Plumpy exclaimed as she picked up the tiny Zero, rubbing her face against his tender cheek passionately.

        “Plumpy! Stop it!” Mellow reached out her paws to pull Plumpy away but lacked the strength. Thankfully, Fist quickly stepped in and lifted Plumpy from behind, freeing Zero from her clutches. As Zero recovered from the shock, he said, “It must be the potion in that glass tube—it has turned me small.”

        “Well, such a peculiar potion must be a creation of  Merbromin…” Mellow explained while observing Zero, her face contorting as if she was experiencing some kind of inner struggle. Eventually, unable to resist the urge, she gently stroked Zero’s hair and made a few extra strokes due to its temptingly soft texture.

        Zero was surprised but he quickly regained composure. Wearing a forgiving smile, he softly said, “If you want to touch my hair, just go ahead. I don’t mind.”

        “Cough. No, no need for that,” Mellow averted her face to conceal her embarrassment, then she continued, “Now we know Merbromin made the potion, let’s hurry and find her.”

        “But Merbromin isn’t here. She went to the city center to find some ingredients early in the morning,” Plumpy interjected as she had also calmed herself.

“We don’t know if that potion has any side effects, so let’s go to the city center and find her as soon as possible. Plumpy, Fist, you’re both coming too,” said Mellow.

        However, as soon as the group arrived at the city center, Plumpy was distracted by the delicacies on the street and forgot their original purpose. She dashed into the crowd, and Fist followed suit to retrieve her. Meanwhile, Mellow and Zero, who were left behind, completely lost sight of their pals. Unable to push through the bustling crowd due to their diminutive physiques, the two could only huddle together on the side, anxiously waiting for their companions.

        “Plumpy that idiot! We shouldn’t have brought her along!” Mellow stomped her foot in frustration. Zero gently patted her shoulder to comfort her, “There’s no need to be angry. We’re not in a rush. Everything is going to be fine as long as we’re patient.”

        Unfortunately, their patience only brought a sleazy-looking man to them. The man cast a malicious gaze up and down at Mellow and then smirked, saying, “Oh my, look what adorable little kids we have here. What are you doing in such a boring place? Here, let me take you to somewhere fun.”

        “Tut!” Mellow could not help but roll her eyes. With crossed arms, she scolded the man dismissively, “Get lost! Stay away from us, you disgusting creep!”

        “You little brat! I was going to treat you gently, but your attitude has changed my mind!” The man angrily lunged at Mellow, but Zero stepped in front of her, swiftly delivering a sweeping kick that sent the man flying far away.

        “No one can hurt my pal!” Zero’s calm demeanor transformed into a blazing fury, ignited by his determination to protect his friend.

        Watching Zero, who remained sturdy and trustworthy despite his shrunk body, shielding her from harm, Mellow was deeply moved. Her eyes shimmered slightly, filled with warmth.

        ‘No matter how his appearance changes, Zero is always Zero, the unwavering man who would do anything to protect his pals.’

        Thanks to the commotion, Plumpy and Fist eventually found Mellow and Zero.

        Afterward, Fist and Plumpy—who overcame the temptation of food—took Mellow and Zero to Merbromin. As Merbromin helped to undo the potion effect with her profound knowledge, Zero regained his normal body, finally putting a happy end to the unexpected incident.
STORY_2878:
In a forsaken town, where the moonless night stretched to the horizon, casting an eerie darkness that intensified the unsettling silence, dilapidated buildings stood like invisible beasts warning any intruders to stay away from this forgotten land.

        Still, someone ventured into the treacherous heart of the abandoned town regardless of the ominous ambiance—a couple, holding hands, strolled through the town’s entrance.

        The young man with emerald hair wore a vibrant yellow tailcoat meticulously coordinated with a pristine bowtie and a boutonniere, which stood out vividly in the dark like a radiant sun. The woman by his side, on the other hand, wore a rather understated attire—a midnight blue evening gown adorned with subtle golden embroidery that exuded an air of refined elegance.

        Their lavish attire seemingly suggested they were heading to the most extravagant party rather than to the depths of a desolate town.

        “Jack, why did you bring me here?” Elizabeth, the woman, asked, her voice filled with curiosity.

        “Today is the anniversary of our first date, so I have prepared a surprise for you,” Jack replied, lifting Elizabeth’s hand to gently place a kiss on her knuckles. 

        “Well, you know the consequences if you fail to surprise me,” Elizabeth teased, flashing a sweet smile at Jack as she playfully grazed his chin, leaving a trace of blood.

        Instead of showing any sign of anger, Jack caressed the bloodstain with a mesmerized expression as he whispered, “You can do anything you want to me.”

        The young man, Jack, was not only a detective but also an artist with a morbid fascination for death. The woman, Elizabeth, was a noble who attained eternal youth through the fresh blood of young maidens.

        In the past, Jack had been commissioned by some villagers to find the missing girls in the village. It was during the investigation that he encountered Elizabeth, the culprit, and fell deeply in love with her at first sight. The two’s passionate romance blossomed swiftly, but the intense emotions flooded Elizabeth with worries, followed by a clash of values. In a moment of turmoil, Elizabeth accidentally took Jack’s life.

        After numerous hardships, Jack managed to resurrect and leave the underworld. It was after a long and winding journey that he finally regained his memories of Elizabeth. He returned to her side and shared a sweet and happy life ever since.

        And today, like any other of their sweet and happy days, Jack led Elizabeth into the forsaken town. They walked through narrow alleyways, one after another, until they reached a dilapidated estate where the remnants of the building still hinted at its past grandeur.

        “We’re almost there,” Jack said, gracefully bending down at the foot of a staircase, offering his hand for Elizabeth to hold as they descended. They passed through a half-blocked doorway before arriving at a vast garden.

        Despite the absence of a gardener, the garden thrived, bursting with vibrant colors as flowers bloomed in a riotous display. Their hues contrasted beautifully with the twinkling stars in the boundless night sky, captivating the beholders’ eyes.

        Unfortunately, the picturesque scene was marred by a lifeless body lying at the heart of the blossoms.

        “So…is this part of your surprise as well?” Elizabeth asked.

        “No, it is not,”  Jack replied, his face immediately darkened as he approached the lifeless form for closer inspection.

        It was the body of a boy,  approximately seven or eight years old. His limbs were twisted at unnatural angles and his skin was covered in horrifying bruises, all evident that he had suffered brutal torture before meeting his untimely demise.

        ‘What a grotesque scene of death. The perpetrator must be incurably repugnant…’ Jack’s mood further darkened at the sight of such an inelegant death.

        “The body is still warm, which indicates that the boy died recently. The murderer must still be around,” Jack concluded

        “Are you going to bring him out?” Elizabeth asked.

        “Of course,” Jack replied with a rarely cold and menacing look as he continued, “He ruined my surprise for you with such an unpleasant body. That’s unforgivable!”

        “Don’t be angry, my dear.” As captivating as the look of rage on Jack’s face, Elizabeth could not bear to see him upset, so she gently put her arms around his neck from behind and whispered to his ear softly, “Let me help you.”

        As Elizabeth tapped into her powers, blood burst forth from her body, spreading and solidifying as it converged in one direction. Within moments, the blood returned with a ragged middle-aged man hung at its end that had transformed into a crimson hook.

        “Wh-what do you want? Le-let go of me!” The man struggled and roared desperately.

        “Give you the punishment you deserve, of course,”  Jack said, stepping forward and placing a small knife against the man’s throat, “You’ve ruined our surprise date and the audacity you showed me that repulsive sight.” A disarming and devilish smile curled upon his lips as he pressed his hand downward—

        “ARGHHHH!” A piercing scream echoed throughout the abandoned estate. It was a shrill and resonant cry but it quickly died away, turning into feeble groans, and eventually, subsided into silence.

        “Phew. Another masterpiece,”  Jack said, looking at his art with excitement. He turned to face Elizabeth, awaiting her evaluation.

        “It’s fantastic. I knew my Jack is the most remarkable man in this world,” Elizabeth expectedly praised her beloved without hesitation. Just as she was about to hold him in an embrace, Jack suddenly restrained his excitement. Giving Elizabeth a knowing glance, he whispered, “I hear something.”

        Elizabeth immediately hushed, her ears attuning to the faint sound of suppressed weeping coming from the upper floors of the manor. Exchanging a glance, they ventured into the crumbling manor and cautiously walked up the precarious spiral staircase. Finally, they reached a room at the end of the corridor on the second floor, where the sorrowful cries grew closer.

        Jack pushed open the wobbly door only to find several children bound by ropes. The children recoiled in fear, seeking refuge in the corner of the room the moment they saw Jack.

        “Don’t be afraid. It’s all over now,” Jack spoke in a gentle tone to soothe the children. His demeanor was unexpectedly tender, leaving Elizabeth momentarily stunned.

        Afterward, Jack and Elizabeth escorted the children back to the police station in the nearby town.  By the time everything was settled, dawn had already broken. Holding Elizabeth’s hands, Jack spoke, his handsome face filled with profound remorse, “I’m sorry, Elizabeth. I’m sorry for letting my surprise for you turn into a fright instead.”

        “It’s alright,” Elizabeth shook her head, hesitating for a moment before asking the question she had harbored, “Jack, do you…do you want children?”

        Jack appeared surprised. “Why ask?”

        “I noticed how you became infuriated at the sight of the boy’s corpse, and how gentle you were with the children. Besides, you’re always with Ed, so I know you like children and enjoy being around them. But my body is incapable of bearing a child… ” Elizabeth struggled before finally mustering her courage and continued, “If having children is what you dream of, you can go—”

        Before Elizabeth could finish her sentence, Jack placed a finger over her lips. Gazing deeply into her eyes, he spoke with tenderness and affection, “I don’t need children. I don’t need anything that might divert your love away from me. Elizabeth, all I need is for you to love, solely me, until eternity.”

        “Jack…” Elizabeth gave a soft chuckle, wrapping her arms around Jack’s waist. She murmured blissfully, “You’re right. I was in my own head. We don’t need anyone else. We just let our love burn like the most fervent flame until the very end of the world.”
STORY_2879:
In the bitter cold tundra, where snow fell endlessly with howling wind, there was only one igloo with a gentle radiance seeping through the walls of ice. Inside the igloo, a girl lay on a bed made of stones, her face plastered with a sickly green pallor.

        By the girl’s side was a young boy who gently wiped her face with a towel dampened with hot water. His movements were delicate and tender as if tending to the most precious treasure.

        The boy was a Druid named Dodo. Long ago, his tribe was annihilated by the demons but a Penguin Druid saved him, making him the only survivor of his kind. Since then, he lived with the Druid and penguins, holding a deep resentment toward the demons who had slaughtered his tribe. Ironically, fate led him to save a girl who turned out to be one of them.

        Dodo called the girl—who had lost her memory—Sasa, and he took her back to his teacher so she could be treated. However, Sasa ran away after Dodo mistakenly believed she hurt one of the penguins and attacked her. Later, Dodo learned of his mistake and decided to bring Sasa back. It was after much hardship that he finally found the unconscious girl and took her back to his teacher.

        Still, the series of incidents and injuries left Sasa’s body in a feeble state, and it filled Dodo with guilt. Therefore, Dodo volunteered to take care of Sasa while his teacher was away searching for herbs.

        Perhaps sensing Dodo’s tender care, Sasa gradually awakened from the coma. As her long, thick lashes fluttered slightly, Dodo exclaimed with excitement, “Sasa!”

        “Hmm… Where am I… Ah!”  Sasa opened her eyes, bewildered as she surveyed her surroundings. When she caught sight of Dodo, her entire body immediately tensed up. She crawled to a corner of the room despite her frail boy, fixing a wary gaze on the boy.

        “You… I…” Sasa’s distrustful gaze brought Dodo a profound sense of shame and distress. Not knowing what to say, he instinctively approached her only to intensify her hostility, prompting her to arch her back and glare at him.

        “St-stay away from me! Go away!” Sasa shouted in fear. She even grabbed something nearby and hurled it toward him, trying to drive him away.

        “I… Ouch!” Although Dodo tried to explain, his words were disrupted by the object that hit him. The room descended into chaos for a moment until the Penguin Druid came.

        “Dodo! Out of the igloo now!” The Penguin Druid grabbed Dodo’s shoulder and pushed him toward the igloo’s entrance.

        “But…”

        “You’ll only agitate her by staying here. Both of you need a moment to calm down.”

        “I… Okay.” Following the Penguin Druid’s advice, Dodo left the igloo. Right before he stepped out of the room, he saw the Penguin Druid gently draw Sasa in her arms to comfort her. He heard her crying inconsolably, which filled his heart with inexplicable emotions.

        ‘I jumped to the conclusion too quickly and misjudged her. I hurt her when she didn’t do anything wrong.’ After a moment of hesitation and inner struggle, Dodo decided to wait outside the igloo. He stayed in the snow for the entire night until the first light of dawn jolted him awake.

        Dodo rubbed his eyes. Just as he was about to head to the river to wash his face, he caught a glimpse of a petite figure walking out of the igloo.

        ‘It’s Sasa!’ Dodo recognized the girl at a glance. Worried that she might hurt herself again, he stealthily followed her and noticed that she was heading toward the river, looking for water to freshen up. However, unfamiliar with the tundra, she accidentally stepped onto an unsafe thin ice.

        As expected, the ice soon broke beneath Sasa’s feet. Just as she was about to fall into the icy river, someone hurried over and caught her. He then leaped onto a safe patch of thick ice before he released his grip on her hand.

        “Are you alright?” Dodo asked, his face filled with concern.

        “...Yes. Thank you.” Despite the terrifying experience with Dodo, Sasa could sense his genuine care at that moment, so she slightly lowered her guard, feeling less hostile than she had been the day before.

        “No-no need to thank me.” Meanwhile, Dodo, who detected Sasa’s softened stance, quickly took the chance to apologize, “I-I misunderstood you earlier. I thought you were hurting the penguin, but you were actually trying to protect him from the seals… It was all my fault. I wrongly accused you, and I’m sorry! Could you forgive me?”

        “...No,” Sasa softly refused after a brief moment of silence.

        ‘Right, it’s only natural. Of course, she wouldn’t forgive me that easily after what I did to her.’ A wry smile tugged at the corner of Dodo’s mouth as he turned around to walk away. However, two hands grabbed the hem of his clothes and stopped him. He lowered his head and saw Sasa’s sparklingly innocent eyes.

        “Unless you take me to see the penguins, then I’ll forgive you.” Sasa shyly smiled.

        “...Of course, I can do that.” It was only then that Dodo felt a great sense of relief, and he responded with a radiant smile.

        “Let’s go see them now!” Sasa eagerly held Dodo’s hand and ran toward the penguins. Meanwhile, the Penguin Druid, already awake, stood by the igloo, watching the two with a warm and doting gaze...
STORY_2881:
At the gate to the realm of gods, the Court of Ophiuchus defeated Pontos with the help of his companions, Mitty and Marble, the Court of Canis Major and Minor. As Pontos fell to the ground, unconscious, memories from the past flooded back and churned within his chaotic mind, forcing him to relive his past once again…

        Following Khaos’ guidance, the gods arrived on the continent of Tarones and began extracting the power of elements to create a new realm for their kind. After spending several years on the continent, Pontos was summoned back to the realm of gods to join the others in constructing their home. 

        As the master of water elements, Pontos was duly tasked with creating rivers, lakes, and oceans in the new realm. Occasionally, he would also supervise the military and train with them. One day, a sergeant walked up to Pontos with some documents to brief him on the upcoming tasks after the training.

        “Lord Pontos, we need you to create five lakes and ten rivers in the north today,” the sergeant reported nervously, fearing that he would provoke the temperamental Pontos.

        “Tut! More lakes and rivers…” Pontos’ expression turned grim, clicking his tongue in annoyance. With a furrowed brow, he asked, “What comes after that? What else do I have to do?”

        “Well…” The sergeant frantically flipped through the documents and said, “After that, you need to create three rivers and two lakes in the east. Then, you’ll move to the south where we need two waterfalls and one ocean. And finally, eight lakes in the west…”

        “Enough!” Irritation continued to rise in Pontos as he listened. Eventually, he cut short the sergeant’s report. Startled, the sergeant immediately shut his mouth and rigidly stood at attention.


        ‘Create a lake, create a waterfall, create a river… It’s always about water, water, WATER! How boring! The human realm is much more interesting than that. Why do I have to stay here and do these tedious tasks while Zeus that bastard can do whatever he wants in the human realm? That’s enough! I’m going to the human realm today, no matter what!’

        “I’m not doing it today!” The line of Pontos’ thought only provoked resentment within him, so he followed his heart and refused the tasks.

        “Bu-but what if Lord Khaos asks about the progress?!”

        “Just make up some excuses. Anyway, I’m going to the human realm now!” Turning a deaf ear to the sergeant’s urge, Pontos turned around and headed straight for the gate after leaving those words. However, someone intercepted him as he was transported to the lower part of the realm of gods.

        “Lord Pontos, it is Lord Khaos’ order that you’re not allowed to go to the human realm,” said Zeus, the King of Gods, taking a bow. Yet, contrary to his seemingly respectful demeanor, his eyes and tone revealed his arrogance and disdain for Pontos, which only further fueled Pontos’ indignation.

        “I’m going and you can do nothing to stop me!”

        “In that case, please forgive my impudence,” Zeus spoke humbly, but his actions carried a murderous intent as a bolt of lightning materialized in his hand, aiming for Pontos with a menacing momentum—

        Boom!

        A deafening explosion shook the realm, turning everything white momentarily with a blinding light. But soon it faded away, revealing Pontos still standing on the ground despite being struck by the lightning. Some parts of his skin had been scorched, emitting thin wisps of white smoke, and there was nothing more.

        “Tut! Your thunderbolt indeed hurts, but it’s no different than a mosquito bite to me,”  Pontos grinned arrogantly while stretching his muscles. “Now it’s my turn!”

        Pontos’ gaze sharpened as he summoned water elements which swiftly coalesced into multiple water spheres. At his command, all the spheres surged toward Zeus at a fierce speed. However, a mysterious wall made of purple pneuma suddenly appeared before Zeus, blocking all the spheres and melting them one by one.

        “This is…chaotic power!” Pontos quickly recognized the true nature of the purple pneuma. Glaring at Zeus, who held a purple sphere in his hands, Pontos questioned through his clenched teeth, “Why do you possess Khaos’ power?!”

        “It was bestowed upon me by Lord Khaos, of course, to prevent someone as stubborn and ignorant as you from causing trouble. I suggest you go back now before it’s too late.”

        “Humph! No! Why should I listen to the words of a coward who basks in reflected glory?”

        “Such a fool,” Zeus shook his head resignedly while gathering the chaotic power within his palm. In an instant, the purple pneuma transformed into numerous tentacles that forcefully captured Pontos by his limbs and torso.

        “Let go of me!” Pontos attempted to muster his powers, struggling to break free. Yet, the tentacles dissolved and absorbed his strength, turning his resistance futile.

        “Stop wasting your powers. Lord Khaos’ power is not something you can withstand—”

        “Shut your mouth!” Pontos roared furiously. His rebellious nature refused to submit even in the face of Khaos’ superior powers, let alone tolerate the insult from Zeus, whom he deemed as weak. Regardless of the risk of being consumed by the chaotic power, Pontos unleashed all the water elements he could muster, pouring out every ounce of his strength.

        “Arghhhhh!” Following Pontos’ hoarse cries was the sound of the breaking chaotic power. The tentacles, unable to withstand Pontos’ immense powers, shattered and disappeared with a loud bang. The power’s backlash sent Zeus flying to a distance. He fell onto the ground with blood oozing from the corner of his mouth as he murmured, “No… That’s impossible… How did you break free… Ah!”

        As soon as Pontos regained freedom, he commanded the water elements to form a torrent, capturing the fallen Zeus and lifting him high into the air. The table was turned in a fleeting second.

        “See. You have Khaos’ power, but so what? You still lost. Even if you had the world’s most extraordinary weapon, an incompetent like you could never utilize its full potential,” Pontos coldly asserted, raising his right hand and clenching it tightly. The water surged and tightened around Zeus, eliciting a shrill scream from him. 

        The sight of Zeus, who had been haughty, falling into a wretched state brought Pontos a sense of pleasure. With a malicious smile, he taunted, “What a melodious scream. Well, I shall generously forgive your impudence and grant you a swift death!”

        Just as Pontos was about to deliver the final blow, several beams of starlight descended from afar, accurately severing the torrent around Zeus, who gasped eagerly for air as he fell back to the ground.

        “Pontos, that’s too reckless of you,” said Aether, the trusted aide of Khaos, furrowing her brows as she looked at Pontos.

        “Hmph! He started it!”

        “Zeus was merely following Lord Khaos’ order. What are you doing here anyway? Shouldn’t you be creating the rivers in our new realm?”

        “Tut! It’s so boring doing the same thing every day. I just wanted to take a break in the human realm.”

        “A break?” Aether sneered. “What I see is a man looking for an excuse to slack off, Pontos. Now, be a good boy and go back to do what you’re supposed to do, or I will report your actions to Lord Khaos.”

        “You—” Pontos stared at Aether resentfully only to be subdued by her imposing aura.

        Pontos, who was well aware of Aether’s powers—which were far stronger than Zeus—and her favor with Khaos, knew he could not turn the tide solely with his strength the way he had done a moment ago.

        “Fine! I’ll go back and work on those rivers and lakes!” Pontos replied begrudgingly. Ignoring Aether’s reaction, he returned to continue his mundane tasks…
STORY_2882:
During the raging war between humans and the gods at the entrance to the realm of gods, Phanes, the God of Fire, threw himself into the fray. Eventually, he grew exhausted, leaning against a wall to seek respite. The elements enveloped his body and began to replay memories of the past in his mind…

        In the distant past, Khaos embarked on a cosmic odyssey in search of a new home for his people, and Phanes, blessed with exceptional talents, became a courtier of Khaos.

        Unfortunately, in his eagerness to please Khaos, Phanes entrusted a planet with potential to Khaos’ son, Erebus, to explore. However, Erebus subjectively deemed the planet unsuitable for habitation and returned only with the resources he depleted from it, disregarding the original purpose of the mission.

        Khaos, of course, was infuriated upon learning the failed mission. He not only punished Erebus but also also expressed deep disappointment in Phanes for instigating the ill-fated decision behind the scenes.

        To regain Khaos’ trust, Phanes devoted sleepless nights to patrolling and surveying the cosmos, tirelessly searching for potential planets with previous resources that would appease Khaos. After days of searching, he finally found one.

        ‘This planet is marvelous! Though it may not be suitable for us to live, the celestial remnants that form it give birth to everlasting sparks of life, which can give us boundless energy! Lord Khaos will surely be pleased to know this!’

        Phanes’ eyes lit up with excitement as he gazed at the planet engulfed in blazing flames before him. Unable to contain his anticipation, he eagerly approached the planet and landed on its hardened surface, only to feel a powerful tremor that shook the ground.

        Initially, Phanes assumed it was a routine seismic activity of the planet. But as the tremors intensified and he sensed the surface shifting, he realized something was amiss so he swiftly leaped into the air. Yet, a dark figure came charging at him at a ferocious speed, giving Phanes little time to react that he only managed to raise his arms in defense. He felt a numbing sensation in both his arms as his body was forcefully pushed back.

        It was after his body stabilized that he could see the assailants—two enormous rock creatures standing menacingly on the planet’s surface, glaring at Phanes with their mouths slightly agape. Then, they spewed forth flames capable of scorching all creation.

        ‘They must be the indigenous creatures of this planet, born from the fiery essence contained within the celestial remnants,’ Phanes thought. “Judging by their attack just now, they possess formidable strength and heat resistance. They are worthy adversaries indeed.’

        Phanes’ brain began to spin, speedily processing the information, but the rock creatures seemed unwilling to let him contemplate. Soon after they drew in the flames around them, they swiftly conjured two massive fire balls before their mouths and took aim at him.

        A searing wave of heat surged toward Phanes, evaporating the moisture on his skin and leaving a parched sensation. Yet, in the face of such terrifying heat, Phanes did not falter. Instead, he met it with confidence, extending his hands to catch the blazing fireballs.

        “I fear no flame, no matter how strong it is, for I am the mightiest God of Fire!” Phanes exclaimed. Harnessing the power within him, he transformed into another manifestation of flames, enveloping the incoming fireballs. At first, the two flames engaged in a struggle, none of them willing to yield. However, the radiance of the fireballs gradually dimmed as Phanes’ flames consumed it entirely.

        “Phew, the fire on this planet is truly remarkable. It refuses to accept defeat and seeks an opportunity to retaliate even after assimilation,” Phanes chuckled confidently. “But it has no hope to win! Now it’s my turn!”

        With a wave of Phanes’ hands, the two fireballs split into an array of countless small fire bullets before him. As he closed his fingers into a fist, the fiery projectiles shot forth like rain, targeting the joints and weak spots of the rock creatures, causing intense explosions.

        The series of explosions shattered the two rock creatures from within, turning their once indomitable forms into pieces and putting an end to their lives completely.

        “All right, now that the enemies have been vanquished, it’s time to get what I need.”

        Phanes landed on the planet once again. Without interference from the rock creatures, he successfully harvested all the energy of the planet and compressed it into a single red ore before returning to the realm of gods. Despite his weariness from the battle, he did not rest but went directly to see Khaos.

        “Phanes, what is it?” Khaos seemed less than pleased, his gaze filled with impatience as he looked at Phanes.

        “Lord Khaos, I have discovered an intriguing planet. It possesses an everlasting flame, and I have extracted its power for you.” Phanes respectfully presented the red ore to Khaos, hoping for praise and recognition.

        Unfortunately, Khaos’ reaction was far from what Phanes had anticipated.

        “I have already assigned Aether the task of planetary exploration. You can just give it to her,” Khaos said, showing no surprise at Phanes’ discovery and instead knitting his brow as if annoyed.

        “But the power is—”

        “That’s enough, Phanes. I need to focus on building the new realm of gods. I don’t have time for such trivialities. Just go find Aether, and don’t make me say it twice.”

        “...Yes, Lord Khaos.” Phanes felt a deep sense of discontentment, but he could only swallow his emotions facing Khaos’ scrutinizing gaze. Knowing that he had missed the opportunity to gain Khaos’ trust, he reluctantly handed over the hard-earned red ore to Aether…
STORY_2883:
As Gaia regained her power from the giant tree in the Divine Woodland, she accidentally delved into the tree’s memories and discovered that the gods had seized the elements in the continent of  Tarones, leading to numerous wars and disasters that befell the humans.

        Overwhelmed with guilt, she decided to help the humans and the land by sabotaging the gods’ device used to extract the elements. However, her actions were discovered by Aether.

        A dispute erupted between the two goddesses. Gaia found herself no match for Aether, who was backed by Khaos, and was inevitably wounded. Fortunately, she managed to make her escape in a flock of running animals.

        “Da-darn it! What are these vines made of? Why are they getting tighter?” During Gaia’s escape, she heard a loud cry from a girl somewhere in the forest. She could tell the girl’s spirited personality just from the tone as the girl shouted, “ Ugh! Help! Can somebody help me?”

        ‘...Let’s go and take a look.’ Sitting atop a floral deer, Gaia raised her head and motioned the deer with a gentle pat. The deer swiftly turned its heels and ran toward the direction of the girl’s cries.

        In no time, they came across a girl who was tightly entangled by some vines in mid-air. The comical sight left Gaia so dumbfounded that she could not help but think, ‘What on earth did she do to get herself stuck like this?’

        “Oh, oh, oh! You, beautiful lady over there! I’m so glad you’re here! Could you please help me?” The girl called out to Gaia eagerly. However, instead of helping the girl right away, Gaia observed her cautiously. With her voice tinged with wariness, she asked, “How did you end up stuck in the vines?”

        “Well… I…” The girl stammered, seemingly reluctant to tell the truth, which made Gaia even more alert. Her tone grew colder as she asked, “I’m afraid I can’t help you if you’re not willing to tell me the truth.”

        “Umm… Okay! Fine! I’ll tell you!” The girl closed her eyes and sheepishly confessed, “It’s all because I was feeling peckish. The fruits on this tree looked so tempting that I climbed up to pick them, but I slipped and fell into this pile of vines!”

        Coincidentally, the girl’s stomach growled as if to prove her point, bringing a scarlet flush to her face. As embarrassing as it was, her candid reaction earned Gaia’s favor, prompting her to let her guard down.

        As Gaia gently put her hand on the deer’s body, the deer gracefully leaped to the front of the tree so that Gaia could press her hands against the trunk and channel her power. Sensing her will, the tree loosened the vines and freed the girl who began stretching her tingling limbs after she landed on the ground safely.

        “Thank you for helping me,” said the girl with a bright smile. She seemed to have an infectiously ceaseless positive energy that even inspired Gaia, who was feeling low at the moment.

        However, the joyful atmosphere was abruptly interrupted by a scream.

        ‘The animals are in distress! Someone is attacking the forest! I have to protect them!’ Gaia’s expression changed. She quickly mounted the deer and left, paying no attention to the girl.

        The deer carried Gaia to the entrance of the forest. Yet, the once flourishing forest was now littered with the corpses of animals, and the earth was stained with crimson. The gruesome scene ignited a fiery anger with Gaia, turning her eyes red. Her gaze was coldly directed on the marauding hordes of demons responsible for such devastation.

        “No one shall harm the animals and this land!” Gaia shouted, channeling her power to summon a ball of powerful green light. Numerous tree saplings emerged from the ground and attacked the rampaging demon troop. Meanwhile, soft vines sprouted between the branches, providing aid to the injured animals.

        However, the demons kept coming, and Gaia’s fatigue began to show since she had already depleted her power while destroying the extraction device, coupled with the injuries she had received during her fight with Aether. Seizing the opportunity, the demon army gathered and relentlessly poured through the breaches.

        Just as the demon army was about to break through into the forest, a dazzling flash of light appeared, forming a magical barrier that blocked their entry point. Standing not far from the barrier was the girl whom Gaia had saved earlier, holding a staff emanating a soft glow of magic. It was she who had conjured the barrier.

        However, the situation remained dire even with the girl’s help. Her face contorted as she quickly grew overwhelmed and shouted, “Whoa! There are too many of them! I can’t deal with them alone! Blond guy, come out and help me!”

        In response to her plea, a translucent figure materialized. It was a young nobleman dressed in aristocratic attire with shoulder-length blonde hair that seemed even more luxurious than the girl’s. His exquisite features were so refined that they transcended the boundaries of gender. Still, the resolute aura he exuded revealed his identity as a masculine male. He was Earl Nathaniel, one of the heroes in the past. His soul had been long fused into the elements, yet a soul that represented the origin awakened him and tasked him with guiding the girl to the place of destiny.

        Giving the girl a resigned look, Nathaniel crossed his arms and said, “I’m afraid I can’t be of much help. There are too many demons.”

        “Then, then, what do we do? We can’t let them kill those adorable bunnies!”

        “...Didn’t you awaken your power?” Nathaniel sighed as he put a hand on his forehead.

        “Oh! Right!” Nathaniel’s question woke the girl. Revitalizing her spirit, she called out loudly, “Heroic spirits of the past, help me take down my enemies!”
