STORY_2925:
Under the pale light of a full moon, two opposing factions clashed fiercely within the dense forest. Blood rained as flesh was torn under the clashing swords and magical explosion, staining the lush green earth a deep crimson. Countless lives were lost in the brutal conflict, leaving only a lone knight and a sorcerer standing on the battlefield. Both were battered and bloodied, barely clinging to life, yet neither would yield.

        They were both nobles from a certain nation, each fueled by one objective: to claim the fabled magical oil lamp, no matter the cost.

        “Die!” With a final, desperate strike, the knight emerged victorious. He raised the gleaming golden lamp high above his head, his face alight with triumph. Yet, his celebration was cut short by a last-ditch spell from the dying sorcerer.

        The coveted lamp slipped from the knight’s trembling fingers. It tumbled to the side and rolled into a nearby river. Carried by the stream, it eventually came to rest on a shallow bank amidst a pile of debris where only the pale moonlight bore witness to its true form.

        ‘At last, it’s over…’ sighed Genie, the spirit bound to the lamp. For as long as he could remember, countless men had fought through bloodshed in pursuit of his wish-granting powers. The loss of lives had never brought him joy but only sorrow and despair, which was why even as he lay abandoned on the riverbank, possibly for centuries to come, he felt no fear or loneliness—only relief.

        ‘Now, no one will die because of me.’ Genie thought.

        However, his peace was short-lived.

        A young woman came sprinting along the river. Amidst her clumsy and unsteady steps, she failed to noticethe debris strewn across the ground and tripped, landing hard on her bottom. 

        “Ouch… That hurts… Huh?” She winced as her eyes caught a glimmer of gold. Out of curiosity, she brushed aside the trash and uncovered the shimmering lamp.

        “This looks like a very valuable lamp. What’s it doing in the garbage?” The woman, Ada, muttered, running her fingers over the lamp. There on the bottom, she found some strange markings. “These look like ancient symbols… Uh oh! I-I’m going to be late!”

        Ada, suddenly remembering her job as a university teaching assistant, hastily stuffed the lamp into her bag and dashed off to work, barely making it in time.

        The morning passed in a blur, and it was not until lunchtime that Ada finally had a moment to breathe. When she opened her bag to take out her meal, she spotted the lamp she had found earlier inside. Setting her lunch aside, she picked up the lamp for a closer look.

        “These symbols do look familiar,” Ada murmured, “I think I’ve seen them in one of those old manuscripts…” Unable to contain her curiosity, she took the lamp and dashed to the university library where she found a book on ancient inscriptions after digging through a dusty corner.

        “Hmm… ‘Only...one who reads my name... and dusts me… shall become my master’…” Ada read aloud, her face wrinkling in a thoughtful frown. “Does it mean I have to wipe it clean?”

        She took out her handkerchief and gently wiped the lamp while whispering the name engraved on it, “Genie?”

        Boom! White smoke billowed from the lamp’s spout, and a plump, golden figure emerged. Ada yelped in terror, dropping the lamp as she screamed, “Ahhh! A-a ghost!”

        “How rude! I am no ghost,” the figure declared indignantly, crossing his arms as he glared at the shaking woman, “I am Genie, the spirit of this wish-granting lamp.”

        “A wish-granting lamp?”

        “That’s right. I can grant you three wishes. Now, tell me, what is your heart’s desire?” asked Genie.

        “Umm…” Ada hesitated, her face twisting in thought. “I’ve never thought about this question before, and I… I can’t think of anything right now.”

        ‘That’s a first—I’ve never met someone who doesn’t know what to wish for,’ Genie thought, letting out a sigh. “Well, there’s no rush. Take your time. Just call me when you’ve made up your mind.”

        “Are you going back to the lamp?”

        “Yes. Is there something else you need?”

        “I’m going to have lunch. Would you like to join me?” Ada asked with a warm smile. Her kind invitation took Genie by surprise. Though he had met masters who treated him well, no one had ever regarded him so kindly as if he were just a normal friend.

        Unable to refuse Ada’s offer, Genie agreed. That first meal together marked the beginning of a bond that would deepen over time. One lunch turned into many, and soon Genie grew accustomed to living with Ada.

        Ada was the only child of her family. Having lost her parents at a young age, she became reserved and introverted. With few friends, she found pleasure and solace in books, and her academic excellence eventually led to her position as a university teaching assistant. Her simple and unassuming life left her with no burning desires, and as such, she never asked Genie to grant her a single wish.

        Years turned into decades, and Ada became an old and frail lady. Even so, she never once used the lamp’s power. On her deathbed, Genie stood by her side, his heart heavy with sorrow and confusion. “Why did you never make a wish?” he asked, “You know you could have simply asked me to restore your youth…”

        Ada shook her head and said, “Genie, immortality isn’t necessarily a gift. Life is only precious because it ends. The same goes for wishes. Magically granted wishes don’t bring people true joy; they can never be as fulfilling as achievements made through hard work.”

        “But I’m the wish-granting lamp—I’m supposed to make your wishes come true…”

        “You did, Genie,” Ada said with a serene smile. “You granted my greatest wish by staying by my side. You gave me companionship in a life that could have been unbearably lonely.”

        Genie remained by Ada’s side until her final breath. When she passed peacefully, the magic binding Genie to her broke. His form dissolved into mist, and he disappeared, destined to find his next master in another corner of the realm…
STORY_2926:
At the peak of a towering mountain, skeletal remains of ancient dragons rose above the horizon, piercing through the clouds. It was a majestic place also known as the home of the Runedragons.

        Inside one of the mountain caves a small crimson dragon lay sleeping soundly, her tail curling tightly around her body and bubbles forming from her nostrils. As dawn broke over the mountain, the warm golden sunlight streamed into the cave and jolted her awake.

        “Oh no! I overslept!” cried the crimson dragon, Hong Ai, as she opened her eyes. She quickly unfurled her wings and flew into the sky. Unfortunately, she was a step too late—the dense morning mist filled with elemental powers, the very sustenance of the Runedragons, had already cleared under the sun. She missed her breakfast.

        “How… how could this happen…” Hong Ai muttered, clutching her empty stomach. Her head dropped in disappointment as she hovered in the air.

        To her dismay, two Runedragon flew past her, their conversation stinging her like a slap in the face. One of them, patting their full stomach, turned to the other and said, “Thank goodness you woke me up in time. I almost overslept and missed breakfast again.”

        “Well, what do you expect? I’m your Souliade—it’s my duty to take care of you,” the other replied.

        The Runedragons were born in pairs. Each dragon had their own Souliade, a destined partner who would protect them and share an eternal bond, except for Hong Ai—she was born alone, without a Souliade.

        “And you can count on me when you’re in danger!” the first dragon said cheerfully.

        “Ha, that’s reassuring.” the other replied. The two’s voices faded into the distance as they flew away. Whether intentionally or not, one of them even patted their full belly again, which made Hong Ai seethe with jealousy and frustration, feelings that she was too proud to admit.

        “Missing a meal isn’t so bad. I’ve put on some weight recently anyway—it’s just the diet I need,” Hong Ai muttered with a bitter sniff. Rubbing her reddened eyes, she swallowed her hunger and descended to the open fields below where pairs of young Runedragons gathered.

        Each stood with their Souliade side by side, waiting for their instructor to arrive. They all gave Hong Ai a sympathetic look when they saw her arriving alone, their gazes making her chest tighten. Still, she raised her head high, puffed out her chest, and deliberately landed in the most conspicuous spot, attempting to hide her wounded pride behind a tough façade.

        Moments later, the instructor, an elder Runedragon, arrived. After transforming into a tall, regal woman, she began teaching the young Runedragons various theories and knowledge, but Hong Ai quickly grew bored, her head nodding as she struggled to stay awake.

        “That concludes today’s theory lesson,” the instructor said. “Now, we’ll move on to flight training. Each pair will work together to overcome obstacles and complete a circuit around the peak” She paused when her eyes landed on the lone Hong Ai among all the other paired students. Her heart softened as she recognized the special student who was born without a Souliade, and gently she said to Hong Ai, “This training is rather challenging. Attempting it alone could be dangerous, so you don’t have to participate—”

        “No!” Hong Ai interjected loudly, “I’ll do it! I can complete the training on my own!”

        “But—” The instructor hesitated, but she relented after seeing the determination in Hong Ai’s eyes. “Very well. But please, be careful.”

        “I’ll be fine!” Hong Ai declared boldly before flapping her wings and flying to the training venue alongside her peers.

        At first, the flight went smoothly. Hong Ai’s competitive spirit flared as she surged ahead, overtaking her peers until an accident occurred—a jagged rock on the cliffside suddenly broke and fell straight toward her.

        Normally, Hong Ai would have been able to dodge the falling rock with ease. However, she failed to do so as a wave of dizziness washed over her and sapped her strength.

        ‘Dang it…’ she thought bitterly. ‘It’s all because I missed breakfast this morning… Am I going to die like this… If only I had a Souliade by my side…’

        Just as Hong Ai was about to resign herself to her fate of being crushed by a falling rock, a shadow streaked through the air. A dragon dove in at lightning speed, narrowly knocking Hong Ai out of harm’s way just in time. After he took her back to the ground, he transformed into a handsome young man. His name was Qing Gui, the current leader of the Runedragons.

        His sharp and dark brows furrowed as he glared at Hong Ai, his voice cold and stern. “What were you thinking of attempting the flight training alone when you were clearly not feeling well?”

        “I… I… I…” Hong Ai stammered under his piercing gaze. The weight of frustration that she had suppressed for so long finally broke through. She burst into tears and began to wail loudly, “I just… I didn’t want to be looked down on… Even if I’m born without a Souliade… I don’t need anyone’s pity… Waaaaah!”

        Qing Gui’s anger quickly turned to sympathy when he heard Hong Ai’s hysterical sobbing. Rubbing his forehead, he let out a long sigh and said, “We are all your family. Everyone Runedragon here is willing to help you even if you don’t have your own Souliade. All you need to do is tell us your struggles.”

        “R-Really?” Hong Ai blinked her teary eyes and asked innocently, “Then… will you partner with me for the flight training?”

        “Sure,” Qing Gui replied as his form shifted back into a dragon. He spread his wings and rose into the air. He then turned back to Hong Ai and called, “Come, let’s fly together.”

        “Okay!” Hong Ai quickly forgot her frustration and eagerly followed Qing Gui. Under his guidance, she completed the flight training with ease. Impressed by her optimism and resilience, her fellow classmates gathered around her, cheering and offering their support, and that was the first time she realized the true meaning and warmth of companionship.

        Though Hong Ai came to understand that she was not alone, a small part of her heart still yearned for a Souliade. Little did she know that she would get her wish shortly afterward…
STORY_2927:
A massive nine-tailed fox hurtled through the forest, its figure flitting like a phantom as it raced toward the Heavenly Kingdom with a large water pouch, filled with water it had collected from Mount Buzhou, clutched in its jaws.

        The fox was named Daji, a vixen awakened by elemental forces. In the past, her greed had led her astray. She had been lost on the path of power and atrocity, breaking laws until she met Jiang Ziya, a Xian who showed her the way to redemption. She followed him to the Heavenly Kingdom to begin her path of spiritual refinement. However, her bestial nature had yet to be fully tamed, and her old habits still lingered—as they did now…

        Upon returning to her residence in the Heavenly Kingdom, Daji shifted into her human form. She carried the water pouch, intending to water the peach tree she had carefully nurtured in front of her house, where she unexpectedly saw a young elf audaciously snapping off one of the branches.

        In a moment of fury, the feral part of Daji’s nature that had been long dormant rose back to the surface. With a single leap, she seized the young elf by the neck. 

        “You insolent little brat, how dare you lay your hand on the peach tree I’ve tended with such care!” she hissed, her beautiful face wearing a murderous smile.

        “I-I-I only wanted to pick a branch to show my mother…” the elf stammered.

        “Humph! I don’t care what your excuse is. You shouldn’t have messed with my tree,” Daji sneered.         “Consider yourself lucky to be young—I’ll spare your life. BUT, you must pay for what you did—with your cultivation.”

        “N-no! Please, I was wrong! Please forgive me…” Tears streamed down the young elf’s face as she pleaded.

        “Crying won’t help you. Now, accept your punishment!” Daji channeled her power into her palm, ready to strip the elf of her cultivation. However, a yellow talisman flew through the air and struck her hand, forcing her to stop. The young elf took the chance to flee. Boiling with rage, Daji prepared to strike again, but a firm hand pressed down on her shoulder.

        “Daji, enough,”  Jiang Ziya said in a low, commanding voice. However, Daji’s rage only grew as she watched the young elf escape into the distance. She turned to Jiang Ziya, her eyes blazing with anger, and questioned, “WHY did you stop me?”

        “Her crime did not warrant such punishment.”

        “She offended me—that is a crime enough for death!” Daji argued.

        “Live and let live; that is the greater virtue.”

        “But I am THE nine-tailed vixen! Why should I tolerate such humiliation?” Daji’s tails lashed behind her.

        “Precisely because you are so powerful. That is why you must show restraint,” Jiang Ziya replied, his tone unyielding.

        “I don’t understand!” Daji stomped her foot, her nine tails flicking vigorously. “If living in this place means enduring such indignities, I’d rather return to the human realm!”

        She spun on her heel and stormed off. Yet, she slowed her pace after walking a short distance and glanced back over her shoulder, only to see that Jiang Ziya had not come for her. With her rage burning even brighter, she quickened her steps and left the Heavenly Kingdom.

        “Unbelievable! I’ve already spared that little brat’s life. Why must he stop me from taking her cultivation? She broke a branch of my precious peach tree! She would have died miserably if she had met the old me!” Daji grumbled.

        “I agree,” a voice came from the shadows. “This place is too small for you, Daji. With a talent like yours, you deserve much better than this.”

        Daji stopped and glanced warily into the darkness, her voice cold as she said, “Who’s there? Stop hiding and show yourself!”

        The speaker stepped into the light—it was a six-tailed vixen. She bowed respectfully to Daji. “Please, forgive my intrusion, but I couldn’t bear to see a great vixen like you suffer like this.”

        “Cut to the chase. What do you want?” It was clear to Daji that the vixen would not lurk at the entrance to the Heavenly Kingdom without a purpose—she must have come with an agenda.

        “You are as perceptive as they say,” the six-tailed vixen said. Lifting her head, she locked eyes with Daji, her face brimming with confidence and ambition, “I came to invite you to join our clan and restore our clan’s honor. Why stay here, bound by the archaic rules of the Heavenly Kingdom, when you have such unparalleled powers? You should leave this place.”

        Daji hesitated. The vixen’s words struck a chord deep within her, stirring something she could not quite define. She considered the offer for a split second, but then shook her head and said, “No. I won’t go with you.”

        “Why not?” The vixen was genuinely puzzled.

        “...Because there is something I can’t leave behind there,” Daji replied, her voice uncharacteristically gentle as an image of Jiang Ziya’s steady, resolute face surfaced in her mind.

        After the conversation with the vixen, Daji’s anger had already subsided. As she turned to leave for the Heavenly Kingdom, her gaze fell upon a familiar figure in the soft, flickering lantern light. Her heart skipped a beat, and she felt an inexplicable sense of hope.

        “Jiang… Shang,” she called softly.

        Jiang Ziya slowly walked toward her. He raised a hand to gently brush a stray lock of hair from her cheek and said, “I asked a skilled man to fix the peach tree, and it’s already blooming.”

        It did not take long for Daji to realize that Jiang Ziya was comforting her in his own way, and all the frustration she had felt earlier disappeared without a trace.

        “Then let’s go see it!” she said, beaming with a smile more radiant than the peach blossoms she had grown. With their hands intertwined, they walked side by side, their figures slowly vanishing into the night’s shadows as they headed home.
STORY_2928:
In the palace of the Vahalian Kingdom, a clatter of hurried footsteps echoed through the corridors near the royal gardens as a group of maids frantically searched high and low, calling out, “Prince Modi! The ceremony is about to begin!”

However, no one answered their calls. Left with no other choice, they moved on to search elsewhere. As their footsteps faded, a rustling sound came from a tall tree in the garden. A young boy dressed in formal attire leapt down from its branches. After brushing off leaves from his clothes, he chuckled with a smug grin, “Heh, finally got rid of them.”

                The boy’s name was Modi, prince of the Vahalian Kingdom. Today was a momentous occasion—the day the king would introduce him to the subjects, which was why a swarm of maids had been fussing over his appearance from the early morning. However, Modi, thoroughly annoyed, seized the opportunity to slip away unnoticed.

        He then began strolling happily through the gardens, hopping from one spot to another, fiddling with the colorful flowers and crouching down to observe ants scurrying across the ground. He was completely absorbed in his little world until he approached the edge of the garden, where he was startled by the muffled sound of someone sobbing.

        ‘W-w-what… Could it be the ghost of the garden the head maid mentioned?’ Modi’s mind raced with a mixture of fear and curiosity. Ultimately, his intrigue outweighed his fear, so he tiptoed toward the source of the sound. There, he saw a boy about his age quietly crying, crouching down near an iron fence.

        ‘So it’s not a ghost… What a bummer.’ Modi sighed in disappointment. When he was about to turn and leave, something about the boy’s sorrowful sobbing tugged at his heart, so he decided to stay and approach the boy.

        “Hey! What are you crying about?” Modi asked bluntly. The boy looked up, his face streaked with tears. Strangely, his features bore an uncanny resemblance to Modi’s.

        Seeing Modi, the boy hastily stifled his tears and gestured toward the iron fence. “I… I couldn’t save it… Sniff…”

        Only then did Modi notice a little fox caught between the iron bars of the fence. Its fur was stained bright red as blood slowly oozed from the scrapes on its body. Modi’s chest tightened at the sight, and he gasped, “This… this is bad. We’ve got to get it out of the bars.”

        “I tried, but the bars are too strong. I couldn’t pull them apart on my own,” the boy said, his voice choked with guilt.

        “I’ll go find a tool!” Modi hurriedly dashed back into the garden. Before long, he returned with a heavy spade left behind by a gardener. Together, the boys used the spade as a lever to pry the bars apart. Sensing the bars had been loosened, the little fox immediately wriggled its body. The moment it was free from the grip, it darted into the bushes beyond the garden with a swish.

        With his face lighting up with relief, the boy turned to Modi and said with a friendly grin, “Thank you!”

        “Heh, it’s nothing,” Modi replied, rubbing his nose while trying to play it cool by suppressing the swelling pride in his chest.

        However, the boy’s eyes suddenly widened, and he shouted, “You’re hurt!”

        Modi looked down to see a blood-seeping cut, about the length of half a finger, on his wrist, likely left by accident when he dragged the spade. He had barely noticed it until the boy pointed it out, and now the sting and the pain came rushing to the forefront of his mind.

        “Let me bandage it for you!” the boy said anxiously. He pulled a clean handkerchief from his pocket and carefully wrapped it around Modi’s wrist, then precociously advised, “This is just to stop the bleeding for now. You need to go back and get it properly cleaned, or it’ll get infected.”

        “Yeah, yeah, I got it.”

        The boy then glanced up at the sun hanging high in the sky. Realizing how much time had passed, he stood up hurriedly and said, “I’ve got to go.”

         “Wait! What’s your name?” Modi called after him.

        “I’m Magni. What about you?” the boy replied.

        “Modi. Let’s play together next time!” Modi said.

        “Sure!” Magni waved Modi goodbye enthusiastically as he ran off. Little did the two boys know that they had made a promise that could never be fulfilled…

        Later, during the ceremony, Modi and Magni stood on opposite sides of the stage, surrounded by different groups of nobles. It was not until the king presented them both as the heirs to the throne that they realized the ironic truth—they were half-brothers, children of the same father but different mothers; they were born to compete for the crown. And in that moment, they both understood: the promise they had made was nothing more than a fleeting dream, one that could never come true…
STORY_2929:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.4

        Two figures—one tall, one short—stood guard on either side of the secret passage entrance to the Madfang’s base. They remained vigilant as they scanned the surroundings until a loud growl shattered the silence.

        “Uuugh...” Plumpy, the cat, clutched her flat stomach and squatted down with a pitiful whimper.

        “Plumpy, are you alright?” Fist, the “dog”—one of the dogified cat thieves—asked, rushing to her side with concern.

        “I’m starving...” she replied, her eyes teary with hunger. “It’s all because we left in such a hurry before my food delivery arrived.”

        Not long ago, Mellow—the leader of the cat thieves—had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their headquarters.

        During the fight that ensued, Fist and several cat thieves were turned into dogs by a spray of a mysterious potion. To reverse the transformation, the cat thieves followed Teddy to a secret passage that led to the Madfang’s base. While Tim and the others sneaked inside, Plumpy and Fist were tasked with guarding the entrance, ready to assist when needed.

        Plumpy had ordered breakfast delivery, but the sudden turn of events forced her to leave the headquarters on an empty stomach with her crew, and now her stomach could not stand the hunger.

        “I’ll go get you something to eat,” Fist, unable to bear watching his girlfriend suffer, offered.

        “Yes, please! I want a piping-hot grilled fish!” Just the mention of food made Plumpy’s eyes sparkle. Fist, whose heart melted at the sight, took off without hesitation to find her some delicious fish, leaving her alone at the entrance. 

        “I wonder if Tim and the others have gotten the potion… Ohh… That cloud looks like grilled chicken… Slurp…” Plumpy gazed at the sky, blue after the rain. She began to drool as the clouds turned into tasty dishes in her eyes.

        “Hmm?” Her cat ears perked up suddenly. A look of desire spread across her face, and her mouth watered as she took a deep sniff. “That smell… grilled fish! Where is it coming from?”

        Driven by hunger, Plumpy forgot all about her mission and followed the scent until she reached a five-story building.

        “There it is! The top floor!” She stared at the rooftop. There were no footholds on the smooth walls—a climb would be nearly impossible. However, that was not enough to stop Plumpy—her craving for food only unlocked her potential.

        “I’m not leaving without that grilled fish!” After taking a few steps away from the building, she dropped to all fours, tensed her muscles, and sprinted forward at full speed. At the last second before the collision, she propelled herself into the air and leaped onto the wall on the third floor. Then she began clawing her way up toward the top.

        ‘O-oh no! I’m slipping!’ The force of gravity started to pull her back, and she lost her momentum, but the aromatic smell of grilled fish, like a carrot dangling before her, fueled her determination.

        “I GOT THIS!” Gritting her teeth, she vaulted upward with a final push and grabbed the edge of the rooftop with both hands. 

        “Phew…” She dangled for a moment before hauling herself over. Through the iron-barred window, she saw them—three steaming grilled fish, fresh out of the oven, on a plate.

        “Grilled fish! I’m coming!” She exclaimed as she broke the burglar bars with brute force, entering the room through the window. Her eyes lit up at the sight of the mouthwatering fish. She lunged forward without hesitation, grabbed the fish with her bare hands, and devoured them.

        “Ahh, I’m so full... So happy… Woah!” Cradling her round belly, she turned around and froze when she found dozens of kittens staring at her in fear, huddling in the corner of the room, more precisely, a cage.

        “This should be the Madfang’s base… What are you all doing here?” Plumpy tilted her head, confused.

        “W-we were kidnapped,” one of the kittens said bravely. “And it’s not just us. They kidnapped the puppies, too.”

        “Huh?” Plumpy looked around to see dozens of young puppies locked in a cage on the opposite side. A similar plate was placed nearby with roasted drumsticks.

        “But why would they kidnap you?” she muttered, scratching her head.

        “The Madfang’s leader, Cork, kidnapped us to frame the Clawhaven!” the kitten exclaimed in indignation. “I heard them talking about kidnapping the puppies and kittens, and blaming it on the Clawhaven to stir up the dogs in the organization against us. It’s all a part of his plan to turn all cats into dogs!”

        “Yeah!” one of the puppies cried, rushing to the bars. “Cork made a deal with a human, asking her to drug all male dogs and make them infertile after he turns all the cats in town into cats. That way, he can hoard all the female dogs for himself and live out his fantasy of a canine harem!”

        “WHAT?” Plumpy’s fur bristled in fury. “He is a married man—and he still wants other female dogs?! That’s disgusting! Unforgivable!”

        “His wife is so kind and sweet, and he still betrays her. We can’t stand it either!” the puppy whimpered. “Big Sis, can you help us? We want to tell our parents about that awful leader’s scheme!”

        ‘Big Sis… Heehee, that sounds kind of awesome…’ Plumpy thought, swelling with pride under their adoring gazes. Puffing her chest, she declared confidently, “Sure! Leave it to me! Big Sis will get all of you out of here!”

        “Hooray! Finally, we can get out of here!”
“Thank you, Big Sis!”

        The puppies and kittens cheered in gratitude. Plumpy basked in her moment of glory until the sound of approaching footsteps snapped her back to reality.

        “Shh! Someone’s coming!” She immediately signaled all the kittens and puppies to stay quiet. She crept to the bars and peeked out, only to see five adult dogs enter the room. One of them carried a cage—inside were more kittens and puppies.

        “Seriously? We still have to catch more? Didn’t the boss say he’d deal with those stinking cats today?” one of the dogs grumbled.

        “He wants backup. Just in case,” another replied.
        “Ugh, what a pain…”
        “Enough complaining. Let’s just get them in and go have a barbecue,” the leader said, comforting his subordinates. As they moved forward, someone suddenly darted out and snatched the cage from the dog’s hands.. 
 
        “Who’s there?” the leader snarled.

        “Ha! It is I, the super Big Sis—Plumpy,” Plumpy said with a grin, striking a cool pose before opening the cage and freeing the young captives. “Here to save the day!”

        “Tut! I don’t care if you’re a hero or a freak! No one messes with the Madfang!” the leader barked, “Get her!”

        “Well, take this!” Plumpy charged fearlessly.

        “Gah!” With perfect aim, she hurled the leftover fish bone like a dart and pinned one of the dogs to the wall. 

        “Ow!”
        “Ugh!”
        She then knocked out two other dogs with two flying plates.

        “ARGH!” Another dog howled in agony after taking a vicious kick to the groin.

        “...Damn it!” The leader promptly turned and ran as he found his group losing the fight.

        “Big Sis! Let’s escape while we can!” one of the kittens shouted.

        “Alright! Follow me, stay close!” Plumpy led the kittens and puppies down the stairs, knocking aside three more guards with ease.

        It was after a moment of running that they finally reached the exit on the first floor. Their hearts pounded with hope as they ran toward the gate, only to find the doorway surrounded by dozens of adult dogs.

        “We’ve got you!” The leader who fled earlier grinned smugly, flanked by reinforcements. “Surrender now and we may— ARGH!”

        WHAM! A heavy punch sent him flying.

        “Plumpy! There you are!” shouted Fist, his fist still clenched.

        “Fist!” Plumpy cried joyfully.

        “What happened?” Fist asked, frowning at the ring of hostile dogs.

        “I’ll explain later. Just help me kick these dogs’ butts first!”

        “Got it!” Despite not knowing the full story, Fist did not doubt Plumpy’s words; he trusted her completely. Together, they took down every enemy in their path. Even the kittens and puppies joined in, swarming the adult dogs, and the battlefield was cleared in no time.

        “Phew… I’m exhausted. I think I’ve digested all that grilled fish I had a few minutes ago…” Plumpy flopped onto the ground and sighed.

        Fist reached into his coat and handed her something wrapped in a cloth, and said, “Here… Your grilled fish.”

        “Aww! Fist, you’re the best!” I love you so much!” she squealed, giving him a big hug. She even planted a kiss on his cheek. She then dug into the food again, oblivious to the fact that her kiss had turned Fist red from head to toe. 

        “Plumpy! Fist!” a familiar voice called from afar. The two turned and saw someone running toward them—it was Tim and the other cat thieves!
STORY_2930:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.3

        In the Madfang’s base, four refined dog ladies sat gracefully on a velvet sofa in the lounge, their eyes fixed on the dog man performing magic tricks before them.

        “Behold, the firebird!” shouted the “dog”, Copperfield, one of the cat thieves. With a dramatic exhale, a roaring plume of orange fire erupted from his mouth, transforming into a blazing bird that flew around the ladies before vanishing into the air.

        The ladies all gasped at the magical performance, clapping their hands with admiration and exhilaration.

        “Wow, that was amazing!”
        “Incredible!”
        “Do it again! Do it again!”

        ‘Phew... Good, they’re enjoying it. I might be able to buy us more time this way,’ Copperfield thought while glancing at the door. ‘I wonder if Tim and the others are making progress.’

        Not long ago, Mellow—the leader of the cat thieves—had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their headquarters.

        During the fight that ensued, Copperfield and several cat thieves were turned into dogs by a spray of a mysterious potion. To reverse the transformation, the cat thieves sneaked into the Madfang’s base with Teddy’s help, hoping to steal a sample so Merbromin could create an antidote.

        On their way to the laboratory, however, the group ran into Teddy’s aunt, Bonnie, and her close friends, who asked them to help as servants. To avoid blowing their cover, Copperfield stepped forward to distract the ladies with his magic tricks long enough for Tim and the others to slip away.

        He then helped carry the ladies’ luggage and accompanied them to one of the lounges. Just as he was going to excuse himself, the ladies, enchanted by his magic tricks, insisted he stay and continue his performance. To avoid raising suspicion, Copperfield reluctantly obliged and began throwing every trick and sleight-of-hand he had into entertaining them.

        “Why don’t we take a break?” said Bonnie, her voice soft and warm. “You must be tired from doing all the magic tricks for us. Here, have some water.”

        “Thank you.” Copperfield, who was indeed starting to feel fatigued, gratefully accepted the offer. However, the other three ladies were not pleased, and one of them scoffed, “Humph, he should feel honored to perform for us.”

        “Honor or not, he’s still a member of the organization,” Bonnie replied gently.

        “Bonnie, you’re too soft! That’s why Cork walks all over you!”

        “Exactly! He didn’t even show up on your birthday! What kind of husband is that?” another lady chimed in.

        “He’s just busy,” Bonnie still tried to defend her husband. “There have been kittens and puppies going missing lately. He’s been dealing with that.”

        “Busy, my tail,” the friend sneered. “I bet he’s ‘dealing’ with something else.”

        “No… I trust him.”

        “Sure, nothing can break you two apart,” the friend drawled, rolling her eyes. Then she turned to Copperfield and said, “Hey, you. Had enough of a break? Get back here and keep going—”

        BEEP—

        Suddenly, a sharp alarm went off and shattered the serenity in the building, startling the ladies and sending a chill down Copperfield’s spine.

        ‘Something must have happened to Tim and the others! I need to get to them—now!’ While the room was plunged into chaos, Copperfield dashed to the door and opened it slightly, only to find his companions—Tim, Merbromin, and Teddy—barreling toward him in a panic with over a dozen hulking dogs chasing them.

        “Copperfield! Let us in!” Tim yelled. Copperfield immediately opened the door wider. As soon as his teammates tumbled inside, Copperfield pulled a palm-sized piece of gum from his pocket. He tossed it into his mouth and began chewing it rapidly. Then he spat it out and slapped it onto the door—where, astonishingly, it began to swell like yeasted dough, sealing the entrance shut in moments.

        THUD! A loud bang echoed from the outside as the dogs hit the door, which held strong thanks to Copperfield’s magic gum.

        “This should keep them outside for a while,” Copperfield breathed a sigh of relief. Just as he turned to ask Tim if they’d gotten the potion, he froze—Bonnie and her friends were staring at them with suspicion and hostility.

        “Who are you people? What are you doing here?” Bonnie demanded.

        “Wait—this isn’t what it looks like! We didn’t do anything bad—”

        “Lies!” one of the dog ladies snapped. “If you didn’t do anything bad, then why were you running?”

        “Because they were protecting me,” Teddy stepped forward and said.

        “Teddy!” Bonnie gasped. “Why are you dressed like that? And you’re hurt! Who did this to you?”

        “It was Uncle Cork,” Teddy lifted his head, revealing the truth. “He tried to kill me so that he could have the organization all to himself. It was the cat thieves—Copperfield and the others—who saved my life.”

        “Wh-what?” Bonnie staggered in disbelief. “There must be a misunderstanding. Cork wouldn’t do this to me…”

        “Ma’am, I understand how you feel,” Merbromin interjected, placing the evidence—the stack of photos they had found in the laboratory—in front of her. “But the truth is, your husband is far worse than you know.”

        Bonnie took the photos with trembling hands. As her eyes scanned the photos, seeing Cork locked in intimate embraces with other dog ladies, the gentle expression on her face twisted into a grim scowl. With fury radiating from every inch of her once-composed presence, she crumpled the photos in a clenched fist.

        “How dare he lie to me… and hurt my dear nephew…” Bonnie grumbled, exuding a terrifying aura that left every cat and dog in the room stunned. No one dared to make a sound as she growled, “Cork, it seems I’ve stayed gentle for too long that you’ve forgotten that I share the same blood as my brother!”

        “I’m coming with you. That bastard needs to learn what it means to betray me,” she said to the cat thieves.

        “Y-Yes, ma’am!” Copperfield immediately sprang into action, conjuring a flurry of shimmering magic bubbles that carried them out the window and flew beyond the walls where Plumpy and Fist were waiting for their return…
STORY_2931:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.8

        In a derelict factory, long abandoned on the city’s outskirts, a massive mechanical dog known as the Madfang Titan lay on the ground, its neck caught beneath a steel gate. From the forcibly broken cockpit door, one could see the maze of complex machinery within.

        A slender catl—Ghostie, a member of the cat thieves—stepped into the cockpit, her paws making barely a sound. Her eyes sparkled with curiosity as she marveled at the futuristic chamber, clasping her hands in awe. “Wow… This is amazing.”

        Not long ago, Mellow had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their headquarters.

        After defeating the assassins, they learned that Teddy’s uncle, Cork, planned to turn every cat in the town into dogs. And so, Mellow led Choux, Wimpy, Ghostie, and the “dogified” Zero to cripple the dogs’ “meeting” with the cats in the abandoned factory and ultimately thwart Cork’s sinister scheme.

        Unexpectedly, Cork sealed the factory and ordered his pawns to attack the cats with spray guns, trying to turn them all into dogs after his true intentions had been exposed. Thankfully, the cat thieves united, joining forces to overcome their adversaries. Not only did they manage to neutralize the canine forces, but they also managed to rescue the missing kittens and puppies, reunite them with their families, and bring Cork’s crimes to light.

        Cornered by all the enraged parents, Cork decided to call upon his last resort—his mechanical dog, the Madfang Titan, trying to wipe out the cats with one last attempt. However, Zero and Mellow took the Titan down. Zero then handed over Cork to his wife, Bonnie. While the Titan sat unmanned beneath the gate, Ghostie, intrigued, quietly climbed aboard for a closer look.

        “Hm… I see. So that’s how the control panel works…” Ghostie mumbled as she crawled under the console and poked around with curiosity, oblivious to the woman who darted into the cockpit behind her. As the woman slid into the pilot’s seat, she began moving her fingers, rebooting the Titan in the blink of an eye, and the robot began to transform.

        “Woah!” Ghostie yelped as she tumbled across the metal floor because of the sudden transformation. It was not until the transformation was complete that she could finally see the purple-haired woman, oddly familiar, after her head stopped spinning. She heard her mumbling through clenched teeth, “I knew I couldn’t trust that stupid dog! Good thing I came prepared, and I won’t let you slip through my fingers again!”

        ‘Wait… Isn’t she the mad scientist who kidnapped Ali Baba and the cats?!’ Ghostie’s eyes widened in shock. The woman—Blodgett—was too focused on the controls to notice Ghostie, who, though, had an arguably weak presence. She stared at the monitor, where Mellow and Zero were shown, and muttered, “Cats should be erased from this world!”

        She reached for a red button. Although Ghostie did not know what the button was for, she knew it could not be something good.

        ‘I can’t let her do this!’ Ghostie pressed herself low to the floor, her eyes narrowing as she propelled herself like a shadow toward her target—

        THUD!

        Ghostie tackled Blodgett. Both of them rolled onto the cold metal floor.
 
        “Ow… My head…” Blodgett groaned, clutching the back of her skull. She looked up only to see Ghostie glaring at her, alert and tense. Her voice choked with rage as she yelled, “You sneaky little feline! I can’t believe you hid in the cockpit to ambush me!”

        “I didn’t hide—I was here first!” Ghostie argued. “Besides, you were going to do something to my pals. Of course, I had to stop you!”

        “You cats are all the same, so annoying! That’s why I’m going to turn every last one of you into dogs!”

        “But… why?” Ghostie asked, genuinely confused. “Why do you hate cats so much? We’re no different from dogs or humans. We’re all living beings of this land. We should coexist, equally.”

        “Heh. How poetic,” Blodgett sneered. “The truth is, equality doesn’t exist. Even in your little cat thieves crew, there are ranks. You, for example… You’re always forgotten, left behind. Didn’t you notice? Your friends have all left.”

        “What…? Ah—!” Startled, Ghostie glanced at the screen. Unexpectedly, Blodgett stepped forward and shoved her toward the cockpit’s open edge, where Zero had ripped off the door earlier. It would be a three-story drop if she fell.

        “No!” Ghostie barely managed to grab the ledge, her body dangling in the air. A cold wind bit at her fur. She tried to climb back up, but Blodgett stomped hard on her right hand with a high-heeled boot.

        “Look at you, one of the renowned cat thieves, yet abandoned and forgotten. Just like I was…” Blodgett looked down at Ghostie with her nose in the air. A hint of agony and embarrassment flashed across her eyes, but she soon took her arrogant facade back on. “So forget equality—it’s pointless!”

        “...No,” Ghostie growled, fighting the pain. Her right hand throbbed, her body hung in the air—but her heart burned with resolve as she continued to confront Blodgett. “Perhaps you’re right… My pals do sometimes forget about me, but they always come back for me!”

        Then she reached for the bell hanging from the collar on her neck and yanked it off—

        BEEP-BEEP-BEEP! A shrill alarm echoed across the factory. A blinding light came from the collar, casting rainbows in every direction. Blodgett flinched and loosened her foot’s grip.

        “What did you—”

        “Right here!” A sweet voice emanated from beyond the walls, drowning out Blodgett’s question. Hurried footsteps came closer, and moments later, a dozen figures broke into the factory—it was the cat thieves!

        “There! Mellow! Ghostie’s on top of the metal thing!” cried Plumpy, spotting Ghostie instantly with her keen eyes thanks to the collar’s beacon. “Oh no! She’s hanging off the edge! About to fall!”

        “Tut! I just can’t have a day off without worrying about you guys, can I?” Mellow huffed, sitting on Zero’s shoulder. Then she decisively commanded, “Copperfield, cloud trick, now!”

        “Alright! Leave it to me!” Copperfield whipped out two knitting needles and a white ball of yarn. As he wove, the thread came to life, expanding outward and swelling into a giant fluffy cushion that floated like a cloud.

        “Zero! Fist!” Mellow shouted.

        “On it!” Zero and Fist responded simultaneously while each grabbed a side of the cloud and hurled it beneath Ghostie.


        Realizing the cats’ plan, Blodgett lunged for Ghostie. Little did she know Ghostie would let go before the cushion even reached her. Even as she fell, her expression—a smile with tears in her eyes—said it all: I wasn’t forgotten. My pals came back for me!

        Poof!

        Ghostie landed on the cushion unharmed. All the cat thieves rushed to her side. Plumpy tackled her, screaming in relief, “Waaah! Ghostie! I’m so glad you’re okay! We were so worried—didn’t know if you were trapped…” 

        “Thank you for coming back for me,” Ghostie said softly while patting Plumpy’s back. Then she looked at Mellow. “She… She’s in the cockpit.” 

        “I know. I won’t let her get away this time,” Mellow grinned. At her signal, the team moved in, surrounding the Titan. They successfully captured Blodgett, dragging her before Mellow.

        “We meet again, Miss Inventor,” Mellow said, looking down at Blodgett from atop Zero’s shoulder. “As I recall, we still have a few scores to settle.”

        “Spare the chatter and just kill me,” Blodgett spat, her face showing no trace of remorse.

        “Oh, I’m not killing you,” Mellow replied, “Since you hate cats so much… What better punishment than to turn you into what you loathe most?”

        “No! No! I don’t want to become a cat!” Blodgett vehemently protested, but Merbromin stepped forward and struck her unconscious. He then signaled Plumpy and Fist to carry her away to the medical lab, where the punishment awaited…

        Afterward, with Bonnie’s support, Teddy took over the Madfang. As for Cork, rumor has it he was injected with the infertility potion he had Blodgett make for him, forever destroying his dream of living in a canine harem.

        The cat thieves returned to their usual lives—sometimes traveling the world alongside Ali Baba, sometimes robbing the rich to help the poor, and their legend lived on…
STORY_2932:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.7

        In a derelict factory, long abandoned on the city’s outskirts, a crowd of cats and dogs stood united. Their gazes locked on the tall Dalmatian cornered before a wall, burning with fury, indignation, and disbelief.

        “So this is what they mean when they say what goes around comes around,” Zero, the “dog,” thought quietly. 

        Not long ago, Mellow had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their doorsteps.

        After defeating the assassins, they learned that Teddy’s uncle, Cork, planned to turn every cat in the town into dogs. And so, Mellow led Choux, Wimpy, Ghostie, and the “dogified” Zero to cripple the dogs’ “meeting” with the cats in the abandoned factory and ultimately thwart Cork’s sinister scheme.

        Although they managed to expose Cork’s true intentions to the cats, Cork, with his pretense shattered, sealed the factory and ordered his pawns to attack the cats with spray guns, trying to turn them all into dogs.

        To everyone’s surprise, Wimpy and Choux unleashed their potential and rose to the occasion. Wimpy locked all the dogs’ spray guns while Choux jammed the cannons with bread loaves and united the other cats to take down the dogs with stink bombs—fermented herring pies.

        However, Cork, cunning as ever, stirred his subordinates’ emotions, exploiting their love for their children to incite vengeance. The situation teetered on the edge of a crash until Plumpy and Fist arrived, breaking in through one of the gates with the kidnapped kittens and puppies. Then Teddy told everyone the truth: the mastermind behind all the kidnappings was none other than his uncle, Cork.

        “He used us?”
        “I can’t believe he used us and hurt our children!”
        “Unforgivable!”

        With all his crimes completely exposed, Cork was cornered by a crowd of enraged parents. Knowing he could not talk his way out, he decisively turned and ran.

        “He’s escaping!”
        “Stop him! Don’t let him get away!”

        The cats and dogs immediately chased after him, but they were too late. As soon as Cork reached the dock outside the factory, he leapt into the cockpit of a three-story-tall mechanical dog, the Madfang Titan, and controlled it to swat away pursuers with one mighty paw, knocking several cats and dogs out cold.

        “Argh!”

        “Hahaha! With the Madfang Titan, no one can stand against me!” Cork bellowed with triumph. His eyes locked on his nephew, Teddy, who stood beside Mellow.

        “It’s all your fault… If it weren’t for you, my plan would’ve succeeded!’ Cork growled. “I’ll erase you—like you never existed!”

        Placing all the blame on his nephew, Teddy, he maneuvered the Titan straight toward the little dog—

        BOOM!

        The Titan’s front paw slammed into the ground, leaving a pit and stirring a cloud of dust—there was no way anything could have survived that impact.

        “Heh, that’s what you get for standing against me, Teddy—”

        “Uncle. Don’t you think you’re celebrating too soon?” Teddy’s voice cut through Cork’s victorious laughter.

        Cork froze, then slowly turned, only to see a large dog holding Mellow and Teddy in his arms. It was Zero, who had rescued them at the last second.

        “Even if you get on that metal dog, Zero and I can still take you down!” Mellow said confidently.

        “Yeah,” Zero smiled and added, “Together, we’re stronger.”

        “Humph! You arrogant felines! If one slap can’t take you down, I’ll just give you some more. Let’s see if your stamina outlasts my Titan!” Cork retorted. 

        Cork charged again. However, it was a cramped factory. Whenever the Titan moved, it either crashed into a wall or the ceiling, sending debris flying everywhere. All the cats and dogs had to scramble for their lives while shielding their children. Still, many were wounded and bruised by falling rubble.

        “This is too dangerous. Someone may die from this,” Mellow whispered urgently. “Zero, draw it outside!” Then she looked to Tim, who knowingly nodded and passed the order to evacuate the other cats and dogs.

        “Got it! Hold tight!” Zero tightened his grip on Teddy and Mellow. He then waited for an opportune moment to sprint under the Titan’s legs, heading straight for the exit.

        “Wanna run? Not a chance!” Cork, of course, followed suit and ran outside the factory. With its movements no longer constrained by limited space, the Titan’s speed became faster, which made it even harder for Zero to evade its attacks.

        ‘He’ll eventually catch us if we keep wasting our stamina like this… It seems I have to do something!’ The usually imperturbable Zero unusually narrowed his eyes. His spirit ignited. As the Titan lunged again, he nimbly dodged the attack and struck back with a powerful punch to its front paw.

        CLANG!

        They heard a resounding clang, but there was not even a crack in the paw’s surface. Instead, a jolt of pain numbed Zero’s entire arm. He froze for a split second—just enough for Cork to retaliate. With a swing of its tail, the Titan flung the cats into the air. The only thing Zero could do was to shield Teddy and Mellow with his body before they crashed into the ground.

        “Zero!” Mellow cried out.

        “I’m… I’m okay…” Zero groaned while forcing himself to his feet. Despite his injuries, he lifted Teddy and Mellow, continued his run, but slower now.

        “That thing’s too sturdy. We can’t fight it head-on,” Mellow said.

        “Then what do we do?” Teddy asked anxiously. “If we don’t stop it soon, we’ll all be dead.”

        “I know…” Mellow said, her eyes narrowing as she studied the Titan. Its wagging tail and frenzied movements gave her an idea. “I’ve got an idea, but I’m not sure it’ll work—”

        “Let’s try it,” Zero interjected, his eyes devoid of doubt. “I believe in you.”

        “Zero…” Mellow was moved. Smiling at Zero, she said, “Alright then, help me grab that giant clock over there first!”

        “On it!” Zero did not question her. He obediently ran to the corner and picked up a disc-sized clock half his height. “Now what?”

        “Throw me and the clock toward the factory gate. Hard,” she said.

        “…What?” He hesitated, concerned about Mellow’s safety.

        “Trust me. I’m gonna be fine,” Mellow reassured him with a confident smile. Zero nodded and then began running toward the factory gate while holding the clock high in the air with Mellow clinging onto it. With a fast run-up, he gathered momentum and threw them into the air—

        “WOOF!” The Titan stopped, eyes locked on the flying disc. Its tail began to wag madly, and like a dog chasing a toy, it pounced.

        “What are you doing? Obey my commands!” Cork yelled, tugging the console. Still, he failed to redirect the Titan’s direction.

        ‘Error! Error! Program overridden by canine instincts. All commands rejected.’ The mechanical voice repeated.

        “Damn it! You useless dog! What are you doing chasing a FRISBEE?” Cork roared. He helplessly watched as the Titan jumped and caught the giant clock in midair. Surprisingly, Mellow was not on the clock—she had landed at the factory’s entrance, her hand grabbing the lever as she shouted, “Zero!”

        “Got it!” he answered. The moment the Titan landed, he leaped forward and delivered a flying double kick to its rear. WHAM! The Titan stumbled straight into the factory gate.

        “Nice kick!” Mellow cheered while pulling the lever. CLANG! The steel gate dropped, trapping the Titan’s neck beneath it. It struggled violently, but still, it could not break free from the heavy gate.

        Just then, Zero propped himself up from the ground. He climbed onto the Titan’s back and reached the cockpit door. Holding the door from both sides, he summoned a burst of strength as he shouted, “HA!”

        CRACK! He ripped the door open. His eyes met with Cork, who had just unfastened his seatbelt, ready to flee but frozen by the unexpected turns of events.

        “I GOT YOU!” Zero slowly said with a gentle smile—but to Cork, it was the smile of a demon. He then reached in and grabbed Cork by the collar to haul him out of the cockpit.

        “We’re not done! I will get my revenge! By then, all of you will—” SLAP! A resounding slap in the face silenced Cork. However, it was not Zero, who delivered the slap. It was Bonnie—Cork’s wife and Teddy’s aunt.

        “Bonnie… Wh-what are you doing here?”

        “I’m here to deal with you, of course,” Bonnie said with a ferocious grin, baring her sharp teeth. As she raised a paw, her friends joined her and hauled Cork away.

        “Well, now that everything's settled, let’s go home—” Mellow said, but her voice was drowned out by a mechanical screech.

        To her surprise, the fallen Titan moved! In the blink of an eye, it shifted into a humanoid robot, rising to its feet under the gate.

        “I knew I couldn’t trust that stupid dog! Good thing I came prepared, and I won’t let you slip through my fingers again!” A woman in a white lab coat with purple hair grumbled through her teeth, her voice shrill and furious.

        She was none other than Blodgett, the mad inventor who had once kidnapped Ali Baba. The same human who had been working with Cork.

        Sitting in the cockpit, she stared at Mellow and Zero, her eyes glowing with a twisted gleam as she mumbled, “Cats should be erased from this world!”
STORY_2933:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.1

        On a rainy morning, a small dog—more precisely a boy with canine features—covered in mud and wounds, lay curled up in the thick, dew-kissed grass, his body trembling as he let out weak, pained whimpers. The cold drizzle fell on his body and slowly sapped away his body heat, gnawing away at his will to survive with a deadly chill.

        The boy struggled to open his eyes. He gazed at the cloudy sky above as raindrops trickled down his tender face, leaving a trail.

        ‘Am I… dying? But I’m not ready to die yet… Is there anybody… anybody who can help me?’ Despairing thoughts echoed in the boy’s mind like a faint cry for help.

        Suddenly, he heard a rustling noise—someone was walking through the grass. His ears twitched instinctively as his body tensed, alert. He tried to push himself up, but his strength failed. A sharp pain tearing through his wounds sent him back into the mud. With his mind fading as the last ounce of his strength waned, all he could do was helplessly watch a petite figure step into his line of sight—a girl with feline features.

        Standing with her arms crossed, the girl exuded a sense of maturity beyond her youthful appearance. Her bright, sparkling eyes gazed at him with exasperation and empathy. He heard her mutter, “A dog passing out in the wild? I can’t just leave you here, can I?”

        The girl’s voice and expression somehow brought the boy an inexplicable sense of relief, soothing his frayed nerves, and he slipped into unconsciousness before he knew it.

        When the boy opened his eyes again, he found himself no longer lying in the muddy grass but instead in a clean and spacious living room. He propped himself up on the sofa only to see the bandages on his body—all his wounds had been treated so well that he felt no discomfort.

        “You’re finally awake,” a kittenish voice called out. The boy turned his head and recognized the girl who had saved him. Behind her stood several people with feline features, likely her companions.

        “Thank you for saving my life. My name is Teddy,” the dog said and bowed his head in gratitude. His refined manners revealed his well-bred upbringing.

        “I’m Mellow, and they are my crew,” the catgirl introduced herself before cutting to the chase, “Why were you so badly injured? What happened?”

        “I…“ Teddy hesitated as if struggling with whether to reveal the truth.

        Ding-dong!  

        “Oh! That must be the food delivery I ordered!” Plumpy exclaimed excitedly and bounced toward the door. The boy next to her, Fist, immediately offered, “I’ll go with you.”

        “His injuries are quite severe. Let’s eat first and talk later,” said Merbromin, the cross-dressing man who had tended to Teddy’s wounds.

        “Agreed. Food first, worries later,” chimed in Zero, a laid-back male cat who wore a harmless smile.

        However, a strange unease gnawed at Teddy. His instincts screamed at him, prompting his gaze to dart toward the door where Plumpy and Fist were heading. Through the little gap beneath the door, he spotted pairs of eyes gleaming with malice. His heart sank, and he shouted, “Wait! Don’t open the door—”

        “Huh?” Plumpy froze mid-motion, but the door had already been cracked open. A large dog lunged through the gap, slamming into Plumpy and knocking her to the ground.

        “Grrrr-WOOF!” The dog snarled viciously as it charged toward Teddy on the sofa, its gaping maw ready to bite down on his head—

        Bang!  

        A fierce punch sent the dog flying with a deafening crash. It was Zero, who shook his hand, his eyes gleaming with flaring fury as he growled, “Don’t you dare mess around on my turf, mutt!”

        “Plumpy! Shut the door, quickly!” Mellow shouted orders to Plumpy as soon as she recovered from the shock. Suddenly, a terrified scream came from one of the cat thieves, Wimpy, whose legs knocked together in a pigeon-toed stance.

        But before Plumpy could move, a terrified scream came from Cork, who pointed shakily toward the floor-to-ceiling windows behind Mellow.  

        “T-th-the w-windows…” Wimpy stammered, his legs trembling as he pointed at the row of floor-to-ceiling glass windows behind Mellow. 

        “What?” Mellow turned only to see more large dogs leaping at the glass!

        CRASH!  

        With a loud crash, the windows shattered into countless pieces. The dogs stormed into the room, targeting the cats in the living room.

        “AHHH! Don’t bite my butt!” Wimpy shrieked, stumbling forward and falling flat on his face as a dog lunged at him. Just as the dog’s sharp teeth were about to sink into his bottom, someone stopped the attack with a frying pan.

        “I’m not helping you. I just can’t stand these stupid dogs,” Choux said with a sneer, but her next move contradicted her words—she pulled out another pan and knocked the dog unconscious.

        “Everyone, stay calm!” Mellow climbed onto Zero’s shoulders and shouted to rally her team, “These dogs are all bark and no bite. Just keep your cool, and we can take them down!”

        Hearing the leader’s words, the cat thieves regained their composure and their movements became more coordinated, turning the tide of the battle in an instant.

        The dogs, now battered, began retreating with frightened whimpers. Just as victory seemed certain, a deep voice cut through the chaos.

        “Well, well. Looks like I underestimated you, Master Teddy. Your bodyguards are tougher than I thought.” A towering figure emerged from the pack of dogs—Arnold, a man with canine features just like Teddy.

        “Arnold…” Teddy said as he stared at the man with a complicated expression. “You’ve betrayed my father.”

        “What can I say? Cork made me an offer I couldn’t refuse,” Arnold said with a shrug. “I’ll deal with you once I finish these dumb cats. Don’t worry, though. I’ll make it quick out of respect for your dead father.”

        Mellow, sensing danger, immediately shouted, “Watch out!” However, Arnold was even faster than she had anticipated. Raising a large spray gun, he pulled the trigger.

        Pssshhh!

        A thick cloud of gas erupted from the weapon, engulfing the entire room. Zero reflexively shielded Mellow with his body while Fist protected Plumpy. Tim, Copperfield, and Merbromin gathered in a circle to protect the other cat thieves, including Choux, Ghostie, and Wimpy. It was not until the gas cleared that they withdrew their arms.

        “Ahhh!” Wimpy screamed, staring at the other cats in horror. “Ti-Tim! You… Your faces!”  

        “What?” Tim hurriedly looked down at himself, only to discover the shocking truth. “Why… Why am I suddenly a dog?”

        “M-me too!” Copperfield shouted. It turned out that all the cats who had come into direct contact with the gas—Zero, Merbromin, Fist, and others—had transformed into dogs!

        “Hehehe… Now you see how powerful we are,” Arnold sneered. Taking advantage of the chaos, he ordered his dogs, “Now finish them!”

        “Woof!” The dogs charged again, and the cat thieves—now dogified—struggled to fend them off. The tables had turned again. Just as it seemed they would lose the fight, Mellow’s voice rang out like a beacon of hope. “Don’t panic! We can still fight even as dogs!”

        Despite her petite form, Mellow managed to rally her companions with her words and unwavering determination.

        “Yeah! Even as a dog, I’m still fabulous!” Merbromin responded while delivering a flawless spinning kick that sent a dog flying. 

        “Yeah, I’ll keep Plumpy and everyone safe!” Fist roared, overcoming his urge to chase his tail as he knocked out another dog.

        “Tut! I can’t believe they calm down so quickly…” Arnold, sensing the tides turning, decided to retreat. “Damn it. I’ll be back with reinforcements,” he muttered, but Mellow had already seen through his move, so she patted Zero’s shoulder and commanded, “Don’t let him escape!”

        Zero leaped into action, landing in front of Arnold and delivering a knee strike to his gut. Arnold collapsed, and the remaining dogs fled in fear, leaving the cat thieves in the now disordered room.

        Mellow turned to Teddy, her expression stern. “I think you owe us an explanation.” 

        “I’m truly sorry for dragging you all into this,” Teddy said, lowering his head in shame. “My father was the leader of the Madfang. A few years ago, my parents passed away because of illness. At the time, I was too young to take over my father’s work, so my uncle and aunt stepped in. But my aunt never liked the organization, so in the end, it was my uncle who took control of the organization.”

         “But then, you grew up. Your uncle saw you as a threat and decided to get rid of you… Am I right?” Mellow, who had already pieced together the rest of the story, interrupted. 

        Teddy nodded. “I didn’t have much interest in reclaiming the leader’s position, but I changed my mind after I overheard my uncle’s conversation with a human last night. They mentioned a meeting with the cats of the Clawhaven today to discuss the recent disappearances of kittens and puppies, but the meeting is, in fact, a trap—they plan to use this opportunity to turn all the cats in this town into dogs. It’s such a crazy plan, so I stepped in to stop him…  but that only provoked him, and now he wants me dead…”

        “What?! Turning all cats into dogs? That’s insane!” Copperfield shouted in indignation.

        “We can’t let this happen,” Tim said as he adjusted his glasses. “And we also need to figure out how to turn ourselves back into cats.”

        “Agree. I can’t stay in a dog’s body forever,” Fist said with a stoic face but deep down he was freaking out, basically screaming in his mind, ‘Oh no… Plumpy might break up with me if I don’t turn back into a cat… No! I won’t let that happen!’

        “Thank you all!” Teddy straightened up and promptly spoke, “I know where the transformation potion is stored. It’s in our base, and I can lead you there!”

        “If I can get a sample of the potion, I should be able to create an antidote,” Merbromin added.

        “...There’s no time to waste. We’ll have to split into two teams,” Mellow said after a brief moment of contemplation, revealing her plan. “Tim, Copperfield, and Merbromin, you’ll go with Teddy to the Madfang’s base to take the sample while Plumpy and Fist stay outside the base, in case anything happens. And I’ll take the rest of the team to stop the dogs’ scheme.”

        “Understood!” the cat thieves answered in unison before splitting up to carry out their mission…
STORY_2934:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.5

        In a secluded corner not far from the city center stood an old, abandoned factory. Long forgotten and untouched, it had become the perfect place for shady dealings no one was meant to see.

        Now, the place was packed with cats and dogs, each side staring daggers at the other. Tension thickened the air like storm clouds. It was clearly not a friendly gathering.

        A tall, imposing Dalmatian, Cork, stood at the center, glaring down with disdain at a long-haired cat as he barked, “Release our puppies now—or don’t blame me for what happens next.”

        “Cork, I’ve already told you many times—we didn’t kidnap your puppies,” the long-haired cat, Miro, though smaller than the dog, replied calmly. “We’ve lost quite a few of our kittens, too. I came here hoping we could work together to find the kidnapper and rescue the missing younglings. But if this is the attitude you’re bringing to the table, the Clawhaven has no reason to continue this farce of a cooperation.”

        “Spare me your lies, Miro,” Cork scoffed, “Only you conniving cats would stoop so low as to kidnap children and use them in your schemes. Shame on you.”
 
        “I—”

        “No, shame on you, Cork!” A sweet voice cut through the air before Miro lost his cool. Several figures leaped in through the factory’s gate. The one who had just spoken—Mellow, the leader of the cat thieves—stood atop a “big dog,” striking a dramatic pose as the others landed behind her.

        “Humph! This isn’t the place for some little furball like you to talk,” Cork sneered, unimpressed by the unexpected guests.

        “Well, we’re here on behalf of your nephew, Teddy,” Mellow declared boldly, showing no fear of Cork’s words of disdain. She turned to Miro and continued, “Leader of the Clawhaven, the dogs were never interested in peace. This entire ‘meeting’ was a trap so they could turn all of you into dogs with a special potion!” 

        Not long ago, Mellow had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their headquarters.

        During the fight that ensued, Tim, Copperfield, Zero, Merbromin, and Fist all turned into dogs because of a spray of a mysterious potion while trying to protect their companions. The unexpected turn of events plunged the cat thieves into sheer panic, but Mellow quickly rallied them, leading them to take down the assassins one by one.

        Later, Teddy revealed the truth: his uncle and the current leader of the Madfang, Cork, had planned to turn all cats in the town into dogs. He tried to rise against his uncle only to lead himself into a life-and-death situation, lying in the wild with wounds all over his body until Mellow found him.

        To thwart Cork’s sinister plan and to find a way to reverse the transformation, the cat thieves split into two teams: one to infiltrate the Madfang’s base and steal the potion and research notes, the other—Mellow, Choux, Wimpy, Ghostie and the “dogified” Zero—to cripple the dogs’ “meeting” with the cats in the abandoned factory.

        “WHAT?” Shocked, Miro looked at Cork, whose darkened expression confirmed Mellow was telling the truth. His fur bristled with rage as he yelled, “Cork, how dare you try to set us up!”

        “Hah! And so what if I do? None of you can escape now!” As soon as Cork let out a loud howl, all the iron gates slammed down, trapping the cats inside the factory.

        Clang! Clang! Clang!

        All the dogs in the factory dropped their pretense, aiming spray guns at the cats. Their eyes burned with visible hostility. Wimpy could not help but tremble violently, his legs bowing inward as fear gripped his tiny frame.

        Unfortunately, his reaction seemed to have entertained one of the dogs standing before him. The dog deliberately stepped forward, pressing the cold barrel of his gun against his waist.

        The cold touch made Wimpy squeal, which only delighted the dog further. He leaned in and growled, “There’s no escape. You’re all becoming dogs today.”

        “No… I-I don’t want to become a dog!” Wimpy’s fear peaked as he heard the dog’s threat, and his instincts took over. He whipped out a few tools and moved his fingers with incredible speed—and in the blink of an eye, he made a lock on the dog’s gun!

        “W-What did you do?” the dog cried, trying to pull the trigger, but it was jammed tight by Whimpy’s lock.

        ‘Th-that’s it! If I just lock all their guns, they won’t be able to spray the potion! And then I won’t turn into a dog!’ The sudden realization ignited a fire within Wimpy. His fear vanished, replaced by a thrill of excitement. He then began darting between the dogs like a whirlwind, locking the dogs’ guns one after one before anyone could stop him.

        “Everyone, assist Wimpy!” Mellow shouted as she noticed Whimpy’s movement. All the cat thieves sprang into action, covering Wimpy as he did his work. The cats from the Clawhaven also joined the fight after realizing Mellow’s group was on their side.

        Thanks to all the cats’ support, Wimpy managed to secure every last spray gun. Yet, the work left him utterly drained—he collapsed as he locked the final gun. Choux immediately rushed over to catch him.

        “Haha… Making locks is so fun… hehe…” Wimpy mumbled deliriously, his cheeks flushed with both fatigue and excitement.

        “Tut! Stupid cats!” Cork growled through his teeth, watching his plan fall. However, he soon regained his composure and sneered, “Just a few locks can’t take me down!”

        With a twisted grin, he took out a small round device and pressed a red button. A mechanical rumble echoed through the factory. Panels in the ceiling slid open to reveal a black void from which descended multiple cannons, their barrels aiming directly at the cats.

        “I knew you cunning felines would get in my way,” Cork sneered, holding up a remote and laughing triumphantly. “Good thing I always have something up my sleeve. Now—DIE!”

        He pressed the green button on the remote—
STORY_2935:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.6

        In an old, abandoned factory not far away from the city center, the cat thieves and the cats of the Clawhaven stood under siege by the Madfang. Multiple cannons protruded from the ceiling, aiming squarely at them. Both parties looked at each other sternly with tension crackling in the air—one spark, and clashes would erupt.

        “These cannons must be loaded with that transformation potion too… Are we really going to let these stupid dogs win?” Choux thought, her heart sinking with despair.

        Not long ago, Mellow had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang, unaware that her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their doorsteps.

        After defeating the assassins, they learned that Teddy’s uncle, Cork, was plotting to turn every cat in the town into dogs. And so, Mellow led Choux, Wimpy, Ghostie, and the “dogified” Zero to cripple the dogs’ “meeting” with the cats in the abandoned factory and ultimately thwart Cork’s sinister scheme.

        They managed to expose Cork’s true intentions to the cats, only to provoke the sinister Dalmatian. Abandoning his pretense, Cork sealed the factory and ordered his pawns to attack the cats with spray guns. To everyone’s surprise, the tables soon turned as Wimpy unleashed his potential in a moment of fear, locking every gun before the dogs could fire it.

        However, Cork was one step ahead of them. He revealed the cannons hidden in the ceiling. All of them were loaded with the transformation potion. All he needed was one spray, and all the cats, with no room to escape, would all turn into dogs.

        ‘No! I refuse to accept this fate! Never!’ Choux shook her head violently. Her pride and fiery spirit surged as she decided to take her fate in her hands, ‘Fine. Then I’ll bet everything I’ve got—on my ultimate skill… cooking!’

        The dire situation somehow turned into the key that unlocked Choux’s potential. She swiftly pulled out a bundle of long rectangular objects from her backpack. With astonishing precision and speed honed through years of culinary mastery, she hurled them toward the cannon muzzles—one, two, ten—jamming every single cannon in under a second, right before Cork pressed the button to release the potion.

        He pressed the green button on the remote—

        However, nothing happened. The factory remained silent. Confused, Cork pressed the button again. Still, nothing happened.
 
        “Why isn’t it WORKING? I just tested this yesterday…”

        ‘Error! Error! Mechanical malfunction detected. Unknown objects detected in cannon muzzles. Firing sequence aborted.’ A robotic voice came from the remote. Cork immediately looked up at one of the cannons, only to see its muzzle clogged with a round, golden-brown object. It was a loaf of bread.

        “YOU did this!” Cork shrieked, glaring at Choux and the other cat thieves surrounded by his subordinates while stomping his foot in frustration.

        “Aha! Nothing beats a good, crusty loaf of dalieba bread! Just hard enough to jam a cannon!” Choux said with a victorious grin.

        “Wait… Where were you hiding all those loaves of bread?” Wimpy asked curiously.

        “Don’t ask. Just know they were a gift from a peace-loving blue entity.”

        “Grrr!” Cork growled through his clenched teeth. Still, he remained undefeated, his eyes flaring with fury. “Even without those spray guns, we are still more than enough to tear you stupid cats apart! ATTACK!”

        “WOOF! WOOF!” The battle cry echoed as the dog threw down their useless spray guns and closed in on the cats with their claws out and teeth bared. A carnage was about to unfold—

        SLAP!

        A cream pie hit one of the dogs right in the face, coating his entire muzzle in a sticky and putrid goo. The smell hit so instantly and violently that it made the dog grimace with agony.

        “I-it… stinks…” the dog gagged. His eyes rolled back as he collapsed to the floor, unconscious.

        “Yes!! I know no one can withstand the power of herring pies!” Choux cheered, then began taking out more foul-smelling pastries from her backpack and throwing them at the dogs. She even handed some off to her mouse chefs, who scurried around distributing pies to the other cats.

        “What… So what about all these pies? Where did they come from?” Wimpy asked out of curiosity again as he blindly hurled a pie at an oncoming dog.

        “Stop asking! I told you—they were from a justice-loving blue entity! He would tell you not to imitate what we are doing because wasting food is shameful!” Choux answered mysteriously.

        Choux’s herring pie assault sent the dogs writhing on the ground, overwhelmed by the stench.

        “Come on! Don’t tell me you’re just going to let them win like this!” Cork shouted in desperation, trying to restore the dogs’ morale with an emotional speech. “They kidnapped your children! Is a little stink strong enough to make you forget your love for them?”

        “...Yeah, they hurt my son… Unforgivable…”
        “...My daughter… Give me back my daughter…”
        “Unforgivable… They must pay…”

        Driven by grief and rage, the dogs pushed through the stench and staggered to their feet, their eyes blazing with vengeance as they slowly advanced again.

        “Tut! I don’t even like you guys. Why can’t you just let us go?” Choux clicked her tongue and grumbled. She and the other cat thieves had no intention of hurting the dogs, knowing very well that they had fallen for Cork’s lies. However, it seemed that mercy was no longer an option. Just as both sides were about to clash—
