        BOOM! BOOM! The factory’s gates shuddered under a powerful impact, then again, and again, until a dent eventually turned into a hole that allowed dozens of small figures to run inside.

        “Papa!”
        “Mama!”
        “Waaah—!”

        The clear, innocent voices of children rang through the room. Everyone turned to see dozens of kittens and puppies, safe and alive, running toward their parents. All the dogs and cats immediately rushed forward, drawing their beloved children into tight, tearful embraces.

        “Whew… We made it just in time,” said Plumpy, wiping sweat from her brow. Fist chivalrously handed her a handkerchief.

        “Wait… What just happened? N-not that I care. I’m just… curious.” Choux asked.

        “Let me explain,” a small dog came and said. It was Teddy, the rightful heir to the Madfang. “My uncle, Cork, was the true kidnapper responsible for all the missing kittens and puppies! He did it to make you all hate the cats, so he could use you to realize his twisted dream of turning every cat into a dog!”
STORY_2936:
Finale of The Master Cathieves - Ch.2

        “So this is the base of the Madfang…” Tim adjusted his glasses, his gaze fixed on an unremarkable building in the distance.

        Not long ago, Mellow—the leader of the cat thieves—had rescued a wounded boy: Teddy, the rightful heir to the dog organization, Madfang. Yet, her act of kindness had drawn the canine assassins to their headquarters.

        A fight ensued during which Tim, Copperfield, Zero, Merbromin, and Fist were sprayed with a mysterious potion that turned them all into dogs while trying to protect their companions. The unexpected turn of events plunged the cat thieves into sheer panic, but Mellow rallied them, leading them to take down the assassins one by one.

        Later, Teddy revealed the truth: his uncle and also the current leader of the Madfang, Cork, had been planning to turn all cats in the town into dogs. He tried to rise against his uncle only to lead himself into a life-and-death situation, lying in the wild with wounds all over his body until Mellow found him.

        To thwart Cork’s sinister plan and to find a way to reverse the transformation, the cat thieves split into two teams: one to infiltrate the Madfang’s base and steal the potion and research notes, the other to cripple the dogs’ plot against the cats. Following Teddy’s lead, the four “dogs”—Copperfield, Fist, and Merbromi—and Plumpy, who remained a cat, made it to the Madfang’s base.

        “How are we supposed to get in? There are guards at the entrance,” Copperfield muttered, squinting toward the main gate where two towering guard dogs sat watch, their eyes sharp and unblinking.

        “There’s a secret passage my aunt once told me about. Not even my uncle knows it exists,” said Teddy, guiding the group to a hidden entrance.

        “There’re too many of us, and we may alert the enemy,” said Tim, stepping up to lead in Mellow’s absence. “Fist, Plumpy—you two stay here and keep watch.”

        “Got it! Just grab that potion and come back as quick as possible—my grilled fish delivery should be arriving at our headquarters soon,” Plumpy grumbled, still thinking about her undelivered food. 

        “Leave it to us,” Fist said tersely, watching as Tim and the others disappeared into the secret passage.

        Just as Teddy promised, the secret passage was both hidden and secure, and they made it safely to a cluttered storage room within the base. Cautiously peeking out the door, Copperfield exhaled in relief as he saw the coast was clear. “No one’s outside. Let’s move.”

        “I’ll take you to the lab,” said Teddy.

        “No, you can’t just walk out there like that,” Tim stopped Teddy. “The dogs here all know who you are. It’s too risky for you to walk out there not knowing who’s friend or foe.”

        “Then what should I do?” Teddy asked with a puzzled frown. Merbromin flashed him a mischievous smile and said, “Leave it to me.”

        Fifteen minutes later, Teddy was transformed into an adorable “girl” dressed in a pink dress. Merbromin looked at him and gave a contented nod, commenting, “You’ve got real potential for this… Ever thought of cross-dressing full-time just like me?”

        “No, thank you,” Teddy retorted flatly, tugging awkwardly at the lace tied around his neck, then stepped out of the storeroom.

        The group quickly moved along the corridor, walking toward their destination—the laboratory. Thanks to their now dogified appearances, they did not catch anyone’s attention until a group of elegant dog ladies approached from the opposite direction.

        “Good. Hey, you, come and help us,” one of them said, waving them over.

        “What now?” Copperfield whispered. Teddy whispered back and said, “That’s my aunt in the middle. The rest are her friends. They might get suspicious if we refuse their request. Let’s play along for now.”

        “I’ll distract them. You guys go,” Copperfield said, gritting his teeth.

        Before anyone knew it, Copperfield stepped forward to greet the ladies. He even performed a little magic trick, eliciting delighted giggles from the group.

        “Let’s go,” Tim said and nudged Teddy and Merbromin toward the laboratory, seizing the opportune moment Copperfield had created for them. Thankfully, they encountered no more dogs and soon arrived at a thick iron door.

        “This is the lab my uncle built for that human,” Teddy said.

        Suddenly, they heard the whirr of machinery from the door. As if responding to Teddy’s voice, a screen on its right lit up. The face of a robotic sentinel appeared, looking right at them as a mechanical voice came from the speaker, “Please say the passcode.”

        “The passcode?” Tim turned to Teddy. “Do you know it?”

        “I-I don’t. My uncle always just walked right in. Now that I think about it, someone inside must’ve opened the door for him…” Teddy replied

        “No passcode, no entry,” the robot intoned coldly.

        ‘Am I going to be stuck in a dog’s body like this forever…? …No! I refuse to stay like this! Even if there’s only a 0.52% chance of success, I have to try it!’ Clenching his paws, Tim decided to take a risk. He asked, “Why do we have to give you a passcode just because you ask for one?”

        “I am A.R.C.077 (Access Regulation Core). It is my responsibility to prevent unauthorized individuals from entering this laboratory.”

        “Yeah? And we’re supposed to just believe you? How do we know what you said is true?” Tim questioned.

        “Humph. Ignorant species. I do not need to prove myself to you,” A.R.C.077 responded, its monotonous voice somehow tinged with a hint of disdain.

        “Heh. So you can’t prove yourself. I wonder what kind of stupid inventor created you—a bucket of bolts with no brains!” Tim commented in a deliberate attempt to provoke the robotic sentinel.

        “Don’t you insult my master!” A.R.C.077 retorted angrily, “I am the greatest artificial intelligence system in this world! I can solve any problem or question!”

        “Oh really?” Tim pointed at Merbromin and asked with a cold sneer, “Then tell me—is that a boy or a girl?”

        “A stinky…” The robotic sentinel’s voice faltered as Merbromin uncorked a strangely smoking vial and poured its content onto the screen.

        Psssssh— A corner of the metal frame melted as soon as a drop of the liquid touched it, releasing a puff of smoke that framed Merbromin’s beautifully painted face.

        “So, what am I?” Merbromin whispered with an impish grin. His face twisted with madness behind the swirling fumes.

        “Y-you are… @#$%#(*%— Unable to compute! Unable to compute!” The robotic sentinel stammered in fear. The system crashed and the door opened.

        “Phew... Can’t believe that worked,” Tim muttered, wiping the cold sweat from his brow.

        “Tim, that was amazing!” Teddy looked at Tim with admiration.

        “Of course! That’s the power of decimals—and a big assist from Merbromin!” Tim beamed, but the victorious grin on his face soon disappeared as Merbromin gave a flirtatious tap on his shoulder. “Enough gloating. Let’s go inside and get that potion,” he purred.

        Inside the lab, Merbromin quickly located the transformation potion. He took a quick sniff of it and said, “Mmm… I see… It shouldn’t be difficult to make the antidote.”

        “That’s great— Hey! There’s something behind the shelf…” said Tim, noticing a silver case hidden in the shadows. He pulled it out and opened it to find another vial—and a stack of photos, each showing a large dog in affectionate poses with various female dogs.

        “That’s my uncle!” Teddy exclaimed, pointing at the dog in the photos. “But I don’t recognize any of these women… Oh no, he’s been cheating on my aunt!”

        “It seems more than that…” Merbromin sniffed the vial. “This is a potion that causes male dogs to become infertile.” 

        “Infertile... cheating... What the hell is this man trying to do?” Tim muttered with a thoughtful frown. However, an earsplitting alarm went off before he could put the pieces together.

        “Dang it! There was a trap under the case—it triggers the alarm when the case isn’t placed in the right place within certain time period,” Tim gritted his teeth in frustration. “That conniving scumbag!”

        “Save the cursing,” Merbromin shouted, “We gotta run!”

        “Right!” Tim hurriedly grabbed Teddy and Merbromin and bolted for the door.
STORY_2937:
One day, two lecherous men dragged a young, beautiful girl out of her home. The girl struggled desperately, but her feeble resistance was, of course, no match for the men’s brute strength. As she was pulled onto the street, an elderly woman staggered out of the house. Clutching onto the hem of the girl’s dress, she pleaded with all her might:

        “Please… Please don’t take away my granddaughter!”

“Old lady, we’re actually doing your granddaughter a favor,” one of the men said. “This town is so poor and backward. She’ll live a much better life if she comes with us to the mountain and becomes our chief’s concubine.”

        “No! I don’t want to go!” The girl screamed, her voice hoarse with desperation. However, all the villagers nearby quietly shut their doors and turned a blind eye lest they become the next target. 

        “You don’t have a say in this—” Unexpectedly, a powerful blow sent the man flying through the air before he could finish his sentence. He hit the ground with a thud and lost consciousness.

        “W-Who are you? M-mind your own business!” The other man stumbled back, glaring defensively at the assailant, a young man.

        “Lü Bu.” The young man arched his bold, thick brows. The sense of unrestrained vigor, unique to teenagers, made his presence all the more commanding. “I can’t stand cowards like you who prey on the weak, bullying women in broad daylight. Fight me instead if you’ve got any balls!”

        “I—” The man could tell Lü Bu was an extraordinary warrior based on the attack earlier. Though fear crept into his voice, he tried to maintain a false bravado. “We’re the Northern Wind brigands! Our chief will hunt you down if you mess with us!”

        “Hah!” Lü Bu scoffed with disdain. “Is that so? Then let him come after me—if you even make it back alive to tell him.”

        Without another word, Lü Bu swung his halberd, slicing the man in two. The grisly sight made the girl and her grandmother shudder in terror, frozen in place.

        “Hey! Is this chief strong?” Lü Bu turned to the girl, who hesitated for a moment before nodding timidly. She said, “V-Very strong. They say he defeated a squad of demons that tried to take over his fortress.”

        “Hahaha! Good! Then let me, Lü Bu, pay him a visit!” Lü Bu grinned wildly and set off immediately after asking the girl for the fortress’s location.

        Half a day later, Lü Bu arrived at the gates of the brigands’ fortress. Without any attempt to conceal himself, he strode boldly into its gates. Strangely, no one stopped him. The gates were unguarded, the pathways eerily empty, and not a single soul could be seen within the building.

        As confusing as the situation was, Lü Bu shrugged off his doubts and marched straight into the main hall. As he stepped inside, a striking figure caught his eye—a young man dressed in crimson robes, holding a large calligraphy brush, stood silently before the chief’s desk.

        Even from behind, Lü Bu could feel the man’s overwhelming power and presence. His blood surged with excitement as he gripped his halberd tightly and called out, “You must be the brigands’ chief! I am Lü Bu, and I’ve come to challenge you!”

        “Wait! I’m not—”
        “Take this!”

        Lü Bu charged, refusing to give the young man a chance to explain. He raised his halberd high and brought it down in a thunderous strike, forcing the young man to lift his giant brush to block the attack.

        The clash of metal and wood echoed through the hall as the two exchanged blows in rapid succession. In mere moments, the two had crossed weapons dozens of times, testing each other’s strength with every strike.

        The young attempted to clarify himself, only to let Lü Bu’s relentless attacks kindle his fighting spirit. Gradually, his movements became sharper, his blows increasingly cunning, leaving several fresh, bleeding wounds on Lü Bu’s body. Surprisingly, the young boy only laughed in exhilaration. His strikes grew wilder and more ferocious as he was fueled by the thrill of combat and the razor’s edge between life and death, 

        However, an unexpected intruder disrupted the high-stakes duel.

        “You damned Xian! I, the chief of the Northern Wind Brigands, will never bow to you! Prepare to die!” Emerging from the shadows was none other than the true leader of the brigands. He had been lurking in the dark, planning to use all his forces to ambush the Xian whom the Heavenly Kingdom sent to eradicate his fortress.

        “So, you’re a Xian?” Lü Bu, though irritated at having his thrilling battle interrupted, reluctantly lowered his halberd and frowned at the young man.

        “Yes. My name is Tongtian Jiaozhu, though I’m sure you sensed something was off from the start,” Tongtian Jiaozhu replied with a sly arch of his brow, a playful smirk on his lips.

        “I don’t care who you are—if you’re strong, I’ll fight you!”

        “Hahaha, you’re stubborn, and I like it,” Tongtian Jiaozhu said with a laugh, then gestured toward the encroaching bandits. “But what now?”

        “Humph, a fight I start is a fight I’ll finish!” Lü Bu let out a wild laugh, hefting his halberd as he charged into the bandits and delivered a series of merciless strikes. Blood splattered in every direction, fueling the frenzy of the fight.

        Tongtian Jiaozhu joined in without missing a beat, and the two fought with a seamless synergy despite it being the first day they had met. Though outnumbered by hundreds, their combined strength kept the tide of bandits at bay.

        The cries of the bandits echoed through the fortress. Their blood soaked the dirt and stones, painting the ground crimson. Lü Bu and Tongtian Jiaozhu, though drenched in the blood of their enemies, wore exhilarated smiles, as if they had transcended the fear of life and death. Their overwhelming presence struck terror into the hearts of the brigands, and some dropped their weapons and fled in panic.

        One deserter quickly led to another, and soon the brigands were scattering like leaves in the wind, desperate to escape the two battle maniacs as fast as they could. The chief, frantic to restore order, tried to rally his men, but Lü Bu ended his efforts with a single, devastating thrust of his halberd, impaling him through the chest. The chief’s eyes widened in shock, frozen with disbelief and bitter hatred as he crumpled to the ground. With their leader slain, the remaining brigands all lost their will to fight and fled.

        “Phew… I’m exhausted…” With the enemies gone, Tongtian Jiaozhu let out a heavy sigh of relief and sank to the ground. The relentless battles had sapped his strength and pushed him to his very limit. Digging into his robes, he retrieved two small white porcelain bottles and casually tossed one to Lü Bu.

        “Here, take a swig.”

        “What’s this?” Lü Bu asked, catching the bottle.

        “It’s the brigand chief’s prized stash. I’ve already tried it—it’s top-notch, the best kind for a celebration. Cheers to our victory,” Tongtian Jiaozhu said, throwing his head back to take a hearty gulp.

        Lü Bu found it almost unbelievable, seeing how carefree and unrestrained Tongtian Jiaozhu was. The gods he had encountered before were invariably arrogant and self-righteous, looking down on all others while viewing demons as sworn enemies. Yet, this Xian before him turned out to be a man of great magnanimity. He treated Lü Bu not with disdain or prejudice, but as an equal, a comrade bound by shared battle. For the first time in a long while, Lü Bu felt the pressure in his heart slightly lifted.

        With the tension in his brow released, he lifted the porcelain bottle and followed Tongtian Jiaozhu’s example, tilting his head back for a deep, unrestrained drink.

        “Good, good! That’s the spirit!” Tongtian Jiaozhu exclaimed with a wide grin. Then, he disappeared briefly into the chief’s quarters, rummaging around before returning triumphantly with more fine wine. The two drank side by side, their unrestrained camaraderie filling the air with shared laughter. This day marked the beginning of a rare and genuine friendship that eventually became a bond of sworn brotherhood through countless life-and-death battles afterward…
STORY_2939:
In the vast open plains, a bronze-skinned maiden with long, silvery hair knelt by a towering ancient tree. At its base lay a small mound of earth, beneath which rested the body of a lioness she had loved like family.

        The maiden’s name was Inanna, a young woman from a nearby tribe who studied under Anu, an Ancient God. Every day, she would wander the plains after her lessons, allowing the solitude of nature to help her untangle the wisdom she had learned. 

        One fateful evening, Inanna’s path crossed with a lioness and her two cubs surrounded by a pride of hostile lions. Without hesitation, she stepped in and saved them. From that day forward, the lioness and her cubs followed her, and Inanna, moved by their loyalty, took them in, allowing them to become an inseparable part of her life, a family bound by fate.

        However, a lion’s lifespan is far shorter than a human’s, and before long, the lioness succumbed to the passage of time. Inanna buried her beneath the ancient tree, but no mound of soil could bury the grief that consumed her.

        It was Inanna’s first taste of the bitter pain of loss. Day after day, she returned to the grave and wept until her tears ran dry. She could not eat or sleep; everything seemed to fade into grey under the leaden weight of her sorrow.

        The cubs, Alfie and Lily, felt Inanna’s anguish. They followed her wherever she went, refusing to leave her side even as hunger gnawed at their bellies. Together, the three of them spiraled deeper into exhaustion, their spirits dimming like a flame starved of air.

        And it was in this frail state that they drew the attention of a predator. A lion, ever watchful for prey, set its eyes on them. As Inanna and the cubs mourned beneath the tree, the lion summoned its pride and quietly encircled them, and it was too late by the time Inanna realized the danger.

        The leader of the pride let out a thunderous roar to signal the attack. The lions charged. On any other day, Inanna could have easily summoned the elements and conjured a shield to protect them. Yet, days of starvation and exhaustion had robbed her of strength, and she could only watch as the lions closed in—

        “ROAR!”

        A fierce growl shattered the air—not from the attacking lions, but from Alfie and Lily. It turned out that the two cubs leapt forward, placing themselves between Inanna and the prowling lions despite their unmatured bodies.

        However, the pride was too strong. As the clash dragged on, the cubs’ injuries multiplied. Blood stained their fur, and their movements grew sluggish. Watching them struggle made Inanna’s heart ache with guilt.

        ‘No! Please—don’t take them away from me too! I can’t bear to lose anyone else!’ Inanna’s mind cried out in desperation.

        Fortunately, her plea was answered. A sudden wind swept across the plains—Dumuzi arrived. Summoning his power, he called upon the elements, turning the air and earth into a swirling tempest. The pride scattered under the might of his magic. The leader of the pride, though reluctant, ultimately retreated with its kin as its instincts prevailed.

        “Inanna, are you hurt?” Dumuzi hurried to her side, his voice filled with concern.

        “I’m fine,” she said, her voice trembling as she clutched Dumuzi’s arm. “But Alfie and Lily—they’re hurt! Please, help them!”

        Reassured that Inanna was unharmed, Dumuzi turned his attention to the cubs. Their wounds, though bloody, were shallow. Watching as he quickly healed them and restored their strength, Inanna let out a shaky breath of relief.

        “Inanna, I know how much you’re hurting,” Dumuzi said gently, brushing a strand of her silvery hair aside as he gazed at the lioness’s grave. “But you can’t let the grief consume you. She wouldn’t have wanted to see you like this. And Alfie and Lily… they need you.”

        “I…” Inanna looked at the cubs, and they gazed back at her, their eyes filled with a quiet understanding. They nuzzled her hand, offering a gentle, wordless comfort with their warm fur.

        ‘Dumuzi’s right. I have to be strong,’ she thought. ‘For them. For the family I still have.’

        “Alfie… Lily…” Inanna’s voice cracked as she pulled the cubs into her arms. All the regret and grief she harbored burst forth in a torrent of tears as she whispered, “I’m sorry… I’m so sorry…”

        From that day forward, though the ache of the lioness’s absence never truly left her, Inanna no longer let herself wallow in sorrow. She rose and continued to live for both herself and the family that remained by her side…
STORY_2940:
The summer sun blazed like an unforgiving furnace, casting waves of heat over the earth. Even a few minutes outdoors were enough to leave one drenched in sweat, so one could only imagine the misery of a man, a woman, and two dragons—one white, one red—trekking through the thick, suffocating forest.

        This peculiar group included Sunnie the Gourmet Hunter, Colin the White Dragon Rider, and their respective dragon companions—Wilson the red dragon and Saxon the white dragon. Sunnie had first crossed paths with Colin in the most chaotic circumstances—she had stumbled into a battlefield and accidentally sabotaged his meticulously crafted plans. Furious, Colin chased her down to demand recompense. But somehow, in a twist of fate, Sunnie managed to recruit him as a companion on her quest for legendary delicacies.

        After failing to track down the elusive Ithaca pigs, Sunnie set her sights on the northern region, where the mythical golden apple was said to grow. Yet, the journey was long and grueling, and they had only made it halfway despite days of travel.

        “I’m starving… and it’s so hot…” Sunnie groaned, dragging her feet as though weighed down by invisible stones. The girl who usually brimmed with infectious energy now looked utterly defeated, weak like a wilted plant. Her voice was barely more than a whimper as she said, “I can’t… Colin, Colin, I can’t walk anymore… Let’s take a break…”

        Colin stopped and turned to face her, his forehead glistening with sweat. For someone as fastidious as he was, it was an unbearable affront to his dignity, so he agreed and said, 
“Fine. My back’s completely soaked, and I can’t stand it. I see there’s a stream nearby—let’s go there so I can freshen up.”

        “No… I don’t have the strength to walk over there… I’m so hungry, I feel like my stomach’s been boiled dry… I need food right now…” Sunnie whined, clutching her growling belly. Even Wilson landed beside her, mimicking her movements as if to show solidarity.

        “What—” Colin gave her a look of pure disbelief, as if Sunnie were some kind of monster. He shook his head in exasperation and asked, “You ate five bowls of rice and an entire spread of side dishes. Your appetite scared everyone at the inn. And now, you’re telling me that you’re hungry just three hours later? What… What is your stomach even made of?”

        Sunnie innocently beamed at him. “It’s just an ordinary stomach!”

        “Forget it. Saxon and I will head to the stream while you and Wilson go find some food.” Colin sighed, realizing it was a futile endeavor to understand the fathomless nature of  Sunnie’s appetite. 

        By the time Colin returned from the stream, feeling refreshed and in a much better mood, he saw Sunnie sitting in the shade with food in both of her hands. The aroma of delicacies filled the air, making Wilson drool uncontrollably, his tongue nearly dragging on the ground.

        The sight left Colin puzzled. He had only gone for a few minutes. How did Sunnie even get her hands on so much food? He frowned. “Where did all this food come from?”

        “Mmmph…” Sunnie swallowed a mouthful of chicken, pointed toward a massive tree in the distance, and said, “I found it under that big tree over there. Someone must’ve forgotten to take it with them. It’s so hot, you know? If I didn’t eat it, it’d have gone bad. I was doing them a favor!”  

        “Why would someone leave so much food there…” Colin’s frown deepened as he walked closer to the tree and squinted. Beneath its massive trunk, he spotted a small stone altar piled with offerings. His heart sank. Slowly, he turned back to Sunnie, his voice low and urgent. “That’s not someone’s forgotten picnic. Those are offerings for the ancient tree spirit!”

        But his warning came too late.

        The air suddenly shifted. The treetops shivered despite the absence of wind. Shadows pooled across the ground like ink seeping into the earth. Sunnie and Wilson froze in place, their bodies stiffening as dark, wooden patterns began to creep across their skin. Their arms and faces slowly hardened into bark, their expressions frozen in the exact moment they had been mid-bite into a drumstick.

        “Hey! What’s happening? I can’t move!” Sunnie cried out, her voice filled with panic.

        “I am the spirit of the ancient tree,” a deep voice echoed through the forest. “Those who steal my offerings shall face punishment.”

        “Indeed, they’re guilty, but they didn’t mean any harm. Can’t you forgive them just this once?” Colin raised his head to plead with the spirit.

        A long silence hung in the air before the spirit finally replied, “Very well. Since their actions were not born of malice, I shall give them a chance. A rogue cursed vine has been strangling my true form, feeding on my power for days, yet I can’t get rid of it. I will lift their curse as soon as you remove it for me.”

        “Deal!” Colin said without hesitation, but the confidence on his face instantly crumbled when he arrived at the spirit’s true form. There, he saw a grotesque vine, as thick as a python, wrap around the tree’s trunk with a foul, sticky liquid dripping to the ground in nauseating globs. The stench was so vile that it made Colin’s face contort in revulsion. 

        “That’s… disgusting. I don’t want to touch it. ” He turned to Saxon. “Saxon, why don’t you just burn the whole thing down?”

        “No! Absolutely not!” the spirit sharply interrupted. “Using fire will damage my body. You must remove it by hand.”

        “BY HAND?” Colin’s voice cracked as he repeated the spirit’s words. He shook his head vigorously and said, “No way! We’re not doing that!”

        “I’d rather fight an entire army than touch that thing…” Saxon muttered, recoiling in disgust.

        “Wh-what now? So Wilson and I are just going to stay wooden forever?” Sunnie wailed. “Does that mean I’ll never eat again? Nooooo! This is the worst thing that’s ever happened to me!”

        Wilson howled alongside her, their combined cries so loud that it made both Colin and Saxon clutch their heads in agony. Eventually, Colin snapped, throwing up his hands as he roared, “Fine! Fine! We’ll do it!”

        Grumbling under his breath, Colin donned every piece of clothing he could find, while Saxon reluctantly followed suit. Slowly, they approached the ancient tree and began peeling the cursed vine away. Each strand he pulled off splattered him with more of the vile, sticky liquid. The overpowering stench made him gag repeatedly, and his vision blurred. Meanwhile, Saxon used his tail to sweep away the loosened vines, but even he could not avoid getting coated in the vile goo.

        ‘UGH! This is all that idiot’s fault!’ Colin fumed inwardly as he yanked another vine loose. “Once this is over, I’m going to make her regret eating that food!”

        “Colin! Watch out!” Sunnie’s shout jolted him out of his angry thoughts. It turned out that the cursed vine, sensing its doom, lashed out in a final act of desperation. It coiled its tendrils into sharp, blade-like shapes and struck at Colin with ferocious speed.

        Shing!

        Fortunately, Colin’s reflexes kicked in. His sword flashed in the air as he struck, severing the deadly tendrils in one swift motion. The vine let out an unearthly shriek before disintegrating into a wisp of black mist.

        “Thank you for freeing me from that cursed vine,” the tree spirit said. As it cast a light upon Sunnie and Wilson, the wooden patterns on their skin slowly disappeared, and they found themselves able to move again.

        “I’m back!” Sunnie cried, leaping forward to give Colin a hug. “Thank you, Colin! You’re the be—”

        However, she froze mid-sentence as the stench hit her. Her face turned pale. She recoiled, gagging violently. “Ugh… Wh-what is that smell?”

        With his face turning an alarming shade of red, Colin mumbled through his clenched teeth, “Are you thanking me or insulting me?”

        “I’m really grateful, I swear!” Sunnie yelped, frantically stuffing mint leaves into her nose while scurrying to Wilson’s back for cover.  “But you know, my nose has limits…”

        “I’m going to take a bath!” Colin bellowed and stomped off toward the river.

        Saxon sighed heavily and followed him. “I’m coming too.”

        “I’ll have food ready when you get—”

        “No, you won’t!” Colin shouted back as he stormed away.
STORY_2941:
Bathing in the pool, Elizabeth traced delicate lines in the water with her fingers, a sweet smile playing on her lips. Shrouded in a veil of steam, her fair, alabaster skin glowed with an otherworldly allure that could entrance any man.

        Carefully and tenderly, she scrubbed every inch of her flawless skin. She was preparing for something special—for today was a day to be remembered.

        From behind, Jack approached her silently. Gently, he lifted her chin with his fingers. Elizabeth languidly turned to him, wrapping her arms around his neck and pulling him close. With the softest whisper in his ear, she asked, “Darling, do you know what day it is?”

        Jack smiled and said, “Of course. It’s the anniversary of our 10,000th kiss.”

        Then he leaned in and captured her lips with his own. Elizabeth, naturally, returned the kiss with fervor. Their breaths intertwined as the kiss deepened, and the steam in the bathroom seemed to thicken, cloaking them in an intimate warmth.

        It was after a rather long moment of shared passion that Elizabeth gently pushed Jack away. Her eyes sparkled with affection as she said playfully, “Slow down, my dear. Our date’s after dusk. I need time to get everything ready.”

        “Of course, my love,” Jack planted a soft kiss on her cheek before taking his leave. “I’ll look forward to your surprise tonight.”

        Once her bath was done, Elizabeth made her way to the dining room. She decorated the space with care. Yet as she stood at the doorway, surveying her work, she frowned.

        “This is too plain,” she muttered to herself. “It needs more color… and flowers. A bouquet of roses—roses as red as blood.”

        Determined to make the evening perfect, Elizabeth went to the flower shop and got a bouquet of fresh crimson roses in her arms. On her way back, she let her thoughts wander, her heart brimming with excitement for the date. However, a sharp, whistling sound sliced through the air and interrupted her musings.

        Her instincts flared as danger approached. Without thinking, she conjured two wings of blood, unfurling them in front of her as a shield.

        The next moment, a bullet slammed into one of her wings with such force that it nearly pierced through, sending her stumbling backward. The bouquet fell from her arms, causing the crimson petals to scatter across the ground.

        Elizabeth steadied herself, her eyes narrowing as she scanned her surroundings. But before she could fight back, a second bullet tore through the air, striking the exact spot where her wing had yet to recover.

        She moved swiftly, dodging just in time. Still, the bullet grazed her arm, leaving a thin trail of blood.

        “Humph, coward,” Elizabeth hissed, masking her fury with a smile that did not reach her eyes. Those eyes, however, glinted with deadly malice.

        Following the trajectory of the bullet and the faint scent of gunpowder, she spread her wings wide and took off in pursuit of her assailant. Her chase led her to an abandoned red-brick house. However, she did not enter the building. Instead, she used her powers to amplify the size of her bloody wings.

        With a single, sweeping motion, she slashed her wings through the air.

        [i]Boom![/i]

        The house split cleanly down the middle, collapsing in a cloud of dust and debris. As a figure frantically stumbled out of the building, coughing, Elizabeth conjured a rain of blood-made spears, pinning him against the wall—it was a man in glasses, his eyes gleaming with a manic light.

        “Who are you?” Elizabeth demanded coldly. “And why did you attack me?”

        The man let out a deranged laugh. “As long as you’re gone… Lisa will finally be happy.”

        “Lisa? Who is th—” Elizabeth frowned, but before she could ask further, a strange dizziness overcame her. Her knees buckled, and she fell to the ground. Her spears dissolved, freeing her attacker.

        “The poison’s finally working, huh?” the man said callously.

        Elizabeth’s mind raced. She recalled the second bullet that had grazed her arm. “You poisoned the bullet…”

        Unrestrained, the man walked toward her while pulling a gun from his waistband and pointing it at her. “For Lisa’s happiness, you must die.”

        Then he pulled the trigger.

        [i]Clang![/i]

        A knife flew from above and deflected the bullet. In the same instant, someone landed between Elizabeth and the man.

        “Jack!” Elizabeth exclaimed in surprise. But Jack’s eyes did not light up with joy as he saw her. His expression darkened as soon as his gaze fell on her wounded form. With his eyes burning with fury, he turned to the man and growled, “Midgley, what do you think you’re doing?”

        “Everything I’ve done is for Lisa! She came to see you, yet you’re in love with [i]her[/i]!” Midgley said with twisted madness. “If I kill her, Lisa will finally be happy!”

        Jack’s patience snapped. He raised his voice, “That’s nonsense! Lisa loves [i]you[/i]!”

        Midgley froze in disbelief. “That’s impossible! She looked so happy when she wrote that letter to you!”

        “...That’s because she was writing about you, you idiot!” Fed up with Midgley’s stubbornness, Jack took out a knife and strode, pressing it against Midgley’s throat as he demanded, “I don’t care what has happened between you and Lisa. Just give me the antidote NOW!”

        “...Did Lisa really say that she loved me?” Midgley obstinately asked despite that Jack’s knife had left a cut on his skin.

        “Go ask her yourself!” Jack growled.

        “Here!” Midgley hastily tossed a vial to Jack before running away.

        Jack immediately gave the antidote to Elizabeth, who recovered within moments. She looked at him, her expression a mix of exhaustion and curiosity. She asked, “What was all that about?”

        Jack took her hands—soft but cold—in his. His grip was so firm yet gentle, as though trying to convey a thousand unspoken words. He then told her everything—about his time of amnesia, about Lisa, and about the accident where he mistook Lisa for her because of their resemblance.

        Sorrow flickered briefly within Elizabeth’s eyes, and it made Jack’s chest tighten, so he immediately apologized, “I’m sorry… I hate myself for hurting you.”

        Elizabeth shook her head, her brows furrowed. “No, I’m not upset because of that. I’m upset because I wasn’t there with you when so many important things happened.”

        “You don’t blame me?”

        “You were searching for me, even when you didn’t remember me. That proves your heart has always been mine,” Elizabeth said, her eyes holding only compassion but not a single hint of doubt.

        Elizabeth’s words made Jack’s heart bubble with emotions. 

        [i]She just gets him. She always does.[/i]

        Overwhelmed by her unwavering trust, he lifted her hands, now warm in his grasp, and kissed them tenderly. 

        “Of course,” he murmured. “I’ve always been yours.”
STORY_2942:
Traveling across the vast lands of Tarones, Jackie often spent nights under the open sky. On this particular evening, she sat by the bonfire as usual. The fire elements, sensing her solitude, gathered around her and conjured memories of her past, reminding her of the warmth of days gone by…

        It happened in one of the winters. Jackie spotted a familiar figure—a boy—when she stepped out of her house. Unexpectedly, snow started falling. The boy shivered slightly as he read the book in his hands.

        “What are you doing here?” Jackie asked, feigning indifference. She knew full well why Stephen, the teenage boy before her, was standing there—waiting to walk to work with her.

        “I’ve been reading this wonderful poetry collection. The lines… they really spoke to me. I wanted to share them with you.” Stephen closed the book and turned to look at her, his eyes brimming with enthusiasm and sincerity.

        “I’m not interested,” Jackie replied curtly, flicking her sleeve dismissively. Stephen had confessed his feelings for Jackie, but she turned him down. Ever since then, most of her words to him carried a cold edge.

        “I figured you’d say that,” Stephen said. “So I wrote them down for you instead. You can read them when you feel like it.” Before Jackie could respond, Stephen slipped the manuscript into her pouch. She didn’t bother to take it out, and the two quietly made their way to the post office.

        As they arrived at the post office entrance, they saw a familiar old man carrying a heavy basket. Stephen quickly stepped forward and took the basket from him. As he held the door open, he asked with a cheerful grin, “Uncle Sam! Here to send your granddaughter another letter?” 

        “Yes, her birthday is coming soon,” the old man replied. “I’ve put together a big package for her.”
        The basket was filled with beautifully wrapped gifts, their colorful paper glinting under the light. Seeing the thoughtful effort he had made, the other postmen joined the conversation. Their cheerful laughter soon filled the post office with a heartwarming air.

        “Oh, by the way! Isn’t Stephen’s birthday coming up next week?” one of Jackie’s colleagues suddenly recalled while organizing the mail. Stephen, who was still helping Uncle Sam prepare the package, didn’t hear the comment, so everyone else quietly agreed to plan a surprise party for him.

        “His birthday…” Jackie murmured to herself. For some reason, the image of Stephen writing poetry popped into her mind—how he would often retreat to a quiet corner of the office during breaks, scribbling down his thoughts with his quill.

        Soon, Stephen’s birthday arrived. Everyone waited in the office, prepared to surprise him. As he returned from his mail deliveries and pushed open the door, they jumped out with a cake in hand and greeted him with cheers.

        Stephen beamed with joy as he accepted their heartfelt blessings. Laughter and chatter echoed in the post office as they spent the afternoon celebrating together. When the day came to an end and their colleagues started heading home, only Jackie and Stephen remained behind. Just as Jackie was about to leave, Stephen called out to her.

        “I found something on my desk today,” he said, holding up a fountain pen. “I think it’s a gift for me, but there’s no name on it—just a handwritten note that says ‘Happy Birthday.’”

        Jackie turned back, her eyes drawn to the pen in his hand. Her heart skipped a beat, but before she could say anything, Stephen continued, “But it’s broken.”

        Feigning nonchalance, Jackie grabbed an envelope from a nearby desk and handed it to him. “Is that so? Try it again.”

        Stephen immediately unscrewed the pen’s cap and drew a few strokes on the envelope. “Look, no ink,” he said, holding it up.

        “That’s impossible…” Jackie stepped closer, taking his hand to adjust the angle of his grip. “See? Now it’s working—”

        She stopped mid-sentence as she looked up and realized how close they were. Stephen gave her a warm smile. Flustered, Jackie quickly turned away.

        “Thank you to the mysterious gift giver,” Stephen said with a teasing lilt in his voice. “Her handwriting was beautiful. I’ll make sure to write more poems for her.”

        ‘I shouldn’t have written anything at all,’ Jackie thought, her face glowing crimson in embarrassment. She avoided his gaze and hurried to the door without speaking another word, while Stephen followed her, grinning from ear to ear.

        Back then, Jackie thought these peaceful days would last forever. Little did she know that they would soon fade into bittersweet memories, slipping away like the snow melting under the sun…
STORY_2943:
Belle’s family ran an inn in the countryside. Recently, a young merchant arrived and rented a room. His name was Sam. With his charming demeanor and eloquent speech, he quickly won the favor of the entire village—young and old, men and women. The young women, in particular, were especially enamored with him.

        “I made this… Please, try it…”

        Belle spoke softly, her voice barely above a whisper, like the hum of a gnat. Her cheeks flushed as she placed a steaming bowl of stew on Sam’s table. When he flashed her a dazzling smile, her heart raced, and she quickly fled back to the kitchen, too shy to stay near him. She only dared to make such a bold gesture because her parents were away.

        ‘Was that too forward of me? Did he like it? I added honey to the stew this time… Will it suit his taste?'

        Her thoughts ran wild as she nervously peeked out from behind the kitchen door, watching Sam. Only when she saw him take bite after bite, seemingly enjoying the meal, did she let out a deep sigh of relief.

        Just then, the soup on the stove began to bubble over, hissing loudly as it spilled onto the floor. Startled, Belle rushed to clean up the mess.

        “Need a helping hand?” Sam suddenly appeared at the kitchen door, a playful smile on his face.

        “No… no… I can handle it,” Belle stammered. Her cheeks burned as she turned her face away and avoided his gaze. Sam, however, seemed amused by her reaction and didn’t leave. Instead, he struck up another conversation.

        “Oh, by the way, the food was delicious. Honey dishes are quite popular in the city right now.”

        “Really?” Belle’s eyes lit up with excitement. The brightness in her gaze seemed to catch Sam off guard.

        The two began talking enthusiastically about the culinary wonders of the city. As Sam described the intricate and magical dishes, Belle couldn’t help but feel a deep longing to experience it all for herself. Sam went on to paint vivid pictures of how gorgeous the city was: enormous plazas, dazzling clothing, and a bustling, glamorous life. Everything he said made Belle’s imagination run wild.

        “If only I could live in the city,” she murmured wistfully.

        “Why not go there yourself?” Sam said softly as he stepped closer to her.

        “But…” Belle’s words trailed off, her mind a chaotic swirl of thoughts as Sam drew nearer. Her heart raced madly, not just from his words but also from his proximity.

        He reached out and gently brushed a strand of hair from her face, his gaze warm and intense. The heat in his eyes sent a shiver through her, and she reflexively stepped back. But before she could retreat further, he pulled her into his sturdy arms.

        “What…”

        “You don’t like it?” Sam’s voice was low and tender, his eyes locked onto hers. Belle was at a loss for words. His face was so close that the cool tip of his nose almost touched hers, and she could almost hear the steady rhythm of his heartbeat.

        “What… what are you doing…” Before she could finish, Sam leaned in and kissed her. For a moment, she froze in surprise, but soon she melted into the kiss.

        When their lips finally parted, Belle was breathless, her cheeks flushed. Sam grinned mischievously, while Belle lowered her head, avoiding his gaze. Yet, her heart swelled with sweetness. Though no words were spoken, Belle was certain she had become Sam’s lover.

        That night, Belle lay in bed, her thoughts consumed by dreams of the city. She imagined a life with Sam, side by side, in a bustling metropolis. Her heart burned with a fervor she had never felt before—a fire of excitement and longing.

        The next day, Belle gazed at Sam with adoration as he skillfully pitched his product to a customer. She didn’t fully understand what he was selling—some kind of potion that claimed to accelerate crop growth—but it didn’t matter. She was captivated by his charm and eloquence.

        After the customer left, Belle approached Sam with a glass of warm water, her eyes brimming with affection. Her parents, however, noticed the change in her demeanor and frowned in concern. Little did they know a pair of envious and malicious eyes was watching them from the shadows.

        Sam’s business in the village flourished, but soon rumors began to spread like wildfire. It was whispered that Belle had seduced Sam with her body. As the gossip grew more outlandish, some even claimed she had used her charms to entice other men as well.

        Belle’s parents were frantic, like cats on a hot tin roof. In a small village like this, such rumors could ruin a woman’s reputation forever. Though they had initially liked Sam, they knew he wouldn’t stay in the village for long. Besides, the last thing they wanted was to let their daughter leave with this man.

        “Sam! What should I do? My parents want to marry me off to a foolish farmer—” Belle burst into Sam’s room, her voice filled with desperation. But she stopped short when she saw him packing his belongings.

        “You… you’re leaving?” she asked.

        “My business here is done. It’s time for me to go back to the city. I’m leaving tonight,” Sam replied calmly.

        “But what about me? What will I do after you’re gone?”

        Seeing her the distraught look on her face, Sam set down his bag and took her hand in his. Smiling, he slipped a silver ring onto her middle finger.

        “Come with me. I’ll take you to the city tonight. We’ll go together. I love you.”

        Belle had never imagined that a single sentence could bring her such overwhelming joy. Tears streamed down her face as she nodded fervently, unable to speak through her sobs.

        That night, the two of them slipped away from the village under the cover of darkness. Belle took one last look at the place she had called home, but Sam’s gaze gave her the courage to move forward.

        “Once we’ve settled, I’ll give you a grand wedding,” Sam said with a smile that made Belle’s heart soar.

        But Belle knew nothing of the truth. Little did she know that the potion Sam had sold would soon be exposed as completely ineffective, and he would squander all the money he had earned in the village. And the life Belle had imagined? What awaited her in the city was nothing but the harsh reality…
STORY_2944:
Jack was cheerfully selecting clothes from his closet.

        Today marked the anniversary of Jack and Elizabeth’s 10,000th kiss, and the two had planned a special celebration. Naturally, Jack wanted to be well-prepared. However, just as he was deciding on an outfit, a strong, acrid smell wafted in from outside, causing him to frown.

        “Something’s burning…”

        Setting down the clothes, Jack followed the smell to the castle’s backyard garden. There, he found an unusual sight: one of the pumpkin triplets was tied to a wooden stake while a roaring fire blazed beneath him.

        “Burn him! Burn him!”

        The two younger pumpkins danced gleefully around the stake, torches in hand, their faces lit with bizarre delight.

        “What did he do?” Jack asked, finding the scene both peculiar and amusing.

        The two pumpkins turned to him and said indignantly, “He was chatting with a girl on the street! And worse, she said he was cute! It’s already unbearable watching you and Elizabeth flaunt your love in front of us! We must burn him today!”

        “You’re just jealous!” the eldest pumpkin screamed, twisting and wriggling against the ropes.

        “No, we’re not!” the younger two shouted in unison. “We’re the avengers of all the single people!”

        “Oh, does that mean you’re taking revenge on me and Elizabeth as well?” Jack said, chuckling as he pulled out a knife and toyed with it near his lips. His voice carried a playful, yet unmistakable hint of menace that sent a chill through the pumpkins.

        The two younger pumpkins froze for a moment, then sprang into action. Thankfully, they were loyal enough to untie their older brother before bolting like the wind.

        “I was only joking, but their reactions were way over the top.” Jack shook his head, chuckling softly. 

        Just as Jack turned to head back to his room, he stopped abruptly when something caught his eye in the fire. Amid the burning debris, a white object stood out. Curious, Jack bent down and retrieved it from the flames. It was a half-burned letter—and it was addressed to him.

        Though much of the letter was destroyed, the signature remained intact, revealing the sender’s identity: Lisa, the scholar.

        Jack’s thoughts drifted back to a time when he had lost his memory and stayed in Lisa’s laboratory. Mistaking Lisa for Elizabeth, due to her icy, pale skin and striking blue hair, he had clung to her during that difficult time.

        Though Lisa had often appeared cold and indifferent, she had quietly cared for him in countless small ways. Yet, their parting had been anything but amicable; it was a memory that still weighed upon him.

        From the remaining portion of the letter, Jack learned that Lisa wanted to meet him. Fortunately, the date and location were still legible, and the meeting was set for today at noon. He still had plenty of time before his evening date with Elizabeth.

        “I owe her an apology,” Jack thought, recalling the image of Lisa’s tear-streaked face during their farewell. A pang of guilt and faint heartache stirred within him.

        When Jack arrived near the meeting place, he saw a familiar yet distant figure. Lisa stood there with her back facing him. Jack approached slowly and stopped at a respectful distance.

        “Lisa,” he called softly. She turned to face him, her expression calm and composed, as though she had never let out those heart-wrenching screams and cries during their farewell.

        For a moment, Jack was at a loss for words. The face before him, so similar to Elizabeth’s, left him uncharacteristically flustered. Seeing his rare unease, Lisa broke into a lighthearted laugh.

        Her laughter eased Jack’s taut nerves, bringing a faint smile to his lips.

        “Have you found her?” Lisa asked gently. “The woman you love?”

        “…Yes, I’ve found her.” Jack’s expression softened immediately at the thought of Elizabeth. “And haven’t you found someone as well? In your letter, you said you’d found the love of your life.”

        A rosy flush rose to Lisa’s fair cheeks. “Yes, after you left, he’s been by my side ever since. I didn’t want to keep him waiting anymore. When I heard that Fort Stirling would pass through this city, I decided to write to you—to say goodbye to my past self.”

        Jack closed his eyes briefly, then opened them and said earnestly, “I’m glad you’ve moved on. Still, I owe you for the way things ended. If you ever need help in the future, you can come to me.”

        “Thank you.” Lisa smiled softly. Though she accepted his offer, she knew in her heart she would never use it. “Goodbye, Jack.”

        Jack nodded, saying nothing more as he watched Lisa unregretfully turn and walk away until her figure disappeared into the bustling streets.

        Seeing Lisa’s happiness brought a bittersweet feeling to Jack’s heart, and he found himself missing Elizabeth more than ever. 

        Just as he eagerly turned to head back to the castle, however, he heard a deafening explosion from a nearby alley. The sharp scent of blood that followed sent an ominous chill through Jack’s body.

        “Elizabeth… I need to go and see if it’s her!” Without hesitation, he broke into a sprint, racing towards the source of the sound—
STORY_2945:
After the war against Odin, the demons abandoned Todd—who had repeatedly spiraled out of control—on the battlefield. The curse they had inflicted upon him still lingered, forcing Todd to rely on dreams to suppress the chaos within his body. That day, after a brutal battle with the remaining enemies, Todd lay weakened on the snow-covered field, surrounded by countless corpses. As his consciousness faded, he slipped into a familiar illusory land…

        “Lucy…”

        A familiar voice echoed in his ears. “Wake up, sleepy head.”

        Todd opened his eyes and pushed himself up from the pile of snow. Before him stretched an endless forest blanketed in white, where he saw her—the lover he had lost long ago. She turned back to him with a warm smile, her figure blending beautifully with the drifting snow in a scene so heartbreakingly serene.

        The snow was cold and pure; it looked nothing like the scorched and bloodied soil of the battlefields where Todd had spent days wandering. He knew everything before him was only an illusion, a figment of his mind, but he couldn’t bring himself to shatter it.

        Lucy didn’t stop or wait for him; she moved slowly into the woods, her figure growing smaller against the falling snow. Todd scrambled to his feet and chased after her desperately. His boots sank deep into the fresh snow, causing him to stumble, but he pressed on, determined. Yet, the snowfall grew heavier, and the distance between them stretched infinitely. No matter how fast he ran, he couldn’t catch up. He could only watch her silhouette gradually fade into the storm.

        “Don’t leave me, Lucy… This is the only place where I can be with you,” Todd cried out silently, his heart breaking. “Lucy, Lucy!”
        His legs felt heavy as if shackled by the snow, but through half-closed eyes, he caught sight of a shadow standing still in the distance. Hope stirred within him, and he forced himself forward. Yet, as he drew closer, he realized it wasn’t Lucy. It was a little girl with a tapir by her side.

        “Johanna…? No, who are you?” Todd murmured, his voice tinged with confusion. Something about the girl stirred a faint ache in his chest.

        “We are Druids, guardians of dreams,” the girl said, giving Todd a concerned look. “We travel through people’s dreamlands. Just now, we heard your cries.”

        Todd’s heart clenched. With fear flickering in his eyes, he took a step back and said, “You’re here to wake me up, aren’t you? No, I’m staying here! Don’t take this dream away from me!”

        “No, we’re not here to wake you,” the girl replied. “If you wish to stay in this dream, why not let us change it into a sweet one? We can help you.”

        “Change it? You mean… I can stay with them forever?”

        “Yes,” the girl said with a nod. “You can.”
The little girl raised her hands, conjuring a gleaming blade with her powers. With a swift swing of her arm, she slashed through the snowy landscape and created a jagged crack. Through the opening, Todd saw something that made his heart ache with bittersweet joy: his old home, the one he had desperately dreamed of returning to.

        Inside, he saw Lucy sitting in a rocking chair by the fireplace, gently swaying back and forth as she held their baby daughter in her arms. The firelight cast her in hues of soft gold. She smiled at Todd the moment she saw him and waved him over.

        Todd stepped through the crack. He knelt beside Lucy, his eyes fixed on their baby girl. The child reached out with her chubby little hand and grasped his pinky tightly.

        “Don’t worry,” Todd whispered, his voice trembling with emotion. “Daddy will never let go of your hand again.”

        The warmth of his daughter’s touch and the familiar scent of Lucy filled him with a profound sense of peace and nostalgia. Even though he knew it was all an illusion, Todd willingly surrendered to it, content to remain in this dream for eternity.

        “Now that the maddened howls have quieted, we can finally rest. Am I right, black piggy?” the girl said softly to the tapir. Then, they quietly closed the crack, sealing Todd inside that warm and perfect dream where a family of three huddled together by the fireplace, basking in the glow of their love.

        “Rest well, my dear,” Lucy said tenderly, placing her hand on Todd’s head. Her gentle touch soothed his restless soul, filling the void in his heart with a false joy. Tears rolled down his face, leaving a smudge of red in the snow around him.

        On the battlefield, Todd’s lifeless body lay motionless among the corpses. His weary form, once wracked with chaos and despair, now rested peacefully, forever lost in the depths of his eternal dream…
STORY_2946:
Evening had fallen, but the grand hall of the Magic Academy remained brightly lit, illuminated for the school’s annual ball. Students, dressed in elegant and extravagant evening attire, slowly trickled into the venue.

        Amidst the bustling crowd, a young boy stood out. He wore a crisp white shirt, immaculately pressed, paired with tailored black trousers. Attached to one of his suspenders was a delicate boutonnière. With his finely sculpted features framed by his soft, honey brown hair, he looked like a little prince carved from the finest porcelain.

        Merlin was one of the brightest students at school. His outstanding appearance and intellect naturally drew the admiration of his fellow pupils. The moment he stepped into the hall, he was swarmed by his female admirers. Yet, being the center of attention only made his stomach clench. Flustered, he couldn’t help but take a step back, only to bump into a passing girl. The cup in her hand flew into the air, its content—dark juice—spilling all over Merlin’s clothes.

        “I-I’m so sorry!” The girl’s voice trembled, her eyes brimming with anxious tears as she stared at the spreading stain on his shirt.

        “No, it’s not your fault. I wasn’t paying attention. If anyone should apologize, it’s me,” Merlin reassured her gently. He took out a handkerchief and started dabbing at the stain, but his efforts were in vain.

        Just then, one of the sophomores in charge, noticing the commotion, strode over. After examining the stain on Merlin’s shirt, he said, “This won’t come out, I’m afraid. But don’t worry—we have spare clothes in the changing room on the second floor. I’ll take you there to get changed.”

        “Thank you,” Merlin replied sincerely and followed the sophomore up the spiral staircase. From the second floor, everything on the dance floor came into clearer view. However, what caught Merlin’s eye most was not the lively party downstairs but the extravagant dresses on the girls who had surrounded him earlier.

        [i]“Their dresses… Their dresses are so beautiful… How I wish—”[/i]

        “Merlin?”

        “Ah!” Startled, Merlin snapped out of his thoughts.

        Looking at him with concern, the sophomore asked, “You’ve been spacing out. Are you hurt?”

        “No! I’m fine. I just got a little distracted,” Merlin hastily replied, quickening his steps to catch up. He forced himself to focus and followed the sophomore to the changing room.

        “All the spare outfits are in the wardrobe. Pick anything that fits. You can leave your stained clothes here and come back for them later.”

        “Thank you. I can handle it myself. You should head back to the ball,” Merlin said politely.

        “Alright then,” the sophomore said with a nod, turning to leave without hesitation.

        Alone in the room, Merlin opened the wardrobe and began searching for a shirt that fit. Yet, his eyes were suddenly drawn to something tucked away on the side—a gown.

        “I… I’m just taking a look,” Merlin thought to himself as he slowly pulled the dress out. It was a dark purple satin gown with a high-waisted silhouette flowing into cascading layers as soft as clouds. Silver constellations were delicately embroidered across the bodice, and under the light, the fabric shimmered like spilled starlight.

        Merlin felt his heartbeat quicken when he brushed his fingers against the gown. A strange, unspoken desire stirred within him—a feeling he had always known but had kept locked away, bound by invisible chains. But at that moment, all the chains seemed to disappear. He knew clearly that the gown wasn’t meant for a boy like him, but he just couldn’t suppress the overwhelming urge.

        “Just for a moment… it won’t hurt to try it on, right? Since no one else is here…” he murmured under his breath as he began to change.

        The soft and cool texture of the fabric sent a shiver down Merlin’s spine along with an unfamiliar yet strangely exhilarating sensation. When he finally stood before the mirror, fully dressed in the gown, he froze—he looked perfect in the dress.

        His reflection stared back at him. He was still Merlin, the boy with the almost-too-refined countenance. Yet, at the same time, he looked like another person. It was like seeing another version of himself, one that had always existed in his dreams, waiting quietly to be awakened.

        For the first time, he… No, [i]she[/i] truly saw herself. Not the perfect student, not the polished boy everyone admired, but a radiant girl who finally put on a gown that made her heart soar.

        It wasn’t a costume. It wasn’t a fantasy. It wasn’t a fleeting whim.

        It was [i]her[/i].

        Something seemed to have bloomed in her chest. All her life, she had felt something was wrong, something she couldn’t name or explain. But now, it all made sense.

        [i]“I was never ‘him.’ I’ve always been ‘her.’ I just didn’t know it until now.”[/i]

        This night was no longer just the night of the school’s annual ball—it was the night [i]she[/i] was truly born.
STORY_2947:
Waves of heat shimmered in the air under the blazing summer sun. Still, a farmer continued his work, directing his bull to plow the fields. But the scorching heat was hard enough for a man to endure, let alone a bull. Exhausted from the unending labor, the animal couldn’t help but stop to pant heavily.

        However, the farmer was merciless. Showing no regard for the bull’s struggle, he picked up a long whip and lashed it brutally. His harsh voice echoed through the fields as he barked, “No slacking off, you beast!”

        The pain ignited a fury deep within the bull. Years of exploitation and cruelty had pushed its temper to the brink, and now its pent-up rage finally exploded. With a thunderous bellow, it reared its head and broke free, shaking off both the bridle and the farmer.

        Ignoring the farmer’s furious cries, the bull ran for its life. Even though it barely had much strength left, it pushed itself forward with everything it had. Eventually, it managed to escape the farmer’s pursuit and disappeared into the dense shade of a forest.

        Exhausted and disoriented, it wandered in the woods. Guided by its instinct, it found a quiet spot under a large tree where it finally lay down to rest. But before it could fully relax, a rustling sound from above startled it. It looked up, only to see a man falling from the treetop. Reflexively, it leapt to its feet and rushed over just in time to catch the falling man with its back.

        “Ugh… What happened? How did I fall?” It was a gentle-looking young man. His simple but clean robes gave him the air of a wandering hermit. Tilting his head in thought, he suddenly exclaimed, “Ah… I must’ve dozed off again while practicing asceticism. I lost my balance, that’s why I fell.”

        “Moo!” The bull let out a low call, as if it agreed, which drew the young man’s attention.

        The young man slid off the bull’s back. He smiled warmly as he gently stroked its head. You saved me, didn’t you? Thank you, bull.”

        “Moo!” The bull called again, nudging the young man’s hand with its head, as if to say, “Don’t mention it.” Its reaction made the young man’s smile grow even wider.

        “It must be fate that brought us together. I’m just a humble Xian in training. I can’t promise you fine clothes or lavish feasts, but I can provide you with fresh grass for meals. What do you say? Would you like to come with me?” the man asked.

        “Moo!” The bull raised its head and let out a spirited call. It began circling the young man excitedly; its actions made its intentions clear. It knew this was the better choice to follow this carefree young man rather than return to the cruel farm, where endless labor would only end with it becoming a meal on the table.

        And so, the man and the bull set off together. Little did the bull know that this decision would change its fate forever, transforming it from an ordinary beast into the legendary Bull King, the Great Sage who would one day lead all elves in the Heavenly Kingdom…
STORY_2948:
To refine his powers as an Onmyōji, Abe no Seimei bid farewell to his Master and embarked on a journey of ascetic training. In his travels, he exorcised youkais and protected people from disasters. By fate’s design, he met three children and took them in as disciples.

        Together, the four traversed the land, crossing mountain after mountain until the three young disciples’ legs buckled under exhaustion one day. Seeing them completely worn out, Seimei decided to halt their progress and spend a night in a quiet village nestled in the mountains.

        “Enough resting. Get up,” Seimei said, looking at his eldest disciple, Akikane, and his third disciple, Natsuaki, who were both sprawled on the bed. His voice was calm, but there was a hint of urgency. “Let’s go find something to eat before the sun goes down.”

        “I can’t… Master, my legs feel like they’re going to break…” Akikane groaned, clutching his leg in pain.

        “Same here… I can barely move…” Natsuaki muttered, limbs spread wide, too tired to even lift his eyelids.

        “Ah... You two are truly hopeless, ” Seimei shook his head with a sigh, then turned to his second disciple, Fubuki, who sat quietly nearby. “Well then, Fubuki, it looks like it’s up to us to go get some food.”

        “Yes, Master.” Fubuki nodded obediently, taking Seimei’s hand as they walked toward the village market. However, before they could go further, a rushing villager caught their attention.

        “Good news! They’ve caught that monster, and they’re about to burn him alive!” the man shouted breathlessly to a neighbor chopping wood in the yard.

        “Finally! That will put our minds at ease!”
“Yeah! Let’s go see!”

        Fubuki tugged lightly at Seimei’s sleeve and whispered, “Master, should we follow them and see what’s going on?”

        “Yes. That was my thought as well.” Seimei’s face grew solemn as he nodded. The two then followed the villagers to the square.

        Crowded with villagers, the square was filled with clamorous, excited voices. At its center, a boy lay on the ground, his hands and feet bound by ropes, surrounded by villagers whose faces twisted with disdain.

        The boy dropped to his knees, his voice desperate. “Please, let me go! I’m not a youkai!”

        An elder—the village chief—stepped forward, his voice cold as he spoke, “You can see things that others cannot, and you speak of things yet to happen… How could you not be a youkasi?”

        The crowd murmured in agreement, their voices mounting into a feverish uproar.

        “I swear I’m not a youkai!” the boy pleaded, his eyes wide with fear and grievance. “I don’t even know why I have these powers!”

        However, his explanation didn’t convince the villagers. Instead, it only made their fear and rage grow stronger.

        “Don’t listen to him! He’s lying!” one of them shouted.
        “Yeah! Burn him, or he’ll bring disaster upon us all!” another voice cried.

        Lost in their unfounded fear, the villagers were ready to sacrifice the innocent boy. Just as the child was about to meet his grim fate, a cold, steady voice cut through the crowd:

        “STOP! Hear me first!” It was Seimei, standing at the edge of the crowd, his voice calm yet filled with unquestionable authority.

        The village chief snorted, his face filled with suspicion and disdain. “An outsider is trying to disturb our peace. Everyone, stop him!”

        At the chief’s command, all the villagers grabbed their tools and charged toward Seimei.

        But Seimei showed no fear, only disappointment in his eyes. Quietly, he raised two fingers and began channeling his powers. A glowing sigil then appeared. Lowering his gaze, he whispered, “Bind.”

        Suddenly, all the villagers felt a crushing weight upon them, as though invisible threads were holding them in place.

        The chief’s expression changed instantly. Realizing the young man before him was no ordinary man, he forced a smile and said, “Ah… I didn’t know you were an Onmyōji.  Please forgive this old man for his ignorance.”

        Despite the chief’s change of attitude, Seimei’s gaze remained stern. Staring at the chief, he said in a sober tone, “You nearly killed an innocent child.”

        “How can you be sure he isn’t a youkai?”

        “There’s no trace of evil energy on him,” Seimei replied, his eyes piercing as he looked directly at the boy. “In fact, I sense a faint scent of pure pneuma flowing from him… This boy may possess powers you lack; still, he is, after all, a mortal like you.”

        “Even if what you said is true, he has caused so much trouble to our village,” the chief argued.

        “Even so, that doesn’t justify burning a boy alive,” Seimei said firmly, his eyes blazing with unwavering conviction.

        The chief’s words of protest died in his throat. His face shifted from pale to flushed before he spat angrily, “Humph! Do as you please. We only want him gone!”

        “Then I shall take him with me,” Seimei said, his words leaving no room for doubt. He stepped forward and untied the boy.

        After they were back in the inn, Fubuki helped clean the boy’s body and even borrowed a set of fresh clothes from Natsuaki for him to wear.

        When the boy finally calmed, Seimei knelt to meet his gaze and asked softly, “What is your name?”

        Tears glimmered in the boy’s eyes as he stammered, “Shige… Shigeharu…”

        “Nice to meet you, Shigeharu! I’m Fubuki, your second sister in training!” Fubuki said with a warm smile.

        Natsuaki rushed forward, grasping Shigeharu’s hand with enthusiasm. “And I’m Natsuaki, the third among us disciples. And this is our eldest brother, Akikane!”

        Akikane gave a kind smile and nodded.

        “Here, let’s go home together,” Seimei said, extending a hand to Shigeharu. His voice was so warm and irresistibly inviting. 

        Their kind gestures brought Shigeharu a wave of relief, melting away his fear and uncertainty in an instant. Hope and warmth replaced the loneliness in his eyes. Slowly, he reached out and took Seimei’s hand, his voice barely a whisper. “Yes…”

        In that moment, Abe Seimei did more than help a helpless child—he led him out of darkness and into a future filled with light.
STORY_2949:
Born in a prosperous and peaceful little town, Paimon was blessed with a rare gift—a singing voice that stirred the hearts. As a child, she loved nothing more than to sing. She always sang softly to herself as she stood upon the stone steps in the garden, dreaming that one day she might become a singer admired by all.

        Yet fate is often cruel. Paimon’s appearance bore a congenital flaw, a disfigurement so unpleasant to behold that made her a laughingstock of the town, mocked and scorned wherever she went.

        Even so, Paimon never gave up her dream. She kept practicing day and night, pouring her soul into her songs while tempering her spirit in the fire of music. It wasn’t until the town’s annual singing competition came that this girl with a dream gathered her courage, donned a mask, and stepped onto the stage she had longed for all her life.

        The moment she started singing, the judges were all amazed, their hearts seized by her beautiful voice. However, their admiration soon turned to ridicule and undisguised contempt when she removed her mask as the chief judge told her. Then they gave her the most cruel comment: “You can never become an idol.”

        In that instant, Paimon’s entire world fell apart. Her heart bled as though cut by a thousand blades. Tears slid silently down her cheeks as she fled the stage in disgrace. She ran until she reached the desolate wilderness where her suppressed anguish erupted into bitter cries that echoed in the emptiness.

        The pain of rejection was unbearable, and for the first time in her life, she thought of giving up her dream.

        It was then that Belial, a man who called himself the King of Demons, appeared. With a nonchalant yet confident smile, he said, “I can help you.”

        “Help me?” Paimon asked, puzzled.

        “Yes. I can restore your beauty and give you a chance to start over.”

        “But why? Why would you help me?” she asked.

        “Because a precious gem should never be buried in dust. Your voice holds the power to change the world.”

        It was such a sudden and almost unbelievable offer. Paimon had doubts, but she yearned more for a change, a stage where she could sing freely. She simply couldn’t resist the temptation, even knowing Belial was no man of virtue. And so, she accepted his proposal.

        Days later, Paimon’s appearance transformed beyond recognition. Her once dull, rough skin became fair and smooth. Her twisted, grotesque features now turned into those of a porcelain doll, delicate and beautiful. Her frail, misshapen body blossomed into graceful elegance. She was no longer the girl that everyone had despised and mocked, but the radiant center of attention.

        Following Belial’s guidance, Paimon swiftly rose to fame as a singer. When the day of her first grand concert arrived, she stepped onto the stage she had dreamed of for so long amid the thunderous cheers of the crowd. The lights blazed, the audience gazed upon her with fervor, and the music roared like a storm.

        She could feel her heartbeat quicken as an indescribable excitement surged through her veins, causing her body to tremble.

        [i]“My dream finally came true…”[/i]  She closed her eyes, drawing a deep breath to steady her emotions. Then, she stepped forward, and with the most dazzling smile, she sang the most enchanting melody.

        Her song soared through the air and echoed in the hall. The audience was enraptured, lost in her otherworldly voice that also carried a soul-seizing power, drawing all who heard it deeper into her spell…
STORY_2950:
Finale of Gifted Scientists - Ch. 8

        Hurried footsteps echoed in the dimly lit space as our figures raced up the long staircase, quickly reaching the top—the surface.

        “Phew, we’re finally back!” Nicole, the red-haired girl, breathed a sigh of relief as she stepped out of the Everdark Land, back to the bright corridors of the research lab. She excitedly hugged Einstein, the white-haired boy.

        “But I wonder how Edison’s doing... I hope he’s alright.” A hint of concern flickered across Einstein’s eyes as he spoke in a low voice.

        Months earlier, Einstein had received an invitation from the Lomond Manor, a scientific organization, to join them as a scientist. However, on the day of his arrival, he was attacked and knocked unconscious by unknown assailants. When he woke up, he found himself faced with a series of difficult challenges.

        Only until afterwards did he learn that it had all been a test created by the Lomond Manor for newcomers. Nevertheless, his exceptional gift made him one of the qualified candidates, and eventually earned him a place on the team for an extremely challenging mission—the subterranean exploration

        Today was supposed to be the day of their departure. Yet the unexpected struck—the institute’s security system had been compromised, and the demons, who had long been watching from the shadows, seized the opening of the disappearing defensive barriers and mounted a full-scale invasion.

        To secure the progress of the subterranean exploration, Darwin, one of the golden scientists, volunteered to lead most of the other scientists in repelling the demons. Meanwhile, Galileo, another golden scientist and the exploration team leader, led Einstein, Edison, and Nicole into the underground to continue the mission.

        Following Nicole, the four scientists successfully avoided the mad beast, Behemoth, guarding the first level, and arrived at a ceremonial site on the second floor, where they rescued Descartes, a newly born machina.

        With Schrödinger’s help, the group uncovered the history and secrets buried deep within the underground city. Their discovery brought a dawning realization: to quell the chaos on the earth and turn the tide for humanity, they would need to awaken the machinas. Thus, they decided to return to the surface with Descartes and report their findings to the Headmaster, only to be confronted along the way by the scientific order known as the Ashes of Life.
