        Unfortunately, Sea Pearls formed only along sheer coastal cliffs, guarded by flocks of vicious Sea Pearl Birds. There was no practical way for Long Yangjun to collect them alone. Asking someone else for help would have been the obvious solution, but he had never been the type to ask favors.

        “This is driving me insane!” Long Yangjun grunted. Having had enough of staring at failed swords, he decided to find another way to work off his frustration.

        So he dressed and left the workshop. Before long, he arrived at a tavern hidden away in a secluded corner of the shopping arcade. The place had a certain reputation among men looking for male company—the perfect place for his hunt. After ordering a drink, he found himself a seat and waited.

        With a face like his, Long Yangjun didn’t wait long. A tall, broad-shouldered man soon approached with a drink in hand. Wearing a confident smile, the stranger sat down beside him and asked, “Mind if I join you?”

        “Go ahead.” Long Yangjun returned the smile and rested a hand casually on the man’s shoulder. “And after we finish these... why don’t we do something more fun?”

        The suggestion was obvious enough. The man eagerly finished his drink and took Long Yangjun toward the tavern’s back exit. The moment they were outside, he pushed Long Yangjun against the wall and began running his hands over him.

        “GET AWAY FROM HIM!” A furious shout cut through the alley when the two had barely gotten started. Before either of them could react, a powerful flying kick sent the man hurtling into a stone wall and crumpling to the ground, completely unconscious.

        “Are you all right?” Long Yangjun’s supposed rescuer asked, rushing over. “Don’t worry! I already took care of the guy who was attacking you. And there’s no need to thank me. I, Zhang Liao, never ask for a reward for doing what’s right—AGH!”

        But before Zhang Liao could finish his heroic introduction, Long Yangjun drove an elbow against his neck and pinned him to the wall.

        “Doing what’s right?” Long Yangjun hissed. The interruption was the last thing he needed after the day he’d already had. His expression turned cold as he glared at Zhang Liao and said, “You just ruined my night!”

        “Huh?” Zhang Liao blinked at him in complete confusion. “B-But that guy had you pinned against the wall! Wasn’t he attacking you? How did I ruin anything?”

        Long Yangjun gave a cold, amused laugh. “You’re a virgin, aren’t you? No wonder you couldn’t tell what we were doing.”

        Zhang Liao could be dense at times, but even he understood the implication at once. His entire face flushed with embarrassment as he stammered, “I-I-I swear I didn’t mean to! I’m so sorry!”

        “And what good does apologizing do me now? You knocked him unconscious,” Long Yangjun said. His eyes swept over Zhang Liao’s muscular build. Apparently satisfied with what he saw, he gave a small nod. “Well, I guess you can take his place. Virgins aren’t usually my type, but I suppose I can make an exception.”

        “Oh no! No! Absolutely not!” Zhang Liao shook his head violently. “You’re only supposed to do something like that with someone you truly love!”

        “Someone you truly love?” Long Yangjun chuckled. “All right, then. Let’s see how long that belief of yours lasts.” 

        Certain that Zhang Liao’s convictions wouldn’t survive temptation, Long Yangjun ignored the man’s protests and slipped a hand beneath his clothes. But Zhang Liao slipped cleanly out of his hold before he could even touch his chest. The man scrambled up a nearby tree like a monkey and stared down at Long Yangjun in horror.

        “D-Don’t you dare try!” Zhang Liao cried, clutching his loosened clothes closed like a young lady defending her dignity.

        [i]‘This man... He’s something.’[/i] Long Yangjun was surprised. He had never seen anyone move with such speed and ease, and it gave him another idea. A smile tugged at his lips as he said, “Fine. I won’t force you. But in exchange, I need you to do something for me.”

        “...I won’t do anything that goes against my principles,” Zhang Liao replied warily.

        “Relax. It’s an easy job. I just need you to fetch something for me.” Long Yangjun spoke nonchalantly, carefully leaving out the details.

        After a moment’s hesitation, Zhang Liao agreed. “Fine. We have a deal.”


        Long Yangjun then led him to a towering cliff near the coast. Pointing toward a cluster of brilliant blue stones growing from the cliff face far below, he smiled. “I need you to bring me one of those.”

        Zhang Liao stared over the edge. The bottom of the cliff was nowhere in sight. “...And this is what you meant by easy?”

        “If you find it too difficult, we could always spend the night together instead. I wouldn’t mind.”

        “But I would!” Zhang Liao clenched his teeth. “I’ll get it!”

        After taking a deep breath and flexing his hands, he climbed over the edge. For all his complaints, he quickly made his way down the sheer rock face, darting between footholds with remarkable agility until he reached the Sea Pearls and pried one loose.

        Just as he prepared to climb back, a deafening cry came from the sky. A giant bird swooped down and snatched him from the cliff, its talons closing around his body as it carried him high into the air.

        “NO!” Zhang Liao struggled desperately, but the bird’s iron grip left him almost helpless. He could barely move, much less break free.

        A knife suddenly flashed past him and struck the bird squarely in the wing. With a shriek of pain, the creature released its grip, sending Zhang Liao into a free fall.

        Zhang Liao’s stomach dropped as he plunged through the air. His heart pounded so violently he thought it might burst from his chest. Then, at the last possible moment, a strong arm caught him around the waist.

        It was Long Yangjun. After striking the bird with his knife, he had broken into a run, timing his leap to meet Zhang Liao in midair and catch him securely in his arms. Zhang Liao’s heart began to race as he became suddenly aware of the faint floral scent on Long Yangjun’s body. He had never known what it was like to feel so safe in someone else’s arms, and it sent a strange flutter through his heart.

        [i]‘Th-This is it! This is what it feels like to fall in love! I’ve finally found the woman... No, the man of my dreams!’[/i]

        Long Yangjun released him once they landed, but the emotions that had awakened in Zhang Liao remained.

        Zhang Liao looked at Long Yangjun, his face flushed as he pressed a hand to his pounding chest. When he finally spoke, his voice trembled with embarrassment. “I... I think I’ve fallen for you.”


        Long Yangjun looked mildly surprised, but only for a moment. Then a faint smile touched his lips. “Sorry, but I don’t do real feelings.”

        He took the Sea Pearl from Zhang Liao and walked away without another thought. Zhang Liao had barely had time to fall in love before finding himself heartbroken. The rejection stung, but he quickly pulled himself together.

        [i]‘I’m not giving up! I’ll win his heart no matter what! Then I’ll marry him and bring him home as my wife!’[/i]
STORY_2973:
The bright red banner of the Tianzheng Escort Chamber fluttered above its gates in the morning wind. Inside the main hall, Wu Zetian sat at the head of a long table, turning through the pages of a thick ledger as she reviewed the latest accounts. Several months had passed since she severed ties with her family and joined Zhangsun Wuji’s sect. Using Zhangsun Wuji’s connections and reputation, she had established her own escort chamber, and it had grown faster than most expected.

        When Wu Zetian first opened her doors, not everyone was convinced she could keep it going. The idea of a woman running such a dangerous business had drawn plenty of doubt, but one successful delivery after another gradually silenced the rumors and turned them into respect.

        “My lady!” An escort hurried into the hall with an excited smile. “The silk shipment has been delivered. The merchants were so pleased they sent us a plaque with our name written in gold. They said we should hang it outside the chamber!”

        Wu Zetian looked up from the ledger and said calmly, “Record the gift. We’ll accept the plaque, but there’s no need to hang it. If Tianzheng is going to make a name for itself, we’ll do it through our work.”

        The escort nodded and returned to their work. Wu Zetian had always been strict in business and generous when it was deserved, and over time, that had earned her the respect of everyone under her command. In only a few months, Tianzheng had gone from an untested newcomer to one of the most talked-about escort chambers in the region, even drawing attention away from the long-established Wu family business.

        It was everything Wu Zetian had wanted; she had finally built something beyond her father’s shadow. Yet just as Tianzheng was about to make its name, her hard-won success faced its greatest test…

        The opportunity to take Tianzheng another step forward came when an official commission arrived asking them to transport a shipment of military supplies to the border.

        It was a prestigious job, but also a dangerous one. If anything happened to the cargo, Tianzheng would lose far more than its reputation; mishandling an official shipment could bring punishment from the imperial court itself. Knowing how much was at stake, Wu Zetian chose to lead the convoy personally.

        On the morning of their departure, the wagons stood ready outside the city as the escorts made their final preparations, blades gleaming coldly in their hands. There, Wu Zetian gave her final instructions: “There can be no mistakes on this job. If we run into trouble, don’t waste time fighting them. Remember, the cargo’s safety always comes first!”

        The escorts answered in unison, and the convoy set off with spirits high. The journey remained uneventful until they entered a mountain road, where black-clad figures appeared along the slopes. But they didn’t attack the escorts. Instead, they rushed straight toward the wagons while hurling explosives with burning fuses into the convoy.

        [i]‘Whoever sent these men has no interest in stealing the cargo; they want the entire shipment destroyed.’[/i] Wu Zetian saw through their plan immediately. 

        “Get back!” she shouted, rushing toward the wagons with her umbrella. With several quick sweeps, she knocked the explosives away from the wagons and sent them flying into the surrounding woods. Sparks flew as the charges exploded among the trees, but the cargo remained untouched.

        Realizing their plan had failed, the attackers immediately began to retreat. 

        “My lady, should we go after them?” the escort captain asked, watching the black-clad men disappear into the trees.

        “No.” Wu Zetian kept her eyes on the retreating men, then shook her head. “I already know who sent them.”

        [/i] ‘Money wasn’t their goal. They were only here to destroy the shipment and ruin our reputation, and only a few people benefit from seeing this happen…’[/i] The answer that came to her mind was one she had hoped never to consider. 

        Once the shipment was complete, Wu Zetian gathered her people and headed straight for the Wu family escort chamber. Outside the gates, escorts from both sides stood facing one another, weapons drawn and tempers running high.

        “Master Wu!” She stepped forward and shot, fixing her father with a cold stare. “You sent men to destroy an official shipment for your own gain. You know what kind of crime that is. If you have any shame left, surrender yourself now!”

        Her father gave a contemptuous snort. “You ungrateful child! You are the eldest daughter of the family, yet you dare come here and accuse your own father? To turn against your family and slander your own blood—what kind of daughter does such a thing? A woman as vicious as you deserves nothing but death!”

        Wu Zetian did not rise to his anger. Instead, she smiled faintly and raised one hand. Several of her men immediately brought forward a group of bound prisoners, and the anger vanished from her father’s face the moment he recognized them. 

        They were the same men who had attacked the convoy that morning. Wu Zetian had once managed the Wu family’s escort chamber and knew its grounds better than anyone, including the secret passage her father used when he wanted something kept out of sight. While she completed the delivery, she had quietly sent several of her people to search it, and the attackers had been found exactly where she expected.

        Color drained from her father’s face. With the men he had hired standing before him in chains, there was no explanation he could offer.

        “Take him into custody,” said the officials who had accompanied Wu Zetian.

        Her father did not plead for mercy. Instead, he suddenly laughed.

        “Good. Very good. I brought this on myself, I suppose. But do you really think you’ve won?” He turned to Wu Zetian and said coldly, “You may have made a name for yourself now, but it’s only temporary! Zhangsun Wuji can think as highly of you as he likes, but it won’t change the way the world sees you. You’re just a woman! No matter how far you climb, you’ll spend your life fighting for a respect they’ll never truly give you!”

        Wu Zetian’s gaze shifted slightly, but she remained silent as she watched the officers take her father away.

        That night, the escort chamber remained brightly lit long after the streets outside grew quiet. Inside the hall, the escorts raised cup after cup in celebration, but Wu Zetian had gone out into the courtyard alone.

        She stared into the dark, starless sky. Her father’s words still stung her like poisonous thorns.

        All her life, she had wanted her father’s recognition. Now she had built Tianzheng and turned it into a name that many respected, and still, none of it had changed how he saw her.

        “It’s only temporary…” she murmured, remembering the contempt in his voice. Her fingers tightened around her umbrella until its metal frame gave a faint creak.

        For the first time, she wanted more. Her wish was no longer for Tianzheng to prosper, or for her to have the strength to protect herself. What she wanted was something greater: power no one could question, power that would leave no room for anyone to look down on her again.

        “If the world sees women as weak, then I’ll prove them wrong by taking every power they thought was beyond my reach!”

        The hurt in Wu Zetian’s eyes slowly hardened into something colder and far more determined. Her father’s words had started a raging fire, and with it came a new burning ambition: to seek power for herself!
STORY_2974:
Amid the roaring flames, a graceful figure danced across the stage beneath a shower of lights, slipping between spinning blades with impossible precision. Every turn drew gasps from the audience, and every step brought another wave of applause. Once again, Cleo stood at the center of everyone’s attention. She smiled and waved as she took her final bow. Only after the curtain slowly fell did she return backstage.

        The moment Cleo stepped behind the curtain, her assistant hurried forward to help her change out of her stage costume, only to find the wound beneath the fabric. “Cleo... you’re bleeding!” 

        “It’s nothing,” Cleo answered calmly. “Don’t worry about it.”

        She had long since stopped counting the wounds. To keep the audience entertained, she had constantly challenged herself with increasingly difficult performances, pushing her body beyond its limits show after show. Her body was covered with scars, but she had never cared about them. Because more than anything else, she feared the day when the audience would no longer look her way. So she always gave everything she had to the stage—even her life.

        Until that day, she pushed too far.

        The flame dance was meant to be Cleo’s greatest performance yet. She had spent countless hours preparing, hoping it could bring her an even greater round of applause. But something went wrong during the final act. She misjudged her final step and fell to the burning floor. The flames caught her legs, and she could only watch helplessly as they burned.

        The accident took her legs, as well as her dream.

        Lying in the hospital bed, Cleo stared blankly at the ceiling as fear closed around her like a powerful flood. She thought, [i]‘No… I can’t stop performing! I can’t lose the applause! If I can never go back on stage... then I’d rather die!’[/i]

        The thought haunted her for days. She feared being forgotten, and she could not imagine a life where she would never again stand beneath the lights and hear the audience cheer. 

        Just as she sank into despair, a deep voice broke the silence. “I can hear your soul crying, Cleo.”

        Cleo looked up in surprise, only to see a figure slowly emerge from the shadows. It was a man with green hair and a charming yet rebellious smile.

        “Who… Who are you?” she asked cautiously.

        “My name is Belial.” The man snapped his fingers. An elegant chair appeared beneath him, and he sat down. Then, he said with pride, “I am the King of Demons.”

        “I can help you, and I am the only one who can,” he said. “Your legs. Your strength. Your stage. With my power, you will never again give a performance that falls short.”

        “Why would you help me?” Cleo asked. She knew well that nothing in this world came without a price.

        “Because of your soul,” he answered. “I need a soul like yours.”

        “So you want to take my soul?”

        “No, I just need you to form a pact with me and become one of my servants,” Belial said with a friendly smile, but Cleo immediately noticed the calculation hidden beneath his words.

        [i]‘He’s hiding something. But what does that matter? I’ve already lost everything.’[/i] Cleo lowered her head and thought quietly.

        The memories of the stage remained vivid in her mind. Every song, every rhythm, every moment beneath the lights reminded her of the dream she had not finished chasing. She had not come this far just to let it all disappear. She wanted to return to the stage and hear the applause again. For that, she was willing to pay any price.

        “I’ll do it.” Cleo slowly raised her head, determination shining in her eyes.

        “Wonderful. I like people who make decisive choices. Here, get your prize,” Belial smiled, gathering his power at his fingertips. A vortex of energy formed in his hand before moving into Cleo’s body.

        Cleo felt a strange force enter her. For a moment, it felt as though her entire world had been torn apart and rebuilt. Her legs healed before her eyes, and the pain faded away, replaced by a strength she had never known before.

        “You’ll thank me someday.” Belial’s voice was low and captivating. “Everyone won’t be able to take their eyes off you, and you will become the brightest star on the stage.”

        Cleo slowly stood. A faint smile appeared on her face as she felt the power flowing through her body. She was no longer the helpless girl she had once been. With this power in her hands, she could finally choose the life she wanted.

        Not long after, Cleo stood on the stage again. Every performance she gave was more astonishing than the last. The flames that once destroyed her had become part of her greatest performances, dancing around her like a storm and making every movement even more captivating. The applause never stopped, and beneath the golden lights, Cleo felt the joy she had once dreamed of. For a fleeting moment, it was as though she were standing once again atop that golden pyramid, lost in a dream.

        But the power that brought her back came with a price. The flames burned bright on the stage, their heat reaching deeper into her soul with every performance. She had never looked more radiant, but the more she gave to the stage, the closer she came to death. The stage had become both the place where she felt most alive and the place that was slowly consuming her…
STORY_2975:
The sun was sinking behind the mountains, bathing the road in deep gold as a man and a woman raced through the fading light. The man was Jiang Ziya, an Xian general of the Heavenly Kingdom, lean and stern with a bundle of bamboo scrolls secured across his back. Running beside him was Daji, a beautiful nine-tailed vixen whose usual poise was betrayed by the faint crease of impatience between her brows.

        “Seriously? We only dealt with that evil spirit in the water this morning,” she frowned as she complained under her breath. “And now we’re being called out again? I haven’t even had a chance to rest properly!”

        “Some things just can’t wait,” Jiang Ziya said as he slowed to a stop and turned his attention toward the village in the distance. “Several children have gone missing, and the entire village is living in fear. This morning, some villagers came to my door and begged me for help on their knees. How could I call myself a Xian if I simply ignore their need?”

        Daji glanced at him. There had been a time when she would have laughed at the troubles of the mortals and walked away without a second thought. Yet after spending days with Jiang Ziya, something in her had changed. Little by little, a warmth she had never known before had found its way into her heart.

        “All right,” she said with a smile; the tenderness in her voice made her feelings obvious. “Since you insist, then I’ll come with you.”

        By the time they reached the edge of the forest, the last of the sunlight had sunk beyond the mountains. A cold, unnatural presence hung among the trees, and according to the villagers, every missing child had vanished somewhere inside these woods.

        Jiang Ziya stopped at the tree line, his expression sharpening. “I can sense the devil pneuma here. We’ll need to search carefully.”

        “Then let’s split up,” Daji said. Then she shifted into her fox form and slipped into the woods to the left, disappearing into the deepening shadows.

        Jiang Ziya took the path to the right. The deeper he went, the colder and damper the air became. As the night wind whispered through the leaves, he moved carefully with his sword in hand. Before he had gone much farther, hurried footsteps sounded behind him.

        “Ziya! I found something. Hurry, come with me!”

        He turned to see Daji hurrying toward him with an anxious look on her face. She reached for his hand, but he made no move to follow. Instead, he watched her in silence.

        For a moment, confusion crossed her face, though the familiar sweetness in her voice remained.

        A flicker of confusion crossed her face. Speaking with a familiar playful charm, she asked, “What’s wrong?”

        “You’re not her.” Jiang Ziya’s voice turned cold as a talisman flared to life in his hand, and for a moment, the entire forest seemed to freeze around the weight of those words.
        For a split second, “Daji” froze. A cruel glint passed through her eyes as the illusion broke apart around her, revealing a woman engulfed in flames. She was beautiful, almost seductively so, yet there was something feverish and dangerous about her beauty. Her eyes burned with a cold, merciless fire as she looked at him. She was Bao Si, a woman of fiend blood. 
        “Humph. Impressive, General Jiang.” Bao Si gave a cold laugh, her eyes blazing with contempt. “Too bad you’ve gotten to my sister. If I don’t get rid of you, she’ll only get more tangled up in these mortal attachments.”

        The words had barely left her lips when flames roared up and took the shape of a serpent, lunging straight at Jiang Ziya.

        Fire burst against the glowing shield and scattered into sparks, setting the nearby trees alight as smoke rolled through the forest. Red flames and golden talisman light flashed between the trunks while Jiang Ziya steadily advanced. Bao Si’s power was formidable, but his command of Taoist arts was more precise, and before long she found herself being forced back.

        With a low shout, Jiang Ziya took out several more talismans. They flared into a wall of golden light just as the flame struck. In a spray of sparks, fire spread quickly through the nearby trees as smoke rose between the branches, the forest flashing red and gold with every clash. Bao Si was losing ground. Her attacks were powerful, but Jiang Ziya met each one with calm precision and kept closing the distance. Before long, she was being driven back with little chance to counter.

        Gritting her teeth, Bao Si reached into her sleeve and threw something at Jiang Ziya’s feet. A moment later, the missing children appeared before him, restored to their true size as the spell on them fell away. Fire circled their bodies, trapping them in place as they cried out in terror.
        “Stop!” Jiang Ziya shouted.
        “Ha. Take another step, and I’ll burn these children alive.” Bao Si gave a cold laugh. “So tell me, which will it be? You or them?”

        “Leave the children out of this. Take me instead.” Jiang Ziya made his choice almost immediately, and there was no fear in his answer. It took Bao Si by surprise, but only for a moment as she covered it with a mocking smile.

        “How noble of you, General. Then allow me to grant your wish.” Bao Si said, her taunt followed by a flare of power. Horns appeared at her brow as flames rose around her, gathering into a blazing sphere in her palm. She hurled it at Jiang Ziya with all her strength. 

        Suddenly, a flash of silver swept across the darkness as Daji cut in between them, her nine tails whipping through the fire. The blazing sphere burst apart, scattering flames through the air as she stood in front of Jiang Ziya, and the flames around the children vanished under her power.

        “Bao Si!” Daji roared, her voice cutting through the glade. She was furious, but there was also pain in her eyes. “What are you doing?”

        Bao Si froze at the sight of her. Confusion flickered across her face, but she quickly forced it down and answered with a bitter laugh. “Sister, how can you still not see it? You used to live however you wanted—no rules, no attachments. But he’s changed you, and I was trying to protect you!”

        “Enough!” Daji’s nine tails unfurled behind her as her power surged through the air. “Maybe I didn’t understand it before, but I do now. A life of endless killing isn’t what I want. It never was. Don’t make me regret saving you, Bao Si!”

        Daji’s words hit Bao Si where it hurt most. Her face tightened with pain as she fought to keep her emotions under control. She took a step back without seeming to realize it, then another, until she was standing at the edge of the cliff.

        “No… This can’t be true… Sister would never say something like that…” Bao Si murmured in disbelief, her hands shaking as her power broke loose. Fire flared unpredictably around her, and she stumbled back from it instinctively. By the time she realized where she was, there was barely any ground left beneath her feet.

        “Bao Si!” Daji shouted, moving almost immediately as Bao Si lost her footing. She caught Bao Si’s arm with her tails and slowly pulled her back from the edge.

        Still trembling from the near fall, Bao Si stared at Daji in confusion and asked, “Sister… You said you regretted saving me… Then why… Why did you save me again?”

        “I regret letting you go down the wrong path,” Daji replied. “I’ve never regretted saving your life.”

        “Sister…” For a moment, Bao Si could only stare at her. Tears slipped silently down her face as memories of that night of bloodshed came back to her—the despair she had felt when watching her parents die protecting her, and the hand Daji had offered her in her darkest moment.

        “Sister…” Bao Si’s voice turned hoarse when she finally spoke. “Then what am I supposed to do? Will you teach me?”

        Daji’s eyes softened. She returned to her human form and held out a hand, her voice gentle but determined as she said, “The world can be cruel, Bao Si, but there are still things in it worth protecting. If you truly want to change, then come with me, and we’ll find yours together.”

        “…All right. I’ll come with you, Sister.” With trembling fingers, Bao Si slowly took Daji’s hand —the same hand that had saved her twice. She decided to follow her again, but this time, toward a future filled with light…
STORY_2976:
It was a dark, quiet night. The forest lay still until the sound of hurried footsteps broke the silence. A young man and woman stumbled along the mountain path, their clothes stained with mud from their desperate flight.

        Torchlight flickered among the trees as a large group of servants searched the forest. At their head, an armed guard called out into the darkness, “Young Master! His Majesty has already decreed your marriage. You cannot defy an imperial command! Please, come back before you make a terrible mistake!”

        The man—the young heir of a noble family the guards were searching for—hurried through the woods, holding tightly to the hand of the beautiful young woman beside him.

        They pressed on until they came across a secluded cave hidden deep in the mountains. The heir quickly led the woman inside, and the two waited in silence as the search continued outside. Only when the torchlight began to fade into the distance did they finally allow themselves to relax, but they both knew it was only a matter of time before they were found.

        The beautiful woman’s name was Yang Yuhuan. Only a few months earlier, she and a young scholar had made a pact to die together for love. The scholar drowned in the sea, but she survived, washed back to shore by the waves, where the heir happened to find her.

        Knowing nothing of the scholar’s death, the young heir thought Yuhuan was simply a damsel in distress and brought her home. As he cared for her, sympathy gradually turned into affection, and the two eventually fell in love. His family, however, refused to accept their relationship. They even appealed to the emperor, who ordered the young heir to marry a princess instead. Furious that his family had gone so far to keep them apart, he decided to run away with Yuhuan. But before they could get far, his family discovered their escape and sent the guards after them.

        “Yan, my love, it’s only a matter of time before they find us. No matter how far we run, you’re still the heir, destined to marry the princess, while I…” Yuhuan said, “I’m nobody.”

        “No!” The heir pulled her into his arms, as though holding her close could somehow protect her from everything threatening to tear them apart. “How could I marry someone else? You’re the only woman I love!”

        “So do I… You’re the only man I love...” His answer brought a smile to Yuhuan’s face, but beneath her happiness lay a trace of sadness and quiet resolve. She reached into her sleeve and took out two small porcelain bottles, their pale surfaces gleaming faintly in the moonlight. She opened one, and a faint medicinal scent filled the cave.

        “It’s poison. Once we drink it, no one will ever be able to keep us apart again, and we can be together forever,” she said.

        The young heir froze. For all his declarations of love, the thought of actually dying left him shaken. Sweat gathered on his brow and his breath quickened as he stared at the bottle in Yuhuan’s hand, unable to bring himself to take it. Was death really the only way for them to be together?

        “I see… You’re the heir to a noble family after all.” Yuhuan saw his hesitation, and tears began to fill her eyes. “You have your whole life ahead of you. You’re meant to marry the princess, while I… I have no one and nothing. I should never have asked you to give all that up for me. You should go back. Forget about me. I don’t want to be the one holding you back.”

        “No! I could never betray you!” Gritting his teeth, the young heir snatched one of the bottles and drained it.

        His body began to shake almost immediately as the poison slipped down his throat. The color drained from his face, and his eyes slowly lost focus. He reached for Yuhuan one last time, trying to touch her face, but his strength gave out before his hand could reach her.

        “Yu... huan...”

        “Thank you for dying for me. I’ll never forget how much you loved me,” Yuhuan leaned close and whispered into his ear as he collapsed into her arms. When he breathed his last, she bent down and kissed him, drawing every last trace of his life force into her body.

        The red floral mark on her arm glowed as power coursed through her body. A new petal formed, bringing the pattern one step closer to completion.

        “Just one more man, and my core will finally be restored,” she murmured.

        “You monster! I won’t let you take another life!” A cold voice came from behind her. In the same instant, golden chains burst from the ground and closed around Yuhuan. She struggled to turn and saw a Taoist priest entering with a sword in hand, a talisman burning fiercely between his fingers.

        “Who are you?” Yuhuan demanded, fixing him with an icy glare. “What are you doing here?”

        “I have been following you for some time.” The priest fixed her with a hard stare. “Yang Yuhuan, you prey on men with your beauty, lure them to their deaths, and feed on their life force. Your crimes will not go unpunished!”

        “They chose to die with me,” Yuhuan replied, her voice soft but chilling. “How can you call that my crime?”

        “Enough of your lies!” the priest roared. Golden light flared along his blade, and a bolt of lightning came crashing down upon Yuhuan.

        Yuhuan staggered under the attack. The strain on her damaged core sent a burst of excruciating pain through her body, but she gritted her teeth and endured it, her hatred only growing stronger.

        “WHY?” Yuhuan screamed, her voice raw with anguish and rage. “I was the victim! All I ever did was take back what I was owed! If the heavens condemn me for that, then I’ll tear them down myself!”

        Yuhuan’s eyes turned red as a tremendous force gathered around her. The petals on her arm suddenly flew free and swept around her, striking the golden chains again and again until the priest’s spell broke.

        The priest stumbled back in shock, but there was nowhere to run. The petals sharpened into blades and came at him all at once, cutting through his shield before he could defend himself.

        “ARGH!” The priest’s cry ended abruptly as they pierced his body from every direction, and moments later, there was nothing left of him but a fine mist of blood.

        Yuhuan held out a hand. As she drew the last of the priest’s life force into herself, she felt the wound in her core heal completely, and a brilliant light burst from within her. Slowly, she rose to her feet. The crimson flower on her arm was finally complete, and she could feel her restored power coursing through her.

        “At last… My core is whole again, and my power is back,” she whispered. Then, a beautiful but unsettling smile crossed her face. “So that’s how it is... Betrayal, hatred, love… In the end, they’re all nothing more than fuel for my power.”

        Yuhuan disappeared into the forest that night, but her power spread across the mountains even after she had vanished from sight.

        The woman returning to the human world was no longer the vulnerable beauty she had once been, but an enchantress who had turned her back on love and cared only for power. And this time, she would bring nothing but trouble wherever she went…
STORY_2977:
The scent of incense hung heavy in the room as Mo Xi studied herself in the bronze mirror. The woman staring back at her was no longer pale and sickly; after weeks of rest, her body had regained its health and its curves. Once, the sight of that body had filled her with disgust. Now she stood naked before the mirror, coldly considering how she could use it—

        —to avenge Shan, the girl she had loved and lost.

        For as long as Mo Xi could remember, the dresses she wore had always felt more like shackles than clothes. She had often wanted to tear them off and be free of them for good. Yet today, she took one from the folding screen and deliberately dressed herself layer by layer, hiding that desire for freedom beneath silk and embroidery.

        Her transformation continued at the dressing table. She softened her complexion with pale powder and shaped her brows with a few careful strokes, then used her fingertips to brush a vivid red across her lips. With that final touch, a breathtakingly beautiful woman emerged in the bronze mirror.

        [i]‘Shan… I swear I’ll make him pay for what he did to you… no matter what it costs me.’[/i]

        Mo Xi then walked slowly toward the front gate, each step calculated to show off her beauty. There, she waited for the general’s return.

        The general reacted exactly as Mo Xi had expected. The moment he dismounted, his attention went straight to her, and the desire in his eyes was everything she needed.

        “My Lord, I must apologize for not attending to you properly while I was unwell,” she said, meeting his gaze with a coy smile. “I am feeling much better today, and I hope you’ll give me a chance to make it up to you.”

        “Oh?” The general raised an eyebrow. “And how do you intend to do that?”

        “By taking good care of you, of course. Please come with me.”

        Taking his hand, Mo Xi led the general back to her room and brought him to the bed. Everything she needed was already waiting on the table: a cup and a white porcelain bottle filled with a fragrant fruit wine she had prepared for him. 

        “It has been a long day, my Lord. Please, have some wine and rest,” Mo Xi said softly as she poured a cup and offered it to him. But the general had learned long ago not to trust food or drink simply because someone placed it in his hands. Instead of drinking it, he put an arm around Mo Xi’s waist and raised the cup to her lips.

        “Drinking alone is no fun. You first, my dear.” The general’s tone was gentle, but the hand holding the cup left no room for argument. With little choice but to play along, Mo Xi drank from his hand.

        [i]‘So he isn’t all brawn and no brain after all. Good thing I took the antidote beforehand,’[/i] Mo Xi thought.

        The general watched her closely for a moment. Only after seeing that she was perfectly fine did the general finally drink from the cup. It wasn’t long before his gaze slowly lost focus. His eyelids grew heavy, and within moments, the drug had robbed him of his senses.

        When he woke up, he found himself bound tightly to the bed. He pulled against the ropes with all his strength, but couldn’t loosen them at all.

        “Save your strength. You’re not going anywhere,” Mo Xi said, her voice bearing none of the gentleness she had shown him before.

        “Mo Xi! Damn you! Untie me! I’ll kill you!” The general flew into a rage as he realized what she had done, and he began shouting every insult he could think of.

        Mo Xi ignored his threats and calmly returned to the dressing table. She wiped away her makeup, undid her elaborate hairstyle, and tied her hair back like a man’s. When she finally turned to face the general, he almost failed to recognize her. Dressed in a simple black outfit with a sword in hand, she looked more like a handsome young man than the woman he had known, and there was a coldness in her eyes that he had never seen before.

        “W-What are you going to do?” Only then did the general realize he had badly misjudged her. She was nothing like the weak, harmless woman he had taken her for, and something about her determination unsettled him.

        “What am I going to do?” Mo Xi gave him a small smile. Her face remained calm even as she drove the sword through the center of his palm, drawing a scream of agony from him.

        “I came to avenge Shan,” she said, her voice cold and unwavering. “And I’m going to make you pay for everything you did to her.”


        The lingering fragrance was soon lost beneath the stench of blood. Once the general was dead, Mo Xi set the room ablaze and watched as it burned, her face calm and unreadable in the shifting firelight.

        The fire soon had every servant in the estate rushing to the room. With everyone’s attention fixed on fighting the flames, Mo Xi slipped away unnoticed, dressed as a man. The town that had confined her for so long was finally behind her, and for the first time, she was free to go wherever she pleased…
STORY_2978:
The palace of Folkvangr was always quiet.

        Everyone was too busy to talk. Messengers hurried through the corridors. Officials moved constantly between chambers carrying stacks of military reports, and every list of wounded soldiers seemed longer than the last.

        Though no smoke or fire reached the palace, the shadow of war hung over every corner.

        In those days, Young Swegde often sat alone in the corridors with a stuffed doll in her arms, watching the adults come and go.

        Whenever a maid happened to notice her, she would stop and reassure her, “Your Highness, please wait in your room. His Majesty will come to see you once he has finished with military affairs.”

        But Swegde knew her father was unlikely to come. It wasn’t because he didn’t love her; it was simply that the demons had attacked again.

        Whenever the warning beacons outside the city were lit, her father and his generals would remain in the strategy room until late at night. Swegde had once peeked through the half-open door and seen her father bent over a map, his brow drawn tight as the discussion went on around him.

        She hadn’t understood any of their words, but she could see how exhausted her father was. She knew it was better not to bother him, so she learned to entertain herself.

        Before long, she began to feel like one of the old books left forgotten in some corner of the palace: always there, but with no one who had time to open and read it.

        That evening was no different.

        Two soldiers stood guard outside the strategy room while low voices carried through the door behind them. Swegde waited for a while with her doll pressed to her chest, but eventually, she quietly turned away and made her way down the staircase toward the royal library in the northern wing.

        The library was almost always empty, which was one of the reasons Swegde loved it.

        She loved books because they never disappeared into meetings or hurried away when the demons attacked. All she needed to do was open one, and it stayed with her for as long as she wanted. 

        “What should I read today…?” she murmured, walking on tiptoe as she wandered between the shelves.

        She could recognize some words on her own, and when she couldn’t, the illustrations usually helped her understand the rest. She had read a sailor’s journal about sea monsters, an illustrated book of medicinal herbs, and even a volume about the frozen lands of the North, where ribbons of light shimmered across the night sky.

        Eventually, a thick book on a high shelf caught her attention. She climbed onto a small ladder and stretched as far as she could, but her fingers barely reached the edge of its spine. Refusing to give up, she leaned a little farther, and the ladder began to wobble.

        “Ah!”

        Swegde grabbed the shelf to steady herself. The bookcase shook, and an old wooden box that had been balanced precariously on top slid loose and fell heavily to the floor.

        The box burst open in a cloud of dust, sending Swegde into a coughing fit. Once the dust had settled, she crouched beside it and found several ancient books wrapped in cloth. Their covers were worn and their pages yellow with age.

        She carefully lifted the book resting on top.

        A young man in light armor was painted on its cover.

        His expression was gentle but resolute, and the sword in his hand shone so brightly that it seemed capable of cutting through the night itself.

        Swegde stared at the picture for a long moment, an unfamiliar warmth rising in her chest as she slowly sounded out the name on the cover.

        “Fre… yr…”

        She had heard that name before. Her father had once told her that the royal family’s ancestors came from the North, and Freyr had been part of the bedtime stories he told her. But she had never heard the rest of them. More than once, a messenger had arrived at the door before he could finish.

        Swegde carried the book to the window and began to read.

        Much of the writing had faded, and water stains had even blurred some of the lines. It took her some time to make sense of each page, but the more she understood, the more absorbed she became.

        The book told of Freyr and Lævateinn, the sword he had carried into battle. Lævateinn was no ordinary weapon, nor was it meant to prove its wielder’s strength. The sword answered conviction, shining brightest in the hands of someone who fought to protect others.

        “Lævateinn…” Swegde whispered, tracing the sword in the illustration with one finger before hugging the book to her chest. Somehow, it already felt more important than any toy she owned.

        Then, with one small fist held firmly against her chest, she said, “I’m going to find the Lævateinn, the legendary sword Freyr left behind. If I find it, I can help Father. Then I can help everyone defeat the demons too.”

        Much later that night, Swegde fell asleep at a desk in the library. Freyr’s book lay open beside her, surrounded by sheets covered in crooked handwriting and unfinished notes.

        Outside, the cold wind blew past the palace windows, and the threat of the demons still hung over the kingdom. In her sleep, however, Swegde dreamed of a rainbow bridge leading her across a frozen sea and over burning mountains. The light ahead guided her onward until, at last, she reached the place where it faded, and there a sword waited quietly for her.

        Years later, when the demons pushed Folkvangr to the brink of defeat, Swegde stood before her father and asked to leave in search of Asgard, the sacred land.

        To everyone else, it might have sounded like a desperate plan born from fear. But for Swegde, the idea had not come to her in that moment; it was a promise she had made during the lonely days of her childhood and had carried with her ever since—

        —to find Lævateinn and become someone capable of protecting everything she held dear.
STORY_7001:
“Along with the utilization of Runes’ power, scholars began studying the meaning behind the pictographic Runestones.  From ruins, we have traced a tribe which once used the heart shape as their totem figure.  As manuscripts suggest, the curves on the heart were downward-curling horns, and the angular lower part was the jaw of an open mouth...”

        “Let, let go of me...”

        “Listen quietly!”  She tightened her grip.  “The heart shape totem manifested the image of the Mother of Inferno.  This also explains the prayer about ‘life’ in the scripts: ‘Mother of Inferno, you bless us with eternal flame, protecting the earth from contamination, securing the purity of bloodlust.’  However, this ‘heart’ tribe was eliminated by other tribes, for that they feared the power of this Ancient God.”

        Tightly tangling the heretic with her long tentacles, she gradually dragged him to a gigantic flaming-orange sphere.

        “Who was the one to have defined that life must advance, and that life must have its own goal?  Maybe there is a kind of creature that lives for the sake of living since its birth.  It might also create numerous aimless lives in its own image —”

        “No!  Please don’t kill me!  I don’t want to die!”

        “Kill?  Why would I kill you?  I’m helping you cross your own limits and enter the world of immortality.”  Her thick tentacles again lifted the man and pulled him to her.  “Gods are obligated, Demons are weary, Humans are vulnerable...Every race has a way to die, but only Elder Gods can enter the hall of eternity!”

        The Great Mother pushed the heretic against the giant sphere, prompting pained cries from him.  His body swelled and peculiar tentacles protruded from his mutilated body.  His screech turned into groan-like absurdities, a sound caused by his deformed mouth chewing his tongue.

        Just then, an enormous shadow was cast over the sky, covering the witch and her followers.  The burgundy body of “Mother of Inferno” was weaving in the sky; its winding claws were dropping fiery spheres grabbed from its blazing abdomen.  The witch and the heretics all dropped to their knees in prayer, praising the glory of the Elder God; however, the “Mother of Inferno” simply kept weaving and did not respond.  It opened its mouth, with multiple sets of jaws visible, and slowly flew towards Enochian Tower...
STORY_7002:
Underworld abounded with souls of the deceased, among whom, Abe no Seimei stood silently in his Onmyōji outfit.  His eyes stayed closed, as if he was meditating or listening to something.  In front of him was the river of underworld, a virtual river manifested by numerous souls of the deceased proceeding together closely.  Abe no Seimei should be one of them, but he did not follow other souls and dive into the river; instead, he stood alone beside it.

        Although Hades was the lord of underworld, he rarely concerned himself much with the matters of the underworld, which includes the souls of the deceased.  However, Abe’s peculiar act drew his attention, so he approached the Great Onmyōji...

        “Mortal, one has to discard all after one’s demise.  Though reluctant you might be, you have to let it go.”

        ‘Shigeharu and Fubuki are in danger.’

        “Did you listen to me?”

        ‘I have to go back...and help them...’

        With that said, Abe no Seimei turned to the exit of underworld.  Hades attempted to halt him, only to discover that he was unable to move.  It was not until Hades scanned his own body did he notice four gigantic white foxes gripping his limbs between their teeth.

        Hades conjured small amounts of dark elemental power, believing that this could eliminate the beasts.  But he soon realized that the four foxes not only did not vanish, but their jaws only clenched tighter on him.  The four foxes represented Abe’s determination to return to the realm; his firm resolution would not falter regardless of obstacles.

        Hades comprehended at the moment: this soul was different than the others.  It had immense power.  If he chose to challenge the Onmyōji to a duel, it would be a mutually destructive one.  Hades sneered before saying, “Can you order them to release me?  I do not intend to stop you anymore.”

        Abe no Seimei did not reply; he merely whistled sharply.  The four foxes jumped back before vanishing.

        ‘Thank you for your understanding.’

        Abe no Seimei did not even turn.  He continued walking onward his expressionless words.  As long as he could return to his disciples, he was willing to sacrifice anything...
STORY_7003:
Night wind rustled through leaves on the mountain.  To ensure she was on the right path, the moonlight shining through the gaps in the leaves was all Yaoji had.  Pouch in arms, Yaoji walked with increasing worry.  She was supposed to meet a person under the orchid tree beside the pavilion.  But he had not appeared after a long wait...

        Does he no longer want to be with me?  Or does he think like the others, that I should marry that man from money?  No, he has probably just been hindered in the dark...Trying to shake the worry out of her head, she again hurried on her way.  She was hoping to see him as soon as possible; only then can she assuage her worry.

        The rustling of leaves grew louder.  It did not sound like it was caused by the wind, but rather by a gigantic creature rubbing against them.  She had heard rumors about a ferocious animal around, could it be...?  Yaoji broke into a trot without looking back, as if doing so would mean being caught by the animal.  She did not turn until she reached an open field.  All that was there was an orchid tree by the road with its flowery petals floating down.  Yaoji gradually caught her breath while her panicked heart calmed.

        Night wind rustled through weeds on the mountain, with which came smell of blood.  Yaoji turned to the source of the scent, and was surprised to hear crunching sounds from the weeds.  Without trees’ cover on the open ground, moonlight fell on the mound, and in the light, she could see a tiger devouring its prey — a tiger!  Yaoji could not help but gasp; she was so terrified that she covered her mouth to avoid her breathing sound attracting the tiger’s attention.  She kept her eyes on the tiger while carefully moving backwards.  Suddenly, a sense of familiarity emerged; it prompted Yaoji to focus her sight on the food in the tiger’s mouth, and the soft pieces scattered around —

        Upon recognizing who the prey was, Yaoji gave out an uncontrollable wail; the sound captured the tiger’s attention, causing it to growl towards Yaoji’s direction.  Fear rendered Yaoji’s legs numb.  She could merely stood against the trunk on her back.  Before Yaoji, orchid petals danced in the wind, but the growling tiger was nearing...but wait.  Why am I under a tree?  It was not until now that Yaoji realized that she had never returned to the road, and there was something wrong about the tree.  However, a shadow flew at her, forever denying her the chance to know the answer.  Just then, a blinding light radiated from the orchid tree!

        When the light dissipated, the orchid tree was no longer there and instead, a woman with Yaoji’s appearance stood where the tree had.  However, she was now unclothed, and on her head grew a pair of tree-branch horns, covered with blossoming orchid flowers.  Having been stalking nearby, the tiger seized the chance to leap at the woman; she, on the contrary, merely put her hand on its head, and its motion stopped.  The blinding light reappeared, this time from her hand, rendering the tiger docile.  The tiger even nudged its head against the woman before bringing a piece of the fresh meat for her.  The woman took a bite, and a smile spread across her face...
STORY_7004:
Simon was dragged to a ruin by a gang of werewolves.  The ruin had long been deserted and thus, had become the base of the werewolves.  Yet, for some unknown reason, Simon seemed not unfrightened by the imminent danger at all.  Instead, he was smiling.

        “Darn kid!  How dare you throw stones at us?”  Werewolves forced Simon to kneel, and raised their weapons towards him.  Just as they were about to hack him apart, a man dashed out from the forest.  It was the Paladin King of Light.  He skillfully knocked away the werewolves’ weapons with his spear and hit them using the pole end.  The werewolves knew that they were no match of the Paladin King of Light, so they ran away hastily.  The Paladin King of Light untied Simon and left the ruin without looking back.  Simon followed him excitedly...

        “I knew you would come!  You defeated them so easily; you are so great!”

        “Did you notice my skills and agility?  I am very suitable to succeed you!”  Since the Paladin King of Light rescued him for the first time, Simon had long been determined to be his successor.  In order to gain the Paladin King’s recognition, Simon tried to expel the werewolves for the villagers and challenged the gnomes to save the weak.  But he did not realize that every time, he actually needed the Paladin King to rescue him instead.

        The Paladin King halted his steps and said coldly, “I have rescued you for the last time.  Stop creating trouble and stop following me!  You are not qualified to be my successor.”

        The Paladin King’s words left Simon startled.  Looking at the departing Paladin King, he shouted resentfully, “I’m sure you will regret this in the future!  When the time comes, don’t come back to find me!”  Simon punched the wall hard, accidentally activating a mechanism of the ruin.  Before he could react, he was brought into a secret chamber along with the revolving wall.

        In the secret chamber laid a suit of glittering armor.  It had been hidden there for centuries; yet, it was still glittering and flawless, without any trace left by time.  Deeply attracted by the armor, he walked towards it as if he had lost his mind.  He just thought: if he possessed the armor, he could surpass the Paladin King of Light.  He stretched his hands towards the armor...

        A dazzling light shone from the ruin.  “Bang!”  An explosion tore a hole in it.  Simon, who was wearing the armor, slowly walked out of the ruin.  His body was inundated with power, emitting a sense of formidability.  He pointed his weapon towards the blue sky and swore an oath, “I shall surpass the Paladin King of Light; everyone will honor me as a great hero!”
STORY_7005:
Rahu grew up in a temple.  His adopted father instilled a benevolent heart into him, telling him to be kind to friends and enemies alike.  Hence he had always lived with this principle.  When Rahu reached adulthood, he became a priest in the temple.  However, his adopted father deemed him lacking in worldly experiences, so he asked Rahu to practice asceticism outside the temple.

        Soon after his departure, he ran into bandits by a stream in the mountain.  Not a slight shred of fear appeared within him.  He attempted to understand them, and realized that they had been forced into a life of crime.  Therefore, he guided them back onto the right track.  The bandits were touched by his universal loving kindness and hence, abandoned their reprehensible way of life.

        “True benevolence brings awakening.”  He deeply believed this.

        Rahu journeyed through myriad countries and discovered that people in need numbers as many as there are stars in the sky.  The benevolent Rahu constantly realized his principle by endeavoring to help those who require it.

        On his journey to the west, Rahu arrived at a small country.  Gloominess and the musty stench of blood occupied every corner.  No one can be seen on the streets: it looked like an abandoned city.  Suddenly, aggressive pneuma blasted from the center of the city.  Rahu turned only to see a peculiar purple creature floating in the air.  The three-headed creature had six arms.  It focused its three purple-glowing eyes on Rahu, leaving him trembling in fear despite his usual calm.  The creature leapt straight at him, his intention to kill palpable; its hands grabbed him by the throat.

        “Abandon...evil...” Though in danger, Rahu still hoped to reform the creature.

        “Abandon evil?  I’ve killed so many people but it’s the first time I’ve met someone as interesting as you!  Torturing you should be fun!”

        The creature cracked into laughter.  It broke Rahu’s limbs, prompting screams from the latter, blood showered all around.  The creature was soaked with his blood; the screams and gore triggered an even wilder laugh from the creature.  However, the creature’s hands trembled.  It looked at its six arms in discontent.

        “So, this body has reached its limit, huh?”  The creature murmured.  It raised its head and glimpsed at Rahu, its sharp teeth shown when it grinned.  It thrusted its many hands into Rahu’s wounds on his limbs; soon, Rahu’s body merged fully with the hands and exuded immense power.

        “What a perfect vessel for me!  This body now belongs to me, Asura!”  After throwing back his head in a laugh, Asura started admiring his new body.

        His lips curled, and uncanniness flashed across his eyes: “True benevolence is to let people die a painless death!”
STORY_7006:
“Another new magistrate?  Hmph.  No magistrate is able to govern this town; continuing to send new ones won’t make a difference.”  An old guard murmured in the magistracy of Luohua Town.

        Luohua Town was notorious for its citizens’ maliciousness.  The immorality here had affected all of the previous magistrates.  However, a town has to have a governor after all, so the central government still sent officials here as replacement.  They hoped that at least one magistrate could resist the corruption and better yet, end the town’s immorality.  This time, the official sent to Luohua was Shaohao, who was known for his integrity.  He was to be accompanied by two constables.

        Just as Shaohao entered the town, he heard a woman teaching her young son, “Remember.  Learn how to steal and fight.  That way,  you can steal every last dollar from the wealthy!”

        “Absurd!”  Shaohao found parents teaching their children to sin preposterous, and hence, he could not help approach and berate the woman: “How can you pollute your son’s mind like this?”

        “What do you know, outsider?”  The woman retaliated: “I don’t want my son to be eaten by Qiongqi!”

        With that said, the woman rushed off, dragging her son behind her.  Shaohao was left startled as he watched two’s figure disappear into the distance.  After he had arrived at the magistracy, Shaohao asked the old guard what the woman had meant.  It was not until then did he find out about the ferocious monster that had been plaguing Luohua Town for more than ten years.

        The monster was called “Qiongqi”.  It preyed upon the righteous while the  malicious, on the contrary, were spared and even gifted with game and food.  The townsmen tried to evict it, but not only were they unsuccessful, several among them were actually killed.  Since then, the people in Luohua Town sinned, hoping for Qiongqi’s blessing.

        The words enraged Shaohao.  He vowed to eliminate the monster to restore order.  Having once experienced life without having to fear Qiongqi, the old guard was touched to see the new magistrate’s determination to reclaim peace for the town.  He endeavored to convince the other guards to follow the new magistrate.  Seeing the willingness of those staffing his magistracy in helping Luohua Town, Shaohao’s determination to eliminate the monster and restore morality became more resolute.

        Shaohao brought all guards of the magistracy up the mountain to hunt the monster.  Under the elderly guard’s lead, they journeyed into the depths of the mountain, when the monster suddenly appeared and snapped at Shaohao!  Just as his two constables were about to jump into the fray to help, the old guard ordered the guards to restrain the two men, leaving Shaohao to be eaten by Qiongqi.

        “Why...?”  Shaohao asked before taking his last breath.

        “Luohua was once a poor town.  It was not until we learnt how to steal were we able to feed ourselves.  All the town’s good people are dead.  Luckily you came along —  I was beginning to worry who to feed to Qiongqi.”  The old guard’s voice did not fluctuate, as if he was having an ordinary conversation.  “Working for the interest of the townsfolk seems to count as doing good though.  Although Qiongqi did not eat me, it has never given me any game.”

        As if able to understand, Qiongqi ripped off one of Shaohao’s arms and carried it to the old guard.

        “I am not yet cold-blooded enough to cannibalize.  Save it for yourself.”  The old guard watched as Qiongqi chomped the last bit of Shaohao’s body.

        Though it just finished a meal, Qiongqi greedily stared at the two constables.  One of them struggled out of restraints and shoved the other towards the beast.  With a clench of its jaw, Qiongqi decapitated the falling constable and carried the head to the one who had pushed the victim, as if a gift.  The surviving constable was frightened in hiding behind the old guard’s back.

        Qiongqi grinned in content, blood-mixed saliva seeping: ‘That’s right.  Evil will grow within your heart and grant you power!  Next time, you will be bold enough to stand before me like this old man.’
STORY_7007:
“Hm?  Where is the singing coming from?”

        “They must be Gods’ emissaries coming to celebrate the king’s coronation.”

        On the day of the king’s coronation, all the citizens heard an unknown chant, though none were certain who exactly was singing; only the king could see fylgjur hovering in the sky.  Whenever someone nears death, fylgjur would wail, announcing the coming death.  Hence, they were also called “obituary fylgjur”.  Paying no regard to their wails, the king brimmed with joy as he succeeded the crown.

        The royal clergy had been teaching the king from his childhood on how to effectively govern.  Whenever the king needed to give a decision, the clergy’s voice would seemingly ring in his head, reminding him to first consider his country and subjects.  Occasionally, the haunt would agitate the king.  He was the king after all; his decisions should not be affected by anyone.

        It was already late at night, but the king was still awake, head buried in documents.  Suddenly, sorrowful wails rang from outside the window...

        The king had heard fylgjur’s wails before the coronation day, but there were no obituaries of anyone issued in the next few days, so the king’s memory about the wails had faded.  However, the wails ringing through his ears had reminded him of the incident; fear immediately surged: “Could it be that...I’m the one...who’s near death...?”

        The next day, the news of the king’s demise spread across the country.  The royal clergy, Kavanagh, led all in the national mourning.  During the service, fylgjur’s chants gradually loudened, but this time, only Kavanagh could see a fylgja hovering outside the window.

        After the funerary services ended, Kavanagh returned to his bedroom and changed, before stealthily entering the royal family’s secret passageway.  Blood was smeared all over the corridor; Kavanagh walked towards where the bloodstain was the darkest, and murmured to the crimson-covered wall —

        “Father, I have sent the king to underworld to face the punishment he deserves.  Back then, I had no idea that he was responsible for your death!  Only when a saint dies would a number of fylgjur appear at the same time.  I had already felt something was wrong when I saw that many of them.  And when I was suddenly forced to succeed your place, I was sure that something had happened to you.”

        “And that king dared say you taught him to govern with benevolence!  You know what he said last night?  He claimed that you had incessantly interfered with his decisions, and that you did not obey his orders.  And saying that your voice still lingered in his mind after your death...Bullcrap!”

        “He even claimed that he decided to kill you because he heard fylgjur’s wails.  Father...fylgjur’s wails...are they announcements of deaths?  Or are they the precipitators of such deaths?  My hands...Their wails have also caused my hands to be covered in blood. Father...now I probably don’t deserve to be with you again after my death, do I?”

        “Now your blood’s covered by his blood...Perhaps mine should also be added on there...I’m not like the king; I’ll atone for my own sins.”  Kavanagh stroked the bloody wall before him.  The glass in his hand dropped and shattered, and the wall was sprayed with another layer of fresh blood.

        That day, the chanting from the fylgjur never halted.

        Fylgjur sing their requiems not for blessings, nor do they care about the cause of death; they chant only for the deceased.  However, their wails can amplify the negativity within Humans, severing their connection with rational thought.  The surging emotions would drive actions that are out of characteristics, even if it means taking the lives of others —
STORY_7008:
“Your Majesty, we think it is time to recapture the seas that have once belonged to us.”  Dragon warriors of the sea clan suggested to Ao Guang the Dragon King in the hall of the Dragon Palace.

        “We have stayed in the deep seas for so long, and our life has been peaceful.  Why do you think we should join the war?”

        “With all due respect, our letting of other creatures seize the oceans is insulting our honor as the sea clan.  The blue shall be our dominion!  With the other races now warring against each other, we should grasp this chance and regain rule over Your Majesty’s waters!”

        “Fellow warriors, you should still remember the reason why we have chosen to hide here.  We have just recovered from the deterioration of our clan.  How do you think we can take back the seas?”

        “If I remember correctly, there is a sealed nine-headed dragon in ancient legends.  If we summon it —”

        “Nonsense!  The nine-headed dragon is a ferocious creature of time immemorial.  How dare you think of releasing it!  And for waging a war!”  Ao Guang’s usual composure vanished; his bellow of anger shook even the entire Dragon Palace, prompting the dragon warriors to hurriedly kneel: “Your Majesty, please calm!”

        The dragon warriors at present did not have complete knowledge of the incident about the nine-headed dragon, so he neither blamed nor admonished them and instead, he merely gestured at them to leave.

        The words “nine-headed dragon” had reminded Ao Guang of his most resisted memory, like a gust forming huge waves on a calm sea.  With his recollection stirred, the nine-headed dragon’s roar was as if still reverberating in Ao Guang’s mind...

        Back then, Demons yearning for elemental power incessantly invaded the depths of the seas.  To defeat them, the sea clan summoned the nine-headed dragon.  Its roars resembled infants’ cries, so it was also known as the Nine-infants.  At first, the Nine-infants had enormous influence on the war, earning numerous victories for the dragons of the sea clan.  However, in the myriad fights with Demons, the Nine-infants was gradually contaminated by demonic power through its wounds, prompting increasing difficulties for the sea clan to control the Nine-infants.  Deranged, the Nine-infants could no longer distinguish friends and enemies, and eliminated every living creature on the battlefield.

        “Guang, tell the others to retreat first!  I’ve got a way to deal with this maniacal dragon.”  A white dragon of almost the same size as Ao Guang swam to him and said.

        “Yun, what’re you planning to do?”  With the Nine-infants rampaging the seas, Ao Guang dared not be rash.

        “I’m the best caster of sealing-magic in the clan.  What do you think I’m going to do?”

        “Don’t even think about doing it all by yourself!  There’s gotta be a way when all the four of us are together —”

        “Just tell them to leave!  If we waste any more time on arguing, the Nine-infants is going to kill us all!”

        “Hmph.  Ao Yun, you think merely yourself is enough to seal the Nine-infants?”  A red dragon also came to join the two after it had heard their conversation.

        “Ming!”

        Then, a black dragon also approached: “So, all my older brothers are ready to risk their life in sealing the Nine-infants.  How can I retreat and leave you behind?”

        “Shun...”,  “Shun?  Even you have—”

        The most arrogant dragon in the clan, Ao Ming, had willingly forfeited the chance to win individual honor, and agreed to offer his help, let alone the kindhearted Ao Shun.  Their generous support surprised Ao Yun, who had intended to handle the nine-headed dragon alone: “Hahaha!  This is great!  All the four of us are staying; Guang, Ming, and Shun, let’s seal the Nine-infants together!  Please lend me your power when the time comes!”

        “Just cut the crap.”,  “Of course!”  The red dragon and the black dragon both swam to the white dragon’s side, waiting for approval from the blue dragon, Ao Guang.  With no other excuses to stop them, he led his brothers to the Nine-infants.

        The Nine-infants weaved its body, its nine heads separately claiming lives on the battlefield, both Demons and dragons of the sea clan.  The Ao brothers listened to Ao Yun’s instructions, and swam to the four cardinal directions.  With the Nine-infants at the center, Ao Yun murmured a spell, instantly trapping the Nine-infants with a magic circle; but only this procedure had already consumed much of Ao Yun’s power.  Upon seeing the establishment of the magic circle, the other three dragons channeled their power to fortify the trap, earning time for Ao Yun to cast the sealing magic.  Focused on channeling power into the circle, Ao Guang failed to notice that his second and fourth brother were secretly sharing their last bit of power with Ao Yun, whose power was about to be depleted.  Finally, Ao Yun did not disappoint the others, and successfully sealed the Nine-infants.  However, he himself also perished after exhausting his power...

        Suddenly, a roar resembling infant cries reverberated in the oceans, snapping Ao Guang awake from his memories.  “Th...This bellow!  That’s impossible!  Did they violate my prohibition, and release the Nine-infants from the seal?!”

        Ao Guang led the remaining dragons to where the Nine-infants had been sealed, only to find the dead bodies of dragon warriors flowing along the current.  The seal was broken, and the Nine-infants was nowhere to be seen...
STORY_7009:
“Hm?  Where did my bread go?”  A woman looked at the windowsill in her kitchen, and said in surprise, “Oh my, did someone just steal it?  So thefts are really increasing!”

        If she stuck her head out of the window right now, she would see an unbelievable scene on her right — her bread was floating away in the air!  The bread hid among churns of milk; even the milkman himself was unable to notice the extra bag of bread on his cart.  Just as the cart entered a city, the bread dashed into the shades between buildings.  Avoiding the crowded streets, it moved swiftly in secluded alleys, and floated into an abandoned manor.

        The bread stopped on a ragged table.  Then, the trousers and clothes on the nearby bed began to move, as if someone was picking them up and getting changed into them.  As the bread moved with the Human-shaped clothes, it was gobbled in the air; if there were head and limbs, it was most surely someone eating the bread in those clothes.  However, where the head should be was no head; so were the limbs.

        Suddenly, the half-eaten bread fell onto the floor.  The clothes bent towards the trousers; the collar neared the knees, and the sleeves wrapped around where the “head” should be.  The clothes threw themselves hard onto the bed.  The trousers started to tremble, while heavy pant of fluster sounded, “All...of you...Die...”

        The clothes continued to writhe, and the bed was in a mess.  All of a sudden, the clothes bounced from the bed and rushed out —

        “Ahhhh!  Clothes!  Clothes are flying around!  And they even tore themselves?”

        “Ahhhhhh!  A pipe is moving by itself!”

        “The pipe is killing people!  Run!”

        Screams abounded through the streets.  The residents could only see a pipe chasing and hitting people.  After cracking the door of a meat shop, the blood-stained pipe fell onto the ground.  This time, people saw a knife moving.

        “No!  Please don’t kill me!”  The owner of the meat shop pleaded the knife he always used for mercy, yet the knife did not listen to him.

        Blood splashed forward from the shop owner’s body as the knife withdrew from him.  The blood started to form a figure at where the knife was floating.  People, therefore, began to be able to see a translucent man-like figure fiercely stabbing the owner!

        The man-like figure returned to the streets.  Losing sight of the scattered people, it broke into shops to kill everyone in sight.  Constables rushed to the scene with their guns.  Yet, it was difficult for them to lock on the translucent figure as it had already wiped off the stain; shooting spells randomly might hurt the innocent residents.  Two of the constables charged, trying to stop the figure, but they were unable to land their strike at the almost invisible figure; instead, they were even stabbed!  Even more unfortunately, the figure grabbed a gun from the constables...

        The screamings from the residents had spread to a hill of a nearby town.  A few people were standing by a wood house on the hill; they were Illuminated Savant and his subordinates.

        “So, he indeed accomplished his mission to kill, but he seems a bit out of control.  Is it because of the virus itself, or is it the side effect of the medication?”  Illuminated Savant shifted his focus from the town to the report on his hands: “Data’s still insufficient...Hey you, find someone to collect his blood sample.”

        “Understood.”

        “Keep an eye on him.  ‘7009’ is a precious subject.”  Illuminated Savant ordered his subordinates.

        “In our experiments in Human-invisibility, ‘7009’ is the only one whom we can say is successful.  Yet, his invisibility is still unstable, we still need to collect data from various experiments.”  He murmured as he read through the report, “How long can he turn invisible this time?  He did once become invisible for the whole day to avoid the guards, and escaped from the lab.  But this time... maybe around half a day?  Hmmm... Let’s keep observing.”

         “If the experiment is successful, I’ll have an invincible assassin squad!  Hahahaha!”
STORY_7010:
“Tezcatlipoca is a monster who brings about disasters.  Hundreds of years ago, it ran amok and radically affected people’s lives.  The only reason why the realm is now peaceful is because our God sealed him in a smoking mirror.”  All the country’s people listened to this story when they were growing up and hence, a religion based on the smoking mirror was well established.  The mirror was passed down to every generation of the royal family, and it was placed in the temple of mirror for people to worship it.

        “We earnestly beg Your Majesty to reconsider!”  All officials kneeled before their new king.

        The king flipped his wrist to signal them to stop begging: “Still enthralled by that nonsense tale after these many years, huh?  And every day, you people go to the temple and worship that ragged mirror!  Idiots!”

        “With all due respect, Your Majesty, it is not just a tale, it is also a traditional religion that has been in our country for hundreds of years.  It is because we are blessed by our God’s smoking mirror that our country can prosper.”

        “I do not need some old mirror to make this country prosper!  If the people have enough money and food to worship that mirror, maybe they should pay more tax and contribute more to the country!”  The new king glared angrily at the officials: “I now order you.  Take down the temple of mirror!”

        Surrounded by pleading voices of the people, the soldiers loyally carried out the king’s order.
