STORY_10919:
Above the homeland of the Akashics, a woman hovered in midair with her hands casually stuffed in her pockets, gazing down at a magnificent building—the Archives of the Origin, the most sacred place of the Akashics, said to house the most extensive collection of knowledge in the universe, revered as a treasure trove by all seven races.

        “So, this is where the Akashics live,” the woman, known as Möbius, muttered as she chewed on bubble gum. With an exaggerated shrug, she commented in disbelief, “Seriously? Worshipping that pretentious fraud? Do these gods even have brains?”

        Her sharp, mocking gaze swept over the Akashics walking on the ground. Her brow furrowed for a second before it turned into a twisted smile. “It doesn’t matter,” she said with a chuckle. “They’ll all be gone soon enough, so who cares if they’re brainless?”

        She tilted her head back. A feverish red appeared on her pale skin, her eyes filled with a delirious longing as if her mind had wandered to some sweet vision. She gasped softly as her voice trembled, “And then… I’ll find you. I’ll see you. I’ll touch you. Oh, Azathoth, my dear Azathoth… I miss you so much…”

        Lost in her fevered fantasy, she hugged herself so tightly that her sharp nails dug deep into her skin, causing blood to stream down her arms in rivulets. Yet, she simply did not care. The pain was as though a desperate attempt to ease the unbearable ache of her yearning, a physical reminder of her true purpose.

        “Ahhh…” she sighed, her breath quivering as she came down from her fevered reverie. As her ravenous gaze shifted back to the Akashics below, a wicked grin spread across her face. She licked her lips and murmured, “Time for a ‘fun’ little game.”

        With a snap of her fingers, an eerie vortex appeared beneath her feet. She leaned back and let herself fall into the churning void. In the next second, she appeared before one of the Akashics on the street.

        “Woah! W-who are y—” Before the Akashic could finish his question, Möbius reached into the void—the Infinity Chamber—and pulled out a gleaming sword, then she slashed it across his neck.

        Splash! A spray of blood flew up into the air and bloomed like the most grotesque flower, showering everything in red. Yet, Möbius laughed like a child, jumping gleefully in the crimson rain.

        “Hahaha! How beautiful! I am truly the best!”

        The gruesome spectacle sent the surrounding Akashics into sheer panic. Screams filled the air as they scattered in all directions. However, Möbius was unforgiving. Using her ability to slip through space, she hunted them down one by one, each kill more brutal than the last.

        In mere moments, the tranquil plaza became awash in blood. One might even mistake the ground for a glistening crimson lake. Strangely, the dreadful scene of carnage somehow possessed a grotesque beauty, so much so that Möbius could not help but pause to admire it. She even crouched to dip her fingers into the pond of blood to blend the colors more perfectly.

        “STOP!” A furious shout came from a distance and halted Möbius’s movement.

        “Finally.” A triumphant smile graced her lips as she slowly rose to her feet and turned to face the man of the voice—a regal-looking Akashic, clearly someone of high standing, judging from his commanding presence.

        “I won’t let you go any further!” the Akashic declared, summoning a finely crafted dagger. It was his special token—an artifact each Akashic was born with—that allowed him to access the Bibliotheca of Truth, an enigmatic place between dimensions that granted its wielder unimaginable power and knowledge.

        As the Akashic channeled his power into the dagger, it flared with brilliant light. His consciousness surged beyond the physical plane, reaching toward the ethereal gates of the Bibliotheca of Truth. However, just as he was about to cross the threshold, Möbius appeared before him and blocked his path.

        “Thank you for showing me the way,” she said with a playful grin. Then, she lunged forward, wrapping her arms around him and activating her unique ability: consciousness imbrication. This ability allowed her to devour her target, including his identity and powers, on the strip of infinity. 

        The Akashic did not even have time to scream before his existence disappeared into Möbius’ consciousness. Möbius, on the other hand, nonchalantly fiddled with his token. Unexpectedly, she dove it into her palm. She unemotionally proceeded to infuse the dagger with her powers to alter the contact despite blood gushing from the wound.

        “Heh. Here I come, Bibliotheca of Truth,” she whispered, closing her eyes as her consciousness slipped through the dimensional barrier.

        She found herself in an infinite space filled with countless gates. At the center was a glowing orb, pulsating faintly as it floated in the air. It drifted toward her, its light flickering as though deliberating. When it finally stabilized, a flat, mechanical voice echoed through the space, “The Lord of Dreams, Ghroth—”

        “Don’t call me that,” Möbius interjected, “I’m not the Lord of Dreams anymore. Just as you’re no longer Abhoth, but the Bibliotheca of Truth.” Spinning a golden kunai—one of her favorite collections with a radiant sheen that reminded her of Azathoth’s piercing gaze—that she had retrieved from her Infinity Chamber, she said, “My name is Möbius now.”

        “Möbius… the eternal recursion,” the Bibliotheca mused, its light flickering mockingly. “A fitting name for your hopeless obsession with the Lord of Destruction even after being stripped of your power and demoted to the lower dimension.”

        “Ha! And you think you’re any better?” Möbius retorted, staring at the orb in displeasure. “You turned your back on Daoloth for your greed for knowledge. Your madness is no less profound than mine.”

        “Indeed,” the Bibliotheca conceded, moving upward and downward as if giving a nod. “But I doubt you came here just to argue with me.”

        “Of course not. Why would I go to all the trouble just to argue with someone reptilian like you?” Möbius said, reclining lazily in midair with her legs crossed. Then, she tilted her head to the side and said, “I’m here to propose a deal.”

        “…What could we possibly need from one another?”

        “Don’t you want it?” Möbius leaned backward, hanging upside down. Her chest swelled with confidence as she lifted her chin and continued, “The knowledge of the high-dimensional realms.”

        The Bibliotheca’s light flickered wildly—its equivalent of a gasp.

        “I want to go to the high-dimensional realms to find Azathoth,” Möbius continued. “Help me, and I’ll take you with me.”

        “…How?”

        “Simple. Do what you did for Daoloth.”

        “You want me to open pathways to alternate realms for you?”

        “Exactly. I need power,” Möbius said, raising her clenched fist. “The kind of power that can break through dimensions.”

        “It is not something that can be done shortly,” the Bibliotheca warned.

        “I don’t care how long it takes,” Möbius replied. “As long as I can find and be with him, I’ll give everything I have.”

        “…You’re insane,” the Bibliotheca said after a pause. “I can help you. After all, the pathways already exist. But all I can do is provide access.”

        “I knew you were a conniving bastard. Good thing I’m far too brilliant to fall for your trick,” Möbius replied.

        She then stood, closing her eyes to feel the flow of powers around her. As she did, the final fragments of her memories as Ghroth, the Lord of Dreams, coursed through her consciousness...

        In the liminal void between dimensions hid a boundless realm, the realm of dreams, where consciousness of countless beings drifted aimlessly. At its center rested Ghroth, the Lord of Dreams, its massive, unblinking eye fixed on the enormous dragon coiling beneath the sea of consciousness—a dragon she had been guarding as if it were its most precious treasure.

        That dragon was none other than Azathoth, the first life to emerge in this universe. In the distant past, after awakening from its slumber, Azathoth, who was driven by the primal instinct of destruction, destroyed itself and gave rise to Daoloth, the primordial dragon of creation. Exhausted by the constant destruction, Azathoth once again drifted into a deep slumber, and his breath materialized into a new realm, and with it, Ghroth.

        Eons later, as Azathoth matured in consciousness, it awakened once more and roamed the cosmos in pursuit of Daoloth. The two created an eternal cycle of destruction and creation, which gave birth to many powerful beings. Yet, the two never truly connected, not until the birth of Tarones, where their fates finally intertwined. However, their union created a fatal flaw in Daoloth, leaving it on the verge of collapse.

        To save Daoloth, Azathoth made a terrible sacrifice by swallowing the high-dimensional force that resided within it. The conflicting forces tore Azathoth’s soul apart, turning it into an entity of madness—a fool of infinite destruction.

        Even though Daoloth was desperate to release Azathoth from the endless suffering, it lacked the strength to do it alone. Therefore, it placed its faith in future possibilities, resolving to form a pact with Ghroth, who was hopelessly obsessed with Azathoth.         Together, they devised a plan: Ghroth would plunge Azathoth’s fractured consciousness into the depths of the realm of dreams, while Daoloth, with its follower, Abhoth, would traverse countless parallel worlds in search of the means to restore Azathoth’s sanity.

        Eventually, Daoloth found a solution, one that required immense time and patience. Nonetheless, Ghroth did not care. Its existence was defined solely by its love for Azathoth, and every moment of its consciousness revolved around the dormant dragon. However, Ghroth finally realized something was amiss when tremors rippled through the realm of dreams.

        “Daoloth, you’ve broken our pact.” Its enormous eye turned toward a woman floating midair. It was Daoloth, manifested in the mortal realm as Tawil the great mage.

        ‘I have merely come to understand Azathoth’s true will,’ Tawil said calmly, meeting Ghroth’s monstrous gaze without fear. “He refuses to remain a pawn in this cosmic game. He has chosen to destroy the board.”

        “I’ll go too!”  Ghroth roared, “I want to stay by Azathoth’s side!”

        “No, you can’t,” Tawil replied, shaking her head. “You are the final piece—the necessary piece to maintain the illusion of error.”

        “I don’t understand! I don’t understand! I don’t understand! I don’t understand! I DON’T UNDERSTAND!” Ghroth’s cries turned to frenzied howls. Hatred burned in her eyes as she glared at Tawil. “If you disappear, Azathoth will be mine! I’ll kill you! I’ll kill you! I’ll kill you!”

        As Ghroth summoned its powers, countless tendrils erupted from every direction, each carrying a force destructive enough to obliterate an entire realm. It lashed out all its tentacles at Tawil, but not a single strike reached her. An invisible barrier blocked all of Ghroth’s attacks.

        “I knew we could never understand each other…” Tawil let out a long, quiet sigh. “But he needs your power, so I’m sorry.”

        She then raised her staff. Elemental forces gathered around the staff and coalesced into a shimmering blade. With a simple swing of the blade, she sliced Ghroth’s vast form into countless pieces that scattered across the realm of dreams until only a faint, flickering orb of light remained in the air—Ghroth’s consciousness.

        “In the new era, the realm of dreams no longer needs a master.” Cupping the fragile orb in her hands, Tawil guided it toward a dark vortex. “From now on, you will no longer be Ghroth. You will be reborn as Möbius in the mortal realm, and there you will find your fate.”

        ‘No! NO! I won’t be separated from Azathoth—’ Möbius’s cries echoed in vain as she was sent into the swirling void. Her consciousness fragmented, scattered, and reassembled as it fell until it finally landed on a distant star, where she sank into a long slumber…

        It was after countless days and nights that Möbius finally awoke in the mortal realm. Afterward, she proactively searched for a way to ascend to the high-dimensional realms and reunite with Azathoth. Her relentless search eventually led her to the Bibliotheca of Truth, and thus, to the homeland of the Akashics.

        When Möbius returned from the long flow of memories, she opened her eyes. From her Infinity Chamber, countless weapons shimmered into existence around her, each one wreathed in radiant streams of magic, their points aimed at her body.

        ‘Azathoth, I will find you and stay by your side, even if I must tear my soul into a thousand pieces.’

        The moment she closed her eyes again, the weapons plunged into her flesh, tearing her frame into countless fragments which passed through the pathways that the Bibliotheca opened. They scattered across different dimensions and formed new, fractured incarnations of Möbius, venturing into the realities to harvest the chaotic forces she needed to fuel her ultimate purpose: to restore her soul and ascend to the high-dimensional realms…
STORY_10920:
In the quiet depths of a remote forest, a pair of slender arms writhed in pain. A muffled scream, smothered by a coarse gag, echoed faintly under the shroud of midnight until scarlet streaks marred the fair skin, the arms freezing in defiance before falling lifelessly to the earth. Only the night sky bore silent witness to the atrocity, pitiless and unmoved.

        “Phew, this one put up quite a fight. Took me long enough to kill her,” a tall young man muttered, a satisfied smirk spreading across his blood-splattered face, a grotesque reminder of his latest kill.

        The man was named Stark, a notorious fugitive on the Heptara Unies’ most wanted list. He had murdered nearly a hundred women. His methods were as sadistic as they were unforgiving, which made his name a whisper of terror among women everywhere. Tonight, yet again, he had found himself another victim whom he ruthlessly toyed with before discarding her in the desolate wilderness.

        “Ugh, I got blood all over me. I gotta find somewhere to clean myself up,” Stark grumbled, tugging at his blood-soaked clothes with disgust. He surveyed the dark woods around him before his eyes landed on a small lake in the distance. “Well, well, would you look at that—there’s a lake here. Seems like luck’s still on my side.”

        Stark strode toward the lake, where he crouched at the edge and dipped his hand into the water. The moment his fingers touched the water, an eerie shimmer appeared from the lake. It rapidly turned into a burst of blinding light that enveloped him in the blink of an eye, forcing him to shut his eyes.

        When he opened his eyes again, he found himself in a bizarre space, surrounded by translucent walls in twisting shapes that defied logic—it was as though he had been trapped inside some bizarre container. High above his head was an indescribable creature slithering in the air.

        “You’ll need more than a creepy monster to scare me!” Stark, though momentarily stunned by the unusual sight, sneered. He quickly regained his composure, gripping the massive blade about half his height—a weapon he had used countless times to dismember his victims.

        Lowering his stance, Stark gathered his strength. With a guttural shout, he sprinted forward and leaped into the air just before hitting a translucent wall. He used the surface as a foothold to propel himself upward, then raised his blade and swung it down with all his might at the floating creature.

        Swish! The blade struck true. The creature was cleanly sliced in half, plummeting to the ground with a thud.

        “Gotcha—” Stark’s triumphant shout died in his throat as he watched the severed halves begin to squirm, reforming into two identical creatures. With their wounded flesh restored, they resumed their haunting, serpentine movements.

        “You’ve got to be kidding me!” Stark growled in frustration. Seizing the moment before the creatures could ascend further, Stark lunged at them, his blade a blur as he hacked them into pieces once more. To his dismay, just as moments ago, his attack did not slay the creatures but only allowed them to multiply.

        Now, four creatures surrounded him with their “mouths”—tendrils—writhing and quivering, almost as if mocking him. The sight gave Stark a sudden flashback to his childhood when he was constantly cornered, mocked, and humiliated. The old rage reignited within him, burning fiercer than ever. He roared, “You bastards! Don’t you dare laugh at me!”

        The creatures’ mocking gestures, coupled with the translucent cell, only deepened Stark’s madness, plunging his mind into turmoil. His perception began to blur, the lines between reality and memory twisting together. He no longer saw alien creatures but the faces of his childhood tormentors, and eventually, the old hatred deep-seated within him consumed all rational thought.

        From his pocket, he pulled out a spherical crystal carved with intricate magical runes, its power brimming just beneath its surface. It was a magical explosive Stark had purchased from a dark merchant at the cost of his life’s savings, his trump card prepared for his escape from the authorities. Its destructive force was said to be capable of leveling an entire building.

        “Let’s see you survive this!” Stark snarled, imbuing the explosive with his magic and hurling it into the space between the creatures.

        BOOM! The explosion was deafening, shaking the entire space while thick smoke engulfed everything. However, as the smoke cleared, Stark, who was certain of his victory, crumbled into sheer horror…

        The creatures were not destroyed. Instead, they had multiplied, each no larger than a finger. They squirmed toward him, their tendril-like mouths opening and closing in hunger as they swarmed him. Dozens, then hundreds, clung to his body and began gnawing at his flesh.

        Stark swung his blade wildly, screaming in defiance, but his strikes were futile. The creatures were too small, too numerous. Each swing of his blade only created more of them. Eventually, the swarm swallowed him.

        Oddly, Stark felt no pain as they devoured him. He could only watch helplessly as his body was consumed piece by piece. His arms, his legs—until only his head remained. And still, he lived, an astonishing fact that horrified him, just like the imperishable creatures before him.

        “AHHHH… Ahhh… Let me die… Please, just let me die!” Stark begged, his voice trembling with desperation as he struggled to accept the truth. However, the creatures showed no interest in his head. They slithered away, leaving him alone in his eternal torment…

        “Life is but a canvas for madness, painted with the colors of fear,” a sharp, childlike voice sang. “May our glorious master feast upon this banquet of despair and ascend to the throne of the higher realms.
STORY_10921:
In a bustling city, an extravagant banquet unfolded in the most opulent hotel downtown. In the shimmering hall, crystal glasses clinked amidst the murmur of well-dressed guests. Everyone, wearing exquisite makeup and a dazzling smile, was steeped in the intoxicating allure of superiority.

        At the center of the hall stood a tall, striking woman surrounded by some of the guests. Her name was Lauder, a renowned collector in the city. This gathering was not merely a banquet but a stage for collectors to flaunt their rare and unique acquisitions.

        “Lauder, is it true you’ve acquired the McCollough Trap?” one of the collectors inquired curiously.

        A coy smile graced Lauder’s lips, revealing a hint of pride, “Indeed, I have.”

        “But that’s the infamous cursed painting!” another collector said, her voice tinged with fear. “Over ten collectors have died after they acquired it… Aren’t you afraid?”

        “Those are nothing more than exaggerated rumors,” Lauder replied, taking a sip of the wine in her hand. Her fingers ran through her long hair as she nonchalantly commented, “I’ve had the painting for over three months now, and as you can see, I’m perfectly fine.”

        “Classic Lauder,” one collector exclaimed, his voice dripping with exaggerated admiration as he tried to leave Lauder with a good impression, “Any piece becomes docile in your hands.”

        The chorus of flattery swelled as each collector vied for her favor. Their obsequiousness fed Lauder’s vanity.         Her laughter lingered while she continued the conversation, relishing their praise. Just as her joy peaked, her vision suddenly blurred. A pure, blinding white smothered her sight as if someone had poured thick white paint into her eyes. Strangely, the white faded, just as quickly as it came, and her vision returned to normal.

        ‘Perhaps I’ve drunk too much… It’s probably time to go home and rest,’ Lauder thought, brushing off the momentary vision loss. She bid farewell to her fellow collectors and returned to her secluded mansion on the mountainside. After a warm bath, she made her way to her collection room, as was her nightly ritual.

        Her steps carried her to a particular piece—a half-length oil painting that had dominated tonight’s conversation, the McCollough Trap. It was a simple composition of black and white lines, which somehow exuded an inexplicable sense of oppression.

        ‘Curses? That’s just the jealous ramblings of those who can’t have what I have…’ she thought egotistically. But then, her gaze froze. “What’s that?” she murmured, her eyes narrowing as she noticed a glaring spot of red in the monochrome painting. Taking a step closer, she confirmed her suspicion: there was a vivid, blood-red stain between the black and white lines.

        “Ugh! Useless servants, they can’t even keep my collection properly!” Lauder muttered in irritation. She turned to call for someone to clean it, only to see the red stain begin to spread.

         “What… what is this?” she stammered. Standing in stunned silence, she watched as the crimson bled outward and eventually consumed the entire painting. The lines twisted and bent, contorting into the shape of a grotesque beast.

        The creature writhed vigorously, as though attempting to escape the confines of the canvas. Only then did Lauder react, letting out a scream as she turned and fled the room. She stumbled down the hallway, her breath ragged after she slammed the door to her bedroom shut behind her. Her chest heaved as she slumped onto the floor with her back pressed against the door.

        “Wh-what was that monster? Ah!” she gasped. Suddenly, a sharp pain shot through her eyes. She reflexively shut her eyes tightly against the agony. When the pain finally subsided, she hesitantly opened them again, only to witness a picture that made her blood run cold—everything around her had become monochrome lines, reduced to unnerving patterns just like the cursed painting.

        What frightened her even more—dozens of crimson dots emerged between the lines, and one by one, they coalesced into grotesque beasts, each writhing and clawing, desperate to break free.

        Panic surged through her. She threw open the door to escape, only to find the hallway beyond was the same—a labyrinth of black and white lines that stretched endlessly. A piercing scream escaped her lips as fear overwhelmed her, “No… no! Don’t kill me!”

        She ran blindly, her mind a haze of terror, until she reached the front door. But when she flung it open, the sight before her shattered what little sanity she had left.

        She began running blindly, trying to flee from the maze of terror, until she reached the front door. However, when she flung it open, what she saw shattered what little sanity she had left—the world outside was no different. The garden, the trees, the sky—everything was reduced to the same maddening lines. Even the stars were replaced by the cursed geometry.

        Only then did Lauder finally realize there was no escape. Overcome with a feeling of utter despair, she collapsed onto the garden path where her hand brushed against something cold—the gardener’s shears. She recognized it despite its now distorted appearance.

        “Right… It won’t exist if I can’t see it…” she whispered, a manic smile spreading across her face, and without hesitation, she raised the shears and plunged them into her eyes.

        Swish! A splash of crimson erupted and stained the monochrome world, but Lauder laughed, her voice high and delirious as if she could not feel the pain.

        “Yes… Now I can’t see anything—” Her laughter ceased abruptly; her smile froze. Her hands clawed at her face as she shrieked in horror, “No! Impossible! I’m blind now—I shouldn’t be able to see! Why am I still seeing the lines… No! I don’t want to die! Stay away from me! NOOOOOOOOO!”

        Her screams echoed through the mansion, piercing the quiet night. And then, silence.

        “Forever ensnared, forever lost in the endless prison of the senses. The final bell shall toll the sorrow of the end,” a sultry voice murmured, soft and poetic. “Let the despair of mortals weave a path to our glorious master’s return.”
STORY_10922:
In a cramped underground arena, the audience’s cheers reverberated through the stifling air, thick with the coppery tang of blood, creating a symphony of violence as the battle in the center continued. It was no ordinary fight but a brutal underground tournament where life and death were secondary to the thrill of carnage.

        In the center of the right was two fighters. One of them was Cliff, a towering man—over two meters tall—known as the “Iron Wall Giant” for his imposing height and muscular frame. With the strength to crush a wild hound with his bare hands, his ruthlessness had led many fighters to their demise beneath his fists. Though some were lucky enough to escape alive, they were left broken, physically and mentally. His infamy spread far and wide, but greed, like fire to moths, always drew challengers eager to test themselves against him, only to meet the same grisly fate.

        Tonight’s challenger was no different—a foolish man lured by the promise of glory and wealth. Despite his agility and fit physique, he looked like a child facing a ferocious adult standing beside a behemoth like Cliff, who was twice his size.

        The result of the fight was predictable. As in so many matches before, Cliff toyed with his opponent, turning the fight into a cruel game with his overwhelming physical superiority, and his brutality did not stop even when his opponent collapsed onto the floor, defenseless. The gory match eventually ended when the man lay motionless in a pool of blood, barely clinging to life, while Cliff raised his hands triumphantly to the roars of the crowd.

        “Hahaha! I’m the strongest! No one can defeat me!” Cliff bellowed, drunk on his victory. Later that night, he gorged himself on delicious food and fine wine, his ego swelling with every indulgence. After the celebratory feast, he staggered home in a drunken stupor. When he turned a corner, he unexpectedly stepped on something soft, a creature.

        “Argh, what the hell?” Before he could react, the creature sprang to life and retaliated, sinking its sharp, unseen teeth into his ankle. He cried out as the sudden pain snapped him out of his stupor, then looked down at the source of his misery—a bizarre insect with translucent wings, no larger than half his palm.

        It was not something Cliff had seen before. Still, despite its unfamiliarity, its diminutive size made him scoff.

        “How dare you bite me! You damned bug!” he growled. Reaching out, he tried to crush the insect, but it flew away with uncanny speed and attacked again, which enraged him.

        “You little bastard! I’m gonna kill you!” Cliff roared, swinging his fists wildly at the insect. However, it seemed to sense his murderous intent—it decisively retreated, buzzing away toward the shadows. 

        “Oh no, you’re not running away from me!” Cliff snarled. Fueled by rage, he charged after the insect, lunging only to watch it evade him by the narrowest of margins. He was just so close, so he kept chasing, unaware that the illusion of near-success drew him deeper and deeper into its game.

        Unwittingly, Cliff followed the creature out of the city. The streets led him to the edges of a forest, but he was so fully consumed by the chase and the idea of destroying that elusive insect that he barely noticed.

        “Damn it! It got away again! That lucky bastard… Wait… Where am I? These trees… I don’t remember them being this tall…” Cliff looked around in confusion.

        Only until then did he realize that the vegetation around him had grown unnaturally large. What had once been shrubs barely reaching his shoulders now towered over him, their thick branches forming a suffocating canopy.

        But that was not the most horrifying realization.

        “What… Why is it… so much bigger?” Cliff muttered, staring at the insect hovering before him. It was no longer the size of his palm. The creature now rivaled him in height, its grotesque form looming over him. Then it hit him—

        ‘No… It’s not getting bigger… I’m getting smaller…’

        His body involuntarily trembled as the terrifying truth settled into his mind. Fear coursed through him like ice. The creature, he now understood, was beyond anything he could comprehend—something far more powerful than him. The instincts honed through countless battles screamed at him to flee, so he turned and ran.

        However, the world around him had already changed. The path back to the city was gone, swallowed by endless greenery. The trees grew taller with every step he took, their roots twisting into monstrous shapes that seemed to mock his retreat. His breaths turned into ragged gasps, his chest heaving as despair overtook him, just like the countless opponents he had crushed before—helpless and terrified.

        The insect, now vast enough to blot out the sky, descended before him, crushing the little hope Cliff had left like the harbinger of a storm. Faced with such insurmountable power, the once-mighty “Iron Wall Giant” collapsed to his knees before the diminutive creature he had despised moments ago. His pride, his strength, his ego—all shattered.

        “No… Please… Please don’t kill me… Just pleas—” he begged, his voice trembling with desperation.

        Smack!

        The creature silenced Cliff’s pleas with its massive tail, crushing his body like a tiny ant. The once invincible fighter was reduced to a formless mass in the mere blink of an eye, his blood and viscera mixed with the muddy ground.

        “Fools who wallow in their ignorance, revel in your delusions of grandeur, blind to the truth beyond your narrow world,” a cold voice echoed through the forest, its tone dripping with disdain, “But your souls, weak and unworthy as they are, shall nourish our glorious master. Let insanity pierce reality, and let error become truth.”
STORY_10923:
On a lightless spiral staircase that stretched on without end, a middle-aged man, gripping a staff tightly in his hand, ascended with a grave expression in the suffocating silence. The sound of his footsteps echoed faintly off the pale, featureless walls, amplifying the unease that gnawed at his mind.

        The man’s name was Farke, a great mage of the Starmage. Not long ago, he had accepted a mission to gather rare materials that only grew on a distant, uncharted planet where dangerous creatures prowled. Though the task was fraught with peril, Farke’s considerable experience had seen him through, allowing him to complete the mission without harm.

        While he piloted his spaceship back across the cosmos. He paused to admire the birth of a new star—a moment of cosmic beauty that filled the sky with radiant brilliance. However, as the light enveloped him, his vision blurred, and he lost consciousness. By the time he awoke, he found himself trapped in this strange, labyrinthine staircase.

        Farke had tried every spell attacking the walls and the stairs to create a way out, but his magic only dissipated into nothingness. Drained and helpless, he gave up on using magic and turned to exploration, hoping to uncover some clue about this eerie space.

        Yet no matter how far he walked, the walls remained the same—pale and featureless. Only the steps beneath his feet shifted subtly, giving him a faint reassurance that he was moving forward and not simply treading in place.

        Time itself seemed to dissolve in this eternal staircase. Just as Farke felt the crushing weight of despair begin to take hold, a sound broke through the silence: footsteps. His heart leapt with sudden hope. He quickened his pace, running toward the source of the sound, desperate to escape the suffocating isolation.

        The footsteps grew louder, and soon, at a bend in the staircase, he came face-to-face with another person—a man in tattered clothing, his face obscured by a thick, unkempt beard.

        “Thank goodness! Finally, someone else!” Farke exclaimed, his voice trembling with relief. “Please, tell me—what is this place? How do we get out of here?”

        The man’s lips moved, but his voice was faint and broken, as if he had not spoken in years. “...ll you…”

        “Pardon?” Farke stepped closer, his brow furrowed in confusion.

        “I… I’ll kill you!” The man abruptly lifted his head, his bloodshot eyes wide with unhinged fury. “I’ll kill you! Kill you!”

        Before Farke could react, the man summoned a staff and hurled a spell at him.

        Farke dodged clumsily, his mind reeling as he yelled, “Wh-why are you attacking me? If we work together, we could escape this place!”

        “There’s no escape…” the man replied, his voice filled with despair. “But… I might finally be free if you’re gone!”

        The man’s attacks grew more ferocious. Farke had no choice but to defend himself, raising his staff to counter the onslaught. The battle raged on until, at last, Farke managed to overpower his gaunt and frail opponent, landing a decisive blow that sent the man crumpling to the ground, unconscious.

        ‘He’s a mage like me… His strength in magic is formidable… almost equal to mine… ’ Farke thought grimly, his grip tightening on the staff. ‘But he really meant it when he tried to kill me. If I don’t kill him now, I’ll regret it later…’ He then approached the fallen man and raised his staff for a finishing strike. However, just as he prepared to deliver the fatal blow, countless pale hands erupted from the walls and stairs, grasping the unconscious man and dragging him until his body completely disappeared into the featureless surface.

        “Who… Who’s there? Show yourself!” Farke shouted into the emptiness. His voice echoed through the staircase, but there was no response, only silence.

        “Damn it… DAMN IT! I’ll find out who you are!” Farke’s sanity cracked. The series of incomprehensible horrors had pushed him to the brink, his mind teetering on the edge of madness. He sprinted up the endless staircase, lashing out his frustration at the walls and steps.

        His magic carved deep scars into the pale surface until his frantic charge ended as he tripped over something cold. He looked down and saw a skeletal corpse at his feet.

        He recoiled in horror as his gaze fell to the corpse’s deformed hand—its middle and ring fingers were missing a joint.

        “No… no, it can’t be…” Farke whispered. Trembling, he raised his right hand. The same deformity stared right back at him—the missing joints were a scar he had carried ever since his first mission as a mage, when a monster had mutilated his hand.

        A dreadful realization clawed its way into his mind, leaving him trembling with fear.

        “NO! It CAN’T BE!” Farke frantically searched the corpse. Around its neck, he found a rusted silver locket that held an eerily familiar photograph, a faded image of a woman holding a baby—his wife and child. 

        “Hahaha… So this is how it ends… This is my fate… forever trapped on this staircase…” The discovery plunged Farke into the depths of despair. His laughter dissolved into sobs. Raising his staff, he pressed its tip to his chest and conjured a magical sphere that could pierce his heart; all he needed was a simple push. “If drowning in solitude is my destiny, I’d rather end this torment once and for all… ARGH!”

        However, as the sphere charged, a sudden pain wracked his body, forcing him to drop the staff. He tried again, only to be stopped by the same agony. His legs buckled under the weight of the brutal reality. He murmured in disbelief, “...So even death is beyond my reach… Wait…”

        Only then did Farke recall what the man had said and the spells he had cast. The truth struck him like a hammer, and he let out a broken laugh, more pained than any scream. “So he was me… I’ll go mad in this place, die alone, and become another skeleton on these cursed stairs… Hahaha…”

        With staggering steps, Farke resumed his climb, like a feeble creature forcibly washed away by the inescapable tide of fate until it reached its doomed end.

        Behind him, pale hands emerged again and pulled the skeleton into the staircase, devouring the maddened soul it had contained.

        “Madness with despairing fear is the most exquisite feast,” a raspy voice whispered through the mysterious staircase. “May this delicacy nourish the soul of my glorious master and the dreams she holds.”
STORY_10924:
It was a scorching afternoon. An old woman diligently tilled the barren soil with her hoe. Sweat trickled down her deeply lined face. After hours of physical labor, her head began to spin because of exhaustion. Just as she was about to collapse, a pair of flawless, alabaster arms caught her.

        “Mother, are you all right?” the maiden asked with concern.

        “Ah… Medusa, you’re back from the academy.”

        “Yes, and I’ll take it from here. Go back to the house and rest,” Medusa said. She gently took the hoe from her mother’s hands and began to work the fields until sunset.

        Drained by hours of farmwork, Medusa made her way to the seashore, her skin covered in sweat and dirt. She dampened a clean towel in the ocean water and wiped her face. The calm water reflected a beautiful girl, youthful and radiant. Even dirt could not hide the brilliance in her bright, lively eyes. She had a face that could inspire awe in anyone who beheld it.

        However, Medusa did not see beauty in her reflection, only invisible chains, a girl shackled by poverty, burdened by an aging mother, forced to live in this desolate corner of the suburb while the vast, exciting world lay beyond her reach.

        “No, I will never give up,” Medusa muttered through gritted teeth. Her frustration boiled over as she picked up a stone and hurled it into the ocean, sending ripples across the calm surface. As if trying to silence fate with her defiance, she grumbled, “I will achieve greatness and live an extraordinary life where glory and applause will never die and bring me the highest honor!”

        “Heh!” A soft, mocking laugh came from nearby, shattering Medusa’s moment of resolve.

        She jumped to her feet, her voice sharp with anger. “Who is it? Stop eavesdropping and show yourself!”

        “I was here first. It is you who disturbed my peace,” said a towering man emerging from the waters, swimming around a jagged rock. His face, wet from the sea, conveyed a commanding presence, someone of strength and authority. He was none other than Poseidon, the God of the Sea, the ruler of the vast oceans, and the brother of the King of the Gods, Zeus.

        “Who… are you?” Medusa asked, her tone softened as his imposing aura diminished her fury.

        “You want to achieve greatness, you said?” Instead of answering Medusa’s question, Poseidon posed one of his own, his deep voice brimming with curiosity.

        “...Yes. Isn’t that what everyone desires?” Medusa replied, her eyes lighting up with hope. “Everyone dreams of becoming a hero, of leaving their mark on the world.”

        “But do you know the price of becoming a hero?” he asked, amused as if he had heard the innocent words of a child. With an almost fatherly tone, he continued, “A hero must face the fear of death, endure the agony of betrayal, fight endless battles, and shoulder responsibilities so heavy they will crush you… Can you, a delicate little girl, rise to such burdens?”

        “I…” Medusa hesitated, shaken by his words. However, she quickly retorted, “Who hasn’t suffered in life? At least heroes shine brightly, even if only for a moment.”

        “Foolish child,” Poseidon scoffed. He looked at her with quiet exasperation if he was talking to an ignorant child. “If you truly wish to grasp glory, then become a priestess. Leave this barren countryside and see the world, and then you will come to understand the insignificance of mankind and recognize your limitations.” 

        “And then I will prove my worth and achieve my dream.” Medusa lifted her head. Illuminated by her newfound confidence and determination, her exquisite features looked even more dazzling than ever, and for a fleeting moment, Poseidon’s heart skipped a beat.

        “I will live a life of greatness,” Medusa declared with conviction, unaware that her courage and recklessness would soon lead her to an irreversible tragedy—

        Medusa did become a priestess, and she fell in love with Poseidon. While romance continued to blossom between the two, Poseidon often hummed a tune, a demonic melody which she unknowingly memorized and later sang before Athena. The goddess, enraged, placed a curse on her and transformed her into a gorgon, a monster with a serpent’s body and hair. In the end, Medusa, indeed, embarked on a path of “greatness”, only different from what she had envisioned…

STORY_10950:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch. 6

        In the grand and majestic Hall of Magic deep within the Midsummer Palace of Fairy Hollow, every detail of its refined decor emphasized its significance.

        At the center of the hall stood a golden pedestal, atop which rested an ancient, weighty tome. Despite its blank and featureless cover, it had a dreadfully awe-inspiring presence that drew all who gazed upon it into its mysterious depths. It was the Bythos, the most precious magical grimoire of the Nomarie fairies, passed down through the ages.

        The Nomarie fairies, born alongside the primordial dragons’ creation of Tarones, were gifted with the power to harness elemental forces. Their exceptional magical talents earned them the favor of Daoloth, the Lord of Creation, who bestowed upon them the Bythos, a magical grimoire that stored various powerful magic spells. 

        Written in higher-dimensional script, the grimoire’s contents were nearly impossible to comprehend; one could only decipher a fraction of its secrets even with a lifetime of effort. Still, even the smallest fragment of its knowledge granted immeasurable power. However, the primordial dragons later disappeared, and the Nomarie fairies lost their guide. With a limited lifespan, the fairies decided to pass down the sacred mission of decoding the Bythos across generations.

        Beside the golden pedestal lay a silver coffin. Inside rested a young woman, her eyes closed in eternal slumber, yet her beauty remained undiminished even in her deathbed. Her body, shrouded in a strange magical formula, remained uncorrupted, giving her an illusion of life, as though she might awaken at any moment.

        Kneeling beside the coffin was a young man. His hand gently caressed the woman’s face as he whispered with deep affection, “Carmen… Soon, we’ll meet again. This time, I will make sure you live a life of happiness…”

        The young man, named Oberon, was the King of the Nomarie Fairies. The woman in the coffin, Carmen, was a Protodemon and also the third reincarnation of Cellulu, Oberon’s beloved wife.

        Years ago, Cellulu had met her untimely demise due to illness. Unable to move on, Oberon devoted himself to the Bythos, eventually unraveling a spell to track one’s soul. He found Cellulu’s reincarnation, Huaxu, but he arrived a step too late—she had already married another man. Though heartbroken, Oberon chose to protect her from afar. Yet, tragedy struck again when the demons took her hostage, using her as leverage against him. Refusing to become a burden, she took her own life and perished alongside her captors.

        Determined to prevent history from repeating, Oberon sought out Cellulu’s next reincarnation, Bixia, as soon as he could. In that life, the two fell deeply in love, and for a brief, beautiful moment, he believed they would finally grow old together. Yet, their happiness was short-lived as Bixia fell victim to a cursed venom that drove her into a murderous frenzy. With no cure to be found, Oberon had no choice but to end her life with his own hands. 

        Overwhelmed by the weight of guilt, Oberon was convinced that his presence brought only misfortune to those he loved. So, he vowed to stay away, watching over Cellulu’s next reincarnation, Carmen, silently from the shadows. Despite his resolve, fate brought them together once more on the battlefield, where Carmen, as the leader of the demon troop, died, impaled by the blades of the Nomarie fairies.

        Both physically and mentally devastated, Oberon brought Carmen’s body back to the Hall of Magic and tethered her soul to it using the Bythos. It was not after countless sleepless nights that he discovered the spell he sought—the magic to alter the cycle of reincarnation.

        Oberon stood and drew a golden dagger. Slowly, he began carving intricate symbols into the left side of his chest, magical runes passed down from ancient times and laden with immense power.

        When the symbols formed a circle, the skin within it miraculously turned translucent, revealing his pulsating heart. Unlike any ordinary heart, Oberon’s was composed of five radiant colors—a unique trait of the Nomarie fairies.

        Born as incorporeal, prismatic spirits, the Nomarie fairies only gained physical forms as their essence coalesced into a fairy heart after gathering enough elements. As their magical power grew, their hearts would bear the colors of elements, and only a few in the Nomarie fairies’ history had achieved a heart of five colors—the Quinfaerie Heart. As the King of the Fairies, Oberon was the sole bearer of such a heart in his generation.

        “I failed you… I am the reason for all your suffering… That’s why I must give you happiness,” Oberon murmured, his gaze fixed on Carmen’s face. “Even if it costs me everything.”

        Placing a hand over his chest, he began chanting in a strange, enigmatic tongue, the primordial language that deconstructed the very fabric of the world. With each word he uttered, his heart throbbed violently, its vibrant hues trembling before spilling forth a radiant energy that coalesced into a glowing, palm-sized orb of colors.

        The excruciating process left Oberon drained and trembling, his forehead drenched in cold sweat. He could barely stand without using the coffin for support. Still, he smiled, the curve of his lips tinged with both relief and a maddening fervor.

        “This time, you’ll be reborn as a Nomarie fairy, with the strongest body and unparalleled magical talent…” Extending his hand over Carmen’s body, he removed the magic that was holding her soul. The body crumbled to ash and scattered into the air as soon as a mass of light—Carmen’s soul—emerged and fused with the glowing orb. With the elemental forces gathered within, the orb quickly transformed into a new fairy heart, then the body of a small child.

        Oberon caught the child in his arms. She opened her clear, innocent eyes and asked, “Who… who are you?”

        “I am Oberon, King of Fairy Hollow, and I will protect you as you grow,” Oberon replied. His voice brimmed with unmistakable tenderness as he looked down at her youthful countenance and gave her his most sincere blessing, a prophecy of her promising future:

        “Your name is Titania, a child favored by fate, who shall forever stay under the King’s wing. In your hands rests the golden stone of dreams that will keep you safe and well fed, upon your head the evergreen crown of laurels that will always bring you victory, and on your feet the sacred feathered boots that will lead you on a smooth path. Your light shall never fade in the ever-changing tides of fate.”

        The spell, of course, did not come without a price; Oberon had to sacrifice his powers as well as his longevity. Without the Quinfaerie Heart’s power, his life would gradually fade away into exhaustion. Even so, he willingly accepted it. He would have no regrets, even in death, as long as he could witness Titania live happily ever after.

        Afterward, Oberon claimed that an illness had robbed him of his fairy heart’s power. Though there were murmurs of dissatisfaction and doubt, he quickly silenced them and secured his position as King of the Fairies.

        True to Oberon’s prophecy, Titania grew into a prodigy and thrived under his protection. Her extraordinary combat and magical talents set her apart from her peers. She excelled effortlessly in everything she undertook, whether it was difficult physical combat techniques or advanced magic spells.

        However, their peaceful days ended as the demons’ attack grew more vicious and threatening, and eventually, during one such confrontation, Oberon was wounded while defending his people.

        When Titania heard the news, she frantically rushed to Oberon. She did not stop even when her shoes slipped off in her haste. When she stumbled into his chamber, she found him sitting on his bed, his torso wrapped in bandages. His beautiful features, now clouded by an inexplicable weariness, carried a sickly pallor. Despite his imposing frame, there was an air of fragility about him, as if he might crumble at any moment.

        Titania had never seen Oberon so vulnerable before, a sight that pained her heart. She instinctively stepped forward, only to pause as she saw Oberon’s brows suddenly furrow. In a sharp, angry tone, he barked, “Enough! I don’t want to hear another word!”

        “Your Majesty, you, of all fairies, should know how dangerous the demons can be,” said the middle-aged fairy standing near the foot of the bed. Though his posture was slightly bowed, there was no trace of submission in his demeanor. His sharp gaze and commanding presence exuded an intimidating authority as he continued, “This is the best course of action.”

        Titania recognized the man immediately—he was Alberich, the high priest of the Nomarie fairies. It was said that he had served since the reign of the previous King of the Fairies. Supported by multiple noble houses, he had formidable influence in Fairy Hollow, and his voice carried significant weight in matters of governance.

        “I will not agree to this!” Oberon reiterated firmly. “There is no need to worry about the demons. They have yet to fully control that power. If we can strike this month and show them the cost of their audacity to invade our land, they will retreat on their own.”

        “...Since you insist, I shall await news of your success, My Lord,” Alberich replied, his words a veiled remark. He then turned to leave, but stopped as he walked past Titania, casting a scrutinizing, faintly mocking glance at her. Just as Titania was about to speak about his unpleasant gaze, Oberon’s voice cut through the silence. “Titania, come to me.”

        Alberich’s disturbing gaze immediately paled in comparison to Oberon’s call. Titania’s attention immediately turned to Oberon as she rushed to the bedside. Her worried eyes scanned him so intently as though Oberon had lost a limb, which made him chuckle.

        “It’s just a small wound. There’s no need to worry.”

        “How can this be called a small wound? You’ve never been injured this badly before…”

        “It was just a moment of negligence,” Oberon admitted, “I didn’t realize the demons had developed new weapons. But I promise you that it won’t happen again.”

        Titania stared at Oberon’s wounds, so severe that the bandages could not fully conceal them. Gritting her teeth, she finally blurted out, “I want to fight the demons too!”
 
        “No,” Oberon replied firmly.

        “Why not? I may be young, but I’m the best in my class at both combat and magic. I’ve even completed the live-combat training without a scratch! I won’t be a burden to you!”

        Titania looked directly at Oberon, her eyes filled with unwavering determination, which was as heartwarming as it was heartwrenching to him. He knew her request came from concern for his safety, but to him, nothing was more important than her, for she was the love of his life. He had worked so hard to keep her safe in this lifetime, and he would not allow even the slightest harm to come to her.

        Placing a gentle hand on her head, full of tender and profound affection, he said softly, “I need you to protect Fairy Hollow for me. Only when I know you’re safe can I fight without any distractions. So please stay in the palace, Titania, for my peace of mind, would you?”

        The man’s plea was so humble that Titania could not refuse but reluctantly agreed, “… Fine.”

        Later, Oberon drifted into sleep due to exhaustion while Titania stayed by his side. She watched over him quietly, her eyes never leaving his face for even a moment. It was not until his breathing grew slow and steady as he had fallen into a deep slumber that she finally allowed herself to show the feelings she had been suppressing during the entire conversation.

        Over the years, Titania had secretly observed Oberon more than a thousand times. Yet, it was only in moments like this—when he was asleep—that she could openly act on her feelings. Summoning her courage, she stealthily rested her cheek against his chest. She could feel the warmth radiating from his body as she listened to the steady rhythm of his heart.

        The moment of intimacy made her heart flutter. It was a feeling as if everything around her had faded away, leaving only her and Oberon in the world with that steady, calming sound of his heartbeat. Only in moments like this—hidden and fleeting—did she dare to reveal her true feelings.

        Titania knew Oberon loved and cared for her deeply. Still, she could not ignore the invisible line he had drawn between them. Whenever she tried to cross that line, he would quietly pull away to maintain the distance between them, which was why she dared not show him her true feelings, lest she destroy the bond they shared.

        Sometimes, Titania wondered if her love for Oberon had driven her mad. In reality, he was always distant and restrained. Yet in her dreams, he was tender and loving, like a completely different person, burying his head in her arms like a child. She had dreamed more than once that he sat beside her on a grassy meadow, gazing at the vast starry sky with her. He occasionally glanced at her, so tenderly that every glance felt like a silent confession of love. Together, they strolled through fields of colorful flowers, where he gently tucked a bloom into her hair. He gazed at her so affectionately as if she were the most beautiful fairy in the world. He took care of her when she was ill, wiping every drop of cold sweat from her brow as though she were his most priceless treasure. Only in those dreams could she feel his love and love him freely in return.

        Every time she woke, she found herself lost in the lingering sweetness of her dreams, only to recall that it was nothing more than a fleeting fantasy when she returned to the cruel reality. Even she could not help but mock herself for clinging to such illusions. Her unreciprocated feelings were perhaps the reason that she kept weaving one beautiful dream after another, grasping at faint hopes that could never be realized.

        After all, she was just a secret admirer who could only steal brief moments of intimacy to soothe her restless heart. After taking what little comfort she could, she forced herself to leave Oberon’s side. Casting one last, long look at his sleeping face, she turned to leave, only to find Alberich standing at the door.

        Alberich revealed a truth Oberon had kept from her: the demons were a far greater threat than she had imagined.

        The war had already claimed over half of the Nomarie warriors’ lives, and most survivors were gravely injured. It had become clear that the Nomarie population—already dangerously small—would face extinction if the war dragged on.

        At first, Titania refused to believe Alberich. However, as she investigated, she found the truth to be even grimmer than he had described, and the wounds on Oberon’s body testify to it—his injuries grew more severe, more horrifying as each return from the battlefield.

        The once-prosperous Fairy Hollow had become shrouded in despair. Cries of grief echoed in the air and made Titania’s heart ache. It was amidst the pain that she made her decision.

        “You’ve come,” said Alberich, turning to face Titania. He seemed not surprised, as though he had been expecting her in the Hall of Magic deep within the Midsummer Palace.

        “Yes,” Titania replied. “I’ve come to end this war.”

        That night, Alberich not only revealed the truth about the war but also proposed a solution to bring it to a decisive end: a spell he had deciphered from the Bythos, which would create a protective barrier that could shield Fairy Hollow from any external threats. However, the spell required a great sacrifice: a Quinfaerie Heart, and Titania was the perfect choice.

        However, this spell was nothing like the one Oberon had cast for her with a portion of the elemental energy from his fairy heart; it demanded an entire heart as a sacrifice. To give up her heart meant to give up her life. So, Titania hesitated. She loved her life, and she wanted nothing more than to stay by Oberon’s side. However, as the scars on Oberon’s body and the countless Nomarie fairies lost to the war crossed her mind, she knew she had to make a choice.

        Stepping onto the magic circle Alberich had prepared, Titania looked toward the west—the direction where Oberon and his army were fighting the demons. Tears blurred her vision as she regretted not being able to see him one last time. All she could do was clasp her hands, lower her head, and whisper the most sincere prayer for the man she loved.

        [i]‘My dearest King, Oberon, may the brilliance of the skies shine upon you, may the earth’s soft soil kiss your heels, and may the gentle breeze of the tides soothe your soul.’ [/i] 

        Smiling softly, she closed her eyes as the magic engulfed her. 

        [i]‘May you be free from all misfortune and your days be filled with happiness. My soul shall watch over you, forever, until the end of time.’ [/i]

        Far away on the western front, Oberon suddenly felt a searing pain in his chest, one that tore at his very soul. Memories of every heartbreaking farewell flooded back to him, and a terrible premonition took hold of him.

        ‘Titania… No… Something has happened to her, but how… She should be safe in Fairy Hollow … Is she?’

        However, what happened next extinguished the last flicker of hope he had—

        A radiant five-colored light erupted from the borders, forming an iridescent barrier around Fairy Hollow. All the demons that crossed its threshold were instantly obliterated without a trace, changing the tide of battle in the blink of an eye. The Nomarie soldiers, though having no clue of what had happened, erupted in joyous cheers at the unexpected victory. Oberon, however, stood frozen, his face pale with dread.

        “This is the Fairy Domain! Alberich, that bastard! What did he do to Titania?”

        It did not take long for Oberon to recognize the magic spell described in the Bythos. Even though it was the perfect solution to end the war, he had vetoed it without hesitation when Alberich first proposed it, knowing what kind of price the spell required—Titania, the only fairy who had the Quinfaerie Heart. She was his world, his everything, and he would never allow anyone to lay a finger on her. Yet, he had failed to see that Alberich would go against his wishes and cross that forbidden line.

        Terrified and frantic, Oberon cast a spell and raced back to the Midsummer Palace, leaving the battlefield behind. Desperation consumed him as he pushed open the door to her chamber, his eyes sweeping over every corner of the room, but that graceful figure that had occupied his mind was nowhere to be seen. With his heart pounding with worry, he grabbed a maid and demanded Titania’s whereabouts, only to learn that she had gone to the Hall of Magic. His panic peaked, and he immediately rushed to the hall as quickly as he could. At that moment, he was still clinging to the faint hope that it was all just his misguided intuition, that Titania was safe. However, just as in every lifetime before this one, he was once again a step behind fate, helpless as he watched his beloved woman falling again into the cruel grasp of tragedy…

        “Titania… why…” Oberon whispered, his voice trembling at the tragic sight. Step by step, he walked to the center of the hall where Titania lay beside the pedestal, her eyes closed in repose, as if she were in the midst of a sweet, peaceful dream. Yet, the gaping hole on her chest, the hollow cavity where her heart had been, shattered that illusion, a glaring reminder that Oberon had once again lost the love of his life.

        “Why… why did you leave me…” Oberon collapsed to his knees beside Titania, his voice hoarse with anguish and despair as he uttered his heart-wrenching question.

        There were no tears on Oberon’s face, his eyes dry as a barren desert; his tears had long dried up from countless nights of loss and grief. Yet the pain ravaged his body, like a disastrous fire that would not die until his soul was burned to ash.

        “I tried… again and again… I even sacrificed my fairy heart’s power… yet she died again, tragically… to protect Fairy Hollow…”

        Oberon’s voice was low, no more than a whisper, as he muttered to himself, his words trembling with a maddening obsession. Suddenly, he stopped. His eyes lit up as he had an epiphany, as though a missing piece of the puzzle had finally fallen into place. With newfound clarity, he mumbled, “Yes… It’s always been Fairy Hollow… I was forced to take the throne after my father died in the war, and I lost the opportunity to find a cure for Cellulu…

        The endless cycle of tragedies had pushed Oberon into an abyss of unrelenting obsession. He needed a reason, an explanation—something to justify why the love of his life had always been doomed to such unforgiving fates, something to convince him that all his sacrifices had not been in vain.


        “Huaxu… If those nobles hadn’t stopped me in the name of protecting their interests, I could have saved her… No, I could have found her before she was forced into that marriage if the nobles hadn’t foolishly reassigned the frontline soldiers…  Bixia, too, died because of the venomous Gu from Fairy Hollow… And Carmen… She died under the fairies’ blades… And now Titania… She sacrificed herself to protect those damn fairies… to protect this cursed Fairy Hollow…”

        “I see it now! It is clear now! She will never be happy as long as Fairy Hollow—all those selfish, complacent fairies—exist!”

        Covering his forehead, Oberon burst into a hoarse, broken laugh that quickly grew into a loud, maniacal cackle, dripping with unshakable obsession. The tender and righteous light in his eyes was gone. His eyes now burned with flames of destruction as hatred and vengeance consumed his mind.

        “Then I’ll destroy Fairy Hollow! I’ll kill every last one of those wretched fairies! And I will use their cries of misery and despair as an offering to my poor, beloved Titania!”
STORY_10951:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch. 5

        In a damp and filthy basement, a girl of about ten years old was shackled to the cold stone wall. A burly man slowly walked toward her, his face devoid of emotion, with a gleaming knife in his hand. Suddenly, he drove the blade into the edge of the girl’s eye socket.

        “ARGHHHHHHH—!” The girl let out a blood-curdling scream as she thrashed violently under the unbearable pain. The chains on her hands clanged loudly against the wall. Yet, the man quickly subdued her desperate resistance, pinning her down with one hand while twisting the knife with the other.

        Thud! Something wet and fleshy hit the ground. The girl’s screams and the clang of chains ceased abruptly, leaving only the sound of her ragged breaths echoing in the silent basement.

        “Ugh! How disgusting!” said a young girl in an opulent gown, covering her nose and mouth with a delicate handkerchief as she cast a glance at the bloodied eyeball lying on the floor in disdain.

        “You know she can’t help it, Sister,” a young boy in equally fine attire remarked as he joined her side. With his chin arrogantly lifted, he added, “Lowly born mongrels can never rid themselves of that scent of filth in their blood. ”

        “Heh…” Despite being tortured to the brink of death, he let out a low, mocking chuckle. Her head drooped, but the derisive undertone of her laughter was unmistakable, which only irked the siblings even more.

        “What are you laughing at, Carmen?” the boy demanded, his brows furrowing in irritation.

        “I’m laughing at you,” Carmen replied, slowly raising her head. Blood dripped from her empty eye socket, leaving a horrifying streak of crimson on her left face. Her right eye, burning fiercely, glinted with a wild madness. For a moment, she seemed to be administering the torture instead of the one suffering it. 

        “I’m laughing at how ugly your faces are, twisted with jealousy,” she sneered, “You just can’t stand me because Father praised me after I beat you in last week’s competition—”

        Slap!

        A stinging slap from the girl cut Carmen’s words short. However, even the slap was not enough to satisfy the girl’s boiling rage. She viciously ground the heel of her shoe into Carmen’s shin, eliciting a muffled groan of pain.

        “You’ve always been a pain in the neck,” the girl grumbled in indignation. “I was kind enough to spare your pathetic life, but how dare you try to win Father’s favor? That’s beyond disgusting!”

        “Right back at you,” Carmen shot back with a cold smirk. “Your devotion to tormenting me over so many years also disgusts me.” Her words of defiance only fueled the siblings’ fury even more.

        Carmen, along with the young boy and girl, were all children of Grand Duke Escamillo, one of the seven noble houses of the Protodemons. The siblings’ mother was the Grand Duke’s lawful wife, making them legitimate children with pure and noble blood. Carmen, on the other hand, was the product of a fleeting indiscretion—an illegitimate child born of Escamillo’s dalliance with a lowly servant.

        From a young age, Carmen’s sibling had relentlessly bullied and humiliated her. Yet, her mother, with her humble status, had only told her to endure their hostility in silence and avoid conflict. Nevertheless, Carmen refused to bow her head. She trained tirelessly and seized every opportunity to prove her worth to her father, but she underestimated how malicious her siblings could be.

        “Humph, you won’t be so arrogant for much longer,” the young boy sneered and snapped his fingers. At his signal, the burly man moved again, this time gouging out Carmen’s other eye.

        The excruciating pain and serious blood loss dulled Carmen’s senses. She was so overwhelmed by the searing agony that she did not even register the man unshackling her from the chains. Her body crumpled to the ground, her vision consumed by an impenetrable darkness. All she could faintly hear was the girl’s haughty voice.

        “We’ll let you live for Father’s sake. But know your place—and don’t ever show your face around us again!” With those venomous words, the girl and boy left with their entourage, leaving Carmen behind—blind, bleeding, and utterly vulnerable.

        ‘I will never forget this day. I swear I will make them pay for the pain I endured today, twice over!’ Even as darkness engulfed her, Carmen’s fiery resolve remained unextinguished, only burning brighter than ever. She was like a fish thrown into boiling water—her skin scalded, her bones breaking—still, she would never stop fighting and thrashing until she leaped out of the water and sank her teeth into the very hands that had cast her into the flames.

        The mounting rage and resentment kept Carmen’s body taut and alert. So when someone approached her and gently drew her into their arms, she instinctively struggled, despite her frail body.

        “It’s okay now. I’m here to help you.” A warm, gentle male voice broke the silence, trembling with sorrow and regret. It was as if the speaker shared her pain, as though her suffering was his own.

        That genuine empathy in the man’s voice broke through Carmen’s defenses. She let her guard fall, her body relaxing as she surrendered herself to the stranger’s warm embrace. His arms carried a soft, melancholic fragrance of flowers, and for the first time in Carmen’s life, she felt the warmth of unconditional love and care—a kind of selfless affection she had never known.

        “It hurts…” Carmen murmured, her voice soft and unguarded. There was an inexplicable sense of familiarity in the man’s embrace, as if someone had held her like this a long, long time ago. Yet she had no memory of ever being embraced by a man, not even her father. That man had never been the sort to show affection, let alone hold her, which made this warm embrace even more tempting to her. She could not help but let herself sink deeper, pressing her face against the man’s chest, nuzzling like a child seeking comfort.

        “It won’t hurt anymore… Soon, the pain will be gone… I’m sorry…” The man’s voice trembled, speaking words Carmen could not quite understand. “I thought staying away from you was for the best…” As he spoke, his voice cracked with emotion, trailing off into quiet sobs. The sound tugged at something deep in Carmen’s heart, causing an inexplicable ache.

        As much as she wanted to reach out a hand and console him, her body refused to obey. Her injuries were so severe that they had drained her of all strength, and finally, she succumbed to a deep coma.

        When Carmen woke again, she was no longer in that filthy basement. Instead, she found herself in a tranquil and comfortable space where she could feel soft, warm sunlight on her skin. The air was fragrant with the scent of blooming flowers, which seemed to fill every corner of the room.

        Carmen raised her hand to touch her empty eye sockets, only to feel the soft texture of bandages—someone had wrapped her wounds with care. The pain in her eyes was gone. Lifting her arm to her nose, she took a faint sniff and caught the faint scent of flowers; whoever had brought her here had also washed her body and dressed her in fresh, soft clothing, replacing the blood-stained rags she had on before.

        “You’re awake.” It was that man from the basement. His voice, gentle and tender as ever, gave Carmen a sense of unreality, and it took her a few seconds to process what was happening.

        “Who… are you? Why did you save me?” Carmen asked, her voice laced with suspicion. Her past, filled with cruelty, had taught her that no aid ever came without a price.

        “I…” The man hesitated. As though he was carefully choosing his words, he only spoke after a moment, “Your mother once helped me in the past, and  I’m simply here to return the favor. You need not worry. Just get the rest you need.” 

        Carmen tilted her head in the direction of the man’s voice, a swirl of complex emotions rising within her. She knew better than anyone that her frail, powerless mother could never have helped a man like him. A man with such strength and skill, capable of infiltrating the heavily guarded basement without being detected and carrying her out without so much as a scratch, would never have needed anything from someone as insignificant as her mother.

        But Carmen had no choice. Even if she exposed his lie and rejected his protection, how could she, a blind, helpless girl, possibly survive in a world where her half-siblings would hunt her down with relentless malice? How could she grow strong enough to one day stand against them?

        So she accepted his explanation. She had to. 

        And yet, as strange as it was, she had this inexplicable feeling that he would never harm her, a feeling that even surprised herself. As someone who had grown up in a world of deceit, where scheming and betrayal were no news, she had long lost the ability to trust anyone, not even her mother. Yet here she was, placing an inexplicable trust in this stranger.

        “I understand,” Carmen replied, her voice hoarse from her slumber. Then she sincerely added, “Thank you.”

        “There’s no need to thank me. Just focus on recovering.”

        A warm, broad hand rested gently on her head, softly ruffling her hair. The intimate gesture, surprisingly, did not irritate her; instead, it caused a prickly feeling in her nose, filling her eyes with unshed tears. She was like a lost child who had finally found comfort after wandering injured and alone.

        In the days that followed, Carmen stayed in the room and continued her recuperation. The man did not come to see her every day, but he was attentive. He arranged for the best servants to tend to her needs, ensuring her every care was met with meticulous detail. 

        And whenever he did visit, he always took it upon himself to tend her. She could hear the soft clinking of a spoon as he scooped a spoonful of food for her. He always blew on it gently to cool it before bringing it to her lips. Every time, he brought exotic potions that were helpful for her recuperation. Whenever his fingers brushed hers as he handed her the potions, she would feel her heart race uncontrollably. It was as if something had quietly begun to blossom deep within her.

        Once Carmen’s condition improved, he began teaching her magic. After breaking down the incantations word by word, he guided her through them slowly and encouraged her to repeat after him. Strangely, Carmen found his lessons rather familiar, as though long ago, there had been someone just like him, patiently teaching her in the same gentle way. 

        Over time, Carmen’s body gradually recovered. Aside from her lost eyes, she had recovered completely, even becoming healthier than she had been before her injuries.

        “You’ve recovered well,” the man announced one day with a satisfied smile in his voice. “Now, it’s time to heal your eyes.”

        “My eyes… Can they be healed?” Carmen stammered in disbelief. She had long resigned herself to a lifetime of darkness, never imagining that such a miracle could be possible.. 

        “They can. Trust me,” the man replied, his tone firm and confident. His words carried an unmistakable strength that seemed capable of dispelling any shadow in her life.

        “I trust you,” Carmen said without hesitation. She followed his instructions and braced herself for the grueling treatment process that ensued. 

        The pain was excruciating, leaving her drenched in cold sweat. Still, she clenched her teeth and swallowed her cries of agony because she did not want to disappoint her. Through sheer willpower, she endured the physical agony and regained her sight. 

        The night before Carmen was to remove the bandages, she could not sleep, her thoughts restless as she tossed and turned in bed. Finally, she sat up and pushed open a window to let the night breeze wash over her.

        The air carried the delicate scent of flowers, the same scent that the man had—a fragrance she had grown to love, but not because she liked flowers. It was not until that moment that clarity struck her—she only loved the scent because it reminded her of him.

        She liked him. No, she loved him. Deeply, profoundly. She did not fall in love merely for his kindness or the fact that he had saved her life. It was something deeper, something even she could not explain. Even though she knew nothing about him, not his face nor his name, her heart had been irrevocably bound to him.

        It felt as though, from the moment she was born, her very existence had been destined for this—to love this man, a feeling that seemed to have been written in her soul.

        ‘Finally… tomorrow I’ll finally be able to see him with my own eyes…’ The thought of regaining her sight paled in comparison to the joy of being able to see the man. She could not help but imagine the moment when she would behold his warm smile, his caring gaze, and the tender way he spoke to her. Her heart fluttered with excitement at the imagination, brimming with eager anticipation.

        However, her hopes were shattered.

        The next day, she removed the bandages. With her vision restored, she saw a servant respectfully hand her a letter. It was a letter from the man—more precisely, a farewell—saying that he had to leave because of some pressing matters, and he was sorry that he could not meet her. He wrote her heartfelt advice and earnest blessings, wishing her a bright and free future.

        Carmen gripped the letter tightly, her brows furrowing deeply. She knew it was not a simple farewell letter—it was his way of drawing a line between them and severing their connection.

        Her heart ached. It felt as though someone had reached into her chest and forcibly torn away a piece of her. She could not fathom the man’s true intention. During the days she had spent with the man, she had felt his undeniable love for her. His touches were restrained yet full of yearning; the care in his voice was unmistakable, no matter how hard he tried to conceal it—every gesture and word had been proof of his feelings. So why did he leave?

        Carmen’s mind raced with questions. She desperately wanted to confront him, to demand an answer. Why would he push her away when he cared for her so deeply? But to her despair, she had nothing—no means to seek the truth, for she did not know who he was, where he was, or even what his name was.

        ‘I need power. Only with enough power can I seize what I want!’

        Determined, Carmen threw herself back into the ruthless battles of family inheritance.
