She poured everything she had—every ounce of knowledge and skill she had learned from him—into defeating her half-siblings. True to her vow, she repaid every humiliation she had suffered, twice over. Her exceptional talent in magic earned her the trust of her father, Escamillo, who began assigning her important missions, and she completed them with unrivaled achievement, solidifying an unshakable position of power.

        Yet, even with her growing influence, Carmen was not satisfied. She craved more—something higher, something untouchable, a power so great it could shake the heavens and earth. Her ambitions did not go unnoticed—her father made her an offer: if she could conquer Fairy Hollow, he would name her the heir to his title and grant her the family’s highest authority.

        Fairy Hollow was the homeland of the Nomarie fairies, a land of bountiful elemental energy. Under the fairies’ stewardship, it had flourished into a haven of prosperity, with fields of miraculous herbs and treasures, and, most coveted of all, the Bythos, an ancient magical grimoire said to have been written by the primordial dragon of creation.

        Though Carmen knew that conquering Fairy Hollow would be no easy task, she accepted the challenge without hesitation. Leading an army, she marched on the fairies’ sacred land. However, the Nomarie fairies proved far more resilient than she had anticipated. 

        The battlefield quickly fell into a stalemate. Yet, time was not on Carmen’s side. It became clear that the demon army would inevitably falter, slowly worn down by a lack of supplies, while the Nomarie fairies, with the abundant resources of their homeland, would only grow stronger as the conflict dragged on.

        ‘I can’t lose… I must claim the title of Grand Duke... Only then can I find him... Only then can I be with that man I so desperately desire...’

        Carmen’s gaze turned toward the King of the Fairies standing at the center of the enemy forces. The king was young and strikingly handsome, yet his commanding presence radiated an authority far beyond his youthful appearance. With every strike, he unleashed powerful magic, effortlessly taking down the demons that dared approach him. His power was undeniably overwhelming.

        ‘If I can kill him, the fairies’ morale will weaken, and with that, I can lead the demon forces to victory.’

        Driven by an unrelenting desire, Carmen abandoned the safer option of retreat and chose instead to gamble everything on a reckless attack—she charged toward the King of Fairies alone, slaying every fairy who stood in her way. Her movements were swift and precise, each swing of her blade laced with deadly determination. Her assault caught the fairies off guard, and against all odds, she managed to break through their defenses and stand face-to-face with the king.

        “Prepare to die, King of the Fairies!” She shouted, raising her sword high and preparing to strike. But to her surprise, the king did not draw his weapon to defend himself. Instead, his eyes widened in shock as he instinctively called out, “Carmen!”

        That voice struck Carmen’s heart like a thunderclap, reverberating through the deepest corners of her soul. She recognized it immediately, then it dawned on her: the man standing before her was the very person she had been searching for, the one who had filled her every thought, her every dream.

        The murderous intent in her eyes melted right away, replaced by a tender affection. Lowering her sword, she withdrew her attack and smiled at him with joy. “There you are—”

        However, a sword pierced through Carmen’s back before she could finish her words. Behind her stood a fairy soldier, one of the king’s guards, who had rushed to protect him. Her face froze in disbelief as she looked down at the crimson stain spreading across her chest. She could feel the warmth of her life draining away with each passing second. A profound sense of helplessness washed over her.

        “Ah… I guess I couldn’t repay your kindness after all...” she murmured, a pained smile forming on her lips. Tears streamed down her face as she turned her gaze toward the King of the Fairies. Her lips trembled as she mouthed her final words, pouring all her love into one single sentence:

        I love you.

        “No... No! Stop!” Oberon, the King of the Fairies, shouted, his voice filled with desperation. He tried to rush to her side, but the soldiers surrounding him held him back. He could only watch in agony as a swarm of fairies attacked Carmen.

        The Nomarie soldiers, blinded by rage and hatred, ignored their king’s desperate pleas. Their blades mercilessly tore through Carmen’s fragile body. Unable to withstand the onslaught, she fell to the ground, blood pooling beneath her in a dark, viscous puddle.

        “No! NOOOO!” Oberon screamed as he finally broke through the barrier of soldiers and rushed to Carmen’s side. Ignoring the bewildered stares of the fairies, he cradled Carmen’s lifeless body in his arms. Desperately, he attempted to heal her with magic, but it was too late—her life had already slipped away.

        Shock, disbelief, despair, and grief collided within Oberon, each emotion tearing at him like a brutal symphony. His body trembled violently, as if his very soul had been thrown from the heavens and shattered into pieces. His breaths came in ragged gasps, and his vision blurred with the red haze of fury.

        “WHY?” Oberon threw his head back, his anguished roar tearing through the air. His voice was raw with fury and pain as he glared at the storm-laden sky. “I distanced myself from her… I stayed away… and yet I still brought her suffering… and led her to such a tragic end… WHY?”

        “I will change this cruel, ridiculous fate!” Ignoring the chaotic battlefield, Oberon rose to his feet. With Carmen’s lifeless body cradled in his arms, he flew straight toward the heart of Fairy Hollow, to the Midsummer Palace, making his way to a solemn chamber deep within its halls.

        At the center of the chamber stood a radiant golden pedestal, atop which rested an ancient, weighty tome. Despite its blank and featureless cover, it had a magnetic presence, drawing all who gazed upon it into its mysterious depths. It was the Bythos, the most treasured magical grimoire of the Nomarie fairies.

        For centuries, the Nomarie Fairies had painstakingly worked to decipher the grimoire’s secrets. Yet, they had barely managed to understand a fraction of the knowledge it held, even after all their efforts. Still, even the smallest fragment of its knowledge granted them immeasurable power. It was through the Bythos that Oberon had found the spell to restore Carmen’s lost eyes after spending sleepless nights unraveling its mysteries.

        The Bythos had given Oberon hope—hope that had also led him to countless moments of soul-crushing despair.

        Years ago, Oberon’s beloved wife, Cellulu, had succumbed to illness and met her untimely demise. Unable to move on, Oberon devoted himself to the Bythos, eventually unraveling a spell to track one’s soul. He found Cellulu’s reincarnation, Huaxu, only to realize a cruel truth—she had already married another man. 

        Though heartbroken, Oberon chose to protect her from afar. Yet, tragedy struck again. The demons abducted her, trying to use her as leverage against him. Refusing to become a burden, Huaxu took her own life, perishing alongside her captors.

        Determined to prevent history from repeating, Oberon sought out Cellulu’s next reincarnation, Bixia, as soon as he could. In that life, the two fell deeply in love, and for a brief, beautiful moment, he believed they would grow old together. 

        Yet, fate was unforgivingly brutal toward Oberon. Bixia fell victim to a cursed venom that drove her into a murderous frenzy. With no cure to be found, Oberon had no choice but to end her life with his own hands. TOverwhelmed by the weight of guilt, Oberon was convinced that his presence brought only misfortune to those he loved. So, he vowed to stay away, watching over Cellulu’s next reincarnation, Carmen, silently from the shadows. Still, despite his resolve to remain distant, tragedy had once again found her.

        “This time, I won’t let you suffer again. I will ensure that you live happily, free from sorrow, free from pain,” Oberon vowed as he gently laid Carmen’s body on the floor. He lowered himself to one knee before the grimoire, his deep eyes burning with madness born from repeated despair and grief as his mind teetered on the edge of collapse. “Even if it costs my life… even if I must sacrifice all my power… I will rewrite this absurd, cruel fate!”
STORY_10952:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch. 3

        A colossal dragon—a Petrogon—soared through the skies, its sharp eyes narrowing as though searching for something. Finally, a glimmer on the jagged cliffs below caught its attention. As faint and brief as the glimmer was, the dragon, guided by its keen instincts, did not miss it. 

        With its eyes brightened with joy, it flapped its wings and dove toward the cliffside, hovering over the source of the light. Nestled between the cracks was a charcoal gray crystal, shimmering faintly with an otherworldly hue under the sunlight.

        ‘It really is the Aurascale Crystal,’ Huaxu, the Petrogon, mused, a pleased smile forming on her maw. ‘With this, I can finally ease Xuanlü’s pain.’

        Huaxu extended her claw, ready to pry the crystal from the stone. Her focus was so fixed on the task that she failed to notice the subtle movement and the faint contours of an eye on a rock near the crystal. What had appeared to be a jagged stone was, in truth, a camouflaged predator—a massive lizard lying in ambush.

        The lizard had waited patiently beside the crystal, biding its time for unsuspecting prey to approach. And now, as Huaxu let her guard down, it made its move, lunging with its gaping maw and razor-sharp teeth—

        Swoosh! A magical arrow streaked through the air and pierced the lizard’s right flank in the nick of time, eliciting a pained screech before the beast bolted away, leaving Huaxu frozen in place.

        Then, a tall fairy gracefully descended from the air. It was a strikingly handsome man, yet the tension in every inch of his refined face quietly betrayed the unspoken anxiety within him. As Huaxu met his gaze, she felt some kind of invisible force drawing her into his deep and enigmatic eyes, in which she saw layers of emotion impossible to ignore. 

        It was a storm of joy, longing, grief, sorrow, and pain—a roaring torrent so profound yet tender that Huaxu, for a fleeting moment, felt as though she were someone vitally important to him. His gaze carried a leaden weight that stirred an inexplicable ache within her.

        Regret. Sorrow. Mourning. Different emotions washed over her all at once, unbidden and overwhelming. Yet, they all felt strangely distant at the same time, veiled by a thin layer of mist. It was as though her soul had been cleaved in two—one half roaring with elation, and the other observing coldly, detached from the moment.

        The unfamiliar sensation left Huaxu stunned, unable to speak for a moment. The clashing emotions and the ineffable feelings of helplessness eventually turned into a single tear that escaped from her large right eye. Even her body mirrored the division within her soul: one half trembled under the weight of endless grief, while the other remained calm and distant.

        Huaxu’s tears left the man flustered. His voice brimmed with urgency and worry as he fired a series of questions, “You’re crying… What’s wrong? Are you hurt? Let me see!” 

        His questions pulled Huaxu back to reality from the whirlpool of emotions. She shook her head in response before tapping into her powers. Under a soft light, her body shifted from a dragon to a graceful, intelligent-looking woman with delicate features. When she deftly landed on the ground, her right hand reflexively lifted the hem of her skirt—a small, unintentional gesture that shook the fairy even more. It deepened the complexity of emotions held within his eyes: a wistful longing for the past, tinged with the resignation of someone weighed down by reality.

        “Thank you for saving me,” Huaxu said, “May I ask your name, Sir? I, Huaxu, will do everything to repay you should you ever need assistance in the future.”

        “I’m Oberon. It was nothing, really. Just the least thing I could do,” he replied, his voice steady as he regained his composure, lifting a polite, gentle smile. “As I assume, if I may, you must be here to gather the Aurascale Crystal, a crystal known for replenishing energy and soothing the spirit, are you? Is someone in your family unwell?”

        “Yes, my husband’s Lumin was damaged during a recent injury. I came in search of this stone to soothe his pain.” Huaxu explained matter-of-factly.

        “Your husband…?” Oberon’s smile suddenly froze, the corners of his lips trembling as if he had just heard something utterly inconceivable. His voice, barely audible and fragile as a whisper, drifted out: “Bu-but… you look so young. How could you already be married?”

        “We were wed just half a month ago,” Huaxu replied, her tone composed and unhurried, unaware that her words struck Oberon like a thunderclap. “So not too early, I suppose.”

        “Half a month ago…” Oberon muttered, stunned by the truth. A hollow, bitter laugh escaped his lips, tinged with deep sorrow. “Ha… so you’re still newlyweds…”

        “My husband and I grew up together. We’ve been in each other’s lives for so long that marriage is just a natural progression, and we’re not couples attached to ceremonies or romantic notions.” Huaxu’s response was unemotional, almost detached. Her words were devoid of the shyness or sweetness one might expect from a newlywed, but only a matter-of-fact acknowledgment of what seemed inevitable—a word most suitable to describe her relationship with her husband, Xuanlü.

        Sharing a bond forged through years of companionship and unwavering trust, the two relied on each other: Xuanlü was always the one Huaxu turned to whenever she encountered difficulties. Yet, their relationship lacked the possessive or passionate nature that fits the definition of romantic love. What they had was nothing but a connection akin to that of family, deep, but unromantic.

        However, both their families and friends believed their union was destiny; even Xuanlü himself firmly held this belief, cherishing Huaxu as if she were his true love. He saw protecting her as his responsibility, and eventually, he was gravely injured while shielding Huaxu in an accident.

        Overwhelmed by gratitude and a sense of debt, Huaxu agreed to Xuanlü’s proposal, and she married him half a month ago.

        Oberon looked at Huaxu, his expression constantly shifting as he wrestled with his emotions. His lips quivered, but his voice stuck in his throat, unable to utter even a word. After several attempts, the light in his eyes dimmed. Silence reigned until he asked in a faint and fragile voice, “Are you… happy now?”

        “It’s… fine,” Huaxu replied. Her eyes held a profound depth as she looked at Oberon, her voice gentle but resolute, carrying a weight far greater than her tone suggested. Her words dropped on the fairy’s heart like a hammer. “But there are things in life that aren’t just about happiness, wouldn’t you agree?”

        In that brief exchange of glances, Oberon understood the deeper meaning in her words—a quiet acknowledgment of his feelings for her, and a polite refusal that shattered all his hope.

        Yet, her gentle rejection only deepened his frustration. His face turned ashen as he stood in silence.  In the end, all he could manage was a defeated sigh, nodding in agreement, and he murmured, “Perhaps you’re right.”

        “I should take my leave then. My husband is waiting for me at home.”

        While Oberon stayed quiet, Huaxu decisively transformed back into her dragon form. With a swift motion, she plucked the Aurascale Crystal from the cliff and soared into the skies. As she ascended, the boundless expanse of the clear blue sky stretched before her, yet her sharp eyes caught sight of the lonely man below. He had not moved a muscle, as if time had stopped for him.

        ‘Why... Why does he look so alone… It’s like he’s been abandoned by someone, left to endure an eternity of solitude in this world of fleeting joy and endless sorrow…’

        Perhaps, if it had been half a month ago, Huaxu might have been bold enough to ask Oberon what had happened to him that left him such a heart-wrenching expression. She might have sought answers, tried to uncover the cause of the inexplicable ache in her chest. Yet, it was too late now. Everything had already been decided. Everything had already been decided. The only thing left for her to do was flap her wings and fly away from this man who deeply shook her heart.

        What Huaxu did not know was that Oberon’s gaze—filled with longing, unwillingness, and deep sorrow—never wandered away from her. He watched her intently, his eyes following her until she disappeared completely from view, as though trying to carve her image into the depths of his soul. Moments later, tears slipped from the corners of his eyes as the emotions he had desperately held back broke free. 

        ‘Why… Why did it come to this… If not for those selfish nobles and their foolish games half a month ago, perhaps I wouldn’t have missed my chance with her…’ The thought struck him like a dagger. He could not help but clutch his chest and sink to one knee under the weight of grief.

        Oberon was the King of the Fairies, ruler of the Nomarie fairies who resided in Fairy Hollow. With his father, the previous King of the Fairies, having perished in a battle against the demons, and his mother, overcome with grief, having taken her own life shortly after, he had taken the throne at a young age. During those dark days, his childhood companion, Cellulu, unwaveringly stayed by his side and guided him through sorrow. Yet fate was cruel—Cellulu, frail by nature, succumbed to illness after only a few years, leaving Oberon devastated.

        Refusing to let their bond relinquish, Oberon spent numerous sleepless nights studying Bythos, a magical grimoire passed down across generations. He poured his soul into deciphering its secrets for over twenty years until he finally uncovered a spell capable of tracing one’s soul and discovered the location of Cellulu’s reincarnation.

        As much as Oberon wished to reunite with her, the demon army breached the border defenses just as he was about to leave the palace. As the King of the Fairies, he had no choice but to set aside his quest and address the crisis, only to discover that the nobles’ selfish actions were the cause of the breach. They secretly reassigned border troops to protect their estates, which ultimately presented the demons with an opportunity.

        By the time Oberon had resolved the chaos and restored order, half a month had passed—the same half a month during which Huaxu had married Xuanlü. The cruel twist of fate, the perfectly timed coincidence, left Oberon with regret and bitterness, fueling his anger toward the nobles only further.

        ‘I was too late… What’s done is done. I have no right to pursue her; all I can do now is ensure that, within my power, she lives a good life…’ Oberon thought.

        A week later, Oberon made his way to the Deep Cloud Glen where Huaxu lived, once he had gathered his thoughts and steadied his emotions. He waited patiently at its entrance for her to appear.

        It just so happened that Huaxu was leaving her home. Her steps froze as her gaze fell upon Oberon’s figure, as familiar as it was strange to her. A wave of unease and joy surged in her heart all at once, emotions she knew she could not afford to reveal. She quickly suppressed inner turmoil, forcing a calm expression and steadying her voice. “It’s you…”

        “I’ve come to see you,” Oberon replied.

        “What can I help you with?” she asked.

        “I want to…” Oberon shook his head, then corrected himself, “I would like to propose a trade with the Petrogons.”

        “A trade?”

        “I’d like your people to help gather resources for us, the Nomarie fairies from Fairy Hollow. In return, we will provide herbs, magical tools, as well as treatment for the wounded in your clan.”

        “That sounds like a deal that benefits us far more than it does you. Why?” Huaxu bit her lower lip before hesitantly asking, “Is it… because of me?”

        “It is, but not entirely,” Oberon admitted. He continued honestly, “We Nomarie fairies are never fond of battles or venturing beyond our homeland. However, there are resources we cannot acquire without leaving our borders. We are willing to exchange what we have for what we need. If it’s not your clan, it would simply be another; it’s nothing more than a simple trade. There’s no need to complicate it.”

        “Well… This isn’t something I can decide on my own,” Huaxu said after a pause. “But if this is your request, I shall do everything in my power to support it in return for your kindness in saving my life earlier.”

        The compelling offer naturally piqued the Petrogons’ interest. Although some remained skeptical about the fairies’ credibility, Huaxu managed to convince them to agree to a trial partnership.

        Afterward, Huaxu became the most active participant in the partnership, venturing far and wide to gather the resources the fairies needed. Occasionally, Oberon would request to join her, using an ostensible excuse about getting a better understanding of the world outside Fairy Hollow. Huaxu, of course, knew his true intention, but neither of them ever addressed it directly. Instead, they remained professional, carefully preserving an unspoken agreement as they embarked on these expeditions together.

        In their shared adventures, Oberon always shielded Huaxu whenever danger arose. He always kept her close, but never too close to cross the moral boundaries. When they discovered rare resources, they always exchanged glances and a smile—a silent acknowledgment of mutual respect and camaraderie. Within those moments of understanding, they found an unspoken connection. Nevertheless, they both remained firmly anchored to the limits they had silently agreed upon and never overstepped the line.

        Under the starry night sky, Oberon and Huaxu stood side by side, gazing up at the heavens. In Huaxu’s past life, he would have shared her joy when she laughed and offered her a warm embrace when she wept. But now, they were separated by a thin, invisible wall that brought them painfully close yet kept them worlds apart. As his gaze shifted quietly toward her beautiful face, lit by the soft curve of a smile, a faint trace of regret flickered in his mind, but it was quickly replaced by acceptance.

        ‘Though we cannot be together as lovers, being her closest confidant, and quietly protecting her like this, is not such a bad thing after all.’

        However, fate is never so kind.

        The demons, who had long been lurking in the shadows, waiting for the right moment to strike, finally found the perfect leverage. They laid a trap, luring the Petrogons by spreading false rumors about rare resources in a distant region. When the Petrogon fell into the ambush, Huaxu took it upon herself to cover her companions’ retreat, staying behind to ensure their escape. But in doing so, she was captured by the demons and used as bait to coerce Oberon.

        Word soon reached Oberon. Frantic, he was desperate to mount a rescue, but the nobles once again stood in his way, arguing that risking their resources and people to save another clan was unacceptable. Their incessant bickering infuriated Oberon, who silenced their protests with harsh punishment and eventually quelled their dissent. Even so, he was a step too late.

        Refusing to be used as a pawn against Oberon, Huaxu fought back with every ounce of strength she had. In an act of desperation, she detonated her Lumin, unleashing a catastrophic surge of power that obliterated the demon encampment and annihilated her captors, but at a dreadful cost that left her body on the brink of death.

        When Oberon finally arrived, all he saw were corpses sprawled across the scorched earth in the charred ruins of the demon stronghold. Amidst the desolation, he found Huaxu, who was leaning against a large boulder, her body drenched in blood and her eyes dimming the second it went by. However, a flicker of light reignited the life in her eyes as she caught sight of him.

        “You’re here…” she whispered, her voice weak and barely audible, like a candle’s flame flickering in the wind, ready to extinguish at any moment.

        Her labored voice pierced Oberon’s heart like a blade. Tears brimmed over his eyes as he sobbed, his voice choked with guilt and anguish as he said, “It’s all my fault… It’s all because of me… I’m the one who did this to you!”

        “No… it has nothing to do with you… It’s just my luck…” Huaxu murmured, summoning the last vestiges of her strength to smile. Even at the verge of death, after experiencing such a cruel twist of fate, she still could not bring herself to be harsh toward him. All she wanted was to offer this man—whom she had always wished to draw closer to, yet she could never be near—the tender words she had not had the chance to fully express.

        “Don’t grieve for me…” she said softly, her gaze lingering on his face as if trying to etch it into her soul for eternity. “I have no regrets… I’m glad I didn’t become a burden to you… and that’s enough for me...”

        “No! How could you ever be a burden!” In the face of Huaxu’s impending death, Oberon cast aside all notions of morality and restraint, pulling her into a desperate embrace. Blood seeped through her skin and soaked into his pristine white garments, staining them with deep crimson. Still, his embrace remained firm and unwavering. He buried his face into her shoulder, as if clinging to her warmth could somehow anchor her to life. “I’ll take you back for treatment. There has to be a way to save you. Just hold on a little longer—I swear I’ll save you!”

        “No… It’s no use…” Huaxu, too, abandoned her reservations. For the first time, she wrapped her arms around Oberon. She no longer suppressed the wave of emotions that had swelled within her heart for so long. Her love, tender and profound, poured out with every gentle pat of her hand against his back, a silent confession of all the unspoken feelings she had carried in this life. Then, she whispered, “Thank you… for coming to find me.”

        “You… you knew?” Oberon asked, his voice tight with emotion.

        “I had a feeling… that we once fell deeply in love at some point in the past… Otherwise, why would anyone go to such lengths for a stranger? ” Huaxu admitted, her gaze growing distant. Her voice began to fade. With her head resting lightly on Oberon’s shoulder, she gave him one last request: “But next time… next time, come find me sooner… don’t be late again…”

        “I will…” Oberon replied with a muffled voice as he struggled to choke back his sobs. “I promise. Next time, I’ll come sooner… so please wait for me...”

        “Alright… I’ll wait for you…” With those parting words, Huaxu breathed her last. With her face still wearing a faint, peaceful smile, it seemed she had simply fallen asleep, but Oberon knew clearly that she would never wake again.

        “Huaxu… Huaxu… NOOOOOO!” Oberon called her name over and over, his voice raw with desperation, but he never got his answer. The silence confirmed the unbearable reality: she was gone. A part of him seemed to have died with her, leaving a hollow void inside him. Unable to contain his grief, he broke down. His anguished cries echoed across the desolate battlefield, wrenching the hearts of those who heard them…
STORY_10953:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch. 2

        It was late at night. While the rest of Fairy Hollow lay quiet under the night sky, the Hall of Magic in the Midsummer Palace remained aglow. Inside, a man stood hunched over a desk cluttered with parchment. His face was lined with exhaustion, but a faint smile broke through as he gazed at the heavily amended sheet before him. He breathed a sigh of relief and murmured, “At last... I’ve finally found it… The magic that can trace one’s soul… I’m going to find you, Cellulu...”

        The man was Oberon, the current King of the Nomarie Fairies.

        The Nomarie fairies, born alongside the creation of Tarones, were gifted with the ability to harness elements. Their unparalleled magical aptitude earned them the favor of Daoloth, the primordial dragon of creation, who bestowed upon them the Bythos, a magical grimoire inscribed with powerful magic spells.

        Scripted in higher-dimensional language, the grimoire was incomprehensible to ordinary beings; one could only decipher a fraction of its secrets even with a lifetime of effort. Still, even the smallest fragment of its knowledge granted its reader unimaginable power. However, the primordial dragons later disappeared, and the Nomarie fairies lost their guide. Given the restriction of mortality, they decided to pass down the sacred mission of decoding the Bythos across generations.

        Over the past twenty years, Oberon had immersed himself in the study of Bythos, spending countless sleepless nights deciphering its mysteries. Apart from the time when he was required to fulfill his duty as the King of the Fairies, he barely left the Hall of Magic. He pored over the grimoire’s pages for one reason only: to find a way to reunite with his beloved, Cellulu, who had met her untimely demise.

        Oberon and Cellulu were once childhood friends whose bond deepened with time. When Oberon lost his parents, Cellulu unwaveringly stayed by his side, offering solace and guiding him through sorrow. Their close companionship quickly turned into love that culminated in their union. However, their days as a couple were fleeting—Cellulu, frail by nature, succumbed to illness after only a few years, leaving Oberon to drown in grief.

        Though devastated, Oberon promised to find Cellulu again in her next life. With that vow etched into his heart, he threw himself into the study of Bythos, determined to uncover magic capable of tracing his wife’s reincarnation. And now, after two decades of relentless effort, his search finally bore fruit.

        “Cellulu, I miss you so much…” Oberon whispered, his hand reaching for a small scented sachet—timeworn but still clean—resting on the desk, a gift Cellulu had crafted for him long ago. She had personally picked flowers and herbs known to calm the mind, ground them, and stuffed the filling into the sachet, hoping the fragrance could soothe his pounding headaches from the sleepless nights and the endless burdens as the king long ago. His fingers brushed over the delicate stitching. It was as though he could still feel Cellulu’s warmth imbued in every careful stitch through the worn fabric. 

        Time had dulled the sachet; its once-vivid colors had long faded, and so had its soothing fragrance. Nevertheless, it was still Oberon’s most treasured possession.

        The memories of their happy days together drifted through Oberon’s mind like stars scattered across a night sky—countless and radiant. He still remembered the gentle touch of her hand on his cheek when she woke him from slumber, calling out to him with her sweet, gentle voice. She always brought him food when he was overwhelmed by national affairs, insisting he finish every bite under her watchful eyes before returning to work.

        Every tiny moment, every seemingly insignificant act of care, remained vivid in Oberon’s memory. Her love for him was so profound, so tender, that even now, he could feel her presence in every step he took, in every decision he made. It was as though her love had woven itself into the very fabric of his being, a constant reminder that, once upon a time, there had been someone who loved him more deeply than he could ever imagine. However, reality was cruel. Those blissful moments now stood in stark contrast to the emptiness of his present—a man walking alone through a world that felt colder with each passing day.

        The prolonged torment of solitude only caused Oberon’s yearning for Cellulu to grow like wild weeds, gnawing at his heart and mind. Yet, with the discovery of the soul-tracking spell, he was finally free of that crushing despair, and he could not wait a second more to set out and find the love of his life. Just as he was about to leave the hall, hurried footsteps came from the hallway.  He frowned as a sense of foreboding tightened around his chest.

He quickly strode toward the commotion—the palace’s entrance, where he saw a soldier, bloodied and disheveled, stumble toward him. He caught the soldier before he collapsed, his voice low but urgent as he asked, “What’s going on?”

        “The western… the western border… The demon army has breached our border!” the soldier gasped, clutching at Oberon’s hands with desperation. His eyes brimmed with tears as he pleaded, “Everyone is going to die… Your Majesty, please, save us…”

        ‘The western border? The defenses there are strong—how could they fall so easily?’ His thoughts raced. ‘Let me just go and take a look.’

        Oberon had no choice but to set aside his quest for Cellulu and deal with the crisis at hand. Casting a spell, he transported himself to the western border. From his vantage point in the sky, he surveyed the battlefield below and noticed an astonishing fact—there were only a fraction of the soldiers he had expected to see.

                “Why are there so few troops here? Where has everyone gone?” he sharply demanded after rescuing a group of soldiers besieged by the demons.

        “They… they were conscripted by the nobles nearby,” one soldier stammered, his voice trembling under Oberon’s stern gaze. “Th-the nobles said they needed protection for their precious herb gardens… With most of our comrades gone, we couldn’t hold the line and… and…” The soldier’s voice trailed away as he saw the King’s expression grow darker.

        Oberon closed his eyes and took a deep breath, struggling to suppress his rising fury.

        ‘The nobles again…’ Oberon thought grimly. The soldier’s answer confirmed his worst fears.

        ‘They’ve never changed, just as selfish as they were when Father was still alive,’ his thoughts continued. ‘Back then, the nobles refused to sacrifice their wealth and interests, forcing my father to fight battle after battle with new wounds adding to the old ones, and those unhealed injuries eventually cost him his life during that demon raid…”

        A wave of sorrow and despair washed over Oberon. It was as though history was doomed to repeat itself, a cruel cycle that mocked the very idea of change. Everything he did seemed futile; he was destined to be swallowed by the persisting selfishness of those he sought to protect, no matter how hard he tried.

        Then, a rhythmic clang of weapons jolted Oberon out of his thoughts. It was the demons, advancing once more with renewed determination and formation. Their audacity presented Oberon with an outlet for the storm of anger and frustration boiling within him.

        Hovering high above the battlefield, Oberon summoned his power. A staff made of flawless crystal appeared in his hands. He held it steady before his chest and took a deep breath before chanting enigmatic words. Every sound he made echoed with immense power, vibrating through the air as the surrounding elements harmonized and created a suffocating weight.

        Countless magic circles materialized around him, pulsating with a threatening crimson light.  The air seemed to shudder under the immense energy, soil and stones spiraled upward, coalescing into a towering giant, even taller than a hillside, that loomed behind him.

        It was no ordinary spell. It was the ancient magic left behind by the primordial dragons, now reappeared by the hands of their creation.

        Oberon cast a cold, unfeeling gaze down at the advancing demons, who were plunged into disarray upon the giant’s appearance. Their ranks broke apart like a hive struck by a storm. Yet Oberon offered them no chance to reassemble. His voice, laced with icy fury, resounded across the battlefield:

        “Perish.”

        At his command, the giant moved, raising its colossal fist high before bringing it down upon the demons. The ground shook violently as the impact turned the soldiers into unrecognizable carnage, their bodies reduced to pulp before they could even scream. The sheer disparity in strength shattered the demons’ resolve, and their fear drove them into a panicked retreat. However, the giant was unforgivingly relentless. Its massive hand swept through the fleeing demons and smashed them into the earth, leaving only fragmented remains in its wake.

        The battlefield became a scene of apocalyptic destruction, a nightmare etched into the minds of all who witnessed it. Both the demons and fairies stood frozen, their eyes wide with awe and dread as they looked up at Oberon. Some even fell to their knees, whispering prayers for his forgiveness and salvation.

        The battle ended in Oberon’s absolute victory, but Oberon knew it was far from the end. Determined to prevent such a disaster from occurring again, he turned his fury toward the nobles responsible for the border’s vulnerability. The nobles, of course, resisted him with everything they had, clinging desperately to their power. It was weeks after the battle that Oberon finally managed to dismantle their schemes and bring the situation under control.

        In the end, all the guilty nobles were forced to withdraw from their positions under the pretense of illness. Under pressure from various factions, Oberon had no choice but to guarantee them the succession of their titles. The decision was nothing but a bandage over a festering wound, and the deeper issues remained unresolved.

        But it was all Oberon could do, and he could only hope his actions would bring the kingdom a second chance. Pushing further would only destabilize the fragile balance he had fought to restore. With the border secured and peace tentatively restored, he was finally able to turn his thoughts back to Cellulu.

        Before dawn the next day, Oberon awakened early. For the first time in years, he allowed himself a moment of care, dressing in a robe that Cellulu had made for him long ago. With anticipation and longing, he began his journey to find the love of his life…
STORY_10954:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch.4

        On a quiet night, when the full moon hung high in the heavens, silently illuminating the path leading to the hilltop, a hazy silhouette moved step by step through the dense underbrush. She arrived at the summit where a large, unyielding rock stood near the cliff’s edge.

        Sitting atop the rock was a tall, slender young man, his right leg bent at the knee. Bathed in the silvery glow of moonlight, his strikingly handsome face bore an indelible sorrow. Solitude, left by countless partings and heartaches, formed a pool of cold grief in his bottomless eyes. The water eventually brimmed over and turned into a stream of tears that quietly fell from the corners of his eyes, evoking a heartache in the girl who beheld him.

        She wanted to lift her hand and wipe away his tears, but a searing light obscured her sight before she could do so. Everything before her was blurred and twisted…

        “No!” The girl awoke with a start, bolting upright in bed. Just like countless mornings before, he exhaled a long, heavy sigh of regret.

        ‘It’s that dream again...’ The girl—Bixia, the Xian of Hundred Flowers from the Heavenly Kingdom—sat deep in thought, troubled. Ever since she could remember, she had been haunted by this recurring dream, and she would always awaken at the same moment: just as she lifted her hand to wipe the young man’s tears.

        ‘Why… Why does he always look so in pain? It’s like he’s been bearing the weight of immeasurable grief and despair… so alone as if he’s been abandoned by the world… That sense of distress around him never seemed to fade, just like a wound that continues to seep blood even as time has long passed…’ The mere thought of that young man enduring such long solitude made Bixia’s heart ache faintly.

        How much she longed to gently wipe away every tear that carried his sorrow, to pour every ounce of her strength into holding his lonely frame tightly, to let her warmth fill the bottomless void in his heart, and to give him all the love she had so a happy smile would finally grace his face…

        But none of that was possible, for she did not even know if the man truly existed. And if he did, she had no way of knowing his name or where he might be. How could she possibly search for him in this vast and boundless world? How could she bridge the chasm of the unknown to reach a heart that was likely already shattered beyond repair? Every question only gave her an overwhelming sense of helplessness and confusion.

        “Sigh…” Bixia let out a long, weary sigh as she arrived at the Heavenly Kingdom’s medicinal gardens. Her lament quickly caught the attention of the nearby Xian, Wangshu Yuanjun, who turned to her and asked with curiosity, “What’s that sigh for? Still thinking about that man from your dreams?”  

        “What nonsense are you talking about?” Bixia rolled her eyes at the questions.

        “It’s not nonsense!” Wangshu retorted, “You’ve been wandering from place to place, just to find that man from your dreams. Because of him, you haven’t attended a single gathering in the Heavenly Kingdom in years! Am I not right?”

        “…And? Is that not allowed?” Bixia replied, her tone defensive.

        “You don’t even know if he truly exists! Yet you’re wasting your precious years chasing a phantom—that’s just foolish!” Wangshu exclaimed, trying to reason with Bixia. “Anyway, there’s a gathering next week, and you must attend. No excuses!”

        Wangshu’s relentless persuasion left Bixia with little room to refuse. Just then, a servant came to inform them that the millennial peach tree, one of the Heavenly Kingdom’s rare treasures, had fallen ill. The King of the Fairies from Fairy Hollow had come to help, but he required the aid of a Xian. Eager for an escape, Bixia immediately volunteered, using it to slip away from Wangshu’s intervention.

        “Phew…” Exhaling a deep breath of relief at the belated moment of peace, Bixia strolled leisurely toward the residence of a senior Xian, where the millennial peach tree was rooted.

        It was early spring, and the Heavenly Kingdom was brimming with vitality. With tender green shoots emerging across the once barren earth, the fresh scent of new growth filled the air, mingling with the gentle warmth of the sunlight. Everything just seemed to be radiating the promise of renewal.

        Still, Bixia’s thoughts remained tethered to that lonely night beneath the full moon even amidst such beautiful scenery. She could not take that man, quietly shedding tears in the dark, off her mind.

        To the other Xians, however, Bixia was nothing more than a misguided dreamer, caught up in illusions. They chastised her for her unsteady resolve, accusing her of clinging to a strange obsession that would only lead her away from the right path of cultivation.

        ‘I can’t forget him… He may very well be left all alone in this world if I, too, give up on him…’ Though she, at times, had entertained the idea of forgetting the man, given the hopelessly faint possibility of her finding him after countless futile attempts, her overwhelming longing for him only strengthened her resolve. ‘No matter what, I can’t abandon him… I must find him…’

        Perhaps Bixia’s unwavering conviction had moved the heavens, for when she stepped into the garden, she saw a familiar figure etched so deeply into her heart.

        The man she had been dreaming of for years—tall and slender yet unyielding—stood before the withered millennial peach tree, his straight posture exuding a resilience akin to a bamboo tree. His handsome face, marred by sorrow, looked upward as he gazed gently at the gnarled roots of the tree. Slowly, he extended a pale, broad hand, placing it against the rough bark. From his palm, a soft and steady energy flowed and nourished the lifeless tree.

        In an instant, countless buds sprouted, covering the bare branches in a vibrant display of crimson blossoms. The rich fragrance of peach blossoms filled the air, and the garden was transformed into a breathtaking dreamscape.

        While all the other Xians were spellbound by the tree’s miraculous rebirth, Bixia’s gaze remained fixed on the man beneath its shade. His refined features, just as she had seen in her dreams, and his mournful eyes that had pained her through many nights now appeared before her, vividly real. He was no longer a phantom of her mind but someone tangible, within her reach.

        Yet, at that moment, Bixia hesitated. She dared not take even a single step forward, fearing any rash movement might shatter this beautiful dream.

        Fortunately, a sudden spring breeze came to her aid, causing a flurry of peach blossoms as it swept through the garden. The petals danced in the wind and brushed past her face. Startled, she let out a soft gasp, drawing the young man’s attention. He turned toward her, and there beneath the swirling snow of crimson petals, their eyes met.

        In that moment, Bixia felt as though a missing piece of her soul had finally been restored. Her life was now complete as she had found her soulmate, a dream many spent their entire existence chasing, a miraculous encounter that filled her with immense joy and dispelled all regrets she had in this lifetime.

        “Finally… You’re here… I’ve waited for you for so long…” Bixia whispered, tears pouring down her face, as a smile of joy lit up her face.

        Drawn to her, the man—Oberon, the King of the Fairies—returned a smile, weary yet relieved. What Bixia did not realize was that Oberon was just as overwhelmed as she was in that moment, his mind churning with emotions he could not possibly put into words. She looked so similar to the ones he had loved before, yet also different. Her clear, bright eyes still carried the soul he had known years ago, but now there was a new sense of liveliness—a spirited grace unique to the Xian she had become.
        
        His gaze unwaveringly locked onto hers, as though he might lose her from his sight once more with just a single blink. Slowly, he stepped forward, taking her hand with great care as he said the words he had repeated countless times in his mind, “I’ve come to find you.”

        This was not Oberon’s first search for the love of his life.

        Many years ago, Oberon’s father had perished in a battle against the demons, and his mother, overcome with grief, had taken her own life shortly after. During those dark days, his childhood companion, Cellulu, unwaveringly stayed by his side and guided him through sorrow. Yet fate was cruel—Cellulu, frail by nature, succumbed to illness after only a few years, leaving Oberon devastated.

        Refusing to let their bond relinquish, Oberon spent numerous sleepless nights studying Bythos, a magical grimoire passed down across generations. He poured his soul into deciphering its secrets for over twenty years until he finally uncovered a spell capable of tracing one’s soul and discovered the location of Cellulu’s reincarnation.

        However, fate was unforgiving toward him. By the time Oberon found Huaxu, a Petrogon who was Cellulu’s reincarnation, she had already married another man. Though heartbroken, he vowed to protect her from afar. Yet tragedy struck again—Huaxu was abducted by the revengeful demons seeking to exploit her as leverage against him. Refusing to become a burden, Huaxu fearlessly fought and detonated her Lumin, unleashing a catastrophic surge of power that obliterated the demons at the cost of her life. 

        Oberon, unable to save her from death’s clutch, could only promise to find her sooner in their next life. The agony of losing her again had haunted him ever since. However, he had kept his promise, finding her in this life as Bixia, and in this moment, he knew that all the waiting, all the suffering, had been worth it.

        Feeling the warmth of his hand, Bixia understood the depth of his feelings as though she could hear the unspoken words he was screaming inside his heart. After years of waiting, they had finally found each other—the missing halves of their souls. Even though they had only just reunited, their connection transcended time itself, igniting a fiery love as though they had never been apart.

        Unfortunately, Oberon, as the King of the Fairies, remained bound by the responsibilities of ruling Fairy Hollow, while Bixia, residing in the Heavenly Kingdom, had her own duties to shoulder. Their obligations made it hard for them to spend their days together, and every separation brought with it the torment of longing.

        On a sunny, breezy afternoon, Oberon hurried to the place where they had first met as soon as he finished his tasks. Bixia was already waiting for him. A radiant smile lit up her face as soon as she saw him. Locked in a passionate embrace, they seemed to pour all the longing they had endured during their time apart into that single hug.

        It was only after a long while that Oberon slowly loosened his hold on her. Keeping his hands firmly on her shoulders, he gazed into her eyes with a deep, unshakable affection that seemed to overflow with every word he spoke. “Bixia, I can’t bear to keep being separated from you like this. The distance is driving me mad. I want to be with you every day. So, will you spend the rest of your life with me?”

        Bixia’s eyes flickered with a mixture of shock and emotion as she heard him. She loved Oberon deeply, yet the thought of leaving the Heavenly Kingdom gave her a pang of reluctance. A storm of conflicting feelings raged within her—elation for Oberon’s proposal, but also hesitation and worry at the thought of leaving the place she had grown up in.

        Oberon, attuned to her thoughts, understood the source of her hesitation. “I know you’ll find it hard to part with your friends here,” he said. “This is where you grew up, so I promise, we can always come back whenever you wish.”

        His words brought unshed tears to Bixia’s eyes. What moved her most was not just his reassurance, but the fact that he could so effortlessly understand her without her having to say a single word. No one in this world understood her better than he did.

        “Of course, I do. I’ve always wanted to just as much as I’ve loved you,” she finally replied. “You have all of me, and my heart will always belong to you.”

        Bixia’s answer filled Oberon with elation. He envisioned a future where they would no longer be apart, where they could share their lives and grow old together.

        Then, they parted ways again, but this time, Bixia was not sad. Instead, she was full of eager anticipation that could hardly be concealed. For the next couple of days, she silently counted down the days until she would leave for Fairy Hollow, taking the time to bid farewell to her friends in the Heavenly Kingdom one by one. At the time, she believed she was stepping toward a life of happiness. 

        However, fate is often unpredictable—disaster struck again without warning.

        The day before Bixia was set to leave for Fairy Hollow, a group of humans arrived at the Heavenly Kingdom, pleading for help. They spoke of bandits attacking their village—pillaging, murdering the men, and abducting the women—and begged the Xians for assistance.

        Driven by compassion, several Xians were sent to aid them. Bixia was not originally included in the mission, but the female Xian assigned to lead the group fell ill at the last moment. She volunteered to take the Xian’s place, seeing this as her final act of service to the Heavenly Kingdom before she left.

        The Xians followed the humans back to their village. Along the way, they saw no trace of the bandits but only a wounded villager lying on the roadside. Concerned, Bixia hurried forward to help, only to learn that it was a trap—the “villager” was a disguised bandit. Before anyone could react, he drew a blade and thrust it toward her. She tried to evade the attack, but the blade still pierced her abdomen, her blood staining her robes red.

        “Bixia!” One of the Xians rushed to her side and immediately treated her wound. Yet, her injury only worsened. The skin around her wound turned into a vivid, unnatural blue that slowly crept across her body.

        “The blade… It’s poisoned… don’t touch the wound…” Bixia gasped, realizing something was wrong with the blade. She felt a blazing heat coursing through her veins, spreading through her body like wildfire. It was as though something foreign was invading her, devouring her from within. Her consciousness began to blur, and what followed felt like a waking nightmare— 

        A cruel, bloody nightmare.

        By the time Oberon arrived, having learned the news, it was already too late.

        There he saw Bixia standing in a field of carnage, surrounded by the shattered remains of her companions. Blood pooled beneath her feet, and her once graceful silhouette had been grotesquely altered. Half her body had changed beyond recognition—her limbs twisted and deformed, her skin rotting with pus-filled wounds, like a horrifying half-monster.

        When she saw Oberon, a single tear slid down from her yet untainted eye. But at the same time, the other half of her face twisted into a sinister, bloodthirsty smile.

        ‘This is the Heart-Eating Gu!’ Oberon thought grimly, instantly recognizing the poison that had taken hold of Bixia.

        The Heart-Eating Gu was a deadly curse created by a noble of Fairy Hollow using a powerful spell in the grimoire. Its poison would travel through one’s bloodstream and take root in the heart, consuming the host’s mind and transforming their body into a monster. Once the curse completely spread through the heart, there was no cure—death, or worse, was inevitable.

        Oberon had outlawed the creation of the Heart-Eating Gu years ago because of its cruel and uncontrollable nature. Yet, some sly nobles had secretly manufactured the poison and even sold it to outsiders. Now, through a cruel twist of fate, Bixia had become one of its victims.

        Seeing Bixia torn between rationality and madness tore Oberon’s heart into a thousand pieces, even more so when he knew how kind and gentle her soul was—a girl who would shed tears over a withering flower. For her to now stand amidst the remains of her companions, whom she had slain with her own hands, the guilt alone would crush her.

        To avoid further distressing Bixia, Oberon forcibly stifled his emotions. He smiled gently, his tone soft and steady as he spoke. “Bixia, it’s alright now. I’m here to save you.”

        “Kil… Kill… kill me…” she stammered, her voice broken. Her body was rigid, as though struggling to suppress something monstrous within her.  “If you don’t… I’ll kill you… K-kill…”

        “No! I can’t!” Oberon cried, his voice raw with anguish. How could he possibly bring himself to harm the love of his life, whom he had been waiting for over decades? He shook his head desperately, pleading, “I can’t do it… How could I ever hurt you…”

        Before him stood the love he had waited for across lifetimes, and he couldn’t bring himself to harm her. 

        “PLEASE!” Bixia screamed, yet her body began to convulse uncontrollably. The poison raged again, forcing her closer to becoming a mindless, bloodthirsty monster. More tears trickled down her cheeks, her voice filled with agony as she begged, “Oberon… Help me end this… I don’t want to become something I loathe… Don’t let me despise myself… Please, lay me to rest…”

        “Damn it… Damn it… DAMN IT!” Oberon roared. He could not refuse Bixia’s final plea. Tears blurred his vision as he channeled his power, summoning the elements to forge a gleaming sword, its edge sharp enough to cut through anything. Then, he let out a guttural scream filled with despair, “AHHHHHH—!”

        The blade struck swiftly as Bixia lunged toward him.

        Slash! Blood sprayed into the air.

        The sword pierced Bixia’s throat. A clean and merciful blow was the gentlest way Oberon could muster to end her life. Still, he could feel the resistance of her flesh against the blade, hear the sickening sound of her blood spilling, and see the deep sorrow and reluctance in her eyes.

        “Th-thank… you… I… love you…” Bixia smiled, as if a great weight had been lifted from her. Her body collapsed to the ground as she whispered her final words.

        Oberon staggered forward, nearly falling as he knelt beside her. Trembling, he drew her body in his arms and held her tightly, frantic and fearful like a guilty child. Tears of remorse and grief streamed uncontrollably down his face, mingling with the tears that remained on her face.

        “Why… Why did this happen again… ” he whispered, his voice breaking with sorrow. “Why couldn’t I make you happy…?”

        “It’s all my fault…” Oberon clung to Bixia’s cold, lifeless body, his entire frame shaking with pain. Blood and tears slid down his face, leaving streaks of crimson.

        No one knew better than Oberon that ending Bixia’s life was the only way to save her. Allowing such a kind and gentle soul like her to become a mindless monster would have been nothing but utter cruelty. Still, he could not forgive himself for taking her life. He despised himself for what a powerless man he was, unable to find another way to save the love of his life. The leaden weight of resentment and helplessness suffocated him and drowned him in despair.

        “It’s all my fault… all because of my desire for your love… You wouldn’t have suffered if it weren’t for me…” The overwhelming feeling of grief and guilt numbed Oberon. He no longer yearned for her love; he only wanted her to be happy and safe. His gaze was hollow, his spirit shattered. His voice softened to a broken murmur: “In your next life… In your next life, I will keep my distance… watching over you from the shadows… until you find the happiness you deserve…”
STORY_10955:
Midsummer Night’s Love - Ch.1

        In the distant days of an old era, amid the continuous strife between the gods and demons, there was a peaceful haven in a secluded corner of Tarones, a land with abundant elements known as Fairy Hollow, where the Nomarie fairies, a tribe that yearned for nothing but tranquility, had made their home. 

        The fairies, uninterested in the wars, had one simple wish: to guard their home in peace. However, fate was mischievously unforgiving…

        One day, a young fairy slowly ascended the grassy slope in Fairy Hollow. At the top of the hill, she spotted a young man sitting on a rock near the edge of a cliff with one knee up.

        ‘Just as I thought, he’s here,’ the girl thought. A smile graced her lips, but it quickly vanished as she noticed something. “Oh no, he’s hurt!”

        The young man’s back was marred with fresh whip marks. Blood was still seeping from the wounds. However, instead of treating them, he sat motionless on the rock, his handsome face emotionless as he gazed out over the vibrant, thriving landscape of Fairy Hollow.

        Worried, the girl quickened her pace and called out to him, “Oberon!”

        “…Cellulu.” Oberon turned to see Cellulu running toward him. Her breath came in short gasps as she climbed. He quickly stood and reached out to steady her, then said with a frown, “Why would you push yourself to climb the hill? You know your body can’t handle that.”

        Born as incorporeal, prismatic spirits, the Nomarie fairies only gained physical forms as their essence coalesced into a fairy heart after gathering enough elements. However, Cellulu’s heart was damaged during her transformation as the demons attacked, leaving her with a congenital defect—a body that was far weaker than her kin’s.

        Nevertheless, Cellulu was never timid or resentful of her impairment. She never wallowed in self-pity over her misfortune. Instead, she faced life with optimism and resilience, like a flower blooming defiantly on a sheer cliff face. It was exactly her unyielding spirit that captivated Oberon, making him fall deeply for her and treasure her above all else.

        “Because I was worried about you,” Cellulu said softly, gripping Oberon’s hand as her gaze fell to the wounds on his back. “What happened? Did you argue with the King again?”
 
        “That stubborn old man!” Oberon grumbled, his voice filled with indignation. “All I want is to explore the world outside Fairy Hollow, but he just won’t allow it! He says it is my responsibility to be the next King of the Fairies and carry on the royal bloodline, and I can’t do whatever I like!”

        The Nomarie fairies had a hereditary monarchy, and Oberon, as the sole heir to the throne, was always under careful observation and protection.

        “He only wants what’s best for you,” Cellulu said gently.

        “I know!  But… if I don’t leave Fairy Hollow, I’ll never find a way to cure you.” Oberon looked down at Cellulu, whose delicate face, although she tried very hard to hide it, revealed a sickly pallor which pained him deeply. He wished more than anything to ease her suffering, and it was unbearable for him to see her endure the agony in silence.

        “Oberon…” Cellulu’s voice trembled with unspoken emotions; words alone could not capture the depth of her feelings. But then her eyes sparkled with mischief, and a playful smile appeared on her lips. “How about I go with you to speak to the King? He may seem strict sometimes, but I know he is actually a soft-hearted man. Maybe instead of direct confrontation, you should try pleading with him!”

        “Plead with my father?” The mere thought of pleading with the king suffocated Oberon. He shook his head and said, “I can’t do that.”

        “You absolutely can!” Cellulu declared, placing her hands on her hips. Her frailty seemed to vanish in the blink of an eye, replaced by a fiery resolve. “I’ll teach you how!”

        Cellulu then began demonstrating. She tugged lightly at Oberon’s sleeve, swaying it gently as she spoke in a coquettish tone: “Father, please, just this one time.”

        Cellulu was clearly teasing Oberon, attempting to lift his spirits with her little “lesson.” She knew how much Oberon worried about her condition, and she only wanted to see him smile again, to forget his troubles, even if just for a moment.

        Her playful act indeed melted some of Oberon’s worries away. He knew she was trying to cheer him up, and all he wanted to do was the same—to make her happy. He wanted to heal her, free her from her suffering. Clearing his throat, he summoned all his courage and stammered, “F-Father… Um… C-could you… pl-please grant my wish.”

        His awkward attempt made Cellulu burst into laughter. Her giggles were so bright and infectious that Oberon’s embarrassment quickly gave way to amusement. Their shared laughter filled the quiet hillside, chasing away all the gloom that had surrounded Oberon, reducing everything to a moment of pure happiness.

        At that time, the two hopefully believed that they could talk the King of the Fairies around over time. However, they had far less time than they had imagined. The King of the Fairies fell in battle, gravely wounded while defending Fairy Hollow from the demons’ assault. Oberon, having a strange foreboding, arrived in his father’s chamber only to find his mother, the Queen of the Fairies, collapsed in a pool of blood—the overwhelming grief of losing her husband had made her decide to follow suit.

        News of the tragedy quickly reached Cellulu. She immediately rushed to the Midsummer Palace, where she found Oberon sitting alone in a dark corner in the chamber, his body shrouded in the shadows like a forsaken soul lost in despair and confusion.

        “Oberon!” Cellulu’s voice broke the silence. The soft glow of lantern lights in the hallway streamed into the chamber as she opened the door, driving away the darkness like stars lighting the night sky with hope. The light startled Oberon, who was still wallowing in sorrow. He looked up at the figure that still stirred his heart. His voice was hoarse as he whispered her name: “Cellulu…”

        Her presence rekindled his awareness. Like a lost child, he murmured, “Cellulu… Do you know… why? Why are they just gone so suddenly… I… I haven’t even repaid their love…”

        Cellulu did not answer. Instead, she ran to him and wrapped her arms around him so tightly as though trying to crush his very bones. The embrace hurt, but the pain was a salvation to Oberon, pulling him back from the abyss of despair.

        He clutched at her dress with trembling fingers. He gripped it so tightly that the veins on his hands stood out, as though he were a drowning man desperately clinging to his last chance at survival. He knew deep down that he would be consumed by the ocean of loneliness and the suffocating darkness once he let go.

        He buried his face in her abdomen, desperately drawing warmth from her as if it could banish the bitter cold inside him.

        “Why does everyone I love have to leave me?” Oberon asked with choked sobs. “My recklessness caused my father to die at the hands of the demons.... And my incompetence made my mother willingly fall into death's clutch… It’s all my fault…”

        “No, it’s not your fault…” Cellulu’s heart ached. Tears trickled down her cheeks as she firmly denied his words of self-condemnation, “Your father sacrificed himself to protect Fairy Hollow—he did it for honor. As for your mother… She just loved him too much to live without him…”

        “....But they still left me,” Oberon muttered bitterly. “They got what they wanted, yet I’m left in this world alone—”

        “No! You are not alone!” Cellulu interrupted, leaning down to press a kiss on the corner of his eye, gently wiping away his hot, sorrowful tears. “I’m here by your side, always and forever. I will never leave you.”

        “Cellulu… Lulu…” Oberon’s voice cracked with emotion. He leaned forward and captured her lips in a desperate kiss, reclaiming dominance.

        With grief and despair hanging over him like a storm cloud, he desperately pulled her closer, chasing her tender lips, hoping her love could fill the gaping void in his heart. Cellulu did not resist but allowed his passion to consume her. She answered him not with words, but with a quiet, unyielding tenderness to soothe his wounded soul.

        Cellulu’s companionship, like sunlight on a spring morning, reinvigorated Oberon. He rose again, ascending the throne and leading the  Nomarie fairies in their battle against the demons. It was after countless days and nights of fierce fights that the fairies finally drove their adversaries away, though with a heavy toll.

        As the fairies celebrated their hard-won victory, Oberon announced his marriage to Cellulu. The two became husband and wife to the cheers and blessings of their kin. He held her hand tightly during the ceremony, believing that her warmth would remain with him until the end of his life. However, fate was cruel. Cellulu’s illness worsened rapidly. Within just a few short years, she became so frail that she could barely leave her bed.

        Still, Oberon remained by her side day and night, tending to her every need. He even spent hours poring over an ancient text, Bythos the magical grimoire, by the light of a flickering lamp.

        Long ago, the Nomarie fairies were born alongside the primordial dragons’ creation of Tarones. Blessed with the ability to harness elemental forces, they developed extraordinary magical talents and received Bythos, a magical grimoire storing various powerful magic spells, from Daoloth, the Lord of Creation.

        Written in higher-dimensional script, the grimoire’s contents were nearly impossible to comprehend; one could only decipher a fraction of its secrets even with a lifetime of effort. Still, even the smallest fragment of its knowledge granted immeasurable power. However, the primordial dragons later disappeared, and the Nomarie fairies lost their guide. With a limited lifespan, the fairies decided to pass down the sacred mission of decoding the Bythos across generations.

        Throughout the years, the fairies had only managed to decipher one-tenth of the grimoire. They uncovered countless powerful spells, but none of them could heal Cellulu, whose body could not hold out long enough for the grimoire to be fully understood. Her life, slowly but surely, slipped away day by day.

        On the final day of winter, Cellulu unexpectedly awoke with rare lucidity. When Oberon entered the room, he found her sitting upright in bed, bathed in the gentle light of dawn. She turned her head as she heard his footsteps, a faint, soft smile spreading across her emaciated face.

        “You came,” she said, her voice as warm and tender as ever, but now tinged with an ethereal quality, like the fluttering of a butterfly’s wings before it falls.

        It had been so long since Oberon had a complete conversation with Cellulu, so he froze for a moment. Then, a sharp pain like a blade pierced his heart as soon as he understood what this moment signified—a sign of their impending farewell. He tried as hard as he could to hold back his tears. He strode to the bed and locked her in a tight embrace like a child refusing to let go of his favorite treasure. He covered her frail body with his own, as though trying to shield her from death itself.

        “Look at you, Oberon, being so clingy,” Cellulu chuckled, holding him back. As she laughed, her mirth turned to tears. “You’re making it so hard for me to say goodbye.”

        “...Then don’t,” Oberon pleaded, tightening his arms around Cellulu. “You promised we’d be together for the rest of our lives.”

        “I’m sorry that I have to break that promise…” Cellulu whispered. With her strength ebbing with every passing second, she could only lean into his arms. “Oberon… just forget me, will you?”

        Oberon pulled back slightly, his eyes burning red with anguish. Slowly and deliberately, he declared, “No, I will never forget you!”

        “But… You’re so afraid of being alone… What will you do without me?” Cellulu’s voice grew weaker, her eyes unfocused. She tried to lift her hand to touch his face, but her body no longer obeyed her will. They were so close, but the distance felt insurmountable. Her struggle pained Oberon, cutting his heart into a thousand pieces. He quickly grasped her hand and pressed it firmly against his cheek. He could feel her warmth slip away.

        “That’s why you have to wait for me…” he whispered. “I’ll find you… no matter how long it takes… I’ll come to you…”

        “You’re impossible…” Cellulu said with a faint smile, her breath coming in agonized pants. “Fine, I’ll wait for you… Just don’t make me wait too long…” 

        “I won’t. I’ll find you soon. I promise,” Oberon said. Looking at Cellulu, who grimaced with pain, he forced himself to utter the words that tore at his own heart apart. “So… you can rest now… You don’t have to force yourself anymore…”

        Scorching tears brimmed over his eyes, trickled down his skin until they disappeared into their clasped hands, endlessly entwined.

        “Alright… I’ll sleep now…” Cellulu murmured. Still, her eyes stayed open, as if trying to etch his face into her very soul. She feared that if she closed her eyes, she would never see him again. Yet, no one could resist the pull of death. Her eyes eventually closed under the weight of fatigue,  and with the last of her strength, she leaned close to his ear and whispered, “I love you…”

        Her body went limp in his arms, and her hand slipped from his grasp. Oberon clenched his jaw, swallowing his anguish as he held her lifeless body. He closed his eyes, letting his tears fall unchecked.

        “Cellulu, my love, please wait for me. I promise I will find you, no matter where your soul drifts, even if it drifts to the ends of the earth or the farthest reaches of the stars. And when I do, we will fall in love again—forever this time…”
STORY_10957:
It was a starry night, and for the first time in days, Xuanlü stepped outdoors. He had been confined to his room for recuperation ever since his accident. It was not until now that he was finally allowed to take a breath of fresh air and let his mind slip away from the boredom that had weighed on him.

        “How are you feeling?” He heard a velvety voice as a graceful young woman, with an indescribable sense of tranquility in her demeanor, walked to his side. The woman, named Huaxu, was Xuanlü’s childhood friend and the one who held his heart.

        “I’m much better after resting for so many days,” Xuanlü replied softly. With his eyes brimming with unspoken affection, so deep that it almost seemed tangible, his gaze never left her for even a second.

        Suddenly, a night breeze came and rustled Huaxu’s hair. Fluttering in the wind, her hair danced like silvery threads under the canopy of stars, her beauty so breathtaking it made his heart tremble.

        “They say it takes a hundred days for the bones to knit and tendons to heal,” Huaxu said, her gaze falling on his wound, her eyes filled with guilt and remorse just as he had anticipated. “Just don’t push yourself too hard.”

        However, what Huaxu did not know was that Xuanlü’s injury was no accident—it was actually a part of his carefully calculated plan.

        Xuanlü was injured while shielding Huaxu from an attacking beast. In fact, he could have easily repelled it with a blast of elements from a distance. Yet, he had chosen to intercept it head-on, deliberately taking the blow just to keep her by his side.

        Because he knew—Huaxu’s heart did not belong here, not to the Petrogons.

        Ever since Xuanlü could remember things, his gaze had always followed Huaxu. He knew her better than anyone else, and it did not escape his eyes that she was always searching for something, or someone. Though he never knew what or who it was, he was smart enough to understand that it was not him she sought.

        “Your Lumin… Does it still hurt?” Huaxu asked again, her voice so soft that it seemed it would fade along with the wind. 

        Raising his head, Xuanlü met her worried eyes. He smiled faintly and said, “It’s nothing. It doesn’t hurt at all as long as you’re safe and sound.”

        “You… you’re such a fool,” she murmured.

        “I don’t mind being a fool,” Xuanlü replied gently. “If it is what it takes to keep your eyes on me.”

        “I…” Huaxu faltered, lost for words. Through years of companionship, Xuanlü and Huaxu had seemed like a perfect match, destined for one another. Both their families and friends believed their friendship would eventually blossom into love. Yet, Huaxu had never felt quite the same as Xuanlü had always felt for her.

        She was grateful for his companionship, and she indeed cherished it. Still, there was always a sense of dissonance within her, as if a piece was missing from her heart, a feeling that she had lost something, and she would never be complete until she found it.

        “I can tell your hesitation over all these years, but I never dared to ask,” Xuanlü admitted. “I was afraid to hear your answer, fearing that it might break my heart. But that accident made me realize what I fear most is losing you. So I’ve decided to tell you how I truly feel.”

        Her lashes quivered, and at last, she whispered, “It’s just that…”

        It’s just what? Just that she had a feeling her destiny lay elsewhere? Just that even she did not know where this feeling of grief came from?

        Xuanlü did not press her for answers. Instead, he simply put his hand over hers. His gaze was steady, filled with unwavering resolve.

        “You don’t have to tell me. I just want you to know that no matter where your heart lies, I’ll be here for you as long as you stay here, with me.”

        Huaxu froze upon hearing Xuanlü’s words. Her heart faltered. He had found a way into her life, a way that she could not possibly resist or escape. Slowly, the struggle in her eyes reduced to peace.

        “This place is good. You, are good,” she said at last—she had made up her mind to repay his kindness. She turned her hand over to clasp his. “I’ll stay here, with you.”

        It was after a moment of surprise that Xuanlü realized what Huaxu had promised. Overjoyed, he pulled her into his arms with tears springing into his eyes, and said, “Thank you… I promise I’ll make you happy…”

        He did it.

        Xuanlü was never a schemer by nature. However, to win Huaxu’s heart, he was willing to pour everything he had into this plan, even if it meant fracturing his Lumin, just to give her a reason to stay, and he was willing to accept it even if that reason was guilt, not love.
STORY_10958:
On the day when Oberon, the King of Fairies, returned from the battlefield with grave injury, Alberich was in the Midsummer Palace. He stood beside the king’s bed when someone burst into the chamber. He reflexively turned his head, only to see a panicked girl, Titania, who came in with one shoe missing, her eyes filled with nothing but genuine worry.

        He watched as she ran toward Oberon. A faint, nearly imperceptible smile tugged at the corner of his lips.

        ‘She’s so much like her… so pure and innocent, just like Cellulu from years ago… They’re both so bright, so clean, so unguarded, which makes one almost want to break them.’ He thought.

        Alberich did not hate Titania; it was quite the contrary—he admired her. A child as pure as she should have long since withered in an era filled with so much corruption and darkness. And yet, she had grown and thrived under Oberon’s wings, bright and untarnished, like a sun that had never known the night.

        Oberon had shielded Titania so perfectly that she knew nothing of schemes, nothing of sacrifice. She wholeheartedly believed that the world was beautiful. And it was precisely her innocent and trusting nature that compelled Alberich to tell her the solution to end the war.

        “There is a spell that can create a protective barrier and shield Fairy Hollow, all the fairies, from any external threats. All you need to do is give up your Quinfaerie Heart.”

        Titania’s expression wavered for a moment. Although she left without saying a word, Alberich had a feeling she would agree to his plan.

        And not long after, his anticipation proved to be true. On the day Oberon left for war, she came to the Hall of Magic.
