        “You’ve come,” Alberich said, looking down at Titania from the raised platform. There was no trace of surprise but only calm on his face, as though he had seen it coming.

        “Yes,” Titania replied. “I’ve come to end this war.”

        The girl made that decision so naturally, as if there truly was something in this world that weighed more than her own life, someone worth giving up her heart for without expecting anything in return.

        Alberich’s mind was conflicted. Half of him mocked the girl’s foolishness, while the other half marveled at her courage. For a moment, her figure overlapped with that of the equally innocent and fearless fairy, Cellulu, he had once known.

        Long ago, Cellulu’s smile filled Alberich with shame. Her smile was dreamily pure and clean, so clean that it made the faint remnants of his conscience ache. So he fled and kept his distance from her. Yet now, another innocent girl stood before him, and this time, he decided to use her.

        He was no longer that young man who had been blinded by glory and lofty ideals. He knew very well that a sacrifice must be made for Fairy Hollow to have a future—someone had to pay the price.

        And she, Titania, was the perfect choice.

        She loved this beautiful yet flawed land and adored those selfish and slothful fairies within it. And among them all, she loved the King of the Fairies, Oberon, whose destiny had already been entwined with doom. She was willing to give up everything she had to protect what and who she loved.

        In her eyes, Alberich saw no calculation, no hesitation—only the unselfish resolve to give her all for love.

        Throughout his life, Alberich had seen many eyes—some sought profit, some asked for love, and some begged for mercy. He understood calculation. He understood the idea of cost. But selflessness? That, he could never comprehend.

        After Titania died, Alberich stood before her body, her warmth still lingering in the air. The serene smile on her face seemed to speak of peace, as if she had no regrets in her tragically short life.

        Only then did Alberich suddenly realize that Titania possessed something he could never have. It was not power, nor status—it was her unquestioning and untainted faith in fate, something he could never attain throughout his entire lifetime.
STORY_10959:
The first time Carmen caught Escamillo’s attention was during the family’s winter trials.

        Escamillo had little interest in the event, for the sparring of children was nothing more than a petty spectacle, not even worth gracing the stage of his mind. Yet that day, the moment Carmen struck, he knew she was different.

        She was not “sparring”; she was hunting.

        Her movements lacked the hollow elegance of aristocratic training—no flourishes, no wasted steps. Every strike was precise, efficient, and utterly ruthless as she crushed her opponent—Escamillo’s legitimate heir, his eldest son—beneath her heel.

        Now, that son, bearer of the noble bloodline, was sprawled in the filthy snow, humiliated and defeated.

        Murmurs of shock rose from the audience. While his wife’s face twisted in embarrassment, Escamillo showed no anger; he did not even raise an eyebrow. He merely lifted his glass of red wine, a faint smile appearing on his lips.

        [i]‘What does that child remind me of…? Ah, yes—a wolf. A wild wolf in the snow. Fierce, primal, and relentless. She has this sense of savagery that can’t be taught—it’s something etched into her very nature, an innate instinct to dominate, to crush those who are ‘nobler’ than her.’[/i]

        From that moment, Escamillo knew that Carmen had value.

        Her birth was so ignoble, almost laughable, that it made her a stain on the family name. However, bloodline had never been the sole measure of worth for Escamillo—he would not mind giving his family name to a dog as long as it served his purposes.

        Yet, Carmen was not a dog. She was a wolf that could hunt—and, more importantly, could hunt for her master.

        Escamillo had no fatherly feelings for Carmen. In truth, he felt no such feelings for any of his children. The word “father” meant nothing to him—it was a title of responsibility, a synonym for “obligations” and “trade”. He did not sire children to love them; he only created them to propagate his legacy, to be his tools in brokering power, and to build him a greater fortress of fame and fortune.

        And Carmen proved she had potential.

        So, Escamillo gave her a sliver of resources, a taste of power, just enough to make her believe she had earned his favor. He did not care what pain she endured. She would be his sharpest weapon as long as she remained useful to him, tearing through the enemies in his path.

        Carmen grew quickly. Too quickly, in fact. Her meteoric growth amused Escamillo, but it also terrified her half-siblings, Escamillo’s legitimate children. So, they turned their sights and anger on her. Just like two noble hounds faced with a wolf prowling through the snow, they bared their fangs, desperate to drive the threat out of their territory.

        Escamillo did not intervene in their skirmishes. Instead, he watched with genuine curiosity. He wanted to see how Carmen would respond—Would she be torn apart, or would she rise from the blood-soaked snow and sink her fangs into her enemies?

        He wanted her to grow stronger.

        Sometimes, he wondered if she knew he was using her. Her eyes had never held that glimmer of wishfulness of a child. Whenever she looked at him, he saw no expectation, no longing—only calculation. She wanted something from him, just as he wanted something from her.

        They both knew it, but neither said it aloud.

        Escamillo found their relationship ideal—clean, balanced, devoid of unnecessary emotions or foolish sentimentality. It was a dynamic of mutual utility, nothing more and nothing less. 

        And that was enough, for he had no use for a daughter who wanted to play house with him.

        All he needed, after all, was a tool—one that could help him achieve his goals.
STORY_10960:
Wangshu Yuanjun had always known that Bixia was waiting for someone, a man from her dreams who never stopped shedding tears alone in the dark. The weight of grief he carried was so vividly profound that it made Bixia’s heart ache, and she yearned to hold his lonely frame tightly to ease his unspoken pain.

        Wangshu knew that Bixia could never forget that man from the moment she first heard Bixia talk about her dream. So, she teased her, calling her a fool caught up in illusions.

        Instead of arguing with her, Bixa only responded with a gentle smile. Her resolve remained unshaken as she began her search, traveling from place to place, chasing after the shadow of the man in her dreams.

        All the Xians in the Heavenly Kingdom either openly or secretly mocked Bixia for her stubbornness. Wangshu had tried to stop Bixia from chasing after a phantom, but she never listened. After countless fruitless discussions, Wangshu eventually gave up. She stepped down to the sidelines and waited with cruel curiosity for the moment when Bixia’s hope would finally break.

        Yet, no one in the kingdom could have predicted that Bixia’s dream would one day come true.

        Wangshu saw it with her eyes—a handsome man stepping toward Bixia beneath the blooming peach tree, his voice deep with emotion as he extended a hand to her and said, “I’ve come to find you.”

        Only later did Wangshu learn who the man was—Oberon, the King of the Nomarie Fairies, a man with extraordinary magical power and vast knowledge of sorcery, like the perfect prince who stepped straight out of a romantic tale.

        Then, a strange emotion—something sharp, cutting, and bitter—surged within Wangshu. It took her a moment to put a name to it—jealousy.

        She was jealous of Bixia. She envied her for having what she could never possess, and for one fleeting moment, a dark thought crossed her mind: if Bixia had never found Oberon, she would have stayed by her side, just as lonely and miserable as she was.

        The thought sickened her. She never knew this side of herself: so selfish, so petty.

        But then, Bixia came running back to her. Her face, flushed with joy, glowed with tears brimming in her eyes. Her smile was radiant, pure like morning dew.

        In that instant, all those feelings of jealousy, resentment, and self-pity dissolved into peace as Wangshu saw that brilliant smile on Bixia’s face.

        ‘I know it has never been easy for her. During all those years of waiting, she endured everything alone—the solitude and the mockery—yet never spoke a word of it. She has always been like a peach blossom in the dead of winter—unbroken by frost, unyielding to storms, steadfast in her hope for spring, for the day she would finally bloom.’ Wangshu thought.

        With her mind now at peace, Wangshu smiled. She stepped forward and said softly, “Go now, silly girl. No one will laugh at you anymore.”

        Bixia’s eyes reddened as she threw her arms around Wangshu in a tight embrace. Then, she turned and took Oberon’s hand. Together, their figures slowly disappeared into a shower of falling petals.

        Wangshu simply stood there and quietly watched until they walked beyond the horizon. Only then did she return to her own long and solitary path of cultivation.
STORY_10961:
A wind swept through Titania’s disheveled hair.

        Oberon knelt on the ground, his hands clinging tightly to her slender yet lifeless body. Even as his hands trembled and his arms ached, he refused to let her go. Her body was still flaccid, her arms hanging naturally, her fingers faintly curled—just as they always did when she rested against his shoulder back in the days, trusting and unguarded.

        But her chest was now hollow.

        The fairy heart that once sustained her life, infused with the power of five elemental forces, was gone. All that remained was a gaping, gruesome void in her chest.

        He had promised to protect her. He had sworn to keep her safe and happy. And yet, once again, she died—so tragically, so alone.

        As Oberon pressed his forehead against the cold skin of hers, he could still smell her scent, a blend of sunlight and herbs. It was the smell of early spring, of her life. And now, just like her soul, that scent was fading, slowly slipping away into the air.

        He had failed to save her. Again.

        Cellulu, Huaxu, Bixia, Carmen… and now Titania. Five lifetimes. He had searched for her across five lifetimes, trying to protect her, only to lose her every time before they could have their happy ending. It was as though fate relished his misery, taking the love of his life away just as happiness was within his reach.

        He had tried every possible means, hoping at first to stay by her side, but in the end, he could only humbly pray for her safety. Yet, the fairies he had once protected were the very ones who brought about her demise time and time again.

        [i]‘This isn’t a sacrifice… This is a murder… and every one of you is complicit.’[/i]

        Oberon’s heart burned with hatred—he hated Fairy Hollow, this idyllic and hedonistic land; he detested those cowardly yet greedy fairies who had taken her kindness, her gifts, for granted. He even loathed the world, blaming it for its capricious brutality as it mocked his every effort, defining his love and devotion as meaningless.

        “Ha… Haha… Ahahaha!” A low and broken laugh bubbled from his throat. The wave of anguish he had suppressed for years quickly grew and erupted into an uncontrollable, manic roar. His voice tore through his chest like shards of glass, ripping apart whatever shred of reason he had left.

        He turned his gaze to Fairy Hollow, its verdant fields bathed in the soft glow of peace and prosperity. His eyes were now cold as steel, sharp as a blade.

        [i]‘I swear I will avenge you, my beloved Titania. I will destroy everything that caused your misery.’[/i]

        The moment the vow left his lips, he ceased to be the King of the Fairies. What remained was a man consumed by madness, driven by love and vengeance.

        He swore he would teach those self-righteous fairies the true meaning of pain, of despair, by stripping them of everything they held dear, just as they had stolen her from him..

        His shadow stretched long behind him as he stepped out of the palace. It was as though a silent declaration of his break with the light. His eyes held no more kindness, no more mercy. He walked into the darkness step by step until his despair and vengeance burned down the loose veil of peace draped over Fairy Hollow into ashes…
STORY_10967:
Nesoi, now a heroic spirit, sat quietly alone within the ethereal expanse of an illusory realm. The elements, sensing her solitude, gathered to weave a dream for her—a vision of what might have been, had she chosen a different path…

        Back in Olympus, the capital city of Odyssey, the home planet of the Holy Gods—

        It was a rare day of rest, yet Nesoi rose early as usual. She stood before her wardrobe, carefully deliberating over her choice of clothing—a side of femininity that she had rarely shown to anyone.

        Today marked her date with Leon. It had been a full month since their last day out, and her anticipation for this day had quietly grown over the passing days.

        It was after what seemed like forever that she finally settled on an outfit and put together a flawless look. With the unique glow of a woman in love, she stepped out of her room, ready for her date. However, just as she was about to leave, a haughty voice stopped her in her tracks.

        “Nesoi, come with me to the study.” It was her mother, Semele, also the Queen of the Holy Gods.

        “…Yes, Mother.” Though reluctant, Nesoi did not refuse her mother’s request—she never did, for she knew all too well how much pain and hardship her mother had endured to protect her in the past.

        She followed Semele into the study, where a guest was already waiting—a tall, broad-shouldered man named Boreas, one of the twelve major gods under the queen’s banner and also Nesoi’s superior, who was in charge of the highly valued Sorcery Corps.

        Nesoi’s uncharacteristically feminine appearance made Boreas’ eyes gleam with intrigue and amusement. He pursed his lips in a playful whistle and smirked. “Well, this is a first—I’ve never seen you out of your uniform. You look quite stunning. I’d say this engagement is turning out to be a pretty good deal for me.”

        “Engagement? What are you talking about?” Nesoi frowned in confusion.

        “You don’t know?” Boreas raised an eyebrow, then turned to Semele and asked, “You haven’t told your dear daughter about your plan to betroth her to me?”

        “WHAT?” Nesoi immediately looked at her mother, her voice trembling with disbelief as she asked, “What is he talking about, Mother?”

        “The engagement is nothing more than a strategic alliance to solidify our family’s power. There’s no need to make a fuss about it.” Semele’s expression remained as calm as ever, her tone devoid of any emotion. It was as though she were discussing some trifling matter, rather than her daughter’s lifelong happiness. Her indifferent remark sent a bitter pang through Nesoi’s heart.

        ‘Mother is always like this—ruthlessly decisive when it comes to power. She is willing to get rid of anything that stands in her way, even if it’s love or family.’ Nesoi thought as memories of her past flooded her mind. All her life, she had lived according to her mother’s rules and wishes. She had not even dared to tell her about her relationship with Leon, fearing to hear her words of displeasure.

        ‘I’ve had enough. I’ve always stayed silent. I’ve kept convincing myself to comply with Mother’s wishes, but this has to stop now. I refuse to be her quiet puppet any longer.’ The suffocating weight of Semele’s control, coupled with the emotional exhaustion that had only grown over time, finally outweighed the filial love Nesoi still harbored, and she made her decision.

        “I will not agree to this engagement. I already have someone I love,” she declared.

        “I know.” Semele’s response carried no surprise. Instead, there was a faint hint of derision. “That Tuxia dragon, Leon, isn’t it? I suppose he’s a decent young man with fair potential, but he’s fortuneless and lacks influence. He can’t help you with your career. He may be an enjoyable company for a romantic fling, but as a husband? Absolutely not.”

        “I don’t mind, to be honest,” Boreas interjected with a casual shrug. “It’s just a marriage of convenience, after all.”

        ‘How… how can they talk about marriage, something so sacred, with such disdain?’ Nesoi clenched her fists, her eyes wide with indignation and disbelief. Then, she said, “No… I won’t accept this engagement. I can’t betray Leon and turn my back against the love he has given me.”

        “Nesoi, what do you think you’re doing?” Semele’s voice sharpened. As the Queen of the Holy Gods, she had always expected absolute obedience from her subordinates. Now, Nesoi’s defiance seemed a challenge to her authority, which made her rage flare. “Are you going to defy your mother all because of an outsider?”

        “He is not an outsider! He is the man I love,” Nesoi argued.

        “Enough!” Semele slashed her hand down in the air and demanded, “Let me make this clear: you will be engaged to Boreas.”

        “I…” Nesoi hesitated, but she quickly gritted her teeth and said resolutely, “No, I will not!”

        “Well… well… Very well.” Semele’s anger reached its peak, her fury twisting into a cold, mocking laugh. “Then I no longer have two daughters, just one.”

        “Mother…” Nesoi called out to Semele, but her mother turned away, refusing to hear another word from her. Knowing that Semele had made up her mind, Nesoi resignedly left the house, her steps heavy with sorrow.

        By then, the sky had turned somber with dark clouds gathering above the horizon, and it began to rain. Yet Nesoi, now abandoned and adrift, seemed oblivious to the pouring rain. She just walked slowly through the rain without a destination.

        ‘Where should I go… Home is no longer an option… Leon… He’s all I have left now.’ In the haze of her confusion, one thought emerged with clarity—a singular beacon of salvation. She did not know how long she wandered through the rainfall, but eventually, her feet led her to the place her heart had desired: the park pavilion where Leon and she would have their date. 

        “Nesoi!” A handsome young man who had been idly waiting in the pavilion, Leon, screamed the moment he saw Nesoi standing in the rain, soaked to the skin. Without hesitation, he dashed into the rain to pull her in. Grabbing her by the arm, he led her under the shelter and began wiping the rainwater from her with his sleeve. However, the amount of rainwater was beyond what a mere sleeve could dry—a fact that filled him with both frustration and heartache.

        “Why didn’t you bring an umbrella? What are you doing walking through the rain like this? What if you get sick—” Leon’s reprimand was abruptly silenced when Nesoi threw herself into his arms. He froze for a moment at the unexpected embrace, then noticed the faint trembling of her body. She clung to him like a wounded animal, fragile and frightened, a rare sight that struck a chord deep in his heart and made him realize something was wrong.

        “What is it?” Leon asked, holding her tightly despite her soaking clothes. “Tell me what happened.”

        “I can’t go back… I don’t have a home anymore…” Nesoi murmured, her voice barely audible. Clinging to him even tighter, she whispered, “You’re all I have now…”

        “There, there. It’s okay. I’m always here for you.” Leon said without hesitation, trying the best to comfort her gently, even though he had no idea what had transpired.

        When Nesoi finally calmed down, she told Leon everything—the engagement, her defiance, and her mother’s wrathful statement of disownment. Without a second thought, Leon decided to take her back to his homeland after hearing her story, and not long after, he stood before his parents and proposed to her.

        “Nesoi,” he said, kneeling on one knee, his eyes brimming with love. “I may not be able to give you political power or wealth, but I promise I will make you happy for the rest of our lives.”

        Leon’s proposal was filled with such pure and fervent love that Nesoi had no reason to refuse. So, with joy in her heart, she accepted him and joined the Tuxia family. From that day forward, the two lived a life of freedom and endless adventure.

        Occasionally, the couple explored mysterious lands. Side by side, they faced every challenge and every adventure. They even accepted requests to aid the weak at times, leaving behind countless heroic deeds that would be praised for generations to come.

        Yet, there was one regret Nesoi could never reconcile with, no matter how fulfilling her life with Leon was—the family she had left behind.

        Whenever the Tuxia dragons organized festivals, Nesoi always watched with envy as other families gathered and worked together. With her thoughts drifting to her distant homeland, to her mother and her half-sister, Ourea, she always quietly prayed for their health and happiness, even as the ache of separation gnawed at her soul.

        But fate, cruel as ever, denied her prayers.

        One day, Nesoi accidentally shattered the porcelain cup that she cherished the most. As she bent down to pick up the shards, Leon entered the room. He had a dark and troubled expression on his face, which gave Nesoi a sudden sense of foreboding. She stood up and approached him, her voice filled with concern. “What happened?”

        Leon hesitated for a long moment. He tried to formulate the words, his mind running through several ways to soften the shocking news, but none seemed fitting. In the end, he decided to speak the truth. “The Holy Gods were attacked by a monster while excavating the ancient relics… And they lost your mother…”

        Nesoi froze upon hearing the news. Her body stiffened as her mind struggled to process Leon’s words. It was after what felt like an eternity that she finally moved her trembling lips and murmured to herself,         “No… That’s impossible… Mother can’t be dead… No! I don’t believe it!”

        “Nesoi, you can’t run from this,” Leon said. “There are still those who need your protection.”

        “Those who need your protection…” She immediately realized who Leon meant. “Ourea… I have to protect her!”

        Nesoi and Leon then hurried to the homeland of the Holy Gods. What awaited them there was a scene far removed from the glory of the past—only the inescapable scars of loss and despair remained.

        The disaster had taken countless soldiers’ lives, and some bodies were so irreparably damaged that their families were left with nothing but empty coffins to grieve over.

        Nesoi and Leon moved through the grieving crowds until they found Ourea huddled in a corner. She seemed utterly detached from the world, her face devoid of emotion.

        “Ourea—”

        “It’s all your fault!” A furious roar cut off Nesoi’s call. It came from a grieving mother who stormed toward Ourea. Grabbing the girl by the hair, she shook her violently as she spat out venomous accusations. “It’s all your stupid mother’s fault! My son is dead because of her! Yet, you’re still here, alive! Why wasn’t it you who died instead?”

        “Stop!” Nesoi’s heart ached at the sight. She rushed forward and pried the woman’s hands off of Ourea, shielding her sister behind her. “That’s enough! She’s just a child! Your son’s death has nothing to do with her!”

        “I… Damn it!” The woman’s slightly returned—perhaps venting her fury had drained some of her strength. As she looked at the pitiful girl, her rage faded into bitter resignation with which she turned to leave, grumbling under her breath.

        “Are you okay?” Nesoi asked, her voice filled with concern as she knelt to face Ourea, who was trembling and shrinking into herself. Yet, her sister did not respond with relief or gratitude. Instead, she looked up, her tear-streaked face contorted with hatred and despair. Glaring at Nesoi, she demanded in a cold tone, “Why did you only come back now? If you’d been here, Mother wouldn’t have died… It’s all your fault… It’s YOUR fault!”

        “I…” Nesoi was lost for words for a moment. Her face contorted with remorse and sorrow as she pulled the sobbing Ourea into her arms and held her close. “You’re right… It’s all my fault. I’m sorry. I should’ve come back earlier. But everything is going to be okay, I promise. I won’t run away again.”

        From that moment on, Nesoi made her decision to stay in the Holy Gods’ abode and shoulder the responsibilities her mother had left behind, even though this choice meant parting ways with Leon…

        [i]“I could never disobey my mother. She has endured so much pain to protect me, and I must repay her.”[/i]
STORY_10968:
Nesoi, now a heroic spirit, sat quietly alone within the ethereal expanse of an illusory realm. The elements, sensing her solitude, gathered to weave a dream for her—a vision of what might have been, had she chosen a different path…

        Back in Olympus, the capital city of Odyssey, the home planet of the Holy Gods—

        It was a rare day of rest, yet Nesoi rose early as usual. She stood before her wardrobe, carefully deliberating over her choice of clothing—a side of femininity that she had rarely shown to anyone.

        Today marked her date with Leon. It had been a full month since their last day out, and her anticipation for this day had quietly grown over the passing days.

        It was after what seemed like forever that she finally settled on an outfit and put together a flawless look. With the unique glow of a woman in love, she stepped out of her room, ready for her date. However, just as she was about to leave, a haughty voice stopped her in her tracks.

        “Nesoi, come with me to the study.” It was her mother, Semele, also the Queen of the Holy Gods.

        “…Yes, Mother.” Though reluctant, Nesoi did not refuse her mother’s request—she never did, for she knew all too well how much pain and hardship her mother had endured to protect her in the past.

        She followed Semele into the study, where a guest was already waiting—a tall, broad-shouldered man named Boreas, one of the twelve major gods under the queen’s banner and also Nesoi’s superior, who was in charge of the highly valued Sorcery Corps.

        Nesoi’s uncharacteristically feminine appearance made Boreas’ eyes gleam with intrigue and amusement. He pursed his lips in a playful whistle and smirked. “Well, this is a first—I’ve never seen you out of your uniform. You look quite stunning. I’d say this engagement is turning out to be a pretty good deal for me.”

        “Engagement? What are you talking about?” Nesoi frowned in confusion.

        “You don’t know?” Boreas raised an eyebrow, then turned to Semele and asked, “You haven’t told your dear daughter about your plan to betroth her to me?”

        “WHAT?” Nesoi immediately looked at her mother, her voice trembling with disbelief as she asked, “What is he talking about, Mother?”

        “The engagement is nothing more than a strategic alliance to solidify our family’s power. There’s no need to make a fuss about it.” Semele’s expression remained as calm as ever, her tone devoid of any emotion. It was as though she were discussing some trifling matter, rather than her daughter’s lifelong happiness. Her indifferent remark sent a bitter pang through Nesoi’s heart.

        ‘Mother is always like this—ruthlessly decisive when it comes to power. She is willing to get rid of anything that stands in her way, even if it’s love or family.’ Nesoi thought as memories of her past flooded her mind. All her life, she had lived according to her mother’s rules and wishes. She had not even dared to tell her about her relationship with Leon, fearing to hear her words of displeasure.

        ‘I’ve had enough. I’ve always stayed silent. I’ve kept convincing myself to comply with Mother’s wishes, but this has to stop now. I refuse to be her quiet puppet any longer.’ The suffocating weight of Semele’s control, coupled with the emotional exhaustion that had only grown over time, finally outweighed the filial love Nesoi still harbored, and she made her decision.

        “I will not agree to this engagement. I already have someone I love,” she declared.

        “I know.” Semele’s response carried no surprise. Instead, there was a faint hint of derision. “That Tuxia dragon, Leon, isn’t it? I suppose he’s a decent young man with fair potential, but he’s fortuneless and lacks influence. He can’t help you with your career. He may be an enjoyable company for a romantic fling, but as a husband? Absolutely not.”

        “I don’t mind, to be honest,” Boreas interjected with a casual shrug. “It’s just a marriage of convenience, after all.”

        ‘How… how can they talk about marriage, something so sacred, with such disdain?’ Nesoi clenched her fists, her eyes wide with indignation and disbelief. Then, she said, “No… I won’t accept this engagement. I can’t betray Leon and turn my back against the love he has given me.”

        “Nesoi, what do you think you’re doing?” Semele’s voice sharpened. As the Queen of the Holy Gods, she had always expected absolute obedience from her subordinates. Now, Nesoi’s defiance seemed a challenge to her authority, which made her rage flare. “Are you going to defy your mother all because of an outsider?”

        “He is not an outsider! He is the man I love,” Nesoi argued.

        “Enough!” Semele slashed her hand down in the air and demanded, “Let me make this clear: you will be engaged to Boreas.”

        “I…” Nesoi hesitated, but she quickly gritted her teeth and said resolutely, “No, I will not!”

        “Well… well… Very well.” Semele’s anger reached its peak, her fury twisting into a cold, mocking laugh. “Then I no longer have two daughters, just one.”

        “Mother…” Nesoi called out to Semele, but her mother turned away, refusing to hear another word from her. Knowing that Semele had made up her mind, Nesoi resignedly left the house, her steps heavy with sorrow.

        By then, the sky had turned somber with dark clouds gathering above the horizon, and it began to rain. Yet Nesoi, now abandoned and adrift, seemed oblivious to the pouring rain. She just walked slowly through the rain without a destination.

        ‘Where should I go… Home is no longer an option… Leon… He’s all I have left now.’ In the haze of her confusion, one thought emerged with clarity—a singular beacon of salvation. She did not know how long she wandered through the rainfall, but eventually, her feet led her to the place her heart had desired: the park pavilion where Leon and she would have their date. 

        “Nesoi!” A handsome young man who had been idly waiting in the pavilion, Leon, screamed the moment he saw Nesoi standing in the rain, soaked to the skin. Without hesitation, he dashed into the rain to pull her in. Grabbing her by the arm, he led her under the shelter and began wiping the rainwater from her with his sleeve. However, the amount of rainwater was beyond what a mere sleeve could dry—a fact that filled him with both frustration and heartache.

        “Why didn’t you bring an umbrella? What are you doing walking through the rain like this? What if you get sick—” Leon’s reprimand was abruptly silenced when Nesoi threw herself into his arms. He froze for a moment at the unexpected embrace, then noticed the faint trembling of her body. She clung to him like a wounded animal, fragile and frightened, a rare sight that struck a chord deep in his heart and made him realize something was wrong.

        “What is it?” Leon asked, holding her tightly despite her soaking clothes. “Tell me what happened.”

        “I can’t go back… I don’t have a home anymore…” Nesoi murmured, her voice barely audible. Clinging to him even tighter, she whispered, “You’re all I have now…”

        “There, there. It’s okay. I’m always here for you.” Leon said without hesitation, trying the best to comfort her gently, even though he had no idea what had transpired.

        When Nesoi finally calmed down, she told Leon everything—the engagement, her defiance, and her mother’s wrathful statement of disownment. Without a second thought, Leon decided to take her back to his homeland after hearing her story, and not long after, he stood before his parents and proposed to her.

        “Nesoi,” he said, kneeling on one knee, his eyes brimming with love. “I may not be able to give you political power or wealth, but I promise I will make you happy for the rest of our lives.”

        Leon’s proposal was filled with such pure and fervent love that Nesoi had no reason to refuse. So, with joy in her heart, she accepted him and joined the Tuxia family. From that day forward, the two lived a life of freedom and endless adventure.

        Occasionally, the couple explored mysterious lands. Side by side, they faced every challenge and every adventure. They even accepted requests to aid the weak at times, leaving behind countless heroic deeds that would be praised for generations to come.

        Yet, there was one regret Nesoi could never reconcile with, no matter how fulfilling her life with Leon was—the family she had left behind.

        Whenever the Tuxia dragons organized festivals, Nesoi always watched with envy as other families gathered and worked together. With her thoughts drifting to her distant homeland, to her mother and her half-sister, Ourea, she always quietly prayed for their health and happiness, even as the ache of separation gnawed at her soul.

        But fate, cruel as ever, denied her prayers.

        One day, Nesoi accidentally shattered the porcelain cup that she cherished the most. As she bent down to pick up the shards, Leon entered the room. He had a dark and troubled expression on his face, which gave Nesoi a sudden sense of foreboding. She stood up and approached him, her voice filled with concern. “What happened?”

        Leon hesitated for a long moment. He tried to formulate the words, his mind running through several ways to soften the shocking news, but none seemed fitting. In the end, he decided to speak the truth. “The Holy Gods were attacked by a monster while excavating the ancient relics… And they lost your mother…”

        Nesoi froze upon hearing the news. Her body stiffened as her mind struggled to process Leon’s words. It was after what felt like an eternity that she finally moved her trembling lips and murmured to herself,         “No… That’s impossible… Mother can’t be dead… No! I don’t believe it!”

        “Nesoi, you can’t run from this,” Leon said. “There are still those who need your protection.”

        “Those who need your protection…” She immediately realized who Leon meant. “Ourea… I have to protect her!”

        Nesoi and Leon then hurried to the homeland of the Holy Gods. What awaited them there was a scene far removed from the glory of the past—only the inescapable scars of loss and despair remained.

        The disaster had taken countless soldiers’ lives, and some bodies were so irreparably damaged that their families were left with nothing but empty coffins to grieve over.

        Nesoi and Leon moved through the grieving crowds until they found Ourea huddled in a corner. She seemed utterly detached from the world, her face devoid of emotion.

Why wasn’t it you who died instead?”

        “I… Damn it!” The woman’s slightly returned—perhaps venting her fury had drained some of her strength. As she looked at the pitiful girl, her rage faded into bitter resignation with which she turned to leave, grumbling under her breath.

        “Are you okay?” Nesoi asked, her voice filled with concern as she knelt to face Ourea, who was trembling and shrinking into herself. Yet, her sister did not respond with relief or gratitude. Instead, she looked up, her tear-streaked face contorted with hatred and despair. Glaring at Nesoi, she demanded in a cold tone, “Why did you only come back now? If you’d been here, Mother wouldn’t have died… It’s all your fault… It’s YOUR fault!”

        “I…” Nesoi was lost for words for a moment. Her face contorted with remorse and sorrow as she pulled the sobbing Ourea into her arms and held her close. “You’re right… It’s all my fault. I’m sorry. I should’ve come back earlier. But everything is going to be okay, I promise. I won’t run away again.”

        From that moment on, Nesoi made her decision to stay in the Holy Gods’ abode and shoulder the responsibilities her mother had left behind, even though this choice meant parting ways with Leon…

        [i]“My marriage must be my decision—even my mother has no right to dictate it.”[/i]

She is the third princess of the Britannian Empire.
Due to her status as a student, she has not yet stepped onto the political stage, but she possesses a noble spirit in pursuit of ideals.
STORY_10970:

Its design philosophy is entirely different from Britannian-made Knightmare Frames, resulting in a distinctly unique silhouette. STORY_10971:

STORY_10972:

While he possesses exceptional military skills, his straightforward personality and firm belief in the goodness of others often lead him to take on significant burdens. Unlike Lelouch, who seeks to destroy the Britannian Empire, he believes in promoting reform from within the system.

STORY_10973: He is a mysterious man who has reappeared to rebel against the Britannian Empire. His true identity remains unknown to this day.
STORY_10974:

The Vincent is the Britannian military’s latest Knightmare Frame model. It was originally developed as a prototype for a mass-production model based on the Lancelot, intended to be deployed to the Britannian military. However, Rolo seized it and made it his personal Knightmare.
STORY_10975:
Kyoshiro Todoh is the combat commander of the Order of the Black Knights. He is the legendary general who achieved the only victory during the invasion seven years ago. Previously a member of the Japan Liberation Front, he joins the Order of the Black Knights after its destruction. Leading the Four Holy Swords, he becomes one of the greatest threats to Britannia.

Zangetsu is one of the new Knightmare Frames developed by Rakshata for the Order of the Black Knights. Designed as the personal Knightmare Frame for Todoh, the combat commander, its performance rivals that of the Lancelot.
STORY_10976: She is a member of the Ashford Academy student council and also a member of the swimming club. She cares deeply about Lelouch. After losing her father in the Battle for Narita, she begins to question Zero’s actions, but...

Cornelia li Britannia is the second princess of the Britannian Empire. She is a fierce warrior who constantly fights on the frontlines, feared by other nations as the “Witch.“

The Gloucester (Cornelia Version) is a fifth-generation Knightmare Frame based on the Sutherland. Specifically designed for close combat between Knightmare Frame, it is a unit with majorly enhanced melee capabilities, exclusively used by Cornelia and her imperial guards. Cornelia’s unit is distinguished by two large horns on its head and is equipped with a lance as its primary weapon.
STORY_10978:
She is a soldier of the Pureblood Faction.
She once served as Jeremiah’s exceptional adjutant, but after Jeremiah's fall from power, she began investigating Zero’s secret.
STORY_10979:

Unexpectedly, Bartley rescues him and transforms him into an experimental subject. During the Black Rebellion, he sinks into the ocean alongside C.C., and his fate remained unknown until he is rescued by V.V. and the Geass Order.

Siegfried is a Knight Giga Fortress that has been retrieved and repaired after it sank to the ocean during the Black Rebellion. Due to its unique neural-link control system, only Jeremiah is capable of piloting it. However, it is later modified so that V.V. can pilot it as well. With the newly added electrical generators, its power has been significantly boosted.
STORY_10980:

The Emperor of Britannia alters his memory after Suzaku has captured him during the Black Rebellion. However, with the help of C.C., he comes back as the demonic king. Subsequently, he ascends the throne and becomes the 99th Emperor, standing at the pinnacle of Britannia and the world.

Shinkiro is a Knightmare Frame that Rakshata has specifically developed for Zero. It boasts absolute defensive power.
STORY_10981:
Kallen Kozuki is the ace pilot of the Order of the Black Knights. To escape Britannia's pursuit and revive Zero, she participated in “Operation Flying Swallow 4.” She feels conflicted about the revelation that Zero is Lelouch.

Reconstructed by Lloyd and Cécile of the former Advanced Special Envoy Engineering Corps (Camelot), it features new equipment such as the wired Radiant Wave Surger arm and the cutting-edge Energy Wing. The modifications have transformed it into an entirely new form, barely resembling its original design.
STORY_10982:
Suzaku Kururugi is one of the Knights of the Round under the direct command of the Emperor, holding the title of Knight of Seven. He pilots the Lancelot and is active in operations all over the world.

Lancelot Albion is believed to be an enhanced version of the Lancelot, but is it truly so…?
STORY_10983:
Li Xingke is a military officer of the Chinese Federation. He is stationed in Area 11 as an attendant to Gao Hai, the High Eunuch. He is a remarkable man who possesses intelligence comparable to Lelouch and combat abilities on par with Suzaku.

Although it was completed long ago, its exceptional specifications made it difficult to find a suitable pilot, preventing it from being deployed in combat. It is equipped with various powerful weapons, including the Baryon Cannon.

She rarely shows emotion and appears indifferent to people and things she has no interest in. She is often seen carrying her mobile phone, frequently taking photos and updating her blog.

In addition, it is equipped with the same shield system as the Lancelot and the Avalon, making it a heavily armored Knightmare Frame with outstanding defensive capabilities.
STORY_10986:
Gino Weinberg is one of the Knights of the Round under the direct command of the Emperor, holding the title of Knight of Three. Although he comes from a prestigious noble family, he attained his current position through his exceptional skill as a Knightmare pilot. Cheerful and friendly by nature, he treats Suzaku as a friend despite his status as one of the Numbers.

The Tristan is Gino's personal Knightmare Frame. It features a transformation mechanism that allows it to switch between the military aircraft-like Fortress Mode and the Knightmare Mode, resulting in its extremely high mobility. Its potential is said to rival that of several imperial guard-class Gloucesters combined.
STORY_10987:
Bismarck Waldstein is one of the Knights of the Round, holding the title of Knight of One, hailed as the strongest knight in Britannia.

The Galahad is the Knightmare Frame exclusively piloted by the strongest Britannian knight, the Knight of One. It is equipped with the mighty sword “Excalibur,” named by the Emperor himself, a masterpiece representing the pinnacle of combat power.
STORY_10988:
Charles zi Britannia is the 98th Emperor of the Holy Britannian Empire. Possessing a Geass that can alter others’ memories, he uses his power to erase Lelouch’s memories as Zero.

His wife, Marianne vi Britannia, was a knight known as “Marianne the Flash,” and the mother of Lelouch and Nunnally.
STORY_10989:

The Damocles is a flying fortress secretly constructed under Schneizel’s orders. Equipped with a high-output nuclear missile, F.L.E.I.J.A., it has multiple Blaze Luminous generators, which grant it near-perfect defense.
STORY_10990:

STORY_11012: She is one of the Norns and the youngest daughter of Mimir. Headstrong and straightforward, she believes that every beginning and ending must be met with sacrifice.

STORY_11014: She is Odin’s wife, who appears in the Void of the Realm. Odin mistakes her for a delicate beauty unversed in the ways of war at first glance. In reality, she secretly conspires with the demons, forcing Odin to grapple with his emotions and his reason.
STORY_11015:
A gleaming spear sliced through the mist-laden sky. Its tip cut through the clouds with a momentum so ferocious that it threatened to tear the heavens asunder, but its strength waned and plummeted toward the earth. Below, an unassuming antelope stood motionless, unaware of the danger until the weapon struck and pinned it to the ground. Its companions bolted in terror, leaving it alone to feel its life slipping away. 

        From the horizon, a young man and a girl approached. The man knelt beside the dying antelope, then murmured a quiet prayer, his blade poised to end its suffering.

        “Didn’t Father tell you to stop praying? Why haven’t you learned?” The girl—Urd, one of the Valkyries—spoke sternly, her piercing gaze fixed on the man, Odin, the patriarch of the Aesir.

        Odin hesitated for a brief moment before he answered, “Mimir told me I must become the faith of my people, that I must never pray in front of them. But, it’s just us here, far from our home…”

        “Odin,” Urd interrupted. “You are not just a leader. If you wish to preserve peace, you must become their god.”

        “And a god does not pray…” Odin murmured as he understood the weight of her words.

        “Yes,” Urd continued. “A god only gives commands—or takes responsibility.”

        The antelope’s faint struggles drew Odin’s attention back to the present. He stepped to its side and quietly slid his blade across its throat to end its pain. 

        Afterward, under Urd’s guidance, Odin left the North and embarked on a journey to reclaim the Armor of Runes. Together, they traversed battle-scarred lands, their path winding through desolate fields ravaged by war…

        “You’ve done preparing the meat? Let’s go. We’re close to our destination.”

        Their journey led them to an abandoned town where the streets were eerily untouched by disaster or violence. Surveying the empty buildings, Odin concluded that the inhabitants must have left of their own accord. Following Urd, he entered one of the deserted houses. Suddenly, Urd stopped in her tracks.

        “I can feel it. It’s still here.”

        “Something so important… they just left it behind?” Odin’s voice carried a note of doubt.

        “Odin, this is your last chance,” Urd said. “Do you truly wish to become the Allfather and sacrifice everything for peace?” 

        “Urd, have you prophesied anything?” Odin asked.

        “No, I never prophesy—I know only the past. Back then, Father knew that the power of the armor would bring tremendous change to the town. Still, he sold it to the garrison commander…” She turned her unblinking eyes to Odin, her expression distant. “Odin, we are all selfish… We gods never act for the salvation of mortals.”

        “Urd, thank you,” Odin said after a pause. “I understand now. Our collaboration is born of necessity, a means to achieve our goals, and as a mortal without power, I must seize every opportunity.”

        “Then stick to your aim till the very end,” Urd said softly, gesturing toward the door with a faint smile.

        Odin pushed open the door and stepped into the dimly lit room. The floor was littered with skeletal remains, and the walls bore scars of battle. At the far end of the room sat a suit of dark purple armor. As he approached, faint light—a soul of the deceased—gathered around the armor, illuminating the runes etched into its surface. It began shaking.

        A hollow voice echoed from the depths of the room. “Traveler… Welcome… I am the garrison commander of this town…”

        “Warrior,” Odin said, his voice calm but firm. “The townsfolk are gone. Your duty is over.”

        “Gone? No! No one leaves! Why would they leave when I have the power to protect them?” 

        The voice rose into a manic howl, filled with rage. “I am not mad! Why don’t they believe me?”

        “He has lost himself in the power,” Urd said quietly, her voice edged with sorrow. “Odin, grant him peace, please.”

        Odin steadied Gungnir, the weapon humming as he gathered his power. With a decisive swing, he flung it toward the armor behind the spirit—

        The weapon pierced through the cracks in the armor and released the soul trapped within, finally turning its torment to rest. Odin reached for the black helmet resting atop the armor. The cold touch of the metal sent a shiver down his fingers as he turned it over, brushing away layers of dust that dulled its sheen. Holding the helmet aloft, he turned to Urd, silently consulting her with his gaze.

        “You know I never stop anything from happening,” Urd replied.

        Odin recalled the question she had posed earlier:

        “Do you truly wish to become the Allfather and sacrifice everything for peace?”

        “You said you never prophesy,” Odin said as he pulled himself back into the moment, his voice tinged with a subtle anger. “It’s just because you refuse to speak. You’ve always stood apart and only watched from the sidelines.”

        “I’ve told you before—I am only here to watch you follow through,” Urd replied, her tone unwaveringly resolute. Her indifference left Odin feeling frustrated.

        Seeing the bones scattered across the room, Odin quietly unbuckled the armor piece by piece. “You know you can’t remain a bystander forever.”

        “Right,” Urd said. “And that is why I will help you become part of history.”

        Her words brought a faint smile to Odin’s face. At last, he had taken his first step toward peace in the North. However, Urd’s expression slowly shifted. Her smile faded as she said solemnly, “You will suffer, Odin.”

        “I know. Mimir already warned me long ago,” Odin replied. Seizing the moment as if it were his chance to strike back, he spoke with unwavering confidence, “But my will shall never waver.”

        For a moment, Urd’s composed exterior faltered. The unyielding fire in Odin’s eyes stirred something deep within her—a flicker of emotion she had long suppressed. Yet, she quickly steeled herself and severed that last piece of sentiment that had no place in her role.

        “Don’t put on the full armor yet,” Urd cautioned. “Start with the helmet. You’ll need time to adapt to its power.”

        “You’re right.” Following her instructions, Odin donned the armor piece by piece. It took him an entire day to attune to the overwhelming energy radiating from the armor.

        “Well done…” Urd said, nodding in approval as she watched Odin clad in the armor. “This is as far as I can guide you. Father will show you the rest, so let’s head back to the North.”

        The two then returned to the North, where Odin began his training under Mimir to master the armor’s immense power. However, with every step forward, the power took a brutal toll. Each attempt to harness the armor’s strength left Odin writhing in agony, forcing him to confront the limits of his will.

        One night, the armor’s power rampaged through Odin’s body again. As the relentless force twisted and battered his soul, his vision blurred, and his mind began to falter. A fleeting thought whispered—surrender, let the armor take you. But then a memory surfaced, vivid and unbidden…

        Years ago, Mimir had stood before the people of the North, posing a question to a young man, Thor, during one of his lessons. “What do you think is the value of life?”

        Thor, having been daydreaming, nudged Odin to answer the question for him. Odin, who was just a child at that time, said nervously, “I-it’s the course of living…”

        Mimir’s eyes widened, surprised by the answer. Thor, worried that he had pushed his friend into embarrassment, quickly interjected, “Life’s value is in achieving glory! In battle—”

        Mimir gestured for Thor to stop and leave, asking Odin to stay. Watching Thor leave gloatingly, Odin braced himself for the chastisement. 

        Losing his parents to wars at a young age, he was adopted and raised by the patriarch of Aesir. The patriarch’s family treated him like their own son. The last thing he wanted was to disgrace his family and his tribe.

        To his surprise, Mimir did not reprimand but smiled at him, “Your answer was good. Could you tell me more?”

        Mimir waited for the young Odin’s answer quietly. The savant’s compliment was not something that the boy had expected, which made his mind go blank. As all the rehearsed responses in his head became pointless, he could only stammer and answer truthfully, “I... I think that the value of life cannot be found within achievements. It’s in the essence of what compels us to do things that benefit others… even if we don’t understand why…”

        “Precisely,” Mimir said. “And because of that, some must sacrifice themselves so others may live fully.”

        “But… shouldn’t everyone live for themselves—”

        “No! Someone must live for others!” Mimir’s voice thundered as he gripped Odin’s shoulders. His unusual emotional response startled the little boy.

        “Odin, would you become that someone? To be the Allfather, a god who is destined to perish for the world?”

        The memory jolted Odin awake from the haze of pain. His resolve crystallized as he remembered his mission, his decision.

        “Yes… I am a god destined to perish…” He opened his eyes. The raging power of the armor surged through him, threatening to consume his soul. But this time, his heart remained steady. “But… I’ve only just begun. It’s not the time yet!”

        “Yes! That’s it! Fight against it! You’re almost there!” Mimir shouted, his voice charged with excitement as he watched the beginning of a legendary hero. “When we perish, we become nourishment for others, until we fade from history.”

        Fueled by Mimir’s encouragement, Odin finally conquered the Armor of Runes with his burning resolve and let the godly power integrate with his body.

        Yet, with the godly power fallen into the hands of a mortal, it would suffocate the heart and mind of its wielder, and Odin knew it from the very beginning. Still, he chose to follow Mimir’s guidance, allowing the armor’s power to consume him.

        Even later, when Odin was sealed in the void, Mimir’s words and the memories of his comrades in the North still lingered, echoing endlessly in his mind…

        ‘You will suffer, for your will never waver. You will remain trapped within crumbled pillars, for your mind never surrenders. You will be sealed in the broken tower for eternity, challenged by spirits one after another. You will be the sacrifice, Odin, bound to the stone of runes. And in an unknown illusion, sealed away, you will wait for doom.’

STORY_11023:
‘I once thought my life was happy and complete.’

        Angrboda thought as she lay in bed, exhausted after another painful episode of the curse. She had once been a calm and gentle woman who loved exploring the world’s mysteries with her husband, Loki.

        She had believed that was how she would spend the rest of her life, but it turned out that fate had other plans. She fell under a demon’s curse, and that curse changed everything, plunging her into a life of endless suffering.

        Every night, Angrboda felt her body screaming in pain. The excruciating agony drained her will, filling her heart with a growing yet hollow fear.

        At those moments, someone—her husband, Loki—would unwaveringly hold her trembling hands, his touch warm and his voice gentle. Even though knowing words could do little to ease her pain, he would still give his all to comfort her:

        “Angrboda, don’t be afraid. No matter what happens, I’ll always be here with you.”

        Loki searched everywhere for a way to lift Angrboda’s curse, but the curse had long become part of her soul. There was no cure. After countless failed attempts, despair began to wear the couple down. The man who had once been so full of light slowly became tired and quiet.

        It was then that Angrboda realized that her existence had become a burden to him. She began to find the pain insufferable, for she could not bear being the reason for her husband’s endless suffering.

        ‘...As long as I carry this curse, I’ll only hurt him more…’’

        One day, she looked at Loki, unconscious on the floor. Just moments ago, in a moment of madness, she had nearly killed the man she loved. But even then, Loki had tried to reach her, unhesitatingly dragging his frail body across the floor—just to comfort her until he collapsed due to pain and exhaustion.

        Seeing him like that broke Angrboda’s heart. She felt overwhelmed with guilt. As hot tears fell from her eyes, she made a quiet decision:

        ‘I have to set him free…’

        Not long after, she found her chance. While Loki fell asleep, completely worn out, she left quietly. He did not notice. He called her name in his dreams, as if they were still together in that sunlit field, holding hands without a care in the world.

        However, that moment of happiness only belonged to the past. Their reality had long since fallen into darkness.

        As her life slowly faded away, Angrboda felt no fear. Instead, she felt a strange peace, for it was not just the end of her life but also her way out of darkness, out of the unforgiving destiny…

STORY_11056:
As the year drew to an end, the festival spirit in Ukiyokyo, the capital of youkais, thickened; the streets were bustling with activity as youkais poured into the shopping arcade, scrambling from shop to shop for their New Year’s shopping. The governor’s mansion, located at the heart of the city, was the busiest of all as the evening marked the annual New Year’s Banquet.

        While all the small youkais in the mansion were busy preparing for the banquet, the host, Governor Hokusai Katsushika, was enjoying herself. She sat in an ancient tree near the mansion’s gates with her back leaning against the trunk and her right leg propped up as she watched them scurry back and forth. Her beautiful face glowed with a trace of contentment. She leisurely shook a long-necked porcelain bottle in her right hand. The vibrant floral patterns on the bottle shifted mesmerizingly with each subtle movement—captivating, elusive, and steeped in mystery.

        “Ah, the plum wine from Mandala is truly exquisite,” Hokusai murmured, raising the bottle to her lips. As she took a sip, a fruity flavor hit her palate, leaving her wanting more. Just as she was about to take another sip, she heard a frantic shout coming from below.

        “Governor! Bad news!”

        “Asabana?” Hokusai glanced down to see her attendant, Asabana the hone-onna, standing under the tree, her face lined with anxiety. Instantly, Hokusai understood the gravity of the situation. Her face darkened, and with a graceful leap, she returned to the ground, standing in front of Asabana as she asked, “What happened?”

        “We’ve received a message—Uchigao is rampaging through the northern district!”

        “Uchigao?” Hokusai froze, then exclaimed in surprise, “Wasn’t he imprisoned in the Cavern of Exile?”

        “Yes, but it seems he’s escaped,” Asabana replied, her tone urgent.

        “The Cavern of Exile is protected by powerful barriers. He couldn’t have escaped on his own. Someone must have let him out.”

        “But… who? Who would do such a thing?”

        “This isn’t the time to find out who the rat is. What we need to do now is stop that vicious creature. Uchigao already slaughtered thousands of youkais before he was imprisoned. We need to put an end to him, or more lives will be lost.”

        “But the New Year’s Banquet is about to begin. If you head to the northern district now, you might not make it back in time.”

        “That’s why I need you to stay here and take care of the banquet. Remember to keep ‘that’ with you, just in case.”

        “...Understood.” Asabana nodded obediently, though her eyes betrayed a hint of lingering concern. “But… will you be alright on your own?”

        “Hah! If I could subdue Uchigao once, I can do it again. Don’t worry,” Hokusai said with a confident wave of her hand, then set off for the northern district.

        Soon, she arrived at the northern district. The local youkai administrator hurriedly greeted her, his face fraught with worry as he said, “Governor Hokusai, thank goodness you’re here.”

        “Spare me the flattery. Where’s Uchigao?”

        “Our guards managed to repel him for now. He’s hiding near the Misty Lake on the outskirts.”

        “Good. Leave him to me. Focus on tending to the injured.”

        With Uchigao’s location confirmed, Hokusai wasted no time heading toward the Misty Lake.

        True to its name, the Misty Lake was shrouded in an eerily dense fog that seemed capable of concealing anything. The lake’s surface was unnervingly still. Hokusai approached the lake cautiously, her sharp eyes scanning her surroundings. Suddenly, the large paintbrush strapped to her back trembled slightly, as if sensing a twisted energy nearby.

        Then, something jumped out of the stagnant water. It was Uchigao, lunging at her like a feral beast. His body reeked of blood that seemed to have soaked into his very skin. Yet, his attack missed.

        It turned out that Hokusai had swiftly propelled herself into the air with her paintbrush and avoided Uchigao’s strike soon after she had sensed the lurking presence. A brilliant sigil scorched itself into the sky as she slipped past the grotesque youkai in a hairbreadth and slashed her brush through the air.

        “Ukiyo-e: Thunderclap!” As Hokusai gathered her powers, a thunderbolt erupted from the glowing sigil and struck Uchigao with a deafening roar.

        “ARGHHHH!”  Uchigao screamed in agony, his body convulsing as the acrid scent of burnt flesh filled the air. Yet even as he writhed, his crimson eyes remained locked on Hokusai with a feral hunger, like a starving predator eyeing its prey.

        “Skin… Let me take your skin… Give me… your SKIN!”

        “Hah! You want my skin? Not a chance!” Hokusai sneered, launching another series of attacks. 

        However, the Uchigao proved to be more resilient than Hokusai had imagined—no matter how many powerful blows he endured, he refused to fall. Instead, he relentlessly pursued Hokusai, determined to flay her alive.

        [i]‘Tut! I can’t kill him. I guess I’ll just have to seal him again like last time.’[/i] As the battle dragged on, Hokusai’s stamina began to wane. The last engagement left a small cut in her skin. Though small, the wound sufficed to remind her that further attrition would be pointless.

        She then pulled out a blank scroll from her belt and bit her finger. Using her blood as ink, she drew a cage on the scroll. As she channeled her power, the scroll flew into the air. While intricate sigils appeared under an iridescent flash of light, Hokusai clasped her hands, her eyes staring coldly at the pouncing monster.

        “Ukiyo-e: Prison!”

        At her command, a crimson cage emerged from the scroll, capturing Uchigao with perfect precision. The monster thrashed and roared, but the cage held firm. Slowly, the cage shrank until it eventually transformed into a red light and disappeared into the scroll along with its prisoner.

        “Phew… Finally, it’s over.” Hokusai stretched her tense shoulders and glanced at the now orange-tinted sky. Scratching the back of her head, she muttered, “Looks like I took too long. I probably won’t make it back in time… Ugh, guess I’ll have to use that.”

        She retrieved another scroll. Unlike the previous blank scroll, this one depicted a vibrant and bustling bird’s-eye view of Ukiyokyo.

        She tossed it into the air, letting it unfurl as she pointed her brush at it. Channeling her power, she shouted, “Ukiyo-e: Worldly Passage!”

        As her voice faded, her body dissolved into light and melted into the paper. A mysterious fire ignited, burning the scroll to ashes that scattered over the lake.

        Meanwhile, the Governor’s Mansion in Ukiyokyo remained bustling with noise. Great youkai arrived one after another, taking their seats and indulging in the revelry as they eagerly awaited the governor’s appearance. However, as time went on, the governor’s absence began to stir whispers among the crowd.

        Finally, Michizane Sugawara, a senior and influential youkai, snorted in irritation. He stood up and slammed his cup onto the table, the crisp sound cutting through the noisy hall. His brows furrowed with impatience as he turned to Asabana, the hone-onna standing beside the governor’s empty seat, and demanded, “Where is Governor Hokusai? How much longer does she intend to keep us waiting?”

        “Exactly! If we miss the auspicious hour, it could ruin the fortune for the coming year!”
“That girl should really mind her manners. To make so many elders wait is utterly disrespectful!

        As Sugawara’s words fell, other great youkais chimed in and expressed their annoyance. A few even cast disdainful glances at Hokusai’s seat, their expressions tinged with ridicule. The atmosphere in the banquet hall grew tense in an instant. 

        The remaining youkais glanced at each other uneasily. Yet, no one was willing to speak up. Sensing the shift in the atmosphere, Sugawara gloatingly puffed out his chest, his tone growing bolder as he said, “The annual banquet is a long-established tradition that cannot be neglected or delayed. If Governor Hokusai refuses to show up, then this banquet shall fall to me to preside over—”

        “Ukiyo-e: Unveil!”

        Suddenly, a clear, commanding voice interrupted Sugawara mid-sentence. The voice resounded across the entire banquet hall as a dazzling crimson light emanated from the scroll in Asabana’s hands, with multiple magical sigils materializing on its surface.

        Without hesitation, Asabana flung the scroll into the air. The scroll unfurled by gravity, releasing a gentle gust of wind that swept through the hall. Magically, pink petals of night sakura blossoms began to spill from the paper, transforming into a magnificent sakura snowstorm. 

        Simultaneously, thousands of ghost flames erupted from the scroll, floating gracefully into the air. They hovered like brilliant fireworks, illuminating the banquet hall in a dazzling display of light. Amidst the glowing flames, Hokusai Katsushika’s figure began to take shape. Riding atop a crimson dragon conjured with ink, she emerged majestically from the scroll. All the youkais couldn’t help but stand in awe in the hall at her grand entrance.
Hokusai leapt nimbly from the dragon’s back and landed directly in front of the governor’s seat. Her movements were sharp and precise, brimming with unquestionable confidence. She raised her head and looked directly at Sugawara, calm and composed.

        “Michizane Sugawara,” she said, her voice steady but laced with an unmistakable threat, “I’m curious—where did you get the audacity to think you could take my place as host?” 

        Sugawara’s face immediately turned pale. Still, he forced himself to maintain composure and said, “I only spoke out of good intentions when I noticed your absence.” 

        “Now that you’ve arrived, of course, the hosting duties return to you. However…”He paused, his gaze flickering to Hokusai’s wound. “It seems you’ve been injured. I wonder if you’ll still be able to participate in the traditional youkai duels later tonight?”

        “Ah, thank you for your concern,” Hokusai replied, raising an eyebrow as a mocking smile tugged at her lips. “But this? It’s just a scratch from my little warm-up. It doesn’t affect me.”

        With that, she twirled her massive brush and flaunted a few moves, her movement effortless and elegant. She finished by pointing the brush’s tip directly at Sugawara, her grin widening into something fierce and wild.

        “Well then, how about you start us off?”
STORY_11057:
It all happened on a holiday morning in Levant, the central district of Canaan, the capital planet of demons…

        While most people in the residential area were still sound asleep, a suspicious figure was sneaking around the neighborhood. It was a tall man dressed in a long black coat with matching black leather gloves. He hid his face with a pair of oversized sunglasses, his hair meticulously slicked back with pomade—a dressing style that seemed completely out of place in such a cozy neighborhood.

        Tiptoing his way forward, he stopped every so often to look around and see if he was safe. Finally, he arrived at a small house located in a corner. He gently knocked on the door, but no one answered.

        “Hmm? Is she not home?” the man murmured, furrowing his brows in concern. “Could something have happened to her?”

Unable to suppress his growing unease, he headed for the fence at the back of the house to quietly peek inside. He was so focused on the house that he failed to notice that someone had silently approached him from behind. The assailant threw him off balance with a kick in his ankle. Then she grabbed his arm and threw him over her shoulder, pinning him to the ground. 

        “Who are you? What are you doing sneaking around my house?” demanded the assailant, a beautiful woman. Her sharp, elegant eyes were filled with vigilance.

        “Wait! Gemma, it’s me!” Gemma stared closely at the man as he hurriedly called out her name.  Her expression quickly shifted to one of disbelief when she heard that familiar voice. She asked under her breath, “Dante? Why are you dressed like this?”

        With a twist of his body, Dante effortlessly pulled Gemma into her arms. He stood up and removed his sunglasses, revealing a refined face and an innocently radiant smile. “Of course, to avoid my ‘stalkers’, my love.” 

        The man’s full name was Dante Karnstein, heir to the renowned vampire family of Levant. It was a highly coveted title that came with high status and public attention. However, in the demon aristocracy, a world filled with betrayal and deception, it also made him a target. So, he had to conceal his track to protect the love of his life, Gemma.

        Gemma looked at Dante, her expression a mix of helplessness and exasperation. Though she was somewhat annoyed, she couldn’t help but relent at his brilliant smile. Ruffling his hair, she sighed and said, “You look even more conspicuous.”

        “Should I have come in a cat mascot costume instead?”

        “Absolutely not!” Gemma retorted, rolling her eyes. But her words soon faded into a soft chuckle when she saw Dante’s mischievous grin and tender gaze. “Alright, stop joking around. Come inside already.”

        Dante followed Gemma into the house, where he saw a beautifully decorated cake on the table, along with other delicious dishes. Curious, he asked, “What’s the feast for today? You even made a cake in my favorite shape—a cat.”

        “Because I’m pregnant.”

        “You... WHAT did you say?” For once, the ever-composed man’s jaw dropped. His entire body froze as the unexpected news hit him, an amusing reaction that made Gemma burst into laughter. Standing on tiptoes, she cupped his face with her hands and planted a soft kiss on his lips. In a gentle voice, she said, “You and I—we, are having a baby.”

        Dante was quiet for a moment. His expression shifted dramatically until he pulled Gemma tightly into his arms with his reddened eyes. Burying his face in the crook of her neck, he choked out, “I... I’m so happy...”

        Born into a household driven by power and profit, Dante had never truly experienced warmth or understood the concept of “family.” It wasn’t until he met Gemma that he found these precious things he had missed in her.

        “Oh my, why are you crying? This is happy news,” Gemma said, though her eyes, too, began to glisten with tears. She smiled, gently patting Dante’s back to comfort him.

        After a while, Dante finally calmed down. Taking a deep breath, he gently touched Gemma’s face and said with unwavering determination, “I’ll talk to my parents. Our child will carry the Karnstein name with pride.”

        “Dante...” Gemma shook her head. “There’s no need to rush. I know your hands are tied.”

        To maintain his status as the Karnstein heir, Dante had to keep his relationship with Gemma, a human, a secret. He had dreams of reforming the vampire society, but the deeply rooted power dynamics were too difficult to shake. Not only had his efforts shown no significant progress, but they had left him in danger time and again.

        Once, Dante was gravely injured in an assassination attempt. It was Gemma, a doctor, who discovered him and nursed him back to health. That incident marked the beginning of their relationship, making Gemma the one light in Dante’s otherwise burdensome life.

        However, the news of Gemma’s pregnancy changed everything. His mind changed. He had to guard his loved ones; the safety of the woman he loved and the child they would bring into the world came first before his dreams. It was his promise for the future—a motto that his family shall uphold till their end.

        [i]‘Carmilla, my dear daughter, I will make sure you live in a world full of love where you grow up safe and happy.’[/i] Dante placed his hand gently on Gemma’s growing belly, offering the most sincere prayer for the life inside as he awaited its arrival. 

         Later, Dante returned to his family estate and confessed his intentions to marry a human. However, they didn’t give him support. Instead, they stripped him of his status as heir and banished him to Area 99, assigning him to manage its chaos…
