STORY_11119:
Upon the mountain ridge, a massive dragon’s skeletal remains stood on the earth, like the spine of the world itself, bracing the heavens above. Beneath the shadow lay a silver-white dragon, its colossal form curled, its breath slow, its eyelids quivering as though it were about to awaken from its slumber.

        Then, with sudden clarity, its eyes opened. It shook its head lightly, then summoned its power—its form dissolving into mist before reshaping into a tall man with silver hair cascading over his shoulders and handsome features that yet carried a sickly pallor. He stepped slowly out of the tent, where dawn spilled through the clefts of stone, gilding the earth in a soft veil of gold. There, seated in the quiet glow, was a young man with hair the color of deep sapphire, still as a statue.

        “Qing Gui, why are you up so early today?” the silver-haired man asked with a gentle smile, his tone warm yet tinged with a hint of fatigue.

        “Bai Hu.” Qing Gui turned and answered with a smile, “I slept early last night and woke early this morning. I couldn’t go back to sleep, so I came here instead.”

        Noticing the poor color on Bai Hu’s face, he asked with concern, “And you? You don’t look well… Are you still troubled over your argument with Xuan Huang?”

        Bai Hu and Qing Gui were both Runedragons. Runedragons were born in pairs, and the partner they were fated to be bonded with was known as a Souliade. Xuan Huang was Bai Hu’s Souliade. Souliades were meant to share a deep, unbreakable bond, woven of trust and devotion. Yet not long ago, Bai Hu and Xuan Huang had a bitter quarrel, and the wound between them had not healed.

        Bai Hu faltered. He couldn’t answer the question as thoughts and emotions churned in his mind like waves crashing against the shore.

        It wasn’t the first argument he and Xuan Huang had. Back in the days when neither of them had fully formed their temperaments, the two had shared a harmonious relationship. But as years passed, Xuan Huang’s fierce and unyielding nature grew ever sharper. He insisted on his own way in all things, which clashed with Bai Hu, who—different from his gentle demeanor—was also stubborn at his core. They found themselves at odds more and more often, and the days of cold silence outnumbered those of reconciliation.

        Seeing Bai Hu’s silence, Qing Gui continued softly,  “As fiery and competitive as Xuan Huang may seem, he truly cares about you. He’s probably drowning in remorse now over what happened yesterday. If you’re willing to take the first step, this rift between you might well mend.”

        Bai Hu recalled the injuries Xuan Huang had suffered searching for Moon Lotus Fruit for him. It was after a long, quiet moment that he finally nodded and said, “...Very well. I’ll go find him.”

        After parting from Qing Gui, Bai Hu returned to his dragon form. He unfurled his wings and soared into the skies,  heading toward the depths of the forest.

        Before long, he found Xuan Huang by a quiet stream, lying beside the water, dozing in the warm sunlight. Bai Hu descended soundlessly, light as the breeze, shifting back into human form as he approached.

        Still, his steps did not escape Xuan Huang’s sharp senses. He sat upright, his eyes tired but vigilance unbroken. He glared coldly at Bai Hu, his voice low and edged with bitterness as he questioned, “What are you doing here? Shouldn’t you be with Qing Gui?”

        “Xuan Huang, I—”

        Before Bai Hu could speak another word, a thunderous dragon’s roar split the heavens—the cry of alarm, signaling an enemy assault upon their stronghold!

        “Back to the stronghold!” Xuan Huang’s expression changed instantly. Both dragons left their grievances behind and transformed into their true forms, wings beating furiously as they sped toward their home.

        By the time they arrived, the demons’ army had already encircled the land. Flames ravaged the valley—what was once a peaceful home now lay in ruins and chaos.

        Rage surged within both dragons as they beheld the desecration of their homeland. Without hesitation, they plunged into the battle. Their wings cleaved through the air as their roars shook the sky, and together they dove straight into the heart of the enemy.

        On the battlefield, metal clashed against scales. The stench of blood thickened the air. Bai Hu spun through the sky, his breath conjuring a gale that hurled several demon warriors aside. Meanwhile, Xuan Huang’s violet form streaked across the battlefield. His roar shook the ground as his claws tore through foes with overwhelming force.

        Watching him charge ahead, Bai Hu felt both pride and fear. Xuan Huang was indeed one of their clan’s fiercest warriors—but that very recklessness put him in danger time and again.

        It was only after a long and grueling fight that the Runedragons slowly gained the upper hand. Sensing defeat, the demons began to retreat. However, Xuan Huang, whose eyes blazed with fury, beat his wings again and surged forward to give chase.

        “Xuan Huang, stop! Come back!” Bai Hu’s voice rang with panic.

        But Xuan Huang was deaf to reason, his eyes blinded by anger and fixed on the fleeing enemy. Bai Hu had no choice but to follow, pushing his weary body onward.

        As the two dragons pursued the enemy, black mist surged—and a demon, Belial, emerged. He had lain in ambush upon the high cliffs, conjuring arrows with his powers and aiming them straight at Xuan Huang.

        “Xuan Huang!” Bai Hu cried in horror, lunging toward him without a second thought.

        The next instant, the arrows flew, streaking toward their mark. Bai Hu threw himself in their path. Agony tore through him as the arrow pierced his abdomen. A metallic taste flooded his throat as blood spilled from the corner of his mouth. His vision began to blur.

        He heard Xuan Huang’s voice—raw, shattered, agonized—but he could no longer respond. With the last remnants of his strength, he turned his gaze toward Xuan Huang.

        “Ah… I can’t hold on.... I can no longer protect you… So, Xuan Huang… my Souliade… please… just don’t do anything stupid again.... All I ask is that you live… safely…”
His unfinished thoughts dissolved into broken breaths, and at last Bai Hu succumbed as his mind sank into the depths of darkness…
STORY_11120:
The scent of metal filled the workshop at the Lomond Manor’s headquarters as Dolak, a towering male Machina, stood before the blazing forge, absorbed completely in his creation. His hands moved with steady precision, skillfully shaping every detail of the dragonary craft inside.

        Meanwhile, a girl with long hair watched Dolak intently from a corner of the workshop. Her name was Nulla, the spirit born from Dolak’s past creation—a dragonware crafted using the corpse of Daoloth, the primordial dragon of creation. Originally a round shield, she could take a humanoid form when she had enough powers, which made her a weapon beyond imagination.

        ‘Will… it work this time?’ She clasped her hands together anxiously, unable to tear her gaze away from Dolak’s every movement. To others, what Dolak was doing might simply seem like the creation of yet another powerful weapon. But to Nulla, this was the moment when her companion—her counterpart—might finally come into being.

        But once again, failure struck.

        With a dull explosion, the metal inside the furnace shattered. Sparks and shrapnel flew like snowflakes. Only a single dark violet scale flickered with a quiet glow in the fire, lying alone at the edge of the forge as if it had been long forgotten, lost in impossibility, which made Nulla’s heart sink in an instant.

        “As I thought… The Lord of Destruction’s power is just too overwhelming, making it difficult to merge with material from this world…” Dolak sighed, shaking his head in resignation. He carefully retrieved the scale and sealed it inside a specially crafted vessel, his face shadowed by the weight of defeat.

        “Master…” Nulla stepped to his side, speaking softly in comfort. “It’s all right. I know you’ll succeed one day.”

        “Nulla…” Dolak gently placed his hand on Nulla’s head, his fingers brushing through her long hair. His voice was filled with deep remorse as he apologized, “Forgive me. You’re the one most disappointed, yet you’re the one consoling me.”

        Nulla nuzzled her forehead against his cold, hard palm. She whispered, “You’ve worked so hard, Master. You haven’t rested properly for the past six months… I haven’t been able to help at all…”

        “Why would you think that?” Dolak shook his head firmly. “Nulla, it’s you who have been keeping me going; you’re the reason I could keep moving forward despite every failed attempt. So don’t worry—I will create your counterpart, a dragonware that shares your existence.”

        Hearing his words, Nulla lifted her head. Her eyes shone with determination as she made up her mind—she wanted to be a part of her master’s project.

        “Master, I think I can help!” she said, her voice trembling with irrepressible excitement. My body contains the power of Daoloth, the Lord of Creation. If we mix a small part of it, perhaps we can suppress the power of Azathoth, the Lord of Destruction.”

        “That’s…” Dolak stared at her in surprise, clearly unprepared for such a proposal. However, as a researcher, his mind quickly entered a storm of thought, contemplating the possibilities. Resting his chin on his hand, he murmured, “Hmm… if I adjust the ratio between the amount of metal and magic power… it may indeed increase our chances of success.”

        “Then let’s try it right away!” Nulla eagerly grabbed Dolak’s hand, her voice filled with anticipation. However, Dolak’s eyes betrayed his hesitation and worry as he gently warned, “But cutting off a part of your body will cause you great pain.”

        “I can take it.” Nulla’s gaze was unwavering, her voice soft yet unyieldingly firm. “I’m willing to endure any pain as long as it leads to success.”

        Dolak paused, silently wrestling with his thoughts. He understood the reason for Nulla’s deep attachment to the creation of another dragonware—her fear and loneliness as a unique being drove her to seek a companion.

        Finally, he drew a deep breath and nodded. “Very well. But I’ll end the experiment if there’s any danger.”

        “Thank you! I won’t let you down.” Nulla’s face lit up with a bright, radiant smile, gratitude shining in her eyes.

        She then returned to her true form and allowed Dolak to slice off a piece carefully. Her body involuntarily trembled from the pain. Still, she endured in silence until the separation was complete. After adding the fragment to the metal parts, Dolak reignited the furnace and began forging.

        Ignoring her injuries, Nulla reappeared in her human form, her eyes fixed unblinkingly on the furnace. When a soft iridescent flame flickered within the forge, she felt a premonition that it would work this time.

        Today marked exactly one year since Nulla’s birth. There was an inexplicable connection of destiny that gave her an unspoken confidence.

        And indeed, just as she had hoped, the scale fused smoothly into the metal, finally forging into a curved blade.

        Dolak lifted the blade, its surface gleaming with magical radiance, and whispered, “Una.”

        Suddenly, immense power surged from the blade. A figure gradually took shape within the magical burst, until at last a tall girl stepped slowly out from the weapon.

        Nulla’s heart overflowed with joy as she gazed at her newborn companion. Her long-awaited wish had finally become reality. The aching void within her was now filled, and all the pain and waiting had found their reward.

        However, when she rushed forward, arms outstretched to embrace Una, her new companion shoved her away. She had this look of disdain as she glared and hissed, “Who are you? Stay away from me!”

        Nulla froze, bewildered by Una’s reaction. Yet, she quickly apologized with a faint smile, her voice gentle and sincere, “Sorry, I got too excited. I’m Nulla. I’m also a spirit born from dragonware, only a year apart.”

        Dolak chuckled, teasing, “Well, I suppose that makes her your older sister.”

        “Damn it! She’s not my sister! And I don’t need one!” Dolak’s words seemed to have provoked Una. With her hair bristling like an angry cat, she growled before storming away, leaving Dolak and Nulla in stunned silence.

        “Uh… Looks like the power of the Azathoth has influenced her personality…”  Dolak muttered helplessly, glancing at Nulla to see if Una’s reaction had upset her. To his surprise, Nulla only returned a soft smile, her voice firm and resolute. “I get it. She’s still new to this world. She needs time. But don’t worry—I’ll win her over.”

        There was no trace of defeat in Nulla’s eyes, only unwavering determination. She silently swore: I will let Una know that we’re inseparable—we’re destined to become the closest family that can’t be replaced!
STORY_11121:
At the Lomond Manor’s headquarters, a black-haired girl walked down an empty corridor. In her hands was a tray, holding a sweet, fragrant cake. She glanced around, a small frown crossing her brow as she muttered to herself, “Where did Una go? I just saw her a moment ago… What am I supposed to do with this cake? I made it just for her, thinking maybe she’ll finally accept me if she tastes it… I’ll go look for her again!”

        The girl quickened her pace and hurried away. Silence returned to the corridor until one of the doors creaked open, revealing a strand of pink hair that belonged to a girl who let out a long sigh after confirming no one was around.

        “Phew… Finally, she’s gone,” she exhaled in relief, brushing her hair back. Her voice betrayed a hint of impatience.

        Her name was Una. Like the black-haired girl, Nulla, she was a spirit born from Dolak’s creations. They were both dragonwares forged from the remains of primordial dragons, Daoloth and Azathoth, and thus possessed sentience, emotions, and the ability to take on a humanoid form, which was something typical dragonwares could not offer.

        Born a year early, Nulla had longed for her counterpart’s arrival. When Dolak finally succeeded in creating Una, Nulla welcomed her with pure warmth and joy. However, her gesture appeared to be too enthusiastic and overwhelming for the fiery-tempered Una, who rejected her and stormed off right after her birth.

        Una thought her blunt refusal would drive Nulla away. Yet the very next day, Nulla found her again with a bouquet of dew-kissed flowers and a gentle smile. Una turned her down again and again. Still, Nulla never gave up. She kept coming back, showering Una with kindness, which somehow only left Una even more annoyed and agitated. A strange emotion emerged whenever she saw the disappointed look on Nulla’s face—it was guilt.

        Una couldn’t comprehend this odd emotion, so all she could do was run from it—just as she was doing now. But this time, someone found her during her escape.

        “Una, what are you doing here?” A warm, gentle male voice called from behind and startled her. She turned to see Dolak, the machina who had created her and Nulla.

        “I… I’m just wandering around,” Una stammered awkwardly, but Dolak saw right through her. With a piercing gaze, he asked, “In the dragonary craft workshop? I don’t think so. You are avoiding Nulla, aren’t you?”

        “I… I’m not—” Una tried to deny it, but the words stuck in her throat soon after she saw his knowing expression. She knew she couldn’t deceive him. Crossing her arms, she resignedly admitted, “Ugh, fine, I’m avoiding her. So what?”

        “Nothing at all,” Dolak replied calmly. He stepped past Una and placed a newly repaired dragonware part back on the shelf. He then turned to her with a faint, meaningful smile. “Tell me, why are you so stressed over this?”

        Una froze. “What…?”

        “If you truly don’t care about her, why does it bother you so much when she’s around?”

        “I don’t care about her!”  Una’s voice rose with irritation. “She’s just too annoying! Every day, she comes to me with cakes, flowers, stuffed animals, like some clingy puppy trying to get attention! I’ve rejected her so many times, and she still doesn’t get it! Is she stupid or what?”

        “She’s not stupid,” Dolak chuckled softly, settling into his chair. With his hands clasped on his lap, he then continued, “She just cares about you too much. She’s been waiting for you from the moment she was born. It’s an urge that she can’t suppress. But how about you, Una? Do you really hate her?” 

        Una’s expression stiffened. She averted her gaze, her voice faltering with uncertainty as she muttered, “I… I just hate how she acts like everything is okay. Like nothing can hurt her.”

        “But she is hurt,” Dolak softened his voice. “Every time you reject her, she comes to me asking if she’s not good enough, if it’s something about her that makes you hate her… She hurts, Una. She just doesn’t want you to know.”

        Una’s face shifted, the feeling of annoyance replaced by a storm of emotions she couldn’t name. She turned her head away and muttered, “So what if she’s hurt? I never asked her to keep coming for me.”

        “No, you didn’t,” Dolak agreed. His voice was gentle, his gaze full of forgiveness and wisdom. “But you never truly shut her out either. Una, remember the day Nulla didn’t find you? If you truly hated her, why did you go out of your way to search for her?”

        “I… I just didn’t want her causing more trouble!” Una retorted stubbornly. “Who knows if she’d try feeding more of those experimental creatures her cakes!”

        Dolak said nothing more, but the knowing look on his face suggested otherwise, which only fueled Una’s exasperation.

        “I’m done listening to your nonsense!” she growled, spinning on her heel to storm out of the workshop. But just then, she heard a cry from the corridor.

        ‘That’s Nulla’s voice!’ Her heart clenched, and before she could think, she bolted out the door.

        She arrived at the source of the commotion to find three researchers surrounding Nulla, one holding a round shield—the very core of Nulla’s being—while the other two cast spells to force her back inside it. Nulla struggled to break free, but the overwhelming force pinned her down.

        “Let her go!” Una roared. In a blur of motion, she sent one of the researchers flying with a powerful strike. She moved like a gust of wind, taking down another researcher in mere seconds.

        “S-s-stay back—or I’ll smash it!” The last one panicked and shouted, raising the shield as a threat.

        Little did he know that his action only made Una explode. With a swift strike, she sent him sprawling, her voice dripping with wrath as she shouted,  “You shouldn’t have touched her!”

        As the researcher fell, the magical restraints on Nulla faded. She slowly walked toward Una, eyes brimming with gratitude. “Una, thank you for saving me.”

        “You idiot!” Una barked, “Why didn’t you fight back when they took your shield?”

        “I… I didn’t want to hurt them...”

        “Tut! So you just let them do whatever they wanted? Ugh, you’re impossible!” Una shouted, her eyes wide with anger.

        “Then why did you save me?” Nulla asked, her eyes brimming with unshed tears as she lowered her head. Her voice was tinged with evident sadness. “Wouldn’t you be happier if they actually took me away?”

        Una froze, her breath catching in her throat. “What are you talking about…”

        Nulla turned away, her voice almost lost in the wind, “I’ve always upset you… Maybe you’ll finally be happy if I’m gone—”

        “I never wanted you gone!” Una shouted, her voice breaking as she finally gave in. Her words came out in a trembling roar full of raw emotion. “You damn idiot! If you really got taken away, I’d be miserable! What part do you not get?”

        “So you would miss me?” Nulla suddenly turned around. There were no traces of tears, but a mischievous smile on her face. “So you don’t want me to leave.”

        “You— You tricked me!” Una’s eyes widened in fury. “You lied to me?”

        “Because you’d never admit the truth,” Nulla laughed, throwing her arms around Una.

        “You—stop it! Let me go!” Una squirmed.

        “No, I’m never letting go. I’m staying with you forever,” Nulla replied.

        Una struggled for a few seconds, but eventually, her energy seemed to deflate, and her hands dropped in defeat. With a reluctant sigh, she mumbled, her voice almost inaudible, “…Just this once.”

        Only then did Nulla finally see through Una; her harsh words and cold rejection were nothing but a pretense. As time passed, their bond deepened, and together, they overcame countless challenges, united by a connection that could never be broken…
STORY_11122:
Brahmic End - Ch. 2

        The air on the thirteenth level of the Brahmic Abyss hung so thick that it seemed stagnant. The pallid stone walls, weathered by years of silence, had aged to the point where even light faltered against them, crawling sluggishly across their surface. In that suffocating stillness, only the clash of metal prevailed. Each strike reverberated through the space, echoing without end, as two figures—a boy and a girl—battled fiercely in the gloom.

        While the girl danced through the air, crimson threads flowed from her fingertips, weaving defenses and assaults as intricate as fate itself. Every move of hers was precise, with such ethereal grace and ease. It was as though she had predicted the future. Her opponent, on the other hand, was a young and raw boy—two horns curved from the sides of his brow, his limbs veined with translucent scales. His strikes were sharp and powerful; each carried a ferocious momentum.

        “You’re still too slow, Sakra,” She said as she slipped aside. Crimson threads bloomed from her fingers, pulling her clear of the boy’s line of attack. As though a dancer held aloft by strings, she stopped midair, becoming the sole vivid color in that gray expanse.

        She looked down at Sakra, her lips forming a slight curve. Her voice was gentle, yet her words were biting cold: “You won’t survive the next level like this.”

        Sakra glared upward, his breath ragged, eyes burning with defiance as he shouted, “Don’t underestimate me, Alayavijnana!” 

        With a guttural roar, the power of the dragon bone surged within him. Veins bulged, muscles swelled, and his pupils turned into slits, like those of a dragon. His horns gleamed gold as streaks of lightning crackled across his now half-dragon body.

        He leapt, unleashing a shockwave that split the ground. Yet his strength carried him too far—he jumped over her head. He panicked for a second, but quickly steadied himself. Twisting his body mid-air, he planted his feet against the ceiling and rebounded downward, striking like a thunderbolt.

        Alayavijnana blinked—she hadn’t expected his sudden shift to attack. He tackled her, pinning her to the ground in a storm of dust. His fist rose, but it did not fall.

        She opened her eyes and met his gaze, unfazed. Their breaths mingled; for a moment, time seemed to freeze around them.

        “Why don’t you strike?” she asked calmly.

        “I… I don’t want to hurt you,” Sakra muttered, turning his face aside.

        Surprise flickered across Alayavijnana’s face. She then let out a little chuckle. Tightening her threads, she reversed their positions with effortless precision, their bodies nearly entwined.

        “You need to be smarter than this, Sakra,” She leaned close, her breath brushing his ear. “Such hesitation will only hasten your death on the battlefield.”

        Sakra’s chest heaved, but he said nothing. As he stared up at her face so close, he felt something stir within him—not fear, not anger, but an ineffable emotion he could not name.

        However, Alayavijnana gave him no time to decipher such a new feeling. She released the threads, rose, and looked down at him. Her tone carried a rare warmth: “Still, you’ve done well. To master the dragon bone’s power in so short a time is no small feat.”

        Not long ago, the gravely wounded Sakra had been cast into the depths of the Brahmic Abyss by a mysterious organization known as the World Regulators. Driven by the instinct to survive, he asked Alayavijnana, the ancient demon imprisoned in the depths of the abyss, for help. The demon, in need of a convenient tool, agreed and implanted a dragon’s bone into his body.

        Through agony that literally tore him apart and reforged his very bones, Sakra clawed his way back from the clutches of death with new powers. He then began his training with Alayavijnana, learning how to wield the dragon bone’s strength—but he was far from satisfied.

        “But it’s not enough!” he cried, clenching his fists, voice thick with self‑reproach. “I’m still not strong enough! I haven’t mastered the dragon bone’s full power—mmph!”

        Alayavijnana silenced him by pressing her index finger against his lips. She smiled, her eyes curving like crescent moons, yet the darkness in her eyes remained fathomless.

        Her finger traced along his jaw. She gently lifted his face, her touch cold yet irresistibly commanding as she said, “Look at me.”

        Sakra involuntarily raised his head. There he met her eyes, vast as the cosmos. Breath fled his lungs for a splitting second; his heart couldn’t help but quiver beneath her stare. 

        “Do not let power consume you,” she whispered. “Only beasts blindly pursue power. And I made you into a dragon—not a beast.”

        “...You’re right.” The strange emotion stirred within him again, even stronger than before. However, Alayavijnana showed no awareness of his emotions—or perhaps it was just a pretense—as she loosened her grip and turned her gaze toward the colossal shadow in the distance.

        In the depths of the darkness stood a monstrous tree. Its roots coiled through the earth, branches drooping like chains, obstructing the path upward.

        “It is time to fulfill your promise,” Alayavijnana said. “To leave this place, we must first destroy that monster—the Bodhi Tree.

        “So that’s the monster created by the World Regulators?” Sakra swallowed as he stared at the unusually overwhelming tree.

        “Yes. The Bodhi Tree is a powerful monster, fused with three guardian artifacts forged by the World Regulators. Only by destroying all three artifacts at the same time can we move forward.”

        Sakra clenched his fists, eyes blazing with resolve. “I will not give up, no matter how many obstacles stand in my way!”

        Alayavijnana looked at the boy’s eyes, which blazed with rage and vengeance. A faint smile graced her lips.

        “Good, Sakra. Let that vengeance of yours be the force that carries us upward.”

        The depths of the Brahmic Abyss trembled once more as though the wheel of fate had begun to turn.

        And in the far darkness, the Bodhi Tree slowly opened its eyes, awaiting the rebels who dared to challenge destiny…
