When dawn broke over the lands of the Arcus elves, the brightest ray of sunlight cut through the thin mist. Through the lattice of a cottage window high on the peak, it quietly spilled across the long table within, casting a soft golden glow over the magic scrolls and torn pages that lay scattered across the table’s surface.

        The cottage was quiet. Only the faint rustle of turning pages could be heard until a knock at the door shattered the peaceful silence.

        “Come in,” said a gentle-looking woman sitting in the room.

        The door opened, and an elderly woman in a deep violet robe stepped into the room. Her hair was streaked with white, yet her posture remained graceful and dignified. Her name was Ruth—Diana’s mother, and one of the elders of the Arcus elves.

        “Diana, there is something I need to discuss with you,” Ruth said. Her voice was soft, yet beneath it lay the weight of worry and quiet resignation.

        Diana looked up from her scrolls. A hint of confusion flickered across her eyes as she set it down. She knew her mother would not have come for something unimportant.

         “What is it, Mother?” she asked calmly, prepared for whatever came next.

        Ruth drew a slow breath before revealing the person behind her. It was a scrawny woman, her face pale, stricken with pain and desperation as she stepped timidly into the room. In her arms was a young girl no older than ten. The child’s body was frail, as fragile as a petal torn loose by the wind. Her face seemed drained of color, her breathing faint.

        “This is my daughter, Hailey. The beasts once took her from me during the invasion ten years ago.”  The woman’s voice trembled with choked sobs. “They imprisoned her and forced her to drink some magic potions that ruined her body. We’ve tried every cure we could find, but nothing worked… I had no choice but to beg Ruth to bring me here. Diana, you are the chief of the Department of Magic in the Heptara Unies. Please… you are the only one who might be able to save her.”

        Diana’s expression softened as she saw Hailey. She gently brushed her fingers across the girl’s forehead. From the unusual chill beneath her hand, she knew this child had suffered far more than anyone her age should have endured. And in those faint, helpless eyes, Diana saw a despair so quiet it made her chest tighten.
 
        “I will do everything I can,”  Diana said. Her answer was firm, but with pain. “But given her physical condition, even if I do find a feasible treatment, she may not be able to withstand it.”

        “I know…” the woman whispered. “Every doctor said the same thing… But I can’t just give up on her… She’s still so young… She hasn’t even gotten to see the beauty of this world… Diana… Please… Help her… I’m begging you…”

        At the woman’s plea, Diana’s fingers curled around a scroll on the table. She took a deep breath. She knew clandestinely that Hailey’s chances were painfully small. Even so, Diana could not bring herself to extinguish the last hope this poor woman and child had left.

        “Do not lose hope,” Diana said at last. “I will find a way. I will not let her fade like this.”

        To find a cure for Hailey, Diana ended her leave early and returned to the Department of Magic at dawn the next day. Locking herself inside the archives, she looked through scroll after scroll. Days slipped by, and still, she found nothing.

        [i]‘Must I just helplessly watch such a young life disappear?’[/i] Diana could not forget Hailey’s eyes. They were supposed to look bright, alive, and full of wonder, yet all she could see that day was despair born of a tragedy the girl never deserved. The memory pressed against her heart like a heavy rock, leaving her with a dull ache.

        [i]‘No… I can’t give up.’[/i] After a moment of wrestling with her reason, Diana gritted her teeth and rose. She made her way into the deepest part of the Department of Magic, where a locked room stood. She opened the door, but there was nothing inside.

        Magically, when she summoned her staff and channeled her power into it, a vast magic circle bloomed across the floor, pulsing with a gentle light. Its glow rose around her like a veil, and then she vanished. The next second, she appeared in a strange, otherworldly space—the Vault of Enchantments, a secret chamber used by the Department of Magic to store valuable magical relics.

        With quiet certainty, Diana navigated through the intricate layers of magical barriers until she arrived at a radiant golden chamber. At its center floated a transparent sphere, within which several torn pages drifted. They were pieces of Bythos, a lost grimoire that was said to cover every spell in the world, yet its content was nearly impossible to decipher.

        Bythos was classified as a forbidden book. No mage was permitted to read it without authorization. But Diana had no time to wait for the permission—Hailey’s life was slipping away.

        Putting a hand on the sphere, Diana released the seal. As soon as the torn pages descended quietly into her hands, her eyes raced across the mysterious script, line after line. Then, on one torn page, she found it—a spell that could borrow life force.

        The spell allowed one to draw life force from another being, but on one condition: the spell must be cast directly onto the target’s soul.

        “Directly onto the target’s soul… The Edict of Peace…” Diana murmured.

        More than ten years ago, the beasts, led by the Phantocaudas, launched a full-scale invasion of the elves’ lands. Only through the combined strength of the other six races was their brutal massacre finally brought to an end. As punishment, a spell known as the Edict of Peace was cast upon every beast’s soul—an invisible leash that restrained them whenever they turned to cruelty.

        The Edict of Peace was exactly what Diana needed. It was perfect—almost too perfect—like some kind of invisible guidance, as if someone had placed the sweetest fruit before her, and all she needed to do was reach out and take it. The temptation was irresistible. Even Diana, who had always lived for others, could not turn away.

        [i]‘The beasts stole Hailey’s health; then it is only fair for them to pay for what they did with their life force.’[/i] With that thought, Diana put her plan into action.

        The treatment succeeded. She saved the young girl from the depths of despair. When she saw light and color return to Hailey’s eyes, she finally felt a small wave of relief, and even just slightly, the happiness washed away her guilt.

        And so came the second temptation.

        Not long after Hailey’s treatment, Diana faced another challenge. For years, she had searched for ways to suppress the Arcus elves’ mating urges, but the research demanded enormous funding she could never quite secure. Just as her worries reached their peak, an unexpected visitor—a wealthy demon merchant—arrived.

        “Chief Diana, I hear that you have been troubled over funding,” the merchant said eloquently with a knowing smile. “I am willing to provide everything you need, but on one condition.”

        Unease crept up on Diana as she looked at the merchant and asked, “What condition?”

        “I heard that you saved an elven girl with magic… ” the man said with a smile. His words were courteous, but beneath his gentle voice lay only cold calculation. “...How about you help us demons with that same magic?”

        At first, Diana hesitated. However, she eventually relented after witnessing another Arcus elf end their life under the crushing weight of their mating urges.

        [i]‘The beasts owe us. We are only taking back what should have been ours.’[/i] Once again, she convinced herself. However, what she did not realize was that she had already crossed the threshold into a bottomless abyss.
STORY_11192:
She is a White Shaman. Brave and deeply principled, she devotes herself entirely to  creating shamanic magic for the greater good.
She created the Voice of Tengri, a collection of sacred instruments capable of suppressing black shamanic magic, to prevent the Black Shamans from spreading ruin across the land.
STORY_11193:
When night fell over the Mongolian Empire, Jamukha was still sitting at his desk inside the royal study, carefully scanning the documents before him. His gaze was weary, his eyes rimmed with red streaks, and beneath them lay bruised crescents that spoke of nights of stolen sleep. His strikingly handsome face now bore an unhealthy pallor, as though color had drained from his skin.

        Just months ago, he was still the crown prince, traveling beyond the empire’s borders with Genghis Khan, the Wishbeast, in search of the Voice of Tengri, the final creation of Ulsun, the White High Shaman. But before they could gather all five instruments, news arrived: his father fell gravely ill.

        Forced to cut his journey short, Jamukha returned to the empire to assist with imperial duties. Yet, before he could fully shoulder the role, his father’s condition worsened rapidly, and the throne swiftly passed to him as his father passed away after one last affliction. 

        It all happened too quickly. Jamukha was unprepared. One moment, he was just a prince; the next, he stood at the head of a nation, struggling to breathe beneath the crown’s weight.

        However, what troubled him most was not the weighty responsibility of ruling an empire, but the threat that loomed beyond their borders—Kokochu, a Black Shaman who commanded the power of another great nation as its priest, conquering neighboring lands as he advanced. And now, his armies were closing in on the Mongolian Empire.

        [i]‘If we don’t act first, we won’t be able to stop what’s coming.’[/i] Jamukha thought with a worried frown. He rose to retrieve a war map, only to be overcome by a sudden wave of dizziness. He staggered, nearly losing his balance. Luckily, a young man rushed forward and caught him.

        “Thank you, Qorci.”

        “Your Majesty! When was the last time you rested?” asked Qorci, the general, his gaze heavy with unspoken disapproval as he looked at Jamukha. “You’ll burn yourself out!”

        “I’m fine…” Jamukha shook his head. Then, he spread the map across the desk, his voice determined as he said, “It wasn’t easy convincing the neighboring nations to join us. If we’re going to strike first and stop Kokochu, I need to come up with the best plan possible.”

        Qorci fell silent, his heart filled with genuine respect for Jamukha. As the new Khagan, what Jamukha carried was not only the fate of the Mongolian Empire but the lives of countless people. And yet, this young man had never shown the slightest hesitation, no matter the situation. So, when Qorci looked into those unwavering eyes, all his words of concern died on his lips.

        “Then give the order,” he said. “Whatever you need, I’ll see it done.”

        With Qorci’s help, the plan took shape faster than Jamukha expected, and all that remained was to rally their forces. But the change came faster before they could take the next step—Kokochu’s armies had already surrounded the empire. Villages were destroyed; many innocent lives were lost along the way, and soon the news reached Jamukha and Qorci.

        “That despicable man!” Qorci growled in rage, slamming his fist against the table. He dropped to one knee and pleaded, “Your Majesty, I request command of the army to rout our foes!”

        Yet, Jamukha withheld his answer. Choosing silence over haste, he thought:

        [i]‘No, that won’t work. The strength against us was far too great. And with Kokochu’s sorcery, even if we gave everything, it wouldn’t be enough. There is only one way left.’[/i]

        “Qorci, that is not the task I’m giving you,” said Jamukha, who at last made up his mind. His voice carried a certain kind of conviction as he continued, “Take an elite unit and the best horses. Go to the nearest nation as fast as you can and request reinforcements.”

        “…What about you, Your Majesty?” Qorci asked, unease creeping into his voice.  “You’re coming with me, aren’t you?”

        Jamukha shook his head. A faint smile, calm and unburdened, crossed his lips. It looked as though he had already made peace with what lay ahead.

        “I am the Khagan of the Mongolian Empire. How could I leave my nation in the face of war?” he said.

        “No! No!” Qorci rose abruptly and protested. “Then let me stay—”

        “That’s an order, General Qorci.” The authority in Jamukha’s voice left no room for argument.

        “Go now. The sooner you return with reinforcements, the better our chances.”

        “…Understood!” Qorci gave a resolute reply, casting aside his hesitation before turning to leave.

        “Wait.” Jamukha halted him. He removed the flute at his side and placed it in Qorci’s hands. He then said, “Give this to Genghis.” 

        Sorrow crossed Qorci’s face the moment he heard Jamukha. Yet, he knew there was nothing he could say to change Jamukha’s mind, so all he could manage was  a choked whisper: “...I will not disappoint you.” 

        With that, Qorci disappeared into the night. Left alone in the room, Jamukha walked to the window and looked toward the horizon, where dawn slowly broke. His voice was low with regret as he mumbled, “Genghis… I’m sorry. Looks like I won’t be keeping my promise after all.”

        Then he closed his eyes. A tear slipped quietly down his cheek. After a moment, he wiped it away. Then he turned and donned his armor. With his sword fastened, he stepped out of the study and marched toward the battlefield that awaited him…
STORY_11194: Loyal and steadfast, he is a general of the Mongolian Empire who commands with honesty and unquestionable strength. Away from the battlefield, however, his awkwardness in worldly affairs often stirs more trouble than resolution.
STORY_11195: It is created to guard the tomb of Ulsun, the White High Shaman, and ensure that no one steals the treasures sealed within.
STORY_11196:
It is a powerful puppet created by the Black Shaman,  Kokochu, using the corpses of Wishbeasts.
It possesses the terrifying ability to absorb others’ fortune.
STORY_11197:
He is a Black Shaman. Cunning and ruthless, he feeds his own ambitions by whatever means, fair or foul.
Serving as the priest of a great nation, he has exhorted the king to wage several wars, leaving countless innocents in the fire of chaos.
STORY_11199:
He is a Barrenont, a determined, mature, and level-headed young boy with an exceptional gift for magic.
Through talent and diligence, he wins the scholarship to a magic academy and becomes one of the rare beastfolk students to study magic.
STORY_11201:
She is a student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and the younger sister of Tatsuya Shiba. She deeply adores her brother, addressing him as “Onii-sama,” and her intense affection is such that those around them often mistake their relationship for that of lovers.
Unlike her brother, she possesses extraordinary magical talent along with flawless beauty. As one of the Course 1 students, also known as the Blooms, she stands among the elite, embodying both exceptional ability and beauty.
She specializes in Freezing Magic, and her power is said to rival—even surpass—that of Angie Sirius, the commander of the USNA Army Magician Unit, Stars.
STORY_11202:
Known by the nickname “Lina,” she has been admitted as an exchange student and has become Miyuki’s classmate in Class A at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School. Her beauty, though different from Miyuki’s, is equally captivating, drawing the admiration of many male students.
Her magical ability is formidable, rivaling even Miyuki’s in power.
STORY_11203:
Serving as the Student Council President at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School, she is regarded as one of the most talented individuals in the school’s history. As the eldest daughter of the Saegusa family, one of the Ten Master Clans, she specializes in Long‑Range Precision Magic.
Though she carries a mischievous, devilish charm, she openly opposes discrimination against Course 2 students and works to create a more inclusive environment at school. Despite her petite stature, she has a strikingly voluptuous figure, and her beauty has earned her a wide following both within the school and beyond.
STORY_11204:
He is a student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School, born into the prestigious Yotsuba family, one of the most renowned lineages among magicians. Despite this heritage, his lack of magic power led to his enrollment as a Course 2 student, where he is derisively labeled a “Weed.”
During the entrance examinations, he achieved an unprecedented score on the written test. However, his performance in the practical exam barely met the minimum passing standard due to a critical flaw.
His true strengths lie in technical fields such as CAD design. In addition, he is highly skilled in hand-to-hand combat, granting him formidable combat capabilities.
Now in his second year, he attends the newly established Magical Engineering Department.
STORY_11205:
He is a student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School. While he struggles with conventional magic, he excels in Decomposition and Regrowth magic, and his proficiency in hand-to-hand combat further elevates his overall combat effectiveness.

Beyond his role as a student, he also serves as a soldier in the 101 Independent Magic-Equipped Battalion of the National Defense Force. During the Yokohama Disturbance, he played a crucial role in repelling the forces of the Great Asian Alliance, ultimately annihilating an enemy naval port with the Strategic-Class magic, Material Burst.
STORY_11206:
She is a first-year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School. Born to parents whose magical abilities were artificially enhanced through genetic modification, she is part of the second generation of “Sakura”, the engineered magician series.
She specializes in barrier magic, and the strength of her barriers rivals even that of Katsuto Jumonji, marking her as an exceptionally powerful magician.
STORY_11207:
She is a second‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and a friend of Tatsuya Shiba. She is the second daughter of the Chiba family, a lineage widely known as the Sword Magicians.
With her bright, outgoing charm and striking beauty, she naturally draws attention wherever she goes. With her bold, energetic personality, she has a way of dragging people into the action, often sparking unexpected chaos.
The Chiba family is a distinguished lineage of kenjutsu users who combine Self‑Acceleration Spell with Weight Magic, and she is an exceptional swordswoman, true to her heritage. Her skill in one‑on‑one combat is remarkable, and her speed is considered unmatched among her peers.
STORY_11208:
He is a second-year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and a friend of Tatsuya Shiba, commonly known by the nickname “Leo.”
He comes from a diverse background, with a father of half foreign heritage and a mother of quarter foreign heritage, which is reflected by his name. With sharply defined features and outstanding athletic ability, he often attracts the attention of female classmates.
He specializes in Fortifying Magic.
STORY_11209:
She is a second‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and a friend of Tatsuya Shiba.
Though occasionally a little airheaded, she is earnest and sincere at heart. Unaware of her own charm, she has become popular among upperclassmen as a “healing‑type little sister” figure.
She is a rare possessor of the Crystal Eyes, a highly prized form of spiritual perception recognized among Ancient Magic practitioners. Her glasses—unusual in this era—suppress her hypersensitivity to Spirit Particle Emissions, preventing her from perceiving them involuntarily.
STORY_11210:
He is the second son of the prestigious Yoshida family, renowned for their mastery of Ancient Magic.
Once celebrated as a prodigy for his extraordinary talent, he suffered a major setback a year before enrolling at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School. During the “Starfall Ritual,” a ceremony meant to summon a dragon god, the ritual failed. The aftermath left him in a prolonged slump, weakening his abilities and leading to his admission as a Course 2 student.
His encounter with Tatsuya Shiba marked a turning point. Gradually overcoming his slump, he regained the power that had once earned him the title of prodigy. By his second year, he advanced into Course 1, reclaiming his place among the elite.
As a skilled practitioner of Ancient Magic, he excels not only in direct combat but also in detection and search techniques. Despite his calm and unassuming demeanor, he possesses remarkable physical ability, making him a versatile magician capable of thriving in any situation.
STORY_11211:
She is Tatsuya Shiba’s younger sister, a first‑year middle school student from the Yotsuba family’s main line, recognized as a candidate for the family’s leadership. Unlike her brother, she possesses extraordinary magical talent. 
She is a girl of striking beauty. Her skin is as white as snow, and her hair is as dark as night. But she remains self‑conscious about her appearance, especially after friends remarked that she resembles a “yukionna,” a snow woman.
Although her magical power is extraordinarily high, she lacks the combat training that Tatsuya has undergone, leaving her ill‑suited for battle.
STORY_11212:
Tatsuya Shiba is a second‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and the elder brother of Miyuki Shiba. Although born into the prestigious Yotsuba family, his unconventional magical abilities led to him being treated more like a servant within the household, serving as Miyuki’s Guardian. His successful completion of Maya’s mission—“Capture Zhou Gongjin”—earned him recognition for both his skill and his unwavering loyalty. Even so, some of the branch family heads remain cautious, and his final evaluation has been deferred until the Yotsuba family’s New Year gathering, the Keishunkai.

Miyuki Shiba is a second-year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and the younger sister of Tatsuya Shiba. In contrast to her brother, she possesses extraordinary magical talent paired with flawless beauty. Consistently ranked first in her year, she excels in Freezing Magic, and her power is said to rival—or even surpass—that of Angie Sirius, commander of the USNA Army Magician Unit Stars. She deeply adores her brother, addressing him as “Onii-sama,” and her intense affection is such that those around them often mistake their relationship for that of lovers. She has been invited to the Keishunkai, but she looks uneasy and reluctant for some reason.
STORY_11213:
He is the head priest of Kyuchoji Temple and a master of ninjutsu, a classified Ancient Magic rooted in the shinobi tradition. He commands respect as a renowned figure who leads many disciples, yet there is always an air of subtle suspicion around him.
He shows genuine fondness for the Shiba siblings, doting on Miyuki while personally guiding Tatsuya in martial arts.
STORY_11214:
As a member of the Great Asian Alliance’s special operations unit, he is recognized as one of the world’s top close‑combat magicians.
Feared for his ferocious temperament, he has earned the title, “Man‑Eating Tiger.”
A leading practitioner of the Fortifying Qigong spell, he can conjure armor harder than steel. Its advanced form, Steel Qigong spell, grants him an impregnable level of defense, making him a near‑unstoppable force on the battlefield.
STORY_11215: He is a second-year student at the National Magic University Affiliated Third High School and the heir to the Ichijo family. He is known by the title “Crimson Prince.”
STORY_11216:
He is a third‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and heir to the prestigious Jumonji family, a lineage of magicians known as the “Iron Wall.”
He is a formidable magician who specializes in Area Defense Magic.
STORY_11217: Holding the rank of Major, she serves as commander of the USNA Army Magician Unit Stars. Within the unit, members are given codenames inspired by celestial bodies, and “Sirius” is reserved for the strongest magician, a title that belongs to her.
STORY_11218:
Ayako Kuroba is the eldest daughter of the Kuroba family, a branch of the Yotsuba clan, and the twin sister of Fumiya. She enrolled at the National Magic University Affiliated Fourth High School in 2096 and is Tatsuya Shiba’s second cousin, a year behind him. As part of the Kuroba family, famed for its expertise in intelligence and covert operations, Ayako has been directing missions since her middle school years. On assignment, she operates under the codename “Yoru.” She excels in Convergence‑Type Fortifying Magic, skillfully wielding techniques such as Perfect Dispersion and Mock Teleportation. However, her abilities are best suited for support and strategy rather than direct combat. Ayako holds deep admiration for Tatsuya and plans to attend the Keishunkai with her twin brother, Fumiya.

Fumiya Kuroba is the eldest son of the Kuroba family, and the younger twin brother of Ayako. He enrolled in the Fourth High School in 2096 and is Tatsuya’s second cousin, a year behind him. Like his sister, Fumiya has been involved in intelligence and covert operations since his middle school years, working under the codename “Yami.”  Because of his delicate appearance, which often leads others to mistake him for a girl, he conceals his identity with disguises during missions. He specializes in Mental Interference‑Type Magic, using techniques like Direct Pain, and serves as the family’s primary combatant. Like Ayako, he deeply admires Tatsuya. He will be attending the Keishunkai as one of the candidates for the Yotsuba family’s next leadership.
STORY_11219:
She is a second‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School, a friend of Tatsuya Shiba, and a classmate of Miyuki Shiba.
She is a highly capable student who ranks second overall in the year‑end examinations, standing second only to Miyuki in magical ability. Her specialty lies in Light-Wave Oscillation Magic Spell.
Though gentle and soft‑spoken by nature, she tends toward strong assumptions, which sometimes causes her to act boldly and even impulsively.
STORY_11220:
He is a young man who runs a Chinese restaurant in Yokohama’s Chinatown while secretly serving as the leader of the anti‑magic organization, Blanche. He has orchestrated various incidents from the shadows to eliminate magicians.
He specializes in Qimen Dunjia and wields a unique form of magic that embeds a synthetic beast, known as Shadow Beast, into talismans.
STORY_11221:
He is the third son of the Kudou family’s head.
With an appearance that rivals Miyuki’s in beauty, he has an almost mystical allure. Yet his straightforward and gentle nature lends him a puppy‑like, approachable charm.
He enrolled at Second High School in 2096. Though his magical power is said to be on par with Miyuki’s, his frail health often forces him to miss classes, leaving him with few close friends.
Capable of wielding a wide range of magic, particularly Emission‑Type Magic, he is said to surpass even Angelina Kudou Shields in mastery of the Kudou family’s secret technique, Parade.
STORY_11222:
She is a second‑year student at the National Magic University Affiliated First High School and the eldest daughter of the immensely wealthy Kitayama family. She is also a friend of Tatsuya Shiba and a classmate of Miyuki Shiba and Honoka Mitsui.
Quiet and reserved, she rarely shows her emotions, though she can be surprisingly direct when speaking her mind.
Counted among the school’s most powerful students, Shizuku specializes in Oscillation‑Type Magic. With exceptional processing ability and vast magical capacity, she can unleash high‑output spells with ease, but she admits her fine control is not her strongest suit.
STORY_11223:
Katsushige Shibata is the eldest son of the Shibata family, a branch of the Yotsuba clan, and a candidate for its next leadership. 23 years old, he serves in the Japan Defense Forces (JDF). Ranking at the very top among the Yotsuba’s combat magicians, he specializes in Convergence‑Type Magic, with a particular focus on Density Manipulation. Towering over Tatsuya with a height of 188 centimeters, he is a formidable magician who has exceptional magical ability with equally strong physical power.

Kotona Tsutsumi is the Guardian of Katsushige Shibata. 24 years old, she belongs to the second generation of the “Musician” series, a line of genetically modified beings with exceptional aptitude for sound‑based magic.  She is romantically involved with Katsushige, and the two are already in a common‑law partnership. However, due to the instability of her modified genes, she has given up on the idea of a formal marriage.
STORY_11224:
She is the eldest daughter of the Tsukuba family, a branch of the Yotsuba clan. 22 years old, she is currently a fourth‑year student at Magic University.
She has exceptional aptitude in all forms of Mental Interference‑Type Magic, a gift that comes from her mother, Fuyuka. Unlike many other branch family members, she maintains a neutral stance toward Tatsuya and has no intention of alienating him.
As one of the candidates for the Yotsuba family’s next leadership, she has been invited to the Keishunkai.
STORY_11225:
She is the current head of the Yotsuba family and the younger twin sister of Miya Yotsuba, making her the aunt of Tatsuya Shiba and Miyuki Shiba. As of April 2096, she is 46 years old, though she appears no older than her early thirties. She has a captivating beauty that blends mature charm with an alluring, almost dangerous elegance.
Her unique magic, Meteor Line, is said to be impossible to defend against or interrupt once activated. Such overwhelming power has earned her recognition as one of the world’s strongest magicians, feared as the “Demon King of the Far East” and “Queen of the Night.”
She has gathered the candidates for the Yotsuba family’s next leadership at the clan’s New Year assembly, the Keishunkai, where she intends to decide on her successor.
STORY_11227: Mori Ranmaru is Kanon’s familiar, a tiny bat who is often seen perched on her shoulder. Small but quick-witted, he remains Kanon’s closest companion through both ordinary tasks and uncertain journeys.
STORY_11228:
Kanon is Izumo’s close friend and a witch who has already completed the rite. Soft and sweet, she enjoys being doted on and tends to rely on those stronger than herself.
Even so, she longs to grow stronger in her own way, hoping one day to shine brightly enough that everyone will look her way.
STORY_11229:
Izumo is a gifted witch with a bright and honest heart, who treasures her friends and never breaks a promise. Carrying a warmth that lifts others and an unyielding will, she is always the first to step forward when danger arises.
After many trials, she received the blessing of Living Grace from the Spring of Saint Walpurgis and became one of the thirteen witches in the prophecy.
STORY_11230: Mochi is Kagurazaka’s familiar. Lively and chatty by nature, he wears every emotion on his face and is always ready with a sharp comment, especially when Kagurazaka or the rest of the group does something ridiculous. Noisy as he is, he is extremely loyal and always supports Kagurazaka in his own way.
STORY_11231:
Kagurazaka is a powerful witch who excels at chain magic. She struggles to put her feelings into words, which often makes her seem cold and distant. Yet beneath her reserved manner lies a tender heart and a quiet resolve to protect those she holds dear.
Awkward at times but deeply reliable, she walks beside her friends through every trial. After receiving the blessing of the Quiet Dark from the Spring of Saint Walpurgis, she became one of the thirteen witches foretold in the prophecy.
STORY_11232: Tomozou is a divine stag that serves as Izumo’s familiar. Blunt, strict, and sharp-tongued, he never misses a chance to lecture Izumo like an elder. Still, his harsh words always come from genuine concern. Calm under pressure and wise from long experience, he is the steady voice that keeps her on the right path.
STORY_11234:
Guardian Goddess is a giantess who guards the seal of Witchhaven. Her towering form carries an overwhelming presence.
Tasked with barring all who trespass into the town of witches, she moves with cold precision and unwavering purpose, devoted entirely to fulfilling the duty she was given.
STORY_11235:
Annette works at the Witches’ Guild, where she handles commissions and guides witches through their assignments. Knowing the guild’s procedures inside and out, she keeps everything moving with quiet efficiency.
Warm, attentive, and wonderfully organized, she is one of the people who make the guild’s everyday work possible.
STORY_11236:
Glen works at the Witches’ Guild as a guard. Serious and watchful, he keeps a close eye on everyone who comes and goes.
Though his role may not seem glamorous, his vigilance helps keep the guild orderly and secure.
STORY_11237:
Sahara is the Witch of Borrowed Pain, one of the thirteen witches foretold in the prophecy.
Having a relaxed elegance that makes others feel at ease, he is naturally good at looking after people. He often eases tense moments with a light remark or an unhurried smile. But when the moment demands it, he is always there to lend a steady hand.
STORY_11240:
Dunhuang is the Witch of Endless Dream, one of the thirteen witches foretold in the prophecy.
Graceful in bearing and gentle in manner, she also serves as the president of the Witches’ Guild. As the one who oversees the affairs of witches, she leads with both compassion and clear judgment. Even in times of crisis, she remains calm enough to see the path forward.
STORY_11243: Shangri-La serves as Deputy Chief of the Department of Security under the Heptara Unies. Calm and deeply disciplined, she can assess danger quickly even in the middle of chaos, then bring the situation under control with as little loss as possible.
STORY_11244:
Late at night, one particular office remained brightly lit within the Enochian Tower, headquarters of the Heptara Unies. After days spent buried in reports, investigations, and emergencies, even Cilovic, Chief of the Department of Security, had reached his limit. Before he knew it, he had fallen asleep at his desk.

        As though sensing his exhaustion, the elements quietly gathered around him and wove a dream, a vision of the fate he might have faced had he made a different choice…

        “You said someone who isn’t a summoner managed to summon a heroic spirit?” Cilovic raised an eyebrow as he took a sip of the extra-strong coffee sitting on his desk. He immediately regretted it—the coffee was brewed with three times the usual amount of grounds. With a grimace, he set the cup aside, rubbed his aching temple, and looked up at the elven woman standing before him—Nocturne, one of the Heptara Unies‘ summoner trainers.

        “Yes,” Nocturne replied in her usual cool, detached tone. “He summoned a heroic spirit and repelled the attackers during the Establishment Day celebration.”

        “That’s certainly a first,” Cilovic murmured, leaning back in his chair. He pondered for a moment before making his decision: “Bring him here. I want to see him myself.”

        Nocturne nodded and left. Before long, she returned with a young boy named Shroy Zagudy.

        The boy had delicate, almost androgynous features. Despite his gentle appearance, there was a quiet, tenacious air about him that caught Cilovic’s attention. More importantly, he could tell that the boy had no idea what kind of danger he had been dragged into.

        [i]‘I'm the adult here. It’s my job to shield innocent children like him with everything I have.’[/i] For once, Cilovic let sympathy influence his judgment. He decided against sending Shroy to the summoners’ practical exam and instead arranged for the boy to stay at the Heptara Unies’ headquarters, with staff members taking turns to keep watch over him.

        But he had underestimated just how far his enemies were willing to go.

        By the time Cilovic finished dealing with the fallout from the Establishment Day attack, it was already deep into the night. Just as he was about to get some rest, his communicator rang.

        He answered immediately, “Milton? What is it?”

        “The Chaos Scale in Pilgrimage has been fluctuating,” said Milton, a Tuxia dragon descended from Bahamut and one of the guardians of Pilgrimage. “It’s below the warning threshold, but the readings are unusually high. It might be worth taking a look.”

        “Understood, I’m heading down now.” After ending the call, Cilovic headed for the Pilgrimage. The moment he arrived at the underground entrance, he knew something was wrong—the doorway stood empty; Milton, who was supposed to be guarding the door, wasn’t there. A bad feeling settled in the pit of Cilovic’s stomach.

        [i]‘...Something’s off… I’m being watched…’[/i] The corridor was dim and quiet; Cilovic could barely see his surroundings. Still, the faint tremor in the air was enough to alert him to the presence lurking in the shadows. Keeping his expression unchanged, he continued toward the entrance—

        —Clang!

        Suddenly, a clang of metals shattered the silence.

        “Oh my, you managed to block my attack.” The voice belonged to a girl who chuckled as she stepped into the light. She looked young and thin, almost to the point of frailty, with pale skin that gave her a perpetually sickly air.

        She then bent down to pick up the silver knife on the floor, one she had shot at him with magic but knocked aside. However, her failed assassination didn’t seem to bother her. If anything, her eyes lit up with amusement, like a child who had just found a new toy.

        “Impressive, Chief of the Department of Security,” the girl applauded. “You didn’t show even a single opening.”

        “Didn't realize I was that famous. Even a little girl like you knows who I am.” Cilovic smiled politely. His eyes, however, remained cold.

        “Don’t call me a little girl. I’m much older than I look,” the girl giggled and said. “Please, call me Cain.”

        “Very well, Miss Cain,” Cilovic said, “Then perhaps you can tell me where Milton, my subordinate, is.”

        “Hm?” Cain pressed a finger to her lips and tilted her head. A moment later, she lightly tapped a fist into her palm with a look of realization. Then she smiled and said, “Oh. You mean him?”


        As Cain spoke, a massive shadow slowly stepped out of the darkness. It was less a creature than a nightmare—a monster with four enormous flower-like heads, each bloom packed with rows of razor-sharp teeth. Hanging from one of those gaping maws was a young man, a dragonfolk, bloodied and barely conscious.

        “Milton!” Cilovic shouted in terror.

        “Oh. So he’s one of yours. Then you can have him back.” Cain said. As she snapped her fingers, the monster opened its jaws and spat Milton onto the floor. Cilovic immediately rushed over to his side.

        “Ch-Chief…” Milton's eyes fluttered open for a moment, but they slipped shut again before he could get another word out.

        Cilovic quickly checked Milton’s condition. Relief flickered through him when he found a pulse, but it didn’t last long.

        [i]‘Milton’s alive, but he’s barely clinging to life. If I don’t get him treated soon, the damage could be permanent.’[/i]

        Cilovic looked at Cain and the monster at her side. Even knowing the answer, he decided to ask. “This probably isn't going to work, but would you let us leave?”

        “I’m sorry,” Cain said, “but I can’t do that.”

        “That’s what I thought.” Cilovic placed Milton against the entrance and stood. A staff appeared in his hand. Facing Cain once more, he calmly declared, “Then I’ll just defeat you myself.

        “No, your fight isn’t with me.” Cain shook her head. “It’s with them.”

        At her words, a thunderous boom shook the entire room. Two colossal figures appeared in a flash of light—two other monsters with an overwhelming aura of menace that looked like the monstrous flower beside Cain. One glance was enough to tell that these creatures were not born of this world’s law of nature.

        “Three against one. That's a little unfair, don't you think?” Cilovic muttered, but years of battle experience had already driven him into motion.

        One spell after another shot from his staff, striking the monsters with ruthless precision. The attacks left visible wounds, but the process was far too slow. Spell after spell flew from his staff, slamming into the monsters in a relentless barrage. His attacks worked, just not fast enough.

        [i]‘I don't have time for this. Milton needs treatment. That means I’ll have to use something more powerful…’[/i] For a moment, Cilovic wavered. Then he steeled himself. ‘Jean. I'm sorry, but I'll have to borrow your power.’

        As he channeled his powers, crimson light erupted from the mysterious markings on his skin. Intricate magic circles bloomed beneath his feet, spreading until they nearly covered the entire path outside the Pilgrimage. Power surged through the air.  It gathered and condensed around his body, weaving itself into layers of radiant light until he seemed clad in gleaming golden armor.

        He then hovered before the entrance to the Pilgrimage and raised his staff. Light gathered at his call, taking the form of a colossal warrior who raised a massive sword of shimmering light, ready to strike.

        When Cilovic opened his eyes, their irises had turned a vivid crimson that matched the glowing markings on his skin. For a moment, he seemed almost beyond mortal. Then he spoke, calm and certain, “Six-layered Magic Formula: Voidfall.”

        As he spoke, the warrior swung its sword. The crushing weight of the spell froze the three monsters in place. The blade came down.

        A sharp crack echoed through the room. Then, in an instant, all monsters were erased. For a moment, peace returned to the Pilgrimage until the sound of enthusiastic applause cut through the silence.

        “Bravo! Amazing!” Cain shouted. The monsters’ destruction didn’t seem to bother her in the slightest. Instead, she looked genuinely pleased, as if she had just witnessed an entertaining performance.

        “Then you’ll be paying the price for this performance by staying here!” Cilovic shot forward to seize Cain. Before he could reach her, a swift figure cut in ahead of him and snatched her away, slipping past his attack.

        Leaning comfortably against her rescuer, Cain smiled brightly. Her body began to dissolve into shadow from the feet up as she said, “I had fun today. Let’s play again sometime.”

        “Wait!” Cilovic called out, but it was already too late. By the time he reached the spot, both the intruders were gone.


        “Tut! They sure know how to run.” He clicked his tongue in annoyance, but he quickly suppressed that feeling, for more pressing matters demanded his attention. Once he took Milton to the treatment room, he reinforced the guards around Pilgrimage. Still, the unease lingered. Something about the whole encounter didn’t sit right with him.

        “What’s wrong?” asked Nocturne. She had been summoned to deal with the emergency and immediately noticed Cilovic’s troubled expression."

        “The girl left too easily. She knew she wouldn’t get another chance after tonight, and yet she left empty-handed...” Cilovic frowned as he pondered in silence. Then it hit him. His head snapped up. “…No. She did accomplish something. She lured me away.”

        “If that’s true… then why tonight?” Nocturne’s eyes widened. The realization struck them both at the same time, and they shouted:

        “Shroy Zagudy!”

        The two rushed toward Shroy’s room, but they were too late. The boy was already on the floor when they arrived. Cilovic crossed the room and lifted him into his arms. The moment he touched him, his expression changed. The body was cold. His eyes were closed, his face pale. There was no breath.

        “They’ve taken his soul…” Cilovic slammed his fist into the floor. “Damn it! This is all my fault. I shouldn’t have left him here.”

        “Chief, you were only trying to protect him,” Nocturne said. “No one could’ve seen this coming.”

        “No. That’s the problem.” Cilovic shook his head. “I focused too much on protecting him. That’s exactly what tipped them off and made them think he was something special. That’s why they targeted him... I made the wrong choice….”

        Guilt and regret consumed Cilovic. To correct his mistake, he ignored Nocturne’s protests and used magic to keep Shroy’s body alive, even if it cost him his remaining lifespan.  At the same time, he dispatched every available hand to search for the boy’s lost soul, hoping to bring back the life of the child fate had cruelly toyed with…

        [i]‘Overprotection only takes away children’s chance to grow. Only by letting them face hardship and failure can they become truly strong, and that is the truest form of protection.[/i]

STORY_11246:
The rainy season showed no sign of ending along the beasts’ frontier.

        Cold wind swept through the narrow streets as fine rain slanted across the slums, and beneath one of the rattling eaves, Reyne, a Corrodent, stood quietly. Half her cloak was already soaked through. Wet hair clung to the side of her face, but her eyes remained cold and focused. In her hand was a crumpled note with a hastily scribbled message—

        “Young beasts. Tonight. Warehouse. Resale.”

        Reyne had not smiled once since House died. Her elder brother had always stood between her and danger, and now he was gone for good. But his death had changed nothing. The world was still just as cruel; traffickers still hunted young beasts, put a price on them, and sold them from one buyer to the next until they disappeared somewhere no one could find them.

        She drew a slow breath of icy air and whispered, “Let’s go.”

        A small group of beasts followed in silence. They were all House’s comrades whom he had trusted with his life.

        The note led them deep into an abandoned industrial district. The warehouse looked half-rotten, its walls stained by years of rain and neglect. The iron door hung ajar while rain drummed from the broken eaves onto the ground in a dull, steady rhythm.

        Inside the dimly lit warehouse, more than a dozen young beasts huddled in cages pressed against a corner, trying to hold back their frightened whimpers.

        There, Reyne saw a child standing, gripping the bars, their tiny fingers white with strain.

        The sight pulled Reyne back to her own childhood—and to the day when House rested a hand on her head and said, [i]“We don’t become strong so people will fear us; we become strong so the weak don’t have to be afraid.”[/i]

        Her hand tightened into a fist.

        “Get them out.”

        Three shadows burst through the windows.

        Glass scattered across the floor as rain and shouts flooded the warehouse.  Reyne dropped the nearest guard with a quick slash of her dagger, while her companions rushed to the children and broke their chains.

        For a few moments, everything went exactly as planned. It was easy, almost too easy—as if someone had left the door open and waited for them to walk right in.

        Just as Reyne’s group was about to take the children out of the warehouse, a crimson magic circle flared across the floor. Its glare swept through the room as heavy iron plates slammed down over every exit. Before anyone could react, acrid smoke poured into the sealed warehouse, carrying a toxin that numbed the nerves.

        “It’s a trap!” Reyne held her breath through clenched teeth, but her limbs still grew heavy, and her vision began to blur.

        “I knew you’d come, you filthy beasts.” A finely dressed man appeared on the second floor. A cold smile spread across his face as more than a dozen armed thugs took position behind him with crossbows aimed at them.

        “You’ve ruined enough of my business. And now you’re going to make up for my losses,” the man said. His leering gaze swept over Reyne as he continued, “You, especially. I imagine you’ll fetch an excellent price.”

        Murder flared in Reyne’s eyes.

        “Shut your mouth!” Reyne lunged at the man, but chains lashed out from a magic circle and caught her arm in midair. She struck the floor hard enough to hear the crack in her ribs. Blood rose in her throat and filled her mouth. She tried to push herself up, but the poison blurred her sight. Through the haze, she could see the children trembling inside their cages, and one of them was crying for their mother 

        Her fingers clawed into the rainwater and grime beneath her as she thought:

         [i]‘Damn it... Is this where I die too? ….Just like House… without changing anything?’[/i]

        Then, a deafening crash shook the warehouse.

        Someone ripped through the iron barricade from the other side. As the acrid smoke cleared, a tall figure appeared in the opening.

        Reyne stared in disbelief and whispered, “...Caesar?”

        “Sorry,” Caesar looked at her and said softly. “I’m late.”

        “So you’re one of them?” The man eyed Caesar warily, but his caution faded into a sneer when he realized Caesar had come alone. “Do you honestly think you can save them all by yourself? Know your limits!” 

        “My limits?” Caesar stepped into the warehouse, his voice low. “Come down here and find out.”

        “Kill him!” the man shouted. The thugs fired their bolts in unison.

        Caesar’s frame surged into the form of a massive beast as crimson sanguine patterns blazed across his skin. With his muscles hardened like steel, the bolts shattered on impact. They couldn’t even break his stride. He slammed into the line of thugs like a battering ram, cutting through them one after another with his claws. Their leader barely had time to run away before Caesar caught him and pinned him to the floor. 
  
        “W-Wait!” the man stammered beneath his claws. “I-I have money! I-I can give you anything you want!”

        “Sorry, but no  amount of money buys mercy for men who prey on children.”

        Caesar knocked the man unconscious, then tossed him onto the heap with the rest of his thugs.

        By the time he reached Reyne in his human form, she had already torn through the chains and reclaimed her dagger. She forced herself to stand, only for the lingering poison to send her stumbling sideways. Caesar caught her by the shoulder.

        “Can you walk?” he asked.

        “I’m not that weak.”

        “Good. You handle the children, and I’ll deal with these men.”

        “You’re giving me orders?”

        “Yes. Just like I used to give House orders.” At House’s name, something shifted in Caesar’s eyes. Reyne caught the pain there and fell silent.

        He turned away and walked toward the unconscious thugs before she could say anything else.

        Only then did Reyne understand that Caesar had not left House’s death behind any more than she had. He had simply learned to carry the grief where no one else could see it, forcing one foot in front of the other because stopping was not an option.

        Reyne hurried back to the cages where the children huddled together in tears. Remembering how House used to comfort her, she held out a hand and said, “It’s okay now. We’re taking you home.”

        Reyne and her companions led the children out through the opening in the wall. They kept close around them until they were safely back in the arms of the parents waiting outside.

        From a short distance away, Reyne watched as the parents reunited with their children in tears. She quickly looked away before anyone could notice the redness gathering around her eyes.

        Caesar walked to her side and offered her a handkerchief.

        “House used to say you were stronger than him.”

        “He was lying. I’m just better at pretending.”

        “Sometimes, pretending you won’t fall is enough to save a great many people.”

        For a while, Reyne said nothing. Then she took the handkerchief. After blowing her nose with a loud, unapologetic snort, she asked, “So what now? What are you going to do?”

        “I’m putting together a mercenary group.” Caesar looked into the distance, watching the families make their way home hand in hand.         A quiet warmth softened his eyes as he said, “We’ll take commissions and make enough to get by. We’ll accept the jobs no one else will and help people no one else thinks are worth saving”

        “...Why?”

        “The beasts have been looked down on for too long, and violence will never change that. We need to show the seven races that beasts are more than brute force and destruction—that we can protect people too.”

        “That… might be the most naive thing I’ve ever heard,” Reyne said.

        “I know.”

        “It also sounds like a lot of trouble.”

        “I know that too.”

        A laugh slipped out before Reyne could stop it—the first real one since House died. She then said, “But I kind of like it.”

        Caesar gave a quiet chuckle and offered her his hand as he said, “Then join me, Reyne. Let’s avenge House our own way.”

        As the morning light broke through the clouds and reached the muddy street, Reyne looked at the reunited families and slowly clenched her fist.

        House was gone, but Reyne still had a life ahead of her. She would live it fully enough for both of them. Taking Caesar’s hand, she nodded and said, “I’m in.”

        Her gaze was as sharp as ever, but now a new light burned within it: a small, resilient flame that rose from the ashes.

        “Just to make it clear,” she added, “If you ever lose your way, I’ll beat some sense back into you myself.”

        “I’d expect nothing less.”

        No one knew it then, but the mercenary group that would one day become known throughout the seven races had just been born in that muddy alley.

        That group would come to be known as the Uncharted Oathkeepers.
STORY_11247:
Turing is a brilliant scientist who once served as headmaster of the scientific organization, Lomond Manor. Gifted with extraordinary insight and creativity, she can analyze even the most difficult situations with remarkable precision. Though delicate in appearance, she is calm, sharp-tongued, and almost impossible to unsettle. When danger strikes, she is often the first to find a way through.

Bermuda is the moving castle Turing built. Dramatic and clingy, he often tests Turing’s patience with his exaggerated antics. Beneath that playful exterior, however, lies immense computational and combat power, making him an unfailingly dependable ally when it matters most.

Cold restraint meets boundless enthusiasm whenever the two are together, and their constant bickering hides a deep understanding of one another. Whether traveling across the universe, protecting Enigma, or facing an unknown threat, Turing and Bermuda always find their own way to overcome it side by side.
STORY_11248: Gulu is a chef robot who lives in Enigma. With precise calculations, he can balance every flavor in a dish to perfection. Though his body is made of cold steel, he welcomes every guest with warmth, filling the town’s daily life with laughter and comfort.
STORY_11251:
Kehinde is a weapons developer at Square Obelisk. Bursting with confidence and wild creativity, he approaches every invention with a passion bordering on obsession. 
His bold manner and impulsive nature can make him difficult to manage, but the brilliance behind his designs speaks for itself.
STORY_11252:
Hazel is a machina who once served as Turing’s trusted assistant at Lomond Manor and now works as her housekeeper. Patient and observant, she handles every task with care, and Turing trusts her completely.
Her quiet presence keeps Enigma in perfect order. Behind that gentle manner is a firm and disciplined strength—one that has also made her, at least in Bermuda’s eyes, his greatest rival.
STORY_11253:
Flywheeler is one of Enigma’s most popular entertainment robots. Agile and fearless, he takes the wheel of a dazzling mechanical vehicle and draws crowds with his death-defying stunts.
He lives for the stage and the applause, but treasures even more the sense of belonging Enigma has given him. Nothing delights him more than carrying an audience from laughter to breathless amazement.
STORY_11254:
Matheta is a young Spiritual Beast working at Square Obelisk. Easily flustered and somewhat clumsy, she often creates trouble while trying to set things right. Yet her mistakes never come from carelessness. 
Sincere at heart, she places unwavering trust in her companions.
STORY_11256:
Throp oversees personnel affairs at Square Obelisk. Calm and rational, he speaks with the measured certainty of someone used to keeping situations under control.
While others get swept up in the thrill of research, he weighs every risk against its reward, making him one of the organization’s most practical and level‑headed members.
STORY_11257:
Corespore is the heart of the Fissospore collective, commanding the swarm with terrifying adaptability and an extraordinary capacity to learn. 
It can mimic the forms and behaviors of those around it, making it a grave and ever-evolving threat no one can anticipate.
STORY_11260:
In the endless realm of illusion, Caesar, now a heroic spirit, remained asleep in the silent void. Yet the regrets he carried with him kept his soul from finding peace, even after death. Sensing his unrest, the elements gathered their power and created a dream, allowing him to witness the life he might have lived had he chosen another path…

        During the representative trials, House, Caesar’s closest friend, was accused of cheating and stripped of his qualifications. He attempted to appeal the decision, but his plea was dismissed without consideration. Consumed by anger and frustration, he gathered his fellow Corrodents and launched a series of protests against the authorities, which eventually escalated into acts of destruction. In response, the representative of beasts issued a kill order against House and his companions. Unable to stand by while his friend was condemned, Caesar hurried to the representative and pleaded for mercy, but his words fell on deaf ears.

        Exhausted and defeated, Caesar trudged back to his cave empty-handed. Just as he was about to lie down and rest, he noticed something had changed.

        [i]‘These things aren’t where I left them. Someone has been here… Could it be—’[/i] 

        Caesar’s heart tightened at the thought. Ignoring his exhaustion, he carefully searched the cave for any misplaced objects, then placed them back exactly where they belonged one by one.

        When he placed the final object, a brilliant light suddenly gathered in the air and transformed into a tiny beast no larger than his palm. It circled Caesar several times before flying toward the entrance. There, it stopped and looked back at him, as if urging him to follow.

        [i]‘It’s a message from House!’[/i]  Caesar hesitated. [i]‘But could this be a trap?’[/i] 

        [i]‘No… even if it isn’t, I cannot meet him. House has chosen a path I can’t follow.’[/i]

        After a moment of silence, he clenched his teeth and crushed the little beast in his hand. Then, burying his doubts deep within his heart, he returned to his bed and closed his eyes.

        However, even after falling asleep, Caesar found himself trapped within a nightmare.

        “House! No! STOP!” Caesar woke with a start and shot upright. Before he could steady his breathing, his communicator suddenly buzzed. A terrible premonition rose within him, but he forced it down and answered the call.

        “Inspector Caesar! The Corrodents are attacking the central city! We need your help immediately!”

        [i]‘Could it be House and his group… No, I have to stop him!’[/i]

        “Understood. I’m on my way!” Caesar ended the call and quickly composed himself before rushing toward the central city. On the way there, he passed through streets scarred by destruction and saw buildings left in ruins. The sight weighed heavily on his heart, but seeing no injured civilians gave him a brief sense of relief. 

        Unfortunately, that relief was short-lived. By the time Caesar arrived, it was already too late.

        There, he saw a group of men walking from the other end of the street, their uniforms stained with blood and their expressions cold. They looked as though they had just stepped off the battlefield.

        “Caesar, there you are. We’ve taken care of the rebel leader,” the representative of beasts said as he stepped forward. A victorious grin formed on his lips as he continued, “He was a very cunning man. He remained behind alone to hold us off so his companions could escape. But don’t worry, we’ll capture them all soon enough.”

        “No… That can’t be…” Caesar’s eyes widened in disbelief. Clenching his teeth, he pushed past the representative and his guards and rushed toward the central plaza. What awaited him there was a sight he would never forget—

         House stood in the center of the plaza, his beast form impaled by countless sharp blades. His eyes remained wide open, filled with resentment that refused to fade even after his death, his face still carrying the defiance he held until the very end.

        “HOUSE— !” Caesar’s cry echoed throughout the plaza, carrying a grief so deep that it seemed to tear through his very soul. Tears streamed down his face as he collapsed before House’s body. Only when his voice had faded into a broken whisper did his cries finally cease.

        Holding back his grief, he removed the blades from House’s body one by one. After pulling out the final blade, he gently closed House’s eyes, hoping his friend could finally find peace in death.

        [i]‘House, I knew you weren’t the kind of man who would ever cheat or deceive people. I will clear your name, I swear!’[/i] Caesar made that vow in his heart. Just as he was about to carry House’s body away, he noticed a familiar figure moving through the shadows.

 
        ‘That is… Lucius, the deputy representative… Why’s he carrying a large bag? …There’s only one way to find out.’ Suspicious, Caesar quickly concealed his presence and quietly followed from a distance.

         Lucius eventually stopped before another figure waiting in the shadows—the representative of beasts. As the two exchanged a glance, the representative quietly asked, “Is it done?”

        “It’s done. A child and a pregnant woman, all in the bag,” Lucius replied.

        “Heh, excellent. This should make things more heated.” The representative shrugged and continued,  “Honestly, that House was such a fool. He had the perfect image of a savage beast, but he was too gentle to act like one. All his attacks avoided civilians. Even this time, he didn’t leave us a single casualty, and I had no choice but to create two victims myself. Now it should be much easier to deal with those Corrodents.”

        “Don’t we have help from the people in the Heptara Unies?” Lucius asked.

        “Humph! Those people are all the same. They don’t like getting their hands dirty, and the moment things get difficult, they start complaining. But I know what they’re really after—they’re just looking for an excuse to demand a bigger share,” the representative scoffed.

        “But this dead child and pregnant woman should be enough to make them cooperate,” Lucius said as he opened the bag and emptied its contents onto the ground. The bodies were horrific, yet neither Lucius nor the Beast representative showed even the slightest emotion. Without a trace of sympathy, they handled the bodies like nothing more than garbage, arranging them to make it appear as though they had been victims of House’s attack.

        Caesar stayed hidden in the shadows, his hands trembling as he watched them leave.

        [i]‘How……? How can they do something like this without feeling anything at all?’[/i] Caesar felt something inside him break. The beliefs he had spent his life protecting, the justice he had placed his faith in, all began to collapse in that moment. The world he thought he understood was nothing like what he had believed it to be.

        Regret and grief filled his voice as he whispered through trembling lips, “House… You were right all along. We can’t change this corrupted world by following the rules. Sometimes, only those willing to take the most desperate measures have a chance to change it…”

        After that day, Caesar no longer sought justice through the path he once believed in. He secretly contacted House’s companions and became their new leader. He cast aside the hesitation and mercy that had once held him back, choosing instead to do whatever was necessary to avenge his friend, House…

        [i]“Whatever happens, House is still my closest friend. I can’t let him walk down a path that will only lead him astray.”[/i]
